●문서명: AI Impact Summit Declaration, New Delhi / 「AI 임팩트 정상회의 뉴델리 선언」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월 21일
●핵심내용:인도 뉴델리에서 개최된 AI Impact Summit 2026의 결과문서로, AI의 혜택을 인류 전체가 공유해야 한다는 원칙 아래 국제협력과 다중이해관계자 참여를 강조한 선언문임. 선언문은 인적자본 개발, 사회적 역량강화, 신뢰 가능한 AI, 에너지 효율성, 과학 분야 AI 활용, AI 자원의 민주적 확산, 경제성장과 사회적 선을 위한 AI 활용을 핵심 협력 분야로 제시함.
① 문서는 AI 혜택이 특정 국가·기업에 집중되지 않도록 국제협력과 다중이해관계자 참여를 확대하고, 개발도상국과 글로벌 사우스의 AI 접근성과 역량을 강화해야 한다고 강조함
② 정상회의 주요 의제로 인적자본·사회적 역량강화, 신뢰 가능한 AI, 에너지 효율, 과학 활용, AI 자원 민주화, 경제성장·사회적 선을 위한 AI 활용을 제시함
③ AI의 신뢰성·안전성·보안성·투명성을 확보하는 자발적 협력 프레임워크를 촉진하고, 과학·경제·사회·지속가능발전에 AI를 활용하되 환경적 지속가능성도 함께 고려해야 한다고 제시함

category: GPAI
title: [GPAI] 2026 뉴델리 이사회 공동의장 요약 성명
document_name: Summary statement of the GPAI Co-Chairs / 「GPAI 공동의장 요약성명」
body:
●기관: OECD / GPAI
●문서종류: 공동의장 요약성명 / 각료급 회의 결과문서
●문서명: Summary statement of the GPAI Co-Chairs / 「GPAI 공동의장 요약성명」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월 20일
●핵심내용:2026년 2월 20일 인도 뉴델리에서 AI Impact Summit 계기 개최된 GPAI Council Meeting의 공동의장 요약성명임. 회의는 싱가포르 Josephine Teo 디지털개발정보부 장관과 한국 배경훈 부총리 겸 과학기술정보통신부 장관이 공동의장을 맡았으며, GPAI가 OECD AI 원칙에 기반해 인간 중심적이고 안전하며 신뢰 가능한 AI를 촉진하는 국제 협력 플랫폼임을 재확인함.
① GPAI는 인간 중심·안전·신뢰 가능한 AI 확산과 경제·사회적 혜택 증진을 위해 회원국·전문가 간 국제협력을 강화하고 있다고 평가함
② 향후 중점과제로 AI 정책 추적, 컴퓨팅 역량·투자 데이터 제공, 히로시마 AI 프로세스 보고 프레임워크 개선 등 신흥기술 분석을 제시함
③ 신뢰 가능한 AI 도구·측정지표와 AI Policy Toolkit 개발을 통해 공유 원칙을 실질적인 정책 지식과 도구로 전환해 회원국의 정책 수립을 지원할 계획이라고 밝힘

category: OECD
title: [OECD] OECD.AI 지수
document_name: The OECD.AI Index / 「OECD.AI 지수」
body:
●기관: OECD
●문서종류: 기술문서 / AI 정책이행 측정지표 방법론 보고서
●문서명: The OECD.AI Index / 「OECD.AI 지수」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월 19일
●핵심내용:동 문서는 OECD AI 권고의 이행 정도를 국가별로 비교·평가하기 위해 개발된 복합 측정 프레임워크인 OECD.AI Index를 소개한 기술문서임. 지수는 OECD 회원국의 AI 생태계를 비교 가능한 방식으로 평가하기 위해 공식통계, 행정자료, 조사자료, 혁신적 데이터 출처를 결합하고, 2023년 및 2024년 결과를 제시함.
① OECD.AI Index는 OECD AI 권고 이행을 모니터링하기 위한 지표로, AI 연구개발·인프라·정책환경·일자리와 기술·국제협력의 5개 영역과 28개 지표로 구성됨
② 지수는 공식통계·행정자료·조사자료·비전통 데이터를 결합하고, 정규화·가중치 부여·민감도 검증 등을 거쳐 국가별 AI 정책·역량 수준을 비교하도록 설계됨
③ 2023~2024년 국가별 지수와 구성요소 간 차이가 크게 나타났으며, 향후 적용 국가 확대와 환경영향·AI 안전성·기업 AI 도입 등 추가 지표 검토가 예정되어 있다고 제시함

category: OECD
title: [OECD] 2025년까지의 AI 벤처캐피털 투자
document_name: Venture capital investments in artificial intelligence through 2025 / 「2025년까지의 인공지능 벤처캐피털 투자」
body:
●기관: OECD
●문서종류: 정책브리프 / AI 벤처캐피털 투자 동향 분석
●문서명: Venture capital investments in artificial intelligence through 2025 / 「2025년까지의 인공지능 벤처캐피털 투자」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월 17일
●핵심내용:동 문서는 OECD.AI Policy Observatory와 Preqin 데이터를 활용해 2012~2025년 전 세계 3만 3천 개 이상 AI 기업과 약 8만 5천 건의 거래를 대상으로 AI 벤처캐피털(VC) 투자 흐름을 분석한 정책브리프임. AI 기업에 대한 VC 투자는 2025년 전 세계 VC 투자액의 61%를 차지할 정도로 확대되었으며, 생성형 AI와 AI 컴퓨트 인프라 투자가 최근 투자 증가를 주도한 것으로 나타남.
① 보고서는 2025년 AI 기업이 전 세계 VC 투자액의 61%를 차지했으며, 생성형 AI 투자도 빠르게 확대되면서 AI가 글로벌 VC 시장의 핵심 투자 분야로 부상했다고 분석함
② AI VC 투자는 미국과 대형 메가딜, 특히 IT 인프라·호스팅 분야에 크게 집중되어 있으며, 초기단계 투자보다 후기단계 대규모 거래의 비중이 높아지고 있다고 평가함
③ 정책방향으로 AI·투자 리터러시 강화, 세제·보조금·공공-민간 공동투자, 규제 샌드박스, AI 스택 전반의 투자 다변화와 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 투자기준 연구를 제안함

category: 일본
title: [일본] AI전략회의·AI제도연구회 중간정리
document_name: 《AI戦略会議・AI制度研究会 中間とりまとめ》 / 「AI전략회의·AI제도연구회 중간정리」
body:
●국가: 일본
●기관: 내각부 AI전략회의 / AI제도연구회
●문서종류: 중간보고서 / 제도 설계 방향
●문서명: 《AI戦略会議・AI制度研究会 中間とりまとめ》 / 「AI전략회의·AI제도연구회 중간정리」
●발표시점: 2025년 2월 4일
●핵심내용: AI 관련 법제화의 방향을 제시한 중간보고서. 2024년 7월 이후 AI제도연구회 논의, 전문가·사업자 청문, 의견수렴을 거쳐 마련되었으며, AI 혁신 촉진과 리스크 대응을 병행하고 법령과 가이드라인을 적절히 조합하는 접근을 제시함. 정부의 AI 사령탑 기능 강화, 기본계획 수립, 히로시마 AI 프로세스 기반 지침 정비, 정부 조달·활용 기준 마련 등이 포함됨.
5대 핵심 축:
① 혁신과 리스크 대응 병행: 연구개발, 인재, 데이터, 컴퓨팅 기반을 지원하면서 위험관리 추진
② 법령·가이드라인 조합: 포괄적 규제보다 기존 법령과 자율지침의 결합 활용
③ 정부 사령탑 강화: AI 정책을 총괄할 정부 내 조정기능 강화
④ 정부 활용·조달: 공공부문이 AI 활용을 선도하고 조달 기준을 정비
⑤ 국제협조: OECD, G7 히로시마 AI 프로세스와의 정합성 및 상호운용성 확보

title: [APEC] 디지털무역·AI·온라인 안전 아태 정책회의 결과
document_name: Digital Trade, AI and Online Safety in Focus at Asia-Pacific Policy Discussion / 「아시아·태평양 정책논의에서 디지털 무역, AI 및 온라인 안전 중점 논의」
body:
●기관: APEC 디지털경제운영그룹(Digital Economy Steering Group)
●문서종류: 보도자료 / 정책논의 결과
●문서명: Digital Trade, AI and Online Safety in Focus at Asia-Pacific Policy Discussion / 「아시아·태평양 정책논의에서 디지털 무역, AI 및 온라인 안전 중점 논의」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월 3일
●핵심내용:APEC 회원경제들은 2026년 첫 고위관리회의 및 관련 회의 계기 중국 광저우에서 디지털 무역, AI, 온라인 안전 등 주요 디지털 정책 현안을 논의함. 논의는 개방적 시장 유지, 디지털 시스템 신뢰 강화, 디지털화 혜택의 폭넓은 공유를 목표로 하며, APEC 인터넷·디지털경제 로드맵에 따른 역내 협력 강화에 초점을 둠.
① APEC은 AI 확산과 디지털 상거래 확대에 대응해 디지털 무역·상호운용성·혁신 촉진과 디지털 전환 위험관리 방안을 논의함
② 라이브커머스·소셜커머스 등 새로운 전자상거래 모델의 중소기업 기회와 소비자 보호 과제를 검토하고, AI 역량 강화 등의 필요성을 강조함
③ 아동 온라인 안전과 디지털 접근성의 균형을 모색하고, 디지털 무역 정책을 뒷받침할 신뢰성 있는 데이터와 측정체계의 중요성을 공유함

category: UN
title: [UNIDIR] 2025년 군사 영역 책임 있는 AI 지역협의에 관한 고찰
document_name: The Global Prism of Military AI Governance: Reflections from the 2025 Regional Consultations on Responsible AI in the Military Domain / 「군사 AI 거버넌스의 글로벌 프리즘: 2025년 군사 영역 책임 있는 AI 지역협의에 관한 고찰」
body:
●기관: 유엔군축연구소(UNIDIR) 안보·기술 프로그램(Security and Technology Programme)
●문서종류: 종합보고서 / 군사 분야 책임 있는 AI 지역협의 결과보고서
●문서명: The Global Prism of Military AI Governance: Reflections from the 2025 Regional Consultations on Responsible AI in the Military Domain / 「군사 AI 거버넌스의 글로벌 프리즘: 2025년 군사 영역 책임 있는 AI 지역협의에 관한 고찰」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월 2일
●핵심내용:동 보고서는 2026년 제3차 REAIM 정상회의를 앞두고 2025년 아시아·태평양, 유럽·북미, 서아시아·중동, 아프리카, 중남미·카리브해에서 실시된 다섯 차례의 지역협의 결과를 정리함. 국가정책과 모범사례, 군사 AI의 위험과 기회, 조달·운용·사고대응, 산업계 참여 및 REAIM의 향후 발전방향을 분석하며, 논의의 중심이 원칙 수립에서 실제 이행과 운영으로 이동하고 있다고 설명함.
① 보고서는 군사 AI 거버넌스에 단일한 접근법은 없으나, 국제법 준수·위험감축·산업계 참여·고수준 원칙의 실무적 이행에서는 지역 간 공통 관심이 확인됐다고 평가함
② 주요 위험으로 비국가무장단체 확산, 오판·확전, 이중용도 기술·사이버 결합, 공급망 보안, 자동화 편향을 제시하고, 배치 전 교육·법적 검토·사고대응·투명성 강화 필요성을 논의함
③ 향후 조치로 역량강화·지식구축·정보공유·대화·산업계 참여·증거 기반 활동·REAIM 제도화를 제안하고, 책임 있는 조달지침·국제기준·정기 훈련과 협력체계 구축을 강조함

category: GPAI
title: [GPAI] 2030년까지 가능한 AI 발전 경로 탐색
document_name: Exploring possible AI trajectories through 2030 / 「2030년까지 가능한 AI 발전 경로 탐색」
body:
●기관: OECD / GPAI
●문서종류: OECD Artificial Intelligence Papers No. 55 / AI 미래 시나리오 분석 보고서
●문서명: Exploring possible AI trajectories through 2030 / 「2030년까지 가능한 AI 발전 경로 탐색」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월
●핵심내용:동 보고서는 2030년까지 AI 역량이 어떻게 발전할 수 있는지를 전문가 의견, 문헌 검토, 전략적 미래예측, 추세 외삽을 결합해 분석한 OECD 보고서임. 보고서는 AI 발전을 단일 전망으로 예측하지 않고, 2030년까지 가능한 네 가지 시나리오를 제시함.
① 보고서는 2030년 AI 발전을 정체·둔화·지속·가속의 4개 시나리오로 구분하고, 정책 논의를 위한 미래 경로로 제시함
② 시나리오별로 AI의 추론·자율성·업무수행 범위가 크게 달라지며, 정체 시에는 인간 의존이 높고 가속 시에는 광범위한 전략 목표와 현실세계 과제까지 수행할 가능성이 있다고 설명함
③ AI 발전의 불확실성이 큰 만큼 정부는 특정 전망에 의존하기보다, AI 진전의 정체와 급가속 양쪽에 모두 대응할 수 있는 유연한 정책·거버넌스 역량을 갖춰야 한다고 제시함

category: GPAI
title: [GPAI] 언론에 보도된 AI 사고와 위험 동향
document_name: Trends in AI incidents and hazards reported by the media / 「언론에 보도된 AI 사고와 위험 동향」
body:
●기관: OECD / GPAI
●문서종류: OECD Artificial Intelligence Papers No. 53 / AI 사고·위험 모니터링 분석 보고서
●문서명: Trends in AI incidents and hazards reported by the media / 「언론에 보도된 AI 사고와 위험 동향」
●발표시점: 2026년 2월
●핵심내용:동 보고서는 OECD.AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor(AIM)의 실시간 언론보도 데이터를 활용해 2022년부터 2025년 9월까지 보도된 AI 관련 사고와 위험의 주제별 동향을 분석한 OECD AI 보고서임. AI 사고·위험 보도는 합성미디어, 아동안전, 사이버공격·사기, 프라이버시, 건강, 지식재산권 등 14개 주제로 분류되며, 보고서는 언론보도 증가·간헐적 급증·감소라는 세 가지 패턴을 식별함.
① 보고서는 AI 사고·위험을 건강·인권·노동권·재산·환경 등에 피해를 초래하거나 초래할 수 있는 사건으로 정의하고, AIM을 통해 관련 언론보도를 실시간 추적한다고 설명함
② 주요 사고·위험 분야로 합성미디어·AI 기반 전쟁·자율주행차·프라이버시 침해를 제시하며, 특히 합성미디어·아동안전·사이버공격·사기·노동시장 혼란 관련 보도가 증가하고 있다고 분석함
③ 일부 분야의 보도 비중 감소가 실제 위험 감소를 의미하지는 않으며, 지속적 모니터링과 함께 판례·학술문헌·공개자료 등으로 AIM의 분석 범위를 확대할 필요가 있다고 강조함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Georgia SB 9 ("Ensuring Accountability for Illegal AI Activities Act")
document_name: Georgia SB 9 (Ensuring Accountability for Illegal AI Activities Act)
body:
Amends Georgia's election laws to prohibit fraudulent election interference using materially deceptive AI media within 90 days of an election. Requires AI-generated campaign ads to disclose AI use. Establishes penalties for violations and authorizes investigations by the Attorney General.

Enacts measures to address the use of AI-generated media in elections. 

Defines "materially deceptive media" and prohibits its publication with intent to deceive voters within 90 days of an election, establishing offenses for fraudulent election interference and solicitation thereof.

Excludes activities protected by the First Amendment, such as satire or journalism. 

Prescribes penalties, escalating from misdemeanors to felonies for repeat offenses, and grants jurisdiction to the Attorney General for prosecution upon recommendation from the State Election Board. 

Allows injunctive relief claims by affected individuals, candidates, or the Attorney General.

Mandates disclosure in campaign ads using AI-generated content, detailing implicated parties, and warning of potential fictitious elements. 

Regulates disclosure visibility and audibility, imposing fines for violations.

Empowers the election oversight commission to investigate complaints and promulgate rules under the act, effective upon gubernatorial approval or legislative enactment.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 682 (Health Care Coverage Reporting 2025)
document_name: California AB 682 (Health Care Coverage Reporting 2025)
body:
Requires health care plans and insurers to report claims that use AI, detailing processed and denied claims, costs, and demographic categories. Directs public website postings and allows regulatory rules on forms and content, ensuring privacy protections.

Regulates health care service plans and insurers in California to report annual claims data, requiring detail on claims processed or reviewed with artificial intelligence or predictive algorithms.  

Requires health care service plans, by February 1, 2026, and insurers, by February 1, 2028, to publicly report prior authorization data online, including approval and denial rates for standard and expedited requests, and timeframes for decisions.  

Obliges plans to include data on AI-assisted decisions in annual payment and dispute resolution reports starting February 1, 2027, disaggregated by demographics from 2029.  

Instructs the director and commissioner to create rules and regulations for report forms and content, ensuring compliance with privacy laws, including the Confidentiality of Medical Information Act and HIPAA.  

Allows directors and commissioners to reject and require correction of inadequate reports, with financial penalties for noncompliance by insurers.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 512 (Health Care Coverage: Prior Authorization 2025)
document_name: California AB 512 (Prior Authorization 2025)
body:
Regulates the use of AI for utilization review and management by health care service plans and disability insurers. Ensures AI tools base decisions on individual clinical circumstances, do not replace provider judgment, and are open for audit. Prohibits AI from denying care based on medical necessity without human oversight.

Restricts the use of artificial intelligence and algorithms in health care service plans and disability insurers for utilization review or management functions based on medical necessity.

Requires that AI tools do not replace health care provider decision-making, discriminate, or rely solely on group datasets.

Ensures AI tools base determinations on enrollee's personal and clinical data and comply with state, federal laws.

Mandates periodic reviews of AI tools' performance and prohibits their causing harm to enrollees.

Prohibits AI tools from independently denying, delaying, or modifying health services; such decisions must be made by licensed professionals.

Obliges plans and insurers to maintain transparency about AI use in their written policies, and permit inspections for compliance audits. 

Aligns with federal guidance on the use of AI by health services. 

Applies specifically to California-based health plans and Medi-Cal managed care to the extent federal approvals are secured.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HR 5784 Artificial Intelligence Wisdom for Innovative Small Enterprises Act 2025
document_name: HR 5784 AI–WISE Act 2025
body:
Instructs the Small Business Administration to create and maintain AI educational resources for small businesses, ensuring accuracy and stakeholder collaboration. Requires an advisory group, emphasizing comprehensibility and impartiality concerning AI tools.

Amends the Small Business Act to require the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to establish educational resources and modules on artificial intelligence for small businesses.

Requires these resources to cover topics such as AI model functions, risk management, privacy, human oversight in AI-informed decisions, and evaluation of AI's impact on operations and productivity.

Instructs the Administrator to ensure the resources are accurate and current by consulting with the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and an Advisory Working Group.

Mandates that the resources be publicly available on an SBA online platform and disseminated through resource partners.

Prohibits the materials from favoring specific AI models or developers over others.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HR7064 AI in Health Care Efficiency and Study Act 2025
document_name: HR7064 AI in Health Care Efficiency and Study Act 2025
body:
Instructs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to study AI strategies to improve healthcare administration and data security. Evaluates AI applications in reducing administrative burdens and enhancing cybersecurity. Requires reporting to Congress on findings, recommendations, and policy options.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to conduct a study within 18 months on AI applications in the healthcare industry.

Tasks the Secretary to evaluate strategies to enhance administrative efficiency, patient record accuracy, and ensure patient data privacy under HIPAA.

Directs the study to include evaluation of AI in reducing administrative burdens, improving data interoperability, and enhancing cybersecurity measures against threats like ransomware.

Instructs the Secretary to consult with various stakeholders including NIST, NIH, developers, and healthcare providers during the study.

Mandates a report, due 6 months after the study, detailing findings, existing AI tool assessments, recommendations for future AI-related research, and policy options to Congress.

Ensures any AI deployment supports administrative efficiency and strong patient privacy protections.

① 보고서는 EU의 농업·보건의료·제조·모빌리티 분야에서 AI 활용이 확대되고 있으나, 전반적인 도입률은 아직 제한적이고 대기업·자원 보유 기관 중심으로 진행되고 있다고 평가함
② 주요 활용사례로 농업로봇·예측분석, 의료영상·의약품 개발, 예측정비·품질관리, 자동주행·교통관리 등이 제시되며, 전문인력 부족과 데이터 품질·상호운용성 문제가 공통 병목으로 지적됨
③ 정책방향으로 부문별 데이터 거버넌스·AI 인프라 강화, 중소기업 지원, 안전한 시험환경, 규제 지침, 공공·민간·학계 협력과 최종이용자 공동설계를 제시함

body:
●기관: ASEAN / ASEAN Digital Ministers’ Meeting
●문서종류: 마스터플랜 / 지역 디지털협력 전략문서
●문서명: ASEAN Digital Masterplan 2030 / 「ASEAN 디지털 마스터플랜 2030」
●발표시점/채택시점: 2026년 1월
●핵심내용:동 문서는 2026~2030년 ASEAN의 지역 디지털협력 방향을 제시하는 전략문서로, 기존 ASEAN ICT Masterplan 2020 및 ASEAN Digital Masterplan 2025의 후속 프레임워크임. ADM 2030은 ASEAN을 “통합되고, 안전하며, 신뢰할 수 있고, 혁신적이며, 포용적인 디지털 공동체”로 발전시키는 것을 목표로 하며, AI를 경제 회복력, 사회적 포용, 혁신, 지속가능성을 촉진하는 핵심 기반기술로 제시함.
① ADM 2030은 ASEAN의 디지털 협력을 통합적·상호운용 가능한 생태계로 발전시키고, AI를 지속가능한 디지털 전환의 핵심 축으로 제시함
② 책임 있는 AI 확산을 위해 공동 거버넌스 프레임워크·국제표준·안전성 평가와 함께 AI 윤리·위험평가·공무원 역량강화를 추진하도록 제시함
③ 2026~2030년에는 녹색 디지털 인프라, AI 기반 지속가능성, AI 안전 네트워크와 위험감독 체계를 구축하고, 이후 ASEAN AI 표준의 글로벌 정렬과 국제 거버넌스 참여를 강화하도록 설정함

body:

●문서명: Future-proofing TVET: Strategies for digital transformation and AI integration / 「TVET의 미래 대비: 디지털 전환과 AI 통합 전략」
●발표시점: 2026년
●핵심내용:동 문서는 UNESCO-UNEVOC가 2025년 5월 말레이시아 쿠알라룸푸르에서 개최한 BILT Bridging Event 논의를 바탕으로, 기술직업교육훈련(TVET)의 디지털 전환과 AI 통합을 위한 정책 방향을 제시한 토론문서임. 문서는 AI와 디지털 기술을 TVET에 도입할 때 기술 자체보다 교사 역량, 제도 거버넌스, 포용적 정책설계, 지속가능한 재원, 산업계 협력에 관해 언급함.
① 문서는 TVET가 AI·디지털화·녹색전환에 대응하는 유연한 평생학습 체계로 전환되어야 하며, 기술은 교사와 인간 상호작용을 대체하기보다 보완해야 한다고 강조함
② AI·교육기술 도입은 명확한 목적과 파일럿·비용편익·학습성과 평가에 기반해야 하며, 정책 초기부터 교사·학습자·산업계 등 현장 주체의 공동설계가 필요하다고 제시함
③ 강한 거버넌스·교사와 기관 역량·공공민간 협력·지속가능한 재원과 인프라를 기반으로 국가·기관·국제 차원의 AI 기반 TVET 전략과 재숙련·향상훈련 체계를 강화하도록 권고함

body:
●기관: UNESCO
●문서종류: 안내서 / 사법부 대상 AI 기초 가이드
●문서명: AI Essentials for Judges / 「판사를 위한 AI 핵심 안내서」
●발표시점: 2026년
●핵심내용:UNESCO가 판사와 사법 종사자를 대상으로 AI의 기본 개념, 사법 분야 활용 가능성, 위험, 예방·시정 조치를 설명한 실무형 안내서임. 동 문서는 2023년 UNESCO가 96개국 사법 종사자를 대상으로 실시한 조사에서 법률전문가의 44%가 AI를 업무에 활용하고 있으나, 기관 차원의 교육이나 지침을 받은 응답자는 9%에 그쳤다는 결과를 바탕으로 작성됨.
① 사법부의 AI 도입이 전략 수립과 데이터·인프라 점검에서 출발해야 하며, 법원은 AI 시스템과 데이터에 대한 통제권 유지의 필요성을 언급함
② AI는 사건관리·문서분석·판결문 초안 보조 등에 활용될 수 있으나, 법적 분석과 최종 판단은 판사와 법원 인력이 수행해야 한다고 제시함

category: National – Strategy
org: Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services
title: Zimbabwe National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030
body:
Zimbabwe's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030 is led by the Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services and sets a national framework to harness AI for inclusive growth, innovation and national sovereignty. It defines strategic pillars on AI talent development, infrastructure and computational sovereignty, sectoral adoption, research and innovation, international collaboration, and governance and ethics.

The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030 establishes a national framework to harness artificial intelligence for inclusive growth, innovation and digital sovereignty, aligned with Vision 2030 and national development strategies. It addresses the opportunity presented by advances in AI while recognising risks such as inequality, skills shortages, fragmented data systems, infrastructure limitations and weak governance. The strategy seeks to ensure Zimbabwe shapes the adoption of AI in line with local values, national priorities and the Ubuntu philosophy.
The strategy is structured around six strategic pillars: AI Talent and Capacity Development; AI Infrastructure and Computational Sovereignty; AI Adoption and Service Transformation; AI Governance, Ethics and Regulatory Framework; AI Research, Development and Innovation; and Strategic International Collaboration and Diplomacy. These pillars focus on strengthening AI literacy and education, expanding research capacity, building secure compute and data infrastructure, promoting responsible and widespread sectoral adoption, and establishing ethical and regulatory safeguards. The strategy builds on identified national strengths, including high literacy levels, indigenous knowledge systems and an emerging digital ecosystem, while addressing gaps such as brain drain, limited institutional resources and data silos.
Target sectors include agriculture, mining, healthcare, education, financial services, manufacturing, transport and logistics, energy, public services, environment and climate resilience, and defence and security. AI is positioned as a tool to improve productivity, service delivery, governance transparency and economic diversification, with particular attention to inclusion of rural communities, women, youth and small and medium enterprises. The strategy was developed through a multi‑stakeholder process involving government, academia, the private sector, civil society, the diaspora and international partners.
Implementation, oversight and accountability are supported through defined governance mechanisms. Strategic direction is provided by the National AI Council, while day‑to‑day coordination, execution and monitoring are led by the AI Strategy Implementation Office, supported by sector‑specific Technical Working Groups. A dedicated Monitoring and Evaluation Framework defines indicators, targets and reporting processes across the strategy’s lifecycle, supported by public reporting and periodic reviews. Ethical considerations are integrated throughout, with commitments to human dignity, privacy, transparency, inclusivity, safety and accountability guiding AI development and deployment in Zimbabwe.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Use of AI in Business Intelligence System - Skrinja
body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation is planning to introduce AI-based predictive analytics into the Business intelligence system Skrinja (‘box’), which is used by different public authorities to analyse data about their policy area, like public sector salaries, public tenders and administrative procedures, supporting data-driven decisions in real time in public administration.

Slovenia’s Ministry of Digital Transformation is preparing to expand the country’s central business intelligence system, Skrinja, by integrating AI-driven predictive analytics. Skrinja already serves as a platform for public authorities to analyse data on areas such as public sector salaries, tenders, and administrative processes, helping improve oversight and efficiency. The planned upgrade seeks to move beyond descriptive analysis and enable real-time, forward-looking insights to support more effective, data-driven decision-making across public administration.

category: National – Strategy
title: Sweden’s AI Strategy
document_name: Sveriges AI-strategi
body:
Sweden’s AI strategy is a comprehensive national framework to make the country a global top-10 AI leader. It promotes responsible, secure, and trustworthy AI while strengthening innovation, research, and competitiveness. The strategy focuses on increased adoption across society, improved public services, and international cooperation, supported by an action plan and annual follow-up.

Context
Sweden’s first comprehensive AI strategy addresses the need for a coordinated national approach to artificial intelligence to strengthen competitiveness, public sector efficiency, and research capacity. It responds to previously fragmented efforts and seeks to leverage AI to drive societal benefit, sustainable development, and innovation, while managing risks related to privacy, security, and intellectual property. It also aims to position Sweden in an increasingly competitive global AI landscape.
Objectives
The overarching objective is for Sweden to become one of the top ten countries globally in AI. The strategy aims to:
Promote responsible, secure, and trustworthy AIIncrease AI adoption across society, particularly in the public sectorStrengthen research, innovation, and business competitivenessDeliver tangible societal benefits, including improved public servicesEnhance Sweden’s global position and technological capabilitySweden also aims to become world-leading in the use of AI in public administration.
Implementation and future development
The strategy will be implemented through an action plan with ongoing and planned measures, including:
AI and data related assignments across government agenciesReforms to enable more efficient data sharingAppointment of a national AI coordinatorStrengthened international cooperationImplementation is supported by annual follow-up, with the Swedish Agency for Digital Government and the Swedish Post and Telecom Authority responsible for monitoring progress, analysing developments, and proposing additional measures.
This approach enables continuous adaptation and supports scaling across sectors, as well as alignment with EU and international frameworks.
Process and evaluation
The strategy builds on earlier policy work, in particular:
The AI Commission’s report Roadmap for Sweden (SOU 2025:12)Sweden’s Digitalisation Strategy 2025–2030Going forward, it will evolve through regular follow-up, policy adjustments, and international benchmarking, including within the OECD framework.

category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
title: Santo Domingo Declaration — Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean
body:
The Santo Domingo Declaration is the outcome document of the Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, held on 25–26 June 2026 in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Supported by UNESCO and CAF, it approves a Roadmap f2026–2027 focused on governance and regulation, talent and the future of work, protection of vulnerable groups, environment and sustainability, and infrastructure, building on prior summits in Santiago.

The Santo Domingo Declaration was adopted on 25–26 June 2026 during the Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, hosted by the Government of the Dominican Republic. It was approved with the strategic backing of UNESCO and development bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF), and builds directly on two earlier summits, Santiago, Chile (2023) and Montevideo (2024), which established a regional AI governance process, including a dedicated Working Group and a first Roadmap covering 2024–2025.
The declaration values the outcomes of that first Roadmap, noting it enabled progress in developing regional instruments to strengthen AI governance. It highlights that the new Roadmap 2026–2027 represents a transition from planning towards active implementation, with an emphasis on building sustainable capacities and practical mechanisms to consistently address, in line with international human rights norms, specific challenges including AI-driven disinformation, equitable access to technology, and AI's associated environmental impact. The declaration underscores that regional leadership on ethical AI requires coordinated governance mechanisms, prepared human talent, protection of groups in vulnerable situations, responsible environmental policies, and robust, accessible, sustainable technological infrastructure.
Under the Roadmap 2026–2027, countries commit to a 12-month implementation horizon structured around five strategic lines: governance and regulation; talent and the future of work; protection of vulnerable groups; environment, sustainability and climate change; and infrastructure. Concrete outputs to be promoted include a Regional Group of Disinformation and AI Specialists, a rapid-response intervention Playbook, an open online course on gender-mainstreaming competencies in AI, a regional data infrastructure standard, and studies and workshops on technological infrastructure and data sandboxes.
On governance and oversight, the declaration consolidates the Working Group on the Ethics of AI as a permanent coordination body responsible for monitoring the Roadmap's implementation, periodically updating its outputs, and coordinating with other regional and international networks. It also establishes the Ministerial and High Authorities Summits on AI Ethics as an annual recurring space to review progress, approve new initiatives, and ensure continuity of the regional process.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: SPARK - "Accelerating Planning and Approval through AI"
body:
SPARK ("Accelerating Planning and Approval through AI") is a German initiative developed by the Federal Ministry for Digital and State Modernization and financed via the Climate and Transformation Fund. It provides agentic AI tools that accelerate complex planning and approval procedures by analysing application files, checking completeness and plausibility, and preparing decision proposals, while final decisions remain with staff. The tools were released as open source in April 2026.

SPARK is a central project of the Federal Government to modernise public administration through artificial intelligence. It addresses challenges in planning and approval procedures. The software was developed through an innovation partnership with the Federal Ministry for Digital and State Modernization developing the solution and the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy initiating and financing it as the department responsible for the development of Germany's hydrogen infrastructure.
The modules are modular, scalable and transferable to a variety of administrative procedures. First agents are already working in Hamburg for the approval of hydrogen core grid lines. The modules published so far cover the extraction of relevant information from application documents, formal completeness and plausibility checks, and supporting functions for process overviews, subsequent submissions and comments. Their basis is AI-supported legal dogmatics connected to legal databases, enabling automated deconstruction of norms and legal evaluation; further modules on substantive examination, legal assessment and decision-making are to follow during the year.
Following the "Best Use of AI in Government Services" award at the World Government Summit in Dubai in February 2026, the modules were made available under the "Public Money, Public Code" principle, allowing municipalities, companies and civil society to use and further develop them without licence fees. A Parliamentary State Secretary stated that approval durations could be halved, while the Federal Digital Minister referred to an estimated 80 percent acceleration of approval procedures based on the project's stage in 2026. For citizens and companies, this is stated to mean shorter waiting times, more transparency and more reliable processing.
Human oversight is central: the AI prepares information and proposals, while the final decision and legal responsibility remain with the responsible employees. The published code is to be understood as a reference and basis for integration rather than a finished security configuration, and a dedicated security review is stated to be mandatory before the AI is involved in productive approval procedures.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: SOPHOS
body:
SOPHOS is an AI‑enabled language learning tool designed for use across the Government of Canada. It was first developed to support Canadian diplomats by providing adaptive training in more than 15 foreign languages aligned with the Interagency Language Roundtable (ILR) scale. The application is now being expanded to offer English and French training that meets federal official languages requirements, helping public servants across all regions access consistent, affordable learning.

The Problem and Opportunity
The federal public service faces a critical gap in bilingual service delivery due to the high cost and limited availability of official language training. Traditional classroom models cost upwards of $70,000 per employee annually, resulting in long wait times and supply constraints. Simultaneously, the Government of Canada requires high language proficiency to deploy agile diplomats abroad. The SOPHOS initiative addresses these pressures by introducing a secure, agentic AI-enabled platform. It provides personalised, consistent learning for both official and foreign languages, ensuring linguistic capacity is no longer a barrier to operational readiness or career advancement.

Objectives of the Initiative
SOPHOS modernises training via a 24/7 AI-driven platform aligned with Public Service Commission (PSC) and Interagency Language Roundtable (ILR) standards. Key objectives include:
Accessibility & Personalisation: Providing real-time feedback, oral practice, and learner-driven maintenance tailored to individual needs.Cost Reduction: Complementing traditional instruction with AI-supported modules to allow for more targeted, affordable language acquisition.Security: Operating within a secure environment to ensure data sovereignty.Diplomatic Capacity: Strengthening international engagement by calibrating foreign language training to ILR proficiency levels.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: R&D Tax Credit System
document_name: 研究開発税制
body:
Japan's core corporate R&D tax credit system providing a 6–14% tax credit on total R&D expenses, with enhanced rates of 12–17% for SMEs, an open innovation add-on of up to 10%, and a new 40% credit for strategic technologies including AI from FY2026.

The Japanese R&D Tax Credit System (試験研究費の税額控除) is a long-standing element of Japan's innovation policy, administered by METI and the NTA. The system operates through blue-form corporate tax returns. Core credit (general category): 6–14% of total qualifying R&D expenses, with the rate sliding upward as R&D intensity increases (R&D expenses as a percentage of total expenses); the credit ceiling is 25% of annual corporate tax liability, extendable to 20–30% depending on changes in R&D spending. SME special rate: 12–17%, with a higher base rate to compensate for limited access to other innovation incentives. Open innovation add-on: an additional up to 10% credit for R&D expenses related to joint or commissioned research with universities and certified research institutions; credit ceiling of 10% of corporate tax. From FY2026, a new strategic technologies track was introduced under the FY2026 Tax Reform: 40% credit for R&D expenses related to six 'national strategic technologies' designated by the Cabinet Office (including AI and robotics; semiconductors and communications; quantum technology; space; bio and healthcare; fusion energy); 50% for joint/commissioned research in these areas with certified institutions; ceiling of 10% of corporate tax. In FY2023, approximately JPY 950B in deductions were claimed under the R&D credit system across all categories. Target audience: all Japanese companies conducting qualifying R&D, from SMEs to large enterprises.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: Prompting Guide for Public Administration
document_name: Guía de prompting para la gestión pública
body:
The Prompting Guide for Public Administration is a national guidance for professionals working at National Public Administration. It supports the responsible use of generative AI by providing practical instructions, legal safeguards, and human oversight criteria for interacting with large language models. It was developed to strengthen institutional digital capabilities while ensuring data protection, transparency, and accountability in the use of AI tools.

The Prompting Guide for Public Administration was developed to support professionals across Argentina’s National Public Administration as the use of generative AI tools rapidly expanded within government. As public servants increasingly rely on large language models for drafting, analysis and information processing, the guide provides a shared institutional framework to ensure that prompting practices are safe, effective and legally compliant.

The guide addresses both skills development and governance. It introduces a practical, structured methodology for prompt design—most notably the ROCLET framework (Role, Objective, Context, Limitations, Style and Output type)—to improve the quality, clarity and reproducibility of AI‑assisted work. At the same time, it establishes clear safeguards covering data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, transparency and bias mitigation. AI‑generated outputs are explicitly defined as preliminary inputs that support, but do not replace, human judgment or legal, technical and administrative responsibility.

Although the guide has not yet been formally published, its expected impact is clear. It is designed to strengthen institutional AI literacy, standardise prompting practices across agencies and reduce risks such as data exposure, hallucinations and overreliance on automated outputs. By embedding mandatory human supervision and traceability into AI‑assisted workflows, the initiative aims to increase confidence, accountability and compliance with Argentina’s legal and administrative framework.

Key challenges emerged during the design phase. Balancing innovation with strict legal and security requirements—particularly around data protection and institutional responsibility—required careful framing. Another challenge was ensuring that the guide discourages dependency on AI outputs while promoting their responsible use. The main lesson learned is that practical, operational methodologies are more effective than abstract principles alone. Clear boundaries, institutional endorsement, targeted training and regular updates are essential for sustainable adoption.

The central purpose of the guide is to professionalise how public servants interact with AI systems, enabling consistent, transparent and responsible use across government. Following formal publication, it is expected to be institutionalised through internal dissemination, training programmes and integration into broader digital transformation and AI‑governance initiatives. Over time, the guide may be updated to reflect technological advances, regulatory changes and feedback from practical implementation.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: National Office of Information Technologies (ONTI) AI Agents Guidelines
document_name: Lineamiento ONTI Agentes de IA
body:
Standard guide that is being developed by the National Office of Information Technologies to guide the design and sizing of projects incorporating Artificial Intelligence Agents in public administration. It is only aimed at national public administrations seeking to adopt this technology in a planned and responsible manner. Its objective is to disseminate best practices, reduce risks, and ensure secure, effective implementation aligned with State priorities and regulations.

The initiative consists of a standard guideline developed by the National Office of Information Technologies (ONTI), as the governing body, to guide the design and sizing of projects that incorporate Artificial Intelligence Agents in public administration. It arises from the lack of common criteria for the development of these systems and the risk of isolated implementations with proprietary standards, design flaws, or deficiencies in security and governance. It also responds to the need to organise the growing adoption of generative AI-based tools within the National Public Administration. 
The guideline aims to establish a common framework that promotes open standards and interoperability, incorporates security, governance, and human-in-the-loop oversight criteria, and facilitates informed decisions regarding the levels of autonomy of the agents. It also seeks to optimise the use of public resources, strengthening the efficiency and effectiveness of technology projects through best practices in architecture, risk assessment, and results measurement. 
While not mandatory, its use is recommended as a best practice guide for the design and sizing of initiatives involving AI Agents. It will be integrated into formal, non-binding technical evaluation processes and updated based on technological advancements. Furthermore, it is complemented by dissemination and training activities targeting technical, legal, and procurement areas, and can serve as a reference for other levels of government, given the guiding role currently played by ONTI's technological standards.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: IPS Córdoba Assistant — AI Policy Analysis Agent for Social Progress Governance (Subnational: Province of Córdoba)
document_name: Asistente IPS Córdoba: agente de análisis de políticas de IA para la gobernanza del progreso social.
body:
The IPS Córdoba Agent is an AI-powered policy tool integrated into the Social Progress Index dashboard for Córdoba’s 427 localities. It analyses quality-of-life data across 12 components and 57 indicators, combining social metrics, trends, and policy literature. More than a chatbot, it provides contextualised analysis and actionable recommendations so mayors and local officials can turn data into informed public policy, targeted investment, and evidence-based decisions.

The Province of Córdoba measures the Social Progress Index across all 427 of its localities over two census periods, producing one of the most granular subnational quality-of-life datasets in Latin America. Despite the richness of this data, a persistent and well-documented gap existed between data production and data use in public administration: mayors, municipal officials, and local planners often lacked the time, technical capacity, or analytical tools to translate 57 social indicators into concrete policy decisions. Complex statistical products were being generated but not acted upon. The IPS Córdoba Agent was developed specifically to close this gap — not by simplifying the data, but by building an intelligent analytical layer on top of it that is capable of reasoning across indicators, localities, time periods, and policy frameworks simultaneously.

The initiative has three core objectives. First, to democratise access to complex social intelligence: any local official — regardless of technical background — should be able to query their territory's social performance in natural language and receive a rigorous, grounded analysis in return. Second, to support evidence-based policy design at the local level by connecting social diagnoses directly to actionable intervention options drawn from provincial development frameworks. Third, to strengthen a culture of data-driven governance across Córdoba's municipalities, embedding AI-assisted analysis as a routine part of local decision-making rather than an exceptional resource.

The IPS Córdoba Assistant is designed and should be understood as a policy analysis agent, not a retrieval chatbot. The distinction is substantial and consequential. A conventional chatbot answers discrete questions by retrieving pre-existing text. This agent, by contrast, performs multi-step analytical reasoning: it interprets a locality's indicator-level results, identifies patterns of improvement or deterioration across dimensions and sub-dimensions, benchmarks performance against provincial averages, infers which population groups are most affected by specific social gaps, and generates policy recommendations grounded in a curated knowledge base that includes academic literature on human development, the provincial development model, and validated intervention frameworks. The agent synthesises all of this into a coherent, contextualised policy narrative — a form of analytical output that would otherwise require a trained policy analyst.

category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
title: HUDERIA – Methodology for assessing the risks and impacts of artificial intelligence systems
body:
HUDERIA is a Council of Europe initiative comprising a methodology adopted in 2025 and a model approved in 2026 to assess risks and impacts of artificial intelligence systems on human rights, democracy and the rule of law. It provides structured, technology‑neutral guidance and tools to help public and private actors identify, assess, prevent and mitigate risks across the AI lifecycle.

HUDERIA is a Council of Europe initiative developed by the Committee on Artificial Intelligence to provide structured guidance for assessing the risks and impacts of AI systems on human rights, democracy and the rule of law. It builds on earlier work initiated between 2019 and 2021 and was formally adopted in stages between 2024 and 2026 to translate human rights principles into practical tools.
The initiative addresses the need for consistent and practical approaches to evaluating AI systems across their lifecycle, particularly as such systems may have complex and context‑dependent impacts on individuals and society. It adopts a socio‑technical perspective, integrating technical, legal, social and economic considerations to help identify and analyse risks, including their severity and probability. 
HUDERIA combines two complementary elements: a high‑level methodology and an operational model. The methodology sets out core processes for risk and impact management, while the model provides adaptable tools such as the Context‑Based Risk Analysis (COBRA) resources. These include stages such as preliminary scoping, risk factor analysis, stakeholder engagement, detailed assessment, and mitigation planning. The process is iterative, requiring regular review to ensure that risks are reassessed as AI systems evolve or operate in changing environments. 
Designed for both public and private actors, HUDERIA is flexible and technology‑neutral, allowing adaptation across sectors, legal systems and levels of capacity. It is a non‑legally binding instrument that supports the implementation of approaches aligned with the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law, with the aim of fostering trustworthy, accountable and rights‑respecting AI.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: Guide to Egypt's National AI Governance Framework
body:
Egypt’s National AI Governance Framework is the suite of all AI Governance instruments and publications that establishes a comprehensive, sovereign, and human centric approach to governing artificial intelligence across the public and private sectors.  Rooted in Egypt’s constitutional values and aligned with global best practices, the Framework positions Egypt as a regional anchor in responsible AI.

The initiative addresses gaps in clear, interoperable rules for responsible AI in Egypt while leveraging AI’s potential to improve public services, spur inclusive growth, and position the country as a regional hub through a sovereign, human‑centric governance framework. Its objectives are to apply a risk‑based model with defined tiers, require a “dual‑check” (ethical impact + technical audit) compliance process for high‑risk systems, and assign clear roles to a central policy body alongside sectoral regulators. 
It also aims to build the enablers for safe adoption - developing human capital, improving data quality and sovereignty, providing sovereign cloud/HPC infrastructure, and supporting SMEs. The guide additionally seeks to align Egypt with international standards for global interoperability. Finally, it establishes a living framework with sandboxes, continuous monitoring, and a phased roadmap to adapt to technological change and inform future legislation

title: GPU provision measures under the National AI Project to support SMEs and startups
body:
Korea's Ministry of SMEs and Startups secured 264 B200 GPUs under the National AI Project to support SMEs and startups. Delivered free via NHN Cloud, two programmes are funded: a manufacturing project (64 GPUs) targeting production and quality control AI, and a startup incubator (200 GPUs) covering strategic AI development, industry-specific solutions, and early-stage founder support. Applications run April–May, support commences June 2025.

Korea's National AI Project, coordinated through the 6th Science and Technology Minister's Meeting, allocated approximately 3,000 of the 10,000 GPUs procured via the 2025 supplementary budget across ministry-level programmes. The Ministry of SMEs and Startups submitted two project proposals, both of which were approved, securing a combined 264 GPUs exclusively for smaller firms and founders.
 
The manufacturing-focused project supports consortiums of technology firms and manufacturing companies, providing end-to-end assistance from R&D through to on-site deployment. Participating consortiums may apply GPU resources to AI training on manufacturing process data, dataset development, and technology validation. The initiative aims to accelerate AI transformation in Korea's SME manufacturing sector and lay the groundwork for a sustainable manufacturing innovation ecosystem.
 
The larger startup incubator operates across three tracks. The Strategic AI Development track (85 GPUs) combines university and government-funded research institute expertise with startup proprietary technologies. The Industry-Specific AI Solutions track (85 GPUs) fosters inter-company collaboration on sector-focused innovation. The Startup for All track (30 GPUs) targets aspiring entrepreneurs, pairing computing access with AI incubation, mentorship, and investment linkage.
 
The initiative responds directly to the persistent barrier that high computing costs represent for smaller firms and first-time founders, reflecting a policy commitment to ensuring AI transformation is not the exclusive domain of large corporations.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: GOV.BR Chatbot
document_name: Chatbot GOV.BR
body:
The Chat GOV.BR is an interface tool that aims to provide and maintain a complete and integrated communication and relationship service with citizens regarding the provision of public services, encompassing multiple channels, digital service, automation, and the use of AI resources, including LLMs, proprietary to the generative IA platform or integrated from third parties, the construction of proactive communication journeys, and integration with government systems.

The Chat Gov.BR was built as a secure platform to manage government AI chatbots using LLMs and RAG technology. This ensures millions of Brazilians get accurate and safe answers to public policies. It is essential because 144 agencies are preparing their own assistants. Our central infrastructure saves costs, protects data, and improves services. 

In the pilot, the GOV.BR Chat helped high school students to enroll in graduation, clarifying doubts about the ENEM (the national exam, similar to "SATs") and SISU (the University selection system after ENEM results). The primary goal of this pilot project was to support high school students throughout their academic journey by providing clear guidance on the SISU system and other public policies. This initiative aimed to increase citizen confidence in official government communications while testing the ability of AI tools to handle massive peaks of demand when millions of people use the system simultaneously. Furthermore, the chatbot collected performance metrics and interaction data, which allowed leaders to make better, evidence-based decisions to continuously improve digital public services.

The initiative then evolved from a simple idea into a functional tool with a dedicated knowledge base. In January 2026, the government sent a proactive message to students to announce the ENEM results. This was a significant evolution because the chatbot moved from a passive tool to a proactive one. Instead of waiting for the student, the government started the conversation to clarify the next steps for SISU. This test showed that the government can share accurate information on a massive scale.

Looking ahead, this pilot is the foundation for a more modern and inclusive digital governance model. After the team assesses the final performance of this project, the goal is to institutionalize the use of AI in government communication.  By using the lessons learned from this education case, the government aims to create "transactional chats." In the future, citizens will not only receive information but will also be able to request benefits and complete government tasks directly through the chatbot.

The initiative has yielded measurable results. In the Education case, we reached 6 million students, with a 3.5% interaction rate and an average of 5 messages per user. With Gov.br support, the chatbot independently resolved 65% of queries, significantly reducing human escalation. We measure these impacts using real-time platform analytics and resolution metrics.

Developing the GOV.BR chatbot brought several challenges. The main risk was the possibility of incorrect or confusing answers due to flaws in the knowledge base. To address this, we implemented a phased testing strategy: we started with internal checks and followed with a pilot group of students. These tests were essential to build the confidence needed for a large-scale launch.

category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
title: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)
body:
The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) is a joint initiative between the European Union, participating European countries and private partners. Its goal is to develop a world‑class supercomputing ecosystem in Europe by providing access to supercomputers, quantum computers, AI factories and research and innovation projects, implemented through coordinated infrastructure deployment, access calls and collaborative programmes.

Under the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU), access to AI compute is provided primarily through the AI Factories programme, which makes AI‑optimised supercomputing capacity available to European researchers, startups, SMEs, industry and public bodies. The initiative focuses on enabling the training and deployment of large‑scale AI models by offering tailored access to high‑performance computing resources combined with technical support.
Rather than offering cash-based cloud credits, EuroHPC provides what functions as an in‑kind compute subsidy. AI startups and SMEs can access supercomputing capacity free of charge for innovation activities through the Industrial Innovation track. This access replaces costs that would otherwise arise from commercial cloud GPU usage, while larger or non‑eligible industrial use cases can obtain compute through pay‑per‑use arrangements.
AI Factories also support publicly funded research and collaborative projects by offering free access to AI compute for scientific applications, including machine learning, foundation models and generative AI. This applies in particular to projects funded under Horizon Europe or the Digital Europe Programme, ensuring that advanced AI workloads can be developed without direct infrastructure costs for eligible users. Access is organised through structured allocation modes that scale from small experimental use to very large GPU‑intensive workloads.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Encyclical letter Magnifica Humanitas
body:
Magnifica Humanitas is an encyclical issued by Pope Leo XIV on 15 May 2026, addressing safeguarding human dignity in the era of artificial intelligence. It calls for immediate and ongoing action to ensure AI serves the common good through ethical governance, regulation, education and shared responsibility. The initiative promotes transparency, accountability and international cooperation to counter inequality, exclusion and technocratic dominance.

Magnifica Humanitas is an encyclical issued by Pope Leo XIV in 2026 that sets out a comprehensive framework for addressing the impact of artificial intelligence on human dignity and society. It forms part of the broader Social Doctrine of the Church and positions AI as a major transformation requiring moral, social and political discernment rather than a purely technical response.
The initiative responds to the rapid expansion of digital technologies, highlighting both their potential benefits and their risks. It recognises AI as “a valuable tool” that can improve living conditions and support decision-making, while stressing that it is not neutral and can “shape decision-making processes” and society itself. The text identifies key concerns, including the concentration of technological power in private actors, the opacity of algorithmic systems, and the risk of exclusion, inequality and manipulation.
A central component of the initiative is the call for governance mechanisms to ensure that AI serves the common good. It emphasises the need for “responsibility, transparency and the governance of AI”, arguing that technological systems must remain subject to ethical oversight and public accountability. The initiative highlights the importance of regulatory frameworks, independent oversight and participatory processes, as well as international cooperation to address the global nature of digital technologies. It also underlines that responsibility must be shared across developers, policymakers and users.
The encyclical further examines the societal implications of AI, particularly in communication, education and the labour market. It warns that automation and digital systems may disrupt employment, create new forms of inequality and reduce human agency if not carefully managed. At the same time, it stresses the role of education in fostering critical thinking, responsible use of technology and an “educational alliance” adapted to the digital age. 
Finally, the initiative frames AI within a broader vision of integral human development. It rejects purely technocratic or efficiency-driven models, advocating instead for a human-centred approach that prioritises dignity, solidarity and social justice. The encyclical calls for a balance between innovation and ethical reflection, ensuring that technological progress strengthens, rather than undermines, human relationships and the common good.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: Egypt's National Generative AI Guidelines
body:
Egypt’s National Generative AI Guidelines provide a principles‑based framework to ensure the safe, responsible, and transparent use of generative AI. The document outlines risks, ethical safeguards, governance practices, sector‑specific guidance, and international alignment to support innovation while protecting human rights, privacy, and public trust.

Egypt’s National Generative AI Guidelines aim to address the emerging risks and opportunities created by rapidly advancing generative AI technologies. The initiative responds to challenges such as misinformation, deepfakes, hallucinations, bias, privacy risks, and declining public trust. It also seeks to leverage the transformative potential of generative AI to strengthen national competitiveness, modernize public services, and empower education, research, and innovation. 
The initiative’s objectives include establishing a principles‑based, risk‑proportionate governance framework aligned with global standards from UNESCO, OECD, the G7 Hiroshima Process, and others. It aims to ensure transparency, accountability, human oversight, and responsible use across developers, deployers, institutions, and individual users. It further sets targeted guidance for high‑impact contexts such as education, public information, and synthetic media, while promoting ethical safeguards and human‑centered design.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: Egypt National Guidelines for Trustworthy and Responsible AI
body:
The National Guidelines for Trustworthy and Responsible AI (the Guidelines) establish a
national reference for the responsible development, deployment, and oversight of Artificial Intelligence systems across the public and private sectors. These Guidelines aim to ensure that AI is used safely, transparently, and ethically, while supporting innovation and digital transformation in alignment with Egypt’s Vision 2030 and the National AI Strategy.

These Guidelines provide a practical, risk‑proportionate playbook for all actors across the full AI lifecycle. They aim to curb malicious, malfunction, and systemic risks while aligning with Vision 2030 and global standards, and prepare institutions for future regulation through readiness self‑assessments.

They provide actionable directions for organizations on how to manage AI
systems responsibly, and seek to:
Protect individuals’ rights and societal well-beingEnsure ethical and trustworthy use of AIStrengthen institutional accountability and transparencyPromote innovation grounded in safety and sound governanceAlign Egypt with leading international standards and practicesThe guidelines apply to all AI actors in Egypt, including government entities; enterprises and private-sector developers; and community actors and individuals.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Digitalization & AI Introduction Subsidy 2026
body:
A Japanese national grant programme — a renamed and AI-refocused evolution of the long-running IT Introduction Subsidy — providing SMEs and micro-enterprises with subsidies to purchase and adopt pre-registered IT tools, with AI-enabled tools now prioritised as a core adoption target.

The Digitalization & AI Introduction Subsidy 2026 is the 2026-cycle successor to the IT Introduction Subsidy (IT導入補助金), Japan's primary SME digitalisation grant since 2017. For the 2026 cycle, the programme was renamed to explicitly incorporate AI, reflecting a strategic shift by the Small and Medium Enterprise Agency (SMEA) and METI towards prioritising AI adoption. The programme subsidises the purchase of pre-registered software and tools from a registry maintained by the secretariat (SMRJ), with AI-enabled tools explicitly prioritised and flagged with a dedicated AI filter for 2026. Applications are handled through accredited IT Introduction Support Businesses, who serve as mandatory implementation partners. The programme offers four streams: a Standard Stream for business process digitalisation; an Invoice Stream for e-commerce and invoice-compliance tools; a Security Stream for cybersecurity services; and a Multi-Party Stream for consortia of 10 or more SMEs pursuing joint DX initiatives. Grant amounts under the Standard Stream range from JPY 50,000 to JPY 4,500,000, covering 50% of costs for standard SMEs and up to 80% for micro-enterprises. A new wage growth requirement introduced for 2026 means repeat applicants must demonstrate a pay increase plan, with partial repayment triggered if targets are unmet. Multiple application rounds run throughout the year from 30 March 2026.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Bioeconomy Strategy for R&I
body:
The Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, in collaboration with different stakeholders, is developing a knowledge-intensive bioeconomy strategy for R&I. This strategy integrates aspects of digitalisation within the sector, including the application of AI. The strategy is accompanied by an action plan with defined timelines.

Latvia’s Investment and Development Agency, working with sectoral partners, is drafting a bioeconomy strategy for research and innovation that emphasises knowledge intensity and sustainability. A key feature of the strategy is the integration of digitalisation tools, including AI, to strengthen productivity, resource efficiency, and monitoring across bio-based industries. The strategy is linked to a structured action plan with timelines, ensuring that measures are not only conceptual but also accompanied by concrete steps for implementation. By embedding AI into the broader bioeconomy framework, Latvia aims to align innovation policy with its sustainability goals while giving local firms and research bodies clearer guidance on future priorities.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Basic Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of Foundation for Trustworthiness ("AI Basic Act")
body:
South Korea's AI Basic Act was passed by the National Assembly on 26 December 2024, taking effect January 2026. It consolidates 19 bills into a national governance framework, establishing an AI Master Plan, the National AI Committee, and an AI Safety Institute, while supporting the AI industry through R&D, data infrastructure, clusters, and SME/startup assistance, and setting transparency, safety and accountability obligations for high-risk and generative AI.

The AI Basic Act followed over four years of legislative discussion, having first been tabled in the National Assembly in July 2020. The 22nd National Assembly merged 19 separate bills through bipartisan agreement, passing the consolidated legislation through the Science, ICT, Broadcasting and Communications Committee on 26 November 2024, the Legislation and Judiciary Committee on 17 December 2024, and finally the plenary session on 26 December 2024. Korea is the second country in the world to enact such foundational AI legislation, following the US Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (October 2023) and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (June 2024).
The Act rests on three main pillars. First, it creates a framework for AI development and trust-based infrastructure: the Minister of Science and ICT may establish and implement an AI Master Plan every three years after gathering input from relevant ministries and local governments, and the Act provides the legal basis for the National AI Committee, chaired by the President and launched in September 2024, as well as the AI Safety Institute, a specialised body protecting citizens' lives, bodies and property from AI risks.
Second, it supports the AI industry through government backing for research and development, standardisation, training data policies, and the promotion of AI adoption. It stipulates the designation of AI clusters, the establishment of AI data centres, and the promotion of AI convergence, alongside measures for securing AI experts, special support for SMEs, and fostering of startups.
Third, it establishes a safe and trustworthy foundation for high-risk and generative AI, defining these categories as regulatory targets and setting obligations around transparency, safety, and operator responsibilities, alongside a legal basis for voluntary safety and trustworthiness certification and AI impact assessments.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Agentic AI Hub
body:
The Agentic AI Hub is a German initiative by the Federal Ministry for Digital and State Modernization, launched on 9 March 2026, pairing 17 municipalities with ten start-ups across 18 pilot projects covering administrative tasks such as housing benefit and naturalisation. Startups and municipalities were selected from around 400 start-up and almost 200 municipal applications.

The Agentic AI Hub is the central interface between public administration and AI start-ups, translating bureaucratic problems into technical prototypes that are safely piloted and, where successful, scaled to what works. Autonomous AI agents take over administrative routines: checking applications for completeness, requesting missing documents, analysing documents and preparing proposals for official decisions. The BMDS leads the initiative, supported by DigitalService.
Pilots are organised around five fields of application: simplifying citizen interaction, supporting citizen-oriented administrative processes, supporting internal administrative processes, building digital tools, and building infrastructure for agentic AI. Selection was carried out by the BMDS and DigitalService, supported by an advisory board from science and industry including representatives of the German Association of Cities, UnternehmerTUM and Merantix, based on strategic fit, representativeness and scalability. The application phase ran from the end of January to the end of February 2026, drawing around 400 start-up and almost 200 municipal applications.
Ten start-ups and 17 municipalities deliver 18 separate pilot projects, each addressing a different use case: forml automates housing eligibility checks in Frankfurt and Düsseldorf; Celonis applies process mining to receivables management in Nuremberg and naturalisation in Munich; Summ AI models processes via voice recording across seven municipalities; LeistungsLotse digitises housing benefit applications in Nettetal; Myosotis/formfix supports care-assistance applications in Cologne and Berlin districts; deepset builds an AI orchestration layer in Borken; lector.ai automates mail sorting in Neckar-Odenwald; and Tucan Systems with Speechmind pilot meeting documentation in Bielefeld.
Over the three months following the March 2026 launch, the BMDS and DigitalService examine each pilot for effectiveness and scalability, with the goal of supporting employees rather than replacing them. In April 2026, parliamentary members raised questions about the limits of automation, transparency and costs, with concrete guidelines and best-practice examples identified as next steps.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: AI-Specific Evaluation Framework for Public Procurement in Korea
document_name: 공공조달 AI 적용 제품·서비스 특화 심사기준 마련
body:
Korea’s Public Procurement Service is developing an AI-specific evaluation framework for public procurement to enable the safe and effective adoption of AI products and services. The initiative introduces new assessment criteria covering AI performance, reliability, transparency, and risk management, addressing the limitations of traditional procurement standards. It aims to support trustworthy AI adoption while fostering innovation and market access for AI suppliers.

Public procurement plays a strategic role in Korea’s AI ecosystem, representing a large-scale demand-side policy instrument. At the same time, Korea became the first country in the world to enact a comprehensive AI Basic Act, establishing overarching principles for trustworthy and responsible AI. However, despite this landmark legislation, clear operational definitions and classification criteria for AI-enabled products and services have remained underdeveloped in the procurement context. Existing public procurement evaluation systems—designed primarily for conventional goods and services—have therefore proven inadequate for assessing AI-enabled offerings, particularly with respect to algorithmic performance, data dependency, model reliability, and potential risks.

This initiative responds to that institutional and practical gap by developing an AI-specific evaluation framework tailored to public procurement. Rather than applying a single, uniform assessment model, the framework introduces procurement-instrument–specific AI evaluation approaches across major programmes, including innovation procurement, excellent product designation, and multi-supplier framework contracts. Each procurement scheme incorporates AI-relevant evaluation criteria aligned with its policy objectives and operational characteristics, recognising that AI products require different assessment logics depending on the purchasing mechanism. Instead of relying solely on legal definitions, the framework provides practical and evaluative criteria to identify and assess AI-enabled products and services within procurement processes. New assessment dimensions include AI model appropriateness, robustness, transparency, lifecycle risk management, and alignment with public sector use cases, complementing existing criteria on public value, performance, and innovation. This approach allows contracting authorities to more accurately distinguish genuinely AI-enabled solutions from conventional products, while ensuring that AI-specific risks are systematically considered.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: AI in Digital Health
body:
The Digital Health Agency’s AI initiative aims to improve how health information is used to support safer, more connected care for Australians. It helps clinicians and consumers by providing faster insights and reducing manual work. The initiative was created to address growing demand for timely, reliable health information and to ensure emerging AI tools are used safely and responsibly in the health system.

The main objectives are to support safer care, reduce manual work, and improve how health information flows across the system. This includes testing practical AI tools that can summarise information, detect patterns and help people find what they need more easily. The initiative also focuses on strong governance, transparency and safeguards so that AI is used in ways that protect privacy and maintain public trust. Over time, the initiative is expected to grow from early exploration into more structured, systemwide solutions. Future work includes developing standards, guidance and processes that help health organisations adopt AI safely and consistently. As confidence increases and successful solutions are identified, the initiative could scale to support national services, clinical environments and consumerfacing tools. The initiative continues to evolve based on feedback from the sector, advances in technology and lessons from early trials. This iterative approach helps ensure that the Agency’s work remains aligned with community expectations, government policy and the real needs of clinicians and consumers.
Results, outcomes and impacts
Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to deliver broader impacts across the health system as tools mature and adoption increases. These expected outcomes include reduced administrative burden, faster access to relevant information, and more consistent application of policy and standards. The initiative aims to support safer and more connected care by ensuring people have access to clearer, more timely insights. Future evaluations are expected to include measurable improvements such as reductions in processing time, increased accuracy of information outputs, and broader uptake of AI supported services within partner organisations. These impacts will help guide where AI investments can deliver the greatest value across the national health
Challenges and lessons learned
From this work, several lessons have emerged. One is that early and ongoing engagement with clinicians, consumers and technical specialists helps build trust and leads to better solutions. Another is that high-quality data and clear policies are essential for safe AI use. A final lesson is that AI initiatives need clear problem definitions—tools work best when they are targeted at specific, well understood tasks rather than broad ambitions. Success in initiatives like this depends on a few conditions: strong governance, access to reliable data, skilled teams, clear communication, and a willingness to learn and adapt. Support from leadership and partners across the health system is also critical to ensure AI is used responsibly and delivers real benefits for clinicians and consumers.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: AI for Care – Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Healthcare in Ireland 2026–2030
body:
AI for Care is Ireland’s Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Healthcare for 2026–2030, developed by the Department of Health and the Health Service Executive. It aims to promote the safe, responsible use of AI across health and social care by improving patient care, efficiency, and research, implemented through a strategic roadmap, four pillars (clinical care, operations, research, public health), and an AI Implementation Framework.

The strategy is designed to respond to key pressures on Ireland’s health system, including rising demand, workforce constraints, and the need to improve efficiency and patient experience. It identifies artificial intelligence as a core enabler of healthcare transformation, capable of improving diagnostics, automating workflows, and supporting clinical decision-making, while also addressing administrative burdens and resource limitations.
Implementation is supported by a dedicated AI Implementation Framework, which provides guidance on how AI projects should be deployed across the health service. This framework includes processes for project design, validation, scaling, and continuous evaluation, ensuring that AI solutions are introduced in a controlled and structured manner. It also ensures alignment with regulatory requirements, including the EU AI Act, and promotes robust governance, safety, and ethical standards in all deployments.
The strategy is built on extensive stakeholder engagement, involving the Department of Health, the Health Service Executive, public bodies, clinicians, academic partners, regulators, and patient representatives. A working group with over 30 stakeholders was established to guide its development, and ongoing collaboration with patients and the public is identified as essential for implementation. This participatory approach reflects the emphasis on transparency, trust, and the inclusion of lived experience in decision-making.
A central element of the strategy is the development of enabling conditions for AI adoption, particularly digital and data infrastructure. The strategy highlights the importance of high-quality, secure, and interoperable data, supported by initiatives such as electronic health records, the National Shared Care Record, and the Health App. A complementary national data strategy is expected to ensure that AI systems are built on reliable data foundations and that data can be accessed, shared, and reused effectively.
The strategy also establishes mechanisms to ensure sustainability and measurable impact. AI initiatives will follow a phased approach, starting with proof-of-concept trials, followed by pilot projects and, where successful, national scaling. Progress will be monitored through defined success factors and evaluation processes, with continuous learning and adaptation built into the implementation model. This approach aims to ensure that AI deployment delivers tangible improvements in patient care, operational efficiency, and healthcare outcomes over time

org: Council for Science, Technology and Innovation (CSTI) / Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) / Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
title: 7th Basic Plan for the Promotion of Science and Technology
document_name: 第6期科学技術・イノベーション基本計画
body:
Japan's national strategic framework for science, technology and innovation, covering the period FY2026–FY2030, which succeeds the 6th Basic Plan. Where the 6th Plan emphasised Society 5.0 as a social vision, the 7th Plan introduces an "actionable science" philosophy and places greater weight on three axes: revitalisation of Japan's basic research capabilities, acceleration of innovation-driven economic growth and integration of science and technology policy with economic security objectives.

The 7th Basic Plan was developed through a consultative process launched by Cabinet Office referral to the Council for Science, Technology and Innovation (CSTI) in December 2024, with a dedicated Expert Committee leading drafting through 2025 and a Cabinet decision adopted in March 2026. The Plan is structured around three strategic pillars. First, reviving Japan's research power: recognising a decade of declining research competitiveness, the Plan prioritises reform of the research environment through increased KAKENHI grants, postdoctoral support and university management reform. Second, innovation and industrial competitiveness: AI, semiconductors, quantum technologies, fusion energy, robotics and biotechnology are identified as strategic technology areas requiring end-to-end support from basic research through to social implementation. AI for Science is a prominent cross-cutting theme, covering AI-enabled research data infrastructure, autonomous laboratory systems and AI integration into research methodology; both GENIAC and the Japan AI Safety Institute operate under the mandate the Plan sets. Third, economic security integration: breaking from previous plans, the 7th Plan explicitly aligns science and technology strategy with economic security objectives, identifying strategically sensitive technology domains, introducing research security and integrity requirements for universities, and adopting a selective rather than uniformly open approach to international collaboration. Attracting global talent and positioning Japan as an international innovation hub are also explicit goals.
