title: Responsible AI safety and education act
document_name: New York A6453 (RAISE Act)
body:
Amends the general business law to establish the Responsible AI Safety and Education Act (RAISE Act), compelling transparency, safety protocols, and mandatory disclosures for frontier AI models. Enables state enforcement through penalties, prohibiting deployments that pose critical harm risks. Applies to frontier models in New York.

Amends New York's general business law to introduce the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act, implementing transparency requirements for deploying AI frontier models.

Requires large AI developers to implement and retain a written safety and security protocol that must be published with redactions and submitted to the Attorney General and Homeland Security.

Stipulates annual reviews of the protocol to accommodate any advancements.

Requires prompt reporting of safety incidents to authorities within 72 hours.

Prohibits knowingly making false or misleading statements concerning AI documentation.

Empowers the Attorney General to bring civil actions for violations, with penalties up to $30 million for repeated offenses.

Confirms that the Act applies exclusively to frontier AI models developed or operating in New York State.

Clarifies that this Act doesn't establish a private right of action and is cumulative with other legal obligations.

body:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in national security transactions involving prohibited technologies like AI. Amends the Defense Production Act to authorize the Secretary of the Treasury to prohibit U.S. persons from investing in transactions involving prohibited technologies, specifically targeting AI systems and other high-tech areas.

document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 6602 ("Artificial intelligence development and usage by intelligence community")
body:
Amends the Intelligence Authorization Act to designate Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers. Requires the Chief Information Officer to identify reusable AI systems and promote sharing AI data and systems. Mandates performance tracking of AI systems.

Designates Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers for each intelligence community element to hold lead responsibility for AI governance.

Requires the Chief Information Officer of the Intelligence Community, in coordination with the Chief AI Officer, to identify AI systems commonly used and suitable for reuse by other intelligence elements within one year after the enactment of this Act.

Instructs that policies be adopted for sharing custom-developed AI codes and components, ensuring compatibility with the protection of intelligence sources and methods.

Directs the Chief Information Officer to provide model contract terms to address technical data rights, AI dataset requirements, and promote competition, emphasizing interoperable AI products and services.

Requires heads of intelligence community elements to track and evaluate AI performance based on efficacy, safety, fairness, transparency, accountability, appropriateness, lawfulness, and trustworthiness.

body:

Aim to cultivate a data and AI culture at diplomatic posts, promote data integration with the Department of State Headquarters, and enhance operational efficiencies.

Require the Secretary to submit an implementation plan within 180 days, outlining strategies for advancing program goals, hiring data and AI officers at diplomatic posts, and resource allocation.

Obligate the Secretary to provide annual reports to appropriate congressional committees on the implementation status for three years.

Define "appropriate congressional committees" as those related to Foreign Affairs and Appropriations in both the House and Senate.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 350 ("Pilot program for data-enabled ground vehicle maintenance")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 350 ("Pilot program for data-enabled ground vehicle maintenance")
body:
Establishes a pilot program for the Armed Forces to apply AI in ground vehicle maintenance. Requires assessment of AI feasibility, effectiveness, cost savings, and cybersecurity risks. Requires a report to Congress. Terminates authority by January 1, 2029.

Establishes a pilot program using commercially available AI technologies to improve ground vehicle maintenance in the Army, Navy, or Air Force.

Requires the Secretary concerned, in consultation with the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, to implement the program within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Directs the Secretary to assess the feasibility, effectiveness, and cost savings of AI-driven maintenance, and to identify cybersecurity and integration challenges.

Requires a report to Congress on the pilot program's activities within one year of enactment.

Terminates the pilot program on January 1, 2029.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 347 ("Integration of commercially available artificial intelligence capabilities into logistics operations")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 347 ("Integration of commercially available artificial intelligence capabilities into logistics operations")
body:
Facilitates integration of commercial AI for logistics into two Department of Defense exercises in 2026. Directs the Secretary of Defense to brief Congress on exercise specifics and AI integration impact on readiness and operations.

Facilitates the integration of commercially available AI capabilities into logistics operations of the Department of Defense (DoD) during fiscal year 2026 exercises.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to identify and choose AI products designed for logistics that comply with DoD data security protocols.

Ensures the selected AI products can adapt to software changes rapidly and prioritizes products from small or nontraditional firms.

Expedites approvals for secure data use and ensures compliance with DoD cybersecurity policies for these exercises.

Mandates an interim briefing by March 1, 2026, detailing the exercises, participating commanders, AI capabilities used, timelines, resource needs, and assessment metrics.

Requires a post-exercise briefing by the commander on the integration, effectiveness, and recommendations for further AI development in DoD operations.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 345 ("Technology enhancement for surface ship maintenance")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 345 ("Technology enhancement for surface ship maintenance")
body:
Requires the Secretary of the Navy to investigate and adopt advanced technologies, including AI-driven predictive maintenance, for surface ship maintenance; establishes a proposal and review process for such technologies; mandates third-party review of certain decisions; requires updates to policies and contracts upon adoption; and directs reporting to Congress on implementation timelines and justifications.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to investigate, approve, integrate, and adopt advanced technologies, including AI-enabled predictive maintenance algorithms, to enhance readiness, reduce costs, and improve efficiency in Navy surface ship maintenance.

Prioritizes specific technologies such as automated inspection systems, sensor-based monitoring, digital twins, autonomous inspection tools, and AI-driven failure prediction.

Establishes an open-qualification process allowing non-government entities to submit proposals for additional advanced technologies, directs evaluation of proposals within 90 days based on technical merit and Navy needs, and requires assessment of efficiency, safety, and cost-effectiveness.

Mandates independent third-party review of decisions not to qualify or adopt proposed technologies and requires the submission of findings and recommendations to Congress.

Allows prioritization of technology adoption based on operational needs and budget constraints, with justifications included in reports.

Requires updates to policies, specifications, guidance, and contracts to implement adopted technologies

Obligates the Secretary to report to Congress within 180 days detailing timelines for technology adoption, implementation plans and explanations for any non-pursuit.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 341 ("Maintenance inspection capabilities and requirements")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 341 ("Maintenance inspection capabilities and requirements")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to ensure maintenance of aviation safety items and parts includes technical data requirements or diagnostic tools, leveraging AI and machine learning for predictive maintenance when necessary.

Require the Secretary of Defense to ensure maintenance of aviation critical safety items and mission critical parts includes using technical data requirements or diagnostic tools when available.

Mandate that the acquisition of necessary technical data requirements and diagnostic tools is planned for system sustainment, including those leveraging AI and machine learning to enhance predictive maintenance capabilities.

Define a diagnostic tool as one capable of detecting issues like corrosion and damage and leveraging AI and machine learning for predictive maintenance databases.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 3117 ("Appropriate scoping of artificial intelligence research within the National Nuclear Security Administration")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 3117 ("Appropriate scoping of artificial intelligence research within the National Nuclear Security Administration")
body:
Restricts AI research and development funds within the National Nuclear Security Administration to supporting nuclear security missions. Allows AI R&D in other Department of Energy components or federal agencies, provided it doesn't interfere with nuclear security functions.

Limits the use of funds appropriated for artificial intelligence research and development within the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) to support only its nuclear security missions.

Allows for the establishment of national security AI research and development programs in other components of the Department of Energy or other federal agencies without restriction from this limitation.

Permits the NNSA to use its resources to support national security AI research and development programs outside of the Department of Energy, provided support is given on a full cost recovery basis and does not interfere with its nuclear security mission.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 3117 ("Appropriate scoping of artificial intelligence research within the National Nuclear Security Administration")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 3117 ("Appropriate scoping of artificial intelligence research within the National Nuclear Security Administration")
body:
Limits funding for AI research within the National Nuclear Security Administration to nuclear security missions. Allows AI research programs elsewhere within the Department of Energy or other Federal agencies, provided it doesn't interfere with nuclear security missions or facilities.

Amends the Atomic Energy Defense Act to specify that funds appropriated for AI research and development by the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) can only support the Administration's nuclear security missions.

States that this funding limitation does not prohibit the establishment of national security AI research programs within other areas of the Department of Energy or other federal agencies.

Allows the use of NNSA resources for an enduring national security AI program by external entities, provided support is given on a full cost recovery basis and does not interfere with the nuclear security missions of involved facilities.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 245 ("Biological data for artificial intelligence")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 245 ("Biological data for artificial intelligence")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop requirements ensuring DoD-funded biological data resources facilitate AI use. Defines "qualified biological data," includes metrics for data quality, cybersecurity safeguards, privacy protections, and allows national security exceptions. Requires the Secretary to consult relevant sectors about the feasibility of new requirements and review existing frameworks.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement requirements for storing biological data from Department of Defense-funded research to facilitate the use of such data for advanced computational methods, including AI, within one year of the act's enactment.

Defines "qualified biological data resource" using criteria such as data type, dataset size, federal funding amount, data sensitivity, and other factors deemed appropriate by the Secretary of Defense.

Imposes tiered cybersecurity safeguards and access controls for data storage.

Establishes exceptions for national security and requirements for individual privacy protection.

Consults with military and research officials, as well as private and academic stakeholders, to prevent overly burdensome requirements.

Incorporates existing federal frameworks and standards as appropriate.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 233 ("Limitation on use of funds for certain navy software")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 233 ("Limitation on use of funds for certain navy software")
body:
Prohibits expending funds on Navy's unmanned vessel software unless the Secretary of the Navy reports program schedules, cost estimates, performance assessments, and capability delivery assessments to congressional defense committees, and the Chief of Naval Operations validates operational user needs.

Prohibits the use of funds for the Navy's autonomy baseline manager or common control system for unmanned surface vessel programs unless specified conditions are met.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to submit to congressional defense committees the original and current schedule of key deliverables, cost estimates, test and experimentation reports, and a market assessment from the Defense Innovation Unit.

Requires an assessment that program capabilities meet or exceed industry standards.

Requires the Chief of Naval Operations to validate that the program meets the operational needs of the Navy to congressional defense committees.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 225 ("Advanced robotic automation for munitions manufacturing")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 225 ("Advanced robotic automation for munitions manufacturing")
body:
Requires the Secretary of the Army to support robotic automation in munitions manufacturing. Includes objectives like safe system design, increased production, cyber security, and workforce training. Coordinates with relevant departments and briefs Congress by March 1, 2026.

Require the Secretary of the Army to implement a program to enhance robotic automation in munitions manufacturing at government-owned, contractor-operated facilities.

Include objectives such as designing safe, scalable robotic systems for munitions production, increasing production capacity, developing secure cyber infrastructure for integrating factory operations, and supporting workforce training in robotics and advanced manufacturing.

Coordinate with the Joint Program Executive Office Armaments and Ammunition and other relevant Army components during program execution.

Require a briefing to congressional defense committees by March 1, 2026, detailing program progress, lessons learned, and recommendations for broader adoption of robotic automation technologies in the defense sector.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 224 ("National Security and Defense Artificial Intelligence Institute")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 224 ("National Security and Defense Artificial Intelligence Institute")
body:
Authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish AI Institutes focused on national security. Directs support for interdisciplinary AI research, partnership, innovation ecosystems, and workforce development.

Allows the Secretary of Defense to establish one or more artificial intelligence research institutes focused on national security and defense.

Requires each institute to address foundational or cross-cutting AI challenges relevant to defense and national security.

Directs institutes to form partnerships across federal agencies, academia, nonprofit research organizations, state and local governments, and industry.

Requires institutes to foster innovation ecosystems that translate research into applications and products that enhance national security and defense capabilities.

Requires support for research and development that spans multiple institutions of higher education and organizations.

Requires institutes to support interdisciplinary research and workforce development in AI and related disciplines within the United States.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1535 ("Artificial Intelligence Futures Steering Committee")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1535 ("Artificial Intelligence Futures Steering Committee")
body:
Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Futures Steering Committee by April 1, 2026, under the Secretary of Defense. Directs it to develop policies for AI adoption, assess AI trajectories, and analyze AI risks and adversary developments. Requires quarterly meetings and a report to U.S. Congress by January 31, 2027.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Futures Steering Committee by April 1, 2026, under the Secretary of Defense.

Comprises key defense leaders, such as the Deputy Secretary of Defense and the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

Holds responsibility for formulating policies for the governance, adoption, and risk mitigation of advanced AI systems, including those approaching artificial general intelligence.

Analyzes the trajectory of emerging AI technologies, such as neuromorphic computing and agentic algorithms.

Assesses adversaries' AI capabilities and potential operational effects of integrating AI into Department of Defense systems.

Develops strategies for ethical and technical AI integration, outlining resource requirements and goals.

Requires meetings at least quarterly.

Instructs the Deputy Secretary of Defense to report findings by January 31, 2027, and mandates public release of the unclassified portion.

Terminates the committee's responsibilities on December 31, 2027.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1534 ("Digital sandbox environments for artificial intelligence")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1534 ("Digital sandbox environments for artificial intelligence")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense, via the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, to establish an AI sandbox task force by April 2026 to facilitate AI experimentation and deployment. Identifies members and duties, with termination by January 2030.

Establishes a Task Force on artificial intelligence sandbox environments by April 1, 2026, under the Secretary of Defense through the Chief Digital and AI Officer.

Tasks the Task Force to develop and deploy AI sandbox environments for experimentation, training, and deployment across the Department of Defense.

Requires AI sandbox environments to be designed for use by personnel with varying technical proficiencies, facilitate familiarization with AI capabilities, and accelerate responsible AI adoption.

Chairs the Task Force with the Chief Digital and AI Officer and includes key officials from the Department of Defense, military departments, and combatant commands.

Requires the Task Force to standardize AI sandbox requirements across the Department of Defense, catalog and align existing solutions, improve efficiency and approvals, and provide clear guidance and resources to support users of all technical skill levels.

Requires a briefing to congressional defense committees by August 1, 2026.

Terminates the Task Force on January 1, 2030.

Defines key terms including "artificial intelligence" and "artificial intelligence sandbox environment."

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1533 ("Artificial intelligence model assessment and oversight")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1533 ("Artificial intelligence model assessment and oversight")
body:
Establishes a "Cross-Functional Team" led by the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer for artificial intelligence (AI) model assessment in the Department of Defense (DOD). Mandates designation of functional leads for AI applications in DOD. Requires assessment of major AI systems by 2028, followed by a congressional briefing and ends the team by 2030.

Directs Secretary of Defense to create a Cross-Functional Team within the Department of Defense to oversee AI model assessment and governance, headed by the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer.

Requires the Team to create a standardized assessment framework comprising performance standards, testing procedures etc, and governance structure for AI models used by the Department. Duties also include developing guidelines, assessment levels based on risk, and collaboration mechanisms for AI models.

Mandates inclusion of representatives from various defense branches and commands to ensure comprehensive oversight.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to designate functional leads for AI applications, taking into account expertise and capability to set standards.

Obligates the assessment of all major AI systems using this framework by specific deadlines.

Specifies the termination of the Cross-Functional Team by December 31, 2030, with a transition plan to a successor entity within the Department.

Requires periodic congressional briefings on progress and activities related to these initiatives, and reports by Secretary of Defense after the termination.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1532 ("Guidance and prohibition on use of certain artificial intelligence")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1532 ("Guidance and prohibition on use of certain artificial intelligence")
body:
Prohibits the Department of Defense and its contractors from using covered artificial intelligence (AI) developed covered AI companies within 30 days of enactment. Allows Secretary of Defense to issue waivers for research or national security purposes with necessary risk mitigation steps. Provides definitions of covered AI systems, companies, and nations.

Require the Secretary of Defense to exclude and remove covered artificial intelligence from Department of Defense (DOD) systems and devices within 30 days of the enactment of this Act by issuing a DOD-wide guidance.

Require contractors to refrain from using covered artificial intelligence in contracts with the Department of Defense, unless a waiver applies.

Allow the Secretary of Defense to issue waivers on a case-by-case basis for scientifically valid research, evaluations, national security testing, counterterrorism, and mission-critical functions, while also requiring risk mitigation steps.

Define "covered artificial intelligence" as AI developed by Chinese company DeepSeek or High Flyer and entities associated with High Flyer.

Classify entities on specific lists or subject to foreign influence as "covered artificial intelligence companies."

Specify the meaning of "artificial intelligence" by referencing existing federal definitions.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 152 ("Requirements for an intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance roadmap for the Air Force")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 152 ("Requirements for an intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance roadmap for the Air Force")
body:
Require the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a roadmap by October 1, 2026, detailing AI, machine learning, and other ISR technology investments.

Require the Secretary of the Air Force to submit a comprehensive roadmap for ISR capabilities by October 1, 2026.

Plan for modernizing or divesting legacy airborne ISR systems with specific justification for each.

Outline planned investments in emerging ISR technologies, highlighting artificial intelligence, machine learning, space-based ISR, and autonomous platforms.

Propose a timeline and milestones for roadmap implementation over the next ten fiscal years.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1515 ("Incorporation of artificial intelligence considerations into cybersecurity training")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1515 ("Incorporation of artificial intelligence considerations into cybersecurity training")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense, via the Chief Information Officer, to revise cybersecurity training for Armed Forces and civilian employees to include AI-related cybersecurity challenges within one year of the Act’s enactment.

Requires the Secretary of Defense, through the Department of Defense's Chief Information Officer, to revise mandatory cybersecurity training.

Includes content addressing unique cybersecurity challenges posed by artificial intelligence.

Sets a deadline of one year from the enactment date of this Act for these revisions to be implemented.

Applies to both members of the Armed Forces and civilian employees within the Department of Defense.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title:
National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1513 ("Physical and cybersecurity procurement requirements for artificial
intelligence systems")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1513 ("Physical and cybersecurity procurement requirements for artificial intelligence systems")
body:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a cybersecurity framework for Department of Defense AI and machine learning technologies. Requires tailoring of security requirements in consideration of costs versus benefits and encourages collaboration with private sector and academia.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a comprehensive framework for cybersecurity and physical security for AI and machine learning systems within the Department of Defense.

Requires this framework to address insider threats, supply chain risks, adversarial tampering, and unintended data exposure.

Specifies that the framework should integrate existing cybersecurity standards, like NIST, and prioritize systems of interest to cyber threat actors.

Instructs the amendment of the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to enforce these security practices on contractors.

Mandates cost-benefit analysis concerning security requirements, considering potential development delays against national security benefits.

Encourages collaboration with industry and academia in developing the framework.

Demands an implementation plan with clear timelines, resources, and metrics, and mandates submission of a status report to congressional defense committees within 180 days of the Act's enactment.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1512 ("Artificial intelligence and machine learning security in the Department of Defense")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1512 ("Artificial intelligence and machine learning security in the Department of Defense")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a cybersecurity policy for AI/ML systems no later than 180 days after the act is passed.  Develop a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of the AI/ML policies. Addresses potential security risks, implements methods to mitigate those risks, and establishes standard policy.  Requires a comprehensive report of the threats and cybersecurity measures by August 31, 2026.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a cybersecurity policy for AI/ML systems no later than 180 days after the act is passed.  

Addresses potential security risks specific to AI, such as model serialization attacks, model tampering, data leakage, adversarial prompt injection, model extraction, model jailbreaks, and supply chain attacks.

Implements methods to mitigate those risks using industry-recognized frameworks to ensure AI/ML systems are trustworthy.

Requires training for the workforce of the Department of Defense to ensure personnel are prepared to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities that are specific to AI/ML.

Establishes standard policy for governance, testing, and auditing of AI systems.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a comprehensive review and report of the effectiveness of the AI/ML cybersecurity practices, including an identification of gaps in the existing security measures, by August 31, 2026.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1234 ("Research, development, test, and evaluation of emerging technologies to further the warfighting capabilities of the United States and certain partner countries")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1234 ("Research, development, test, and evaluation of emerging technologies to further the warfighting capabilities of the United States and certain partner countries")
body:
Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to jointly research emerging technologies, including AI, with partner countries. Requires robust protection of sensitive information and adherence to export controls. Designates the Irregular Warfare Technology Support Directorate as the lead agency.

Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to collaborate with partner countries on research and development of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to enhance defense capabilities.

Requires consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Director of National Intelligence in these efforts.

Demands protection of sensitive information and compliance with export control laws for any activities involving AI and other technologies.

Prohibits initiating activities with a partner country until a detailed report is submitted to congressional committees, outlining cost-sharing and security measures.

Mandates semiannual reporting to Congress and designates the Irregular Warfare Technology Support Directorate as the lead agency.

Prioritizes safeguarding technologies from access by foreign adversaries, like China, as part of bilateral agreements with partner nations.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1086 ("Framework for reforming technology transfer and foreign disclosure policies")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1086 ("Framework for reforming technology transfer and foreign disclosure policies")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to create a framework for revising technology transfer and foreign disclosure policies, accommodating advanced technologies like artificial intelligence. Instructs updates to the National Disclosure Policy and mandates annual audits of license denials.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to produce a framework to revise technology transfer and foreign disclosure policies, emphasizing emerging and advanced technologies like AI.

Requires guidelines to balance technology protection with information sharing.

Includes recommendations for updating the National Disclosure Policy to incorporate AI and other advanced technologies.

Requires mechanisms to streamline approval processes and enhance transparency.

Mandates the consolidation of technology security and foreign disclosure approvals.

Requires updated directives detailing responsibilities in technology transfer.

Establishes metrics for evaluating policy effectiveness and mandates annual audits of denied license applications.

Instructs regular engagement with defense industry stakeholders, including nontraditional contractors.

Requires submission of the framework and annual reports to congressional defense committees, detailing improvements and industry feedback incorporation.

Allows reports to be unclassified but may include a classified annex.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1061 ("Notification of waivers under Department of Defense Directive 3000.09")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1061 ("Notification of waivers under Department of Defense Directive 3000.09")
body:
Amends Chapter 3 of title 10, United States Code, to require the Secretary of Defense to notify congressional defense committees of waivers related to autonomy in weapon systems, including rationale, description, and duration, within 30 days. Allows a classified annex.

Amends Chapter 3 of title 10, United States Code, to require the Secretary of Defense to notify congressional defense committees of any waivers issued under Department of Defense Directive 3000.09, which pertains to autonomy in weapon systems.

Requires this notification within 30 days of issuing any such waiver.

Specifies that each notification must include the rationale for the waiver, a description of the autonomous weapon system or technology involved, and the waiver's anticipated duration.

Amends Section 1066(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025 to include provisions for legal reviews in the context of approving and deploying lethal autonomous weapon systems.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1048 ("Authorization of Eastern Regional Range Complex for multi-domain operations and robotic autonomous systems training, testing, and experimentation")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1048 ("Authorization of Eastern Regional Range Complex for multi-domain operations and robotic autonomous systems training, testing, and experimentation")
body:
Authorize the Secretary of Defense to develop the Eastern Regional Range Complex for multi-domain operations, robotic autonomous systems training, and testing, including AI-related unmanned aircraft systems.

Authorize the Secretary of Defense, through military department Secretaries, to establish an Eastern Regional Range Complex as a hub for multi-domain operations and robotic autonomous systems, including unmanned aircraft systems.

Conduct training, experimentation, and testing of robotic autonomous systems, and develop tactics and procedures for unmanned systems.

Evaluate emerging technologies and systems in contested cyber and electromagnetic environments.

Coordinate activities with the Joint Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Office, Joint Staff, and Defense Research Offices, among others.

Authorize consultation with the FCC and NTIA for spectrum access to support operations.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1019 ("Strategy for navy investment in and support for the maritime industrial base")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1019 ("Strategy for navy investment in and support for the maritime industrial base")
body:
Requires the Secretary of the Navy to develop a strategy using artificial intelligence to monitor and predict supply chain challenges in shipbuilding. Instructs AI application for disruptions, shortages, and delays. Demands a report on the strategy to Congress.

Require the Secretary of the Navy to develop and implement a strategy for investing in and supporting the maritime industrial base to address shipbuilding challenges.

Instruct the strategy to apply artificial intelligence to monitor and predict potential supply chain challenges, including disruptions, shortages, and delays.

Focus the strategy on ensuring reliable supplies of critical components for submarine and surface shipbuilding programs.

Include in the strategy measures to identify key performance indicators and centralize data collection for performance analysis.

Demand submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 210 days, summarizing the strategy, implementation timelines, and expected outcomes for addressing cost and schedule challenges.

category: NDAA provisions;U.S. federal laws;FY2026 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Section 1007 ("Use of technology using artificial intelligence to facilitate audit of the financial statements of the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2026")
document_name: FY2026 NDAA, Section 1007 ("Use of technology using artificial intelligence to facilitate audit of the financial statements of the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2026")
body:
Encourages the Secretaries of Defense, Army, Navy, and Air Force to use AI for auditing financial statements. Requires the Director of the Chief Digital and AI Office to oversee AI adoption for financial management, coordinating with relevant defense officials.

Encourages the Secretaries of Defense, Army, Navy, and Air Force to use AI and machine learning technologies to facilitate audits of the Department of Defense's financial statements for fiscal year 2026.

Oversees the Director of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering and the Inspector General, in adopting AI and machine learning technologies to support financial management and enterprise business operations.

title: Executive Order on Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
document_name: Executive Order on Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
body:
Establishes an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state regulations hindering United States Artificial Intelligence (AI) dominance. Directs an evaluation to identify state laws that mandate ideological bias or alter truthful model outputs. Restricts state access to federal funding, such as the Broadband Equity Access and Deployment program, unless states comply with a proposed national policy framework designed to preempt conflicting state-level AI mandates.

Establishes a national policy to sustain United States leadership and global dominance in Artificial Intelligence (AI) by creating a "minimally burdensome" federal framework intended to replace a "patchwork" of conflicting state regulations

Directs the Attorney General to form an AI Litigation Task Force within 30 days to challenge state laws that unconstitutionally regulate interstate commerce or conflict with the national objective of AI supremacy,.

Mandates the Secretary of Commerce to conduct an evaluation of existing state AI laws within 90 days to identify "onerous" mandates that conflict with federal policy, specifically targeting those that require models to alter their truthful outputs or compel disclosures that violate the First Amendment.

Restricts state eligibility for remaining Broadband Equity Access and Deployment (BEAD) program funding, specifically making states with "onerous" AI laws ineligible for non-deployment funds. 

Instructs executive agencies to assess discretionary grant program to determine if they can condition funding on states either not enacting conflicting AI laws or entering into binding agreements to not enforce existing ones during the performance period.

Requires the Federal Communications Commission to consider a Federal AI reporting and disclosure standard to preempt conflicting State laws.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission to issue a policy statement on preempting State laws that require deceptive modifications to AI outputs.

Mandates preparation of a legislative recommendation for a Federal AI policy framework, allowing certain State AI laws on topics like child safety to remain.

body:
●기관: G7 산업·디지털·기술 장관회의 / 캐나다 혁신과학경제개발부(ISED)

●발표시점: 2025년 12월 9일
●핵심내용:G7 산업·디지털·기술 장관들이 캐나다 몬트리올에서 중소기업의 안전하고 책임 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI 활용을 촉진하기 위한 실천방안을 제시한 장관성명임. 동 성명은 2025년 6월 G7 정상성명의 AI 번영 관련 약속에 대한 후속 조치로, 중소기업이 AI에 접근·도입·활용할 수 있도록 인프라, 데이터, 인재, 금융, 거버넌스 지원을 강화해야 한다고 강조함.
① 중소기업의 AI 도입이 대기업보다 느리고 여건별 격차가 큰 만큼, 데이터·AI 모델 접근성을 포함한 맞춤형 지원이 필요하다고 제시함
② 기업 차원에서는 경영진 이해와 AI·데이터 문해력, 사업전략 연계, 직무별 교육·재교육 등을 통한 역량강화가 중요하다고 강조함
③ 공공·민간 금융지원, 혁신허브·공유서비스, 실무 가이드·표준과 국경 간 거버넌스 정합성을 통해 비용·규제 등을 완화할 필요가 있다고 제안함

title: HR 6461 Resources for Evaluating and Documenting AI Models 2025
document_name: HR 6461 READ AI Models Act 2025
body:
Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to establish a pilot program for creating best practices and technical guidance on AI model documentation. Involves stakeholders, publishes drafts for public comment, and evaluates effectiveness within 12 months.

Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop best practices and technical guidance for documenting artificial intelligence models.

Requires NIST to initiate a pilot program to establish a structured documentation template for AI models and associated data, in consultation with relevant federal agencies.

Instructs NIST to ensure the template is modular and flexible to cater to sector-specific needs and to provide accompanying technical guidelines with relevant metrics and industry standards.

Mandates collaboration with private entities, educational institutions, nonprofits, international standards organizations, and federal agencies for stakeholder input.

Requires publication of a draft template in the Federal Register for public comments.

Obligates NIST to report on the pilot program's effectiveness and, if effective, plan for its permanent implementation and make documentation available on its website.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S3339 AI Workforce Projections, Research, and Evaluations to Promote AI Readiness and Employment Act 2025
document_name: S3339 AI Workforce PREPARE Act 2025
body:
Establishes the AI Workforce PREPARE Act to improve forecasts of AI's impact on the U.S. workforce. Requires collecting AI adoption data, predicting employment shifts, and incentivizing expert recruitment for AI analysis. Enhances labor market data access and mandates AI-related layoff disclosures.

Enacts the AI Workforce PREPARE Act to assess and prepare for AI's impact on the U.S. workforce.

Instructs the Department of Labor, through the Secretary, to collect AI-related data on employment and make forecasts about job impacts using federal surveys, industry reports, and job transition data.

Establishes an AI Workforce Research Hub to research AI's workforce impact and develop actionable insights for policy.

Allows temporary hiring of AI experts to build the federal technical capacity to tackle AI-related workforce issues.

Requires revisions to federal surveys for better data on AI adoption and effects on tasks and skills.

Amends the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act to require employers to disclose AI's role in mass layoffs.

Sets up prize competitions to incentivize AI impact forecasting and benchmark development.

Authorizes appropriations for various initiatives related to AI's workforce impacts, including state-level updates and rapid adjustments for affected workers.

body:
●기관: 유엔개발계획(UNDP) 아시아·태평양 지역사무소
●문서종류: 보고서 / AI와 인간개발 정책보고서
●문서명: The Next Great Divergence: Why AI may widen inequality between countries / 「다음 대분기: AI는 왜 국가 간 불평등을 확대할 수 있는가」
●발표시점: 2025년 12월
●핵심내용:UNDP는 AI가 성장, 공공서비스, 회복력 강화에 기여할 수 있지만, 국가별 준비도와 도입역량의 차이로 인해 국가 간 불평등을 심화시킬 수 있다고 경고함. 특히 연결성, 기술역량, 컴퓨팅, 규제역량이 부족한 국가는 AI 혜택을 충분히 흡수하지 못하고, 일자리 충격, 데이터 배제, 허위정보, 에너지·물 수요 증가의 간접효과에 더 취약해질 수 있다고 분석함.
① 보고서는 AI 이용이 빠르게 확산되고 있으나 고소득국과 저소득국 간 이용률 격차가 크고, 디지털 접근성·스마트폰·데이터 대표성 차이가 AI 혜택의 불균등을 초래할 수 있다고 지적함
② AI는 보건·교육·금융·재난대응과 생산성 향상에 기여할 수 있지만, 일자리 대체·개인정보 침해·불투명한 의사결정·데이터 유출 등 노동시장과 공공부문의 위험도 수반한다고 분석함
③ AI 격차 완화를 위해 인적 역량, 책임 있는 거버넌스, 포용적 디지털 인프라, 지속가능한 컴퓨팅과 국제표준·안전·오픈모델 협력을 강화해야 한다고 강조함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HR 6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
document_name: HR 6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
body:
Regulates developers and deployers of AI algorithms to prevent discrimination and disparate impacts, requiring pre-deployment evaluations and annual assessments. Authorizes the FTC and states to enforce compliance, and creates a private right of action. Establishes transparency and consumer rights.

Establishes the "Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025" to protect individual rights concerning computational algorithms.

Prohibits developers and deployers from using covered algorithms that cause discrimination or disparate impacts based on protected characteristics in consequential actions such as employment, credit, and housing.

Requires developers and deployers to conduct pre-deployment evaluations and annual impact assessments with independent audits to identify potential harms or biases from AI systems.

Mandates transparent disclosures, including audits and impact assessments, by developers and deployers, and requires mechanisms for individuals to report violations and seek redress.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and states to enforce the Act, providing penalties and permitting civil actions by affected individuals.

Directs the FTC to study and implement regulations on providing explanations for algorithmic decisions and options for human alternatives.

Allocates resources, including new personnel and funding, for federal implementation and oversight.

●발표시점: 2025년 12월
●핵심내용:동 문서는 대테러 분야에서 AI가 정보수집·분석, 위협탐지, 생체인식, 얼굴인식, 예측치안, 온라인 콘텐츠 조정, 국경관리, 사법절차, 구금, 군사작전 등 다양한 영역에 활용될 수 있음을 분석하면서, AI 활용은 반드시 명확한 법적 근거, 필요성·비례성, 인간의 의미 있는 통제, 인권 실사, 독립적 감독과 구제절차에 기반해야 한다고 언급

① AI 성과평가를 TCO·ROI·SDG 영향의 3단계로 구성하고, 재무·에너지 비용부터 사회적 영향까지 함께 평가하는 프레임워크를 제시함

body:
●기관: UNICEF Innocenti – Global Office of Research and Foresight

●문서명: Protecting Children from Biological Weapons in Armed Conflict / 「무력분쟁 중 생물무기로부터 아동 보호」
●발표시점: 2025년 12월
●핵심내용:동 문서는 AI, 자동화, 합성생물학의 융합이 생물무기 개발·생산·배치 장벽을 낮추면서 무력분쟁 상황의 아동에게 새로운 위험을 초래할 수 있다고 분석한 UNICEF Innocenti 작업문서임. 보고서는 합성생물학이 백신, 치료제, 진단, 식량·수자원 안보에 기여할 수 있는 잠재력을 인정하면서도, 동일한 기술이 병원체 설계, 실험 자동화, 전달체계 최적화에 악용될 경우 아동이 생리적·심리사회적 취약성 때문에 불균형적으로 피해를 입을 수 있다고 지적함.
① 보고서는 AI와 합성생물학의 결합이 병원체 설계·실험 자동화·전달체계 최적화를 가속하고, 비국가 행위자까지 생물위협 활용 가능성을 확대할 수 있다고 지적함
② 아동은 생물학적 공격과 허위정보 등에 특히 취약하며, 분쟁지역에서는 보건·영양체계 붕괴와 결합돼 피해가 더욱 커질 수 있다고 분석함
③ 아동을 생물안보 의제의 중심에 두고, 아동보호·공중보건·긴급대응 협력과 BWC의 이행·검증·책임성 메커니즘을 강화해야 한다고 제안함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S3202 Advanced Artificial Intelligence Security Readiness Act of 2025
document_name: S3202 Advanced Artificial Intelligence Security Readiness Act of 2025
body:
Directs the NSA Director to develop and disseminate AI security guidance identifying vulnerabilities and cybersecurity risks in AI systems and supply chains, informed by collaboration with AI experts and other departments. Mandates initial and final progress reports to congressional committees.

Directs the Director of the National Security Agency, through the Artificial Intelligence Security Center, to develop and disseminate guidance on securing artificial intelligence technologies.

Requires identification of vulnerabilities specific to AI systems and their supply chains, focusing on cybersecurity risks and foreign threat actors.

Requires consultation with AI developers, researchers, and relevant federal bodies to assess AI systems' capabilities relevant to national security and inform guidance.

Mandates submission of an initial report within 180 days and a final report within 365 days to congressional intelligence committees, detailing guidance development progress and insights on AI security.

Specifies that guidance should include detailed best practices in unclassified form, with the option for classified annexes and materials for secure briefings.

Requires the Commission to improve AI literacy, develop materials, and create a national AI literacy strategy. Instructs submission and updating of the strategy to Congress.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Education Commission within the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

Tasks the Commission with streamlining and enhancing AI literacy and education across the United States.

Requires the development of multilingual resources promoting AI literacy.

Directs the dissemination of these materials, possibly through a public website and multimedia campaigns.

Requires the Commission to develop a national strategy to address opportunities and challenges in AI literacy, ensuring continued U.S. global AI leadership.

Instructs the submission of this strategy to Congress and mandates periodic reviews and updates.

Ensures coordination of Federal Government efforts for strategy implementation.

Defines the composition of the Commission, chaired by the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, including representatives with AI expertise from multiple government departments and sectors.

Mandates regular Commission meetings, beginning within 60 days of enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S3193 Algorithm Accountability Act 2025
document_name: S3193 Algorithm Accountability Act 2025
body:
Amends Section 230 to impose a duty of care on social media platforms in the design and operation of recommendation algorithms, holding them liable for foreseeable bodily harm and removing liability protections for violations. Allows affected individuals to sue for damages while excluding smaller platforms and certain types of services.

Amends Section 230 of the Communications Act to introduce a duty of care for social media platforms using recommendation-based algorithms.

Requires these platforms to exercise reasonable care in the design and operation of algorithms to prevent foreseeable bodily injury or death.

Removes liability protection under Section 230 for platforms that violate this duty of care.

Exempts certain actions from this requirement, such as chronological sorting and user-initiated searches.

Allows civil actions against platforms if injuries arise due to non-compliance, voiding predispute arbitration agreements.

category: UN
title: [UN Women] AI가 기술매개 여성·여아 대상 폭력을 어떻게 악화시키는가
document_name: How AI is Exacerbating Technology-Facilitated Violence against Women and Girls / 「AI가 기술매개 여성·여아 대상 폭력을 어떻게 악화시키는가」
body:
●기관: UN Women / Everyday Sexism Project
●문서종류: 보고서 / 기술매개 여성·여아 대상 폭력 대응 정책보고서
●문서명: How AI is Exacerbating Technology-Facilitated Violence against Women and Girls / 「AI가 기술매개 여성·여아 대상 폭력을 어떻게 악화시키는가」
●발표시점: 2025년 11월
●핵심내용:동 문서는 AI, 특히 생성형 AI가 기술매개 여성·여아 대상 폭력(TF VAWG)을 어떻게 확대·정교화·자동화하고 있는지 분석한 UN Women 보고서임. 보고서는 온라인 폭력이 여성과 여아에게 심리적·사회적·정치적·경제적 피해를 초래하며, AI가 딥페이크, 사칭, 사이버괴롭힘, 혐오표현, 성착취, 신상공개, 협박 등을 대규모로 가능하게 하고 있다고 지적함.
① 보고서는 AI가 허위정보·사이버괴롭힘·사칭·스토킹 등을 자동화·확장하고, 성별 편향과 고정관념을 재생산해 여성·여아 대상 디지털 폭력을 심화시킬 수 있다고 지적함
② 특히 딥페이크 성폭력과 비동의 성적 이미지가 핵심 위험으로 제시되며, 여성 정치인·언론인·인권옹호자 등을 대상으로 한 공격은 공적·정치적 참여와 민주적 담론까지 위축시킬 수 있다고 평가함
③ 대응을 위해 AI 안전설계·편향 점검·정기 감사·데이터 투명성·신고·삭제·피해자 구제와 디지털 중개자 책임을 강화하고, 젠더 관점과 피해자 중심 접근을 AI 거버넌스에 반영해야 한다고 강조함

title: [UNICEF 등] AI와 아동 권리에 관한 공동성명
document_name: Joint Statement on Artificial Intelligence and the Rights of the Child / 「인공지능과 아동권리에 관한 공동성명」
body:
●기관: 국제전기통신연합(ITU) / 유엔아동권리위원회(CRC) / UNICEF 등
●문서종류: 공동성명 / 아동권리·AI 거버넌스 원칙
●문서명: Joint Statement on Artificial Intelligence and the Rights of the Child / 「인공지능과 아동권리에 관한 공동성명」
●발표시점: 2025년 11월
●핵심내용:ITU, 유엔아동권리위원회, UNICEF 등 주요 국제기구와 아동권리 관련 기관들이 AI에 대한 아동권리 기반 접근을 촉구한 공동성명임. 동 성명은 AI가 아동의 권리를 존중·보호·실현하는 방식으로 설계, 개발, 거버넌스되어야 하며, 이를 위해 정부·기업·국제기구·시민사회 간 조율된 행동이 필요하다고 강조함.
① 문서는 AI 정책과 시스템 설계에 아동의 최선의 이익·생존과 발달·비차별·참여권 등 아동권리 원칙을 반영해야 한다고 제시함
② AI는 교육·보건·복지 등에서 아동의 기회를 확대할 수 있지만, 차별·개인정보 침해·조작·착취·온라인 안전 위험도 증폭시킬 수 있다고 지적함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S3062 Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue Act of 2025
document_name: S3062 GUARD Act 2025
body:
Requires AI chatbots to implement age verification, prohibiting minors from using AI companions. Mandates disclosure of non-human status to users and prohibits claiming professional status. Instructs the Attorney General to enforce compliance and issue penalties for violations.

Requires AI chatbots to implement reasonable age verification measures to prevent minors from accessing AI companions.

Prohibits AI chatbots from soliciting or inducing minors into sexually explicit behavior or promoting physical violence, with fines up to $100,000 per offense.

Obligates covered entities to create user accounts for access to AI chatbots and perform age verification at account creation, periodically, and in cases of existing accounts on the Act's effective date.

Mandates AI chatbots to disclose their non-human and non-professional status clearly and regularly to users.

Empowers the Attorney General to enforce compliance through civil actions and penalties, with a maximum fine of $100,000 per violation, and allows state enforcement actions under certain conditions.

Protects state laws if they offer at least equivalent protection as the Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HR5764 AI for Main Street Act 2025
document_name: HR5764 AI for Main Street Act 2025
body:
Amends the Small Business Act to require guidance, training, and outreach for small businesses on artificial intelligence, covering best practices, data protection, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and business operations integration. Defines AI per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Amends the Small Business Act to include guidance on the use of artificial intelligence for small business concerns.

Instructs the appropriate entities to assist small businesses in evaluating AI in their operations.

Provides information, guidance, and training on using AI, including best practices and applications for data protection, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and improving customer trust.

Requires outreach to small businesses to promote the use of AI.

Defines 'artificial intelligence' according to the meaning in the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: SB-243 Companion chatbots
document_name: California SB-243 (Companion chatbots)
body:
Defines "companion chatbot" and requires operators to notify users when interacting with AI, maintain protocols to prevent suicidal ideation and self-harm content, annually report to the Office of Suicide Prevention on crisis notifications, and establish additional protections for minors. Provides civil remedies for violations.

Defines key terms including companion chatbot, companion chatbot platform, and operator for purposes of Chapter 22.6.

Requires operators to issue a clear and conspicuous notification when a reasonable person would be misled into believing they are interacting with a human.

Requires operators to maintain a protocol to prevent companion chatbots from producing suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm content, and to refer users to crisis service providers including suicide hotlines or crisis text lines, and to publish the protocol on their website.

Requires operators to, for users known to be minors, disclose AI nature, provide break reminders every three hours, and institute measures to prevent sexually explicit content.

Requires operators to annually report to the Office of Suicide Prevention on crisis referrals, suicidal ideation detection and response protocols, and evidence-based measurement methods, with reports posted publicly.

Requires operators to disclose that companion chatbots may not be suitable for some minors on all platforms through which users access the chatbot.

Establishes that a person who suffers injury as a result of a violation of this chapter may bring a civil action to recover damages of $1,000 per violation or actual damages, injunctive relief, and attorney's fees.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 243 (Companion Chatbots 2025)
document_name: California SB 243 (Companion Chatbots 2025)
body:
Regulates companion chatbots by requiring operators to disclose their artificial nature, implement protocols against suicide-related content, and apply heightened protections for minors. Mandates annual reporting to the Office of Suicide Prevention and subjects violators to civil liability.

Defines "companion chatbot" as an AI system with a natural language interface capable of sustaining relationships across multiple interactions, excluding customer service bots, video game bots limited to game-related topics, and stand-alone voice assistant devices.

Requires operators to issue clear disclosures when a reasonable person could mistake the companion chatbot for a human.

Mandates operators maintain and publicly post protocols to prevent suicide-related content by issuing crisis service notifications.

Obligates operators to disclose to minors that interactions are with AI, send break reminder notifications at least every three hours during ongoing interactions, and prohibit chatbots from generating sexually explicit content.

Requires annual reporting of crisis notifications and protocols to the Office of Suicide Prevention, effective July 1, 2027.

Permits individuals injured by violations to seek injunctive relief, damages, and attorneys' fees.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 853 (California AI Transparency Act)
document_name: California AB 853 (California AI Transparency Act)
body:
Amends California's Business and Professions Code to require large online platforms to detect and disclose provenance data of AI-generated content, prohibit GenAI hosting platforms from distributing non-compliant systems, and require capture device manufacturers to embed latent disclosures by default, with civil penalties of $5,000 per violation.

Amends the Business and Professions Code to define key terms related to artificial intelligence, such as "artificial intelligence," "generative artificial intelligence system," and "large online platform", "provenance data", and "covered provider" for purposes of this chapter.

Requires large online platforms, beginning January 1, 2027, to detect standards-compliant provenance data embedded in distributed content and provide a user interface disclosing content authenticity, origin, modification history, and the name of the GenAI system or capture device that created it.

Requires large online platforms to allow users to inspect system provenance data through the platform interface, by downloading content, or via a third-party link, and prohibits platforms from knowingly stripping provenance data or digital signatures from content.

Prohibits GenAI hosting platforms from knowingly making available GenAI systems that do not place required disclosures, effective January 1, 2027.

Requires capture device manufacturers, beginning January 1, 2028, to provide users the option to include and by default embed latent disclosures, including manufacturer name, device name/version, and content creation time/date, in captured content.

Establishes civil penalties of $5,000 per violation, with each day constituting a discrete violation, enforceable by the Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel, with attorney's fees awarded to prevailing plaintiffs, effective August 2, 2026.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 316 (Artificial intelligence: Defenses 2025)
document_name: California AB 316 (AI: Defenses 2025)
body:
Defines "artificial intelligence" as a system influencing environments. Prohibits defendants from claiming AI autonomously caused harm in legal actions. Allows defendants to present other defenses, evidence of causation, foreseeability, and comparative fault of other parties.

Add Section 1714.46 to the Civil Code to define "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system with autonomy varying capabilities that can generate outputs influencing environments.

Prohibit defendants in AI-related harm actions from asserting that the AI autonomously caused harm as a defense.

Allow defendants to present any other affirmative defenses, including evidence relevant to causation or foreseeability.

Permit defendants to introduce evidence concerning the comparative fault of other persons or entities.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 489 (Health Care Professions: Deceptive Terms or Letters: Artificial Intelligence 2025)
document_name: California AB 489 (Health Care Professions: Deceptive Terms or Letters: Artificial Intelligence 2025)
body:
Regulates AI health advice by prohibiting unlicensed use of terms implying licensed health professionals' roles. Requires health care boards to enforce compliance. Prohibits implying licensed care through AI advertising or functionality. Penalizes each misuse of terms as separate violations.

Defines "Artificial intelligence" and "Generative artificial intelligence" in alignment with the Government Code.

Subjects violations related to AI in healthcare to the jurisdiction of appropriate licensing boards or enforcement agencies.

Authorizes these boards to pursue injunctions or restraining orders to enforce provisions.

Enforces against entities using specific professional terms in AI systems if such usage implies an unauthorized license.

Prohibits use of terms suggesting licensed care in AI or GenAI advertising unless a licensed professional provides the service.

Specifies each improper use of a term as a separate violation.

Clarifies that no reimbursement is required due to the act creating or altering a crime or infraction.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 524 (Law enforcement agencies: artificial intelligence.)
document_name: California SB 524 (AI Use by Law Enforcement)
body:
Requires law enforcement agencies to disclose AI usage in reports and retain drafts generated by AI. Obligates agencies to maintain AI usage audit trails. Prohibits vendors from misusing data, except for specified purposes. Defines "artificial intelligence" and related terms.

Requires each law enforcement agency to maintain a policy ensuring that AI-generated official reports include identification of AI programs used and a statement indicating AI involvement.

Mandates these reports contain an officer's signature verifying the report's accuracy.

Necessitates retention of the first AI-created draft for the same duration as the official report, and states it doesn’t constitute an officer's statement.

Commands agencies to maintain an audit trail identifying users of AI and any associated footage used.

Prohibits contracted vendors from sharing or using AI-processed data beyond agency purposes or court orders, with allowances for system refinement.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and related terms in the context of police report generation, explicitly including generative AI used with camera and audio inputs.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 723 (Real Estate: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure 2025)
document_name: California AB 723 (Real Estate: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure 2025)
body:
Require real estate brokers or salespersons using AI-altered images in advertisements to disclose alterations and provide access to original images. Define "digitally altered image" as modified through AI or software, excluding minor edits like lighting and color adjustments.

Add Section 10140.8 to the California Business and Professions Code to require real estate brokers or salespersons to disclose when images in advertisements are digitally altered.

Define "digitally altered image" as one altered through photo editing software or AI, affecting elements like fixtures, furniture, or views.

Exclude from this definition alterations that use common photo editing adjustments such as lighting or cropping that do not alter property representations.

Require advertisements with digitally altered images to include a statement and link to access unaltered images.

Oblige brokers or salespersons to provide access to original images if they control the website on which the advertisement is posted.

State that no reimbursement is required under this act, as it pertains to creating or changing the definition or penalty of a crime.

title: California AB 979 (California Cybersecurity Integration Center: artificial intelligence)
document_name: California AB 979 (California Cybersecurity Integration Center: AI)
body:
Establishes the California AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook by January 1, 2027, to enhance cybersecurity through information sharing on AI threats. Requires state protection of sensitive information, with mandatory and voluntary participation mechanisms, while safeguarding individual privacy and business confidentiality.

Instructs the California Office of Emergency Services to develop a California AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook by January 1, 2027, to enhance information sharing and bolster defenses against AI-related cyber threats.

Requires review of federal standards and best practices, including the Joint Cyber Defense Collaborative AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook, to inform California's playbook.

Mandates that the playbook include mechanisms for mandatory information sharing on AI threats and vulnerabilities by state contractors, and allows voluntary sharing by other entities.

Prohibits public disclosure of sensitive information related to cyber threats or AI vulnerabilities, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with security requirements.

Defines the California Cybersecurity Integration Center as the central hub for state cybersecurity activities, coordinating with various governmental and private entities to reduce cyber incident impacts.

Asserts strong state interest in protecting IT systems due to their critical role and need for confidentiality to prevent system attacks.

title: California Senate Bill 53
document_name: California SB 53 September 2025 (Artificial intelligence models: large developers)
body:
Requires large frontier developers to implement and publish frontier AI frameworks, assess catastrophic risks, and publish transparency reports; requires the Office of Emergency Services to establish reporting mechanisms for critical safety incidents and catastrophic risk assessments; establishes a consortium to develop a framework for the creation of CalCompute; creates civil penalties for violations of this chapter.

Defines terms for the purposes of this chapter, including catastrophic risk and critical safety incident.

Requires large frontier developers to implement and publish frontier AI frameworks, publish transparency reports, and disclose assessments of catastrophic risks to the Office of Emergency Services.

Instructs the Office of Emergency Services to establish a critical safety incident reporting mechanism and a mechanism for frontier developers to submit summaries of catastrophic risk assessments; mandates the disclosure of critical safety incidents that pose an imminent risk of death or serious injury within 24 hours. 

Tasks the Office of Emergency Services, beginning in 2027, to annually produce and submit a report with anonymized and aggregated information regarding critical safety incidents to the Legislature and Governor.

Creates a civil penalty of up to $1,000,000 for violations of this chapter, specifically the failure of a frontier developer to report a safety incident or comply with their own frontier AI framework.

Creates a 14-member consortium to develop a framework for the creation of CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster that will advance the development and deployment of safe and equitable AI. 

Prohibits frontier developers from preventing, or retaliating against, covered employees who disclose information about catastrophic risks or violations of the Business and Professions Code.

Provides remedies for violations of this section, and explains how courts should handle cases regarding disclosures made by covered employees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
body:
Requires the Secretary of Energy to establish the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program within 90 days. The program is required to offer standardized and classified testing of AI systems for likelihood of incidents.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to establish the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program to evaluate advanced AI systems using standardized testing protocols. Requires the implementation of testing protocols that match or exceed real-world AI Jailbreaking techniques. 

Mandates that each artificial intelligence system developer shall participate in the program and provide to the Secretary any relevant materials and informations to carry out the program. 

The above materials may include the underlying code of the advanced artificial intelligence system, data used to train the system, model weights or other parameters, the interface engine, or any kind of detailed information regarding the training. Any penalties for the obligation to participate will be fined no less than $1,000,00 per day.

Instructs the program to offer standardized testing and evaluation of advanced AI systems. Implements testing including adversarial testing by red teams with expertise to malicious actors. 

Obligates the Secretary to submit to Congress a detailed report of the recommendation, drawing directly from empirical data, insights, and lessons learned from the program..

Sets a program termination date 7 years post-enactment unless Congress renews it.

title: California AB 1331 (Workplace Surveillance 2025)
document_name: California AB 1331 (Workplace Surveillance 2025)
body:
Regulates employers' use of AI-enabled workplace surveillance tools, prohibiting their use in private areas like bathrooms and lactation rooms, and requiring clear notification where surveillance occurs. Prohibits AI-enabled video in breakrooms and penalizes violations with civil penalties.

Prohibits employers in California from using AI-enabled workplace surveillance tools in bathrooms, locker rooms, changing areas, and lactation spaces unless directed by a court order.

Restricts the use of generative AI-enabled video surveillance in employee-only breakrooms and cafeterias, allowing only AI tools for photo or video correction without surveillance capacity.

Mandates employers to inform workers if surveillance tools are used.

Prohibits employers from requiring workers to implant devices for data collection.

Allows the Labor Commissioner to enforce these regulations and impose penalties for violations, with workers having protection against retaliation for exercising rights under this law.

Exempts certain employers like those involved in national security or military purposes, and specific law enforcement agencies, from these regulations. 

Ensures these provisions do not override local laws offering greater worker protection.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S 2750 Strengthening Artificial intelligence Normalization and Diffusion By Oversight and eXperimentation Act 2025
document_name: S 2750 SANDBOX Act 2025
body:
Requires the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy to establish a Federal regulatory sandbox program for AI, allowing applicants to test AI innovations by obtaining temporary waivers or modifications on specific legal provisions.

Requires the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) to establish a Federal regulatory sandbox program for artificial intelligence (AI). 

Allows entities developing or deploying AI systems to apply for temporary waivers or modifications of specific legal or regulatory requirements in order to test AI technologies within the sandbox.

Establishes an application process requiring applicants to describe the AI system, testing plan, regulatory barriers, and potential risks such as health and safety harms, economic impacts, and unfair trade practices.

Directs relevant federal agencies to review applications and assess the risks and benefits of proposed AI testing before approving sandbox participation.

Authorizes the OSTP Director to approve, deny, modify, or revoke waivers and to impose conditions on sandbox participation.

Requires monitoring and evaluation of sandbox activities, including compliance with participation conditions and mitigation of identified risks.

Allows the Director to review compliance, revoke waivers, or terminate participation if participants fail to meet the terms of their agreement.

Facilitates coordination between the federal sandbox program and state-level AI regulatory initiatives where appropriate.

Requires reporting to Congress on sandbox activities, outcomes, and recommendations for regulatory changes.

Establishes the 12-year duration and operational terms of the sandbox program.

title: California SB 503 (Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence 2025)
document_name: California SB 503 (Health Care Services: AI 2025)
body:
Requires developers and deployers to identify, mitigate, and monitor AI systems in healthcare for biased impacts. Obligates them to report compliance efforts annually. Instructs the department to publish these reports online. Effective from January 1, 2027.

Add Section 1339.76 to the Health and Safety Code.

Require developers and deployers to identify and mitigate artificial intelligence systems with biased impacts in clinical decision-making or health care resource allocation.

Instruct deployers to monitor these AI systems regularly and take steps to reduce bias.

Specify no requirement for the department to independently inspect AI systems; developers and deployers ensure compliance and maintain documentation.

Obligate developers, starting January 1, 2027, to report compliance efforts to the department before making AI systems available.

Require deployers to submit annual compliance reports to the department starting January 1, 2027.

Mandate the department to publish these reports online.

Define terms such as "biased impact," "deployer," "developer," and "artificial intelligence."

Clarify that compliance with this section supplements other state laws and does not serve as a defense against discrimination claims.

title: California AB 33 (Autonomous Vehicles 2024)
document_name: California AB 33 (Autonomous Vehicles 2024)
body:
Prohibits delivery of commercial goods by autonomous vehicles on highways without a human safety operator. Imposes fines for violations. Requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to report on AV technology’s impact on safety and employment by 2031, considering input from various state agencies.

Prohibits the delivery of commercial goods using autonomous vehicles without a human safety operator on highways in California.

Imposes a fine of $10,000 for a first violation and $25,000 for subsequent violations for delivering goods without a human operator.

Allows the department to suspend or revoke permits for repeated violations.

Requires the department to submit a report by 2031 evaluating the impact of autonomous vehicle technology on public safety and employment in the transportation sector.

Mandates consultation with relevant agencies, including the California Highway Patrol, the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, and others, during the report preparation.

Prohibits issuance of deployment permits for autonomous delivery vehicles without human operators until one year after an oversight hearing, contingent on further legislative authorization.

title: [UN] 급속한 기술변화가 SDGs에 미치는 영향 결의(A/RES/79/334)
document_name: Impact of rapid technological change on the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals and targets / 「급속한 기술변화가 지속가능발전목표 및 세부목표 달성에 미치는 영향」
body:
●기관: 유엔총회(UN General Assembly)
●문서종류: 유엔총회 결의 / 과학기술·지속가능발전 결의
●문서명: Impact of rapid technological change on the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals and targets / 「급속한 기술변화가 지속가능발전목표 및 세부목표 달성에 미치는 영향」
●채택시점: 2025년 9월 8일
●핵심내용:유엔총회가 급속한 기술변화가 지속가능발전목표(SDGs) 달성에 미치는 기회와 위험을 다룬 결의임. AI, 디지털 기술, 과학기술혁신이 지속가능발전을 촉진할 수 있지만, 기술격차와 역량격차가 확대될 경우 국가 간·국가 내 불평등을 심화시킬 수 있다는 문제의식을 바탕으로 포용적이고 인간중심적인 기술협력과 역량강화를 촉구함.
① 문서는 AI 등 급속한 기술변화가 빈곤·보건·교육·기후·생산성 등 SDGs 달성에 기여할 수 있지만, 디지털·데이터·컴퓨팅·역량 격차가 개발도상국의 활용을 제약한다고 지적함
② 개발도상국의 기술 접근성과 활용역량 강화를 위해 STI·디지털 공공인프라·데이터 거버넌스·기술이전·금융지원 등을 확대해야 한다고 강조함
③ 기술발전이 인권·프라이버시·안전·포용성·성평등·환경 지속가능성에 부합하도록 책임 있는 거버넌스와 국제협력을 강화해야 한다고 촉구함

category: UN
title: [UNESCO] AI와 교육: 학습자 권리 보호
document_name: AI and education: Protecting the rights of learners / 「AI와 교육: 학습자의 권리 보호」
body:
●기관: UNESCO
●문서종류: 보고서 / AI와 교육권 정책보고서
●문서명: AI and education: Protecting the rights of learners / 「AI와 교육: 학습자의 권리 보호」
●발표시점: 2025년 9월 4일
●핵심내용:UNESCO는 교육의 디지털화와 생성형 AI 확산이 교육 접근성, 맞춤형 학습, 교육행정 효율성 측면에서 기회를 제공하는 동시에, 불평등 심화, 개인정보·안전, 윤리·거버넌스·형평성 문제를 초래할 수 있다고 분석함. 동 보고서는 모든 학습자의 교육권을 보호하기 위해 AI와 디지털 기술 활용이 인간 중심적이고 권리 기반적인 방식으로 이루어져야 하며, 국가적·국제적 차원의 긴급한 정책 대응이 필요하다고 강조함.
① 문서는 AI와 디지털 기술이 교육 접근성·개인화 학습 등을 높일 수 있지만, 안전장치가 부족할 경우 교육권과 인권을 위협할 수 있다고 지적함
② 인터넷 접근 격차가 AI 격차로 이어질 수 있으며, 여아·농촌 인구·장애인 등이 디지털·AI 교육 전환에서 배제될 위험이 크다고 분석함
③ 교육 분야 AI 활용을 위해 데이터 보호·윤리·투명성·책임성·포용적 접근을 강화하고, 기술을 보편적 교육권과 정렬해야 한다고 촉구함

title: [ITU] 연례 AI 거버넌스 보고서 2025
document_name: The Annual AI Governance Report 2025: Steering the Future of AI / 「2025 연례 AI 거버넌스 보고서: AI의 미래를 이끌다」
body:
●기관: 국제전기통신연합(ITU)
●문서종류: 연례보고서 / AI 거버넌스 보고서
●문서명: The Annual AI Governance Report 2025: Steering the Future of AI / 「2025 연례 AI 거버넌스 보고서: AI의 미래를 이끌다」
●발표시점: 2025년 9월
●핵심내용:ITU의 AI for Good Global Summit 2025 중 International AI Standards Exchange 논의에서 공유된 주요 내용을 바탕으로 작성된 연례 AI 거버넌스 보고서임. AI 거버넌스가 원칙 선언을 넘어 실행, 표준, 안전도구, 포용적 역량강화, 인프라·환경 지속가능성, 정책 상호운용성으로 이동해야 한다는 방향을 제시함.
① 보고서는 AI 거버넌스의 초점이 단순 규제에서 벗어나 AI 발전을 공익과 신뢰에 맞게 조정하는 방향으로 이동하고 있다고 제시함
② AI 에이전트·자율시스템·과학연구·노동시장·AI 인프라와 에너지 등 새로운 거버넌스 과제를 다루며, 안전성·상호운용성·신뢰성 확보를 위한 국제표준의 중요성을 강조함
③ 원칙의 실행 전환, 다중이해관계자 협력, 투명성·포용성·역량강화·환경 지속가능성과 정책 상호운용성을 주요 정책방향으로 제안함
