title: [UNICEF] AI 규제와 아동권리에 대한 영향에 관한 글로벌 신속 검토
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Governance in Motion: A Rapid Global Review of AI Regulation and Its Implications for Children’s Rights / 「인공지능 거버넌스 동향: AI 규제와 아동권리에 대한 영향에 관한 글로벌 신속 검토」
body:
●기관: UNICEF
●문서종류: 신속 검토보고서 / AI 규제·아동권리 보고서
●문서명: Artificial Intelligence Governance in Motion: A Rapid Global Review of AI Regulation and Its Implications for Children’s Rights / 「인공지능 거버넌스 동향: AI 규제와 아동권리에 대한 영향에 관한 글로벌 신속 검토」
●발표시점: 2025년 9월
●핵심내용:UNICEF가 AI 규제 강화를 지원하기 위해 국제·지역 AI 프레임워크와 주요 관할권의 AI 규제모델을 검토한 보고서임. 특히 EU, 중국, 영국, 인도 등 4개 관할권의 규제 접근이 아동에게 미치는 영향을 분석하고, 아동권리법에 기반한 선제적 AI 규제가 필요하다고 강조함.
① 보고서는 국제·지역 AI 프레임워크와 EU·중국·영국·인도의 규제모델을 비교해 AI 거버넌스 접근과 아동권리 보호 방식을 분석함
② AI 규제가 초기 단계여서 가장 효과적인 아동권리 보호 접근을 단정하기 어렵지만, 장기적 증거를 기다리는 관망 방식은 부적절하다고 지적함
③ AI가 아동 관련 서비스와 활동에 확산되는 만큼, 아동의 안전·발달·복지를 보호하기 위한 선제적이고 권리기반의 규제가 필요하다고 강조함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 833 (Critical infrastructure: artificial intelligence systems: human oversight)
document_name: California SB 833 (Critical infrastructure: AI systems and human oversight)
body:
Establishes human oversight mechanisms for AI in critical infrastructure. Requires real-time monitoring and annual assessments by oversight personnel. Directs the Department of Technology to provide AI safety training. Limits public access to sensitive infrastructure information under the California Public Records Act.

Establishes the requirement for oversight personnel of operators deploying covered AI systems in critical infrastructure to create a human oversight mechanism by July 1, 2026. This mechanism ensures real-time monitoring and prior review of AI system actions unless deemed disruptive.

Instructs the Department of Technology to develop annual specialized training focused on AI safety protocols and risk management for oversight personnel.

Requires operators to conduct an annual assessment of their AI systems to evaluate compliance, performance, safety, and identify risks, with findings submitted to the Department.

Limits public access to records related to AI oversight in critical infrastructure, protecting sensitive information under the California Public Records Act.

Defines key terms including "artificial intelligence," "automated decision system," "covered AI system," and "critical infrastructure," specifying their roles and impact on public health, safety, and economic security.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 1405 (Artificial intelligence: auditors: enrollment)
document_name: California AB 1405 (AI auditors)
body:
Establishes the AI Auditors’ Enrollment Fund and details requirements for AI auditors in California. Requires auditors to enroll and adhere to industry standards. Prohibits conflicts of interest and unauthorized disclosure of information. Requires the Government Operations Agency to manage enrollments and misconduct reports.

Establishes the AI Auditors’ Enrollment Fund, administered by the Government Operations Agency, to oversee the regulation of AI auditors.

Requires AI auditors to enroll with the agency, pay enrollment fees, and provide detailed information about their practices by January 1, 2027.

Mandates AI auditors to adhere to widely recognized industry standards and avoid conflicts of interest, including prohibiting employment with auditees within 12 months of an audit.

Obliges auditors to provide detailed reports post-audit to auditees, explaining results and compliance recommendations while retaining documentation for at least 10 years.

Prohibits auditors from disclosing confidential information without authorization, except under specified legal circumstances, and prohibits retaliation against employees who report non-compliance.

Instructs the agency to publish auditor information publicly and retain and share misconduct reports for enforcement purposes, beginning January 1, 2027. 

Clarifies that this chapter doesn’t impede audits required by other statutes prior to January 2027, when Section 11549.86 expires.

category: UN
title: [UN] 독립 국제 AI 과학패널 및 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 대화 설립 결의(A/RES/79/325)
document_name: Terms of reference and modalities for the establishment and functioning of the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence and the Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance / 「인공지능 독립 국제과학패널 및 인공지능 거버넌스 글로벌 대화의 설치·운영을 위한 위임사항과 방식」
body:
●기관: 유엔총회(UN General Assembly)
●문서종류: 유엔총회 결의 / AI 거버넌스 제도화 결의
●문서명: Terms of reference and modalities for the establishment and functioning of the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence and the Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance / 「인공지능 독립 국제과학패널 및 인공지능 거버넌스 글로벌 대화의 설치·운영을 위한 위임사항과 방식」
●채택시점: 2025년 8월 26일
●문서배포: 2025년 8월 27일
●핵심내용:유엔총회가 글로벌 디지털 콤팩트의 후속조치로, AI 거버넌스에 관한 두 개의 유엔 메커니즘인 ‘인공지능 독립 국제과학패널’과 ‘인공지능 거버넌스 글로벌 대화’의 설치·운영 방식과 위임사항을 정한 결의임. 동 결의는 AI의 기회와 위험에 대한 과학 기반 평가를 제공하고, 회원국과 다양한 이해관계자가 참여하는 포용적 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 논의의 제도적 기반을 마련함.
① 인공지능 독립 국제과학패널을 설치하여 AI의 기회, 위험, 영향에 관한 과학적·증거 기반 평가를 제공하도록 함을 언급함
② 회원국·유엔기구·민간부문·시민사회·학계 등이「AI 거버넌스 글로벌 대화」를 통해 포용적이고 투명한 국제 AI 거버넌스 논의를 추진함
③ 과학패널의 평가를 글로벌 대화의 정책논의에 활용하고, 두 메커니즘을 글로벌 디지털 콤팩트 이행과 AI 국제협력 강화를 위한 체계로 운영하도록 제시함

title: [중국] ‘AI+’ 행동의 심층 이행에 관한 국무원 의견
document_name: 《国务院关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》/ 「‘인공지능+’ 행동의 심층 이행에 관한 국무원 의견」
body:
●국가: 중국
●기관: 국무원
●문서종류: 국가전략 / 정책 의견
●문서명: 《国务院关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》/ 「‘인공지능+’ 행동의 심층 이행에 관한 국무원 의견」
●발표시점: 2025년 8월 27일
●핵심내용중국 국무원이 AI와 경제·사회 전 분야의 융합을 심화하기 위해 발표한 상위 정책문서. AI를 과학기술, 산업, 소비, 민생, 거버넌스, 글로벌 협력에 접목하여 “인간-기계 협업, 분야 간 융합, 공동창조·공유” 기반의 지능경제·지능사회를 형성하는 것이 목표임. 중국은 풍부한 데이터 자원, 완비된 산업체계, 넓은 응용 시나리오를 강점으로 제시하고, AI를 신질생산력 육성과 중국식 현대화의 핵심 수단으로 위치시킴.
6대 핵심 축:① AI+과학기술: 과학 대형모델, 고품질 과학 데이터셋, 지능형 연구도구를 활용해 과학 발견과 기술개발 방식을 혁신② AI+산업발전: 제조업·농업·서비스업 전반의 지능화 전환을 추진하고, 스마트 네이티브 신모델·신업태 육성③ AI+소비고도화: 지능형 커넥티드카, AI 스마트폰·PC, 스마트로봇, 스마트홈·웨어러블 등 차세대 지능형 단말과 서비스 소비 확대④ AI+민생복지: 교육, 의료, 고용, 생활서비스에 AI를 적용해 주민 건강지원, 학습방식 개선, 업무방식 고도화 추진⑤ AI+거버넌스 역량: 사회거버넌스, 공공안전, 생태환경 관리에 AI를 적용하고, 인간-기계 공생형 사회관리 체계 구축⑥ AI+글로벌 협력: AI를 인류에 이익이 되는 국제 공공재로 보고, 글로벌 사우스 AI 역량강화, 오픈소스 접근성, 유엔 중심 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 협력 강조

title: [APEC] 2025 디지털·AI 장관 성명
document_name: 2025 APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Statement / 「2025 APEC 디지털·AI 장관성명」
body:
●기관: APEC
●문서종류: 디지털·AI 장관성명 / 부문별 장관회의 결과문서
●문서명: 2025 APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Statement / 「2025 APEC 디지털·AI 장관성명」
●발표시점: 2025년 8월 4일
●핵심내용:2025년 8월 4~6일 인천에서 개최된 APEC 디지털·AI 장관회의 결과문서로, “모두의 번영과 지속가능한 성장을 위한 디지털·AI 전환”을 주제로 채택된 장관성명임. 성명은 AI와 디지털 기술을 생산성, 혁신, 공공·민간 서비스 혁신의 핵심 동력으로 보면서도, 안전성, 신뢰성, 접근성, 포용성, 디지털 격차 해소를 함께 고려해야 한다고 강조함.
① APEC은 AI와 디지털 기술이 생산성·효율성·회복력·혁신에 기여할 수 있다고 평가하고, 책임 있고 안전한 기술 도입을 강조함
② AI 확산에 대응해 평생학습·인재역량 강화와 디지털 격차 해소를 추진하고, 고품질·회복력 있는 통신·광대역 및 에너지·자원 효율적 디지털 인프라를 확충할 필요가 있다고 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB-1170, SEC. 46 (AI in Education Working Group 2025)
document_name: California AB-1170, SEC. 46 (AI in Education Working Group 2025)
body:
Requires the Superintendent to convene a working group to develop AI usage guidelines for educational settings. Instructs the group to assess AI use in schools, develop model policies, and report findings by 2027. Specifies transparency, privacy, and academic integrity provisions.

Amends the Education Code to define "artificial intelligence" and establish a working group, convened by the Superintendent, for the safe and effective use of AI in education. 

Requires development of guidance on AI use that benefits pupils and educators, a model policy on AI in local educational agencies, and practices supporting educators’ effective use of AI.

Includes diverse stakeholders in the working group, with at least half being credentialed teachers.

Assesses current and future AI use, conducting public meetings for feedback, and identifying human-centered and replacement AI examples.

Details AI's impact on educational quality, pupil data security, and teacher employment.

Develops AI guidance and model policies addressing academic integrity, data privacy, acceptable uses, and avoiding inequities.

Submits a report to the Legislature by January 1, 2027, presents findings, and posts guidance online. 

Dissolves the working group post-report submission and repeals this section on January 1, 2031.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB-1170, SEC. 35 (Generative AI Training Data Documentation 2025)
document_name: California AB-1170, SEC. 35 (Generative AI Training Data Documentation 2025)
body:
Requires developers to publicly post data documentation for generative AI systems released after 2022, covering datasets used, unless systems focus solely on security, aircraft operation, or national defense. Specifies details including data sources, purposes, and modifications.

Requires developers of generative AI systems or services made publicly available in California to post documentation about the data used for training these systems on their websites by 2026.

Specifies the documentation must include a summary of datasets, sources, and how they support the system's purpose.

Requires disclosure on dataset data points, whether datasets include copyrighted or personal information, modifications made, and whether synthetic data is used.

Exempts AI systems aimed solely at ensuring security and integrity, operating aircraft in national airspace, or developed for national security and defense purposes for federal entities from these documentation requirements.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 1170, SEC. 27-28 (CCPA Amendment 2025)
document_name: California AB 1170, SEC. 27-28 (CCPA Amendment 2025)
body:
Defines "automated processing" and "profiling," addressing AI governance in California Civil Code 1798.140. Requires AI-related regulations to maximize privacy and govern automated decision-making (Section 1798.185). Assigns responsibilities to the California Privacy Protection Agency for regulation (Section 1798.185).

Defines "personal information" broadly, including identification, biometric data, and inferred profiles, affecting AI systems processing such data.

Requires businesses using AI for profiling to comply with privacy regulations, including consumer access and opt-out rights.

Mandates businesses disclose AI logic and outcomes involved in decision-making processes to consumers upon request.

Instructs businesses conducting AI-related research to pseudonymize, deidentify data, and use additional safeguards

Tasked the California Privacy Protection Agency with issuing and updating regulations concerning AI-related data processing, including profiling and automated decision-making.

Requires annual cybersecurity audits and risk assessments for businesses processing significant AI-related data.

Prohibits businesses from sharing consumer data, including through AI models, without consumer consent, for cross-context behavioral advertising. 

Enhances consumer rights regarding AI-related data through opt-out choices and protections against dark patterns or coercive consent practices.

category: Editors' Picks;Miscellaneous documents
title: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan 2025
document_name: 2025 AI Action Plan
body:
Encourages AI innovation by removing regulations, revising funding based on states' AI climate, and reviewing FTC actions. Promotes free speech in AI systems, revises procurement guidelines, and evaluates international AI models. Supports open-source AI use, workforce retraining, and safeguards against deepfakes. Advances AI infrastructure development, cybersecurity, international diplomacy, and semiconductor manufacturing. Prioritizes AI R&D, interpretability, evaluations, national security assessments, and biosecurity measures.

Promotes private-sector-led AI innovation by removing regulatory barriers and rescinding burdensome regulations.

Launches a Request for Information to identify regulations hindering AI progress and proposes regulatory revisions or repeal.

Ensures AI systems protect free speech, revising guidelines to eliminate references to misinformation and bias.

Encourages open-source AI, facilitating access to computing resources and fostering open-weight models for global standards.

Facilitates AI adoption through regulatory sandboxes and promotes sector-specific standards and evaluation measures.

Empowers American workers by prioritizing AI skill development and offering retraining programs for those displaced by AI advancements.

Supports next-generation manufacturing and AI-enabled science with federal investments and data sharing.

Strengthens AI cybersecurity, ensuring secure and resilient AI systems for critical infrastructure.

Leads international AI diplomacy by exporting AI technology and countering foreign influence on governance bodies.

Enhances semiconductor manufacturing and data center infrastructure, streamlining regulatory processes.

Evaluates AI's national security risks, investing in biosecurity and AI interpretability research.

title: Executive Order on Promoting the Export of the American AI Technology Stack
document_name: Executive Order on Promoting the Export of the American AI Technology Stack
body:
Establishes the American AI Exports Program to support the deployment of U.S. AI technologies. Requires the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with other officials, to evaluate proposals. Mobilizes federal financing tools to promote American AI exports globally.

Establishes the American AI Exports Program to promote the development and deployment of U.S. full-stack AI export packages.

Instructs the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with other officials, to implement this program.

Requires proposals to include AI hardware, models, and applications, identify target export countries, outline business models, and comply with U.S. export regulations.

Directs the Economic Diplomacy Action Group to coordinate federal financing tools to support AI export efforts.

Appoints the Secretary of State to develop strategies for promoting U.S. AI technologies and align federal resources to support priority AI exports.

Mandates coordination with partner countries to foster supportive regulatory environments.

Utilizes federal financing measures such as loans, insurance, and technical assistance to support selected AI export packages.

Ensures compliance with applicable laws and appropriations.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Executive Order on Preventing Woke AI In The Federal Government
document_name: Executive Order on Preventing Woke AI In The Federal Government
body:
Directs federal agency heads to procure large language models (LLMs) that adhere to two principles: truth-seeking and ideological neutrality. Requires developers to not intentionally encode partisan or ideological judgments into an LLM’s outputs. Instructs the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance for implementation, acknowledging technical limitations and allowing exceptions for national security systems.

Requires agency heads to procure only large language models (LLMs) that adhere to "Unbiased AI Principles," emphasizing truth-seeking and ideological neutrality.

Defines LLMs as generative AI models that generate natural-language responses to user prompts.

Instructs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to, within 120 days, issue guidance for implementing these principles, considering technical limitations, transparency, and avoiding over-prescription.

Mandates agency heads to ensure Federal contracts for LLMs include compliance with the Unbiased AI Principles, allowing vendor decommissioning costs for noncompliance.

Allows agencies to specify criteria for applying these principles to other AI models and exempts national security systems where appropriate.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Executive Order on Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure
document_name: Executive Order on Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure
body:
Facilitates AI infrastructure development by easing federal regulations, utilizing federal lands for data centers, and providing financial support for AI projects. Directs various agencies to expedite environmental reviews, permitting, and financial assistance for AI-related projects.

Prioritizes the rapid development of AI data centers by easing federal regulatory burdens and using federally owned resources.

Defines “Data Center Project” as facilities requiring more than 100 MW of AI-related load and establishes “Covered Components,” “Covered Component Projects,” and “Qualifying Projects” based on capital investment (≥$500 million), electric load thresholds, national security relevance, or agency designation.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to launch a financial support initiative for Qualifying Projects, including loans, loan guarantees, grants and tax incentives.

Requires agencies to identify categorical exclusions under National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and limits when federal financial assistance constitutes a “major Federal action” to expedite environmental review.

Authorizes the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (FPISC) to designate Qualifying Projects for inclusion on the Permitting Dashboard under FAST-41 for expedited review and transparency.

Directs the Environmental Protection Agency to streamline permitting under the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and other laws, and to identify Brownfield and Superfund Sites for reuse by Qualifying Projects.

Requires programmatic consultation under the Endangered Species Act and directs review of nationwide permits under the Clean Water Act and Rivers and Harbors Act to determine whether activity-specific permits are needed.

Directs the Departments of the Interior and Energy to provide authorizations for federal lands and directs the Secretary of Defense to identify and competitively lease suitable military lands for infrastructure supporting Qualifying Projects.

Revokes Executive Order 14141.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S2367 AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act 2025
document_name: S2367 AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act 2025
body:
Establishes liability for using individuals' data without express prior consent, including AI training. Permits private legal actions for violations. Invalidates predispute arbitration agreements for such claims. Requires transparent disclosure of third-party data use. Sets a federal minimum standard without preempting stronger state laws.

Establishes a federal tort for any individual or entity that appropriates, uses, collects, processes, sells, or otherwise exploits an individual's data without express, prior consent.

Defines key terms such as “artificial intelligence,” “generative artificial intelligence system,” and “covered data.”

Allows individuals to bring civil actions against violators and recover compensatory and punitive damages, injunctive relief, and attorney’s fees.

Requires explicit disclosure and consent for data use by third parties, invalidating consent obtained through coercion or bundled with general terms.

Excludes application of predispute arbitration agreements, ensuring individuals can pursue judicial recourse.

Applies a minimum standard for data protection, allowing states to enforce more stringent protections.

Mandates that courts, not arbitrators, decide the applicability of the Act to disputes, preventing reliance on arbitration clauses.

Ensures specific third-party data usage disclosures to individuals, invalidating non-specific or passive consent.

title: General Purpose AI Code of Practice, Transparency Chapter
document_name: General Purpose AI Code of Practice, Transparency Chapter
body:
Requires general-purpose AI model providers to comply with AI Act obligations, particularly Articles 53 and 55. Obligates providers to maintain, disclose, and update model documentation for compliance assessment. Tasks the AI Office with overseeing adherence to these obligations.

Provides a Code of Practice to enhance compliance with Articles 53 and 55 of the AI Act, focusing on human-centric and trustworthy AI while ensuring protection against AI's harmful effects.

Guides providers of general-purpose AI models in fulfilling documentation obligations per the AI Act, ensuring updated Model Documentation is accessible to the AI Office and downstream providers.

Requires disclosures of contact information to facilitate information requests from the AI Office and downstream providers, ensuring compliance assessment for high-risk AI systems through timely information provision.

Advises on maintaining the quality, security, and integrity of documented information, suggesting adherence to technical standards and protocols.

Encourages voluntary public transparency, allowing public access to non-confidential information, and providing training content summaries as required by AI Act provisions in line with Article 53(1)(d).

Exempts open-source AI models without systemic risk from these requirements, aligning obligations with the proportionality principle.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 412 (Generative artificial intelligence: training data: copyrighted materials.)
document_name: California AB 412 (Use of copyrighted material in Generative AI)
body:
Requires developers of generative AI (GenAI) models to document and disclose copyright-protected materials used for training, enable rights owners to request this information, and comply within 30 days. Exempts noncommercial research and models using publicly available data or owned materials.

Enacts requirements for developers of generative AI (GenAI) models concerning copyrighted materials. 

Requires developers to document any copyrighted materials used for training GenAI models, including identifying rights owners.

Obliges developers to provide website information enabling fingerprint generation compatible with covered materials and created according to widely accepted standards.

Requires a web mechanism to allow rights owners to request information about the use of covered materials, and developers must retain relevant documentation.

Obliges developers to respond to rights owner requests within 30 days, informing them about the presence of their materials in the dataset.

Permits civil actions against non-compliant developers with damages of $1,000 per violation and other remedial measures.

Exempts GenAI models trained on publicly available data, used for noncommercial research, not trained on covered materials, or where the developer owns the rights. 

Limits requests by rights owners to one per calendar quarter unless new information arises.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 412
document_name: California AB 412 (Generative artificial intelligence: training data: copyrighted materials)
body:
Regulates GenAI developers in California by requiring them to document copyrighted materials used to train AI models, make available a mechanism for rights owners to request information regarding the use of covered materials, and respond to rights owners’ information requests within 30 days.

Defines terms for the purposes of this article, including approximate content fingerprint and artificial intelligence. 

Requires GenAI developers to document and identify covered materials used for training their models, including the rights owner of each covered material.

Mandates that developers provide information on their websites that enable the generation of fingerprints that are compatible with covered materials used to train a GenAI model and are generated using accepted industry standards.

Instructs GenAI developers to make available on their websites a mechanism allowing rights owners to request information about developers' use of covered materials.

Obliges developers to assess and respond to rights owners’ requests within 30 days; states that each day after the 30-day period a developer fails to provide a rights owner with the required information constitutes a discrete violation.

Limits rights owners to one request per quarter to the same developer concerning the same model and permits rights owners to bring civil actions against developers who do not comply with this article, including actual damages, injunctive relief, and attorney’s fees.

Exempt models trained using data that the developer makes publicly available, models developed and used for noncommercial academic governmental research, models not trained with covered materials, or models trained using covered materials owned by the developer, from the requirements of this article.

Appropriates $6.168 billion for AI and innovative technologies in border security, including inspection and surveillance upgrades. Restricts funds from untested autonomous surveillance towers. Defines "autonomous" as systems using AI and algorithms for real-time detection and operational adjustments.

Appropriates $6.168 billion to U.S. Customs and Border Protection for fiscal year 2025, with funds available until September 30, 2029, to integrate AI and machine learning in nonintrusive inspection equipment for combating illicit narcotics at U.S. borders.

Restricts the funds from being used to procure or deploy untested autonomous surveillance towers along the southwest and northern borders.

Defines "autonomous" as systems using AI, machine learning, computer vision, or algorithms to detect, identify, classify, and track items in real time, enabling operational adjustments without constant human oversight.

Funds support border surveillance tech upgrades, biometric entry/exit systems, and air/marine operational platforms for rapid response.

Facilitates drug trafficking combatting efforts at U.S. borders, specifically concerning drugs like fentanyl.

Directs resources for screening individuals entering/exiting the U.S. and initial screenings of unaccompanied alien children.

title: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149)
page_url: https://www.legis.state.tx.us/BillLookup/Text.aspx?LegSess=89R&Bill=HB149 - wait until docx version is available
source_urls: https://www.legis.state.tx.us/BillLookup/Text.aspx?LegSess=89R&Bill=HB149 - wait until docx version is available
document_name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (2025 Update) (HB 149)
body:
Establishes the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act, prohibiting AI systems from inciting harm, manipulation, political viewpoint discrimination, and unlawful discrimination against protected classes; requires government agencies to disclose AI use to consumers; establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council and a regulatory sandbox program; and authorizes the Attorney General to enforce compliance and impose civil penalties.

Regulates AI systems in Texas under the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act.

Prohibits AI systems from inciting harm, criminality, manipulation, or discrimination based on political viewpoints or protected classes.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council and a regulatory sandbox program for controlled AI testing.

Requires government disclosure to consumers when AI is used in interactions.

Instructs the attorney general to enforce regulations, manage complaints, and impose fines for non-compliance.

Prohibits government use of AI for social scoring or capturing biometric identifiers in violation of rights.

Mandates that AI must not produce certain unlawful content and must adhere to consumer protections and data privacy.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
document_name: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
body:
Directs the NSA Director to develop an AI Security Playbook to identify vulnerabilities in AI technologies and create strategies to respond to cyber threats, informed by expert engagement and government security involvement. Mandates progress reports to congressional committees.

Directs the Director of the National Security Agency to develop an AI Security Playbook to defend AI technologies from theft by threat actors.

Requires the identification of vulnerabilities specific to AI technologies, with emphasis on threats not typically present or as severe in conventional IT systems.

Instructs the identification of AI components and information that could advance threat actors' capabilities if stolen.

Mandates the development of strategies to detect, prevent, and respond to cyber threats targeting AI.

Requires inclusion of methodologies and assessments in a classified annex and best practices in a public portion for dissemination.

Engages with AI developers and experts for insights and collaboration on security strategies to inform the development of the Playbook. 

Requires the submission of progress and completion reports to congressional intelligence committees within specified timelines.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 480 (Autonomous vehicles 2025)
document_name: California SB 480 (Autonomous vehicles 2025)
body:
Regulates autonomous vehicles (AVs), defining "autonomous technology" and operations on public roads. Requires AV manufacturers to certify safety standards compliance, insurance coverage of $5 million, and testing. Mandates the Department of Motor Vehicles to adopt relevant regulations and allows ADS marker lamps.

Amends the Vehicle Code to establish regulations for autonomous vehicles and their technology.

Defines "autonomous technology" and "autonomous vehicle" following SAE International standards, distinguishing them from vehicles with basic driver-assistance features.

Permits the operation of autonomous vehicles on public roads for testing by designated individuals if specific conditions are met, including possessing the proper driver's license and insurance.

Requires manufacturers to submit an application to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) for the operation of autonomous vehicles, including certifications on safety, insurance, and technology standards.

Instructs the DMV to adopt regulations for insurance, application submissions, and safety standards for autonomous vehicles, consulting experts as needed.

Authorizes the DMV to impose additional requirements for vehicles operating without a driver present.

Requires manufacturers to disclose data collection practices to purchasers and potentially pay fees covering DMV processing costs.

Specifies the addition of ADS marker lamps for autonomous vehicles and mandates zero-emission operation for vehicles of certain specifications starting in 2030.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 420 (Automated decision systems)
document_name: California SB 420 (Automated decision systems)
body:
Establishes rights for individuals to control personal data in AI systems, receive explanations of AI decisions, and seek accountability for harm caused. Requires impact assessments for high-risk AI systems and prohibits AI discrimination. Tasks developers and deployers with implementing risk governance programs.

Establishes a comprehensive framework to govern the use of artificial intelligence and high-risk automated decision systems in California, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and non-discrimination.

Requires all AI systems to provide clear explanations of their data use and decision-making processes.

Mandates informed consent from individuals before using personal data and ensures data privacy aligns with existing laws.

Prohibits AI systems from discriminating based on protected characteristics, and demands regular audits to address biases.

Gives individuals the right to appeal AI-driven decisions and seek human oversight in significant decisions affecting key areas like employment and healthcare.

Obligates developers and deployers to conduct impact assessments on high-risk AI systems, highlighting potential biases.

Prohibits deployment of high-risk systems identified as discriminatory unless mitigations are verified.

Empowers the Attorney General or Civil Rights Department to enforce compliance, issue penalties, and mandate corrective actions for non-compliance.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 60003 ("U.S. Customs and Border Protection technology, vetting activities, and other efforts to enhance border security")
document_name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 60003 ("U.S. Customs and Border Protection technology, vetting activities, and other efforts to enhance border security")
body:
Appropriates $1.076 billion for AI and machine learning to enhance non-intrusive inspection equipment and combat narcotics entry. Restricts funds for untested autonomous surveillance towers. Defines "autonomous" systems as AI-integrated tools identifying items of interest.

Appropriates $1,076,317,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) for AI, machine learning, and non-intrusive inspection equipment to combat illicit narcotics at U.S. borders.

Restricts funds for certain surveillance towers unless they are tested and federally accepted for autonomous capabilities.

Defines "autonomous" as systems using AI, sensors, and onboard computing to automate identification tasks traditionally performed manually by CBP personnel.

title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative")
document_name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative")
body:
Appropriates $500 million to the Department of Commerce for AI-driven system modernization and cybersecurity improvements for Federal information technology systems.

Appropriates $500 million to the Department of Commerce for FY 2025 to modernize federal IT systems using AI and automation technologies.

Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to use funds to replace legacy systems, adopt efficient AI models, and enhance cybersecurity with AI solutions.

Enacts a 10-year moratorium preventing state and local governments from regulating AI models or systems.

Exempts laws facilitating AI deployment or removing legal barriers, provided they do not impose additional requirements unless federally mandated or generally applicable.

body:

Appropriates $124 million to enhance the Test Resource Management Center's AI capabilities.

Allocates $145 million for developing AI to support one-way attack unmanned aerial systems and naval systems.

Assigns $250 million to advance the AI ecosystem and another $250 million to expand Cyber Command's AI initiatives.

Supports the acceleration of Quantum Benchmarking Initiative with $250 million.

Earmarks $500 million to avoid delays in delivering autonomous military capabilities that involve AI technologies.

Includes a $1 billion appropriation for a capital assistance program, including loans and guarantees, aiding AI projects.

Ensures these appropriations and initiatives remain available until September 30, 2029, supporting ongoing AI and technology development in defense.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency")
document_name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency")
body:
Allocates $400 million to accelerate AI-powered unmanned aerial systems and expands the related industrial base. Adds $500 million to advance counter-unmanned aerial systems, including non-kinetic and ship-based programs, emphasizing AI-enabled defense capabilities.

Appropriates $400 million for accelerated one-way attack unmanned aerial systems with advanced autonomy, emphasizing AI capabilities for defense.

Allocates $1 billion to expand the industrial base for one-way attack unmanned aerial systems, further enhancing AI-driven military operations.

Provides $58 million for development, production, and integration of counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, highlighting AI's role in defense against drone threats.

Designates $350 million for non-kinetic counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, demonstrating focus on AI-based alternatives to traditional munitions.

Earmarks $250 million for land-based, and $200 million for ship-based counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, underscoring AI use in diverse defense environments.

Allocates $62 million for AI-enhanced hypersonic strike programs, underscoring importance of AI in cutting-edge military technology.

Requests $500 million for Department of Defense Credit Program to support critical mineral industries, indirectly promoting AI technology development by ensuring material availability.

Permits up to $100 billion in loans and guarantees, indicating a strategic commitment to fortifying supply chains essential for AI advancements within the defense sector.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20002 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for shipbuilding")
document_name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20002 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for shipbuilding")
body:
Appropriates $450 million for autonomy and AI in naval shipbuilding.

Appropriates $450,000,000 for the application of autonomy and artificial intelligence to naval shipbuilding.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare")
document_name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare")
body:
Implements AI tools by 2027 to reduce and identify improper payments in Medicare Parts A and B. Directs the Secretary to contract with AI vendors, recoup identified payments, and report annually to Congress starting 2029.

Mandates the implementation of artificial intelligence tools by January 1, 2027, to reduce and identify improper payments under Medicare Parts A and B.

Directs the Secretary to contract with AI vendors and data scientists to support the implementation.

Requires the recoupment, where practicable, of improper payments identified through AI tools.

Obliges the Secretary to report to Congress by January 1, 2029, and annually thereafter on AI implementation and payment recoupment, including potential improvements and recoupment statistics.

Allocates $12.5 million each from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund and the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund to fund these AI initiatives for fiscal year 2025, with funds available until expended.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs")
document_name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs")
body:
Allocates $140 million for long-range unmanned aircraft systems and $75 million for autonomous maritime systems services. Allows procurement of Arctic Security Cutters by entities other than the Coast Guard. Requires compliance with reporting requirements and advance notification of cost changes.

Appropriates $140 million for long-range unmanned aircraft systems and related infrastructure to improve the US Coast Guard's capabilities. 

Allocates $180 million for maritime domain awareness equipment and services, including $75 million specifically for autonomous maritime systems. 

Allows, through 2030, for entities other than the Coast Guard to acquire, procure, or construct floating dry docks, provided they meet defined requirements. 

Limits design, planning, and engineering expenses to 15% of specified funding allocations for maintenance facilities. 

Exempts acquisitions funded under this act from sections 1131, 1132, and 1133 of title 14, United States Code. 

Mandates compliance with reporting requirements and submission of an expenditure plan to relevant Congressional committees.

Prohibits expenditure during any fiscal year if the Coast Guard is non-compliant with specified sections of title 14, United States Code. 

Requires prior notification to Congress before procurement actions affecting cost or timelines.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
document_name: TAKE IT DOWN Act (2025)
body:
Prohibits the use of AI to create or distribute nonconsensual digital forgeries, establishes criminal penalties and civil remedies, and criminalizes related threats. Requires platforms to establish procedures for removal requests of nonconsensual intimate images, and assigns enforcement authority to the Federal Trade Commission.

Prohibits the sharing of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions online, including those created by artificial intelligence (AI), known as digital forgeries. 

Criminalizes the creation and distribution of such depictions without consent, especially targeting AI-altered, identifiable images. 

Imposes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offenses involving adults and minors. 

Requires covered platforms to establish a clear removal process within one year of the Act’s enactment, to remove valid nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours of the request.

Provides liability protections for platforms that remove content in good faith.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance, treating noncompliance as an unfair or deceptive act. 

Specifies legal exceptions, including disclosures for lawful or investigative purposes.

category: UN
title: [OHCHR] AI 조달 및 배치: 유엔 기업과 인권 이행원칙과의 정합성 보장
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Procurement and Deployment: Ensuring Alignment with the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (A/HRC/59/53) / 「인공지능 조달 및 배치: 유엔 기업과 인권 이행원칙과의 정합성 보장」
body:
●기관: 유엔 기업과 인권 실무그룹(UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights) / 유엔 인권최고대표사무소(OHCHR)
●문서종류: 유엔 인권이사회 보고서 요약본 / AI 조달·배치와 기업·인권 원칙에 관한 정책보고서
●문서명: Artificial Intelligence Procurement and Deployment: Ensuring Alignment with the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (A/HRC/59/53) / 「인공지능 조달 및 배치: 유엔 기업과 인권 이행원칙과의 정합성 보장」
●발표시점: 2025년 5월 15일
●핵심내용:동 보고서는 AI를 직접 개발하지 않고 외부에서 조달·도입하는 국가기관과 기업에도 「유엔 기업과 인권 이행원칙(UNGPs)」이 적용된다고 밝히고, AI 시스템의 구매·계약·배치·운영 전 과정에서 인권 보호와 인권실사(HRDD)를 시행해야 한다고 제시함. 보고서는 현행 AI 규제와 구제체계가 분절되어 있고 집행력이 충분하지 않아, 공공·민간 부문의 AI 조달이 차별, 감시, 개인정보 침해와 같은 인권침해로 이어질 수 있다고 분석함.
① 보고서는 AI가 금융·농업·의료·사법 등에서 편익을 제공할 수 있으나, 개인정보·차별금지·표현의 자유·공정한 재판·노동권·환경권 등 광범위한 인권을 침해할 위험이 있다고 지적함
② 국가와 기업의 AI 조달·배치 과정에서 인권영향평가·인권실사·안전장치가 충분하지 않으며, 고위험 분야와 대규모 감시·실시간 얼굴인식·사회적 점수화·예측치안 등에 강화된 규제와 금지가 필요하다고 제시함
③ 국가·기업에는 정보공개·인권실사·설명가능성·비차별성·피해구제 절차를 강화하고, 시민사회 참여와 사법적·비사법적 구제수단 및 AI 인권역량을 확대하도록 권고함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: H.R. 3447 Chip Security Act
document_name: Chip Security Act 2025
body:
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to mandate chip security mechanisms for location verification before exporting integrated circuit products. Obligates reporting of tampering or diversion. Mandates the assessment and development of additional security mechanisms, considering national security and export compliance objectives.

Mandates the Secretary of Commerce to issue standards for chip security mechanisms on integrated circuit products within 180 days of the Act's enactment.

Requires covered integrated circuit products to include location verification and other security features before export, re-export, or in-country transfer.

Obligates exporters to report any unauthorized change in product location, user, or tampering incidents to the Under Secretary of Industry and Security.

Calls for an assessment within one year to identify additional security mechanisms needed to enhance Export Control Reform Act compliance and prevent unauthorized use.

Directs the Secretary to develop secondary security requirements based on assessment findings and report to Congress with a roadmap for implementation.

Empowers the Secretary to verify ownership and location of exported products and maintain records.

Requires annual assessments of new chip security mechanisms and recommends export control modifications to expand permissible destinations for secure products.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion
document_name: AI Diffusion Rule (US BIS)
body:
Controls the export of AI chips and models outside the United States. Establishes a country-based tiering system to determine applicable restrictions, exceptions, and conditions, including security and reporting safeguards. Creates validated end-user programs to govern exports of AI chips to most countries. Defines an adjustable compute-based threshold for export-controlled AI models.

Imposes export controls on AI models, excluding publicly available models, and expands licensing requirements for AI chips to additional countries.

Establishes three tiers of countries for purposes of determining applicable export restrictions, including eighteen countries able to import AI chips without restrictions (tier 1); countries able to import AI chips through validated end-user (VEU) programs, limited-volume exceptions, and licensing, but otherwise subject to restrictions (tier 2); and countries subject to ongoing restrictions, including arms-embargoed countries (tier 3).

Establishes a Data Center Validated End User (DC VEU) program to govern compute exports related to major AI infrastructure development in second-tier countries, with different pathways and restrictions depending on data center operator nationality. Imposes cybersecurity, physical and personnel security, and sourcing mandates on DC VEU participants, as well as reporting requirements.

Imposes specific computing power deployment restrictions on companies operating in second-tier countries, including relative ratios and numerical caps.

Controls the export of AI models developed using compute above a given threshold, to be adjusted over time based on assessments of publicly available models. Requires cloud computing providers to implement security measures preventing the unauthorized training of models otherwise subject to export controls.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York Senate Bill S3008C ("Part X")
document_name: New York Senate Bill S3008C ("Part X, Algorithmic pricing")
body:
Requires personalized algorithmic pricing providers to disclose their use of personalized pricing and the personal data involved. Directs the Attorney General to enforce compliance, including issuing cease-and-desist orders and seeking injunctions for violations.

Define "algorithm" as a computational automated process using a set of rules.

Require any provider using personalized algorithmic pricing to disclose its use to consumers.

Obligate such providers to inform consumers of the personal data used for dynamic pricing determinations.

Ensure providers give clear and conspicuous disclosure of the price of goods or services.

Authorize the attorney general to issue cease and desist letters to entities allegedly violating this section and seek injunctions through the court if necessary, without requiring proof of damage.

Permit courts to impose civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation and clarify this section as supplemental, not limiting other liabilities under the law.

Specify that the act takes effect 60 days after becoming law.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York Senate Bill S3008C ("Part U")
document_name: New York Senate Bill S3008C ("Part U, AI companion models")
body:
Regulates AI companions by requiring protocols to address suicidal ideation and mandates user notifications about non-human interactions. Empowers the Attorney General to enforce compliance, with penalties benefiting a suicide prevention fund.

Adds Article 47 to the general business law, regulating AI companions.

Defines “artificial intelligence (AI),” “generative AI,” “AI model,” “AI companion,” “operator,” “user,” “emotional recognition algorithms,” and “self-harm,” and specifies systems that are excluded from the definition of AI companion.

Prohibits operators from providing AI companions without protocols to detect and address suicidal ideation or self-harm expressions, and referral to crisis or behavioral health services.

Requires AI companions to notify users about non-human interactions at the start and every three hours during conversations.

Authorizes the attorney general to enforce the article by seeking injunctions and civil penalties against violators, with penalties contributing to a suicide prevention fund.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 3: Generative AI Training Report Pre-Publication Version 2025
document_name: Copyright Office Part 3 Generative AI Training Pre-Publication Version 2025
body:
Recommends allowing AI licensing markets to develop without government intervention; concludes that voluntary market-based solutions are preferable to compulsory licensing. Suggests considering extended collective licensing (ECL) for unworkable sectors.

Suggests that voluntary licensing agreements for AI training are preferable to compulsory licensing solutions, as market-based solutions can reduce transaction complexity and cost and avoid policy inertia.

Proposes extended collective licensing (ECL) as a less intrusive approach for sectors where voluntary licensing proves unworkable.

Discourages opt-out mechanisms but emphasizing consent for uses within statutory rights and acknowledges that Congress may consider exceptions allowing opt-outs.

Addresses antitrust concerns and encourages the Department of Justice to provide guidance.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act
document_name: H. R. 2613 Pipelines R&D Act
body:
Establishes a demonstration initiative and joint research program to advance AI-driven technologies for pipeline systems. Prioritizes AI models for monitoring and predicting pipeline integrity and lifecycle. Allocates funding for AI research in pipeline safety, efficiency, and resilience.

Establishes a demonstration initiative to fund advanced pipeline technologies via competitive merit reviews, focusing on AI-driven advancements in leak detection, sensor technologies, and machine learning for pipeline monitoring.

Directs funding of $45 million in 2026 and $50 million annually from 2027-2030 for relevant projects, with a sunset provision five years post-enactment.

Forms a Joint Research and Development Program involving the Department of Energy and other federal agencies to advance AI and machine learning models for pipeline systems, ensuring security and integrity.

Creates a National Pipeline Modernization Center to commercialize AI-assisted pipeline technologies, requiring competitive selection and location adjacent to existing infrastructure.

Mandates the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop standards supporting AI in pipeline safety, with a $2.5 million annual allocation from 2026-2030.

Aims to leverage and complement existing energy and pipeline safety infrastructure and programs through collaborative interagency efforts and non-federal funding matching.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
document_name: H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
body:
Establishes responsibilities for promoting resilient supply chains and emerging technologies, including AI, to strengthen U.S. national security. Requires Assistant Secretary to assess and respond to supply chain vulnerabilities. Encourages reduced reliance on certain foreign goods. Forms Supply Chain Resilience Working Group.

Assigns the Assistant Secretary of Commerce new responsibilities to promote the resilience of critical supply chains and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. 

Establishes a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group to assess and address vulnerabilities in critical supply chains and technologies.

Mandates consultations with various stakeholders, including government entities and international allies, to improve supply chain readiness and response to disruptions.

Encourages domestic production and reduced reliance on countries posing national security risks for critical goods and technologies, including AI.

Protects voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information from public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

Requires periodic assessments and strategy reports to Congress on supply chain resiliency and emerging technology impacts.

Sets a 10-year term for the act's provisions and requires a public comment period for certain designations and reports.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
document_name: S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
body:
Creates a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group to assess vulnerabilities in critical supply chains, emphasizing AI and emerging technologies. Tasks the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to lead initiatives enhancing supply chain resilience and promoting domestic AI technology production. Requires regular reporting to Congress.

Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote the resilience of critical supply chains and emerging technologies vital for U.S. national security, in consultation with key government figures.

Mandates the creation of a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group within 120 days, comprising multiple federal agencies, to evaluate and model critical supply chains, including those for emerging technologies such as AI.

Directs the Assistant Secretary to identify vulnerabilities, develop response strategies, and assess domestic and allied manufacturing capacities within one year.

Prohibits disclosure of voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information under FOIA, providing protection against unauthorized use.

Necessitates annual reporting to Congress detailing strategies and evaluations of supply chain resiliency, including the role of technologies such as AI.

Limits the Act’s funding to existing resources and imposes a 10-year termination period for the Act’s provisions.

category: 중국
title: [중국] 생성형 AI 서비스 안전 기본 요구사항
document_name: 《网络安全技术 生成式人工智能服务安全基本要求》GB/T 45654—2025/ 「사이버보안 기술: 생성형 인공지능 서비스 안전 기본 요구사항」
body:
●국가: 중국
●기관: 국가시장감독관리총국 / 국가표준화관리위원회
●문서종류: 국가표준
●문서명: 《网络安全技术 生成式人工智能服务安全基本要求》GB/T 45654—2025/ 「사이버보안 기술: 생성형 인공지능 서비스 안전 기본 요구사항」
●발표시점: 2025년 4월 25일
●시행시점: 2025년 11월 1일
●핵심내용중국의 생성형 AI 서비스 제공자가 준수해야 할 기본 보안·안전 요구사항을 정한 국가표준. 생성형 AI 서비스의 훈련데이터, 모델, 서비스 운영 단계에서 발생할 수 있는 안전위험을 관리하기 위한 기준이며, 특히 “여론 속성 또는 사회동원 능력”이 있는 생성형 AI 서비스의 등록관리·검측평가를 지원하기 위한 문서임.
5대 핵심 축:① 훈련데이터 안전: 데이터 출처별 사전·사후 안전평가, 위법·불량정보 5% 초과 데이터 출처 배제, 데이터 출처 다양성, 오픈소스·자가수집·상업 데이터의 출처 추적 및 사용자 입력정보 활용 시 동의 기록 요구② 데이터 내용·권리 보호: 훈련데이터 필터링, 지식재산권 관리전략·민원채널 구축, 개인·민감정보 사용 시 동의 또는 법적 근거 확보 요구③ 데이터 라벨링 안전: 라벨링 인력 교육·시험·역할분리, 기능성 라벨링과 안전성 라벨링 규칙 구분, 안전성 라벨링 데이터의 심사 및 격리저장 권고④ 모델 안전: 모델 생성내용 안전성을 주요 평가항목으로 삼고, 안전위험 테스트셋·안전성 라벨링 데이터 활용, 개발 프레임워크·코드 보안감사, 백도어 탐지, 생성내용 합격률 90% 이상, 위험 질의 거부응답 기준 적용⑤ 서비스 운영 안전조치: 적용 대상·용도 공개, 미성년자 보호, 서비스 한계·모델 개요·개인정보 수집 현황 공개, 사용자 입력정보의 훈련 활용 중지 옵션 제공, 신고·민원처리, 입력 모니터링, 서비스 연속성, 단말형 모델 보안 업데이트 요구

title: [미국] 미국 청소년을 위한 AI 교육 증진 행정명령 제14277조
document_name: Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth/ 「미국 청소년을 위한 인공지능 교육 증진」(EO 14277)
body:
●국가: 미국
●기관: 백악관
●문서종류: 대통령 행정명령
●문서명: Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth/ 「미국 청소년을 위한 인공지능 교육 증진」(EO 14277)
●발표시점: 2025년 4월 23일
●핵심내용미국 청소년의 AI 문해력과 AI 인재 기반을 강화하기 위한 행정명령.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
title: Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act
document_name: Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act April 2025
body:
Establishes the LEAD for Kids Act, mandating AI systems intended for children to assess risk levels and adhere to regulations. Forms a board to oversee compliance, issue guidelines, and ensure AI doesn't adversely impact children. Imposes penalties for noncompliance.

Establishes the LEAD for Kids Standards Board to govern AI systems affecting children in California.

Requires AI developers to classify systems as "covered products" with risk assessments ranging from prohibited to low risk.

Mandates developers to register covered products and submit risk assessments by July 1, 2028.

Prohibits AI use that adversely impacts children's health, safety, or privacy without informed consent.

Requires companion chatbots and systems that assess emotional states or collect biometric data to receive additional scrutiny.

Mandates independent audits based on risk level and public incident reporting for adverse impacts.

Obligates deployers to prevent unauthorized child access and adhere to usage requirements that do not increase system risk.

Prohibits retaliation against employees reporting violations.

Allows the Attorney General to enforce violations with penalties, and provides a private right of action for harmed children.

Creates the LEAD for Kids AI Fund to support these regulatory activities.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth
document_name: Advancing AI Education for American Youth EO
body:
Establishes a Task Force to implement AI education policy, promoting AI literacy and training for educators. Launches a Presidential AI Challenge and prioritizes AI in K-12 instruction through partnerships. Enhances teacher training and apprenticeships related to AI across various sectors.

Establishes a White House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Education to promote AI literacy and proficiency in the United States, chaired by the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

Requires the Task Force to coordinate Federal efforts on AI education, including organizing the Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge to encourage collaboration and innovation in AI.

Mandates public-private partnerships to provide K-12 AI education resources and calls for increased funding and resources to develop AI literacy.

Prioritizes AI-focused training for educators and the integration of AI tools in classrooms through grants and public-private partnerships.

Instructs the Secretary of Education and other Federal entities to support the use of AI in educational settings to improve outcomes.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to increase AI-related Registered Apprenticeships and promote AI skill development through the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA).

Encourages agencies to prioritize AI in educational grant programs.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Arkansas HB 1876 (Ownership of Model Training and Content Generated by a Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool 2025)
document_name: Arkansas HB 1876 (Ownership of Model Training and Content Generated by a Gen AI Tool 2025)
body:
Assigns ownership of AI-generated content to the input provider, unless infringing on existing intellectual property. Grants model training ownership to data providers, with conditions. Treats AI work done by employees under employer direction as employer-owned, adhering to specific criteria.

Amends Arkansas law to establish ownership of content and models generated through generative AI tools.

Grants ownership of AI-generated content to the person providing the input, conditional on the content not infringing on existing intellectual property.

Assigns ownership of trained AI models to the person providing the training data, provided the data is lawfully acquired and ownership rights have not been transferred by contract.

Specifies that if an employee uses generative AI as part of their employment duties, the employer owns the resulting content and trained models, provided the work is within the scope of employment and under employer control.

Clarifies that the section does not confer ownership over content that infringes on existing copyrights or intellectual property rights.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act
document_name: TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act 2025
body:
Requires development of AI weather models for accurate forecasts and disaster response. Promotes public-private partnerships and access to forecasting data. Authorizes funding and technical support while protecting national security and intellectual property. Encourages research and personnel retention strategies.

Mandates the improvement of weather, water, and wildfire forecast accuracy through artificial intelligence (AI) by federal agencies.

Promotes public-private partnerships to expedite AI adoption for mitigating environmental hazards.

Directs the development and curation of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets in consultation with various federal and research entities within four years.

Permits exploration of AI weather models for global, regional, and local forecasting.

Encourages the use of AI to enhance communication and public understanding of weather risks.

Mandates regular reporting to Congress on activities and potential risks of foreign access to U.S. weather data.

Allows the Under Secretary to enter partnerships, including co-investment strategies, for AI and environmental forecasting innovation.

Provides for public access to operational AI weather models, subject to national security and intellectual property considerations.

Authorizes appropriations to support these initiatives through fiscal years 2026 to 2030.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act
document_name: TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act
body:
Directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop AI-based weather models, improve forecasts, and analyze fire environments. Encourages public-private partnerships for AI innovation and workforce development. Ensures open access to non-sensitive data and models.

Directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to use artificial intelligence (AI) for adapting to extreme weather and wildfires.

Mandates the development of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets and AI weather models.

Requires NOAA to explore advanced AI applications to enhance weather forecasts and improve information delivery.

Instructs NOAA to provide technical assistance for AI weather model usage and establish best practices.

Directs the creation of an AI-driven program to predict, detect, and analyze wildfires.

Advocates for partnerships with private and academic entities for innovation in environmental forecasting.

Obligates NOAA to strengthen its workforce expertise in AI applications for weather forecasting.

Allows public access to data and code developed under the Act, with considerations for national security and intellectual property.

Provides guidance on minimizing environmental impacts when using AI technologies in these initiatives.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Health Tech Investment Act
document_name: Health Tech Investment Act
body:
Amends the Social Security Act to require that certain algorithm-based healthcare services receive appropriate Medicare payments. Defines standards for classifying these services, including costs, eligibility criteria, and duration under specific payment classifications, emphasizing the role of AI-driven technologies. Codifies payment policy for AI-related software services.

Amends the Social Security Act to classify algorithm-based healthcare services under Medicare’s new technology ambulatory payment classification.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to assign payment classifications based on cost data submitted by manufacturers, including diverse factors like invoice prices and overhead.

Specifies that algorithm-based services cannot be removed from their payment classification until adequate claims data is available, and mandates a minimum tenure of five years within the initial classification.

Adjusts the criteria for eligibility in new technology classifications to include distinct procedures that use AI, machine learning, or other software when used adjunctively with underlying services.

Defines algorithm-based healthcare services as those using FDA-approved AI or software for clinical guidance.

Mandates the payment system for software services as described in a 2022 Medicare rule, effective from January 2023.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act
document_name: H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act
body:
Establishes pilot projects to evaluate AI and other tech enhancements for cargo inspections at U.S. land ports. Requires assessment of technologies like AI, machine learning, and quantum sciences. Emphasizes privacy protection, cost-effectiveness, and performance. Prohibits additional appropriations.

Mandates the establishment of pilot projects by the Secretary of Homeland Security within one year to evaluate technologies for enhancing inspection processes at U.S. land ports of entry.

Requires testing of at least five types of nonintrusive inspection technology enhancements, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, to aid in detecting contraband and threats.

Ensures private sector involvement and emphasizes cost-effectiveness in technology selection.

Obligates safeguarding data privacy during inspections, with adherence to laws, data anonymization techniques, and regular audits.

Demands reports analyzing effectiveness, recommendations for widespread technology use, and cost breakdowns.

Includes necessary privacy and civil liberties impact assessments and reports before implementation and post-pilot.

Prohibits new appropriations, relying on existing resources for implementation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025
document_name: Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025
body:
Requires the Department of Homeland Security to report on vehicular terrorism threats, including potential misuse of AI in automotive technologies, and countermeasures. Evaluates threat assessments, technological innovations, and collaborative efforts with stakeholders while ensuring respect for individual rights.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security, alongside TSA and CISA, to submit a report on the prevention, deterrence, and response to vehicular terrorism.

Mandates the report to assess threats related to connected and autonomous vehicles and ADAS technologies, including AI-driven cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

Instructs inclusion of evaluations regarding DHS's engagement with public and private stakeholders, focusing on vehicle rental and ride-sharing platforms to prevent misuse.

Calls for recommendations on AI-enabled predictive analytics and vehicle immobilization technologies to detect and mitigate threats.

Demands coordination with enforcement agencies to address vehicular terrorism through intelligence sharing and joint training.

Ensures countermeasures and AI use respect privacy and civil liberties.

Obliges publication of an unclassified report summary for public access and annual briefings to Congress on developments and recommendations.

Defines “vehicular terrorism” as the use of vehicles to commit acts of terrorism.

category: 미국
title: [미국] 정부 내 AI의 효율적 조달 촉진 지침
document_name: M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government/ 「정부 내 AI의 효율적 조달 촉진」
body:
●국가: 미국
●기관: 백악관 예산관리국(OMB)
●문서종류: 연방 조달 지침 / OMB 메모
●문서명: M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government/ 「정부 내 AI의 효율적 조달 촉진」
●발표시점: 2025년 4월 3일
●핵심내용트럼프 행정부의 연방 AI 조달 지침으로, M-24-18을 대체. M-25-21과 함께 연방정부 AI 도입 가속 패키지의 조달 축을 구성함
5대 핵심 축:① 신속하고 경쟁적인 AI 조달② 미국 AI 시장과 공급업체 활용 확대③ 벤더 종속 방지 및 상호운용성 확보④ AI 조달 과정의 과도한 절차 부담 완화⑤ 공공 신뢰를 유지하기 위한 성능·보안·책임성 기준 적용

category: 미국
title: [미국] 혁신, 거버넌스 및 공공 신뢰를 통한 연방정부 AI 활용 가속화 지침
document_name: M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
body:
●국가: 미국
●기관: 백악관 예산관리국(OMB)
●문서종류: 연방기관 대상 지침 / OMB 메모
●문서명: M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
●발표시점: 2025년 4월 3일
●핵심내용트럼프 행정부의 EO 14179에 따라 연방정부의 AI 활용을 가속화하기 위한 OMB 지침. 기존 바이든 행정부의 OMB M-24-10을 폐지·대체하며, 연방기관이 AI를 보다 적극적으로 도입하되 시민권·시민자유·프라이버시 보호장치를 유지하도록 요구함.
5대 핵심 축:① AI 도입 가속: 연방기관이 불필요한 관료적 장벽을 제거하고, 공공서비스 개선·정부 효율성 제고를 위해 임무 중심 AI 활용 확대② 기관별 AI 전략 수립: CFO Act 기관은 180일 내 AI 전략을 수립·공개하고, AI 활용 사례·성숙도·데이터·인프라·인력·조달 계획 포함③ AI 거버넌스 체계: 각 기관은 Chief AI Officer를 지정하고, OMB는 Chief AI Officer Council을 통해 범정부 AI 활용을 조정④ 고영향 AI 위험관리: 권리·안전 등에 중대한 영향을 미치는 AI는 배포 전 테스트, 영향평가, 성능 모니터링 등 최소 위험관리 조치 적용⑤ 투명성·책임성: 기관별 AI 활용 목록, 준수계획, 고영향 AI 예외·면제 현황 등을 OMB에 보고하고 필요한 범위에서 공개

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Memorandum 25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government)
document_name: Memo 25-22  (Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government)
body:
Directs Federal agencies to acquire AI systems in such a way that enhances efficiency, competitive procurement, and mitigates vendor lock-in risks at the lowest cost to the taxpayer. Requires policy updates for privacy, intellectual property, and data management while also mandating interagency collaboration.

Promotes the competitive American AI marketplace by mandating federal agencies to procure AI systems that enhance efficiency and mission effectiveness while avoiding dependence on single vendors.

Ensures taxpayer dollars are safeguarded by tracking AI performance and managing risks as outlined in Executive Order 13960.

Directs agencies to update internal procedures within 270 days to align with this memorandum and OMB Memorandum M-25-21, requiring cross-functional teams for AI acquisitions and addressing intellectual property rights.

Mandates the protection of privacy and intellectual property, emphasizing compliance with federal law and policy.

Specifies that future AI contracts comply with new guidelines by establishing a clear timeline for implementation.

Excludes certain AI acquisitions and activities, such as national security systems and incidental AI use by contractors.

Requires GSA to develop AI acquisition guides within 100 days and establish a shared repository of best practices within 200 days.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Memorandum 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust)
document_name: Memo 25-21 (Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust)
body:
Instructs federal agencies to prioritize AI innovation, governance, and public trust while removing bureaucratic barriers. Requires development of an AI strategy, risk management practices for high-impact AI applications, and appointment of a Chief AI Officer.

Directs all Executive Branch departments and agencies to adopt AI by accelerating AI use and innovation while ensuring responsible deployment and governance.  

Requires removal of barriers to AI innovation, focusing on delivering value for taxpayers and improving public services.  

Instructs agencies to develop and share AI strategies, prioritize American AI products, and enhance workforce AI readiness.  

Directs agencies to designate a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) to oversee AI efforts and improve public accountability.  

Mandates implementation of minimum risk management practices for high-impact AI and provides guidance on AI governance, including creating AI impact assessments and ensuring human oversight.  

Encourages sharing and reusing of AI resources across federal agencies to prevent redundancy and foster collaboration.  

Implements public trust in AI use by requiring performance monitoring and mechanisms for public consultation and feedback.  

Excludes specific domains like national security systems from AI governance requirements.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
document_name: AI and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
body:
Expands NIST's functions to develop workforce frameworks for critical and emerging technologies, including a required artificial intelligence workforce framework. Requires periodic updates and reports to Congress, and mandates the inclusion of professional and nontraditional skill considerations through consultation with industry and government stakeholders in framework updates.

Expands the functions of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to include the development of workforce frameworks for critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Mandates the Director of NIST to develop, publish, and periodically update a workforce framework specifically for artificial intelligence within 540 days of the Act's enactment.

Requires the inclusion of competencies, workforce categories, and work roles relevant to AI in the workforce framework, highlighting career pathways for individuals with nontraditional backgrounds.

Obligates consultation with federal agencies, industry, and educational institutions to develop these frameworks.

Demands reports to Congress on the updates and practical applications of the frameworks, with a focus on increasing employer and educational adoption.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies;Editors' Picks
title: Advancing the Responsible Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government
document_name: OMB Requirements for AI Acquisition in Government
body:
Directs federal agencies to enhance AI acquisition policies by promoting a competitive AI market. Requires interagency collaboration, risk management for AI impacting rights and safety, innovation in procurement, and implement structures to govern and manage business processes.

Directs agencies to improve responsible AI acquisition, emphasizing cross-functional and interagency collaboration, risk management, and market competitiveness.

Requires agencies to update acquisition policies to reflect AI governance responsibilities and share AI acquisition information across the executive branch.

Mandates compliance with risk management practices for AI impacting rights or safety, including managing privacy, security, and discrimination risks.

Urges agencies to prevent vendor lock-in by prioritizing interoperability, transparency, and innovative acquisition practices.

Encourages the acquisition of generative AI for experimentation, while emphasizing transparency, risk mitigation, and environmental considerations.

Applies to all federal agencies, excluding the Intelligence Community and National Security Systems, and sets specific deadlines for compliance and reporting. 

Fosters a diverse AI marketplace by minimizing vendor lock-in and promoting competition through strategic contractual requirements.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies;Editors' Picks
title: Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of Artificial Intelligence
document_name: Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of Artificial Intelligence
body:
Mandates appointment of a Chief AI Officer within 60 days. Requires development of AI strategies. Imposes risk management requirements. Obligates annual AI use case inventory. Encourages removing innovation barriers while ensuring compliance with federal policies.

Requires federal agencies to appoint a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) within 60 days to enhance AI governance and innovation while managing risks, particularly those affecting public rights and safety.
Requires agencies to develop AI strategies to responsibly adopt AI, including generative AI, and to facilitate sharing and reuse of AI models, code, and data.

Imposes new requirements for agencies to manage AI-related risks, including following minimum risk management practices for AI impacting public rights and safety. Obligates agencies to annually inventory AI use cases, identifying those impacting rights and safety, and to report on associated risks and mitigation strategies. Encourages removing barriers to AI innovation related to IT infrastructure, data, and workforce while ensuring compliance with existing federal policies and risk management practices.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2025
document_name: Promoting US Leadership in Standards Act of 2025
body:
Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Department of State to promote U.S. participation in AI standards development. Establishes a web portal and pilot program to support hosting domestic AI standards meetings, with grants for eligible organizations.

Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), in coordination with the Secretary of State, to brief Congress on U.S. participation in AI standards development and opportunities for federal support.

Requires the establishment of a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international AI standards efforts and participation opportunities.

Establishes a pilot program to support AI standards meetings in the U.S. by awarding grants to eligible entities, specifying eligibility criteria for these grants, and defining allowable costs.

Requires annual briefings to Congress on the pilot program's effectiveness.

Directs the development of recommendations for permanent implementation of the program if deemed feasible within two years.
