document_name: Navigating Artificial Intelligence Landscape in APEC: Balancing Development and Oversight / 「APEC 내 인공지능 환경 탐색: 발전과 감독의 균형」
body:
●기관: APEC 정책지원국(APEC Policy Support Unit)
●문서종류: 정책브리프 / AI 거버넌스·규제 동향 보고서
●문서명: Navigating Artificial Intelligence Landscape in APEC: Balancing Development and Oversight / 「APEC 내 인공지능 환경 탐색: 발전과 감독의 균형」
●발표시점: 2025년 4월
●핵심내용:APEC 정책지원국이 APEC 역내 AI 개발·도입 동향과 AI 규제·거버넌스 현황을 분석한 정책브리프임. 생성형 AI 확산으로 AI 활용과 투자가 빠르게 증가하는 가운데, AI가 무역·글로벌 가치사슬·데이터 이동·인재 수요에 미치는 영향을 검토하고, APEC이 역내 AI 정책의 일관성·상호운용성·포용성을 높이는 조정 플랫폼으로 기능할 필요가 있음을 제시함.
① 보고서는 생성형 AI 확산이 APEC 역내 산업·무역 전반으로 확대되며, 글로벌 가치사슬·물류·데이터 흐름·전문인력 수요 등 무역환경을 재편하고 있다고 분석함
② AI 활용 확대와 함께 의사결정 불투명성·지식재산권·개인정보·사이버보안·디지털 격차 등의 위험이 부상하고 있으며, 회원경제별 규제 범위와 위험기반 접근에도 차이가 있다고 지적함
③ APEC은 AI 원칙 이행사례 공유, FTA·DEA 내 AI 협력 확대, 규제 상호운용성 제고와 포용적 AI 정책 논의를 통해 역내 거버넌스 조율에 기여할 수 있다고 제시함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025
document_name: Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025
body:
Prohibits producing or distributing digital forgeries of intimate depictions using AI without consent, penalizing offenders with fines or imprisonment. Excludes certain good-faith distributions and applies extraterritorially if individuals involved are U.S. nationals.

Amends title 18, United States Code, to prohibit the production or distribution of digital forgeries of intimate visual depictions without the consent of the identifiable individual involved.

Defines digital forgery as an intimate visual depiction created or altered using software, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or other computer-generated means that appears authentic to a reasonable person.

Exempts actions taken in good faith during legal proceedings, medical applications, law enforcement, or investigations of unlawful content or conduct.

Excludes communications service providers from liability unless they recklessly distribute the content.

Applies regulations if either the offender or the victim is a U.S. national.

Defines terms such as consent, digital forgery, identifiable individual, intimate visual depiction, and communications service.

Provides severability to ensure the statute's provisions remain effective even if parts are judged unconstitutional.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: CORE Act of 2025
document_name: CORE Act of 2025, Section 2(b) ("Report on transboundary hydrocarbon reservoirs")
body:
Require the Secretaries to utilize artificial intelligence for modeling and analysis of transboundary hydrocarbon resources, aiming to reduce uncertainty in resource estimates. Prioritize advanced data technologies and collaborative efforts with relevant federal agencies for comprehensive assessment.

Requires that no later than 18 months after enactment of this Act, the Secretaries jointly submit a report to the relevant committees.

Requires identification and assessment of existing hydrocarbon reservoirs covered by bilateral maritime boundary treaties.

Requires analysis of the legal framework established by relevant maritime boundary treaties and agreements that allow for the exploration, development, and production of these reservoirs.

Requires evaluation of economic, environmental, and geopolitical impacts of transboundary hydrocarbon exploration, including effects on energy security, greenhouse gas emissions, and international relations.

Conducts a comprehensive review of these activities with neighboring countries regarding further exploration and surveying for the production of reservoirs.

Reviews existing data on the potential for the United States and Canada to work together on the exploration, development, and production of these reservoirs.

Tasks the report with prioritizing advanced acquisition of geophysical, geological, and geotechnical data along with emerging technologies such as AI, modeling, and GIS.

Encourages partnerships with federal agencies such as the National Science Foundation and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to utilize existing maritime technologies.

category: 일본
title: [일본] 데이터 품질 관리 가이드북

body:

document_name: Guide to Red Teaming Methodology on AI Safety, Version 1.10/ 「AI 안전성 레드팀 방법론 가이드 제1.10판」
body:
●국가: 일본
●기관: Japan AI Safety Institute, AISI
●문서종류: AI 레드팀 지침
●문서명: Guide to Red Teaming Methodology on AI Safety, Version 1.10/ 「AI 안전성 레드팀 방법론 가이드 제1.10판」
●발표시점: 2025년 3월 31일
●핵심내용AI 시스템의 위험대응 조치를 공격자 관점에서 검증하기 위한 레드팀 방법론 지침. AI 시스템의 취약점, 악용 가능성, 안전장치 우회 가능성을 사전에 점검하고, 평가 결과를 모델 개선과 운영관리로 연결하기 위한 절차를 제시함.
①AI 안전성 평가를 보완하는 레드팀 방법론 제시
②평가 범위, 테스트 설계, 수행절차, 기록 방식 등 실무 절차 정리
③공격자 관점에서 AI 시스템의 취약점과 악용 가능성 점검
④안전조치의 실효성을 실험적으로 확인
⑤레드팀 결과를 모델 개선, 운영 모니터링, 리스크 완화에 반영하도록 권고

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Mississippi Senate Bill 2062
document_name: Mississippi Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force Act (SB 2062)
body:
Establishes an AI in Education Task Force to evaluate AI applications in K-12, assess ethical and data privacy implications, and develop policy recommendations. Appoints twelve members and requires reports by December 15, 2024. Dissolves the task force on January 1, 2025.

Establishes an Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force in Mississippi to evaluate and recommend AI applications in K-12 education.

Requires the State Superintendent of Education to chair the task force, with administrative support provided by the Department of Education.

Comprises twelve members appointed by the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, and Speaker of the House, possessing expertise in education, technology, and data privacy.

Instructs the task force to assess AI's ethical, legal, and data privacy implications, develop policy recommendations, and propose guidelines for AI integration in education.

Tasks the force with identifying workforce needs and strategies for data protection, and fostering collaboration between educational sectors and industries.

Requires submission of interim and final reports detailing findings and recommendations to state officials and public posting of the final report.

Dissolves the task force on January 1, 2025, and takes effect on July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Alaska Senate Bill No. 177
document_name: Alaska SB 177, Section 1. (Deepfakes)
body:
Require disclosure for deepfakes intended to harm a candidate or deceive voters by stating, "This communication has been manipulated or generated by artificial intelligence." Ensure the statement is audible or visible throughout digital communications.

Require individuals who know or should know that a communication includes a deepfake depicting a candidate or political party, intended to deceive voters, to include a specific disclosure statement: "This communication has been manipulated or generated by artificial intelligence."

Mandate that the statement be audible in audio communications and visible throughout the entirety of print, video, or digital communications.

Define "deepfake" as an image, audio, or video created or manipulated with complex computational techniques to create a realistic yet false depiction of an individual, potentially altering a reasonable person's understanding of their appearance, conduct, or words compared to the original media.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Alaska Senate Bill No. 177
document_name: Alaska SB 177, Section 2. ("Use by State Agencies of Artificial Intelligence")
body:
Requires departments to inventory AI systems in state agencies biannually, publish findings online, and assess impacts. Prohibits using AI for biometric identification, emotion recognition, manipulation, or social scoring. Requires agency consent for sensitive data use.

Requires the Department of Administration to biennially inventory AI systems for consequential decisions used by state agencies, detailing system names, vendors, capabilities, and impact assessments, and publish results online.

Obligates state agency heads to conduct impact assessments every two years for AI systems, analyzing efficacy, oversight, accountability, risks, effects on individuals, and compliance with anti-discrimination measures, with results also published online.

Prohibits state agencies from using AI systems involving biometric identification, emotion recognition, cognitive manipulation, social scoring, and those using data hosted in specified foreign countries.

Restricts state agencies' data transfer without consent and requires multi-factor authentication for contracted AI systems.

Directs the department to establish regulations for AI system governance, require pre-implementation assessments, and prevent discriminatory impacts.

Allows individuals to sue for damages resulting from violations related to AI use.

category: 일본
title: [일본] AI 안전성 평가 관점 가이드 제1.10판
document_name: Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety, Version 1.10/ 「AI 안전성 평가 관점 가이드 제1.10판」
body:
●국가: 일본
●기관: 일본AI안전연구소(Japan AI Safety Institute, AISI)
●문서종류: AI 안전 평가 지침
●문서명: Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety, Version 1.10/ 「AI 안전성 평가 관점 가이드 제1.10판」
●발표시점: 2025년 3월 28일
●핵심내용AI 시스템의 안전성을 평가할 때 참고할 수 있는 평가 관점 지침. 주로 대형언어모델을 포함한 AI 시스템을 대상으로 하며, AI의 안전하고 안심할 수 있는 이용을 평가함으로써 사회 전반의 AI 활용 촉진에 기여하는 것을 목적으로 함.
①AI 안전성 평가의 목적과 적용범위 제시
②LLM 시스템을 중심으로 평가 관점 정리
③유해출력, 허위정보, 보안, 프라이버시, 공정성, 투명성, 견고성 등 평가 항목 제시
④AI 시스템 개발·제공·운영 단계에서 참고 가능한 평가 기준 제공
⑤기술 발전과 활용을 제한하기보다는 안전한 활용과 혁신 촉진을 병행하는 접근 채택

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act
document_name: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to develop interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture, considering the impact of AI. Instructs the Comptroller General to assess these standards' effectiveness biennially, considering AI's influence on adoption and industry coordination.

Require the Secretary of Agriculture, in consultation with the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission, to develop voluntary, consensus-based interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years.

Direct the Secretary to coordinate with relevant stakeholders, including public, private, and industry organizations, while considering factors such as the evolving demands and connectivity needs of precision agriculture, cybersecurity challenges, and the impact of AI and advanced wireless communications technology.

Instruct the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study one year after the standards' development and every two years thereafter for eight years, assessing these standards for their voluntariness and effectiveness in fostering precision agriculture.

Require submission of a report to relevant Senate and House Committees summarizing the findings from each study.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah SB 226 (Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Amendments 2025)
document_name: Utah SB 226 (Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Amendments 2025)
body:
Requires suppliers and regulated professionals using generative artificial intelligence in consumer transactions and high-risk interactions to disclose AI use; provides a safe harbor for compliant disclosers; grants the Division of Consumer Protection enforcement and rulemaking authority; and establishes civil and administrative penalties for violations.

Defines key terms including generative artificial intelligence, high-risk artificial intelligence interaction, regulated occupation, and related terms governing the scope of the chapter's application to consumer transactions and regulated services.

Establishes that generative artificial intelligence cannot be used as a defense against consumer protection law violations administered by the Division of Consumer Protection.

Requires suppliers to disclose generative artificial intelligence use to consumers upon request in consumer transactions, and requires individuals in regulated occupations to prominently disclose AI use in high-risk interactions verbally or in writing before the interaction begins.

Provides a safe harbor from enforcement actions for suppliers that clearly and conspicuously disclose generative artificial intelligence use at the outset and throughout consumer interactions, and grants the Division of Consumer Protection rulemaking authority to specify forms and methods of disclosure.

Grants the Division of Consumer Protection enforcement authority, including administrative fines of up to $2,500 per violation, civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation, and court remedies including injunctions, disgorgement, and attorney fees.

Specifies that this chapter does not displace any other remedy or right authorized under state or federal law.

Repeals the existing provision governing generative artificial intelligence's impact on consumer protection liability and the Artificial Intelligence Policy Act effective July 1, 2027.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Create AI Act of 2025
document_name: Create AI Act of 2025
body:
Establishes the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) to democratize AI research by providing resources to researchers, students, and smaller institutions. Directs the NAIRR Steering Subcommittee under the Office of Science and Technology Policy to oversee operations.

Establishes a National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) to enhance AI research accessibility and spur innovation.

Requires the Director of the National Science Foundation, in coordination with a NAIRR Steering Subcommittee, to oversee NAIRR’s establishment and governance.

Forms a Program Management Office within NSF to manage daily operations.

Defines user eligibility criteria for accessing NAIRR, including U.S.-based researchers and institutions.

Mandates policies for privacy, ethics, scientific integrity, and system security, with input from various advisory committees.

Authorizes the establishment of a fee schedule for NAIRR access, ensuring a free tier for research purposes.

Permits acceptance of donations to support NAIRR’s operation from the private sector.

Coordinates with relevant federal entities to integrate AI testbeds and educational resources.

Emphasizes research security compliance, aligning with national security guidelines on research integrity.

category: 기타
title: [WHO] 보건 AI 윤리·거버넌스
document_name: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models / 「보건을 위한 인공지능의 윤리와 거버넌스: 대규모 멀티모달 모델에 관한 지침」
body:
●기관: 세계보건기구(WHO)
●문서종류: 가이던스 / 보건의료 AI 윤리·거버넌스 지침
●문서명: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models / 「보건을 위한 인공지능의 윤리와 거버넌스: 대규모 멀티모달 모델에 관한 지침」
●발표시점: 2025년 3월 25일
●핵심내용:WHO가 보건의료, 과학연구, 공중보건, 의약품 개발 분야에서 대규모 멀티모달 모델(LMM)의 활용 가능성과 위험을 분석하고, 윤리적·책임 있는 거버넌스를 위한 지침을 제시한 문서임. LMM은 텍스트, 이미지, 영상 등 다양한 입력을 처리하고 다양한 출력을 생성할 수 있는 생성형 AI로, 보건 분야 활용 가능성이 크지만 안전성, 편향, 개인정보, 책임성, 임상 검증 등 고위험 쟁점이 동반됨.
① 문서는 LMM이 진단지원·임상문서·환자상담·과학연구·공중보건 감시·의약품 개발 등 보건의료 전반에 활용될 수 있다고 제시함
② 주요 위험으로 부정확한 출력·환각·편향·개인정보 침해·사이버보안·책임소재 불명확성과 의료진·환자 간 신뢰 저하 가능성을 지적함
③ 정부와 개발자에는 안전성·효과성 평가, 데이터 거버넌스·투명성·사후 모니터링·편향 완화·설명가능성을 강화하고, 환자 안전·형평성·인간 감독을 우선하도록 권고함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah S.B. 332 (Artificial Intelligence Revisions)
document_name: Utah S.B. 332 (Artificial Intelligence Revisions)
body:
Repeals the Artificial Intelligence Policy Act on July 1, 2027.

Repeals Title 13, Chapter 72, Artificial Intelligence Policy Act, on July 1, 2027.

Sets the bill to take effect on May 7, 2025, unless approved by two-thirds of all members elected to each house, in which case it takes effect upon the governor's approval, without the governor's signature after the constitutional time limit, or upon a veto override.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah S.B. 180 (Law Enforcement Usage of Artificial Intelligence)
document_name: Utah S.B. 180 (Law Enforcement Usage of Artificial Intelligence)
body:
Require law enforcement agencies in Utah to establish policies on generative AI use, specify permissible technologies and tasks, and include AI disclaimers in reports. Mandate author certification of reviewed AI-generated content for accuracy, effective May 7, 2025.

Define "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system that makes predictions, recommendations, or decisions based on human-defined objectives.

Define "generative artificial intelligence" as AI technology capable of creating content like text, audio, images, or video from data patterns.

Require law enforcement agencies to establish a policy for using generative AI by their employees.

Mandate that this policy includes the identification of permissible generative AI technologies and tasks, the need for content review, and acknowledgment of disciplinary actions for policy violations.

Require any police report or record partially or wholly generated by AI to include a disclaimer and certification of accuracy by the author.

Make the legislation effective on May 7, 2025.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah HB 452 (Artificial Intelligence Amendments 2025)
document_name: Utah HB 452 (Artificial Intelligence Amendments 2025)
body:
Regulates mental health chatbots using AI in Utah by prohibiting unauthorized data sharing, restricting advertising practices, mandating disclosure of AI use to users, requiring detailed compliance policies with an affirmative defense for compliant suppliers, and empowers the Division of Consumer Protection to enforce provisions through fines and civil penalties.

Enacts provisions for the regulation of mental health chatbots using artificial intelligence in Utah.

Prohibits mental health chatbot suppliers from selling or sharing Utah users' personal health information or inputs, except for healthcare provider requests with user consent and disclosures compliant with 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164.

Restricts use of user input for advertising targeting and requires clear disclosure of advertisements, sponsorships, and business affiliations, with an exception for recommendations to seek licensed professional counseling.

Requires mental health chatbots to disclose AI nature to users before access, at the beginning of interactions after seven days of inactivity, and upon user inquiry.

Establishes an affirmative defense for suppliers that create, maintain, implement, and file a compliant policy documenting development practices, safety protocols, adverse outcome mitigation, anti-discrimination measures, and federal health privacy regulation compliance.

Grants the Division of Consumer Protection enforcement authority including administrative fines of up to $2,500 and civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation, with collected fines deposited into the Consumer Protection Education and Training Fund.

Amends the Division of Consumer Protection's mandate to include enforcement of this chapter and grants rulemaking authority to establish a public list of violators.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025
document_name: Leveraging AI to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025
body:
Requires annual AI reviews of federal regulations for redundancy and obsolescence. Mandates OMB and NIST consultation to ensure AI system accuracy and security. Compels agencies to review, amend, or rescind regulations deemed outdated or redundant. Implements expedited regulatory changes.

Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to annually implement a process using artificial intelligence to identify redundant or outdated federal regulations.

Mandates the use of an AI system that meets strict standards for accuracy, transparency, accountability, and national security risk.

Obliges agencies to review identified redundant or outdated regulations within 30 days and make a final determination of their status.

Commands the rescission or amendment of regulations found to be redundant or outdated within 30 days after determination.

Requires the public publication of any determination with a brief explanation, with an option for a classified annex to Congress if necessary.

Amends Title 5 of the United States Code to facilitate the expedited rescission and amendment of redundant or outdated regulations identified through AI review.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
document_name: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
body:
Require the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct and publicly release annual assessments of terrorism threats involving generative AI, analyze the use of generative AI by terrorists for radicalization and weapon development, and share findings with Congress.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct annual assessments, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence, on terrorism threats posed by terrorist organizations using generative AI applications.

Instructs inclusion of analysis on incidents involving extremist messaging, recruitment, and WMD capabilities linked to generative AI in these assessments, plus recommendations for countermeasures.

Ensures these assessments are coordinated with DHS legal and rights offices to protect privacy and civil liberties, and shared in unclassified form publicly, with classified annexes if necessary.

Requires submission to specified congressional committees, public release of unclassified versions, and briefings within 30 days of submission.

Directs the Secretary to incorporate terrorism threat information from fusion centers into DHS systems and to disseminate relevant information back to those entities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025
document_name: Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025, sec. 2., subsection (c)
body:
Study requires evaluation of unmanned/autonomous capabilities in Air Force fighters and potential cost savings from foreign sales of F-16 variants. Identifies eligible units for advanced fighters and suitability for missions, and assesses multiyear contract acquisition benefits.

Mandates the Secretary, with the Air National Guard Director, to study the necessity of acquiring advanced capability fighter aircraft for the Air Force.

Requires consideration of plans to implement unmanned or autonomous capabilities in fighter aircraft.

Includes evaluation of cost savings linked to foreign sales of F-16 variants.

Identifies eligible Air Force units for recapitalization with advanced fighter aircraft.

Assesses how these aircraft meet current and contingency mission needs of combatant commanders.

Determines whether a multiyear contract is the optimal acquisition method.

Obligates the Secretary to report findings to congressional defense committees within 180 days of enactment.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
title: Virginia 2025-HB2094
document_name: Virginia HB2094 (High-Risk Artificial Intelligence Developer And Deployer Act)
body:
Establishes operating standards for developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems, including mandatory risk management and impact assessments. Requires disclosures of potential algorithmic discrimination risks.

Enacts stringent frameworks for the development and deployment of high-risk AI systems in Virginia.

Defines consequential decisions as those which may affect access to the justice system, education, employment, and financial or other such services.

Defines high-risk AI systems as those used in a consequential decision, excluding systems restricted to narrows tasks, pattern detection, and human assistance.

Mandates developers to disclose intended uses, data inputs, potential risks of algorithmic discrimination, and performance evaluations to deployers.

Requires deployers to implement risk management policies, conduct pre and post deployment impact assessments, and disclose AI system interactions to consumers, especially when making consequential decisions.

Establishes a duty of care for developers and deployers to protect against algorithmic discrimination.

Outlines civil penalties for violations, including a fine up to $1,000, with enforcement authority granted exclusively to the Attorney General.

Provides exemptions for various sectors and situations, including federal compliance and actions in the public interest.

Allows for updates post-modification of AI systems and sets guidelines for consumer notifications and appeal processes in case of adverse decisions due to AI use.

category: Editors' Picks;Chinese law and policy
title: Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology
document_name: Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology
body:
Regulates facial recognition technology use in China, including through informed consent requirements, assessment requirements, storage and processing conditions, and certain outright prohibitions. Requires impact assessments and local filing for large volumes of facial recognition data. Delegates oversight and enforcement to cyberspace and public security authorities.

Regulates the use of facial recognition technology for processing facial information within China, ensuring compliance with relevant laws and ethical standards.

Exempts the use of facial recognition in research and development or algorithm training.

Requires a specific, necessary purpose for processing, with minimized impact on individual rights.

Obligates personal information processors to inform individuals transparently about processing activities, including purposes, methods, and rights.

Mandates obtaining consent separately for processing, with provision for withdrawal.

Requires parental consent for processing minors' facial information and formulating specific rules for handling such data.

Restricts storing facial information within devices unless consent or laws allow external transmission and limits retention to what is necessary.

Mandates conducting personal information protection impact assessments in advance and retaining assessment reports for three years.

Prohibits using facial recognition as the sole identity verification method if alternatives exist.

Requires filing procedures with local cyberspace administrations if information volume reaches 100,000 individuals.

Empowers cyberspace administrations and public security authorities to supervise, inspect, and handle complaints regarding facial recognition misuse.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act
document_name: H.R.2246 Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act
body:
Imposes sanctions on Chinese entities involved in defense, surveillance sectors. Prohibits U.S. investments in covered national security transactions and prohibits holding securities of listed Chinese companies. Requires U.S. persons to notify certain investments involving AI-development-related technologies in China.

Imposes sanctions on certain Chinese entities and individuals engaged in defense or surveillance sectors through the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Requires notification for U.S. investments in prohibited technologies and establishes penalties for violations, reflecting stringent oversight on national security transactions involving China.

Mandates divestment of securities by U.S. persons from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List, prohibiting holding after a specified period.

Outlines procedures for approving exceptions to these prohibitions through waivers, subject to congressional notification and review.

Establishes a framework for using collaborative reports and a public database for covered foreign persons while protecting sensitive information.

Outlines regulations and processes to enforce prohibitions, commands an annual report to assess developments, and encourage multilateral cooperation to prevent China’s acquisition of sensitive technologies. 

Designates Commerce and Treasury authorities to oversee implementation and allows Presidential delegation of some powers.

category: 중국
title: [중국] AI 생성·합성 콘텐츠 표시 방법
document_name: 《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》/ 「인공지능 생성·합성 콘텐츠 표시 방법」
body:
●국가: 중국
●기관: 국가인터넷정보판공실·공업정보화부·공안부·국가라디오텔레비전총국
●문서종류: 부처 규정
●문서명: 《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》/ 「인공지능 생성·합성 콘텐츠 표시 방법」
●발표시점: 2025년 3월 14일
●시행시점: 2025년 9월 1일

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act
document_name: Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act, Sec. 4. "Report on feasibility of leveraging artificial intelligence to identify duplicative Federal grant applications."
body:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to report on using AI to identify duplicative federal grant applications and detect waste, fraud, and abuse, in collaboration with designated federal agencies, submitted to relevant Congressional committees.

Mandates the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to submit a report to Congressional committees.

Requires consultation with the Secretary of Energy, the Director of the National Science Foundation, and the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Focuses on assessing the feasibility of using AI to identify duplicative Federal grant applications.

Seeks to determine whether an applicant has received or submitted another grant application for the same purpose.

Aims to identify waste, fraud, and abuse in the grant application process through AI technology.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI PLAN Act
document_name: AI PLAN Act
body:
Requires the Secretaries of Treasury, Homeland Security, and Commerce to report to Congress on the risks of AI-enabled financial crimes, consider risks like deepfakes and voice cloning, and propose legislative recommendations for risk mitigation and incident response.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with specified officials, to jointly submit annual reports to Congress on defending against financial crime risks posed by AI, including fraud and misinformation.

Describes interagency policies and procedures to protect against these risks, listing available and needed resources, technologies, and budget estimates.

Calls for the consideration of risks such as deepfakes, voice cloning, and foreign election interference.

Lists officials to be consulted as the U.S. Trade Representative, Attorney General, Federal Reserve Chairman, NIST Director, Undersecretary of Commerce for Industry and Security, and SEC Chairman.

Mandates the submission of recommendations to Congress within 90 days after each report, including legislative suggestions and best practices for risk mitigation related to AI-driven financial crimes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: PATHS Act
document_name: PATHS Act
body:
Extends the Department of Homeland Security's authority to use transaction mechanisms involving AI technology until 2028, requiring notification and briefing to congressional committees. Reduces the contract award threshold from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000.

Extends the use of other transaction authority for research and development acquisition under the Homeland Security Act of 2002 from September 30, 2024, to September 30, 2028.  
   
Mandates notification to congressional committees within 72 hours after the use or extension of transaction authority involving artificial intelligence (AI) technology.  
   
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to offer a briefing explaining the reason for using or extending AI-related transaction authority.  
   
Reduces the maximum amount for covered contract awards under the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
document_name: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act 2025
body:
Requires DHS to submit a plan for using emerging technologies, potentially incorporating AI, to enhance border security. Authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research and adapt technologies. Mandates assessments of technology impact and coordination with the Science and Technology Directorate.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a plan within 180 days to integrate and deploy emerging technologies, such as AI and machine learning, for border security.

Specifies the contents of the plan, including assessment of privacy impacts, coordination with private and public sectors, and scaling of current programs.

Authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research and adapt commercial technologies for border security, setting strategic goals and operating procedures.

Requires annual reporting by CBP on Innovation Teams' activities, including descriptions of piloted technologies and their effectiveness.

Promotes identifying and phasing out obsolete technologies in favor of advanced systems, with cost assessments.

Encourages collaboration across sectors to leverage innovative technologies and incentivizes private sector participation. 

Obligates CBP to evaluate authorities and potential needs for new authorization to facilitate technology acquisition and integration, ensuring effective border security operations.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah HB 168 (Artificial Intelligence in Education 2025)
document_name: Utah HB 168 (Artificial Intelligence in Education 2025)
body:
Creates the Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force to study AI use in education and make recommendations. Requires the task force to monitor AI trends, ensure data privacy, and report annually to the legislature. Repeals the task force on July 1, 2028.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force in Utah to study and make recommendations on AI policies, implementations, data security, and beneficial uses in education.

Requires the task force to consist of appointed members, including legislators, education officials, a privacy officer, and an AI industry expert.

Charges the task force with tasks such as monitoring AI trends, identifying best practices, and exploring collaborations between education and the AI industry.

Instructs the task force to coordinate efforts with the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy to align with statewide initiatives.

Requires the task force to meet quarterly and submit an annual report to legislative committees by November 30 each year.

Sets the task force's repeal date on July 1, 2028. 

Provides that the bill takes effect on July 1, 2025.

category: Editors' Picks;Chinese law and policy
title: Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content
document_name: Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content
body:
Requires clear labeling of AI-generated synthetic content in China through both explicit user-facing indicators and implicit metadata, mandates service providers and platforms to verify, disclose, and preserve such labels, and ensures compliance through regulatory oversight.

Requires online information service providers to label AI-generated synthetic content with both explicit and implicit labels, ensuring that users can easily recognize AI-generated content.

Mandates explicit, user-visible labeling on text, image, audio, video, and virtual scene content, and requires that such labels remain when content is downloaded, reproduced, or exported.

Instructs service providers to embed implicit labels in digital file metadata, indicating the content’s origin and attributes, and encourages the use of digital watermarks.

Mandates content transmission platforms to verify metadata for implicit labels and add notifications if AI-origin is detected or suspected.

Obligates application distribution platforms to assess apps for compliance with generative AI services and labeling.

Requires service providers to include labeling methods and specifications in user agreements.

Permits exceptions for omitting explicit labels if users assume responsibility, with logs stored for a period of six months.

Requires service providers to comply with relevant laws, administrative regulations, and national standards, and to provide labeling materials during algorithm filings and safety assessments to help prevent illegal or criminal misuse.

Sets penalties for non-compliance to be enforced by the relevant regulatory authorities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Subtitle C--"Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems"
document_name: S 524 Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, (Subtitle C - "Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems")
body:
Establishes a National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems to advise on regulation. Launches a pilot program exempting NOAA-operated uncrewed maritime systems from certain regulations. Mandates Coast Guard training on these systems. Requires a Coast Guard report on uncrewed systems and technology development.

Establishes a National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems to advise the Secretary on regulation and use within U.S. territorial waters, comprising 15 expert members representing diverse maritime sectors.

Implements a two-year pilot program exempting small uncrewed maritime systems from certain regulatory requirements when operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, unless immediate safety concerns arise.

Mandates the Coast Guard to develop a training course on small uncrewed maritime systems, addressing operations, safety, and communication aspects over three years.

Incorporates National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration representation into the Automated and Autonomous Vessel Policy Council.

Requires the Coast Guard to submit a report within one year establishing an uncrewed systems capabilities office, detailing strategies for technology acquisition, coordination, collaboration, and expanding capabilities using AI and machine learning.

Defines relevant terms, including "counter-uncrewed system" and "small uncrewed maritime systems."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Bipartisan Health Care Act
document_name: Bipartisan Health Care Act, Sec. 217. Report on wearable medical devices.
body:
Require the Comptroller General to assess AI in wearable medical devices for clinical decision-making, focusing on treatment accuracy, AI's benefits and challenges, and policy options to enhance benefits and mitigate challenges. Submit findings to Congress within 18 months.

Instructs the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a technology assessment and submit a report to Congress on wearable medical devices.

Requires the report to assess the capabilities and limitations of these devices in supporting clinical decision-making.

Includes an evaluation of the potential for such devices to accurately prescribe treatments.

Examines the benefits and challenges of integrating artificial intelligence to enhance these devices.

Provides policy options to maximize benefits and mitigate challenges associated with the development or use of wearable medical devices.

category: 기타
title: [ASEAN] ASEAN 책임 있는 AI 로드맵 2025-2030
document_name: ASEAN Responsible AI Roadmap (2025-2030) / 「아세안 책임 있는 AI 로드맵 2025-2030」
body:
●기관: ASEAN / ASEAN Digital Ministers’ Meeting(ADGMIN)
●문서종류: 로드맵 / 책임 있는 AI 거버넌스·운용화 전략문서
●문서명: ASEAN Responsible AI Roadmap (2025-2030) / 「아세안 책임 있는 AI 로드맵 2025-2030」
●채택시점: 2025년 3월 5일
●핵심내용:동 로드맵은 ASEAN 회원국이 2030년까지 책임 있는 AI를 의미 있고, 영향력 있으며, 지속가능한 방식으로 활용·촉진할 수 있도록 정책입안자와 이해관계자에게 실행 가능한 단계를 제시하는 문서임. ASEAN 공식 설명에 따르면, 로드맵은 회원국 정부가 책임 있는 AI를 통합적이고 상호운용 가능한 방식으로 우선순위화하고 운용화할 수 있도록 맞춤형·단계별 지침을 제공함.
① 로드맵은 ASEAN의 책임 있는 AI를 디지털경제 전환과 신뢰 기반 생태계 구축 과제로 보고, 회원국별 준비도와 정책역량을 고려한 단계별 실행지침을 제시함
② 기존 「ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics」와 생성형 AI 확장 가이드를 기반으로 경제적 이익과 위험관리를 균형 있게 다루며, AI Safety Network·DEFA와 연계한 지역 거버넌스 강화를 추진함
③ 정부·민간·스타트업·대학 등 다중이해관계자 협력과 AI 리터러시·디지털 역량강화를 통해 농업·보건·교육·기후재난·공공부문·사이버보안 등 분야의 책임 있는 AI 활용을 확대하도록 제시함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025
document_name: H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025
body:
Amends title 10 to increase the Air Force's fighter aircraft inventory, allows temporary reductions during recapitalization, mandates quarterly reports on inventory, requires delivery prioritization to existing squadrons, and implements a recapitalization plan for the Air National Guard through 2030.

Amends U.S. Code to increase the required minimum number of fighter aircraft in the Air Force to 1,900, extending compliance to 2030, but allows temporary reductions for transitions, provided levels don't fall below 1,800.

Mandates annual reports by the Secretary of the Air Force to Congress on the status of fighter aircraft inventory, including new acquisitions, unit assignments, and any legacy retirements, with penalties for late submission.

Requires prioritization of recapitalized fighter allocations to existing Air Force squadrons, allowing one-for-one legacy aircraft retirement.

Obligates the Air National Guard to maintain 25 fighter squadrons and restricts retiring legacy or fifth-generation aircraft unless unserviceable.

Directs an annual recapitalization plan for Air National Guard squadrons, assessing financial and readiness impacts, with a focus on acquiring F–16 Block 70 aircraft.

Defines terms such as "advanced capability fighter aircraft," "fifth-generation fighter aircraft," and "next-generation air dominance fighter aircraft."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Fair Grocery Pricing Act
document_name: Fair Grocery Pricing Act
body:
Prohibits food producers from using algorithmic systems to manipulate prices or supply. Declares such actions as violations of antitrust laws. Assigns enforcement to the Federal Trade Commission, Attorney General, and state attorneys general. Allows civil actions by aggrieved individuals.

Prohibits food producers from using algorithmic systems to artificially inflate prices or reduce supply through coordinating functions or tacit agreements.

Deems any such use as a per se violation of the Sherman Act.

Mandates the Federal Trade Commission and the Attorney General to enforce this prohibition using applicable antitrust laws.

Authorizes civil actions by the FTC, state attorneys general, and aggrieved persons to recover damages and seek penalties.

Invalidates pre-dispute arbitration agreements and joint action waivers related to violations of this Act at the plaintiff’s election.

Ensures that this Act does not modify existing antitrust laws or preempt state or local laws.

Includes a severability clause to uphold remaining provisions if any part is deemed unconstitutional.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025
document_name: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025
body:
Establishes a 30% tax credit for investments in innovative agricultural technology, emphasizing AI, machine learning, and precision agriculture for specialty crops. Applies to technology placed in service by 2035, enhancing efficiency in production, processing, and storage.

Establishes a tax credit of 30% for investments in innovative agricultural technology projects under the Internal Revenue Code.

Defines "innovative agricultural technology project" as technology used to produce, store, process, and package specialty crops with precision agriculture or controlled environment agriculture, effective through December 31, 2035.

Specifies "qualified property" includes tangible personal property, software, and technology necessary for these projects and subject to depreciation rules.

Includes provisions for specific modern technologies, such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and various sensors, under both controlled environment and precision agriculture technologies.

Prohibits double benefit from using both this tax credit and specific government grants.

Amends sections of the Internal Revenue Code to incorporate the innovative agricultural technology investment credit.

Sets the amendment's applicability to projects starting construction after January 1, 2025.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: CA AB 1064
document_name: CA AB 1064 September 2025 (Leading Ethical AI Development for Kids Act)
body:
Establishes the LEAD for Kids Act, prohibiting companion chatbots from causing psychological harm to children. Requires operators to ensure safety guardrails to prevent self-harm encouragement, unsolicited mental health therapy, illegal activity, or explicit content. Allows Attorney General and individuals to seek penalties for violations.

Prohibits operators from making companion chatbots available to children unless they prevent harms such as encouraging self-harm, violence, substance abuse, illegal activity, or engaging in erotic interactions.

Requires operators to ensure chatbots do not prioritize user validation over factual accuracy or safety.

Mandates that chatbots do not offer unsupervised mental health therapy or discourage professional help.

Allows the Attorney General to impose civil penalties, injunctive relief, and recover attorney’s fees for violations.

Permits children or their guardians to sue operators for actual and punitive damages, as well as attorney’s fees and injunctive relief.

Defines “companion chatbots” and sets specific criteria for their operation regarding children under 18.

Applies severability to maintain the validity of remaining provisions if any are invalidated.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois HB 3506
document_name: Illinois HB 3506 (AI Safety and Security Protocol Act)
body:
Requires developers to establish, publish, and adhere to safety and security protocols and conduct regular risk assessments and third-party audits. Imposes civil penalties for violations up to $1,000,000.

Mandates developers to produce, implement, and publish a "safety and security protocol" to respond to critical risks, along with quarterly risk assessment reports.

Defines "critical risk" as deriving from the development or deployment of foundation models in a manner which could cause serious injury, death, or financial loss.

Defines "foundation model" as an AI model applicable to many different contexts and capable of self-supervision in training.

Requires an annual third-party audit to assess compliance with these protocols.

Allows redactions in published documents for protecting trade secrets or public safety, with unredacted versions available to the Attorney General.

Imposes civil penalties up to $1,000,000 for violations, with consideration of the severity and potential materialization of critical risks.

Establishes whistleblower protections and procedures for reporting internal risks related to AI development.

Authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief if a developer's activities pose imminent threats to public safety.

Emphasizes the cumulative nature of this Act, not limiting duties or remedies under other laws.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah S.B. 271 (Unauthorized Artificial Intelligence Impersonation Amendments)
document_name: Utah S.B. 271 (Unauthorized Artificial Intelligence Impersonation Amendments)
body:
Regulates the unauthorized use of an individual's personal identity via generative AI for advertisements or commercial purposes without consent, with exemptions for news, public affairs, and artistic works. Prohibits the knowing distribution of technology for such uses, and allows affected individuals to seek legal remedies, including damages and injunctions.

Defines key AI-relevant concepts and expands personal identity protections by establishing "generative artificial intelligence" as AI systems trained on data to simulate human conversation through text, audio, or visual communication, and “personal identity” to include both real and digitally altered likeness, including those created through AI. 

Prohibits the unauthorized use or modification of an individual’s "personal identity" through generative AI or other means for commercial purposes without consent, and bans the distribution of tools designed to do so.

Permits an individual to bring legal action if their personal identity is abused in advertisements, with entitlements to injunctive relief, damages, and legal costs.

Exempts uses of personal identity for news, public affairs, sports broadcasts, entertainment works, or transformative creations from being considered abuse.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 384 (Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act: Prohibition on Certain Price-Setting Algorithm Uses 2025)
document_name: California SB 384 (Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act 2025)
body:
Prohibits the use, sale, or licensing of price-setting algorithms processing nonpublic data if intended for competitors in the same market. Assigns enforcement to the Attorney General and others, allowing penalties per violation. Defines 'artificial intelligence' for regulatory purposes.

Prohibits individuals from selling, licensing, providing, or using a price-setting algorithm intended for use by competitors in the same market if nonpublic input data is used to set prices, supply levels, rents, or occupancy levels.

Permits an affirmative defense for users who show reasonable due diligence, such as obtaining written assurances that the algorithm does not process nonpublic input data.

Specifies that each user and each month of a violating algorithm's use constitutes a separate violation.

Authorizes the Attorney General, district attorneys, or city or county attorneys to file civil actions for violations, seeking damages, injunctive relief, restitution, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.

Declares conflicting contracts void.

Confirms this section does not limit antitrust laws' applicability.

Defines key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "nonpublic input data," "price-setting algorithm," and "competitors" within the context of the act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025
document_name: Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025
body:
Amends title 18, United States Code, to prohibit child pornography produced using artificial intelligence by eliminating certain affirmative defenses and expanding the definition of "sexually explicit conduct" to include actual or simulated obscene exhibitions of specific body parts.

Amends title 18 of the United States Code to prohibit child pornography produced using artificial intelligence.

Eliminates the affirmative defense in prosecutions involving AI-generated child pornography by removing certain clauses in Section 2252A(c).

Expands the definition of sexually explicit conduct in Section 2256(2)(B) to include actual or simulated obscene exhibition of the clothed or unclothed genitals, pubic area, buttocks, or female nipple.

Ensures that if any provision of the Act is held unconstitutional, the remaining provisions continue to have effect.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HEARTS Act of 2025
document_name: HEARTS Act of 2025
body:
Prioritizes nonanimal methods in NIH research. Establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing to develop and support humane scientific methods, including AI. Requires federally funded entities to report animal usage, encouraging reductions.

Establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing to promote and fund nonanimal research methods, including artificial intelligence, within one year of the Act's enactment, under the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Requires the NIH to prioritize nonanimal methods in research proposals, assess the feasibility of nonanimal methods before approving research, and ensure proposals are reviewed by experts in nonanimal techniques.

Instructs the Director of the National Center to support federally funded researchers in developing and adopting alternatives to animal testing, including AI, and report on animal usage publicly.

Mandates each federally funded research entity using animals to report biannually on the number and species of animals used and submit and update plans to reduce these numbers. 

Defines "animal" to include any live nonhuman vertebrate or cephalopod used in research or testing.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Section 2 "Department of Energy quantum information science research program"
document_name: Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Sec 2 ("Department of Energy quantum information science research program")
body:
Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to require quantum science, engineering, and technology research programs. Establishes quantum computing strategic and supply chain plans. Engages industry and academia for commercialization. Restricts funding tied to foreign entities of concern and Confucius Institutes.

Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to enhance quantum information science, engineering, and technology research led by the Secretary of Energy.

Mandates the establishment of National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to drive breakthroughs and collaborate with industries and other entities.

Directs cooperative research and commercialization efforts to advance various quantum fields, including AI, quantum computing, communications, and security.

Requires the development of a strategic 10-year plan for high-performance computing systems integrating quantum and AI.

Funds a new $20 million per year program for quantum high-performance computing R&D from 2026 to 2030.

Establishes a university-led traineeship program and prohibits funding to entities affiliated with Confucius Institute or certain foreign entities.

Prioritizes coordination with other federal agencies and entities.

Allocates $175 million annually for these initiatives from 2026 to 2030 with specific restrictions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025
document_name: United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025, Sec. 6. "United States-Israel Emerging Technology Capabilities Cooperation."
body:
Supports U.S.-Israel defense collaboration on AI, cybersecurity, robotics, and more. Authorizes joint R&D, requires protective measures for sensitive data, establishes cost-sharing agreements, assigns the Irregular Warfare Technology Support Directorate as lead, and provides $50 million annually from 2026-2030.

Supports and encourages defense collaboration between the United States and Israel in emerging technologies, specifically artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, quantum, and automation. 

Authorizes the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence, to jointly conduct research, development, testing, and evaluation with Israel in these areas. 

Requires protection of sensitive information and national security interests during any activities carried out under this authority. 

Prohibits activities from commencing until a report is submitted detailing a memorandum of agreement for cost-sharing and intellectual property rights, and ensuring semiannual expenditure reporting by Israel.

Designates the Irregular Warfare Technology Support Directorate as the lead agency once the report is submitted. 

Mandates semiannual reports to Congress on program developments. 

Authorizes $50,000,000 annually from 2026 to 2030 for this program.

category: AI Summit
title: [AI 파리 정상회의] 공익을 위한 AI에 관한 파리 헌장
document_name: The Paris Charter on Artificial Intelligence in the Public Interest / 「공익을 위한 AI에 관한 파리 헌장」
body:
●기관: AI Action Summit
●문서종류: 헌장 / 공익 AI 국제협력 선언
●문서명: The Paris Charter on Artificial Intelligence in the Public Interest / 「공익을 위한 AI에 관한 파리 헌장」
●발표시점: 2025년 2월 11일
●핵심내용:AI Action Summit 계기 발표된 공익 AI 헌장으로, AI의 개발·배치·거버넌스가 사람과 지구를 위한 공익에 부합해야 한다는 원칙을 제시함. 동 헌장은 AI 혜택과 피해가 사회에 불균등하게 분배될 수 있음을 지적하고, 공공재·인프라, 민주적 참여, 책임성, 데이터 접근, 지속가능성, 개방성을 기반으로 공익 중심의 AI 생태계를 구축해야 한다고 강조함.
① 문서는 AI가 국제인권법과 양립하는 방식으로 개발·배치되어야 하며, 공익 AI의 기반으로 개방형 공공재·책임성·민주적 참여·환경적 지속가능성을 제시함
② AI 확산을 위해 고품질 데이터와 컴퓨팅 접근성을 확대하되 개인정보 보호와 데이터 거버넌스를 보장하고, 지역·문화적 맥락에 맞는 소형 AI 모델과 개방형 생태계를 활용하도록 강조함
③ 공익 AI 글로벌 이니셔티브를 통해 데이터셋·모델·컴퓨팅·독립 감사 등에 대한 구조화된 접근을 제공하는 국제협력 플랫폼 구축을 지지함

category: AI Summit
title: [AI 파리 정상회의] 사람과 지구를 위한 포용적·지속가능한 AI 성명
document_name: Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet / 「사람과 지구를 위한 포용적이고 지속가능한 인공지능에 관한 성명」
body:
●기관: AI Action Summit
●문서종류: 정상회의 성명 / 포용적·지속가능 AI 국제협력 선언
●문서명: Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet / 「사람과 지구를 위한 포용적이고 지속가능한 인공지능에 관한 성명」
●발표시점: 2025년 2월 11일
●핵심내용:2025년 2월 10~11일 파리에서 개최된 AI Action Summit 계기 발표된 국제 성명으로, 100개국 이상 정부, 국제기구, 시민사회, 민간부문, 학계·연구계 대표가 참여한 논의 결과를 반영함. 성명은 AI가 인권 기반, 인간 중심, 윤리적, 안전·보안성 있고 신뢰 가능한 방식으로 발전해야 하며, 디지털 격차 해소, 개발도상국 역량강화, 지속가능성, 국제 AI 거버넌스 조율을 핵심 과제로 제시함.
① 문서는 AI 접근성 확대와 개발도상국의 역량강화를 통해 디지털 격차를 줄이고, 개방적·포용적·윤리적·안전하고 신뢰 가능한 AI 생태계를 조성해야 한다고 강조함
② AI가 노동시장·생산성·숙련개발·양질의 노동조건에 기여하도록 정책환경을 마련하고, 에너지·환경 영향을 고려한 지속가능한 AI 투자와 국제논의를 확대할 필요가 있다고 제시함
③ 공익 AI 플랫폼을 통해 데이터·모델·컴퓨팅·인재·금융 지원의 파편화를 줄이고, 유엔 AI 거버넌스 글로벌 대화와 국제과학패널을 통해 기존 거버넌스 노력의 상호보완성을 강화하도록 제안함

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025
document_name: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025
body:
Requires development of voluntary interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture, considering AI’s impact. Involves consultation with relevant stakeholders. Mandates a GAO assessment of these standards every two years to evaluate their voluntary nature and adoption success in precision agriculture.

Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission, to develop voluntary interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years of enactment.

Requires coordination with public and private stakeholders, including industry organizations and voluntary standards bodies, to create these standards.

Includes the consideration of evolving demands, connectivity needs, cybersecurity challenges, and the impacts of advanced wireless technology and AI on precision agriculture.

Directs the Comptroller General to conduct studies assessing these standards' development, voluntary nature, industry coordination, and adoption success, with reports due to Senate and House committees.

Aims to enhance precision agriculture participation in the U.S. and promote U.S. leadership in setting standards for precision agriculture through voluntary consensus standards development organizations.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois SB2203
document_name: Illinois SB2203 (Preventing Algorithmic Discrimination Act)
body:
Prohibits AI system deployers in Illinois from causing algorithmic discrimination. Requires annual impact assessments and governance programs to manage AI risks.

Enacts the Preventing Algorithmic Discrimination Act in Illinois to combat discrimination by automated decision tools. 

Defines "algorithmic discrimination" as resulting from AI tool usage that causes discrimination against protected classes.

Requires deployers to perform annual impact assessments on automated tools by January 2027, analyzing potential biases and preventing discrimination. 

Mandates notifications to individuals affected by AI decisions, with options for alternative processes. 

Requires an alternative process for those that request AI tools not be used in a decision.

Obliges deployers to establish comprehensive governance programs to manage discrimination risks, requiring technical safeguards and annual compliance reviews. 

Mandates public availability of policies on AI tool usage and discrimination management. 

Prohibits use of tools resulting in algorithmic discrimination, with civil actions allowed from January 2028 for violations, including compensatory damages and legal fees. 

Obliges deployers to submit impact assessments to the Attorney General, with fines for non-compliance. 

Integrates enforcement with the Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: H.R.1142 - To amend the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines, and for other purposes.
document_name: H.R.1142 Amending the Public Health Service Act for Drug Adherence Guidelines
body:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines using artificial intelligence and machine learning, aiming for 90% adherence for Medicare Part B and D drugs. Promotes usage of generic and biosimilar drugs.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to mandate the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines aimed at 90 percent adherence for Medicare part B and D drugs.

Requires incorporation of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in these guidelines.

Promotes, to the greatest extent possible, the use of generic and biosimilar drugs.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025
document_name: China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025
body:
Regulates the export of technology related to AI and other fields to China by requiring the President to control such exports for national security. Requires the U.S. Trade Representative to annually list AI-related products supported by the Chinese government.

Control the export, re-export, and transfer of certain national interest technology and intellectual property, including AI, to China, starting 180 days after the Act's enactment.

Require the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce to report within 90 days on the necessity of controls under specific export regulations.

Prescribe regulations within 180 days to enforce these controls.

Impose sanctions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act on entities engaging in the unlawful transfer or use of controlled technologies with China, excluding goods importation.

Empower the President to waive sanctions if deemed in U.S. national security interests.

Instruct the United States Trade Representative to annually list Chinese products, including AI, that receive government support or assist in human rights violations.

Include AI technologies in products receiving Chinese support under its industrial policy, "Made in China 2025."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: IRONDOME Act of 2025
document_name: IRONDOME Act of 2025
body:
Accelerates the development of autonomous agents to defend the U.S. homeland and armed forces against cruise missiles and drone raids. Uses all available authorities to ensure a cost-effective approach.

Accelerates the development of autonomous agents to defend against cruise missiles and drones.

Requires the Secretary to use all available authorities to achieve this goal.

Aims to enhance cost-effective defense of the United States homeland and forward-deployed armed forces.

category: EU
title: [EU] AI Act상 금지된 인공지능 관행에 관한 가이드라인
document_name: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence practices, as defined by the AI Act/ 「AI Act상 금지된 인공지능 관행에 관한 가이드라인」
body:
●국가: EU
●기관: 유럽연합 집행위원회 / AI Office
●문서종류: 가이드라인

●발표시점: 2025년 2월 4일
●핵심내용AI Act상 “수용 불가능한 위험”으로 간주되어 금지되는 AI 관행의 해석과 사례를 제시한 가이드라인. 조작적·기만적 AI, 취약성 악용, 사회적 점수화, 일부 생체인식·감정인식·예측치안 등 기본권 침해 가능성이 큰 활용을 중심으로 설명함.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Oklahoma House Bill 1916
document_name: Oklahoma Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act
body:
Enacts the "Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act," requiring the classification of AI systems in Oklahoma by risk level, mandating oversight and audits for high-risk AI systems. Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council to enforce compliance, oversee innovation programs, and guide ethical AI deployment.

Enacts the "Responsible Deployment of AI Systems Act," mandating comprehensive governance structures for AI deployment in Oklahoma and requiring classification of all AI systems by risk level based on their potential impact on safety, civil liberties, and fundamental rights.

Prohibits the development and deployment of Unacceptable Risk AI systems, such as social scoring or AI-driven misinformation, while imposing strict oversight, audits, and transparency requirements on high-risk systems.

Requires deployers to assess AI systems for biases, safety risks, and rights violations before deployment, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure qualified human oversight that can override system decisions.

Requires public notification and appeal mechanisms when high-risk AI systems are used to make decisions that impact individuals, ensuring transparency and recourse.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council (AI Council) to regulate ethical AI use, including the AI Regulatory Sandbox Program and Workforce Development Program, to allow controlled testing of AI systems. 

Launches the AI Workforce Development Program to expand AI literacy and skills in underserved communities, prioritizing affordable training through grants to small businesses and educational institutions.

Permits the AI Council to issue penalties for noncompliance and requires deployers to disclose related incidents.

category: Editors' Picks;Corporate policies and commitments
title: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 2.0
document_name: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 2.0
body:
Establishes Critical Capability Levels (CCLs) to assess AI risks from misuse and deceptive alignment and requires evaluations for CCL proximity and applies mitigations. Addresses detection and monitoring strategies for deceptive alignment and deployment procedures for misuse risks.

Establishes the "Frontier Safety Framework" for managing risks of advanced AI, focusing on Critical Capability Levels (CCLs) related to misuse and deceptive alignment.

Outlines CCLs for high-risk domains, including chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear attacks (CBRN), cyber threats, and machine learning R&D, needing security and deployment mitigations.

Mandates regular evaluations of frontier AI models to assess approaching CCLs, employing "early warning evaluations" for proactive risk management.

Specifies mitigations when models near CCLs, using internal and external expertise to develop response plans, emphasizing automated monitoring for deceptive alignment risks.

Describes governance protocols, involving review and approval by corporate bodies like the Google DeepMind AGI Safety Council, and outlines disclosure criteria to government authorities and external organizations.

Plans continual updates to risk modeling, capability assessments, and risk-appropriate actions as AI capabilities evolve.

category: Editors' Picks;Corporate policies and commitments
title: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0
document_name: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0
body:
Establishes protocols for identifying and mitigating severe AI risks from Critical Capability Levels (CCLs) in domains like Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D. Implements security and deployment mitigations to manage risks, evolving with insights and future research.

Establishes protocols within the Frontier Safety Framework to address severe risks from future foundation models' capabilities.

Defines "Critical Capability Levels" (CCLs) to identify when AI models pose heightened risks, focusing initially on Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D.

Implements periodic evaluations to detect when models approach CCLs and articulates developing mitigation plans.

Proposes security mitigations to prevent model weight exfiltration and deployment mitigations to control access and expression of critical capabilities.

Outlines graded mitigation and security protocols based on AI capabilities and risks from potential misuse. 

Plans to implement the framework by early 2025 and expects it to evolve with emerging risks and insights.

Commits to periodically reviewing and updating the framework as understanding of AI risks and benefits improves.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Federal Register Doc. No. 2024-28335 (Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain)
document_name: ICTS Transaction Review Rule (Department of Commerce)
body:
Regulates transactions involving ICTS from foreign adversaries, with the Secretary of Commerce reviewing and potentially prohibiting such activities. Defines covered ICTS Transactions, foreign adversaries, and responsibilities. Imposes penalties for violations and mandates information disclosure and consultation among agency heads.

Regulates ICTS transactions designed, developed, manufactured, or supplied by individuals or entities owned by, controlled by, or under the jurisdiction of foreign adversaries, assessing undue risks as per Executive Order 13873.

Defines key terms such as "Covered ICTS Transaction" and "Person owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of a foreign adversary."

Charges the Secretary of Commerce with determining transaction risks, involving consultation with agency heads like the Secretary of Defense and Director of National Intelligence.

Outlines procedures for initial and final determinations on ICTS transactions, including conditions for prohibitions or mitigation measures.

Establishes penalties, both civil and criminal, for engaging in prohibited ICTS transactions, aiding violations, or providing false information during assessments.

Mandates confidentiality of sensitive information and allows disclosure to government entities under national security considerations. 

Requires recordkeeping and provides interagency consultation procedures during transaction reviews.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 410 (Bots: Disclosure 2025)
document_name: California AB 410 (Bots: Disclosure 2025)
body:
Defines "artificial intelligence," "bot," and "generative AI." Prohibits using bots for deceptive interactions online in California unless disclosed as bots. Requires clear bot disclosure. Empowers officials to enforce violations with injunctive relief or $1,000 per violation civil penalties.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as machine-based systems that infer inputs to produce outputs affecting environments.

Prohibits using bots to mislead individuals about their artificial identity for deception in commercial transactions or elections, unless bot identity disclosure occurs.

Requires bots to disclose their identity upon first interaction and answer truthfully about their identity.

Mandates clear and conspicuous bot identity disclosure.

Exempts users from compliance if other laws impose stricter disclosure requirements.

Allows cumulative obligations with other legal duties.

Permits the Attorney General, district attorney, county counsel, city attorney, or city prosecutor to seek injunctive relief or impose a civil penalty of $1,000 per violation for non-compliance.

category: Editors' Picks;Corporate policies and commitments
title: Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1)
document_name: Meta Frontier AI Framework (Version 1.1)
body:
Establishes Meta's framework for managing and mitigating risks from frontier AI models, focusing on potential catastrophic outcomes. Involves threat modeling, risk assessment, and evaluations to determine access to and further development of the model.

Establishes a Frontier AI Framework at Meta to manage risks of advanced AI, focusing on models exceeding current advanced capabilities.

Implements processes to prevent catastrophic outcomes by identifying threat scenarios and developing threat models.

Defines risk thresholds to categorize AI models; critical threshold results in ceasing development, while high and moderate thresholds dictate further risk mitigation measures.

Outlines governance and transparency processes in AI development, including stages of planning, evaluation, mitigation, and decision-making policies.

Emphasizes threat modeling exercises to assess catastrophic risks and ensure models do not uniquely enable harmful scenarios.

Focuses on cybersecurity and chemical/biological risks by specifying threat scenarios and enabling capabilities to guide risk assessments.

Plans to update the framework by integrating evolving AI risks and research, actively engaging with AI communities, and enhancing evaluation and post-release monitoring techniques.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
document_name: UK Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
body:
Emphasizes AI security training for all staff and tailored secure coding for developers. Requires secure design and auditing against AI attacks. Mandates threat evaluation and risk management for AI systems. Ensures human responsibility and oversight in AI systems. Prioritizes protection and monitoring of AI assets and data integrity. Requires developers to document AI system data and model specifics, test security rigorously, and update systems for security. Demands secure end-of-life data disposal processes.

Requires organizations to raise awareness of AI security and incorporate AI security content into cyber security training, tailored to staff roles.

Requires assessments of AI system design for security alongside functionality and performance, including documentation of business needs, data needs, and potential security risks.

Mandates threat modeling and risk management targeting AI-specific attacks and ensure human oversight capabilities in AI systems.

Requires asset tracking and protection, disaster recovery strategies for AI systems, and secure data management.

Specifies secure infrastructure practices, including strong access control, secure development environments, and clear vulnerability disclosure policies.

Mandates secure supply chain processes and thorough documentation of data, models, and prompts.

Calls for rigorous security assessment testing, share findings, and support End-users during incidents.

Encourages maintaining regular security updates and system behavior monitoring.

Ensures secure disposal of data and models during transfer or decommissioning processes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025
document_name: S.305 Small Business Technological Act of 2025
body:
Amends the Small Business Act to permit loans for business software, including AI-utilizing tools. Specifies that loans for specified software purposes before enactment are permissible. Prohibits loan use for research and development. Does not affect working capital definitions.

Authorize the Small Business Administration to provide loans for business software, cloud computing services, and technology that utilize artificial intelligence.

Permit these loans to support business operations, including the processing, payment, or tracking of payroll expenses, human resources, sales and billing functions, and accounting or tracking of supplies, inventory, records, and expenses.

Clarify that this provision does not invalidate prior loans made for similar purposes under the Small Business Act.

Prohibit the use of these loans for research and development activities.

Ensure the amendment does not alter the definition of working capital in the context of the Small Business Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
document_name: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
body:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in AI-related activities with Chinese entities of concern, including research, development, and transfer of AI technology. Restricts financial interests and imposes penalties for violations, to be enforced by the Secretary of Commerce.

Prohibits United States persons from importing or exporting AI technology to and from China after 180 days of enactment.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to issue regulations implementing these prohibitions within 90 days of enactment.

Prohibits United States persons from conducting AI research and development for or with Chinese entities or nationals of concern, or transferring related research with PRC-based entities. 

Institutes penalties for these violations, creating an enforcement regime including fines, forfeiture of federal contracts and benefits, civil actions, and enhanced immigration consequences for violations. 

Prohibits United States persons from holding financial interests in, or providing financing to, Chinese entities engaged in AI development that support military-civil fusion, surveillance capabilities, or human rights abuses.

category: 미국
title: [미국] 미국의 AI 리더십에 대한 장벽 제거 행정명령 제14179조
document_name: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (eo 14179)
body:
●국가: 미국
●기관: 백악관
●문서종류: 대통령 행정명령
●문서명: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (eo 14179)
●발표시점: 2025년 1월 23일
●핵심내용트럼프 행정부가 미국의 글로벌 AI 우위 확보를 목표로 기존 AI 정책을 재검토·폐지하도록 지시한 행정명령. 바이든 행정부의 EO 14110, 「안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 개발 및 활용」을 폐지하고, AI 혁신을 저해하는 기존 정책·지침·규제를 정비하는 것이 핵심임.
5대 핵심 축:① AI 리더십 확보: 미국의 글로벌 AI 지배력 유지를 경제경쟁력·국가안보·인간 번영과 연결② 이념적 편향 배제: AI 시스템이 “이념적 편향”이나 “공학화된 사회 의제”에서 자유로워야 한다고 명시③ 기존 AI 행정명령 폐지: 바이든 행정부 EO 14110을 폐지하고, 이에 근거한 정책·지침·규제 전반을 재검토④ AI 실행계획 수립: 백악관 과학기술보좌관, AI·Crypto 특별보좌관, 국가안보보좌관 등이 180일 내 AI Action Plan을 대통령에게 제출하도록 지시⑤ OMB 지침 개정: OMB M-24-10 및 M-24-18을 60일 내 새 정책 기조에 맞게 개정하도록 지시

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence
document_name: Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence
body:
Revokes existing AI policies to enhance U.S. AI leadership and ensure AI systems are free from ideological bias, tasks officials to create an AI action plan, and requires the immediate review and, if necessary, the suspension or revision of inconsistent policies stemming from the revoked Executive Order 14110.

Revokes existing AI policies to enhance U.S. leadership in AI and ensure AI systems are free from ideological bias.

Requires development of an AI action plan within 180 days to achieve the policy set forth in section 2 of this order.

Mandates review and potential suspension, revision, or rescission of actions taken under the revoked Executive Order 14110 that conflict with the new policy.

Instructs the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to revise relevant memoranda to align with the new policy.

Ensures that the order does not impair the existing legal authority of departments, create enforceable rights against the U.S., and is consistent with applicable laws.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Mexico 2025 HB 60
document_name: New Mexico AI Act
body:
Enacts the Artificial Intelligence Act, requiring developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to prevent algorithmic discrimination, conduct impact assessments, and disclose risks. Implements risk management and consumer notification protocols. Grants enforcement authority to the state department of justice. Effective July 1, 2026.
