Enacts the Artificial Intelligence Act to regulate the use of AI in New Mexico, focusing on high-risk AI systems that make consequential decisions.  

Requires developers to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination and disclose known risks to recipients and the state.  

Mandates impact assessments for deployers, updating them annually or upon modification of AI systems.  

Obliges deployers to notify consumers of AI's role in consequential decisions and provide appeal opportunities for adverse outcomes.  

Exempts trade secrets from mandatory disclosure, but requires consumer notification when information is withheld.  

Confers enforcement authority to the state department of justice, allowing consumer civil actions for violations.  

Sets the effective date for July 1, 2026, with rulemaking by the state department of justice due by January 1, 2027.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies;Editors' Picks
title: Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
document_name: Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (EO 14110)
body:
Directs the federal government to ensure the safety and security of AI systems and take action to protect Americans from their potential risks. Prescribes measures to improve American innovation, competition, and leadership in AI while preserving privacy, mitigating algorithmic discrimination, and addressing labor disruptions. Calls for further responsible deployment of AI in federal government and consumer-facing industries.

Requires federal government to develop and apply standards to ensure the safety and security of AI systems and minimize their risks, including biological risks, cybersecurity risks, and deceptive content risks.

Orders the development of a National Security Memorandum that directs further actions on AI and security.

Directs federal government to support privacy-preserving research and technologies and develop guidance on the collection and usage of commercially available information by federal agencies.

Instructs federal government to prevent algorithmic discrimination by developing guidance and best practices in order to ensure fairness.

Calls for federal government to support the safe, responsible deployment of AI in healthcare, transportation, education, and communications networks.

Requires a report on AI's potential labor-market impacts and the identification of options for strengthening federal support for workers facing labor disruptions

Urges federal government to facilitate the immigration of AI talent to the U.S., catalyze AI research and innovation through a pilot of the National AI Research Resource, and promote competition in the AI ecosystem by providing resources to small businesses.

Directs federal government to maintain U.S. leadership in global AI efforts by expanding multilateral engagements, implementing international standards, and developing guidelines to secure critical infrastructure.

Calls for the advancement of federal government use of AI through the issuance of guidance for agency use of AI, support for agency acquisition of AI products/services, and authorization of rapid hiring of AI professionals.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Massachusetts House Docket 4053 (2025)
document_name: Massachusetts HD 4053 (protecting consumers in interactions with AI systems)
body:
Establishes consumer protections against AI-induced discrimination. Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to document, assess, and mitigate algorithmic discrimination risks, and mandates notification to consumers about AI-influenced decisions.

Amends state law to introduce Chapter 93M, mandating consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence (AI) systems.

Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination and disclose foreseeable risks.

Defines "high-risk AI systems" as those influencing consequential decisions in areas like education, employment, and healthcare.

Mandates developers to provide detailed documentation about AI system data usage, limitations, and discrimination mitigation measures.

Obligates deployers to establish risk management policies aligned with recognized standards, and perform annual impact assessments.

Demands transparency from deployers by notifying consumers before consequential decisions are made using high-risk AI systems, and offering appeal opportunities for adverse decisions.

Empowers the attorney general with exclusive enforcement authority, classifying violations as unfair trade practices.

Allows attorney general to create rules for implementing these requirements, ensuring alignment with national standards.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025, Section 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership."
document_name: Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025 (Sec. 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership.")
body:
Establishes a pilot program for new wildfire technology, prioritizing AI, that connects private entities with federal agencies for testing. Requires annual reports on technology tested, costs, and outreach. Encourages emerging technologies for wildfire mitigation. Expires in seven years.

Establishes a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire technologies within 60 days of enactment.

Requires coordination among the Secretaries of Agriculture and Interior and covered agencies to identify technology priority areas like AI, quantum sensing, and augmented reality for wildfire prevention and mitigation.

Prioritizes covered entities with emerging technologies that address identified issues for participation in the pilot program.

Mandates real-time testing and on-the-ground coordination between selected entities and covered agencies.

Requires public outreach to invite applications from entities for technology testing and demonstration in key priority areas.

Obligates annual reporting to appropriate committees, detailing participating entities, tested technologies, cost estimates, and outreach efforts.

Sets the program's expiration at 7 years after enactment, with annual assessments and recommendations to foster the adoption of promising technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025, Section 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies"
document_name: Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025 (Sec. 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies.")
body:
Requires study on AI feasibility and data needs for wildland fire predictive modeling. Analyzes computing requirements to enhance modeling accuracy and speed. Reviews AI's potential use in predictive models. Submits results to Congress and public within one year.

Require the Secretaries to conduct a study on modernizing wildfire response technologies.

Include in the study necessary improvements to radio communications systems and infrastructure during wildland fire or prescribed fire operations, assessing the quality, reliability, failure impacts, and improvement options.

Assess real-time or near-real-time situational awareness tools for operational firefighters, ensuring interoperability and evaluating additional remote sensing and mapping capabilities.

Conduct a cost analysis of commercially available systems versus internally developed systems.

Analyze wildland fire predictive modeling, focusing on data requirements, computing needs, and the feasibility of using artificial intelligence for more accurate predictions.

Require the submission and public availability of the study results within one year of the Act's enactment to congressional committees and the public.

category: Editors' Picks
title: Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141)
document_name: Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141)
body:
Requires federal agencies to identify, solicit proposals for, and lease federal lands suitable for AI infrastructure and related clean energy projects. Requires the Secretary of State to develop a plan to coordinate AI infrastructure development with U.S. allies and partners, including workforce development.

Requires federal agencies to identify, solicit proposals for, and lease federal lands suitable for AI data centers and related clean energy projects, with the aim of full-capacity operation by the end of 2027.

Emphasizes high labor standards and community collaboration, among other factors, in the selection of sites for projects to account for community health, public safety, and ecological risks and harms.

Mandates cybersecurity, AI model evaluation, supply-chain protection, and other requirements for AI infrastructure developed pursuant to the executive order.  

Directs the Secretary of Energy to facilitate grid interconnection for AI infrastructure developed pursuant to the executive order. 

Calls for an expedited permitting processing for federal sites hosting AI infrastructure and related clean energy projects.  

Directs relevant agencies to take additional enumerated measures to expedite permitting and power procurement for AI infrastructure nationwide.

Requires the Secretary of State to develop a plan for robust engagement with allies on global AI infrastructure development, which includes exchanging best practices for workforce development and ensuring security and resilience in international supply chains.

category: 영국
title: [영국] AI 기회 행동계획: 정부 답변
document_name: AI Opportunities Action Plan: Government Response/ 「AI 기회 행동계획: 정부 답변」
body:
●국가: 영국
●기관: DSIT
●문서종류: 국가 실행계획 / 정부 답변서
●문서명: AI Opportunities Action Plan: Government Response/ 「AI 기회 행동계획: 정부 답변」
●발표시점: 2025년 1월 13일
●핵심내용영국 정부가 AI를 성장, 생산성, 공공서비스 혁신의 핵심 동력으로 삼기 위해 발표한 실행계획. 정부는 이 문서를 “영국을 AI 초강국으로 만들기 위한 계획”으로 규정하며, 컴퓨팅 인프라, AI Growth Zones, 공공부문 AI 도입, 인재·데이터 기반, 규제환경 개선을 종합적으로 추진하겠다고 밝힘.
①AI 연구자와 중소기업이 Isambard AI, Dawn 등 공공 슈퍼컴퓨팅 자원에 접근할 수 있도록 AI Research Resource 추진
②AI 데이터센터와 관련 인프라를 유치하기 위한 AI Growth Zones 조성
③공공서비스 개혁과 정부 생산성 향상을 위한 AI 도입 확대
④AI 인재, 데이터, 컴퓨팅, 조달, 규제환경을 하나의 성장정책 패키지로 연계
⑤기존 규제기관을 활용하는 혁신친화적 AI 규제 접근을 유지

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Law to Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare (California Attorney General)
document_name: Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing Law to AI in Healthcare (California Attorney General)
body:
Provides guidance on how California’s consumer protection, civil rights, competition, and data privacy laws apply to AI use in healthcare; explains California law regarding the use of AI to override doctors’ decisions, discriminate, or infringe on patient privacy.

Encourages healthcare entities in California using AI to comply with existing state laws related to consumer protection, civil rights, competition, and data privacy.

Provides guidance on non-discrimination laws and explains that AI developers, vendors, and users must ensure their systems do not have a discriminatory impact.

Explains the application of California patient privacy and autonomy laws to AI, including the Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA).

Emphasizes the need for compliance with both state and federal regulations with no exceptions for AI-related practices.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: AI in America: OpenAI's Economic Blueprint
document_name: AI in America: OpenAI's Economic Blueprint
body:
Calls on the federal government to promote US leadership in AI development with nationwide rules to boost innovation, secure AI frontier models, and align AI with democratic values. Urges common export policies, national security prioritization, infrastructure investment, and AI education enhancement.

Defines a US strategy emphasizing national competitiveness, model safeguards, and national security for AI, with the federal government leading and consulting with industry.

Promotes export policies to securely share frontier AI models with allies while limiting exports to adversary nations.

Encourages federal support for AI companies, including sharing national security insights and reducing bureaucratic obstacles for collaboration.

Advocates infrastructure development to support AI, emphasizing chips, data, energy, and talent to maintain US leadership.

Proposes common-sense rules for AI safeguarding public safety while fostering innovation, emphasizing provenance data in AI-generated content, and AI user personalization.

Suggests creating AI Economic Zones and a nationwide AI education strategy to enhance AI ecosystem support and competitiveness.

Envisions a Compact for AI among allies for capital and supply chain access, contrasting Chinese-backed infrastructure projects.

Engages in developing training programs for future AI talent, promoting collaboration between government and industry.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York artificial intelligence act (New York AI act)
document_name: New York S1169 (New York AI Act)
body:
Promotes the safe and responsible development, deployment, and use of AI by regulating high-risk AI systems to prevent algorithmic discrimination. Requires independent audits of high-risk AI systems and end-user notification of their use, and establishes reporting requirements for the developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems.

Establishes the "New York AI Act" to ensure AI development and use in New York State is safe, responsible, and non-discriminatory.

Creates whistleblower protections for employees disclosing AI-related non-compliance.

Requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to notify end-users whenever such systems are used to make consequential decisions.

Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to undergo independent audits before and after deployment for algorithmic discrimination.

Mandates detailed reporting by developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to the Attorney General, covering system capabilities and potential risks.

Prohibits the development, deployment, or use of social scoring AI systems that evaluate individuals based on behavioral data, resulting in unfair treatment or rights infringement.

Allows the Attorney General to enforce compliance and provides a private right of action for those harmed by AI non-compliance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York 2025-A768
document_name: New York 2025-A768 (NY AI Consumer Protection Act)
body:
Establishes AI consumer protection with documentation, audits, and risk management requirements for high-risk AI decision systems. Mandates developer disclosures, consumer notifications, and opportunities to contest AI-based decisions.

Enacts the New York Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Act to manage risks of  AI decision systems. 

Requires developers to ensure systems do not cause algorithmic discrimination through regular audits, starting January 2027. 

Mandates developers provide comprehensive technical documentation and risk assessments to deployers. 

Obligates deployers to notify consumers when high-risk AI systems make significant decisions affecting them and to offer explanation and recourse for adverse decisions. 

Imposes a risk management program for deployers to identify and mitigate potential discrimination. 

Allows the attorney general to enforce compliance through audits and penalties, with the possibility of corrective actions to avoid litigation. 

Establishes exceptions for preempting federal law compliance and protects trade secrets from disclosure.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Mississippi Executive Order No. 1584
document_name: Mississippi EO 1584 (Foster Stakeholder Collaboration and Harness AI)
body:
Directs Mississippi's Department of Information Technology Services to inventory AI use in state agencies, evaluate existing AI processes, and develop AI policy recommendations. Aims to safeguard principles of fairness, privacy, reliability, and accountability.

Directs the Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services (ITS) to inventory all AI technologies across state agencies by providing a standardized form.

Mandates ITS to evaluate current AI processes and guidelines at state agencies.

Instructs ITS to develop policy recommendations for the responsible use of AI, emphasizing fairness, privacy, security, transparency, and accountability.

Encourages statewide coordination on AI use, enabling ITS to engage with government stakeholders and industry experts for best practices and strategies.

Requires state agencies to cooperate with ITS by completing AI inventories and designating a staff member for AI coordination.

Implements the Executive Order immediately, with provisions to remain effective until amended, superseded, or rescinded.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Massachusetts HD 396 (2025-2026)
document_name: Massachusetts HD396 (An Act to ensure accountability and transparency in artificial intelligence systems)
body:
Establishes AI accountability and consumer protection laws in Massachusetts. Requires developers to mitigate algorithmic discrimination risks and disclose them. Mandates deployers implement risk management for high-risk AI. Enforces corporate AI disclosure and consumer notification. Grants authority to Attorney General for enforcement.

Establishes Chapter 93M regarding AI accountability and consumer protection in Massachusetts, defining key terms such as algorithmic discrimination and high-risk AI systems. 

Mandates developers to identify, mitigate, and disclose risks of algorithmic discrimination, and requires public summaries of AI systems and biases.

Compels deployers of high-risk AI systems to implement risk management programs and conduct annual impact assessments, with mandatory consumer notifications on consequential AI decisions.

Requires corporations to disclose their use of AI in consumer targeting and behavior influence, ensuring transparency and consumer rights protection.

Exempts small businesses, low-risk systems, and federally compliant entities from certain provisions.

Empowers the Attorney General to enforce regulations, categorizing violations under unfair trade practices, while providing a defense for proactive compliance.

Permits rulemaking authority for the Attorney General to set compliance and notification standards and mandates a public education campaign on AI consumer rights. 

Specifies varying effective dates for sections within 180 days to one year post-passage.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination
document_name: Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination
body:
Prohibits algorithmic discrimination under New Jersey's Law Against Discrimination (LAD) by covered entities. Holds entities liable for discriminatory outcomes from automated tools. Addresses disparate treatment, disparate impact, and failure to provide reasonable accommodations related to AI use.

Clarifies that the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) applies to algorithmic discrimination through automated decision-making tools similarly to traditional discrimination.

Prohibits any form of discrimination facilitated by automated tools, regardless of intent or third-party involvement in tool development.

Requires covered entities, like employers and housing providers, to avoid disparate treatment and disparate impact discrimination in using these tools.

Mandates that entities provide reasonable accommodations to avoid discriminatory impacts, even if automated tools fail to recognize accommodations.

Holds entities liable for discrimination resulting from their use of third-party developed tools, emphasizing the importance of evaluating these tools for bias.

Encourages developers and vendors to design and test automated tools to minimize discriminatory outcomes, thus reducing liability risk under the LAD.

Reiterates the LAD's comprehensive protections against discrimination, regardless of the technology used, and provides resources for understanding these protections.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Healthy Technology Act of 2025
document_name: Healthy Technology Act of 2025
body:
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to include AI and machine learning technologies as eligible drug prescribers if they are state-authorized and FDA-approved, cleared, or authorized by the FDA and other purposes.

Revises the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to include artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies can qualify as a practitioner eligible to prescribe drugs if authorized by the state involved and approved, cleared, or authorized by the Food and Drug Administration, and for other purposes.

Requires section 503(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 353(b)) to be amended by adding the following at the end.

Requires that any artificial intelligence or machine learning technology included as a “practitioner licensed by law to administer such drug” be authorized pursuant to a statute of the State involved to prescribe the drug involved.

Mandates that the artificial intelligence or machine learning technology be approved, cleared, or authorized by the Food and Drug Administration under section 510(k), 513, 515, or 564.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 53
document_name: California SB 53 March 2025 (CalCompute and Whistleblowers)
body:
Establishes a consortium to create "CalCompute," advancing AI in a responsible, equitable manner. Prohibits developers from retaliating against whistleblowers who disclose AI risks. Requires developers to notify employees of their rights, offering whistleblowing avenues and legal protections against retaliation.

Establishes a consortium to create CalCompute, a public cloud computing framework promoting safe and ethical AI.

Mandates CalCompute to foster research benefiting the public and expanding access to computational resources.

Obligates submission of a report by January 1, 2027, detailing CalCompute's framework, including infrastructure analysis, costs, governance, and workforce recommendations.

Introduces whistleblower protections for employees disclosing critical AI risks, including practices leading to severe harm, damage, or misinformation.

Mandates developers to establish anonymous internal reporting processes and ensures responsive investigation.

Authorizes courts to grant attorney’s fees, shift burdens of proof to developers, and issue injunctive relief in whistleblower cases, prioritizing employee protections.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: “Managing Active and Reserve Tech Talent Effectively Act of 2023”
document_name: MARTTE Act of 2023
body:
Establishes a policy to build human capital infrastructure for AI, coding, and computer programming skills across the Armed Forces. Requires alignment of career fields with AI-related work roles, assessment and tracking of skilled personnel, and use of reserve component members’ civilian AI expertise. Mandates implementation plans and ongoing reporting to Congress.

Establishes a comprehensive human capital infrastructure within the U.S. Armed Forces to develop, track, and manage computer programming, coding, and artificial intelligence skills.

Requires the military departments to create career field occupational codes and special skill designators aligned with AI, machine learning, software engineering, and related work roles under the Department of Defense Cyber Workforce Framework.

Mandates assessment and ongoing tracking of personnel who possess AI and coding skills or who have completed relevant qualification processes.

Directs the services to implement a unified strategy and digital platforms to support the identification, assignment, and presentation of AI and coding capabilities to combatant commands.

Requires each military department, under the Secretary’s direction and in consultation with senior digital, information, and manpower officials, to implement the policy and submit implementation plans within 180 days.

Extends similar requirements to reserve components, enabling members to earn occupational designations based on civilian AI and programming experience and requiring processes to track and employ these skills.

Requires annual updates in budget justification materials until all implementation milestones are met.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Workforce of the Future Act of 2024
document_name: Workforce of the Future Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Secretary of Education to award grants for expanding AI and technology education from pre-K to high school. Directs the Secretary of Labor and others to report on AI's workforce impact, emphasizing skills development. Authorizes funding for workforce upskilling and education.

Mandates the preparation of reports by the Secretary of Labor, the National Science Foundation, and the Secretary of Education on AI's workforce impact, identifying data needs, affected industries, and opportunities for stakeholder influence.

Authorizes the Department of Education to award grants to enhance emerging and advanced technology education from prekindergarten through grade 12, focusing on inclusivity for underrepresented communities.

Requires the Department of Labor to grant funds for upskilling workers in industries significantly impacted by AI, promoting lifelong learning and skill certifications.

Prescribes continuous evaluation and monitoring of grant-funded activities, with a focus on sustaining project activities post-grant.

Demands biannual reporting by grantees on fund usage, disaggregated by demographic factors, and a comprehensive report to Congress within five years.

Amends existing education laws to integrate emerging technology education data, emphasizing competency in AI-related skills among students.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
document_name: Workforce for AI Trust Act
body:
Amends the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act to support NSF fellowships for interdisciplinary AI research, emphasizing ethics and responsible practices. Enhances NIST's role in AI governance workforce development and risk management, focusing on education, technical standards, and professional certifications.

Amends the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 to authorize the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support interdisciplinary AI fellowships, encouraging ethical AI practices.

Mandates the NSF to conduct outreach to diverse institutions and groups underrepresented in STEM fields for fellowship applicants.

Directs the NSF to promote AI-based training and workshops across STEM fields to accelerate scientific discovery and technology development.

Requires the integration of diverse disciplinary perspectives in AI research peer review panels.

Instructs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to support education and workforce development to expand the AI governance workforce, focusing on managing AI-related risks.

Mandates NIST to develop technical standards and guidance for AI risk management careers, including mapping, measuring, and validating AI systems.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Workforce Data Enhancement Act
document_name: Workforce Data Enhancement Act
body:
Establishes a grant program for statewide longitudinal data systems to integrate data across education and workforce development systems. Prioritizes cross-state collaborations and addresses AI's role in workforce demands. Emphasizes data privacy, standardization, and public-private partnerships.

Establishes a grant program under the amended Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act for a workforce data quality initiative aimed at integrating and improving statewide longitudinal data systems.

Requires the Secretary to allocate up to 10% of specific funds to eligible entities, mainly state agencies, for enhancing data integration from education and workforce systems to strengthen program quality.

Mandates that eligible entities submit detailed applications describing proposed improvements, expected outcomes, and privacy measures.

Prioritizes grants to entities with multistate collaboration or those focusing on advancing interoperable data, private partnerships, and real-time data reporting, especially concerning emerging technologies like AI.

Permits grant use for developing state data systems, enhancing data standardization, and fostering data-driven decision-making.

Specifies requirements for a maximum three-year grant duration, supplemental funding use, and post-grant reporting on achievements.

Amends funding source provisions to include these new initiatives.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Wildfire Technology Demonstration, Evaluation, Modernization, and Optimization Act
document_name: Wildfire Technology DEMO Act
body:
Establishes a wildfire technology testbed pilot program prioritizing emerging technologies including AI. Requires collaboration with federal agencies and private entities to test and report on new technologies for wildfire prevention, detection, and mitigation over four years.

Establishes a wildfire technology testbed pilot program within 60 days of the Act's enactment, coordinated by the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior.

Incorporates the program into an existing interagency coordinating group on wildfires.

Identifies key technology priority areas, including hazardous fuels reduction, dispatch communications, remote sensing, safety equipment, and operational dashboards.

Partners selected private entities, nonprofits, and higher education institutions with federal agencies for real-time testing during wildfire mitigation.

Prioritizes emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, augmented reality, and advanced communications for wildfire mitigation.

Requires covered entities to submit applications, including technology testing proposals.

Mandates annual reports to Congress on participating entities, tested technologies, costs, outreach efforts, and technology assessments.

Terminates the program four years after establishment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Western Wildfire Support Act of 2023, Sec. 206 ("Study on Wildfire Detection Equipment and Integration of Artificial Intelligence Technologies")
document_name: Western Wildfire Support Act, Sec. 206 ("Wildfire Detection Equipment and Integration of AI")
body:
Requires the Secretaries to study AI integration with wildfire detection technologies. Evaluates AI's impact on detection, management, and prediction of wildfires. Demands results be submitted to Congress and made publicly available within two years.

Mandates a study by the Secretaries on the effectiveness and limitations of wildfire detection technologies in various aspects of wildfire management.

Requires examination of how each technology, if deployed timely and properly, can effectively and efficiently address wildland fire threats.

Examines the integration of artificial intelligence with real-time imagery and weather data in wildfire detection technologies.

Explores how AI integration can enhance the value of these technologies, both individually and collectively.

Requires submission of the study results to congressional committees and public release within two years of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Weather Information for Agriculture Act
document_name: Weather Information for Agriculture Act
body:
Advances the use of AI and machine learning for drought forecasting, strengthens federal drought and soil-moisture monitoring networks, and establishes partnerships for nationwide drought information. Optimizes federal data for drought indicators and authorizes funding for technology upgrades and national soil moisture monitoring.

Reauthorizes the National Integrated Drought Information System and expands its responsibilities.

Requires advancement and deployment of AI, machine learning, cloud technologies, and updated modeling tools for drought forecasting, including a shift to probabilistic forecasts.

Mandates strengthening observational networks and drought indicators by optimizing federal data and addressing gaps in snowpack, soil moisture, groundwater, and rapid-intensification monitoring.

Establishes memoranda of understanding with the National Mesonet Program for coordinated drought information.

Requires migration to probabilistic forecasts and incorporation of new modeling tools with the Climate Prediction Center.

Authorizes appropriations from $15,000,000 in fiscal year 2024 to $17,000,000 in fiscal year 2028 for these activities.

Mandates the development, deployment, and maintenance of the National Coordinated Soil Moisture Monitoring Network.

Requires the Under Secretary to develop, deploy, and maintain the National Coordinated Soil Moisture Monitoring Network, including establishing a user-friendly website, setting criteria for high-quality data, expanding in situ monitoring stations, improving soil-moisture products, and supporting research.

Promotes research, data sharing, and engagement with the citizen science community for soil moisture monitoring, allowing partnerships to provide nationwide soil moisture information.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System")
document_name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 502 ("National Integrated Drought Information System")
body:
Amends the National Integrated Drought Information System to include AI, machine learning, and cloud technologies for drought monitoring and forecasting. Establishes partnerships for coordinated drought information and updates modeling to probabilistic forecasts.

Amends the National Integrated Drought Information System Act of 2006 to advance and deploy next-generation technologies related to drought, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud technologies.

Requires incorporation of flash drought research and tools to enhance timely response.

Mandates utilization of observational networks and refinement of drought indicators for decision-support products by optimizing data from across the Federal Government.

Establishes memoranda of understanding with the National Mesonet Program to provide coordinated, high-quality, nationwide drought information.

Directs the transition of existing drought products to probabilistic forecasts and incorporation of new dynamical and statistical forecast modeling tools.

Authorizes appropriations increasing annually from $15,000,000 in fiscal year 2024 to $17,000,000 in fiscal year 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather or Water Event Risk Communication")
document_name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 402 ("Hazardous Weather Risk Communication")
body:
Improves NOAA's communication system for hazardous weather risks using social, behavioral, and AI research. Coordinates with governmental and educational partners to ensure timely, consistent public information dissemination.

Amends Section 406 of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act of 2017 to enhance communication about hazardous weather or water events.

Requires the Under Secretary to maintain and improve NOAA's system for communicating risks of hazardous weather or water events to the public.

Mandates the creation of a social, behavioral, risk, communication, and economic sciences program to simplify and improve communication of hazardous weather or water events.

Requires recommendations to be based on the latest social, behavioral, economic, risk, and communications science research, validated using rigorous methods, including AI and machine learning.

Ensures coordination with federal, state, local, tribal, educational, and media partners.

Establishes best practices for timely and consistent communications across public platforms.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing Practices")
document_name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 304 ("Data Assimilation, Management, and Sharing")
body:
Establishes data standards and infrastructure to support open science and efficient data transfer, including AI for data assimilation. Forms a consortium to advance data assimilation research and workforce development.

Establishes the requirement for the Under Secretary, in collaboration with the weather enterprise, to develop consistent and open data and metadata standards to support open science.

Instructs the establishment of a program to advance data assimilation methods, including AI and machine learning, and the creation of a university consortium to address research challenges in data assimilation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 116(f) ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network")
document_name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 116(f) ("Algal Bloom Observing Network")
body:
Integrates Federal, State, regional, and local capabilities to establish a national network for harmful algal bloom monitoring, incorporating artificial intelligence. Establishes a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center for data integration and ecological forecasting support.

Amends Section 606 of the Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Research and Control Act to establish a national harmful algal bloom observing network.

Requires the Under Secretary, via NCCOS and IOOS, to integrate Federal, State, regional, and local observing capabilities.

Mandates the use of emerging technologies and data integration methods, including artificial intelligence, for monitoring, detecting, and forecasting harmful algal blooms.

Instructs the IOOS Program Office to coordinate with NCCOS for observations, data integration, and information dissemination.

Establishes a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center to integrate, disseminate, and support ecological forecasting.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization")
document_name: Weather Act Reauthorization, Sec. 108 ("Computing Resources Prioritization")
body:
Requires the Under Secretary and Secretary of Energy to leverage AI and machine learning for NOAA's missions. Establishes centers of excellence for AI advancements. Mandates a report evaluating initiative effectiveness and needs for computing collaboration with the Department of Energy.

Amends the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act to mandate collaboration between the Under Secretary and the Secretary of Energy in leveraging high-performance computing and AI for advanced weather forecasting.

Requires a competitive, merit-reviewed process for initiative applications, including Federal agencies, National Laboratories, and higher education institutions.

Mandates coordination of AI and computing research across NOAA to avoid duplication and enhance predictive analysis.

Supports model comparison, data sharing, interagency collaboration, long-term data archiving, agile computing decisions, workforce development, and compliance with federal research security requirements. 

Directs sharing of model innovations through community-based activities and interagency coordination.

Authorizes leveraging AI to enhance NOAA’s computing infrastructure for critical missions.

Allows establishment of centers of excellence for AI and machine learning in weather forecasting.

Permits multi-year contracts for high-performance and cloud computing systems.

Requires a report to Congress evaluating the initiative’s effectiveness and future computing needs within two years.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act
document_name: Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Act
body:
Authorizes the EPA Administrator to award grants and contracts for emerging technologies addressing water quality. Mandates the use of AI, quantum information science, and robotics for water quality projects.

Authorizes the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) Administrator to award grants and contracts for projects using emerging technologies to address water quality threats.

Establishes the Water Quality and Environmental Innovation Fund, funding it through fiscal years 2024-2028 using fees from the EPA's Motor Vehicle and Engine Compliance Program.

Mandates the use of technologies, including artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and robotics, among others, for water quality projects.

Requires that project results, including data and statistics, be publicly accessible.

Directs the EPA Administrator to report annually to Congress on the benefits, recipients, goals, and effectiveness of funded projects, starting one year after the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Water Infrastructure Modernization Act of 2023
document_name: Water Infrastructure Modernization Act
body:
Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act and Safe Drinking Water Act to authorize grants for smart wastewater and smart water infrastructure technology. Supports AI and intelligent optimization tools to improve water systems' efficiency, reliability, and decision-making.

Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act and the Safe Drinking Water Act to authorize grants for smart wastewater and smart water infrastructure technology.

Requires the Administrator to provide grants for intelligent wastewater treatment systems using AI for predictive maintenance and real-time monitoring.

Mandates grants for smart drinking water systems with AI tools to reduce water loss, improve decision-making, and enhance operational efficiency.

Requires annual reports to Congress on the projects funded and their impacts.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: WIOA Performance Accountability Improvement Act, Section 2, Subsection (c) ("Evaluation of State programs.")
document_name: WIOA Performance Accountability Improvement Act, Section 2, Subsection (c) ("Evaluation of State programs.")
body:
Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to permit states to use machine learning and advanced analytics for improving program operations, outcomes, and evaluation, enhancing data-driven decision-making in state programs.

Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to require states to use data for analyses and ongoing evaluations of programs.

Allows states to use machine learning or other advanced analytics to enhance program operations, outcomes, and identify areas needing further evaluation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Veterans Online Information and Cybersecurity Empowerment Act of 2024
document_name: VOICE Act of 2024
body:
Establishes a grant program to enhance veterans' digital literacy and cybersecurity skills. Promotes media literacy, critical thinking, and understanding of foreign influence tactics. Requires grant recipients and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to report on program effectiveness. Allocates $20 million for specified fiscal years.

Establishes a grant program to promote digital citizenship and media literacy among veterans, requiring the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to award grants to eligible entities.

Mandates grant recipients to develop cybersecurity best practices and improve veterans' competencies in digital and media literacy.

Requires grant recipients to submit a report on their activities and effectiveness one year after receiving funds.

Obliges the Secretary to report to Congress on the program's overall activities and effectiveness after receiving the last report from grant recipients.

Authorizes $20 million in appropriations for fiscal years 2023, 2025, and 2027 to fund the program.

Defines key terms such as "cybersecurity best practices," "digital citizenship," "media literacy," and "eligible entity."

Encourages the Secretary to maintain a list of grant recipients and promote communication among them.

Acknowledges the role of foreign influence campaigns and online scams targeting veterans as critical issues that need addressing.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Veterans Appeals Efficiency Act of 2024
document_name: Veterans Appeals Efficiency Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Secretary to track and maintain information on certain veterans' benefits claims using technology. Permits the Board of Veterans' Appeals to aggregate appeals with similar legal or factual questions. Allows AI use in studying common legal questions.

Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit an annual report on the average length of time remanded claims are pending.

Mandates the use of technology to track and maintain information on specific claims for benefits, including those continuously pursued, in the National Work Queue, or pending a hearing.

Ensures claimants can view reasons for claim deferrals or suspense dates in the National Work Queue.

Authorizes the Chairman of the Board of Veterans’ Appeals to aggregate appeals with similar questions of law or fact.

Obliges the Board to ensure substantial compliance with its remand decisions, allowing waivers if sufficient evidence resolves underlying issues.

Grants the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims supplemental jurisdiction to review eligible claims and remand matters for addressing unaddressed issues or inadequate decisions by the Board.

Directs a study, potentially using AI, on common legal or factual questions before the Board and mandates a report on the findings.

Requires the Secretary to develop a plan for timely assignment of claims and submit it to Congress.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy (VET) Artificial Intelligence Act
document_name: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
body:
Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop voluntary guidelines for internal and external AI assurance, requiring testing and validation to build trust and accountability. Establishes an advisory committee and a federal study to assess assurance capabilities, including their qualifications, safeguards, and infrastructure, and to report recommendations to Congress.

Establishes the "VET Artificial Intelligence Act" to create voluntary consensus-based guidelines for the testing, evaluation, validation, and verification of AI systems, to enhance trust and adoption.

Mandates the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop, publish, and update these guidelines, addressing consumer privacy, harm mitigation, dataset quality, and governance.

Requires the establishment of an Artificial Intelligence Assurance Qualifications Advisory Committee to provide recommendations on qualifications and accreditation for entities conducting AI assurance.

Directs a study to evaluate the capabilities of entities conducting AI assurances, assessing their resources, methodologies, and market demand, and exploring the use of existing accredited facilities for these purposes.

Obliges the publication of guidelines and advisory committee recommendations for assurance qualifications, ensuring alignment with international standards.

Involves stakeholder outreach and collaboration with various sectors to refine guidelines.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
document_name: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
body:
Establishes regulatory sandboxes for financial entities to test AI projects with reduced regulatory burden, requiring applications to detail compliance strategies, potential impacts, and public-interest benefits. Mandates agency review and oversight by requiring annual reports on outcomes, and allows agencies to create additional AI project regulations post-approval.

Establishes regulatory sandboxes allowing financial entities to experiment with AI-driven products and projects under reduced regulatory burdens.

Requires financial entities to apply for sandbox participation by outlining their AI projects, alternative compliance strategies, and expected public benefits, with the inclusion of an assessment of risks for systemic financial stability and national security.

Obligates financial regulatory agencies to review applications within 90 days, with provisions for approval, denial, or extension, and the option for joint applications by multiple entities.

Stipulates data security measures for information provided by AI project sponsors.

Directs each financial regulatory agency to promulgate regulations, including modification procedures and confidentiality protocols, within 180 days of the Act’s enactment.

Mandates annual reporting to Congress on AI test project outcomes, and permits regulatory agencies to designate additional AI projects as qualifying test projects following public consultation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: United States-Israel Health Technologies Cooperation Act
document_name: US-Israel Health Technologies Act
body:
Authorizes $4,000,000 annually (2024-2026) for a bilateral health tech program with Israel emphasizing AI, drugs, vaccinations, and telemedicine. Requires matching Israeli contributions.

Authorizes $4,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2024 through 2026 to fund a bilateral cooperative program with Israel for developing health technologies. Emphasizes advancing technology, personalized medicine, and data usage in relation to emerging infectious diseases.

Includes artificial intelligence, drugs, vaccinations, respiratory assist devices, diagnostic tests, and telemedicine as eligible health technologies. Requires matching contributions from the Government of Israel to access funding. Allows funding for existing bilateral programs or the establishment of new programs in consultation with the Secretary of State under the 2008 Science and Technology Cooperation Agreement.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Trustworthy By Design Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
document_name: TBD AI Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Director of NIST to develop AI system trustworthiness guidelines covering models, data, safety, security, and fairness within one year. Mandates federal agencies evaluate AI systems for compliance, publicly report evaluation status, and appoint Chief AI Officers for governance and oversight.

Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop guidelines for evaluating the trustworthiness of AI systems within one year, covering models, data, and human-AI interactions.

Requires periodic updates of these guidelines, addressing elements like safety, security, privacy, and bias, especially concerning protected classes under Federal law.

Obliges Federal agencies to ensure new AI systems conform to guidelines before deployment and evaluate existing systems within two years to ensure compliance.

Specifies the designation of a Chief AI Officer in each Federal agency to be responsible for AI governance and guideline implementation.

Requires transparency in labeling AI systems as compliant and mandates agencies to report noncompliance and barriers to Congress.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Transparent Automated Governance Act
document_name: TAG Act
body:
Requires the Director to issue guidance on automated systems for critical decisions, including public notice and appeals processes. Obligates agencies to implement the guidance and mandates the Comptroller General to review compliance.

Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance for transparent automated governance, ensuring compliance with privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties protections.

Mandates agencies to disclose and allow appeals when utilizing automated systems for critical decisions affecting individuals’ rights or status.

Instructs agencies to design systems providing plain language notifications and establish appeals processes for decisions made using AI-augmented processes.

Obligates agencies to track the accuracy and reliability of AI systems, and share data with relevant authorities; encourages consultation with governmental and private sectors for guidance development.

Requires the Comptroller General to report on agency compliance, with reports submitted biennially.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Transparency in Bureaucratic Communications Act
document_name: Transparency in Bureaucratic Communications Act
body:
Amends the Inspector General Act to require detailed descriptions of communications between government entities and internet services, covering issues like content moderation and AI-related factors such as data inputs, algorithms, and analysis tools.

Amends the Inspector General Act of 1978 to require a detailed description of communications between federal establishments and internet service or content providers. 

Includes communications concerning content moderation, user content such as posts, photos, and videos, and any interactions related to data inputs, algorithms, modeling, simulation processes, analysis tools, or related technologies.

Aims to enhance transparency in bureaucratic communications with digital platforms.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Transformational Artificial intelligence to Modernize the Economy against Extreme Weather Act
document_name: TAME Extreme Weather Act
body:
Develops advanced AI applications for weather forecasting, enhances AI weather model integration, and improves emissions monitoring. Supports AI use to predict extreme weather impacts and fires. Encourages public-private partnerships and workforce development, ensuring data access while safeguarding national security and intellectual property.

Mandates the development of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets using AI to improve Earth system modeling and weather forecasts.

Requires collaboration with federal agencies and experts to enhance AI weather models and explore AI's role in public preparedness and resilience.

Directs the use of AI for fire environment modeling to predict, detect, and forecast wildfires and associated hazards.

Establishes an emissions monitoring program using AI to analyze global atmospheric data and improve greenhouse gas emission models.

Encourages partnerships with private and academic entities to advance AI in weather forecasting and environmental predictions.

Calls for recruitment and development of a diverse workforce skilled in AI applications for weather forecasting.

Allows public access to data and code developed under this Act, with safeguards for national security and intellectual property.

Supports ongoing research and data acquisition for AI and numerical weather models, ensuring continued advancement in weather prediction technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Tornado Observations Research and Notification Assessment for Development of Operations Act
document_name: TORNADO Act
body:
Requires the Under Secretary of Commerce to improve NOAA's communication system for hazardous events using methods such data analysis supported by artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.

Requires the Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere to improve the communication system of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) for hazardous weather and water events to prevent loss of life and property.

Mandates the establishment of a hazard risk communication office to simplify and improve communication, using the latest social, behavioral, risk, and communication science research, including AI and machine learning technologies.

Instructs the Under Secretary to create a research program to modernize risk-based hazard communication and establish a pilot program for tornado hazard communication.

title: Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act
document_name: TAKE IT DOWN Act
body:
Amends the Communications Act to criminalize nonconsensual intimate deepfakes and requires platforms to remove deepfakes within 48 hours.

Grants the Federal Trade Commission enforcement authority over this act.

Amends the Communications Act to criminalize the non-consensual production and dissemination of pornography, especially when intended to cause harm or when involving minors.

Requires covered platforms to establish a takedown process for such depictions, and mandates them to remove the content within 48 hours upon valid request.

Levels criminal punishments, including imprisonment, on violators of this law.

Grants enforcement authority to the Federal Trade Commission.

Defines key terms relevant to the instrument, including "covered platform," "deepfake," and "intimate visual depiction."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To require a briefing on the national security threats associated with Chinese autonomous ground vehicles operating in the United States.
document_name: HR6896, 2023, Chinese autonomous ground vehicles briefing requirement.
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to brief Congress by March 30, 2024, on national security threats from Chinese autonomous ground vehicles, including data types collected, dual-use technology implications, and potential CCP or PLA use for military planning.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to provide a briefing by March 30, 2024, on national security threats from Chinese autonomous ground vehicles in the U.S., especially vehicles near Department of Defense bases and sensitive U.S. Government facilities.

Requires the briefing to include information on data types collected, dual-use implications of their technologies, and how the CCP or People’s Liberation Army could potentially use collected data for military planning.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To provide for citizen engagement on the development and adoption of Federal civilian agency use of artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
document_name: Citizen Engagement on Development of Federal Civilian Agency Use of AI Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct listening sessions with various organizations on AI use by federal agencies. Encourages similar sessions by these entities. Mandates annual reports to Congress on public opinions about federal AI adoption.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct virtual and in-person listening sessions across the United States for discussing Federal civilian agency use of artificial intelligence.

Requires inclusion of diverse groups in these discussions, such as civil rights organizations, immigrant communities, and academia.

Encourages these groups to hold their own listening sessions and report back on AI development and adoption.

Obligates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a report to Congress within 240 days of enactment, and annually thereafter, detailing public attitudes and beliefs on Federal civilian agency use of AI.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To provide for Federal civilian agency laboratory development for testing and certification of artificial intelligence for civilian agency use, and for other purposes.
document_name: Federal Civilian Agency AI Testing and Certification Act
body:
Requires Homeland Security, via FEMA, to develop AI testing centers for civilian agencies, ensuring rights protection and democratic principles. Establishes an AI Incident Reporting Office. Mandates biannual reports to Congress, and authorizes $20 billion for implementation.

Establishes federal civilian agency laboratories for AI testing and certification under the Secretary of Homeland Security through FEMA.

Mandates development of AI training and testing centers to evaluate AI systems for federal use, prioritizing privacy, transparency, accountability, and protection of individual rights.

Prohibits automated decision-making that threatens due process and constitutional rights.

Requires real-world use cases to inform AI system outcomes in federal settings, ensuring no personal data is used.

Creates a digital repository for use cases, ensuring Federal agencies can train and test AI systems appropriately.

Establishes an Office of Artificial Intelligence Incident Reporting within the Department of Homeland Security for agency collaboration and reporting on AI experiences.

Requires biannual reports from DHS to Congress on implementation, challenges, and resource needs, and agency reports on adverse AI experiences.

Authorizes $20 billion in appropriations to implement these measures.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To prohibit the Secretary of Defense from entering into information technology contracts with entities that provide certain services to China, and for other purposes.
document_name: To prohibit the Secretary of Defense from entering into information technology contracts with entities that provide certain services to China, and for other purposes.
body:
Prohibits the Secretary of Defense from engaging in IT contracts with entities tied to AI research in China or linked through software or data centers. Allows waiver for national security interests. Applies to contracts within three years of enactment.

Prohibits the Secretary of Defense from entering, renewing, or extending IT contracts with entities involved with certain AI-related operations in China.

Forbids contracts with entities controlling facilities in China focused on AI research or development.

Restricts contracts with entities that have allowed Chinese entities access to U.S. government software source codes.

Bans contracts with entities providing military, law enforcement, or dual-use software to Chinese entities.

Prohibits contracts with entities operating data centers in China.

Allows the Secretary to waive these prohibitions if necessary for U.S. national security.

Applies these prohibitions to contracts during three years post-enactment.

Defines “covered Chinese entity” and “material interest” for clarity and enforcement.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To establish in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration a program to improve precipitation forecasts, and for other purposes.
document_name: H. R. 4913 NOAA Precipitation Forecasts
body:
Supports AI and machine learning research to enhance precipitation prediction accuracy and reliability. Encourages collaboration with academic and private sectors to evaluate emerging technologies. Uses high-performance computing to advance Earth System Models' predictive skills for extreme precipitation phenomena.

Establishes a program within the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to improve precipitation forecasts.

Requires the use of fully coupled Earth System Models to enhance precipitation prediction.

Mandates the utilization of high performance computing and other technologies, including machine learning and artificial intelligence, to advance precipitation forecasts.

Supports research and development in collaboration with academic and private sector partners to test and evaluate emerging technologies.

Improves the accuracy, reliability, and timeliness of precipitation predictions across various timescales.

Incorporates social and behavioral sciences to enhance precipitation forecast products and communication.

Coordinates efforts with Federal, State, local, Tribal, and academic entities.

Authorizes appropriations of $15 million annually from fiscal year 2024 through fiscal year 2028 for the program.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To establish a Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, and for other purposes.
document_name: HR3168, 2023, Joint Autonomy Office Establishment
body:
Establishes the Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, responsible for coordinating and accelerating the adoption of all-domain autonomous systems for operational users, and for developing a Department-wide classification framework for autonomous capabilities.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish the Joint Autonomy Office in the Department of Defense, responsible for coordinating and accelerating the adoption of all-domain autonomous systems for operational users, including through the adoption of commercial and defense best practices

Requires the Office to implement an all-domain enterprise autonomous systems software development and testing platform across DoD's classification levels, including an all-domain data acquisition and curation process to build and manage datasets; these datasets and platforms should be released to various services and acquisition programs as they mature.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to ensure that the Office has unlimited access to existing datasets regardless of classification level, and to introduce security protocols to protect data shared with or maintained by the Office.

Requires the Director of the Office must establish a Department-wide classification framework for autonomous capabilities, considering the complexity of autonomous systems, the necessity of human supervision or control, their applicability to various warfighting domains, and costs; the Director must submit this framework along with an explanation of its criteria and requirements to Congress, with updates released no less frequently than once every two years.

Requires the Director to develop and implement plans to standardize planning, resource and integration of autonomous capabilities across the Department; this includes a report assessing the Department's current efforts which identifies acquisition, training and evaluation gaps, as well as recommendations to address these.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To direct the Secretary of Defense to establish a working group to develop and coordinate an artificial intelligence initiative among the Five Eyes countries, and for other purposes.
document_name: H. R. 6425 (Five Eyes countries AI initiative)
body:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish the Five AIs Strategic AI Working Group to develop and coordinate AI initiatives among Five Eyes countries. Requires comparison of AI systems, testing interoperability, ethical frameworks, and expanding innovation efforts.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish the Five AIs Strategic Artificial Intelligence Working Group to develop and coordinate AI initiatives among Five Eyes countries. 

Outlines the organization of the working group, designating a senior civilian or military officer as head, and encouraging participation of Five Eyes Intelligence Oversight and Review Council members. 

Tasks the working group with comparing AI systems, identifying interoperability solutions, and testing AI model redundancy.

Instructs the development of shared strategies for AI research, development, and data management.

Requires the submission of a plan for the establishment and activities of the working group within 60 days and biannual reports to congressional committees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To direct the Director of the National Institutes of Health to establish a grant program to facilitate research regarding the use of generative artificial intelligence in health care, and for other purposes.
document_name: H.R. 7381 (Health AI)
body:
Directs the NIH Director to establish a grant program promoting research on generative AI in healthcare. Prioritizes projects enhancing AI adoption, workforce development, reducing disparities, and improving underserved care. Supports AI applications in documentation, insurance, and customer service efficiency.

Establishes a grant program by the Director of the National Institutes of Health to fund research on the use of generative AI in health care.

Permits research to include enhancing note-taking, reducing administrative burdens, expediting insurance claims, improving customer service efficiency, and other health care improvements.

Prioritizes grants for entities promoting AI adoption in health care, investing in workforce development, mitigating workforce burnout, reducing health disparities, and improving care for medically underserved populations.

Defines eligible entities to include higher education institutions, nonprofit organizations, and various governmental agencies.

Defines "generative artificial intelligence" as AI producing content in response to prompts.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To amend the Communications Act of 1934 to establish technical and procedural standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems created through generative artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
document_name: To amend the Communications Act of 1934 to establish technical and procedural standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems created through generative artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
body:
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to include technical and procedural standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems, specifically addressing generative AI technologies like voice cloning.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to establish standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems created through generative AI.

Includes technologies such as voice cloning and other subsequent technologies as deemed appropriate by the Commission.

Inserts these standards into Section 227(d)(3) to ensure compliance with the updated regulatory framework.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965.
document_name: To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965, Sec. 119. Subsection (c).
body:
Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to allow states to use machine learning and advanced analytics for evaluating and improving program operations and outcomes and identifying areas needing further evaluation.

Amends Section 116(e) of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to require the use of data for conducting analyses and ongoing evaluations of state programs.

Allows states to use machine learning and other advanced analytics to enhance program operations and outcomes.

Encourages identification of areas needing further evaluation through advanced data analysis techniques.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965.
document_name: To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965, Sec. 174., Subsection (a).
body:
Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to evaluate AI use in workforce programs for labor market data and service delivery. Requires studies on AI and technology in workforce systems, addressing AI bias, and impacts of automation on employment.

Amends Section 169 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to evaluate programs using emerging technology, including AI, for enhancing labor market information and data integration.

Mandates studies to assess AI's effectiveness in workforce systems, emphasizing technology's impact on service delivery, labor market data, end-user tools, and potential biases.

Requires analysis of how automation affects employment, skills development, and worker displacement.

Demands evaluation of AI and machine learning adoption by States in workforce systems, assessing accuracy and identifying biases.

Calls for alignment studies between workforce and education systems, using data integration to improve outcomes.

Obliges reports on AI-related studies and evaluations to be submitted to relevant Senate and House Committees and published publicly.

Sets limits on using authority if certain evaluations are not initiated or completed timely.

Requires Secretary-conducted evaluations on the effectiveness of programs under various conditions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Technology in the Parks Act of 2024
document_name: Technology in the Parks Act of 2024
body:
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to extend E-rate support to local parks. 

Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to establish a grant program for technology training programs directed towards needy families in local parks.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to extend E-rate support to local parks, allowing them to access discounted telecommunications services for technology training programs.

Requires the creation of internet safety regulations for parks receiving such services to ensure cybersecurity standards similar to those for schools and libraries.

Mandates the Secretary of Labor to initiate a grant program for technology training directed towards needy families in local parks, focusing on topics like artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and web development.

Limits grant coverage to 10% of the training programs' operating costs and to a duration of no longer than two years.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2024
document_name: S. 3792 Technology Workforce Framework Act
body:
Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop and update an AI workforce framework. Expands NIST's functions to include workforce frameworks for emerging technologies. Mandates reports to Congress on frameworks and their applications.

Expands the functions of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to include developing workforce frameworks for critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI).

Requires the Director of NIST to develop, maintain, and update an AI workforce framework and review it at least every three years.

Mandates the inclusion of professional, support, and operational skills in AI workforce frameworks, considering nontraditional backgrounds.

Instructs the Director to consult with various stakeholders, including federal agencies and educational institutions, in developing these frameworks.

Obliges the Director to produce multilingual resources to support global adoption of these frameworks.

Requires periodic reports to Congress on updates and the process of reviewing workforce frameworks, including the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity.

Directs the development and publication of additional workforce frameworks for other critical technologies, such as quantum information science.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care")
document_name: Tech to Save Moms Act, Sec. 5 ("Report on Technology in Maternity Care")
body:
Requires the National Academies to study AI's role in maternal health care, examine biases, and devise best practices for bias reduction, privacy, and security. Mandates reporting to Congress within 24 months of enactment.

Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to arrange a study with the National Academies on technology use in maternity care.

Requires examination of innovative technology, including AI, and its impact on racial or ethnic biases in maternal health.

Demands analysis of patient monitoring devices and their influence on racial or ethnic biases.

Calls for identification of best practices to reduce and prevent racial or ethnic biases in technology and device use.

Seeks best practices for using these technologies specifically for racial and ethnic minority groups in maternity care.

Instructs evaluation of privacy and security safeguards related to these technologies.

Obliges the National Academies to complete the study and report results to Congress within 24 months of enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act
document_name: Targeting Online Sales of Fentanyl Act
body:
Requires a GAO study on AI's role in detecting and combating illicit online fentanyl and methamphetamine sales, focusing on algorithmic technologies, enforcement mechanisms, and interagency collaborations. Mandates a report to Congress within one year detailing findings.

Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a study on online sales of fentanyl and methamphetamine, analyzing business models, supply chains, and logistics.

Requires examination of the impact on individuals under 18 and federal efforts to combat these sales, including interagency and intergovernmental collaborations.

Analyzes existing federal law enforcement procedures and outcomes over the past 10 years to identify patterns and improvement areas.

Explores how providers use machine learning and other technologies to detect and combat sales of these substances on their platforms.

Evaluates enforcement mechanisms by providers, such as user identification and account suspension.

Requires assessment of referrals to the Federal Government from providers, including investigations and outcomes.

Obligates submission of a report to Congress within one year detailing study findings and determinations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TRAIN Act
document_name: TRAIN Act
body:
Creates an administrative subpoena process for copyright owners to request disclosure of records from AI developers, identifying copyrighted works used in AI training. Permits legal action if AI developers fail to comply, establishing a rebuttable presumption of infringement.

Enacts the "Transparency and Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence Networks Act" or "TRAIN Act."

Requires the United States district court clerk to issue a subpoena to AI model developers or deployers upon request from copyright owners.

Defines artificial intelligence terms including AI models and generative AI models used in the legal context.

Allows copyright owners, with a good faith belief of infringement, to request AI training data records.

Mandates that a subpoena requires model developers or deployers to disclose records of copyrighted works used in AI model training.

Details the procedure for the issuance and execution of subpoenas under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

Creates a rebuttable presumption of copyright copying if the subpoenaed party fails to comply.

Implements the new rules on the date of enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership)
document_name: TORPEDO Act of 2023, Sec. 6 (Reporting requirements on efforts of the Department of State to implement the AUKUS partnership)
body:
Requires submission of reports detailing interagency actions and progress in implementing advanced capabilities under the AUKUS agreement, including AI and autonomy. Assesses export control changes and collaboration efforts among AUKUS partners on AI and other technologies.

Mandates the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, and Energy, to report on the Department of State's implementation of the AUKUS partnership within 90 days of enactment.

Requires the report to detail Australia's progress on various submarine-related goals, including infrastructure, workforce training, and basing support.

Instructs the report to assess Australia's submarine contributions to U.S. defense objectives and provide a strategy for integrating AUKUS and U.S. submarines.

Mandates reporting on U.S. export control processes and recommendations for improvements to facilitate the AUKUS partnership.
