Demands an interagency report on changes to ITAR and export control regimes to enable defense item exchanges among AUKUS members and Canada.

Requires an assessment of efforts to enhance collaboration in AI, quantum technologies, cyber capabilities, and other advanced defense areas.

Obligates the President to brief Congress annually for seven years on AUKUS implementation progress.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program)
document_name: TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program)
body:
Expedites the release of AI and other advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the UK through the Foreign Military Sales program. Establishes a fast-track decision-making process for AI capabilities, with a presumption of approval, and anticipatory release policy.

Requires the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, to compile a list of pre-cleared military technologies and platforms for sale to Australia, Canada, and the UK within 90 days of enactment and annually thereafter.

Expedites the processing of Foreign Military Sales requests from Australia, Canada, and the UK.

Mandates the creation of an anticipatory release policy for key Foreign Military Sales capabilities, including AI, hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, and quantum technologies, with a presumption of approval.

Requires the review and update of interagency policies to incorporate these anticipatory release provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TEST AI Act of 2023
document_name: TEST AI Act of 2023
body:
Requires the NIST Director to establish testbeds to support the development of trustworthy AI systems, examine vulnerabilities in existing systems, and build guardrails for harm prevention.

Requires the Director of the National Institute on Standards and Technology (NIST) to work with other heads of federal agencies and private/public sector stakeholders to build testbeds for supporting the development of trustworthy AI systems and AI guardrails.

Mandates the Secretary of Commerce and Secretary of Energy to enter into a memorandum of understanding that allows relevant agencies across the federal government access to AI-related personnel, facilities, and research at the Department of Energy.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: TAME Extreme Weather Act
document_name: TAME Extreme Weather Act
body:
Mandates the use of AI by Federal agencies to improve weather forecasts, grid resilience, and resource deployment for extreme weather. Develops AI weather models, enhances emissions monitoring, and establishes a fire modeling program. Encourages public-private partnerships and addresses national security concerns.

Mandates federal agencies to use AI to adapt to extreme weather, improving weather forecasts, electrical grid resilience, resource deployment, and public-private partnerships.

Requires NOAA to develop and curate an Earth system reanalysis dataset, build on existing datasets, and develop AI weather models.

Directs NOAA to explore advanced AI applications for weather forecasting, including data assimilation and model emulation.

Tasks NOAA with providing technical assistance on AI weather models and developing best practices and public datasets.

Establishes programs using AI for wildfire detection, emissions monitoring, and illegal wood product tracking, requiring dataset curation and public access to AI code and data.

Instructs the Department of Energy to optimize energy grids using AI, develop environmental review documents, and ensure public access to AI models and training datasets, while protecting national security interests.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024
document_name: Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024
body:
Establishes a National Synthetic Biology Center to award grants for projects integrating AI and synthetic biology in agriculture. Prioritizes research on gene editing, digital agriculture, and AI applications. Requires reporting on funded research and innovation progress to Congress biennially.

Establishes the National Synthetic Biology Center to award grants for advancing synthetic biology in agriculture.

Requires the Center to prioritize research in areas like cellular biology, gene editing, and digital agriculture.

Mandates the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate modeling and measurement for synthetic biological solutions.

Provides grants to eligible institutions, fostering partnerships with entities such as nonprofits and national laboratories.

Sets criteria for grant applications, emphasizing the promotion of synthetic biology technologies and sustainability in agriculture.

Directs the Center to coordinate with technology transfer offices to commercialize innovations.

Requires the Center to maintain a website for disseminating findings and facilitating collaboration.

Obligates the Center to submit biennial reports to Congress on research findings and grant progress.

Authorizes appropriations for the Center's operation and grant awards from 2025 to 2029.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.")
document_name: Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.")
body:
Encourages the use of electronic technologies for fisheries data collection, including AI applications. Requires periodic reviews and reports on these technologies. Establishes an innovation prize and advisory panel to advance electronic technologies in fisheries management, focusing on AI and machine learning.

Mandates the use of electronic monitoring and other technologies in fisheries data collection, allowing vessels to avoid carrying observers if conditions are unsafe.

Requires the Secretary to integrate electronic monitoring and reporting technologies into fishery information collection programs and review these systems every five years.

Directs the Comptroller General to assess the National Marine Fisheries Service's electronic monitoring capabilities and recommend improvements.

Establishes an electronic technologies innovation prize to encourage advancements in AI, machine learning, and data management for fisheries.

Creates an advisory panel to guide the development and deployment of electronic technologies in fisheries, including performance standards and data ownership.

Exempts the advisory panel from the Federal Advisory Committee Act.

Allows Councils to independently develop electronic technologies for data collection and management.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.")
document_name: Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.")
body:
Aligns fisheries data modernization with NOAA's AI Strategy for efficiency.

Aligns the national strategic plan for fisheries data with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Artificial Intelligence Strategy to enhance efficiency and interoperability.

Requires the Secretary, through the Assistant Administrator for Fisheries, to provide a strategic plan to Congress within 180 days, detailing goals, implementation schedules, budgets, stakeholder engagement, and system development.

Solicits expertise from data management and technology experts both within and outside the government to support the strategic plan.

Mandates the Secretary to report annually to Congress on progress in implementing the fisheries data modernization efforts.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2024
document_name: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2024
body:
Establishes a 30% tax credit for investments in innovative agricultural technology, including AI systems, precision agriculture, and controlled environment agriculture, effective for property construction starting after January 1, 2023. Defines eligible technology types and project criteria.

Establishes a 30% tax credit for investments in innovative agricultural technology projects.

Defines qualified property to include tangible personal property, software, and computer systems used in such projects.

Specifies that projects must be placed in service before December 31, 2035, and focus on precision or controlled environment agriculture.

Includes technologies such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and automated systems within the scope of eligible projects.

Allows taxpayers to elect a payment in lieu of the credit for qualifying projects.

Prohibits double benefits for projects also funded by certain federal grants.

Applies the amendments to property construction beginning after January 1, 2023.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act
document_name: Supply Chain Mapping and Monitoring Act
body:
Establishes the Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response Office to monitor and enhance supply chain resilience. Includes AI, machine learning, and robotics as key technology areas. Coordinates with international partners and private sectors to identify vulnerabilities and ensure critical industry sustainability.

Explains in section 2, subsection A the use of a definitions subsection to clarify what the bill does and how it will work across the federal government. Defines key terms, lists the key technology focus areas (including Artificial Intelligence), and clarifies what counts as a supply chain and a supply chain shock. 

Explains in subsection B that within 180 days of enactment, the Secretary of Commerce must establish the Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response Office.

Explains in subsection C that the Office’s mission is to promote US leadership, build partnerships, actively monitor supply chains, strengthen domestic manufacturing and the workforce, prepare for supply chain shocks, support good-paying manufacturing jobs, and improve US competitiveness.

Explains in subsection D and E that the Office will be led by a Senate confirmed Under Secretary who will monitor and assess supply chains, analyze risks and demand, evaluate domestic and allied capacity, review job impacts, and coordinate with other governments and partners.

Explains in subsection G that the Under Secretary must create a unified coordination group with industry, labor, and other partners to plan for and respond to supply chain shocks.

The remaining sections include: 
Requires that within 180 days the Under Secretary must designate critical industries, supply chains, and critical goods and services, allow public comment, and update those designations at least every four years.

Requires regular reporting to Congress, broad interagency coordination with antitrust compliance, voluntary private participation with confidentiality protections, and authorizes $500 million for FY 2024 to 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act
document_name: Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act
body:
Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act to incorporate machine learning in geothermal research. Establishes a supercritical geothermal research program focusing on supercritical conditions. Requires periodic updates to geothermal data repositories. Authorizes funding for research and development through 2030.

Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to include machine learning algorithms in geothermal research and development.

Establishes a supercritical geothermal research and development program within the Geothermal Technologies Office, focusing on well completion, permeability, materials, sensors, and water-rock geochemistry.

Requires the creation of a repository for geothermal data, with periodic updates for data standardization and accessibility.

Mandates a memorandum of understanding for data sharing regarding geothermal development among federal departments.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to drill deep exploration boreholes for geothermal mapping.

Establishes a next-generation geothermal center of excellence to coordinate research, development, and workforce initiatives.

Authorizes $5 million annually from 2026 to 2030 for these activities.

Updates geothermal resource assessments quadrennially to include supercritical geothermal regions.

Requires progress reports on geothermal resource potential and commercialization barriers.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Supercomputing for Safer Chemicals Act
document_name: SUPERSAFE Act
body:
Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish a consortium that identifies toxic substances and develops safer alternatives through computational toxicology methods based on AI and machine learning.

Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to establish a consortium representing federal, state, and academic stakeholders. The consortium will use supercomputing and machine learning to develop models that predict adverse health effects from toxic substances, establishing rapid approaches for large-scale identification of toxic substances and the development of safer alternatives.

Requires the Consortium to recommend how the information produced can be used in risk assessments by the EPA, other federal agencies, and industry.

Appropriates funding to the EPA Administrator to carry out the Consortium and requires the Consortium to make its model predictions public and accessible.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Strengthening Consumer Protections and Medical Debt Transparency Act
document_name: Medical Debt Transparency Act
body:
Establishes a public database for medical debt collection, requiring health care entities to report debt collection practices. Prohibits extraordinary collection actions during pending insurance appeals or before determining patient eligibility for assistance. Requires detailed patient billing information and imposes penalties for non-compliance.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to regulate medical debt collection practices by health care entities and their debt collectors. Restricts extraordinary collection actions while a health insurance appeal is pending, before determining whether a patient qualifies for public or entity-based financial assistance, and until at least 180 days after the initial bill is sent. Requires health care entities or their debt collectors to provide patients with itemized billing statements, payment receipts, and information about available language-assistance services, limits certain nonprofit collection amounts, and requires reasonable efforts to verify debtor identity before collection activity begins. Establishes a public medical debt collection database requiring annual reporting by health care entities on debt collectors used, collection policies and practices, demographic and geographic patterns, debt outcomes, and related metrics, with public online access to the reported information. Creates a civil damages remedy for noncompliance and requires the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to report to Congress on medical debt collection practices using data from the database and other relevant sources.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats
document_name: S. 2346 (Public Health Response to AI)
body:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and report to Congress a strategy addressing AI misuse threats to national health security. Involves public health preparedness, identifying gaps, and mitigating risks like biological weapons.

Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop a strategy for public health preparedness and response to artificial intelligence (AI) threats within 180 days of enactment with the following requirements: a framework for public health preparedness and response to mitigate the risks of misuse of artificial intelligence; an outline of the duties, functions, and preparedness goals for which the Secretary is responsible; gaps in public health capabilities and strategies to address these gaps and strengthen emergency preparedness against AI threats; strategies to mitigate risks, such as the development of biological weapons and treatment-resistant viruses and bacteria.

Requires the strategy to be submitted to relevant congressional committees without compromising national security.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to integrate this AI threat strategy into the broader federal response to public health emergencies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Stop Spying Bosses Act
document_name: Stop Spying Bosses Act
body:
Requires employers to disclose AI-driven workplace surveillance details and prohibits using AI to predict non-work behavior. Establishes a Privacy and Technology Division for oversight. Enables private rights of action and whistleblower protections. Mandates coordination with federal and state agencies.

Prohibits employers from using workplace surveillance to monitor labor activities, ascertain political or religious views, or determine health or immigration status unrelated to job duties.

Requires employers to disclose details about workplace surveillance practices, including data collection methods, frequency, storage locations, business purposes, and third-party transfers, to employees and applicants.

Establishes a Privacy and Technology Division within the Department of Labor to oversee compliance and issue regulations.

Allows employees to access, correct, and request data collected about them and prohibits data transfer to third parties without disclosure and cybersecurity measures.

Grants employees and labor organizations the right to bring civil actions against violations, with potential damages and injunctive relief.

Prohibits predispute arbitration agreements regarding surveillance-related disputes.

Mandates annual reports to Congress on workplace surveillance impacts and recommendations for mitigating harms.

Coordinates with federal and state agencies to ensure consistent regulatory treatment of workplace surveillance.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Stop Smuggling Illicit Synthetic Drugs on U.S. Transportation Networks Act of 2024
document_name: Stop Smuggling Illicit Synthetic Drugs on U.S. Transportation Networks Act of 2024, Section 103. "Development of strategy to accelerate research and development of non-intrusive, advanced inspection technologies to detect illicit synthetic drugs"
body:
Develops a joint strategy to accelerate research, development, and deployment of AI and other technologies to detect illicit synthetic drugs. Requires report submission to specified congressional committees within two years.

Require the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy and the Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy to develop a strategy for accelerating the research, development, and deployment of advanced inspection technologies, including AI and quantum computing, to detect illicit synthetic drugs.

Mandate coordination with multiple agencies, including the National Science Foundation and the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Instruct submission of a report on the strategy to specified congressional committees within two years of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act
document_name: Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act
body:
Appropriates $1,090,000,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection for technology improvements to enhance fentanyl interdiction.

Appropriates $223,000,000 to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to expand fentanyl interdiction and disrupt transnational criminal networks.

Mandates submission of reports by March 31, 2028, on impacts of Border Patrol Processing Coordinator positions and equipment needs.

Creates penalties for damaging or evading border controls, with fines and imprisonment up to 5 years for violations aimed at financial gain or furthering criminal organizations.

Appropriates $1,090,000,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection for technology improvements, including non-intrusive inspection scanning systems and anomaly detection algorithms, to enhance fentanyl interdiction at land borders.

Appropriates $223,000,000 to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to expand efforts to interdict fentanyl and disrupt transnational criminal networks, including funds for additional special agents and joint surge operations.

Mandates submission of reports by March 31, 2028, detailing impacts of Border Patrol Processing Coordinator positions, equipment needs for outbound inspections, and summaries of non-intrusive inspection technology at land ports of entry.

Creates penalties for knowingly damaging or evading border controls, with fines and imprisonment up to 5 years for violations aimed at securing financial gain or furthering criminal organizations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024
document_name: State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024
body:
Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to establish a Flex-Tech Energy Program. Provides financial assistance for manufacturers to enhance competitiveness, including AI adoption. Allocates funding, emphasizes technical assistance, and mandates a minimum 5% funding for Indian Tribes.

Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to establish the 'Flex-Tech Energy Program To Enhance Manufacturing Competitiveness'.

Requires the Secretary to provide financial assistance to State energy agencies or Indian Tribes for developing and implementing flex-tech energy programs.

Requires programs to provide technical and financial assistance to manufacturers for energy studies and for implementing efficiency, cost-saving, and advanced technology improvements, including AI.

Mandates that energy studies of manufacturing facilities evaluate systems relative to design intent, emissions related to the facility, potential energy efficiency, and potential on-site energy measures. 

Allocates at least 5% of funds specifically for Indian Tribes or manufacturers in Indian Country.

Limits financial assistance by capping spending at 50% for energy studies, 50% for implementation, 10% for administrative costs, and the greater of $100,000 or 5% per facility.

Encourages the use of both public and private financing in program implementation.

Provide technical assistance to help states and tribes develop and expand energy programs tailored to small manufacturers and promote advanced manufacturing technologies.

Authorizes $100 million annually from 2025 to 2029 for the program.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Solving the Border Crisis Act
document_name: Solving the Border Crisis Act
body:
Resumes border wall construction and requires compliance with DNA collection laws. Disapproves rule change on asylum claims. Amends treatment for aliens from contiguous territories to ensure return or detention. Sets minimum staffing levels for immigration enforcement and detention facilities funding.

Resumes border wall system construction, requiring the Secretary of Homeland Security to restart halted projects and honor previous agreements.

Prohibits the cancellation of contracts related to border wall construction entered into before January 20, 2021.

Requires the lifting of COVID-19 related suspension of entries and imports not earlier than 120 days after the termination of the public health emergency.

Mandates submission of plans to manage possible influxes related to the termination of COVID-19 suspensions.

Disapproves the rule allowing asylum officers to adjudicate credible fear claims, maintaining exclusive authority for immigration judges.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the return of aliens to contiguous territory or detain them for further asylum consideration.

Establishes minimum staffing levels for various immigration and border enforcement offices, including 25,000 U.S. Border Patrol agents.

Ensures funding for sufficient detention facilities to comply with mandatory detention requirements.

Mandates a report within 60 days on how the Department of Homeland Security is mitigating border encounters.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Social Media and AI Resiliency Toolkits in Schools Act
document_name: SMART in Schools Act
body:
Mandates development and updates of AI and social media impact toolkits on youth. Requires stakeholder consultation. Specifies evidence-based content on digital resilience. Directs tailored guidance inclusion. Instructs dissemination through institutions. Authorizes $2,000,000 for implementation.

Mandates the Secretaries of Education and Health & Human Services to develop educational toolkits about artificial intelligence (AI) and social media's impact on youth.

Requires consultation with various relevant stakeholders, including students, parents & guardians, educators, administrators, and healthcare professionals, to develop the toolkits.

Specifies guidelines for each different type of toolkit, to be appropriately targeted to their multiple intended audiences: students, parents & guardians, educators, administrators, and healthcare professionals.

Directs the Secretaries to develop toolkit dissemination strategies, so that the resources reach their intended audiences.

Authorizes $2,000,000 for facilitating the dissemination of the toolkits.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Small Business Broadband and Emerging Information Technology Enhancement Act of 2023
document_name: S. 2677 Small Business Technology Enhancement Act
body:
Designates a coordinator to assist small businesses in adopting AI and emerging technologies, requiring collaboration with federal agencies. Mandates biennial reports on broadband's impact on small businesses, and updates training for SBA employees on AI technologies.

Designates a senior employee of the Office of Investment and Innovation as the broadband and emerging information technology coordinator to assist small businesses in adopting broadband and emerging technologies.

Requires the coordinator to work with the SBA's chief information officer, chief technology officer, and other relevant federal agencies.

Mandates the coordinator to identify best practices and catalog tools and training for small businesses on broadband and emerging technologies.

Obligates the coordinator to provide training to SBA employees on these technologies and relevant federal programs.

Requires biennial reports on the SBA's activities related to broadband and emerging technologies.

Instructs the Chief Counsel for Advocacy to study and report on the impact of broadband availability, speed, and price, and the deployment of emerging technologies on small businesses.

Amends the Small Business Act to include provisions for increasing small business access to broadband and emerging technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024
document_name: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to develop AI training resources for small businesses, including those in rural and underserved areas. Mandates annual review and updates of resources. Allows grants for AI training. Terminates the program after three years.

Mandates the Secretary of Commerce, in coordination with various agencies, to develop AI training resources for small businesses, including those in rural, Tribal, or underserved areas.

Requires these resources to cover topics such as prompt engineering, financial management, cybersecurity, and government contracting.

Obligates the review and update of these resources every year to ensure relevance and effectiveness.

Coordinates with the Small Business Administration for the distribution of these resources through its network, including development centers and business opportunity centers.

Allows for a grants program to fund training providers using the developed resources.

Demands initial and annual reports to Congress on the progress and impact of the training resources.

Establishes a sunset clause terminating the program three years after the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
document_name: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
body:
Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to develop, update, and disseminate AI resources for small businesses, ensuring applicability, promoting understanding, including case studies, and aligning with international standards. Requires biennial reviews, voluntary usage, and reporting to Congress.

Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to mandate the development and dissemination of AI resources for small businesses.

Requires these resources to include technical standards, best practices, benchmarks, methodologies, and case studies, ensuring they are widely applicable and technology-neutral.

Mandates that resources promote understanding and adoption of AI, adhere to international standards, and incorporate federal educational resources.

Obligates the Director to review and update these resources every two years.

Coordinates with the Small Business Administration for the distribution and utilization of AI resources through its partners, emphasizing voluntary use.

Compels a report to Congress within four years, detailing resources, feedback, and recommendations for enhancing AI utilization by small businesses.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Simplify, Don't Amplify the IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection")
document_name: Simplify IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection")
body:
Requires the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to use AI, including neural machine learning, to calculate tax gap projections, reducing the burden on taxpayers. Limits National Research Program audits to fiscal year 2022 levels while leveraging commercial data analysis tools.

Mandates the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to use artificial intelligence, including neural machine learning, to reduce taxpayer burden during National Research Program audits and improve the accuracy of tax gap projections.

Requires use of AI and data analysis tools to calculate and project the tax gap, which is the difference between taxes owed and taxes collected.

Prohibits conducting more National Research Program audits in any fiscal year than the number conducted in fiscal year 2022. 

Obligates the Commissioner to submit an annual tax gap projection to Congress, detailing the estimate using the latest data available, by July 31 each year.

Defines the term "tax gap" as the difference between tax liabilities owed under the Internal Revenue Code and those actually collected by the IRS.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Shifting Forward Vehicle Technologies Research and Development Act
document_name: Vehicle Technologies R&D Act
body:
Establishes programs for AI-driven vehicle technology research, focusing on electrification, machine learning for manufacturing, autonomous systems, cybersecurity, and advanced energy solutions. Requires periodic reporting and coordination among federal agencies. Allocates funding for these initiatives through 2028.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to conduct a research, development, and demonstration program for advanced vehicle technologies, focusing on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle manufacturing costs.

Mandates coordination with other federal agencies and existing programs on electric vehicle integration and critical material recycling.

Supports the development of advanced batteries, power electronics, electric drive systems, and vehicle electrification technologies.

Includes provisions for cybersecurity and physical security of vehicle interconnections with the electric grid and other infrastructure.

Establishes a program for medium- and heavy-duty commercial and transit vehicles, emphasizing advanced energy technologies and efficiency improvements.

Authorizes the creation of Graduate Automotive Technology Education Centers of Research Excellence to foster advancements in automotive energy technologies.

Allocates substantial funding for these initiatives through fiscal year 2028, with a total authorization exceeding $2.9 billion.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sensible Classification Act of 2023, Sec. 7: Implementation of Technology for Classification and Declassification
document_name: Sensible Classification Act of 2023, Sec. 7: Implementation of Technology for Classification and Declassification
body:
Calls for using machine learning and artificial intelligence for both classification and declassification of national security information and security clearance eligibility assessment.

Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government of the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with various federal actors, to research a technology-based solution to reform the classification system employed by the federal government.

Requires a submission of recommendations to the President.

Mandates the President to submit a report on technology-based solutions to Congress no later than 540 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sensible Classification Act of 2023
document_name: Sensible Classification Act of 2023
body:
Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government, in consultation with key defense, intelligence and declassification officials, to research and report on AI and machine learning solutions for efficient classification and declassification.

Mandates the research and recommendation of AI and machine learning solutions for efficient classification and declassification systems, to be interoperable across the Federal Government.

Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government to consult with key defense and intelligence agencies for technology implementation and submit a report on the recommended solution.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
document_name: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
body:
Prohibits the use of AI to interfere with elections and deprive individuals of the right to vote. Mandates disclaimers on election-related AI-generated content.

Prohibits developers and deployers from using AI to intentionally deceive or defraud individuals of their voting rights in federal, state, or local elections.

Requires election-related AI-generated content to include disclaimers, informing the public that the content was created using AI.

Mandates developers to provide mechanisms ensuring such disclaimers are permanent or difficult to remove.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to issue regulations on disclaimer requirements and enforce compliance.

Obliges developers and deployers to ensure their algorithms meet safety and efficiency standards as outlined.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Secure Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
document_name: Secure A.I. Act
body:
Requires the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to improve accounting for AI security vulnerabilities in their existing databases.

Establishes an AI Security Center within NSA for research and secure AI practices.

Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to update the National Vulnerability Database to include AI security vulnerabilities.

Establishes a voluntary, comprehensive database to track AI security and safety incidents, ensuring confidentiality and standardized reporting.

Requires the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to update the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures Program for AI vulnerabilities.

Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Security Center within NSA to facilitate AI security research, develop counter-AI techniques, and promote secure AI practices.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Secure Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
document_name: Secure A.I. Act
body:
Establishes a voluntary database to track and process identified AI security and safety incidents and risks, and requires the facilitation of research to develop new and evaluate existing safety guidelines and processes.

Establishes a voluntary database to track AI security and safety incidents, requiring the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop mechanisms for sharing incident information while preserving confidentiality.

Mandates NIST to update the National Vulnerability Database to incorporate AI security vulnerabilities and identify characteristics that make the database unsuitable for certain AI vulnerabilities.

Prohibits employer retaliation against employees who report AI incidents, allowing legal recourse for aggrieved parties.

Directs the establishment of best practices for addressing AI supply chain risks, involving multiple stakeholders.

Established the Artificial Intelligence Security Center within the National Security Agency to facilitate AI security research, guidance development, and ensure the availability of test-beds for secure AI research.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sec. 2501. Corporate Citizenship and Ownership, Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023
document_name: Sec. 2501 of 2023 Consumer Protection Act
body:
Requires operators of dominant online platforms with owners (including minority owners) who are citizens of foreign adversaries of the U.S. to sequester data and algorithms from agents of any foreign entity.

Requires operators of dominant online platforms with (a) large numbers of users and (b) ownership groups in which at least 10% of the members are citizens of foreign adversaries of the U.S. to sequester any back-end data or algorithm from agents of any foreign entity.

Also regulates foreign ownership of, and the granting of licenses for foreigners to operate, online platforms featuring large numbers of users, regardless of whether the platform uses AI.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sec. 2412. Duty of Care, Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023
document_name: Sec. 2412 of 2023 Consumer Protection Act
body:
Prohibits non-governmental entities from designing or employing AI, or handling data, in ways that will harm people or discriminate either (a) on the basis of protected class or (b) in granting access to important opportunities and services.

Prohibits non-governmental entities from designing or employing AI, or handling personal data, in a way that will:

(1) Cause physical, psychological, economic, relational, or repetitional injuries to a person;

(2) Discriminate on the basis of standard protected classes, including race and nationality; or

(3) Discriminate in the granting of access to important services and opportunities, including employment, credit, and education.

Exempts private groups not open to the public from the requirements outlined above.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act
document_name: Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act
body:
Prohibits sports wagering operators from using AI to track individual wagers, target promotions, or create gambling products like microbets. Requires operators to follow strict data security and consumer protection standards, including preventing underage gambling and ensuring contest integrity.

Prohibits sports wagering operators from using artificial intelligence to track individual wagers, target specific individuals with offers or promotions, or create gambling products like microbets.

Requires sports wagering operators to ensure data security and to take reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized access or dissemination of wagering and customer data.

Mandates real-time or near-real-time sharing of anonymized sports wagering data with the State regulatory entity.

Imposes strict consumer protections, including restrictions on AI use, limits on deposits, and mandatory affordability checks for high-value wagers.

Establishes comprehensive standards for licensing, recordkeeping, and employee background checks to ensure the integrity and accountability of sports wagering operators.

Requires cooperation with investigations by regulatory authorities and sports organizations, and mandates robust internal controls for operators.

Prohibits advertising targeting problem gamblers or individuals ineligible to wager, and restricts broadcast times and content. 

Enforces restrictions to maintain contest integrity and prevent betting on certain events and by prohibited individuals.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: STOP HATE Act of 2023
document_name: STOP HATE Act
body:
Mandates social media companies to submit terms of service reports to the Attorney General's office that provide data on how artificial intelligence is being used to flag content and manage disinformation.

Requires social media companies to make their terms of service publicly available.

Requires social media companies to disclose content moderation data, including the total number of flagged items, actioned items, user engagement, and how artificial intelligence is used to support content moderation efforts.

Allows Attorney General's office to bring a civil penalty of $5,000,000 per violation per day against social media companies who fail to meet these requirements

category: U.S. federal laws
title: STAND with Taiwan Act of 2024, Section 11 ("Prohibition on investments by United States financial institutions that benefit the Government of the People's Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party")
document_name: STAND with Taiwan Act of 2024, Section 11 ("Prohibition on investments by United States financial institutions that benefit the Government of the People's Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party")
body:
Prohibits U.S. financial institutions from investing in entities tied to China's government or military and sectors like AI, robotics, and quantum computing, as identified in strategic plans like "Made in China 2025" and the "14th Five Year Smart Manufacturing Development Plan."

Prohibits United States financial institutions from making investments benefiting the Government of the People's Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party.

Mandates the Secretary of the Treasury to enforce this prohibition within three days of a covered determination.

Defines prohibited investments as monetary investments to entities owned or controlled by the Chinese government, Chinese Communist Party or People's Liberation Army.

Includes investments that benefit priority industrial sectors identified in Chinese strategic plans, such as "Made in China 2025" and the "14th Five Year Smart Manufacturing Development Plan."

Specifies prohibited sectors including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and robotics.

Defines "United States financial institution" to include investment companies, private equity firms, venture capital companies, and hedge funds that qualify as United States persons.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: STAND with Taiwan Act of 2023
document_name: STAND with Taiwan Act
body:
Imposes sanctions on China if its military invades Taiwan, including blocking property, prohibiting trades, and investment restrictions. Targets Chinese officials, institutions, and entities involved in aggressive actions. Coordinates with allies for sanctions, allowing exceptions for national security or intelligence activities.

Mandates the imposition of sanctions on the People's Republic of China if the People’s Liberation Army initiates a military invasion of Taiwan. 

Requires sanctions against Chinese officials and entities involved in military campaigns or efforts undermining Taiwan's security and infrastructure.

Blocks property and imposes visa restrictions on identified Chinese officials and affiliates involved in military and coercive actions against Taiwan.

Prohibits U.S. financial institutions from investments that benefit Chinese government-controlled entities or priority sectors like artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies.

Bans the listing and trading of securities of Chinese entities on U.S. securities exchanges following an invasion.

Prohibits the importation of goods from China post-invasion unless exceptions for national security are made.

Grants the President authority to enforce sanctions and provides for penalties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: SPEED through Screening Act
document_name: SPEED through Screening Act
body:
Requires the TSA Administrator to develop strategies to reduce patdowns and item divestiture during airport screenings using advanced technologies, including AI. Authorizes $20 million for research and deployment, mandates data collection, and allows publication of anonymized statistics.

Requires the Administrator to submit strategies within one year to reduce patdowns and the need for item divestiture during passenger screening without compromising security.

Considers technological improvements, discrimination reduction among passenger populations, and next-generation screening technologies in developing these strategies.

Mandates a feasibility study on allowing increased volumes of liquids, aerosols, gels, and powders on aircraft without reducing security.

Permits deployment of detection at range technology for screening, subject to feasibility assessments and prioritizes reducing patdowns and enhancing security for vulnerable populations.

Obligates collection and publication of anonymized screening statistics, considering privacy and civil rights, utilizing AI and noninvasive technologies.

Allocates $20 million for fiscal year 2024 to research and deploy improved screening technologies.

Requires annual briefings to congressional committees and a Comptroller General review within two years on the Act's implementation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: SCAM Platform Act
document_name: SCAM Platform Act
body:
Requires the Federal Communications Commission to create an AI-based tool within one year to help the public identify likely scams. Specifies that the tool must accept various submission formats, evaluate scam likelihood, and provide a scam likelihood rating.

Mandates the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to develop an artificial intelligence-based tool to help the public identify likely scams within one year of this Act's enactment.

Requires the AI tool to accept various submission formats including emails, text messages, website URLs, and scans or photographs of physical materials.

Obliges the tool to evaluate the likelihood of submissions being scams and provide a rating to reflect this likelihood.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Defines "scam" as any scheme designed to defraud by inducing a recipient to take actions against their interest, through false or misleading information.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: SAFE from PRC Investments Act
document_name: SAFE from PRC Investments Act
body:
Amends the Securities Exchange Act to require public companies and exchange-traded funds to disclose ties to the Chinese government or Communist Party, including board memberships, financial operations, military involvements, and data management, focusing on governance and security implications.

Requires public companies and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) investing in companies with ties to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to disclose whether senior officials of the PRC government or Communist Party of China (CPC) sit on their boards or have executive roles.

Mandates disclosure of cash held in PRC operations, restrictions on cash repatriation, and details of assets, liabilities, and technology transfers.

Obligates reporting on interactions with CPC officials, expenditures on PRC operations, and any lobbying activities in the United States.

Compels ETFs to reveal ownership, CPC branches, contractual agreements, and involvement in PRC industrial policies or military contracts of invested PRC companies.

Requires disclosure of PRC companies’ products and services, U.S. defense contracts, and involvement in sectors like AI, telecommunications, and semiconductors.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: SAFE Bet Act
document_name: SAFE Bet Act
body:
Prohibits the use of AI in tracking wagers, creating targeted promotions, and developing gambling products in sports wagering operations. Requires sports wagering programs to include consumer protection, integrity standards, and restrictions on AI use. Establishes a national self-exclusion list and mandates annual surveys on problem gambling.

Establishes the "SAFE Bet Act," setting minimum federal standards for sports wagering, which includes restrictions on AI use by sports wagering operators. 

Prohibits operators from using AI to track individual wagers, target specific individuals with promotions, or create gambling products like microbets. 

Mandates state sports wagering programs to ensure compliance with standards, including consumer protections and advertising restrictions, and requires operators to maintain data security and recordkeeping. 

Enforces reporting of suspicious transactions and mandates cooperation with investigations into sports wagering activities. 

Creates a national self-exclusion list to prevent individuals from placing sports wagers across states, and establishes public health initiatives to monitor gambling addiction. 

Permits states and tribes to enact stricter sports wagering regulations and does not preempt their authority to tax sports wagering.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S5344 Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024
document_name: Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024
body:
Promotes democratic AI governance and human rights in technology development and deployment. Requires the Coordinator for Digital Freedom to address AI governance implications on democracy. Mandates annual reports analyzing global threats to digital freedom, including AI management risks, and offering protection recommendations.

Requires the United States to prioritize digital freedom in foreign policy and diplomatic engagements.

Mandates cooperation with countries committed to democratic technology use and development.

Appoints a Coordinator for Digital Freedom within the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy to advance global digital freedom.

Directs the Coordinator to engage with international actors to counter digital authoritarianism and support human rights-compliant technology governance.

Instructs the Coordinator to promote democratic governance of artificial intelligence, emphasizing human rights and democracy.

Requires ongoing publication of guidelines for protecting digital freedom in cyberspace, including the AI Risk Management Profile.

Obliges annual reporting on global digital freedom, analyzing threats like digital authoritarianism, censorship, and AI governance risks.

Advises on improving digital inclusion and information integrity.

Tasks the Coordinator with making recommendations to enhance digital freedom through diplomatic channels.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S.4870, A bill to require reports on artificial intelligence regulation in the financial services industry.
document_name: S.4870, A bill to require reports on artificial intelligence regulation in the financial services industry.
body:
Require federal financial agencies to report to Congress on AI knowledge gaps, usage, governance standards, regulatory needs, interagency issues, and resource requirements within 90 days. Exclude confidential supervisory and nonpublic information from reports.

Require the Federal Reserve, FDIC, OCC, NCUA, CFPB, the Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate, and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives to report on AI knowledge gaps in financial services within 90 days.

Mandate which tasks are being assisted or completed with AI in the Institutions that agencies regulate.

Assess current AI governance and oversight standards for AI oversight by the agency.

Identify additional regulatory authorities required by the agency to execute the mission agency.

Clarify overlapping AI regulatory issues between agencies.

Evaluate current and planned agency use of AI over the next three years, including fiscal and staffing impacts.

Determine necessary resources and monetary to require the agency to adapt to AI changes and oversee its use in the regulatory landscape to oversee how AI is adopted across operations. 

Ensure reports exclude confidential or nonpublic information.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S.4862, A bill to ensure that new advances in artificial intelligence are ethically adopted to improve the health of all individuals, and for other purposes.
document_name: S.4862, A bill to ensure that new advances in artificial intelligence are ethically adopted to improve the health of all individuals, and for other purposes.
body:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to require NIH to develop AI resources and datasets for health research, and to provide education for ethical AI use. Requires hospitals to request patients' consent for EHR data sharing. Allocates $660 million for AI initiatives.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to mandate the NIH Director develop AI resources and datasets for health research, provide AI expertise, and maintain data access resources.

Authorizes $400 million for NIH AI initiatives in fiscal year 2025.

Directs the National Coordinator for Health IT to utilize electronic health records for research, establish data standards, and align with national interoperability frameworks.

Appropriates $10 million for data collection and $50 million for data standards.

Requires hospitals to request patient consent to use health records for research, contingent upon patient approval.

Expresses the Senate's view that NIH representation is crucial in steering committees for national AI research resources.

Mandates the National Library of Medicine to establish data-sharing facilities and create a core data science program.

Appropriates $100 million each for these library initiatives in fiscal year 2025.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: S.4306, Five AIs Act 2024
document_name: Five AIs Act 2024
body:
Establishes the "Five AIs Strategic Artificial Intelligence Working Group" to coordinate AI initiatives among Five Eyes countries. Tasks include enhancing AI interoperability, testing systems, managing data, leveraging commercial AI technologies, and sharing results with allies. Controls export of technical data.

Establishes the "Five AIs Strategic Artificial Intelligence Working Group" within 90 days to coordinate AI initiatives among the Five Eyes countries (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, and the US).

Requires the Secretary of Defense and Director of National Intelligence to lead and designate a head for the Working Group.

Mandates the Working Group to develop strategies for AI interoperability, ethical frameworks, and innovation among the Five Eyes countries.

Instructs testing and evaluation of AI systems for intelligence sharing and battlespace awareness.

Emphasizes leveraging commercial AI technologies and managing data-informed AI systems.

Requires submission of a plan within 60 days and biannual reports on the Working Group's activities.

Specifies control of knowledge and technical data by individual countries under their export laws.

Allows termination of the Working Group on September 30, 2028, with possible extension for national security interests.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024
document_name: Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024, SEC. 7208. "HIGH-PRIORITY RESEARCH AND EXTENSION INITIATIVES."
body:
Establishes grants for developing and evaluating agricultural uses of AI. Emphasizes AI applications that improve specialty crop production. Supports agricultural innovation by integrating AI into farming practices.

Establishes research and extension grants for developing and evaluating the agricultural application of artificial intelligence.

Emphasizes the use of AI to improve specialty crop production.

Authorizes these initiatives under the amendments to the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990.

Encourages research projects that focus on innovative methods and technologies enhancing agricultural efficiency.

Places potential emphasis on mechanizing agricultural processes, though AI-specific focus is primarily on specialty crop production.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024
document_name: Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024, SEC. 7518. "DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY, AND                NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION JOINT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES."
body:
Authorize collaborative AI-focused research among the Department of Agriculture, Department of Energy, and National Science Foundation, enhancing algorithms for agriculture and rural energy systems. Establish memoranda of understanding, promote data sharing, and improve agricultural efficiency and emissions reduction.

Mandates the Department of Agriculture, Department of Energy, and National Science Foundation to conduct joint R&D activities.

Requires establishing memoranda of understanding to coordinate efforts.

Authorizes collaborative research in AI, machine learning, large-scale data analytics, and predictive analysis to optimize agricultural and rural energy systems.

Facilitates development of methods for handling large data sets related to agriculture, environment, and supply chain.

Promotes open data sharing and collaboration between federal agencies, labs, educational and nonprofit institutions, industry, and more, ensuring compliance with federal regulations.

Supports infrastructure and workforce development for research identified as necessary by the involved agencies.

Permits reimbursable agreements and collaborations with other federal agencies to enhance R&D effectiveness.

Requires a report within two years detailing interagency coordination, achievements, future opportunities, and ongoing coordination efforts.

Stipulates consistency with existing research security regulations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Richard L. Trumka Protecting the Right to Organize Act of 2023, Sec. 309 (GAO Report)
document_name: Richard L. Trumka Protecting the Right to Organize Act of 2023, Sec. 309 (GAO Report)
body:
Analyze the impact of Sections 101(a) and 101(b) on technology and algorithm use. Require the Government Accountability Office to report findings to Congress. Allow the President to recommend legislative modifications based on these findings.

Mandates the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to study the impact of Sections 101(a) and 101(b) on employee coverage under the National Labor Relations Act, focusing on union formation and collective bargaining.

Requires the study to analyze impacts on employee flexibility, compensation, grievance resolution, and technology use, including AI and algorithms.

Directs the GAO to gather input from stakeholders, including business enterprises and labor organizations, consulting relevant congressional committees.

Obliges the GAO to report its findings to the House and Senate committees six months after the study begins and make the report public.

Instructs the President, after the report's release, to consider its findings and potentially recommend modifications to Sections 101(a) or 101(b) within 60 days.

Expresses the House's intent to evaluate any presidential recommendations regarding the modifications.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024
document_name: Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024
body:
Requires covered agencies to study and report on AI data and methodologies, assess compliance with federal laws, and recommend needed changes. Authorizes requiring disclosures from AI vendors and entities about model data, design, and function. Prioritizes immediate implementation where necessary.

Enacts the "Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024".

Mandates a study by covered agencies to establish and recommend standards for AI data categorization, AI model training practices, and data source identification.

Requires assessment of AI model design, functionality, and compliance with federal laws including anti-discrimination and consumer protection.

Obligates the issuance of a report within six months from enactment, detailing study findings and advising on potential legislative or regulatory revisions regarding AI disclosures.

Empowers covered agencies, post-report, to mandate AI data reporting and disclosure by regulated entities and vendors, including data sources and model training specifics.

Urges implementation of such requirements prior to report completion if deemed necessary.

Defines "covered agencies" as key financial regulatory bodies, and "regulated entities" as those overseen by these agencies, including credit unions and financially regulated persons.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety
document_name: Research and Development Program on New Approaches to Data Analysis for Aviation Safety
body:
Establishes a research program using AI and machine learning for aviation safety data analysis. Requires collaboration among FAA, NEXTOR III, NASA, and industry partners.

Establishes a new research and development program by the FAA’s NEXTOR III to develop new data analysis approaches for aviation safety.

Includes use of new algorithms and AI methods for analyzing various data sets such as weather, equipment performance, flight delays, safety incidents, and communications.

Requires collaboration among Consortium member institutions, aviation industry partners, FAA units, and NASA’s Aviation Safety Reporting System for data sharing and testing.

Prioritizes understanding human factors contributing to aviation safety risk, including fatigue, distraction, workload, organizational culture, communication, and adherence to safety procedures.

Seeks to improve the design of highly automated aircraft to reduce mode confusion and increase awareness of flight parameters.

Authorizes $20,000,000 annually from 2024 to 2029 for program execution, including grants to participating institutions and FAA units.

Terminates the program 6 years after establishment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Rail Worker and Community Safety Act, Sec. 13 (Equipment Inspections)
document_name: Rail Worker and Community Safety Act, Sec. 13 (Equipment Inspections)
body:
Require AI-based inspection technologies for rail inspections to be verified by a Qualified Mechanical Inspector.

Requires the Secretary of Transportation to issue regulations within 12 months of enactment.

Prohibits the movement of trains from switchyards before completing all required brake inspections.

Allows only Qualified Mechanical Inspectors to sign off on inspection forms for locomotives and rail cars.

Ensures that inspections using AI or camera-based systems for verification and validation of the check under part 215 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations by the Qualified Mechanical Inspector.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: RESTRICT Act
document_name: RESTRICT Act
body:
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to identify, prohibit, and mitigate risks from foreign adversary transactions and holdings involving AI, ICT, and other critical technologies, and allows the President to order divestment when such investments threaten national security.

Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to review, restrict, or prohibit certain information and communications technology (ICT) transactions between U.S. persons and foreign adversaries when they pose national security risks.

Empowers the Secretary to identify, deter, disrupt, investigate, or mitigate risks from covered transactions, which are broadly defined to include dealings with foreign adversaries or entities subject to their jurisdiction. 

Defines "covered transactions" broadly, including those involving foreign adversaries or entities under their jurisdiction.

Establishes procedures for the Secretary to refer covered holdings posing national security risks to the President, who can then compel divestment or take other actions to mitigate risks.

Prioritizes critical ICT areas such as AI, quantum computing, and telecommunications for evaluation.

Exempts actions from standard administrative and judicial reviews, limiting legal challenges to specific high courts.

Imposes civil and criminal penalties for violations, including fines, imprisonment, and forfeiture.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: REAL Political Advertisements Act
document_name: REAL Political Advertisements Act
body:
Requires political advertisements containing images or video generated with artificial intelligence to include clear disclaimers. Directs the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to define AI-generated content, issue implementing regulations, and report on compliance and enforcement.

Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require any political advertisement containing images or video footage generated in whole or in part using artificial intelligence to include a clear and conspicuous disclaimer, with specific formatting requirements for text, audio, video, and other media to ensure visibility and audibility.

Directs the Federal Election Commission to promulgate regulations within 120 days of enactment to implement the disclaimer requirement and define "content generated by artificial intelligence" to reflect both current and emerging uses of generative AI.

Requires the FEC to submit biennial reports to Congress assessing compliance and enforcement, recommending modifications, and identifying further measures to enhance transparency and accountability in political advertising.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: R U REAL Act
document_name: R U REAL Act
body:
Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to amend the Telemarketing Sales Rule to require the disclosure of artificial intelligence usage in telemarketing.

Directs the FTC to revise the Telemarketing Sales Rule to require the disclosure of AI usage to impersonate a human being in telemarketing.

Mandates the FTC to impose financial penalties on violators of this new rule, especially towards individuals and entities with the intent to defraud, cause harm, or wrongfully obtain anything of value through AI telemarketing techniques.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: QUIET Act
document_name: QUIET Act
body:
Directs Congress to amend the Communications Act of 1934 to require disclosure of the use of artificial intelligence in voice call or text message impersonations.

Directs Congress to amend the Communications Act of 1934 to mandate the disclosure of artificial intelligence usage in voice call or text message impersonations.

Mandates the imposition of financial penalties on those who fail to complete the required disclosure of artificial intelligence usage during robocalls.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Providing Individuals Various Opportunities for Technical Training to Build a Skills-Based Cyber Workforce Act of 2024
document_name: Cyber PIVOTT Act
body:
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish the "PIVOTT Program" for expanding cybersecurity education and training.

Requires CISA to partner with community colleges and technical schools to offer programs and internships aiming to build a skills-based cyber workforce.

Provides full scholarships to eligible students, covering all educational and associated costs.

Mandates a two-year service obligation in a cyber role for program participants, with exceptions for military service.

Specifies eligible institutions and program components, including skills-based exercises and internships.

Directs CISA to conduct outreach initiatives and host recruitment fairs.

Establishes program completion benefits, including access to a cyber training database and additional certification opportunities.

Sets terms for scholarship repayment if obligations are not met and allows for waiver of repayments in cases of hardship.

Outlines enrollment targets and requires reporting on program enrollment and CISA's education and training initiatives.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protecting the Information of our Vulnerable Adolescents, Children, and Youth Act
document_name: Kids PRIVACY Act
body:
Defines "process" as an operation, potentially automated, performed on "covered information" including collecting, disclosing, inferring, etc. Mandates "verifiable consent" before processing of data, data minimization, data access transparency, security measures, and limits to harmful practices.

Defines "process" as an operation, potentially automated, performed on "covered information" including collecting, disclosing, inferring, etc.

Mandates obtaining "verifiable consent" from teenagers or parents before processing their data.

Requires operators to minimize data collection and retain data only as necessary.

Obligates transparency and the provision of a clear privacy policy detailing data practices.

Prohibits targeted advertising and harmful data processing practices.

Establishes rights for teenagers and parents to access, correct, and delete data.

Imposes strict security measures for processing children's and teenagers' data.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act
document_name: Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act
body:
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to penalize false or misleading drug communications by social media influencers and healthcare providers. Requires guidance and regulations for telehealth providers. Authorizes FDA to conduct AI-enhanced market surveillance of drug promotions.

Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to impose civil penalties on social media influencers and healthcare providers who make false or misleading communications about prescription drugs.

Mandates the issuance of guidance within 180 days to define false or misleading communications and outline compliance procedures.

Expands the definition of "manufacturer, packer, or distributor" to include telehealth providers involved in drug advertising.

Requires reporting of payments related to drug promotion to the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

Authorizes market surveillance activities using AI to monitor prescription drug promotions on social media and coordinate efforts with the Federal Trade Commission.

Allocates $15 million annually for fiscal years 2025 to 2029 to support these activities.

Establishes a process for notifying drug manufacturers of non-compliant communications by influencers or healthcare providers.

Ensures the severability of the Act's provisions, maintaining validity even if parts are invalidated.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protecting Kids on Social Media Act
document_name: Protecting Kids on Social Media Act
body:
Prohibits social media platforms from using algorithmic recommendation systems for users under 18, and bans access of users under 13. Requires age verification and parental consent for minors on social media, and establishes enforcement mechanisms and a secure digital identification credential pilot program.

Requires social media platforms to verify the age of users beyond simple attestations, using current age verification technologies.

Prohibits social media platforms from allowing individuals under 13 from accessing their services.

Mandates parental or guardian consent for users under 18, requiring platforms to take reasonable steps to verify this consent.

Prohibits the use of algorithmic recommendation systems on individuals under 18, except for contextual suggestions or advertising.

Establishes a Pilot Program for secure digital identification credentials to facilitate age and parental consent verification, overseen by the Secretary of Commerce.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state attorneys general to enforce compliance, with civil penalties for violations.

Grants extraterritorial jurisdiction for violations involving individuals in the United States.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
document_name: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
body:
Directs the NIST to establish task forces to develop standards for identifying AI-generated content. Mandates disclosures of AI origins through robust watermarks and content provenance metadata.

Directs the NIST to establish task forces focused on the development of technical guidelines for identifying and labeling AI-generated content, including metadata, watermarking, and digital fingerprinting.

Supports the development of standards to provide cryptographically verifiable content provenance metadata and robust watermarks. 

Requires providers of generative AI applications to ensure that content created or modified by such applications includes a disclosure of its AI origin, and to collaborate with providers of covered online platforms to provide these disclosures to users.

Prohibits online platforms from removing such disclosures and mandates clear display of AI origin information to users.

Enforces compliance under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Defines self-regulatory guidelines approved by the FTC as compliance alternatives.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024
document_name: Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024
body:
Establishes competitive processes for AI, cloud, and data infrastructure procurement by the Department of Defense, prioritizing security and data rights. Requires updates to regulations for data protection and penalties. Mandates reports on AI market competition and innovation to congressional committees.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to require competitive awards for cloud computing, data infrastructure, and foundation model solutions to promote security, resiliency, and competition.

Ensures that the Government retains exclusive data access and use rights.

Requires prioritization of intellectual property, data rights, and interoperability during procurement processes, with consideration for multi-cloud technology where suitable.

Directs updates to the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to protect government-furnished data used in AI development and prevent unauthorized disclosure.

Imposes penalties for violations, including fines and contract termination, but allows exemptions where national security is not compromised.

Obliges annual reports from the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff assessing competition and market dynamics in the AI industry, with recommendations for legislative and administrative actions.

Ensures public accessibility of these reports through the Department of Defense's website and other no-cost methods.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023
document_name: Protect Working Musicians Act of 2023
body:
Limits liability under antitrust laws for Individual Music Creator Owners who collectively negotiate or refuse licensing to Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms or companies developing or deploying generative AI. Specifies conditions for collective negotiations, ensuring consistency with antitrust laws.

Grants Independent Music Creator Owners immunity from antitrust liability for collectively negotiating music licensing terms with Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms or developing or deploying generative AI.

Defines "generative artificial intelligence" as AI systems generating novel text, video, images, audio, or other media based on prompts.

Defines “Individual Music Creator Owner” as an individual or group of musicians, producers, mixers, or sound engineers who own their copyrights and either earn less than $1 million annually in licensing revenue or qualify as a small business.

Defines “Dominant Online Music Distribution Platform” as an online service for listening to sound recordings with over $100 million in annual music-related revenue, excluding entities eligible for certain statutory licenses.

Requires that collective negotiations among Independent Music Creator Owners be nondiscriminatory, not limited to price, and directly related to negotiations with Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms or generative AI companies.

Ensures that collective negotiations do not involve parties other than Independent Music Creator Owners, Dominant Online Music Distribution Platforms, or generative AI companies.

Stipulates that the Act does not modify, impair, or supersede existing antitrust laws beyond the specified provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2024
document_name: Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits producing or distributing digital forgeries of intimate visuals without consent, with penalties up to 5 years imprisonment or fines. Exempts good faith distributions for specific purposes. Excludes service providers unless reckless. Defines digital forgery. Establishes extraterritorial jurisdiction. Ensures severability.

Prohibits the production or distribution of digital forgeries of intimate visual depictions of identifiable individuals without their consent, under penalty of fines or imprisonment up to 5 years.

Exempts distributions made in good faith to law enforcement, during legal proceedings, for medical purposes, or in reporting/investigating unlawful content or conduct.

Excludes communications service providers from liability unless they knowingly or recklessly distribute such content.

Defines "digital forgery" as intimate visual depictions created or altered using software, machine learning, AI, or other computer-generated means to appear authentic.

Establishes extraterritorial jurisdiction if the offender or victim is a U.S. national.

Ensures severability of the Act’s provisions if any part is found unconstitutional.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
document_name: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
body:
Prohibits knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated media related to Federal elections.

Prohibits knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media related to Federal election activities or candidates. Exempts broadcasters, streaming services, and periodicals if they disclose authenticity concerns and covers bona fide news or satire. 

Allows affected candidates to seek injunctive relief or damages, including attorney's fees, for violations. Requires plaintiffs to prove violations with clear and convincing evidence.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting United States Leadership in Standards Act of 2024
document_name: US Leadership in Standards Act
body:
