Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to increase U.S. participation in AI standards development. Establishes a pilot program to support U.S. meetings on AI standards. Requires web portal creation and congressional briefings on progress and effectiveness.

Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to brief Congress on opportunities for U.S. participation in developing AI standards within one year.

Requires the establishment of a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international AI standards efforts and participation opportunities.

Mandates federal agencies to report their participation in AI standards activities using a mechanism developed by the NIST.

Initiates a pilot program to support U.S.-based AI standards meetings through grants to eligible entities, with funding covering up to 50% of meeting costs.

Authorizes $10 million for the pilot program from fiscal years 2024 through 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting Responsible Evaluation and Procurement to Advance Readiness for Enterprise-wide Deployment for Artificial Intelligence Act
document_name: PREPARED for AI Act
body:
Establishes a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers Council. Mandates risk classification for AI use. Prohibits specific AI activities, including emotion detection. Directs procurement updates. Requires AI risk evaluation and monitoring. Stipulates documentation and transparency. Establishes annual reporting. Prohibits high-risk AI uses.

Requires the establishment of a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers Council to coordinate AI use in federal agencies.

Mandates agencies to develop risk classification systems for AI use cases, categorizing them as unacceptable, high, medium, or low risk.

Prohibits AI use for certain activities, such as mapping facial features for emotion detection or categorizing individuals based on biometric data for sensitive traits.

Directs updates to the Federal Acquisition Regulation to ensure AI procurement includes risk and impact assessments.

Requires agencies to implement processes for evaluating AI risks and to conduct ongoing monitoring, especially for high-risk use cases.

Stipulates comprehensive documentation and transparency requirements for AI models and data.

Establishes annual reporting protocols for obstacles in AI testing and evaluation, promoting interagency collaboration to address challenges.

Prohibits the use of AI for certain high-risk applications and mandates public disclosure of AI inventories and risk classifications.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2023
document_name: Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act
body:
Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote U.S. leadership in AI and strengthen supply chains. Mandates a resiliency program. Requires coordination with agencies. Promotes domestic manufacturing. Supports best practices. Mandates regular reporting on AI supply chains.

Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote U.S. leadership in emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), and strengthen critical supply chains and national security.

Mandates the establishment of a critical supply chain resiliency and crisis response program within the Department of Commerce, which includes mapping and monitoring AI supply chains.

Requires coordination with other agencies, industry, and international partners to identify vulnerabilities and prepare for supply chain shocks affecting AI technologies.

Promotes the growth of domestic manufacturing capacities for AI and other emerging technologies and encourages the relocation of manufacturing facilities to the U.S. or allied countries.

Supports the development and dissemination of best practices for supply chain resilience, including the use of blockchain and other technologies to authenticate and trace critical goods.

Mandates regular reporting on the state of AI and other emerging technology supply chains, including assessments of vulnerabilities and recommendations for enhancing resilience.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023
document_name: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2023
body:
Requires the secretary to work with the Director of the National Institute of Standard and Technology and the Federal Communication Commission to develop percussion of agriculture and practices to approach new precision agriculture with private company standards. Mandates a study every 2 years and then the following 8 years to ensure these standards are up to date. These studies are voluntary and the coordination with the consensus standard is voluntary.

Requires the Secretary of Agriculture, to coordinate with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission to advance on Precision Agriculture.

Focuses on, Global positioning system, satellites, yield monitors, soil mapping, sensors for gathering data on crops, internet and other forms of technology. 

Requires these standards to address the evolving demands and connectivity needs of precision agriculture and consider cybersecurity challenges and the impact of AI and advanced wireless technology. Including the demands of growing need for precision agriculture in the US. 

Ensure that this technology has the support of these offices by conducting repeated studies that are up to the private companies standards. 

Mandates a study every 2 years and then the following 8 years to ensure these standards are up to date. These studies are voluntary and the coordination with the consensus standard is voluntary.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act
document_name: Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act
body:
Defines privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) and instructs the National Science Foundation to support research on them. Directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy to coordinate with NSF, NIST, and the FTC to accelerate PET development and use, and to report to Congress on implementation.

Defines “privacy-enhancing technologies” (PETs) to include methods such as differential privacy, synthetic data, and federated learning.

Instructs the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support PET research by awarding research projects related to privacy preserving technologies including algorithms, machine learning, and other computational processes used to protect privacy when handling data.

Amends (D) of 4(a)(1) of the Cybersecurity Research and Development Act.

Directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) to coordinate with NSF, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to accelerate the development, deployment, and use of PETs.

Requires OSTP to report to Congress on progress made in advancing PET research and policy recommendations to improve interagency coordination using PETs.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024
document_name: Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits rental property owners from using coordinators to manipulate rental prices. Prohibits coordinators from facilitating non-competitive agreements and engaging in anti-competitive mergers. Empowers the FTC and state attorneys general to enforce the Act.

Prohibits rental property owners from using coordinators for algorithmic price coordination, deeming such actions per se violations of the Sherman Act.

Prohibits coordinators from facilitating non-competitive agreements among rental property owners or performing coordinating functions.

Prohibits coordinators from acquiring another coordinator if it lessens competition, violating the Clayton Act.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission, the Attorney General, and State Attorneys General to enforce the Act with the same powers and duties as the FTC Act, Sherman Act, and Clayton Act.

Allows civil actions by injured persons to recover treble damages and litigation costs, with the option to invalidate pre-dispute arbitration agreements.

Clarifies that the Act does not preempt State, Tribal, or local laws that supplement its provisions.

Ensures severability of the Act if any provision is deemed unconstitutional, maintaining the effectiveness of remaining provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preventing PLA Acquisition of United States Technology Act of 2023
document_name: Preventing PLA Tech Acquisition
body:
Prohibits federal entities from partnering or collaborating with specific Chinese institutions (that engage in on technologies, including AI. Requires creating a website listing these technologies and entities. Demands annual reports and audits on research relationships with said Chinese entities.

Prohibits covered U.S. entities from engaging in scientific research or technical exchanges with Chinese entities of concern, particularly in technologies like AI, identified as priorities in China's military-civil fusion strategy.

Requires the Secretary of Defense, with other officials, to maintain a website listing prohibited scientific research areas and Chinese entities of concern.

Mandates covered entities to report annually on any research relationships with Chinese entities of concern and allows audits to ensure compliance.

Precludes entities violating prohibitions from receiving federal financial assistance.

Permits exceptions for fields not substantially contributing to military-civil fusion.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to issue regulations to enforce these provisions and coordinate enforcement across federal agencies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act
document_name: Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act
body:
Establishes a task force to help formulate appropriate AI regulations in the financial services industry and requires the task force to produce a report for Congress with these recommendations within one year.

Establishes a task force examining the fraudulent use of artificial intelligence in the financial services sector.

Instruct the task force to solicit public feedback from industry and expert stakeholders, including depository institutions, credit unions, third-party vendors, and AI experts.

Directs the task force to produce a report for Congress within one year that identifies potential risks from AI misuse, and proposes AI fraud detection measures, among other legislative recommendations.

Terminates the task force 90 days after the final report's issue.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024
document_name: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits using pricing algorithms trained with nonpublic competitor data. Requires detailed reporting and certification of pricing algorithms used in commerce. Mandates transparency in algorithmic pricing for entities with over $5 million revenue. Establishes penalties for violations. Directs FTC to study pricing algorithms' impact.

Prohibits the use of pricing algorithms incorporating nonpublic competitor data.

Requires entities using or distributing pricing algorithms to submit detailed reports to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) or Attorney General upon request, detailing development, data usage, and algorithmic rules.

Mandates certification of report accuracy by a high-level corporate officer.

Ensures confidentiality of submitted reports, allowing information sharing only between the Department of Justice, FTC, and National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Imposes civil penalties for violations, including fines and injunctive relief.

Presumes collusive behavior in antitrust cases involving certain uses of pricing algorithms, allowing for rebuttal and assigning joint liability.

Obligates disclosure to customers and employees when prices or terms are set by algorithms, including specifics on price discrimination and third-party algorithm developers.

Directs the FTC to study and report on the impact and prevalence of pricing algorithms within two years, including potential consumer harm and benefits.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities Act
document_name: Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities Act
body:
Defines “covered sectors” to include artificial intelligence and directs the President to identify such technologies posing national security risks when developed or acquired by countries of concern. Requires regulations to prohibit certain covered activities, mandate notification for others, and authorizes enforcement, reporting, and penalties to implement these restrictions.

Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in covered activities involving certain technologies and products in countries of concern, particularly in sectors like AI, if they pose acute national security threats.

Requires the President to annually identify and publish lists of such critical technologies and products.

Mandates U.S. persons to notify the President of any covered activities that may threaten national security.

Directs the President to issue implementing regulations defining covered activities and compliance procedures, subject to public notice and comment. 

Empowers the President to impose civil penalties for violations and to delegate enforcement authority to federal agencies.

Requires periodic reporting to Congress assessing notifications, regulatory effectiveness, and potential amendments.

Directs the Secretary of State to conduct bilateral and multilateral engagement with allied governments to promote comparable screening mechanisms.

Allocates $25 million annually for implementation and allows direct hiring to support administration.

Permits the President to issue waivers for activities deemed in the national interest, with required congressional notification.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preserving Telehealth, Hospital, and Ambulance Access Act, Sec. 105 (Report on Wearable Medical Devices)
document_name: Preserving Telehealth, Hospital, and Ambulance Access Act, Sec. 105 (Report on Wearable Medical Devices)
body:
Requires the Comptroller General to assess and report on wearable medical devices' capabilities and limitations in clinical decision-making, focusing on AI's benefits and challenges, and proposing policy options to enhance benefits and mitigate challenges.

Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a technology assessment of wearable medical devices within 18 months of the Act's enactment.

Requires the report to include an analysis of the devices' potential to accurately prescribe treatments.

Examines the benefits and challenges of using artificial intelligence to augment wearable medical devices.

Proposes policy options to enhance benefits and mitigate challenges in developing or using such devices.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
document_name: Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
body:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Safety Review Office to evaluate AI models for national security risks, requires AI developers to follow red-teaming and cybersecurity standards, and prohibits deploying risky AI models.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Safety Review Office to oversee national security risks from advanced AI, particularly chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and cyber threats.

Mandates developers of AI models with significant computational power to report red-teaming and cybersecurity practices, and compliance with safety standards.

Requires evaluations and pre-deployment reviews for AI models posing potential threats, overseen by an Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Safety.

Orders the creation of standards for know-your-customer protocols and red-teaming techniques to mitigate advanced AI risks.

Permits the Attorney General to enforce compliance, with civil fines up to $1,000,000 daily and potential imprisonment for violations.

Allocates $50,000,000 for implementing these measures to ensure AI advancements remain secure and beneficial for U.S. interests.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
document_name: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
body:
Requires the Election Assistance Commission to issue voluntary guidelines addressing AI use and risks in election administration. Includes guidelines on AI benefits, cybersecurity risks, accurate information sharing, and combating election disinformation impacting public trust.

Cites the Act as the “Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act”.

Requires the Election Assistance Commission to submit a report with voluntary guidelines to Congress, State and local election offices, and the public within 60 days of enactment.

Includes guidelines addressing the risks and benefits of using AI in election administration.

Addresses the cybersecurity risks posed by AI technologies in elections.

Guides on managing AI-generated information to ensure the sharing of accurate election information.

Provides guidance on how to distribute and generate information from AI and prevent it from creating disinformation during elections that undermines public trust.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
document_name: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
body:
Requires the Election Assistance Commission to develop voluntary guidelines addressing AI use and risks in elections, emphasizing AI's role in election disinformation. Directs a study on AI's impact in the 2024 elections, with findings used to update guidelines.

Requires the Election Assistance Commission to develop and issue voluntary guidelines for election offices addressing the use and risks of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in election administration within 60 days of enactment.

Mandates inclusion of guidelines on the risks and benefits of AI in election activities, cybersecurity risks, the impact of AI-generated information on sharing accurate election information, and the spread of election disinformation.

Directs the Election Assistance Commission to study and report on the use and impacts of AI technologies in the 2024 federal elections by November 5, 2025, including the sharing of AI-generated information and the use of AI by election offices.

Requires the Election Assistance Commission to review and update the voluntary guidelines based on the study's findings.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023
document_name: Political BIAS Emails Act of 2023
body:
Prohibits email providers from flagging elected political emails as spam without user direction. Requires quarterly transparency reports on flagged political emails. Mandates data disclosure to campaigns upon request. Obliges providers to offer email deliverability best practices. Enforces via FTC. Defines key terms.

Prohibits email service providers from using filtering algorithms to flag emails from political campaigns that consumers have elected to receive as spam without user direction.

Requires providers to publish quarterly transparency reports detailing instances of political emails flagged as spam, including breakdowns by political party and filtering algorithm usage.

Mandates email providers to disclose specific spam-filtering data to political campaigns upon request, with limitations on request frequency.

Obliges providers to offer best practices to political campaigns for improving email deliverability to primary inboxes.

Enforces these provisions through the Federal Trade Commission, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Defines key terms including “filtering algorithm,” “operator,” and “political campaign.”

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority")
document_name: Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority")
body:
Mandates regulations for data provision, public content repositories, and ad disclosure. Compels algorithm reporting and content moderation transparency.

Requires platforms to make available public repositories of highly disseminated content and major public accounts, including content samples and metadata.

Obligates platforms to disclose advertising information, including ad content, targeting parameters, and dissemination metrics, while protecting user privacy.

Requires disclosure of the use of platform algorithms in the recommendation, amplification, or restriction of content and advertising

Compels platforms to report on recommender and ranking algorithms, detailing inputs, objectives, and significant changes, without revealing trade secrets.

Demands transparency in content moderation, with statistics on policy violations, identification methods (including artificial intelligence), and government orders.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Threats to Health Security")
document_name: Pandemic Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("AI Threats to Health Security")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to contract the National Academies to assess AI vulnerabilities, including open-source and large language models, to health security. Includes roles, responsibilities, and risk mitigation recommendations. Mandates initial and follow-up implementation reports from the National Academies to Congress on findings and subsequent health security actions.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to seek a contract with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct a study on AI-related health security vulnerabilities within 45 days of enactment.

Mandates the study to assess risks posed by AI advancements, including those related to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats, and the ways AI may enable, enhance, or protect against such threats.

Describes roles and capabilities of HHS agencies and other Federal entities in identifying, preparing for, and mitigating these vulnerabilities.

Summarizes ongoing Federal activities related to the identification, understanding, and mitigation of these risks.

Identifies current or anticipated gaps in roles, responsibilities, and capabilities regarding AI-related health security.

Provides recommendations for improving Federal efforts to identify, prepare for, and mitigate these vulnerabilities.

Requires the National Academies to submit a report on the study to the Senate HELP Committee and the House Energy and Commerce Committee within 2 years.

Mandates the Secretary of HHS to submit a follow-up report on actions taken to mitigate AI-related health security risks within 1 year after the National Academies’ report.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: PATHS Act
document_name: PATHS Act
body:
Extends the authority for AI-related transactions under the Homeland Security Act to 2027. Requires notification and briefing to Congress within 72 hours of using AI transaction authority. Reduces covered contract award amounts from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000.

Extends the research and development acquisition pilot program under the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to September 30, 2027.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to notify and brief Congress within 72 hours regarding the use or extension of transaction authority involving artificial intelligence technology.

Reduces the threshold for covered contract awards from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000 under the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: PAID Act, Sec. 3 (Requirements for Private Passenger Automobile Insurers)
document_name: PAID Act, Sec. 3 (Requirements for Private Passenger Automobile Insurers)
body:
Prohibits insurers from using specific personal factors, including gender and credit score, to determine car insurance rates. Requires submission to FTC to ensure no disparate impacts from algorithms. Mandates public access to underwriting rules.

Recognize that auto insurance is required in all states except New Hampshire, and that driving uninsured can lead to serious penalties.

Recognize that many insurers use variables to determine what consumers pay based on individual details (income proxies), not actual crash risk, which can block customers from preferred rates.

Prohibit auto insurers from using certain personal factors to decide whether a consumer can get coverage or what a consumer pays.

Prohibit insurers from considering gender, education level, job or occupation, employment status, homeownership status, ZIP code, census tract, marital status, credit score, consumer reports, previous insurer, or prior purchase of insurance from that insurer when determining eligibility or price.

Require insurers to submit information to the FTC within one year of enactment and every two years thereafter.

Require insurers to provide the FTC information showing that their marketing, underwriting, pricing, claims handling, fraud investigations, and any algorithms or models used in these activities do not create a disparate impact.

Require insurers to make underwriting rules and rate filings available for public inspection.

Clarify what counts as a violation and prohibit any use of banned factors that raises costs, restricts coverage, or blocks discounts.

Preserve the authority of federal and state agencies to enforce prohibitions against unfair or deceptive practices.

Recognize that state regulations still apply and that federal law overrides state law only to the extent a state rule conflicts with this Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Oversee Emerging Technology Act
document_name: Oversee Emerging Technology Act
body:
Requires federal agencies substantially engaged with emerging technologies to appoint a senior official as an emerging technology lead. Tasks them with advising on AI use, policy expertise, interagency collaboration, and procurement input. Mandates informing Congress of appointments and responsibilities.

Requires the head of each covered federal agency engaged in emerging technologies to appoint or designate a Senior Executive Service individual or equivalent as an emerging technology lead.

Mandates that these leads advise agencies on the responsible use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Obliges these leads to provide expertise on responsible policies and practices, collaborate with interagency bodies, and input on procurement policies.

Instructs the President to inform Congress within 180 days of enactment about the appointed leads and their authorities and responsibilities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Outbound Investment Transparency Act of 2023
document_name: Outbound Investment Transparency Act
body:
Amends the Defense Production Act to establish an investment screening mechanism targeting AI and other sensitive sectors. Requires U.S. persons to notify the Treasury of certain investments in countries of concern. Mandates annual reporting and promotes international coordination.

Requires mandatory notification by U.S. persons engaging in specific foreign investments related to advanced sectors, including artificial intelligence, to the Secretary of the Treasury.

Defines covered activities involving equity interests, debt obligations with governance rights, and joint ventures in countries of concern, with specific focus on AI and other advanced technologies.

Establishes penalties for non-compliance, including failure to notify or providing false information.

Mandates the creation of regulations to ensure clarity and minimize compliance burdens, with a focus on transparency and stakeholder involvement.

Directs the Secretary of State to engage with allied countries to coordinate investment screening mechanisms and share information on covered activities.

Requires annual reporting to Congress on trends, national security risks, and recommendations related to these foreign investments in AI and other sectors.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Open Translation Center Act of 2024
document_name: Open Translation Center Act
body:
Establishes the Open Translation Center to translate and analyze documents from designated countries using AI and other technologies. Requires a board to oversee, appoints members from relevant government agencies, and mandates cooperation with U.S. and foreign entities.

Establishes the Open Translation Center (OTC) to translate and analyze foreign language materials from designated countries for public dissemination, enhancing understanding of foreign governments, economies, and cultures.

Administers OTC either as a separate entity or a nonprofit and requires a governing board of five appointed members with relevant expertise, independent of the U.S. Government.

Tasks OTC with translating documents into English, providing analyses, and making materials publicly available while respecting copyright laws.

Requests OTC to use software, programs, artificial intelligence, and other technologies to ensure timely translations.

Requires cooperation with federal agencies and stakeholders, and authorizes consultation with foreign governments after certification by the Secretary of State.

Designates the Secretary of State as the primary sponsor, with potential sponsorship from other federal agencies such as the CIA.

Allocates funding of $85 million for fiscal year 2024 and $80 million for subsequent years through 2028 for OTC operations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Online Privacy Act of 2023, Sec. 106 ("Right to individual autonomy")
document_name: Online Privacy Act, Sec. 106 ("Individual autonomy")
body:
Prohibits collecting, processing, maintaining, or disclosing personal information for behavioral personalization without consent. Requires annual consent renewals. Mandates non-personalized versions if consent is denied. Allows service denial if non-personalization is infeasible. Exempts small businesses.

Prohibits covered entities from collecting, processing, maintaining, or disclosing personal information for behavioral personalization without affirmative express consent.

Requires covered entities to obtain express affirmative consent before providing behaviorally personalized products or services, and annually thereafter.

Mandates providing non-personalized versions of products or services if consent is denied, or core aspects if full functionality without personalization is infeasible.

Allows denial of products or services if no core aspect can function without personalization and consent is not given.

Permits processing personal information for usability improvements using aggregated data, provided the output is uniform and independent of individual characteristics.

Excludes optimizations aimed primarily at increasing user engagement time from the definition of "usability."

Exempts small businesses from these requirements.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act
document_name: Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Novel, Advanced Spectrum and Communications Technology Networks Promotion Act
document_name: Advanced Communications Technology Networks Act
body:
Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to support the establishment and implementation of technologies for electromagnetic spectrum management, including artificial intelligence systems.

Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to support the establishment, prototyping, and implementation of technologies for electromagnetic spectrum management, such as artificial intelligence systems for operating advanced antenna arrays and artificial intelligence systems to enable dynamic spectrum access.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: No ICBMs or Drones for Iran Act of 2023
document_name: No ICBMs or Drones for Iran Act of 2023
body:
Expands and incorporates sanctions related to Iranian unmanned aerial systems (UAS). Mandates a strategy against, and reports on support for, Iran’s UAS program.

Expands sanctions under the Comprehensive Iran Sanctions, Accountability, and Divestment Act of 2010 to include unmanned aerial systems (UAS).

Incorporates UAS under arms embargos of the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act and Iran-Iraq Arms Non-Proliferation Act of 1992.

Requires the President to submit a strategy to counter Iran's UAS program including export controls of US materials, identification of actors supporting Iran's UAS program, assessment of compliance with such restrictions, and coordination with US allies in furtherance of these actions

Mandates a report on support for Iran’s UAS program from domestic industries, individuals, or entities in Iran and related technology transfers to foreign actors, to be updated as necessary.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: No CCP Consultants Act
document_name: No CCP Consultants Act
body:
Prohibits the Department of State from working with contractors who have previously consulted for or fail to disclose conflicts of interest relating to foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns, including any Chinese state-owned entity or entity under the ownership and control of the PRC or CCP that is engaged in national security industries, such as producing AI-related products and services.

Prohibits the Department of State from entering, renewing, or extending a contract to contractors that, in the past year, have consulted for foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns, including any entity under China’s control engaged in national security industries, such as producing AI-related products and services. 

Requires companies seeking to provide consulting services for the Department of State to disclose any conflict of interest with foreign entities above, or they may face a debarment of up to five years.

Requires the Secretary of the Department of State to issue procurement policies for the Department to implement the above prohibition, clarify disclosure requirements and penalties when soliciting contracts, and share best practices for how companies can avoid accidentally contracting with foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: No AI FRAUD Act
document_name: No AI FRAUD Act
body:
Establishes property rights in likeness and voice, transferable post-mortem for ten years. Prohibits unauthorized cloning and replicas, imposing liabilities. Specifies damages per violation. Allows punitive damages and attorney fees. Provides First Amendment defense. Exempts negligible harm. Sets four-year limitations period.

Establishes property rights for individuals in their likeness and voice, treating them as intellectual property that is transferable and descendible for ten years post-mortem.

Prohibits unauthorized distribution, transmission, or availability of personalized cloning services, digital voice replicas, or digital depictions without the individual’s consent, imposing liabilities for violations.

Specifies that unauthorized use incurs damages of $50,000 per violation for cloning services and $5,000 per violation for voice replicas or depictions, plus actual damages and profits.

Allows for punitive damages and attorney fees for injured parties and invalidates disclaimers as a defense.

Provides a First Amendment defense, balancing public interest with intellectual property rights, and considers commercial use and impact on the value of the original work.

Exempts negligible harm from liability and defines harm to include financial, physical, and severe emotional distress.

Sets a four-year limitations period for civil actions and ensures no preemption of other rights or laws.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: No AI Audits Act
document_name: No AI Audits Act
body:
Limits IRS use of AI for audits by requiring guidance as rule-making and adherence to NIST explainability principles. Requires Comptroller General to audit and report on IRS's AI use. Mandates that only IRS staff can initiate taxpayer investigations.

Limits the Internal Revenue Service's (IRS) use of artificial intelligence (AI) for audits or investigations.

Requires any IRS guidance on AI for audits to follow rule-making procedures under Section 553 of Title 5, U.S. Code.

Prohibits the IRS from conducting audits or investigations initiated by AI unless the AI meets explainability principles set by the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Mandates the Comptroller General to audit and report on the IRS's AI use, including a cost-benefit analysis and the impact on taxpayer rights.

Stipulates that IRS investigations or examinations must be initiated by a staff investigator, with documentation including the investigator's contact information.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Next Generation Military Education Act
document_name: Next Generation Military Education Act
body:
Requires the Department of Defense to develop AI and machine learning courses for military personnel, expand the Digital On-Demand Program to all members and employees, and incorporate AI risks into annual cybersecurity training.

Amends the National Defense Authorization Act to require the Department of Defense to develop and provide distance education courses on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for Armed Forces personnel.

Mandates these courses to cover AI literacy, ethical use, data protection, and awareness of AI-generated content.

Requires military departments to ensure access and notify personnel about these courses.

Obligates the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress on the progress of these activities.

Expands participation in the Digital On-Demand Program to all Department of Defense entities and personnel, promoting AI education.

Incorporates AI risks and threats into annual cybersecurity training for Armed Forces and civilian Department of Defense employees.

Requires annual reporting to Congress on the expansion and promotion of the Digital On-Demand Program. 

Defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence" and "Digital On-Demand Program."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Windstorm Impact Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2024
document_name: National Windstorm Impact Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2024
body:
Integrates machine learning and advanced technologies into windstorm research, supporting interdisciplinary collaborations. Enhances understanding of climate change impacts on windstorms. Allocates funding for research, infrastructure, and resilience measures to mitigate windstorm effects across diverse communities.

Amends the National Windstorm Impact Reduction Act of 2004 to include provisions for understanding climate variability and its impact on windstorms, aiming to inform future building codes.

Supports the integration of emerging technologies, such as machine learning, in research and engineering activities related to windstorm mitigation.

Encourages interdisciplinary research, including collaborations between social scientists and engineers, to enhance atmospheric measurements relevant to building engineering.

Promotes the use of advanced construction methods and materials to strengthen properties against windstorms and related impacts.

Mandates an analysis of the need for a tornado research facility to study tornado impacts on buildings.

Requires research into public response to windstorm risks and factors influencing risk communication and reduction measures.

Allocates specific funding amounts for the program from fiscal years 2025 to 2029.

Sets deadlines for reports and analyses, including future research infrastructure needs, to be completed by specified dates.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies)
document_name: National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies)
body:
Assigns responsibilities to various U.S. agencies for wildland fire research, prediction, and mitigation, including AI-driven data analysis and modeling. Focuses on developing tools, improving fire-weather forecasts, enhancing coordination, and promoting fire-resistant infrastructure and practices.

Mandates NIST to conduct research on wildland fire impacts, firebrands, novel materials, and performance-based mitigation tools.

Requires NIST to coordinate federal wildland-urban interface fire investigations and develop methodologies for assessing fire impacts on communities.

Directs NSF to support research on wildland fire risks, tools, technologies, and the social and economic factors influencing fire risk reduction.

Instructs NOAA to improve wildland fire understanding through research, weather forecasting, data interoperability, and high-performance computing.

Tasks NOAA with establishing a Fire Weather Testbed and supporting extramural research on wildland fires.

Requires FEMA to support community risk assessment tools, public outreach, and best practices for fire-resistant construction and response.

Directs NASA to support wildland fire research, modeling, data systems, and the development of novel monitoring tools.

Instructs EPA to research wildland fire smoke characteristics, impacts on air and water quality, and communication of risk reduction strategies.

Mandates DOE to develop tools for energy sector resilience to wildland fires and coordinate data resources for improved fire understanding and prevention.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Strategy to Utilize Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Efforts Act
document_name: Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Act
body: Requires the President to develop a national strategy for using microreactors in natural disaster response. Involves consultation with multiple federal agencies and includes assessments, goals, and recommendations for deploying microreactors efficiently and safely, emphasizing technological integration and partnerships.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act, Sec. 16 ("Department of Energy Quantum Information Science Research Program")
document_name: National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act, Sec. 16 ("DOE Quantum Information Science Research Program")
body:
Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to require the Department of Energy to enhance quantum information science research, including AI integration, through new research centers, strategic planning, and industry outreach, with up to $130 million annually authorized through 2027.

Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to mandate the Secretary of Energy to implement a quantum information science, engineering, and technology research program.

Establishes National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to advance quantum technology, networking, sensing, and communications infrastructure.

Requires cooperative research initiatives with industry, National Laboratories, and academic institutions, covering artificial intelligence, machine learning, quantum communications, sensing, networking, and other quantum technologies.

Mandates providing research experiences and training for students in quantum-related fields.

Directs the creation of a 10-year strategic plan for quantum high-performance computing that integrates artificial intelligence and machine learning, to be submitted to Congress.

Supports outreach to industry to promote commercialization and energy-sector applications of quantum technology.

Authorizes up to $130 million annually from fiscal years 2024 through 2027 to carry out these activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Patient Safety Board Act of 2024
document_name: National Patient Safety Board Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the National Patient Safety Board (NPSB) to prevent patient safety events. Empowers NPSB to monitor, study, and propose solutions. Grants authority to request changes and review reports. Mandates annual audits. Forms Patient Safety Research Division. Requires privacy and AI compliance. Prohibits use in civil cases.

Establishes the National Patient Safety Board (NPSB) within the Office of the Secretary of Health and Human Services to prevent and reduce patient safety events.

Empowers the NPSB to support federal agencies in monitoring patient safety, studying causes of patient safety events, and formulating preventive solutions.

Grants the NPSB authority to request changes to patient safety measures, review reports, and make them publicly available within one year of study commencement.

Mandates annual audits and reports to Congress on progress, including detailed solutions and unaddressed needs.

Forms a Patient Safety Research and Development Division to aggregate and analyze patient-level data, identifying and anticipating safety events and disparities.

Requires compliance with privacy laws and AI governance frameworks, including NIST's AI Risk Management Framework and the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.

Prohibits the use of NPSB reports as evidence in civil liability cases but allows their use in developing standards of care.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Mesonet Authorization Act
document_name: National Mesonet Authorization Act
body:
Establishes the National Mesonet Program to improve weather observations using non-Federal data sources. Prioritizes collaboration with commercial, academic, and other sectors. Provides financial support for enhancing data collection capabilities. Mandates regular reporting and sets funding allocations through 2028.

Establishes the National Mesonet Program within the National Weather Service to improve weather observation and forecasting.

Requires the program to leverage commercial, academic, and other non-Federal weather data to enhance coordination across sectors.

Targets improved environmental observations to support baseline forecasts and warnings, and to enhance numerical weather prediction performance.

Mandates integration of greater density and types of weather observations, including local and regional networks and satellite constellations.

Provides financial and technical assistance for State, Tribal, private, and academic entities to build or upgrade mesonet systems, contingent on agreements to share data.

Forms an advisory committee to recommend improvements and expansions of available data.

Obligates regular briefings to relevant Congressional committees on program activities and progress.

Allocates specified funding amounts for fiscal years 2024 through 2028 to support the program's implementation and expansion.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VII ("Department of Homeland Security Activities")
document_name: Drone R&D Act, Title VII ("DHS Activities")
body:
Establishes research support for advanced air mobility and unmanned aircraft systems, emphasizing cybersecurity, safety, and data management. Creates a Counter-UAS Center of Excellence. Allocates funding for research, development, and coordination with federal agencies to prevent duplicative efforts.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to support research, development, evaluation, and testing of advanced air mobility, unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), and counter-UAS systems.

Directs coordination with relevant Department of Homeland Security offices and programs, including the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

Requires production of standardized, secure, and privacy-protected data sets for advanced air mobility and UAS systems.

Supports establishing one or more Institutes to advance research in these fields.

Establishes a Counter-UAS Center of Excellence within the Department of Homeland Security.

Specifies selection criteria for host institutions, emphasizing past performance, geographic proximity to federal facilities, and capabilities in AI and machine learning.

Permits use of funds for fundamental research, evaluation, education, and training related to counter-UAS systems.

Sets the federal share of grants at no more than 75% of costs.

Authorizes appropriations totaling $30 million to $36.5 million from fiscal years 2024 to 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title VI ("Department of Energy Activities")
document_name: Drone R&D Act, Title VI ("DOE Activities")
body:
Advances unmanned aircraft systems and AI technologies through research, education, and financial support. Establishes data management strategies and interagency coordination. Allocates funding from fiscal years 2024 to 2028 for eligible entities to enhance DOE missions.

Mandates the Secretary of Energy to execute a cross-cutting research, development, and demonstration program for unmanned aircraft system (UAS) technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Requires coordination across relevant DOE offices, including the Artificial Intelligence Technology Office.

Requires the Secretary to set goals for unmanned aircraft systems research; build on existing research efforts; provide undergraduate and graduate training across AI, machine learning, sensing, materials, and energy technologies; establish a robust, interoperable data management strategy; and support dedicated institutes to advance unmanned aircraft systems and DOE mission priorities.

Awards financial assistance for research in both fundamental S&T areas and applications.

Mandates the Secretary to promote technology transfer by partnering with industry,
make available DOE research facilities and high-performance computing infrastructure, and coordinate with other federal departments to avoid duplication and ensure complementary activities.

Authorizes appropriations totaling $276,282,638 from fiscal years 2024 to 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title IV ("National Science Foundation Activities")
document_name: Drone R&D Act, Title IV ("NSF Activities")
body:
Supports research and education on AI integration into advanced air mobility and unmanned aircraft, encouraging ethical use, cybersecurity, data management, and workforce development. Establishes partnerships and coordinates with agencies to enhance domestic development, allocating specific funds through 2028.

Mandates the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support research and STEM education in advanced air mobility and unmanned aircraft systems.

Supports fundamental research on technologies including AI, safety, autonomous control, materials, and communications systems.

Funds research on practical applications such as weather prediction, disaster response, and infrastructure monitoring.

Supports research on data modeling, validation, security, and ethical use, including privacy concerns.

Encourages middle and high school STEM education related to unmanned aircraft systems through curriculum development and student engagement activities.

Promotes undergraduate and graduate education through curriculum development, hands-on research opportunities, and scholarships.

Develops a skilled technical workforce, including veterans, through national centers and community college programs.

Facilitates public-private partnerships and interagency coordination to avoid research duplication.

Authorizes appropriations increasing from $50 million in 2024 to nearly $61 million in 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research and Development Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes")
document_name: Drone R&D Act, Title II ("National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes")
body:
Establishes a program to fund Institutes focusing on unmanned aircraft systems, including AI research. Encourages partnerships, supports interdisciplinary education, and requires data management strategies. Allocates $5 million annually for 2024-2028. Prioritizes merit-based selection and avoids duplicative efforts.

Establishes a program to award financial assistance for creating and supporting a network of National Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Research Institutes.

Requires collaboration among public and private organizations, including Federal agencies, academic institutions, and industry, to form these Institutes.

Mandates the Institutes to focus on economic or social sectors and address ethical, societal, safety, and security implications of unmanned aircraft systems.

Supports interdisciplinary research, education, and workforce development, including broadening participation of underrepresented communities.

Provides funds for managing data sets, developing testbeds, conducting research, and supporting AI and machine learning related to advanced air mobility systems.

Imposes a competitive merit review process for awarding financial assistance and prohibits duplication of efforts.

Authorizes $5 million annually for fiscal years 2024-2028 to support these activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National Critical Capabilities Defense Act of 2023
document_name: National Critical Capabilities Defense Act
body:
Defines "national critical capability sector" as including artificial intelligence and defines "covered activities" as being related to "national critical capability sectors". Establishes the "Committee on National Critical Capabilities" to review U.S. investments abroad threatening national security.

Defines "national critical capabilities sector" as sectors, including artificial intelligence, subject to regulation described in the bill.

Establishes the "Committee on National Critical Capabilities" to review U.S. investments in foreign countries that may threaten national security.

Requires U.S. persons to notify the Committee of covered activities in critical sectors, including artificial intelligence, at least 90 days before initiation.

Instructs the Committee to review and potentially mitigate risks posed by such activities, with authority to prohibit or regulate investments.

Defines "covered activities" broadly to include acquisitions, joint ventures, and other engagements with foreign entities in critical sectors.

Identifies countries of concern, including China, Russia, and North Korea, where such investments are scrutinized more closely.

Grants the Committee authority to enforce compliance, including imposing civil penalties up to $250,000 or twice the amount of the covered activity.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: National AI Commission Act
document_name: National AI Commission Act
body:
Establishes the National AI Commission, an independent and bi-partisan commission in the legislative branch responsible for reviewing and recommending measures to mitigate AI risks and protect US leadership in AI development

Establishes the National AI Commission, an independent and bi-partisan commission in the legislative branch responsible for reviewing and recommending measures for the US to mitigate the risks and possible harms of AI, and to ensure US leadership in AI innovation and development.

Directs the National AI Commission to review the Federal Government's existing approach to AI oversight and regulation, including the existing distribution of oversight and regulatory authorities across various agencies, and to recommend governmental structures that may be needed to regulate powerful general-purpose AI systems.

Instruct the National AI Commission to submit an interim report to Congress and the President within six months, a final report with its findings and recommendations for a binding regulatory framework no later than six months after the interim report, and a follow-up report within one year of the final report's submission.

Requires the National AI Commission to comprise twenty commissioners appointed by the President and by Congressional leadership, with ten appointed by each party and co-chaired by a Democratic appointee and a Republican appointee.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: NTIA Reauthorization Act of 2023, Sec. 203 ("Spectrum management improvements")
document_name: NTIA Reauthorization Act, Sec. 203 ("Spectrum management improvements")
body:
Develops and supports AI systems for advanced antenna arrays and dynamic spectrum access. Encourages workforce development and partnerships for prototyping advanced communications technologies. Identifies spectrum management technologies like dynamic spectrum access and network sensing for Federal frequency assignments.

Requires the Under Secretary, in coordination with the Commission and in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop, establish, prototype, and support the implementation of models, methodologies, and inputs for spectrum management decisions involving AI systems, advanced antenna arrays, and dynamic spectrum access technologies.

Mandates the development of AI systems to enable dynamic spectrum access, Internet of Things networks, and other advanced communications technologies.

Amends Section 104 of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to require the identification and facilitation of technologies that promote dynamic spectrum access, network sensing and monitoring, and optical and quantum communications.

Encourages the development of a skilled workforce for prototyping advanced communications technologies.

Supports partnerships among institutions for workforce development in advanced communications technology prototyping.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act
document_name: NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act
body:
Requires collaborative AI research by the USDA and NSF, emphasizing emerging technologies like AI, machine learning, and robotics for agriculture. Establishes memoranda of understanding, promotes data sharing, and supports infrastructure and workforce development. Requires reporting on achievements and opportunities biennially.

Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture and the Director of the National Science Foundation to conduct collaborative research and development activities, including those involving artificial intelligence and digital agriculture, to advance their mission priorities.

Requires the establishment of memoranda of understanding to coordinate these activities through competitive, merit-based processes.

Permits collaborative research in key areas, such as AI, machine learning, automation, and digital agriculture.

Encourages data sharing and collaboration among federal agencies, educational institutions, and nonprofit entities.

Supports research infrastructure and the development of translational technologies for commercial use.

Facilitates public-private partnerships and awards grants to educational institutions to establish a Center for Agricultural Research, Education, and Workforce Development.

Authorizes reimbursable agreements to enhance research effectiveness and mandates a report to Congress on interagency coordination and future collaboration opportunities.

Ensures research security consistent with the CHIPS Act of 2022.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: NSF AI Education Act of 2024
document_name: NSF AI Education Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the NSF AI Education Act of 2024, providing scholarships for AI and quantum hybrid computing studies at undergraduate and graduate levels. Creates AI-focused professional development fellowships, training grants for agriculture, and AI excellence centers. Promotes AI education, outreach, and workforce frameworks, prioritizing underserved areas and diverse institutions.

Establishes the NSF AI Education Act of 2024 to provide scholarships and fellowships for AI education at various educational levels, including undergraduate and graduate studies. 

Mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) to award scholarships for AI studies in fields such as agriculture, education, and advanced manufacturing, prioritizing institutions in underserved areas.

Directs the NSF to create professional development fellowships for AI and related emerging technologies, fostering collaboration between academia and industry.

Requires grants for AI training at land-grant colleges and universities, focusing on agricultural applications.

Authorizes the establishment of Centers of AI Excellence at community colleges and vocational schools to advance AI education and training.

Advises on guidelines for AI use in primary and secondary education and supports AI education research.

Prohibits funding to institutions in violation of anti-discrimination laws.

Directs the development of workforce frameworks for AI and other emerging technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: NO FAKES Act of 2024
document_name: NO FAKES Act of 2024
body:
Establishes rights for individuals over digital replicas of their voice or likeness, requiring consent for creation and use. Imposes liability for unauthorized replication. Provides safe harbors for online services complying with takedown notices. Limits preemption of existing state laws.

Establishes the right for individuals and right holders to authorize the use of their voice or visual likeness in digital replicas, treating it as a property right that is licensable but not assignable during the individual's life.

Allows post-mortem transfer and licensing, enabling rights to be inherited and renewed under specific conditions.

Imposes liability for unauthorized production, distribution, or public display of digital replicas without consent, with certain exclusions for news, historical, and public interest uses.

Provides safe harbors for online services that act promptly to remove unauthorized replicas upon notification.

Preempts conflicting state laws, except for those existing before January 2, 2025, or those addressing sexually explicit or election-related replicas.

Applies only to conduct and contracts occurring after the enactment date, while granting rights retroactively to deceased individuals' estates.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Modernizing Wildfire Safety and Prevention Act of 2024, Section 405 ("Joint Office of the Fire Environment Center (Report Recommendations 104, 105, 106)")
document_name: Modernizing Wildfire Safety and Prevention Act of 2024, Section 405 ("Joint Office of the Fire Environment Center (Report Recommendations 104, 105, 106)")
body:
Establishes a Joint Office to test AI/ML for fire management, supporting risk modeling and resource allocation. Requires collaboration with local entities and data sharing. Ensures development of decision support tools and air quality monitoring, with a $150 million annual budget.

Establishes the Joint Office of the Fire Environment Center within one year, under the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

Requires the Data Services branch to test AI and machine learning technologies to aid fire management, suggesting resources based on real-time fire conditions.

Mandates the provision of science-based, data-rich services for fire management, including predictive and decision-support tools.

Develops a technological common operating environment to integrate air quality data and other public health information.

Forms a 12-member board governing the Joint Office, including federal and non-federal wildfire community representatives.

Empowers the Joint Office to contract with government and private entities for necessary supplies and services.

Authorizes $150 million annually from fiscal years 2025 to 2034 for the Joint Office's operations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review Act
document_name: Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review Act
body:
Requires the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance on using AI and technology for retrospective regulatory reviews. Mandates agencies to submit and implement plans for reviewing regulations using this guidance, identifying obsolete or burdensome regulations.

Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to report on the progress of making agency regulations available in machine-readable format within 180 days.

Mandates the issuance of guidance within 18 months on using technology, including AI, for conducting retrospective reviews of agency regulations.

Instructs agencies to use technology to identify obsolete, ineffective, or problematic regulations and adequately train personnel in its use.

Obliges agency heads to submit a detailed plan within two years for implementing the guidance, including identifying regulations for review.

Compels agency heads to implement the strategy for retrospective review within 180 days after plan submission.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review
document_name: Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review
body:
Requires agencies to use AI in retrospective reviews of regulations. Directs the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance on AI use for identifying obsolete or burdensome regulations. Mandates agency plans and implementation strategies for these AI-assisted reviews.

Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to report on the Federal Government's progress in making agency regulations available in machine-readable format within 180 days after enactment.

Mandates the OMB Director to issue guidance within 18 months on using technology, including AI, for efficient and accurate retrospective reviews of regulations.

Obliges agency heads to submit a detailed plan within two years for implementing OMB guidance on retrospective reviews, identifying regulations for review, and including necessary data and analysis.

Directs agency heads to implement the submitted plan within 180 days of submission, focusing on retrospective regulatory reviews.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
document_name: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
body:
Defines artificial intelligence using existing legislation and includes AI in data governance. Requires the Chief Data Officer Council to identify AI opportunities and enhance data practices. Mandates biennial reports on AI use and data governance improvements in agencies.

Amends title 44 of the United States Code to define "artificial intelligence" and "data governance."

Requires Chief Data Officers to focus on data management and governance, including AI-related data standards.

Mandates the Chief Data Officer Council to enhance data governance, evaluate new technologies, and ensure AI use improves government operations.

Directs the Council to report on data governance progress and provide recommendations for AI and emerging technology adoption, including data transparency and privacy.

Obliges the Director to issue guidance on implementing Council recommendations and maintain a public inventory of Chief Data Officers.

Sets reporting requirements for the Comptroller General on the Council's effectiveness and challenges.

Establishes a sunset clause, rendering the section ineffective after December 14, 2031.

Prohibits the allocation of additional funds to implement the Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
document_name: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
body:
Extends the Chief Data Officer Council's authority to improve federal data governance. Enables agencies to securely adopt AI by appointing Chief AI Officers and mandating reports on data governance best practices, AI use cases, and synthetic data security.

Amends section 3520A of title 44, United States Code, to extend the Chief Data Officer Council's authority to improve Federal data governance.

Requires the Council to identify opportunities to enhance data governance for reliable and secure adoption of emerging technologies and AI.

Mandates appointment of a representative from Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers to the Council.

Obligates the Council to submit biennial reports detailing recommendations for developing datasets and data governance policies to support AI adoption.

Instructs the Council to assess data governance challenges, clarify roles among senior agency leaders, and recommend best practices for AI data use.

Requires recommendations for data ownership policies to ensure government rights and pre-procurement AI reviews.

Directs the Director to issue guidance based on Council reports.

Mandates an annual data management report to Congress clarifying Chief Data Officers' roles in AI governance.

Sunsets the amendments seven years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Methane Emissions Mitigation Research and Development Act
document_name: Methane Emissions Mitigation Research and Development Act
body:
Establishes a program for methane emissions detection, including AI-driven analytics and machine learning improvements. Forms a consortium to enhance leak detection and repair strategies through data sharing. Funds national facilities for advancing methane measurement standards and rapid technology testing.

Requires the Secretary of Energy, in consultation with the EPA and other federal agencies, to implement a program for methane emissions detection and mitigation research, development, and demonstration.

Mandates cooperative agreements with state/local governments, higher education institutions, and for-profit entities for technical assistance in preventing and responding to methane releases.

Establishes publicly accessible resources for best practices in pipeline systems, production wells, storage facilities, and emission reduction technologies.

Supports research into technologies for accurate methane emissions quantification, including improvements in data analytics, machine learning platforms, and Lidar detection technologies.

Forms a Methane Emissions Measurement and Mitigation Research Consortium to prioritize research, facilitate data sharing, and develop cooperative leak detection and repair strategies.

Requires annual reporting to Congress on the Consortium's activities, findings, and progress, and a merit review after five years.

Authorizes specific appropriations for the Secretary of Energy and Secretary of Commerce to support these initiatives through 2029.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act
document_name: Medicare Transaction Fraud Prevention Act
body:
Establishes a two-year pilot program using predictive risk-scoring algorithms for oversight of Medicare payments. Requires testing, evaluation, and review considering AI ethics guidelines. Authorizes human review of transactions flagged by algorithms. Permits intervention in high-risk transactions, including notifications and potential Medicare card terminations.

Establishes a pilot program under the Medicare program to test the use of a predictive risk-scoring algorithm for overseeing payments related to durable medical equipment and clinical diagnostic laboratory tests.

Requires the pilot to run for two years, starting no later than January 1, 2025, with voluntary beneficiary participation.

Mandates algorithm development in collaboration with industry representatives and modeled after real-time consumer feedback mechanisms, with scores ranging from 1 (least risky) to 99 (most risky).

Conditions use of the algorithm on prior testing and evaluation considering the AI Bill of Rights and requires notifying affected beneficiaries about data processing and implications.

Allows transaction review and possible suspension based on high-risk scores, offering beneficiaries the chance to dispute inaccuracies.

Requires that alerts for identified fraud risks be communicated to beneficiaries, along with guidance on reporting suspected fraud to law enforcement, and authorizes determination of Medicare card termination to prevent fraud.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: MedShield Act of 2024
document_name: MedShield Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement the MedShield program using AI for pandemic preparedness. Leverages AI for pathogen surveillance, vaccine and therapeutic development. Allocates funding from 2025 to 2029 for program execution.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement the MedShield program, utilizing artificial intelligence for pandemic preparedness and response.

Mandates the use of AI for developing a global pathogen surveillance system, accelerating vaccine development, and optimizing pathogen tracking and therapeutic interventions.

Obligates the Secretary to integrate recommendations from the National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence and coordinate with federal agencies and international partners.

Directs the development of a plan to enhance public health and medical services as part of the National Response Framework.

Sets funding authorization at increasing annual amounts from $300 million in fiscal year 2025 to $500 million in fiscal year 2029.

Requires submission of a detailed report on the program's plan to relevant Congressional committees within 180 days of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Maintaining Innovation and Safe Technologies Act
document_name: Maintaining Innovation and Safe Technologies Act
body:
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance by January 1, 2026, on Medicare payment requirements for remote monitoring devices with AI components that transmit health data for patient management and treatment.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance by January 1, 2026, on Medicare payment requirements under part B of title XVIII of the Social Security Act for remote monitoring devices.

Mandates that the guidance specifically address devices that incorporate artificial intelligence components, such as continuous adjustment features.

Requires that these devices must transmit information to healthcare providers for the management and treatment of individuals to qualify for payment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: MEANS Act
document_name: MEANS Act
body:
Establishes the Office of Manufacturing Security and Resilience to enhance supply chain resilience, focusing on critical goods. Supports domestic manufacturing, reduces reliance on concerning countries, and incentivizes relocation of facilities. Provides loans, loan guarantees, and sets criteria for eligible entities.

Establishes an Office of Manufacturing Security and Resilience within the Department of Commerce to oversee the Manufacturing Security and Resilience Program.

Mandates the Under Secretary to develop and implement a strategy to strengthen supply chains for critical goods, reducing reliance on concentrated supply chains, particularly from countries of concern.

Requires collaboration with other federal agencies to support allies and key international partners in building manufacturing capacity for critical goods.

Incentivizes domestic manufacturers to relocate production from countries of concern and increase production capacity, using loans, loan guarantees, and other financial supports.

Prioritizes support for activities that enhance the resilience, security, and diversity of supply chains and address supply chain shocks.

Mandates periodic submission of strategy reports and program evaluations to Congress, with updates every four years.

Allocates $35 billion for fiscal years 2024-2028 to fund the program, with specific allocations for loans, loan guarantees, and administrative costs.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Lummis-Gillibrand Responsible Financial Innovation Act, Sec. 1001 ("Executive Office of the President Appropriations")
document_name: Responsible Financial Innovation Act, Sec. 1001 ("EOP Appropriations")
body:
Authorize appropriations for AI-related specialist positions in the Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Economic Council, each receiving $2.5 million annually from 2023 to 2027, to coordinate federal activities and advise on innovative technologies.

Authorize appropriations of $2,500,000 annually from fiscal years 2023 to 2027 to the Office of Science and Technology Policy for hiring specialists in AI, crypto assets, and distributed ledger technology, available until the end of the subsequent fiscal year.

Require these funds to support positions coordinating Federal activities and advising the President on research and development strategies related to these technologies.

Authorize similar appropriations of $2,500,000 annually from fiscal years 2023 to 2027 to the National Economic Council for hiring specialists in AI, crypto assets, and distributed ledger technology, also available until the end of the subsequent fiscal year.

Require these funds to support positions coordinating Federal activities and advising the President on financial and economic policies related to these technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3)
document_name: Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3)
body:
Prohibits issuing algorithmic payment stablecoins. Requires registration or authorization for issuing payment stablecoins in the U.S. Limits issuance by non-depository trust companies to $10 billion. Establishes safe harbors for limited issuance and foreign regulatory equivalence. Adjusts thresholds for inflation.

Prohibits any person from issuing, creating, or originating an algorithmic payment stablecoin in the United States.

Mandates that payment stablecoins can only be issued by a registered non-depository trust company with a limit on nominal value or an authorized depository institution as a national payment stablecoin issuer.

Prohibits the offer or sale of payment stablecoins in the United States except by a U.S. person living in the U.S.

Requires the Board to adjust the issuance threshold for inflation every four years.

Directs the Board to establish safe harbor regulations, allowing limited issuance of payment stablecoins under specific conditions and fostering innovation and competition.

Allows safe harbor status for issuers regulated by equivalent foreign authorities.

Intends the section to have extraterritorial effect, extending its reach beyond U.S. borders.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Living Wage for Musicians Act of 2024
document_name: Living Wage for Musicians Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits AI entities from being classified as artists and requires the Federal Register to establish the Artist Compensation Royalty Fund.

Prohibits artificial intelligence entities from being classified as artists under this act.

Requires the establishment of the Artist Compensation Royalty Fund to help provide financial support to those whose employment was negatively impacted by AI.

Mandates service providers to collect and deposit a living wage royalty fee and a percentage of non-subscription revenue into the Fund.

Authorizes the Fund Administrator to impose penalties for violations and non-compliance by service providers.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Literacy in Future Technologies Artificial Intelligence Act
