document_name: LIFT AI Act
body:
Establishes awards for developing K-12 AI literacy curricula. Supports research and professional development to enhance AI literacy. Defines AI literacy as the ability to use and interpret AI effectively and ethically.

Establishes the "LIFT AI Act" to advance AI literacy in K–12 education.

Empowers the Director of the National Science Foundation to award competitive grants to higher education institutions or nonprofits for developing AI literacy curricula and evaluation methods.

Endorses AI literacy education to prepare a skilled workforce and maintain U.S. leadership in AI.

Recognizes the importance of AI literacy in mitigating ethical challenges and adapting to rapidly evolving AI technologies.

Supports the development of curricula focussed on AI competency, AI literacy evaluation tools, and professional development courses in AI literacy for educators.

Encourages incorporating AI literacy in existing curricula, emphasizing responsible AI use.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Leadership in CET Act
document_name: Leadership in CET Act
body:
Establishes a pilot program to expedite patent examination for AI and other emerging technologies, encouraging U.S. innovation and leadership. Permits fee waivers and limits application numbers. Terminates after issuing certain patents or accepting 10,000 applications, with possible renewal.

Establishes a pilot program for expediting patent applications related to critical and emerging technologies, including AI, microelectronics, and quantum information science.

Requires the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office to expedite patent processing through petitions.

Permits waiver of certain fees and requirements for accelerated examination processes.

Limits eligibility to U.S.-based entities or inventors and restricts applications to original, nonprovisional patents.

Terminates the program after issuing a patent within five years or upon accepting 10,000 applications, with a potential renewal for the same criteria.

Mandates public availability of information regarding application numbers, acceptance, and issued patents on the Office's website.

Requires a report to Congress assessing the pilot program's effectiveness post-termination, exempting this data collection from the Paperwork Reduction Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Land Grant Research Prioritization Act of 2023
document_name: Land Grant Research Prioritization Act of 2023
body:
Amends the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 to allow research and extension grants to be made for developing agricultural applications of AI.

Amends the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 to allow research and extension grants to be made for developing and evaluating agricultural applications of AI, with an emphasis on the use of AI to improve specialty crop production.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: LISTOS Act
document_name: LISTOS Act
body:
Requires large online platforms to ensure consistent enforcement of content moderation, including through automated processes, across languages. Mandates disclosures on processes, establishes an advisory group, authorizes enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission or State Attorneys General, and establishes a pilot program for international research, including tool development, to address non-English online communication inciting harm.

Requires covered platform operators to ensure that content moderation processes are reasonably consistent across languages in which the platform conducts monetization practices, while allowing enforcing entities to consider practical limitations and prohibiting mandates on specific content decisions.

Requires platform operators to report on processes, including automated processes, for content moderation annually to the Federal Trade Commission (Commission) and the public.

Requires platform operators to ensure that user tools for reporting content and automated actions are accessible in all languages offered by the platform.

Establishes the Advisory Group on Language-Sensitive Technologies under the Commission to provide best practices on the application of language-sensitive AI technologies to ensure nondiscriminatory application, and for the Commission to make available the results.

Empowers the Commission and State Attorneys General to enforce compliance, treating violations as unfair or deceptive practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Mandates the Commission to promulgate further regulations for carrying out the Act within 120 days.

Directs the United States Agency for International Development, in coordination with the Department of State, to set up a pilot program supporting international research, including tool development, to address non-English online communication that incites harm, and to report results to Congress and make them publicly available. Authorizes $3,000,000 in each of the fiscal years 2024 and 2025 in appropriations for the program.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Know Your App Act
document_name: Know Your App Act
body:
Requires application stores to prominently display the primary country of origin for each application. Allows users to filter or receive disclaimers for apps from concerning countries. Requires the Treasury and Commerce Secretaries to submit to Congress a list of foreign countries that subject app developers to control by the government of the country over content moderation, algorithm design, or user data transfers.

Requires covered companies to publicly list the primary country of origin of each application on the app store page with prominent display.

Mandates that covered companies provide an option to filter out apps from countries of concern and display disclaimers if data could be accessed by a foreign government.

Requires the Treasury and Commerce Secretaries to submit to Congress a list of foreign countries with a national law that subjects the app developers to control by the government of the country over content moderation, algorithm design, or user data transfers. Goes into effect 180 days after the act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency)
document_name: Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency)
body:
Requires platforms using opaque algorithms to notify users about their use and data application and mandates the option to switch to input-transparent algorithms.

Requires online platforms using opaque algorithms to provide users with clear notice about the use of such algorithms and how user-specific data is utilized. 

Mandates platforms to allow users to easily switch between opaque algorithms and input-transparent algorithms. Prohibits differential pricing or service denial based on a user's choice to use an input-transparent algorithm.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce these requirements as violations of unfair or deceptive practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act. 

Ensures that trade secrets, confidential business information, or privileged data are not required to be disclosed. Preserves the ability of platforms to allow users to personalize content restrictions and interactions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Kids Online Safety Act, Sec. 13 ("Filter Bubble Transparency Requirements")
document_name: Kids Online Safety Act, Sec. 13 ("Filter Bubble Transparency")
body:
Requires covered internet platforms to inform users about opaque algorithm and user data usage and provide detailed algorithm operational information. Mandates offering an input-transparent algorithm alternative and prohibits discrimination against users of this alternative.

Requires providers of covered internet platforms that use opaque algorithms to notify users about their use and provide detailed information about their operation, including their features, user-specific data collection, and algorithmic inputs in an easily accessible form.

Mandates platforms to offer an easily accessible input-transparent algorithm alternative and prohibits discrimination, via methods like differential pricing, against users who choose the alternative.

Empowers enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission to treat violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Exempts small downstream providers and non-profit organizations from certain enforcement provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024
document_name: Justice in Forensic Algorithms Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to establish a program to create and maintain testing standards for computational forensic software, including AI-enabled software for evidence analysis.

Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish a program (“Testing Standards”) to create and maintain testing standards for computational forensic software, which includes software that relies on AI-enabled automated or semiautomated computational processes to analyze or interpret evidence.

Requires Testing Standards to solicit public input, address the potential for disparate impacts on protected groups, and specify requirements for publicly available documentation by developers, validation processes by those using computational forensic software, reports provided to defendants regarding software used, and how to test software and report results. 

Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish a program (“Testing Program”) that tests computational forensic algorithms according to the testing standards, using realistic and representative sample data and adversarial examples, and publishing results. Requires software to be re-tested after significant changes. 

Requires Federal law enforcement agencies only to use computational forensic software tested by NIST’s Testing Program and only after conducting an internal validation and making results publicly available. 

Requires evidence from computational forensic software to be admissible only if it has been submitted to NIST’s Testing Program and the developers waive legal claims against the defense analyzing or testing it. Requires information about the software (e.g., source code) and results from analyses by the software to be shared with the defendant.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Jobs of the Future Act of 2023
document_name: Jobs of the Future Act of 2023
body:
Requires the Secretary of Labor and the NSF Director to submit interim and final reports on AI's workforce impact. 

Mandates identification of necessary data, affected industries, and vulnerable demographics. 

Requires analysis of skills and education needed to work with AI.

Demands recommendations to mitigate displacement and promote equitable AI education. 

Requires collaboration with educational institutions, industry stakeholders, and federal agencies.

Requires the Secretary of Labor and the Director of the National Science Foundation to submit interim and final reports on AI's impact on the U.S. workforce.

Mandates these reports to identify data necessary for analyzing AI's workforce impact, industries most affected by AI, and demographics vulnerable to job displacement.

Requires analysis of skills, expertise, and education needed to work alongside AI and methods to deliver these to the workforce.

Demands recommendations to mitigate workforce displacement, promote knowledge sharing, and ensure underserved demographics have access to necessary AI-related education.

Requires collaboration with educational institutions, industry stakeholders, and federal agencies in preparing the reports.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023
document_name: Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023
body:
Allocates $40 million annually for dislocated worker grants aimed at training workers displaced by automation. Prioritizes partnerships in high-risk areas. Mandates outcome reports.

Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to support projects addressing the training needs of workers likely to be displaced by automation.

Prioritizes grants for partnerships in areas with high concentrations of affected populations or industries susceptible to automation.

Requires eligible partnerships to provide training services, develop curricula, and offer employment benefits, such as transportation stipends and paid leave.

Mandates grant recipients to submit comprehensive reports on training outcomes, including transitions to new positions and earnings data.

Expands the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to include training for workers impacted by automation.

Allocates $40 million annually from 2024 to 2028 for national dislocated worker grants to address impacts of automation.

Ensures grant usage aligns with labor standards and nondiscrimination provisions under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: International Artificial Intelligence Research Partnership Act of 2024
document_name: International Artificial Intelligence Research Partnership Act of 2024
body:
Establishes international AI research partnerships, encouraging U.S. cities to collaborate with international counterparts while aligning with U.S. research priorities. Prohibits partnerships with cities in countries of concern. Limits research to non-national security areas. Allocates $20 million annually for implementation.

Establishes international artificial intelligence research partnerships between U.S. cities and their international counterparts to promote AI leadership, economic cooperation, and workforce development.

Encourages public-private partnerships, including nonprofits and academic institutions, to support these AI research collaborations.

Requires coordination with the National Science Foundation to align activities with U.S. AI research priorities and leverage existing resources.

Prohibits partnerships with cities in countries deemed a national security concern or detrimental to U.S. foreign policy.

Limits research to non-national security AI areas and mandates adherence to export control regulations.

Authorizes the Secretary of State to enter contracts to facilitate partnerships and allocates $20 million annually from 2025 to 2028 for implementation.

Mandates annual reporting on partnerships, research scope, city participation, coordination efforts, and implementation challenges to relevant congressional committees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Title V, Section 510 ("Management of artificial intelligence security risks")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2025, Title V, Section 510 ("Management of artificial intelligence security risks")
body:
Requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology to update vulnerability management processes for AI security risks. Establishes a voluntary database to track AI security and safety incidents. Evaluates standards for AI vulnerability reporting. Encourages best practices for AI supply chain risks.

Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to update the National Vulnerability Database to incorporate AI security vulnerabilities within 180 days.

Requires the development of a voluntary database to track AI security and safety incidents, ensuring confidentiality and standardized reporting formats.

Instructs the Director to evaluate AI incidents for potential inclusion in the database, prioritizing critical infrastructure and high-impact cases.

Directs the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to update the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures Program to address AI security vulnerabilities.

Initiates a multi-stakeholder evaluation of consensus standards for AI vulnerability reporting, with a report due to Congress within 180 days.

Requires collaboration to develop best practices for managing AI supply chain risks, focusing on data collection, documentation, and the use of open-source and proprietary datasets.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Title V, Section 505 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2025, Title V, Section 505 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center")
body:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Security Center within the NSA. Provides a research test bed, develops counter-AI guidance, promotes secure AI adoption, and coordinates with NIST. Ensures access to proprietary models for qualified researchers and sets usage terms.

Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Security Center no later than 90 days after day of enactment within the National Security Agency's Cybersecurity Collaboration Center.

Requires The Artificial Intelligence Security Center shall carry out the following functions:

Requires a subsidized AI security research test bed for private sector and academic researchers, including secure access to proprietary third-party models with vendor consent.

Develops guidance to prevent or mitigate counter-artificial intelligence techniques.

Promotes secure AI adoption practices for national security systems and the defense industrial base.

Coordinates with the Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute of the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Mandates terms of usage for researcher access to the test bed, ensuring limitation on research publication to protect classified or proprietary information.

Ensures test bed availability to federal agencies on a cost-recovery basis.

Requires the director to leverage existing infrastructure and resources provided under section 5.2 of the Executive Order dated 30, 2023 in relation to safe, secure, and trustworthy development of AI.

Defines counter-AI as techniques to extract information about or manipulate AI systems to compromise their confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Title V, Section 504 ("National security procedures to address certain risks and threats relating to artificial intelligence")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2025, Title V, Section 504 ("National security procedures to address certain risks and threats relating to artificial intelligence")
body:
Requires the President to develop procedures for notifying the government of AI-related security risks. Mandates government threat briefings to AI vendors. Obligates a briefing to Congress on agency responsibilities, industry outreach, and public education plans regarding AI risks.

Recognized by Congress that AI systems demonstrate growing capabilities in areas such as synthetic media and computer programming.

Advances in AI capabilities and increased access to large-scale models and advanced computing have significantly accelerated the adoption of AI across the United States and globally.

Increase of AI systems become more advanced and widely accessible, they increase the risks of misuse, including security threats, privacy violations, and failures in critical sectors such as healthcare, infrastructure, and transportation.

Requires the President to develop and issue procedures within 180 days of enactment to address risks related to artificial intelligence systems.

Recognizes that vendors of computing capabilities, AI developers, commercial users, independent researchers, and other entities may notify the U.S. government of AI-related risks.

Identifies security risks that compromise the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of AI systems and their supply chains, including training and test data, frameworks, and computing environments.

Identifies biosecurity risks, foreign malicious influence, and other unlawful activities facilitated by artificial intelligence systems.

Requires mechanisms for the Federal Government to provide threat briefings to AI vendors regarding foreign exploitation and malicious activity.

Defines “appropriate committees of Congress” as the intelligence committees and the Senate and House Homeland Security committees.

Requires briefings to Congress outlining agency responsibilities for outreach, plans for industry engagement and public education on AI risks, and the use of existing laws, guidelines, and risk management frameworks.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title V ("Matters Pertaining to United States Economic and Emerging Technology Competition with United States Adversaries"), Subtitle B ("Next Generation Energy, Biotechnology, and Artificial Intelligence")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Title V ("Emerging Technology Competition"), Subtitle B ("Next Generation AI")
body:
Requires the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 to conduct an assessment on economic and technological capabilities on the Peoples republic of china, of using civil nuclear energy for intelligence community capabilities. Requires the policy to create a plan on for private individuals or companies to notify federal agencies about specific risks or threats involving artificial intelligence.

Requires the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 to conduct an assessment on economic and technological capabilities on the Peoples republic of china. 

Requires detailed assessment that prepares consultation with different working groups who will asses the People Republic of China's use of  artificial intelligence, next-generation energy technologies, biotechnology that identifies competitive technologies in practice used by China, opportunities to counter the practices described in sub-clause 1, countries that China targets for exports of civil nuclear technology, countries best positioned to use U.S. civil nuclear technologies for export purposes, US vulnerabilities in the technology supply chain, and way to counter exports of China in technology. 

Requires public utility service contracts to last up to 10 years, or up to 30 years for intelligence community agencies if deemed necessary for national security, and permits annual payments from yearly appropriations.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to assess whether civil nuclear reactors could feasibly and advisably power intelligence community facilities with unique energy needs, identify any additional requirements or obstacles, and report the findings to Congress within 180 days.

Requires policies to be established by Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence capabilities to amends the statute by updating a subsection reference, redesigning subsection (b) as subsection (c), and inserting a new subsection after subsection (a).

Requires these capabilities to be carried out in one year after the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 to set policies for how the intelligence community acquires, uses, and maintains AI, including shared definitions, performance monitoring and auditing, vulnerability testing, dependency tracking, and documentation standards (including for training data and third party models), with periodic review and updates, plus a conforming cross reference change.

Requires the policy to create a plan on for private individuals or companies to notify federal agencies about specific risks or threats involving artificial intelligence. 

Assessing that artificial intelligence systems demonstrate increased capabilities in the generation of synthetic media and computer programming, has growing capabilities for large-scale artificial intelligence models to be used by individuals, businesses, and governments, have dramatically increased the adoption, and the risks of misuse or failure increase as Artificial intelligence because more accessible. 

Requires that no later than 180 days after enactment, the President shall establish a strategy which vendors, independent rescuers, and third parties who use artificial intelligence systems need to be notified of the elements of different types of risks such as security risks, biosecurity, foreign influence, that are broad aware by the united states government.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 909 ("Requirement to Ensure Intelligence Community Directives Appropriately Account for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Tools in Intelligence Products")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 909 ("Ensure IC Directives Account for AI and ML Tools in Intelligence Products")
body:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief Congress on AI and machine learning guidance in intelligence products within 120 days. Determines whether existing directives provide sufficient guidance and whether updates are necessary, including explanations or update plans and timelines.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief congressional intelligence committees within 120 days on whether current intelligence community directives provide sufficient guidance on the use of AI and machine learning tools in intelligence products.

Mandates the briefing to include a determination of whether Intelligence Community Directives 203 and 206, and other relevant directives, offer adequate guidance on using, sourcing, and providing transparency for AI and machine learning tools.

Requires the Director to assess if these directives need updates to enhance guidance and direction.

Obligates the Director to explain why no updates are needed if deemed sufficient, or to provide a plan and timeline for necessary updates if improvements are required.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 906 ("Programs for Next-Generation Microelectronics in Support of Artificial Intelligence")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 906 ("Next-Generation Microelectronics for AI")
body:
Establishes a program to advance microelectronics research supporting AI that focuses on next-generation computing models and overcoming microelectronics challenges. Requires collaboration with government, academia, and industry, and mandates regular congressional briefings on progress.

Establishes a program to advance microelectronics research, overseen by the Director of National Intelligence through the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity.

Focuses research on next-generation computing models, materials, devices, architectures, and algorithms to enhance artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Promotes advancements in computing technologies through multidisciplinary research, encompassing algorithm design, compute capability, generative AI, photonics-based microprocessors, new materials, optical networks, and AI safety for the intelligence community.

Requires active collaboration with government agencies, academic institutions, and private industry.

Authorizes appropriations for contracts, grants, and other transactions to support the program.

Mandates regular briefings to congressional intelligence committees on program progress, partnerships, and future research priorities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Sec. 758 ("Implementation of Technology for Classification and Declassification")
document_name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 758 ("Technology for Classification and Declassification")
body:
Requires the Administrator to research AI and machine learning solutions for federal classification and declassification. Mandates submission of a technology recommendation to the President. Obligates the President to report to Congress on the recommended solution and adoption decision.

Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government, within 1 year, to research a technology-based solution using machine learning and artificial intelligence for efficient and effective classification and declassification systems, to be implemented on an interoperable and federated basis across the Federal Government.

Requires consultation with key agencies and offices, including the Secretary of Defense, the CIA Director, the Director of National Intelligence, the Public Interest Declassification Board, the Director of the Information Security Oversight Office, and the head of the National Declassification Center at the National Archives and Records Administration.

Obligates the Administrator to submit a recommendation to the President regarding the adoption of the researched technology-based solution.

Permits the Administrator to hire sufficient staff that are carried out in the subsection.

Directs the President to submit a classified report to Congress within 540 days, detailing the recommended solution and the decision on its adoption.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Integrating New Technologies to Empower Law Enforcement at Our Borders Act
document_name: New Technologies at Borders Act
body:
Requires the Department of Homeland Security to plan integrating AI and emerging technologies for border awareness. Specifies assessments, cost estimates, capability gaps, and coordination with other agencies. Emphasizes transitioning new technologies and incentivizing private sector development.

Requires the Department of Homeland Security to develop a comprehensive plan within 180 days to identify, deploy, and integrate emerging and advanced technologies to enhance situational awareness along the northern and southern borders of the United States.

Mandates the inclusion of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, fiber-optic sensing, nanotechnology, optical and cognitive radar, modeling and simulation technology, hyperspectral and LIDAR sensors, and other similar technologies.

Includes an assessment of current technology utilization by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and how capability gaps can be addressed through technology integration.

Requires cost estimates for technology acquisition and maintenance, metrics for measuring technology impact, and an assessment of multi-domain awareness improvements.

Mandates an analysis of other Federal technologies, procurement authorities, and the transition of new technology systems.

Requires coordination with the Department of Homeland Security's Science and Technology Directorate for research, development, and incentivizing private sector innovation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024
document_name: Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024
body:
Requires Medicare Advantage plans to implement electronic prior authorization programs by 2027, ensuring secure data transmission and compliance with technical standards. Mandates transparency in technology use, including AI, and reporting on decision-making, appeals, and access impacts. Establishes enrollee protection standards.

Mandates Medicare Advantage plans, starting January 1, 2027, to implement an electronic prior authorization program for secure electronic transmission of requests and responses, excluding certain formats like facsimiles.

Requires plans, beginning January 1, 2026, to meet transparency requirements, including submitting annual data on prior authorization requests, appeals, and the use of AI technologies in decision-making.

Obligates plans to provide access to authorization criteria and documentation requirements to providers, suppliers, and enrollees upon request.

Empowers the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish response timeframes for prior authorization requests, potentially as short as 24 hours.

Tasks the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission with analyzing and reporting on prior authorization use and recommending improvements.

Directs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to study and report on real-time decision processes and the impact of AI on patient access, especially for rural and low-income beneficiaries.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024
document_name: Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024
body:
Establishes a research program to improve diagnostic safety and quality, including integrating AI-enabled tools. Requires expert panel consultation for data needs, involving the Chief AI Officer. Forms an interagency council to enhance research, policy, and collaboration in diagnosis improvement.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to establish a comprehensive research program on diagnostic safety and quality, focusing on reducing diagnostic errors and integrating AI tools.

Directs funding for new and existing research centers and mandates stakeholder engagement to enhance diagnostic quality and safety.

Requires the convening of an expert panel, including the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer, to recommend data types and sources for research improvement.

Establishes an Interagency Council on Improving Diagnosis in Health Care, including members from AI-related departments, to enhance diagnosis quality and identify research gaps.

Mandates the creation of a strategic federal plan to improve diagnosis, with updates and progress reports submitted biennially to Congress.

Authorizes appropriations for these initiatives from 2025 to 2029, ensuring sustained financial support for improving diagnostic practices and integrating AI solutions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act
document_name: Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act
body:
Incorporates machine learning to improve atmospheric river forecasts. Develops AI-driven tools and models for predicting landfalls and precipitation impacts. Enhances data processing and modeling techniques, using AI for high-resolution forecasting systems. Improves hazard communication methodologies.

Mandates the establishment of an atmospheric river forecast improvement program aimed at reducing loss of life and property due to atmospheric river events.

Requires development of quantitative forecast metrics, incorporating machine learning and data assimilation for improved landfall predictions of atmospheric rivers and associated extreme weather conditions.

Directs the enhancement of dynamic modeling systems to provide detailed forecasts, including snow accumulation and hydrological impacts.

Encourages the integration of innovative observation technologies and AI methods to refine forecasting and improve water resource management.

Supports atmospheric river reconnaissance efforts, ensuring data availability and integration into forecasting systems, and mandates the establishment of observatories along the U.S. West Coast.

Focuses on improved communication and categorization of atmospheric river hazards to aid public understanding and preparedness.

Obliges submission of a comprehensive program plan detailing research activities and resources within 270 days of enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Healthy Technology Act of 2023
document_name: Healthy Technology Act of 2023
body:
Authorizes artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies to prescribe pharmaceutical drugs if approved by the State involved and the Food and Drug Administration

Amends the definition of 'practitioner licensed by law to administer such a drug' in Section 503(b) of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, to include artificial intelligence and machine learning technology

Authorizes AI and ML technology to prescribe pharmaceutical drugs if approved by the State in question, and if approved by the Food and Drug Administration 

Requires such AI and ML technology to be approved by the Food and Drug Administration through conventional channels, including having to provide 90 days' premarket notification if this is deemed a new device

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Health Equity and Accountability Act of 2024, Sec 1013 ("Task Force on Preventing Bias in AI and Algorithms")
document_name: Health Equity and Accountability Act of 2024, Sec 1013 ("Task Force on Preventing Bias in AI and Algorithms")
body:
Establishes a Task Force to provide guidance on preventing AI and algorithmic bias in healthcare. Requires examination of AI's impact on civil rights, health disparities, and outcomes. Mandates a report to Congress and public comment period.

Establishes the Task Force on Preventing AI and Algorithmic Bias in Health Care within 30 days to guide the development of AI technologies that do not exacerbate health disparities.

Composes the Task Force of various health and public officials, including experts on health equity and minority health.

Mandates the Task Force to examine AI and algorithms in healthcare, identifying risks related to civil rights, civil liberties, and discriminatory bias.

Requires submission of a report to Congress within one year detailing findings and recommendations for safe AI implementation in healthcare.

Obliges the Task Force to publish the report on the Department of Health and Human Services' website.

Initiates a public comment period of at least 90 days on the Task Force’s duties and activities.

Allows the Chairperson to appoint additional staff without adherence to certain civil service laws, ensuring flexibility in task force operations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Health Care Price Transparency Act of 2023, Sec. 301 ("Establishing Requirements With Respect to the Use of Prior Authorization Under Medicare Advantage Plans")
document_name: Health Care Price Transparency Act, Sec. 301 ("Requirements Regarding Prior Authorization Under Medicare Advantage Plans")
body:
Establishes electronic prior authorization programs for Medicare Advantage plans, requiring real-time decisions and transparency. Specifies enrollee protection standards, timely response requirements, and detailed reporting, including AI use. Mandates reports to Congress evaluating implementation and challenges.

Requires Medicare Advantage plans to establish an electronic prior authorization program by the third plan year after the enactment date.

Mandates that plans meet enrollee protection standards and transparency requirements by the fourth plan year.

Establishes a secure electronic transmission system for prior authorization requests and responses, excluding certain forms like facsimiles and non-compliant payer portals.

Specifies that real-time decisions must be made for certain prior authorization requests, with exceptions for extenuating circumstances.

Demands detailed annual reporting of prior authorization data, including the use of AI and decision-support technologies, and the publication of this information by the Secretary.

Calls for GAO and HHS to submit reports to Congress evaluating the implementation and impact of these requirements.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Research and Control Amendments Act of 2023, Sec. 2f ("National Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network")
document_name: Algal Bloom Research and Control Act, Sec. 2f ("Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Observing Network")
body:
Establishes a national network of harmful algal bloom observing systems using AI for detection and forecasting. Requires data integration and dissemination through a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center. Coordinates between NCCOS and IOOS Program Office for effective management.

Amends the National Harmful Algal Bloom And Hypoxia Observing Network Harmful Algal Blooms and Hypoxia Research and Control Act of 1998 to establish a national harmful algal bloom observing network.

Requires the Under Secretary, through NCCOS and IOOS of NOAA, to monitor, detect, and forecast harmful algal blooms using emerging technologies and new data integration methods like artificial intelligence.

Mandates the IOOS Program Office to coordinate with NCCOS on data integration and information dissemination.

Establishes a Harmful Algal Bloom Data Assembly Center for data integration, dissemination, and support of ecological forecasting.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HR 7659 Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Establishment of National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems")
document_name: HR 7659 Coast Guard Authorization Act 2024, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems")
body:
Establishes a National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems to advise on regulation and use within U.S. waters. Requires 9 expert members representing diverse maritime sectors, including marine safety, vessel design, and unmanned vehicle research, appointed by the Secretary.

Establishes the National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems.

Advises the Secretary on regulation and use of Autonomous Systems within U.S. territorial waters.

Comprises 9 members appointed by the Secretary with this section and section 15109.

Requires each member of the Committee to have expertise, knowledge and experience in relating to the context of the Committee.

Ensures representation from various groups which should have at least one member.

Ensures that representation includes marine safety, security entities, vessel design, construction entities, unmanned vehicle production, port authorities, vessel operators, National labor unions, maritime pilots, commercial space transportation operators, and academic institutions.

Mandates establishment of the Committee within 90 days post-enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HOME Act of 2024, Sec. 7 (Identification of Unfair Screening Practices)
document_name: HOME Act of 2024, Sec. 7 (Identification of Unfair Screening Practices)
body:
Establishes a program to identify unfair rental housing screening practices using algorithms. Requires annual reporting to Congress on collected information regarding these practices, including background checks and tenant income evaluations.

Mandates the Secretary, the Federal Trade Commission, and the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection to jointly collect information on unfair practices in tenant and applicant screenings, including the use of algorithms.

Requires the identification of practices that prevent access to or retention of rental housing, focusing on tenant background checks, adverse action notices, and tenant income sources.

Obliges the submission of an annual report to Congress detailing the information collected under the program.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: HEARTS Act of 2022
document_name: HEARTS Act
body:
Prioritizes nonanimal methods in NIH-supported research proposals; establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing to promote nonanimal research methods, including AI.

Prioritizes nonanimal methods in NIH-supported research proposals.

Establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing within NIH to develop, promote, and fund nonanimal research methods, including AI.

Mandates the center to provide training and resources to researchers on nonanimal methods.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: H.R. 9626, To direct the Department of Defense to develop a plan for the establishment of a secure computing and data storage environment for the testing of artificial intelligence trained on biological data, and for other purposes.
document_name: H.R. 9626, DOD Secure Computing and Data Storage Plan Development
body:
Establishes a secure AIxBio sandbox for testing AI trained on biological data. Designates the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering to manage it. Involves selecting defense-applicable projects and facilitating partnerships with DoD and academic labs. Requires reporting to Congress.

Mandates the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering to develop a plan for a secure computing and data storage environment, termed the "AIxBio sandbox," to facilitate the testing of AI models trained on biological data.

Requires the AIxBio sandbox to utilize existing Department of Defense infrastructure when feasible and designates the Under Secretary of Defense for managing and overseeing its activities.

Directs the Under Secretary to select projects for the sandbox that demonstrate potential defense applications at the intersection of AI and biotechnology, such as medical countermeasures and biomanufacturing.

Establishes mechanisms for collaboration between Department of Defense laboratories and academic institutions to support AIxBio projects, with streamlined processes for efficient partnerships.

Obligates the Under Secretary to report and brief Congress on the plan within one year of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Government Surveillance Reform Act of 2023, Title VII (Protection of Car Data from Warrantless Searches)
document_name: Government Surveillance Reform Act of 2023, Title VII (Protection of Car Data from Warrantless Searches)
body:
Prohibits law enforcement from accessing vehicle data without a warrant, except with operator consent or in emergencies.

Prohibits law enforcement from accessing vehicle data without a warrant, except with operator consent or in emergencies. 

Defines "covered vehicle data" to include all onboard and telematics data in noncommercial vehicles, excluding certain data types like automotive software and geolocation data for traffic enforcement.
Prohibits the use of any vehicle data obtained in violation of these provisions as evidence in any legal proceedings. Amends the Driver Privacy Act of 2015 to align with these new restrictions on accessing vehicle data.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Generative AI Copyright Disclosure Act of 2024
document_name: GenAI Copyright Disclosure Act
body:
Requires anyone that creates or alters a training dataset for a generative AI system to submit a notice to the Register of Copyrights detailing copyrighted works used in the dataset 30 days before the model being made available to consumers or 30 days after the Act takes effect. Imposes a $5,000 penalty for non-compliance and instructs the Register to create a public database of filed notices.

Requires anyone who creates or alters a training dataset used for a generative AI system to submit a notice to the Register of Copyrights with a summary of any copyrighted works used in the dataset and the URL for the dataset.

Requires the notice must be submitted 30 days before the AI system is made available to consumers or within 30 days of the Act taking effect for systems already available.

Imposes a civil penalty of at least $5,000 for non-compliance.

Requires the Register to establish and maintain a public database of filed notices.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: GRIData Act of 2024
document_name: GRIData Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Energy to identify, analyze, and share data to improve electric grid reliability and resilience. Considers AI and machine learning for enhancing grid operations. Establishes a steering committee and mandates reports and websites for data dissemination.

If you want it to read cleaner with the same content, here’s a tightened version:

Requires the Secretary of Energy to identify, analyze, and share data to improve the reliability and resilience of the electric grid.

Directs the federal government to improve grid reliability data collection and sharing to better inform planning and decisions, including by requiring the Secretary of Energy to work with agencies and stakeholders to gather, analyze, and share data relevant to rural, low-income, disadvantaged, and energy communities.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to consider the timing and frequency of reliability and outage data production or collection so it can support annual reporting on grid reliability and, where practicable, real-time outage restoration information for customers.

Requires the Secretary to collect and use weather data by working with NOAA, National Laboratories, NCAR, and other entities to assess historical and simulated future weather conditions for long-term reliability assessments and resource planning.

Considers the use of emerging technologies, including AI and machine learning, to enhance grid reliability and resilience.

Establishes a steering committee with stakeholders from federal agencies, regulators, and the electric power sector to guide data-related activities.

Mandates the submission of a report to Congress within one year detailing findings and recommendations on data collection and sharing, including consideration of potential security risks.

Authorizes $10 million for the first fiscal year to support these activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024
document_name: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the "Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute" to assist sectors in AI best practices and innovation. Requires AI research and standards development and mandates an international coalition for AI standards. Directs reporting on regulatory barriers and orders prioritized AI training data and Federal AI challenges.

Establishes the "Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute" to assist private and public sectors in developing best practices for AI assessment, provide technical assistance, and promote AI innovation, with a director appointed by the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology.
Requires the Institute to conduct AI research, develop standards, and create guidelines for safe AI development and deployment, including generative AI and foundation models.

Mandates the formation of an international coalition to harmonize AI standards and support bilateral and multilateral AI research collaborations. Directs the Comptroller General to report on regulatory barriers affecting AI innovation and recommend legislative or administrative actions to enhance AI development.
Orders the development of prioritized public data sets for AI training and evaluation, and the establishment of Federal grand challenges in AI to stimulate research and commercialization in key areas.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title VIII "Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions")
document_name: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act ("Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions")
body:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in transactions involving prohibited technologies in national security contexts, including specific AI developments. Requires notifications for such transactions. Establishes penalties, allowances for waivers, and a public database on covered foreign entities.

Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in investments involving covered national security transactions in prohibited technologies, with exemptions permissible by the Secretary for activities deemed in the national interest. 

Allows the Secretary to issue regulations that require notifications for such transactions. 

Introduces penalties for violations, including civil penalties and potential divestment requirements, with the burden of proof resting on the Secretary in enforcement actions. 

Establishes processes for self-disclosure of violations and requests for non-binding feedback regarding transactions. 

Mandates annual reports to Congress detailing enforcement actions and technology assessments. 

Provides for confidentiality of transaction information, but outlines exceptions for disclosure relevant to U.S. national security interests. 

Encourages international cooperation to prevent prohibited technology development or acquisition by countries of concern, such as China. 

Defines key terms, including "prohibited technology" and "country of concern."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title V "Promoting Resilient Supply Chains")
document_name: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act ("Promoting Resilient Supply Chains")
body:
Establishes responsibilities for the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote stable supply chains and emerging technologies, including AI. Requires the formation of a Working Group to assess supply chain resilience and vulnerabilities. Encourages domestic manufacturing of critical technologies.

Expands the responsibilities of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to include promoting the resilience of supply chains related to critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Mandates the creation of the Supply Chain Resilience Working Group composed of relevant federal agencies to assess and model supply chain stability, including those involving AI technologies.

Requires the group to identify vulnerabilities and prepare for potential supply chain shocks that might impact AI and other critical technologies.

Encourages domestic production and manufacturing, specifically focusing on AI and technological advancements.

Obligates periodic reports and assessments to Congress regarding the resilience and capacity of AI-related supply chains and industry preparedness for shocks.

Prohibits reliance on critical goods from countries identified as risks to national security, advocating for sourcing from allies.

Sets a 10-year expiration for these provisions.

Protects confidential data shared voluntarily under this title from disclosure, ensuring privacy concerns in relation to AI-related supply chain information.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Title IX "Take It Down Act")
document_name: Take It Down Act
body:
Prohibits the nonconsensual use of digital forgeries or intimate visual depictions via interactive computer services. Requires platforms to establish quick removal processes for such depictions. Enforces penalties for violations and mandates FTC oversight for compliance.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to criminalize the publication of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including digital forgeries created using AI, in interstate or foreign commerce.

Defines digital forgeries as depictions created with AI or other technological means that are indistinguishable from authentic depictions.

Prohibits the publication of such depictions for both adults and minors, with specific intent requirements such as causing harm or for sexual gratification.

Imposes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offenses involving adults and harsher penalties for those involving minors.

Mandates covered platforms, such as websites with user-generated content, to establish a process for the removal of nonconsensual depictions within 48 hours of receiving a request.

Enforces compliance through the Federal Trade Commission, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts.

Provides exceptions for certain authorized law enforcement and good faith activities and outlines processes for restitution and forfeiture related to violations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act 2025 (Section 217 "Report on Wearable Medical Devices")
document_name: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act ("Report on Wearable Medical Devices")
body:
Requires the Comptroller General to assess wearable medical devices' use in clinical decision-making, focusing on their treatment-prescribing accuracy, AI's role in enhancing capabilities, and policy options to optimize benefits and address development challenges.

Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a technology assessment of wearable medical devices within 18 months of the Act's enactment.

Requires submission of a report to Congress on the capabilities and limitations of these devices in supporting clinical decision-making.

Includes a description of the potential for wearable devices to accurately prescribe treatments.

Examines the benefits and challenges of using artificial intelligence to augment these capabilities.

Suggests policy options to enhance the benefits and address the challenges of developing or using wearable medical devices.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024
document_name: Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024
body:
Requires consumer reporting agencies to provide free credit scores with annual reports upon request. Mandates clear disclosures about differences between credit scores and educational scores. Obligates lenders to provide free credit reports and scores used for underwriting before loan agreements.

Expands the definitions of "credit score" and "educational credit score" under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA).

Requires consumer reporting agencies (CRAs) to provide consumers with detailed explanations of credit score calculations, including key factors affecting scores.

Mandates CRAs to disclose prominently the differences and limitations of credit scores and educational credit scores on their websites and in related materials.

Provides consumers with free credit score disclosures along with their free annual consumer reports upon request.

Requires private educational lenders, motor vehicle lenders, and residential mortgage lenders to provide consumers with free copies of any consumer reports and credit scores used for underwriting before signing loan agreements.

Mandates the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to issue final rules to implement these amendments within two years of enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2024
document_name: Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits knowingly distributing false AI-generated election media to mislead voters or intimidate officials. Exempts certain media organizations if falsehoods are clearly disclosed. Authorizes the Attorney General to enforce violations.

Prohibits the distribution of false AI-generated election media containing materially false information about election details or voter eligibility with the intent to impede voting in federal elections.

Prohibits the distribution of false AI-generated depictions of election officials intended to intimidate or harass officials or deter voting.

Exempts bona fide news entities from these prohibitions if they clearly disclose the falsity of the AI-generated content.

Empowers the Attorney General to enforce these prohibitions through civil actions in U.S. District Courts.

Amends the National Voter Registration Act to prevent states from using unverified databases to remove voters from official lists, requiring government-verified information approved by the Attorney General.

Sets criteria for source information, including monthly updates and non-violation of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

Ensures severability of the Act’s provisions, maintaining the validity of remaining sections if any part is invalidated.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023
document_name: Forest Data Modernization Act
body:
Amends the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Research Act to integrate AI and advanced technologies, including machine learning, for enhanced forest data collection and analysis.

Amends the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Research Act to include forest carbon in resource assessments.

Updates strategic plan to include consistent data collection protocols, integration of new technologies, and enhanced transparency.

Amends the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 to authorize microwave, LiDAR, hyperspectral, high-resolution remote sensing, and machine learning technologies for forest data analysis.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Forecasting Optimization for Robust Earth Climate Analysis and Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Tracking Act of 2024
document_name: FORECASTS Tracking Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the Weather and Earth System Modeling and Data Assimilation Workforce Innovation Program to advance AI in forecasting. Prioritizes multi-model ensemble systems, emerging technologies, and workforce development. Authorizes significant appropriations for research and operational advancements in weather prediction.

Amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to improve subseasonal-to-seasonal weather forecasting by requiring the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to enhance research, data collection, and model development.

Mandates the development of multi-model ensemble forecast systems and data management strategies, and the operationalization of new modeling technologies.

Establishes an Internet clearinghouse for forecasts and related information.

Creates the Weather and Earth System Modeling and Data Assimilation Workforce Innovation Program to support education, recruitment, and workforce development in weather modeling and data assimilation, emphasizing artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Requires the Under Secretary to develop and update a workforce human capital plan and report on the program's effectiveness.

Authorizes appropriations for these initiatives, including $40 million annually from 2025 to 2030 for the workforce program and additional funding for NOAA's weather research activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act
document_name: Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act
body:
Establishes a cybersecurity clearinghouse for the food and agriculture industry. Requires consolidation of cybersecurity recommendations and consultations with various stakeholders. Mandates a study on federal efforts to improve industry cybersecurity.

Defines key terms for NTIA Food and Agriculture Cybersecurity Clearinghouse, including "cybersecurity risk" and "food and agriculture industry."

Establishes a food and agriculture cybersecurity clearinghouse within the NTIA to provide publicly available online resources focused on cybersecurity for the food and agriculture industry.

Requires the clearinghouse to be publicly available online and provide current cybersecurity resources focused on the food and agriculture industry, a support request mechanism, regularly updated FAQ section, and targeted materials for small and non-technical users on critical cybersecurity protections.

Requires the Assistant Secretary to work with relevant agencies to consolidate public and private sector best practices into a set of voluntary cybersecurity recommendations for the food and agriculture industry, including risk-based and cybersecurity-informed engineering, system control planning, protection measures, threat defenses, ransomware response, and data integrity recommendations.

Instructs the Assistant Secretary to consult with private sector, federal agencies, trade groups, and civil society organizations in implementing the clearinghouse.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report on federal efforts to improve cybersecurity in the food and agriculture industry, evaluating effectiveness, resources, coordination, and potential risks of coordinated attacks.

Sunsets the section seven years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Fix Our Forests Act, Section 303 ("Public-private wildfire technology deployment and demonstration partnership")
document_name: Fix Our Forests Act, Section 303 ("Public-private wildfire technology deployment and demonstration partnership")
body:
Establishes a pilot program for deploying innovative wildfire technologies. Prioritizes AI, quantum sensing, and other emerging technologies. Requires reporting on technology deployment, costs, and recommendations for scalable adoption. Connects private entities with federal agencies for real-time testing.

Establishes a deployment and demonstration pilot program for innovative wildfire technologies, including AI, within one year.

Incorporates the program into the National Wildfire Coordinating Group and advances key technology areas like remote sensing and interoperable data.

Requires coordination between selected private entities and federal agencies for real-time technology testing during wildfire mitigation.

Prioritizes entities involved in the Fire Weather Testbed or developing emerging technologies like AI and quantum sensing.

Mandates public outreach to invite applications from entities to demonstrate technologies.

Obligates annual reporting to Congress on program participants, technologies demonstrated, costs, outreach, and recommendations for technology adoption.

Specifies the program's authority will terminate seven years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center")
document_name: Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center")
body:
Establishes a Fireshed Center to assess and predict fire and smoke using AI and data tools. Promotes coordination, data sharing, and streamlined processes among federal agencies and other entities. Disseminates AI-based decision support products for fire risk reduction and recovery.

Establishes a Fireshed Center through collaboration between the Forest Service and the U.S. Geological Survey, involving multiple federal agencies.

Appoints a Director from the U.S. Geological Survey or the Forest Service for a term of up to seven years.

Utilizes artificial intelligence and data tools to assess and predict fire and smoke at the wildland-urban interface for improved management, risk reduction, and recovery.

Promotes data sharing and coordination across federal, state, local, tribal, and private sectors.

Reduces duplication and fragmentation in predictive services and decision support related to wildland fires.

Streamlines procurement and cybersecurity processes.

Develops and disseminates publicly accessible data, models, and technologies for fire risk reduction and recovery planning.

Maintains the Fireshed Registry and supports its operations with personnel and services from the U.S. Geological Survey and the Forest Service.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023
document_name: FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023
body:
Cites the Act as the "FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023." Requires FinCEN to establish research and information-sharing programs on technological advances. Mandates exploration of beneficial innovations. Obligates adoption of necessary technologies. Enables information exchange. Authorizes non-standard transactions. Compels annual reporting to Congress.

Cites the Act as the "FinCEN Modernization Act of 2023."

Requires FinCEN to establish research, development, and information-sharing programs focusing on technological advances like machine learning and data analytics.

Mandates FinCEN to explore and evaluate technological innovations beneficial for financial systems and detect illicit activities.

Obligates FinCEN to adopt necessary technologies for monitoring cryptocurrencies and addressing money laundering and cyber threats.

Enables FinCEN to exchange information with other Treasury offices and federal departments.

Authorizes FinCEN to enter into non-standard transactions and accept contributions, gifts, or donations to support technological advancements.

Compels FinCEN to submit an annual report detailing transactions, contributions, and their justifications and purposes to relevant Congressional committees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2023, Sec. 14 ("Automation and Artificial Intelligence")
document_name: Federal Information Security Modernization Act, Sec. 14 ("Automation and AI")
body:
Requires the Director to issue AI guidance for agency cybersecurity improvement. Mandates annual AI cybersecurity reports to Congress. Orders the Comptroller General to report on AI-related privacy and cybersecurity risks, and study AI's role in federal cybersecurity automation.

Define "information system" as per section 3502 of title 44, United States Code.

Mandates the Director to issue guidance on AI use by agencies to enhance cybersecurity of information systems.

Requires the Director and agency heads to consider AI systems where automation aids cybersecurity.

Obligates the Director to report annually for 5 years to Congress on AI use in enhancing cybersecurity.

Instructs the Comptroller General to report to Congress on AI-associated privacy and cybersecurity risks within 2 years.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report within 2 years on AI and automation use across the federal government for cybersecurity, including automated updates to cybersecurity tools and processes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Federal Improvement in Technology Procurement Act
document_name: FIT Procurement Act
body:
Requires the Federal Acquisition Institute to incorporate experiential learning into certification programs within 18 months. Mandates a cross-functional ICT acquisition training program. Encourages off-the-shelf technologies and innovative procurement techniques. Reassigns AI training responsibility to GSA. Expands Commercial Solutions Opening Authority. Increases simplified acquisition threshold to $500,000. Requires Administrator to issue past performance guidance. Establishes a working group to address Federal vendor base issues.

Requires the Federal Acquisition Institute to incorporate experiential learning into key acquisition certification programs within 18 months.

Mandates the development and implementation of a cross-functional ICT acquisition training program, emphasizing market research, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity.

Encourages the use of commercially available off-the-shelf technologies and innovative procurement techniques like oral presentations and product demonstrations.

Reassigns the responsibility for AI training requirements from the Office of Management and Budget to the General Services Administration.

Expands the Commercial Solutions Opening Authority to include commercial services and mandates public reporting and data collection on its use.

Increases the simplified acquisition threshold from $250,000 to $500,000.

Requires the Administrator to issue guidance on using past performance from a broader range of projects to increase competition.

Establishes a working group to address the shrinking Federal vendor base and recommends actions to remove barriers to qualified vendors.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023
document_name: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2023
body:
Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance on how federal agencies can use NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework to reduce risks.

Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidance on how federal agencies can use NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) to reduce risks, covering cybersecurity for AI systems, requirements for AI suppliers, and training for agencies.

Requires the Comptroller General of the United States to assess the impact of NIST's AI RMF on agencies' AI use within a year, and requires the Director of OMB to report to Congress on agency implementation and adherence to NIST’s AI RMF within a year, and subsequently, at least once every three years.

Excludes national security systems from the requirements above to adhere to NIST’s AI RMF.

Requires the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council to issue guidance on agency AI procurement within a year, to ensure compliance with NIST’s AI RMF.

Requires the Director of OMB to establish an initiative to build agencies’ AI expertise, focusing on hiring interdisciplinary experts and incorporating best practices from existing initiatives.

Requires the Director of NIST to conduct a study on and convene stakeholders to develop voluntary consensus standards to test and evaluate AI acquisitions, develop methods and conduct evaluations, monitor evaluations and adjust methods, and make recommendations to each agency on risks from relevant AI acquisitions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act
document_name: Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act
body:
Establishes governance requirements for Federal AI systems to ensure actions align with laws, promote fairness, manage risks, and maintain transparency. Requires the development of AI charters and oversight, with provisions for public disclosure, privacy protection, and periodic evaluations.

Amends chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code, to establish Federal AI system governance requirements.

Instructs Federal actions involving AI to align with the Constitution, relevant laws, and policies, protecting civil rights and privacy.

Mandates the assessment and management of AI risks before deployment, ensuring AI outcomes remain ethical and accurate.

Requires transparency and explainability of AI systems' purpose, operations, and outcomes to maintain safety and security, and protect against vulnerabilities.

Obligates regular testing and oversight of AI applications to ensure they align with intended purposes and create mechanisms to deactivate AI systems that do not meet standards.

Instructs agencies to publicly disclose AI use to stakeholders and establish notification and appeal processes for AI-based decisions.

Establishes a Federal AI System Inventory for cataloging agency AI governance charters to be publicly available and regularly updated.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Public-Private Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership")
document_name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership")
body:
Establishes a pilot program for deploying and testing wildfire prevention technologies, prioritizing AI and emerging technologies. Requires collaboration between federal agencies and private entities. Mandates annual reports on technologies tested and potential large-scale adoption. Program expires September 30, 2029.

Defines the 'appropriate committees', 'covered agency', 'covered entity', 'Secretaries', and 'Pilot Program'. 

Establishes a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies within 60 days after enactment.

Requires incorporation of the Pilot Program into an existing interagency coordinating group on wildfires.

Mandates consultation with covered agencies to identify key technology priority areas to deploy wildfire prevention technologies.

Partners with selected covered entities to participate in the Pilot Program for real-time and on-the-ground testing of technology during wildfire mitigation activities.

Prioritizes emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence in their, quantum sensing, and augmented reality as apart of their Pilot Program for wildfire mitigation.

Requires the secretaries to work with the head of covered agencies to make these key technology priorities to test and demonstrate the priority areas.

Requires submission of annual reports to appropriate committees, detailing participating entities, tested technologies, costs, outreach efforts, and assessments.

Expires the Pilot Program on September 30, 2029.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VII ("Research, Extension, and Related Matters"), Sec. 7208 ("Centers of Excellence")
document_name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act, Title VII ("Research and Extension"), Sec. 7208 ("Centers of Excellence")
body:
Establishes centers of excellence for research on digital agriculture, including AI and remote sensing. Requires partnerships to enhance coordination and address agricultural challenges. Mandates annual reporting on projects, funding, and intellectual property actions. Extends program duration to 2029.

Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to establish at least one center of excellence to conduct research, extension, and education activities.

Specifies eligible host institutions, including land-grant universities, other agricultural colleges, and accredited veterinary schools, and directs the Secretary to ensure geographic diversity. Requiring each institution may host or co-host only one center at a time.

Requires partnerships with federal agencies, state governments, higher education institutions, and agricultural industry groups to enhance coordination and cost-effectiveness.

Focuses on multiple areas, including digital agriculture, artificial intelligence, agricultural biosecurity, cybersecurity, precision agriculture technologies, biotechnology, and crop protection.

Provides awards for five-year terms, renewable once for an additional five years, for a maximum of ten years.

Prohibits use of funds for construction or facility renovation.

Requires an annual report to the House Committee on Agriculture and Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestryon what projects they are working on, funding for each project, what institutional were involved, cost-sharing, and intellectual property actions to relevant Congressional committees. 

Expands the number of centers from 3 to 8 and extends the program's authorization to 2029.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2024, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Promoting Precision Agriculture")
document_name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Precision Agriculture")
body:
Requires the Secretary to develop voluntary interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture, considering AI impacts. Directs coordination with industry and government stakeholders. Mandates GAO to assess these standards biannually for 8 years, evaluating voluntary adoption and industry coordination.

Promotes United States leadership in developing standards for precision agriculture.

Mandates the Secretary to develop voluntary, consensus-based interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years.

Requires consultation with NIST, FCC, public, and private stakeholders, including voluntary consensus standards development organizations.

Considers the impact of advanced wireless communications technology and artificial intelligence on precision agriculture.

Addresses cybersecurity challenges and connectivity needs of precision agriculture technology.

Directs the Comptroller General to assess the developed standards one year after implementation and biennially for eight years.

Obligates the Comptroller General to report findings to relevant Senate and House committees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Farm Tech Act
document_name: Farm Tech Act
body:
Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program to certify AI software for agricultural use based on the NIST's Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework.
