Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program to certify AI software for the production of agricultural products. 

Bases the certification program on the  National Institute of Standards and Technology's Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework.

Permits certification only if the software performs accurately and meets or exceeds relevant Federal and State standards for licensure, certification, and permitting.

Details specific licensure and certification requirements for various tasks, including commercial driving, manure application, pesticide application and handling hazardous materials.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 102 ("Prohibition on export to People's Republic of China of national security sensitive technology and intellectual property")
document_name: Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 102 ("Prohibit export of national security sensitive technology and IP to PRC")
body:
Prohibits the Secretary of Commerce from exporting national security sensitive technology or intellectual property, including AI-related goods or services, to China. Defines such technology as essential to safeguard the US economy in order to stop material depletion and reduce inflation that impacts demand in China.

Prohibits the Secretary of Commerce from exporting any national security sensitive technology or intellectual property to the People's Republic of China.

Defines "intellectual property" to include patents, copyrights, trademarks, or trade secrets.

Defines "national security sensitive technology or intellectual property" to include contributions to China's military, U.S. economic protection from draining of scarce materials, protection from inflation that impacts demand in China, and components of key products listed under the Trade Act of 1974.

Includes in "technology" goods or services related to information systems, internet-based services, production-enhancing logistics, robotics, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, or computing.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 101 ("Establishment of list of certain products receiving support from government of People's Republic of China pursuant to Made in China 2025 policy")
document_name: Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act, Sec. 101 ("List of products supported by PRC's Made in China 2025 policy")
body:
Requires the United States Trade Representative to annually list Chinese products, including AI, receiving government support under the Made in China 2025 policy. Identifies specific industries such as AI, robotics, and quantum computing for inclusion.

Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to establish a list of products supported by the Chinese government under the Made in China 2025 policy.

Requires the Trade Representative to list Chinese products receiving support from government of the People's Republic of China 120 after enactment of the Fair Trade with China Enforcement Act.

Mandates made by Trade Representative shall include of required product specifications in key Chinese government documents related to Made in China 2025.

Includes products that displace net exports of similar U.S. products.

Enumerates specific industries such as civil aircraft, motor vehicles, advanced medical equipment, agricultural machinery, semiconductors, lithium batteries, artificial intelligence, high-capacity computing, quantum computing, robotics, and biotechnology for inclusion.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Facial Recognition Act of 2023
document_name: Facial Recognition Act
body:
Regulates law enforcement use of facial recognition by requiring court orders, protecting civil rights, and mandating transparency. Prohibits reliance on facial recognition alone for arrests, requires accuracy and bias testing, and establishes reporting, auditing, and public notice requirements.

Prohibits law enforcement from using facial recognition without a court order, except in defined emergency circumstances. 

Mandates regular removal of photos from databases used for facial recognition, including minors and individuals not charged or acquitted.

Requires detailed applications from prosecutors and approval from courts for authorized use of facial recognition.

Prohibits the use of facial recognition with body cameras, for face surveillance, or for immigration enforcement.

Enforces annual accuracy and bias testing by independent entities and prohibits systems that fail to meet minimum standards. 

Requires public reporting and logging of facial recognition use, including demographic data.

Mandates audits of law enforcement agencies' use of facial recognition to ensure compliance and prevent misuse.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: FAIRR Act
document_name: FAIRR Act
body:
Amends the Financial Stability Act to require the Financial Stability Oversight Council to assess AI risks in financial systems, identify regulatory gaps, and recommend improvements. Enhances oversight of AI service providers, imposes treble penalties for machine-manipulated media, and establishes liability for AI deployment.

Amends the Financial Stability Act of 2010 to assign the Financial Stability Oversight Council duties regarding AI in the financial sector.

Requires the Council to coordinate with member agencies on AI-related financial system risks and direct the Office of Financial Research to study AI use by financial institutions.

Obligates the Council to identify AI-related threats to financial stability, including market manipulation and disruption by malign actors.

Mandates submission of a report within 180 days identifying regulatory gaps and recommending solutions, including referencing the NSA's September 2023 Cybersecurity Information Sheet.

Calls for scenario-based exercises to test AI-related financial disruption defenses.

Expands authority to oversee third-party AI service providers to financial institutions.

Increases penalties for securities violations involving machine-manipulated media to three times the standard amount.

Imposes liability on developers for AI model outcomes under Federal securities laws, with limited potential for waivers.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training")
document_name: FAA R&D Act, Sec. 215 ("Air Traffic Control Training")
body:
Requires the assessment of AI, machine learning, and other technologies to improve air traffic control training. Develops a deployment timeline for these technologies. Involves collaboration with stakeholders. Obligates a report to Congress within one year.

Requires the FAA to carry out a research program to modernize and streamline air traffic control training, subject to available appropriations.

Mandates the assessment of advanced technologies, including AI, machine learning, and virtual/augmented reality, to enhance knowledge retention and training effectiveness.

Develops a timeline for deploying proven advanced technologies and processes for accreditation in training programs and facilities.

Includes collaboration with labor organizations and other stakeholders in the research process.

Obligates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress on the research findings within one year of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: FAA Research and Development Act of 2023, Sec. 210 ("Technology review of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies")
document_name: FAA R&D Act, Sec. 210 ("Review of AI and ML")
body:
Requires the Administrator to review AI and machine learning technologies for airport efficiency and safety. Includes examination of jet bridges, airport service vehicles, aircraft taxi, and other areas. Mandates a report to Congress within one year, including China's AI applications.

Requires the FAA to conduct a review of current and planned AI and machine learning technologies to enhance airport efficiency and safety.

Mandates the review to cover applications of AI and machine learning specifically in jet bridges, airport service vehicles, and aircraft taxiing.

Allows the Administrator to include other relevant areas that can improve airport efficiency and safety.

Obligates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress within one year, detailing the review's findings.

Includes a required examination of China's domestic application of AI and machine learning technologies in the report.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024
document_name: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act
body:
Establishes the Export Enforcement Coordination Center to coordinate U.S. export control enforcement, focusing on AI and other sensitive technologies. Requires developing best practices to combat unlawful export transshipment. Authorizes $25 million for fiscal year 2025 establishment costs.

Establishes the Export Enforcement Coordination Center within the Department of Homeland Security to coordinate export enforcement among various federal departments and agencies.

Focuses the Center's efforts on sensitive technologies, including advanced artificial intelligence capabilities, semiconductors, and quantum technology.

Designates the Center as the primary forum for coordinating efforts against unlawful transshipment and diversion of exports, particularly to countries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Requires the Center to develop best practices and disseminate actionable information to the private sector about export control risks.

Mandates the submission of reports to Congress on the value and logistics of posting U.S. and foreign law enforcement officials to enhance export control enforcement. 

Authorizes $25,000,000 for the establishment of the Center for fiscal year 2025.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Exploitative Workplace Surveillance and Technologies Task Force Act of 2023
document_name: Exploitative Workplace Technologies Task Force Act
body:
Establishes an interagency task force to study workplace surveillance and AI decision systems. Evaluates surveillance's impact on various worker aspects, including compensation and safety. Requires reports and recommendations on addressing surveillance and AI technologies in workplaces.

Establishes the White House Task Force on Workplace Surveillance and Technologies within 180 days of enactment.

Mandates the Task Force to study and evaluate the use of workplace surveillance and automated decision systems by employers.

Requires the Task Force to analyze the prevalence, types, and impacts of workplace surveillance across industries, including data collection, storage, security, and transfer practices.

Necessitates examination of the effects of workplace surveillance on worker compensation, performance reviews, scheduling, career advancement, safety, health coverage, and discipline.

Obligates the Task Force to consider the impact on vulnerable populations, including workers with disabilities, low-wage workers, and workers of color.

Orders the Task Force to submit initial, interim, and final reports to Congress, detailing findings and providing recommendations on addressing workplace surveillance and related technologies.

Terminates the Task Force 60 days after submitting the final report.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Expanding AI Voices Act
document_name: Expanding AI Voices Act
body:
Amends the National AI Initiative Act to require the National Science Foundation to award grants to broaden AI research, education, and workforce development. Targets underrepresented institutions, fosters collaborations, and emphasizes ethical practices in AI education.

Amends the National AI Initiative Act by introducing a new subsection focused on expanding AI capacity.

Mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation to competitively award eligible higher education institutions and nonprofit organizations to enhance AI research, education, and workforce development.

Specifies eligibility for institutions not among the top 100 in federal R&D spending, historically Black colleges, minority-serving institutions, Tribal colleges, and their consortia.

Encourages collaborations with various stakeholders, including AI research institutes and private sector entities.

Allows use of funds for AI research programs, faculty development, resource access, community building, workshops, and ethical AI education.

Requires outreach to eligible entities, emphasizing underserved and underrepresented communities.

Ensures awarded projects complement existing programs without duplication.

Considers diversity, geographic distribution, and resource constraints in award decisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Examining Educational Redlining in Lending Act
document_name: Examining Educational Redlining in Lending Act
body:
Requires the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection to annually assess the use of educational data and algorithmic and automated processes in creditworthiness determinations. Mandates reporting to Congress and public disclosure of findings and involved entities to prevent disparate impacts on protected classes.

Requires the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection to assess the use of educational data and automated processes in creditworthiness determinations annually.

Mandates coordination with executive agencies and civil rights stakeholders for these assessments no later than 180 days after enactment.

Examines educational data by of the covered person in determining their creditworthiness. 

Examines the use of the underwriting processes that gathers data points and creating applicants profiles including automated or algorithmic processes.

Recognizes that risk of automated or algorithmic processes that will establish guidelines to prevent disparate impacts on a protected class. 

Obligates the Bureau to report findings and recommendations to Congress 60 days post-assessment.

Requires public disclosure of assessment findings, lists of covered persons using educational data, and list the covered persons that use an underwriting process to create profiles including automated or algorithmic processes that determine creditworthiness.

Defines "applicant’s background" as data derived from an applicant’s attendance at an academic institution, academic major pursued, grades and test scores for admission, and educational attainment.

Defines "certain educational data" as a non-individualized data derived from an applicant’s educational background, such as whether the applicant attended an eligible institution or a junior or community college.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Ensuring Safe and Ethical AI Development Through SAFE AI Research Grants
document_name: SAFE AI Research Grants
body:
Requires the National Academy of Sciences to establish a grant program for the development of safe AI models and AI research; directs and outlines the submission of a proposal for the program in accordance with guiding principles.

Requires the National Academy of Sciences to establish a grant program for the development of safe AI models and AI research.

Mandates the development of guiding principles and ethical considerations for the grant program.

Directs the Director of the National Academy of Sciences to submit a detailed proposal of the grant program to relevant Congressional committees within one year, including a budget, proposed appropriation request, and an evaluation of existing AI models and methodologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Ending FCC Meddling in Our Elections Act
document_name: Ending FCC Meddling in Our Elections Act
body:
Prohibits the Federal Communications Commission from creating or enforcing rules about disclosing AI-generated content in political advertisements, as outlined in a May 22, 2024, draft proposal by the Commission's Chairwoman.

Prohibits the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from promulgating or enforcing any rules related to the disclosure of artificial intelligence-generated content in political advertisements.

Restricts the FCC specifically from acting on the draft notice of proposed rulemaking circulated by the Chairwoman on May 22, 2024, concerning AI-generated content disclosure in political ads across television, radio, or other services.

Bars the FCC from enacting any rules substantially similar to the aforementioned proposal.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024
document_name: Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024
body:
Encourages the intelligence community to explore private sector partnerships for technological advancement. Expands public-private talent exchanges in AI and other fields. Extends exchange duration to five years and limits access to trade secrets. Requires annual reporting to Congress.

Encourages the intelligence community to form private sector capital partnerships and consult with federal partners to improve technological advantages.

Amends public-private talent exchange authority to focus on fields including artificial intelligence, computing, and cybersecurity.

Extends the duration for temporary detail exchanges from 3 to 5 years.

Prohibits detailed private-sector employees from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information of commercial value.

Excludes private-sector organizations involved in employee detail exchanges from being considered as having organizational conflicts of interest by default.

Requires identification and mitigation of conflicts of interest based on specific participation details.

Mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to appropriate Congressional committees on program implementation and recommendations for enhancing the use of authorities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
document_name: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to plan for deploying advanced border technologies. Authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research emerging technologies, including AI, ensuring compliance with privacy and civil rights policies. Mandates annual reporting on technology deployment and effectiveness.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a plan for deploying innovative border technologies within 180 days. 

Requires the plan to assess artificial intelligence’s impact on privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties, and include mitigation measures. 

Directs the establishment of CBP Innovation Teams to evaluate and integrate advanced technologies, ensuring compliance with DHS policies on AI use. 

Focuses on transitioning technologies to CBP programs, addressing potential negative outcomes and capability gaps. 

Instructs annual reporting on Innovation Teams’ activities, technologies piloted, and their success rates. 

Requires coordination with DHS's AI policies to ensure responsible AI use. 

Demands cost-benefit analysis before large-scale technology deployment, ensuring security effectiveness and governmental cost-efficiency. 

Emphasizes collaboration with the private sector, other government entities, and stakeholders for optimizing advanced technology deployment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
document_name: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to develop a plan for identifying, integrating, and deploying advanced technologies, including AI, to enhance border security. Involves privacy impact assessments, CBP Innovation Teams, and collaboration with private and public sectors.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to develop and submit a plan within 180 days to identify, integrate, and deploy advanced technologies, including AI and machine learning, to enhance border security operations.

Mandates inclusion of information on how CBP utilizes its Innovation Teams and other mechanisms to achieve these goals.

Requires assessments of technology contributions, team compositions, and coordination efforts within CBP and DHS.

Identifies non-utilized technologies from other federal agencies that could enhance border security.

Includes an analysis of procurement authorities and whether additional ones are needed.

Demands explanations on scaling existing programs and descriptions of planned security technology programs with objectives, goals, and timelines.

Assesses the privacy and security impact on border communities and legacy technology phase-outs.

Requires coordination with DHS's Science and Technology Directorate to develop and incentivize new technologies.

Specifies metrics for evaluating effectiveness and identifies recent technological advancements in various surveillance and inspection technologies.

Authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research and adapt commercial technologies, establishing procedures and strategic goals.

Requires annual reporting on Innovation Team activities, including successful technology transitions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024
document_name: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024
body:
Requires agencies using or overseeing algorithms to establish civil rights offices addressing bias and discrimination. Mandates biennial reports on algorithmic harms. Establishes an interagency working group on algorithms and civil rights. Authorizes necessary appropriations for implementation.

Require each agency that uses, funds, or oversees algorithms to establish an office of civil rights focused on bias, discrimination, and other algorithmic harms.

Mandate these civil rights offices to employ experts and technologists to address issues related to covered algorithms.

Obligate each office of civil rights to submit biennial reports to congressional committees detailing the state of algorithms, risks of bias and discrimination, mitigation steps taken, stakeholder engagement, and recommendations for further actions.

Establish an interagency working group on algorithms and civil rights, led by the Assistant Attorney General of the Civil Rights Division, with membership from each agency's civil rights office.

Authorize necessary appropriations for agencies to implement the Act's provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2023
document_name: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2023
body:
Requires agencies that use, fund, or oversee algorithms to establish civil rights offices with bias experts. Mandates biennial reports to Congress on algorithmic bias, risks and actions taken to mitigate them.

Requires agencies which use or oversee a covered algorithm to have an office of civil rights employing experts and technologists on bias, discrimination, and algorithmic harms.

Mandates these offices to submit biennial reports to Congress detailing risks from use of algorithms using artificial intelligence techniques within the agency's jurisdiction, mitigation steps, actions taken to engage stakeholders, and recommendations for further mitigation of algorithmic bias and discrimination.

Establishes an interagency working group on covered algorithms and civil rights, led by the Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Eliminating Abusive and Rampant Neglect of Interactive Technologies Act of 2023 (National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention)
document_name: EARN IT Act of 2023, Sec. 3 (National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention)
body:
Establishes a National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention and tasks the Commission with developing best practices for interactive computer service providers.

Establishes a National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention. Tasks the Commission with developing recommended best practices for interactive computer service providers to prevent, reduce, and respond to online child sexual exploitation. 

Composes the Commission of 19 members, including federal officials and appointees with specific expertise in law enforcement, prosecution, victim services, consumer protection, civil liberties, privacy, computer science, and industry representation. Requires two members to have experience in cryptography, data security, or artificial intelligence. Designates the Attorney General or their representative as the Chairperson.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024
document_name: Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024
body:
Authorize $5 million annually to acquire AI and machine learning tools for data analysis in the Office of Economic Analysis and Targeting. Establish and fund initiatives for robust economic security and technological policy, including AI-driven analysis and strategic foreign assistance.

Amends the State Department Basic Authorities Act to establish a Deputy Secretary of State for Economic Security, responsible for U.S. economic security matters including sanctions, trade, and supply chains.

Transfers assets, personnel, and duties from existing offices to this new Deputy Secretary role.

Redesignates and relocates various offices and positions, including creating an Assistant Secretary for Technology and Innovation Security, responsible for policy on emerging technologies and research security.

Establishes an Office of Economic Analysis and Targeting to conduct economic analysis, prepare sanctions targeting packages, and manage a federal database on economic security data.

Authorizes $5 million annually for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to support data analysis.

Allows hiring of additional personnel without standard competitive service requirements to support these new roles and offices.

Designates Foreign Service officers to represent the Deputy Secretary's mission at strategic posts worldwide.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: ENFORCE Act
document_name: ENFORCE Act
body:
Amends the Export Control Reform Act to prevent foreign adversaries from exploiting U.S. AI technologies. Defines "covered AI systems" posing national security risks. Grants the President authority to control activities related to these systems. Requires licenses for certain exports and related activities.

Amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to prevent foreign adversaries from exploiting U.S. artificial intelligence and other critical technologies.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and "artificial intelligence system" as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Specifies an interim and final definition of "covered artificial intelligence system," focusing on AI systems posing serious national security risks.

Authorizes the President to control the activities of U.S. persons related to critical AI systems and emerging technologies essential to national security.

Empowers the President to require U.S. persons to obtain licenses for exporting or transferring critical AI systems and technologies.

Amends the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to align with the updated export control provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Drone Safety and Efficiency Act
document_name: Drone Safety and Efficiency Act
body:
Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to adopt a performance and risk-based approach when reviewing requests for small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS) to be waived from existing regulations.

Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to adopt a performance and risk-based approach when reviewing requests for certificates of waiver under Section 107 of Title 14, Code of Federal Regulations, which establishes rules for the operation of small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS) for commercial purposes. 

Requires the Administrator to use big data analytics and machine learning to conduct the performance and risk-based approach and refrain from using open-ended descriptive prompts in the waiver application.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Do Not Disturb Act
document_name: Do Not Disturb Act
body:
This bill requires robocalls and text messages to clearly disclose at the start when artifical intelligence is being used to mimic a human voice so recipients know when they are intereacting with AI. the bill also gives double the penalties for scams that rely on AI impersonation.

The bill requires robocallers and telemarketers to clearly disclose artificial intelligence at the beginning of any call or text message when it is being use to mimic a human voice. This ensures that consumers are being informed and aware that they are interacting with AI rather than a real person. The bill also raises penalties for violations involving AI impersonations, the fines however are doubled if used AI to commit fraud, cause harm, or wrongfully obtain money. 

On the other hand, internet-based phone providers such as VoIP services are responsible for verifying the identities of their customers, monitoring call and texts that indicate any AI-driven ronocall ro telemarketing activity. Within this it must conduct investigations into suspecious behavior and reporting evidence of violation to the FCC to enforce the law. The bill then requires the FTC to revise existing telemarketing regulations to mandate clear discolure whenever AI is used in calls or texts.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Diversify Tech Act
document_name: Diversify Tech Act
body:
Establishes a task force within the Department of Commerce to promote diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) in the tech industry. Evaluates AI's role in DEIA, monitors minority treatment, and reports on layoffs and DEIA progress.

Establishes a Tech Industry Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) Task Force within the Department of Commerce.

Mandates the Task Force to conduct audits on minority representation, hiring policies, and layoff trends in the tech industry.

Requires submission of an initial audit report to Congress within 60 days of the Task Force’s establishment.

Obliges the Task Force to promote DEIA, offer guidance to tech entities, and consult with stakeholders on DEIA issues.

Tasks the Task Force with advising on outreach programs and encouraging venture capital investment in minority-owned startups.

Mandates annual reports evaluating tech industry progress on DEIA goals, the impact of AI on discrimination, and proposing policy solutions for accountability.

Requires a special report on how 2023 tech layoffs affected DEIA, including potential violations of federal laws.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Disrupt Explicit Forged Images And Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024
document_name: DEFIANCE Act of 2024
body:
Amends the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022, to define "digital forgery" as AI-created intimate visual depictions. Allows civil action for non-consensual digital forgeries. Specifies damages and relief. Permits privacy protections. Establishes a 10-year statute of limitations. Ensures non-preemption.

Amends the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022, to include "digital forgery" as any intimate visual depiction created via AI or other technological means to appear indistinguishable from an authentic visual depiction.

Allows identifiable individuals to bring civil action against those who produce, possess, disclose, or solicit digital forgeries without consent, with knowledge or reckless disregard of the lack of consent.

Specifies relief for plaintiffs, including actual or liquidated damages of $150,000, attorney’s fees, and equitable relief such as injunctions.

Permits courts to issue orders to protect plaintiffs' privacy, including the use of pseudonyms and sealing personal identifying information.

Establishes a 10-year statute of limitations for actions, starting from the discovery of the violation or the individual reaching 18 years of age.

Ensures the Act does not preempt state, federal, or tribal laws that provide at least as much protection.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Disincentivizing Internet Service Censorship of Online Users and Restrictions on Speech and Expression Act
document_name: DISCOURSE Act
body:
Amends Section 230 to limit liability protections for dominant service providers. Deems providers as content creators if they manage content or use targeted algorithms with a discernible viewpoint. Excludes protections for actions against religious material. Mandates public disclosure of content management practices. Reclassifies immunity as an affirmative defense.

Amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 to limit liability protections for dominant interactive computer service providers based on their content management practices.

Deems providers as content creators if they engage in content moderation or use targeted algorithmic amplification that expresses, promotes, or suppresses a discernible viewpoint.

Excludes liability protections for actions against religious material that burden the exercise of religion.

Mandates public disclosure of content management mechanisms and practices by providers to enable informed consumer choices and entrepreneurial activities.

Reclassifies immunity under Section 230 as an affirmative defense, requiring providers or users to prove they are not information content providers in legal actions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Digital Social Platform Transparency Act
document_name: Digital Social Platform Transparency Act
body:
Requires digital social companies to post and translate terms of service, including content moderation details, within 180 days. Mandates semiannual reports to the Attorney General on terms of service updates and content moderation practices. Imposes penalties for non-compliance.

Mandates digital social companies to post terms of service for each platform within 180 days, detailing contact information, content flagging processes, and potential actions like banning or demonetization.

Requires translation of terms into all supported languages.

Obligates companies to submit semiannual terms of service reports to the Attorney General, detailing content moderation practices and AI involvement, including flagged content statistics and appeal outcomes.

Establishes penalties up to $15,000 per day for non-compliance, managed by the Attorney General, who can take legal action.

Specifies the creation of a public repository of reports for transparency.

Excludes platforms limited to direct messaging or transactions from the Act's scope and protects end-to-end encryption.

Defines key terms and grants the Attorney General interpretive authority.

Ensures Act's obligations and penalties are additional to existing laws.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023
document_name: Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023
body:
Establishes the Federal Digital Platform Commission to regulate digital platforms, including AI processes, ensuring fairness, transparency, and safety. Provides for the creation of a Code Council to develop voluntary or enforceable policy related to digital platforms and AI processes.

Defines algorithmic processes as including artificial intelligence techniques and refers to processes that can make decisions, generate content, or provide information, especially as used in social media

Establishes the Federal Digital Platform Commission to regulate digital platforms, including social media.

Provides for the creation of a Code Council to develop voluntary or enforceable behavioral codes, technical standards, and other policies related to digital platforms and AI processes.

Mandates oversight of algorithmic processes, including those using AI, for fairness, transparency, and safety.

Obligates platforms to ensure recommendation systems and other algorithmic processes are free from harmful, abusive, anticompetitive, or deceptive biases.

Imposes regular public risk assessments for harmful content distribution and steps to mitigate such harms, including those from algorithmic processes..

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act of 2023
document_name: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act
body:
Establishes a Defense Department education course on digital content provenance, training specialists on authentication standards and forgery risks. Launches a pilot program to test industry standards for verifying media authenticity in official DoD content, and requires reporting on progress, effectiveness, and potential permanence.

Requires the Department of Defense to establish a course at the Defense Information School to provide education on digital content provenance for DoD media content, covering challenges from digital content forgery, industry-open technical standards, and techniques for secure digital content documentation.

Mandates a report on the curriculum development and implementation plan for the course, including resource needs.

Initiates a pilot program to assess the feasibility of using industry-open technical standards for digital content provenance in DoD media.

Directs the pilot program to verify digital content provenance, apply technology solutions, assess historical records, and develop effectiveness measures.

Requires a report detailing findings, consultations, effectiveness, and recommendations on the pilot program's permanence.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act of 2023
document_name: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act
body:
Requires the DMA Director to establish a DINFOS course on digital content provenance within one year. Mandates coverage of forgery challenges and authentication standards. Obligates a pilot program with an interim report by January 1, 2026, ending January 1, 2027. Defines key terms.

Requires the Director of the Defense Media Activity (DMA) to establish a course of education at the Defense Information School (DINFOS) on digital content provenance within one year of enactment.

Mandates the course to cover digital content provenance, challenges posed by digital content forgery, and the use of industry open technical standards for authenticating digital content.

Obligates the Director to start a pilot program within one year to assess the implementation of industry standards for digital content provenance for official Department media.

Sets termination date for the pilot program on January 1, 2027, with an interim report due by January 1, 2026, to assess effectiveness and feasibility.

Defines key terms including "digital content forgery" and "digital content provenance" to ensure clarity in implementation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Diabetes Act
document_name: Diabetes Act
body:
Requires Medicare to separately reimburse algorithms in automated insulin delivery systems to promote innovation. Expands access to diabetes technologies and training. Establishes new billing codes for insulin pump education. Proposes national coverage decision on insulin pumps. Evaluates barriers to diabetes technology access.

Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to recognize algorithms in automated insulin delivery systems as medically necessary under Medicare, ensuring their separate reimbursement.

Ensures care continuity for individuals using diabetes technology when enrolling in Medicare Part B by January 2026.

Requires development of a process to consider diabetes technologies not currently covered under Medicare Part B for potential inclusion.

Mandates creation of new coding for insulin pump training and education by 2026, to enhance billing and reimbursement transparency.

Obligates the issuance of a national coverage determination for insulin pumps within 180 days from enactment.

Instructs the Comptroller General to report within a year on barriers hindering access to diabetes technologies and services in Federal healthcare programs, reviewing legal and policy issues affecting access.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Detection Equipment and Technology Evaluation to Counter the Threat of Fentanyl and Xylazine Act of 2024
document_name: DETECT Fentanyl and Xylazine Act of 2024
body:
Amends the Homeland Security Act to enhance drug detection capabilities using AI, requiring research and development of equipment for law enforcement. Directs adherence to AI risk management guidelines and prioritization based on DEA threat reports.

Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to enhance the detection and disruption of drugs like fentanyl and xylazine using advanced technologies.

Mandates research and development of equipment for drug detection and trafficking disruption, emphasizing minimal handling and separation of complex mixtures.

Incorporates machine learning and artificial intelligence to predict controlled substance analogues and new psychoactive substances.

Requires the Under Secretary for Science and Technology to adhere to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or its successor.

Establishes research and evaluation priorities using the latest information from reports on drug threats by the Drug Enforcement Administration.

Ensures federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies have access to improved detection technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023
document_name: Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023
body:
Designates the Secretary of Commerce as principal advisor on blockchain and AI policy. Requires development of policies addressing AI-related risks in blockchain. Promotes U.S. leadership and competitiveness in blockchain and AI integration. Establishes advisory committees and reports to Congress.

Designates the Secretary of Commerce as the principal advisor to the President on blockchain technology and related applications.

Requires the Secretary to develop policies and recommendations addressing issues such as decentralized identity, cybersecurity, AI, regulatory compliance, and fraud reduction.

Instructs the Secretary to promote U.S. leadership and competitiveness in blockchain technology through a Blockchain Deployment Program.

Mandates the establishment of advisory committees with diverse stakeholders to support blockchain adoption.

Directs the Secretary to facilitate the development and dissemination of best practices for blockchain technology.

Obligates the Secretary to consult with private sector stakeholders and disseminate research on blockchain technology.

Requires annual reports to Congress on activities, recommendations for legislation, and emerging risks and trends in blockchain technology.

Terminates the Blockchain Deployment Program seven years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act 2024, Title VII ("General Provisions"), Sec. 7032 ("Democracy Programs")
document_name: DOS Foreign Operations Appropriations Act, Title VII ("General Provisions"), Sec. 7032 ("Democracy Programs")
body:
Include AI challenges in the President's democracy strategy within 180 days, focusing on digital security, countering disinformation, and AI-related democracy threats. Allocate funds for digital security and counter-disinformation initiatives as part of broader democracy programs.

Requires the allocation of $2,900,000,000 for democracy programs from various appropriations, including $159,240,000 for the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor.

Mandates the submission of a comprehensive five-year strategy for democracy promotion abroad within 180 days, addressing digital security, countering disinformation, and AI-related challenges.

Prohibits foreign governments from having prior approval over the implementation of democracy programs and protects the confidentiality of implementing partners in undemocratic countries.

Allocates $30,000,000 to protect civil society activists and journalists and $20,000,000 for international freedom of expression and independent media.

Requires the regular informing of the National Endowment for Democracy about planned and supported democracy programs.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to the AUKUS Partnership")
document_name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to AUKUS")
body:
Requires the President to report non-binding instruments related to the AUKUS partnership. Mandates biennial reports on AI and other tech collaboration under Pillar Two, assessing efforts in AI, quantum, cyber, and other advanced capabilities.

Requires the Secretary, in coordination with officials within the Secretary of Defense and others, to submit a biennial report on the AUKUS partnership starting one year after enactment.

Requires assessments of trilateral collaboration efforts in areas including underseas capabilities, quantum technologies, artificial intelligence and autonomy, advanced cyber capabilities, hypersonic technologies, electronic warfare, innovation, and information sharing.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales")
document_name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and UK in Military Sales")
body:
Establishes expedited processing for AI technology transfers to Australia, the UK, and Canada under AUKUS. Requires anticipatory release policy for AI and related technologies in military sales. Mandates interagency review and update of related policies and guidance.

Requires the President to institute expedited policies for defense article and service requests from Australia and the United Kingdom under the AUKUS partnership.

Mandates prioritization of these requests over all others, except those from Taiwan and Ukraine.

Instructs the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to establish an anticipatory release policy for technology transfers to Australia, the UK, and Canada.

Specifies the inclusion of technologies related to submarines, combat systems, hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, and other advanced technologies.

Subjects technology transfer reviews to an expedited decision-making process.

Directs the Secretary and the Secretary of Defense to update interagency policies and guidance to incorporate these anticipatory release provisions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 304 ("Establishment of the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of State")
document_name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 304 ("DOS Chief AI Officer")
body:
Establishes a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer within the Department of State to oversee AI adoption and advise on ethical AI use. Requires collaboration with the Chief Information Officer for scaling AI. Defines AI per the National Defense Authorization Act.

Establishes within the Department of State a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO), potentially dual-hatted as the Department’s Chief Data Officer, and a member of the Senior Executive Service.

Requires the CAIO to evaluate, oversee, and facilitate the responsible adoption of AI and machine learning to inform decisions and support programs and operations.

Designates the CAIO as the principal advisor to the Secretary of State on the ethical use of AI and advanced analytics in diplomacy.

Mandates the CAIO to possess skills in data analytics, AI, machine learning, and organizational change management.

Requires the Chief Information Officer to consult with the CAIO on scaling AI capabilities across software applications.

Defines “artificial intelligence” as per section 238(g) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of State Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 303 ("Task force to address artificial intelligence-enabled influence operations")
document_name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 303 ("AI-enabled influence operations task force")
body:
Establishes a task force to counter AI-enabled disinformation, coordinate with academia and industry, and develop digital content provenance techniques. Requires reporting on progress and collaboration with international bodies to protect national security and mitigate AI misuse.

Establishes a Countering AI-Enabled Disinformation Task Force within 180 days to identify responses to AI-enabled disinformation threats.

Requires the Task Force to collaborate with private industry and academia to develop digital content provenance detection techniques.

Mandates internal coordination within the Department on AI-enabled disinformation issues.

Directs the Task Force to create a unified international approach for standards and frameworks to counter AI-enabled disinformation.

Requires the Task Force to identify necessary tools and resources for detecting AI-enabled disinformation, producing counter-messaging, expanding digital literacy, and coordinating with various stakeholders.

Mandates a report to Congress within one year on the Task Force’s establishment and progress.

Involves representatives from various relevant offices in the Task Force.

Defines key terms including "artificial intelligence" and "digital content provenance."

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Peacebuilding Act of 2023, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace")
document_name: Department of Peacebuilding Act, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace")
body:
Directs the Department of State to give grants to researchers and developers of AI for the public good as well as researchers who prioritize safety and fair use of AI

There shall be in the Department an Office of Technology for Peace,

The Department of State has a vested interest in ensuring Artificial Intelligence is used for the benefit of society. 

Offers grants to researchers and developers who find ways to ensure that AI is beneficial to society.

Emphasizes the Artificial Intelligence for non-malignant purposes in public health, transportation, and sustainable energy.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Section 2
document_name: Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Sec 2 (Quantum Information Science Research Program)
body:
Amends Section 401 of the National Quantum Initiative Act to require the Department of Energy to conduct quantum information science research and promote commercialization. Requires strategic plans for high-performance computing, cooperation with industry, and development of relevant supply chains. Prohibits funding partnerships with entities posing national security threats.

Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to mandate the Secretary of Energy to conduct a program focusing on quantum information science research, development, and commercialization.

Operates National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to facilitate breakthroughs in quantum technologies.

Requires collaboration with industry, National Laboratories, and educational institutions for technology development.

Engages with the quantum technology industry to promote the commercialization of applications relevant to the Department of Energy's activities.

Submits a 10-year strategic plan to integrate quantum and AI with high-performance computing systems.

Establishes an early-stage quantum high-performance computing research program.

Conducts a study on the quantum supply chain to identify growth obstacles and recommends strategies to bolster domestic manufacturing and workforce development.

Launches a university-led traineeship program to develop the quantum workforce.

Coordinates activities with other federal entities to prevent duplication.

Restricts funding from foreign countries of concern and entities deemed harmful to U.S. national security.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Energy Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
document_name: Department of Energy AI Act
body:
Establishes a Department of Energy program to advance AI research and development across various sectors, including security, energy, and infrastructure. Supports AI innovation, data management, facility upgrades, risk management, and partnerships. Allocates $300 million annually from 2025-2030.

Establishes a cross-cutting AI research and development program within the Department of Energy to advance AI tools, systems, and capabilities.

Mandates coordination across relevant offices such as the Office of Science and the Office of Energy Efficiency to carry out this program.

Requires financial assistance for research in areas like AI application in simulations, data analysis, and energy-efficient computing.

Supports technology transfer and the use of high-performance computing infrastructure to develop advanced AI systems.

Establishes data center testbeds to improve energy efficiency in AI training and inference.

Encourages partnerships with federal and private entities to enhance AI research and development.

Emphasizes ethical considerations, cybersecurity, and data privacy in AI projects.

Allocates $300 million annually from 2025 to 2030 for these initiatives.

Requires an assessment of energy security related to data centers and computing resources, with recommendations for policy changes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Energy AI Act
document_name: Department of Energy AI Act
body:
Establishes a centralized AI program within the Department of Energy to develop and deploy advanced AI capabilities across science and national security, including the development of AI models, datasets, and infrastructure. Mandates AI risk evaluation, workforce development, and partnerships, and allocates $2.4 billion annually for five years.

Establishes the Department of Energy AI Act to advance AI capabilities within the Department of Energy (DOE) by creating a centralized AI program focused on research and deployment of AI for science, security, and technology.

Requires the development of AI training datasets, next-generation computing infrastructure, and safe and trustworthy AI models, and directs the creation of eight multidisciplinary AI Research and Development Centers to strengthen U.S. leadership in AI.

Implements an AI Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Program to address safety and security concerns, and allocates funds for STEM education and workforce development, emphasizing AI skill training and diversity.

Establishes a program to use AI to improve federal permitting processes for energy projects.

Directs the Secretary of Energy to assess the impact of data center and advanced computing demand on U.S. energy systems and national security, and to provide recommendations on energy access, domestic deployment, and efficiency improvements.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Department of Defense Financial Audits Using Artificial Intelligence Act
document_name: DoD Financial Audits Using AI Act
body:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to use AI technology for auditing the Department of Defense's 2024 financial statements. Requires AI development to improve audits and replace outdated systems. Mandates surplus funds' rescission and briefing on audit progress and AI technology.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to ensure the fiscal year 2024 audit of the Department of Defense's financial statements uses AI technology.

Requires the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) and the Inspector General to jointly develop the necessary AI technology for facilitating these audits.

Mandates the use of this AI technology to accelerate the retirement of older financial management systems without compromising essential controls or auditing standards.

Orders the rescission and deposit of any identified surplus funds from the audit into the General Fund of the Treasury for deficit reduction.

Obliges the Secretary of Defense to brief the Senate and House Committees on Armed Services within 180 days on the audit's progress and the AI technology development.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Deceptive Experiences To Online Users Reduction Act
document_name: DETOUR Act
body:
Prohibits large online operators from designing user interfaces that impair user autonomy or encourage compulsive usage. Requires affirmative express consent for certain research and mandates disclosure of such research. Establishes independent review boards and empowers the FTC to enforce compliance.

Prohibits large online operators from manipulating user interfaces to obscure, subvert, or impair user autonomy, decision making, or consent.

Requires affirmative express consent from users for covered research and prohibits manipulation aimed at children or teens to encourage compulsive usage.

Mandates large online operators to disclose the purpose of covered research to users every 90 days and ensure transparency.

Obligates large online operators to establish independent review boards to oversee user interface design and research, ensuring compliance and preventing exploitative practices.

Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop resources for user interface design promoting user autonomy, choice, and decision making.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance, establish regulations for independent review boards, and define acceptable conduct for large online operators.

Provides safe harbor for operators acting in good faith per established guidelines.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Data Science and Literacy Act of 2023
document_name: Data Science and Literacy Act
body:
Directs the Secretary of Education to award competitive grants to enhance data literacy education, including areas such as data science, statistics, and AI, from pre-kindergarten through postsecondary levels. Supports curriculum development, educator training, student support, and partnerships with industry and educational institutions, with reporting and evaluation requirements. Authorizes $10 million annually from 2024 to 2028.

Directs the Secretary of Education to award competitive grants to eligible entities to enhance data literacy education from pre-kindergarten through postsecondary levels.

Requires grant applications to detail plans for increasing access to data literacy and STEM education, evaluating project activities, and continuing efforts post-grant.

Mandates the use of grant funds for developing data literacy curricula, providing professional development for educators, and collaborating with industry and educational institutions.

Limits equipment purchases to 15% of grant funds annually.

Obligates recipients to submit biannual reports on grant fund usage, with data disaggregated by race, ethnicity, gender, and eligibility for free/reduced lunch.

Tasks the Secretary with submitting a comprehensive report to Congress within five years, and requires the Institute of Education Sciences to conduct a national evaluation of program effectiveness.

Authorizes $10 million annually for fiscal years 2024–2028, with caps on administrative expenses and program evaluation costs, and adds a requirement for periodic federal reporting on secondary-school STEM teachers.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Data Protection Act of 2024
document_name: Data Protection Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the Data Protection Agency to regulate high-risk data practices, requiring assessments and evaluations of AI systems. Oversees compliance with Federal privacy laws, emphasizing non-discrimination, privacy harm prevention, and transparency in automated decision-making. Conducts audits, enforces laws, supervises large data aggregators, and collaborates with other agencies for consistent regulation.

Establishes the Data Protection Agency (DPA) as an independent entity responsible for regulating high-risk data practices and the collection, processing, and sharing of personal data. 

Defines high-risk data practices, which include the use of automated decision systems and processes involving biometric information, and mandates high-risk data practice risk assessments and impact evaluations.

Empowers the DPA to issue rules, conduct investigations, enforce federal privacy law, and impose penalties on violators.

Requires large data aggregators, those with significant revenue or who process data of many individuals, to report compliance and undergo regular examinations.

Transfers certain rulemaking and enforcement powers from the Federal Trade Commission to the DPA.

Mandates coordination with other federal and state agencies to ensure consistent privacy regulation.

Allows states to enforce protections, provided they do not conflict with this act. 

Authorizes appropriations for the DPA's operations and activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: DOGE Act
document_name: DOGE Act
body:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to report on AI feasibility for identifying duplicative or fraudulent federal grant applications. Prohibits awarding grants based on such applications and establishes tracking systems for federal grant applications.

Mandates the prohibition of federal grant awards to applicants submitting duplicative or fraudulent applications, with an exception for institutions of higher education.

Requires the joint determination of appropriate agencies to award grants when duplicative applications are identified.

Obliges the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to establish an electronic system to track federal grant applications, preventing awards for identical purposes across executive agencies.

Includes specific system requirements, such as storing awardee details and facilitating identification of essentially equivalent work.

Directs the OMB, along with specific federal bodies, to report to Congress on the feasibility of using artificial intelligence to identify duplicative grant applications and detect waste, fraud, and abuse.

Defines terms essential for the Act's implementation, including covered applications and executive agencies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act
document_name: DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act
body:
Requires DOE and USDA to conduct collaborative AI research for agriculture and energy. Establishes interagency agreements for competitive, merit-reviewed processes and supports data sharing, grid security, and technology development. Mandates a report on coordination and achievements.

Mandates the Department of Energy and Department of Agriculture to engage in joint research and development activities.

Requires a memorandum of understanding to facilitate these activities through a competitive, merit-reviewed process.

Allows collaborative research in areas including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and modeling for optimizing agriculture and energy algorithms.

Promotes data integration, sharing, and secure access aligned with Federal regulations.

Encourages workforce development and infrastructure support as deemed necessary by the Secretaries.

Authorizes reimbursable agreements and collaboration with other Federal agencies to enhance research effectiveness.

Obliges the Secretaries to report on interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities within two years to relevant Congressional Committees.

Ensures activities comply with research security mandates under relevant U.S. Code.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act
document_name: DOE and NSF Interagency Research Act
body:
Facilitates collaborative AI research between the Department of Energy and National Science Foundation, focusing on machine learning, data analytics, and computational advancements. Requires interagency agreements and promotes data sharing, infrastructure support, and STEM education initiatives.

Requires the Department of Energy (DOE) and the National Science Foundation (NSF) to coordinate research and development activities.

Mandates the establishment of a memorandum of understanding between the DOE and NSF, utilizing a competitive, merit-reviewed process for project applications.

Authorizes collaborative research in key areas including artificial intelligence, machine learning, data analytics, quantum computing, and computational sciences.

Promotes interagency collaboration and data sharing among Federal agencies, National Laboratories, and other institutions.

Supports research infrastructure development and STEM education initiatives, including internships and professional development.

Allows reimbursable agreements between the DOE and NSF to enhance research effectiveness.

Obligates the DOE and NSF to report on interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities within two years of enactment.

Ensures activities comply with research security provisions under existing law.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: DOE and NASA Interagency Research Coordination Act
document_name: DOE and NASA Research Coordination Act
body:
Authorize collaborative research between the Department of Energy and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, including on machine learning, and collaborative data and infrastructure usage. Requires the DoE and NASA to report to Congress, within two years, on interagency research and development conducted.

Authorizes the Secretary of Energy and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to coordinate research and development activities through a Memorandum of Understanding, or other appropriate agreements, and authorizes competitive awards to carry out activities.

Proposes collaborative activities to include research of focus areas, including machine learning; the development of methods for accommodating large data sets; data sharing between the DoE, NASA, the National Laboratories, and other appropriate entities; and the enabling of NASA to access DoE infrastructure and capabilities. 

Requires the DoE and NASA to report to Congress, within two years, on interagency research and development conducted, results, and on potential for future areas of collaboration.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements")
document_name: DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements")
body:
Amends U.S. Code to require disclosures and inclusion of content provenance technologies for AI-generated false personation records, with specific disclosure requirements based on the form of the record, and imposes criminal and civil penalties for non-compliance.

Outlines transparency requirements for advanced technological false personation records, requiring producers of such records to include content provenance technologies to identify alterations, as well as disclosures to detail the extent of alterations.

Mandates specific disclosure formats for audiovisual, visual, and audio records.

Imposes criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years, for intentionally failing to disclose or altering existing disclosures.

Imposes civil penalties up to $150,000 per violation and allows for private rights of action for damages and injunctive relief.

Establishes coordinators for deepfake-related violations in each U.S. Attorney’s Office.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: DATA Privacy Act
document_name: DATA Privacy Act
body:
Establishes national data privacy standards for covered entities. Requires clear privacy notices. Mandates FTC regulations within one year. Imposes data minimization requirements. Empowers individuals with data rights. Mandates privacy officers for large entities. Grants FTC and state enforcement authority. Allocates FTC resources.

Establishes national data privacy standards for covered entities handling personal data.

Requires covered entities to post clear, accessible privacy notices detailing data collection, processing, storage, and disclosure practices.

Mandates the FTC to create regulations within one year for reasonable, equitable, and non-deceptive data practices, including opt-out and affirmative consent mechanisms.

Imposes data minimization requirements, limiting data collection to what is necessary for specified purposes and ensuring timely deletion.

Empowers individuals with rights to access, correct, delete, and transfer their data.

Mandates large entities to appoint privacy protection officers to oversee compliance and advocate for privacy policies.

Directs the National Science Foundation to support research on privacy-enhancing technologies.

Grants enforcement authority to the FTC and state attorneys general, with civil penalties for violations.

Allocates resources to the FTC for enforcement and compliance activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act
document_name: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
body:
Establishes a CISA Task Force to coordinate AI safety and security efforts, assess initiatives, address workforce gaps, and promote secure AI adoption. Requires biannual briefings to Congress. Ceases effect five years post-enactment.

Establishes a Task Force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to coordinate efforts related to AI safety and security.

Requires coordination of Agency efforts to improve the safe and secure design, development, adoption, and deployment of AI.

Ensures Agency collaboration in interagency and nongovernment AI-related initiatives.

Mandates assessment and evaluation of Agency safety initiatives to address AI challenges.

Leverages expertise to use AI in defending against cyber threats.

Coordinates efforts to advise stakeholders on AI-related cyber risks.

Identifies AI workforce gaps and proposes solutions.

Promotes secure adoption of AI-based software.

Recommends new initiatives for AI safety and security.

Ensures AI efforts meet privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties standards.

Supports publication and accuracy of the Agency’s AI use inventory.

Mandates biannual briefings to Congress on Task Force activities.

Sunsets the Act 5 years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Countering Communist China Act, Title VII ("Matters Related to Defense"), Sec. 701 ("Modifications to Use of Emergency Sanctions Authorities Regarding Communist Chinese Military Companies")
document_name: Countering Communist China Act, Title VII ("Defense"), Sec. 701 ("Emergency Sanctions Regarding Chinese Military Companies")
body:
Requires amendments to emergency sanctions on Chinese military companies to includes sectors like AI.

Mandates the exercise of emergency sanctions authorities regarding Communist Chinese military companies.

Defines affected companies as those engaged in commercial services, manufacturing, producing, or exporting in the AI sector.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Matters Related to Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("Deterring America's Technological Adversaries Act")
document_name: Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("DATA Act")
body:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in transactions involving sensitive personal data with entities subject to Chinese influence.

Requires the President to impose sanctions on foreign persons dealing in connected software applications under Chinese control, facilitating military, espionage, or malicious cyber activities.

Mandates sanctions for foreign persons involved in election interference against the U.S. or its allies, or influencing U.S. policy in favor of China.

Directs the President to determine and report on whether entities like ByteDance and TikTok meet criteria for sanctions.

Empowers the President to block all transactions involving property of sanctioned foreign persons within U.S. jurisdiction.

Allows the President to waive sanctions on a case-by-case basis if vital to U.S. national security interests.

Terminates the section's authorities five years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 102 ("Sanctions with Respect to Communist Chinese Military and Surveillance Companies")
document_name: Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 102 ("Sanctions for Chinese Military and Surveillance Companies")
body:
Requires the President to impose sanctions on AI development activities and ownership by foreign persons to knowingly be involved/associated with the Chinese military and surveillance apparatus.

Requires the President to impose sanctions on foreign persons engaged in significant operations in China's defense or surveillance technology sectors.

Focuses particular attention on foreign persons engaged in AI, machine learning, robotics, quantum information science, and other advanced technologies.

Utilizes the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to block and prohibit transactions involving sanctioned foreign persons' property within U.S. jurisdiction.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Matters Related to Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities")
document_name: Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities")
body:
Identify categories of technologies and prohibit certain activities in sectors related to AI development that that poses acute threats to US national security.

Requires the President to identify, list, and annually update categories of technologies and products in the AI sector that pose acute threats to U.S. national security if acquired by adversaries.

Requires the President to prescribe regulations prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in covered activities involving listed technologies and products in the AI development sector.

Directs the President to submit annual congressional reports on notifications of covered activities and assessing the need for regulatory amendments.

Encourages multilateral engagement to align with allied countries on similar mechanisms for prohibitions and notifications on technologies in the AI sector.

Authorizes $25 million for implementation and allows direct hiring to administer the entire Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Countering Antisemitism Act, Sec. 8 (Online Antisemitism, Holocaust Denial, and Distortion)
document_name: Countering Antisemitism Act, Sec. 8 (Online Antisemitism, Holocaust Denial, and Distortion)
body:
Requires the National Coordinator to conduct annual studies on online antisemitism, including Holocaust denial and distortion. Recommends transparency in algorithms, content moderation, and platform accountability. Submits reports to specific Senate and House committees for 10 years.

Mandates the National Coordinator to Counter Antisemitism to conduct a study on online antisemitism, including Holocaust denial and distortion, within 180 days of the Act's enactment and annually for 10 years.

Requires the study to analyze the prevalence of antisemitic content online.

Recommends to Congress measures to counter online antisemitism, focusing on transparency in algorithmic systems, content moderation, enforcement of community standards, and accountability for individuals and platforms.

Obligates the National Coordinator to submit the report to specific Senate and House committees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Countering Adversarial and Malicious Partnerships at Universities and Schools Act of 2023
document_name: CAMPUS Act
body:
Prohibits Department of Defense funding to entities contracting with Chinese institutions supporting the People's Liberation Army. Denies visas to individuals from these institutions. Limits educational funding and strengthens U.S.-Taiwan partnerships for Mandarin instruction. Lowers foreign gift disclosure threshold.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to create and annually update a list of China-based universities that support the People’s Liberation Army, with the first submission to Congress due within 180 days of enactment.

Requires the Department of Defense to restrict research, development, testing, and evaluation funding from being provided to U.S. entities that maintain contracts with institutions on that list or on the Commerce Department’s Entity List.

Rars entities from being cleared to host or store classified information unless they certify they have no active research partnerships with listed institutions.

Prohibits federal K-12 education funding from going to schools that maintain contracts with China-domiciled entities.

Authorizes grants to U.S. schools to support Mandarin language instruction and Chinese cultural programming in partnership with Taiwan.

Prohibits federal research funds for entities contracting with listed Chinese entities.

Lowers the reporting threshold for foreign gifts to institutions of higher education from $250,000 to $50,000.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Counseling for Career Choice Act
document_name: Counseling for Career Choice Act
body:
Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to enhance career counseling, including using AI for career development.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to expand career counseling opportunities.

Requires career counseling programs to leverage resources and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Cooper Davis Act
document_name: Cooper Davis Act
body:
Amends the Controlled Substances Act to require electronic communication and remote computing service providers to report suspected illegal activities involving controlled substances to the DEA. Permits algorithmic content moderation, imposes penalties for noncompliance, and mandates annual reporting by the DEA.

Requires electronic communication service providers and remote computing services to report to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) any knowledge of crimes involving fentanyl, methamphetamine, or counterfeit substances.

Mandates the report to be filed within 60 days of obtaining such knowledge, including detailed contact and relevant information about the involved accounts.

Allows reports based on reasonable belief and includes optional additional information like geographic location and complete communication data.

Subjects providers to criminal and civil penalties for failing to report or submitting false reports.

States that providers are not required to monitor users or the content of communications proactively.

Obliges DEA to review and potentially investigate reports, sharing them with other law enforcement agencies as needed.

Mandates the Attorney General to enforce these requirements and take measures for data minimization.

Requires DEA to publish annual reports on the number and outcomes of reports received.

Exempts broadband internet access service providers from these reporting requirements.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Contraband Awareness Technology Catches Harmful Fentanyl Act
document_name: CATCH Fentanyl Act
body:
Establishes pilot projects for testing AI and other technology enhancements to improve contraband detection at U.S. land ports of entry.
