Requires assessments of technology effectiveness, integration, and cost. Involves private sector input and mandates reporting to Congress on outcomes and recommendations.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the CBP Innovation Team, to establish pilot projects within one year to test and assess technologies enhancing nonintrusive inspection systems at land ports of entry.

Requires testing of at least five technology types, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum information sciences, to detect contraband, illegal drugs, and threats.

Identifies effective enhancements based on detection accuracy, efficiency, integration capability, cost, safety, and mobility.

Allows private sector input on commercially viable technologies.

Sets termination of pilot projects five years post-enactment.

Requires reporting to Congress within three years and after project termination, detailing effectiveness, recommendations, cost plans, and performance analysis of tested technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024
document_name: Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024
body:
Requires transparency in AI-generated content, mandates development of standards for content provenance, and prohibits tampering with provenance information. Enforces compliance through FTC and state actions. Penalizes unauthorized AI training using non-consensual content. Establishes public-private partnerships for developing standards.

Mandates the development of standards for content provenance and detection of synthetic and synthetically-modified content through a public-private partnership.

Requires tools used commercially to create synthetic or synthetically-modified content to provide the option of including machine-readable content provenance information, with security measures to prevent tampering.

Prohibits knowingly removing or altering content provenance information in furtherance of unfair or deceptive acts.

Prohibits the non-consensual use of content with attached provenance information for training AI systems, requiring express consent and adherence to copyright terms.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state attorneys general to enforce the Act, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts.

Permits private parties to bring civil actions for violations involving content provenance information.

Ensures the Act does not alter existing copyright rights and includes provisions for severability, maintaining the Act’s effectiveness even if parts are invalidated.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Consumer Literacy and Empowerment to Advance Responsible Navigation of Artificial Intelligence Act
document_name: Consumers LEARN AI Act
body:
Directs the Secretary of Commerce to develop a national strategy and conduct a public campaign in collaboration with federal, state, and industry partners to enhance AI consumer literacy and promote understanding of AI capabilities and limitations for informed decision making.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to develop a national strategy and and conduct a public service campaign to enhance artificial intelligence consumer literacy.

Requires the strategy to promote understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, and support informed decisions on AI use.

Instructs the Secretary to coordinate with various federal agencies, local governments, and private organizations to ensure comprehensive strategy development.

Requires the creation of specialized use cases for AI literacy in domains like healthcare, finance, and communication.
 
Mandates the dissemination of educational materials through multiple communication channels, including a dedicated website, and requires periodic updates to these materials.

Obliges the Government Accountability Office to report on existing federal AI literacy programs and the Secretary to annually report on the strategy's progress and effectiveness.

Authorizes necessary appropriations for fiscal years 2025 through 2034 to implement the Act's activities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Computer Science for All Act of 2023
document_name: Computer Science for All Act of 2023
body:
Expands access to computer science (CS) education nationwide, including instruction in AI and computational thinking. Authorizes the Department of Education to fund grants supporting AI-related curriculum, teaching training, and equitable participation in CS programs.

Requires the Secretary of Education to award grants to states, local educational agencies, and eligible Tribal schools to expand computer science education, including instruction in artificial intelligence and computational thinking.

Mandates grant recipients to provide every high school student with access to computer science education within five years, ensure a progression of computer science education from prekindergarten through middle school, minimize enrollment and academic achievement gaps, and monitor and evaluate program activities.

Requires the use of grant funds for teacher training, expanding access to learning materials, and reducing equity gaps in STEAM education for underrepresented groups.

Permits grant funds to be used for building regional collaborations, hiring instructional personnel, and disseminating effective practices.

Limits use of grant funds for equipment purchases to 15%. Directs the Secretary to reserve at most 2.5 percent of funds available for grants under this section for national activities.

Authorizes $250 million for fiscal year 2024 and the following four fiscal years.

Requires grant recipients to report biannually on the use of funds and disclose student demographics.

Mandates the Secretary to report to Congress within five years on program expansion recommendations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review)
document_name: Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review)
body:
Amends the Energy Policy Act to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to collaborate with agencies and tribes for environmental assessments. Considers project effects and requires use of open-source models. Evaluates impacts on grid reliability and energy prices.

Amends Section 2403 of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 to refine the framework for environmental review in Federal Energy Regulatory Commission licensing proceedings. It requires FERC, other agencies, and Indian Tribes to focus on the ongoing and reasonably foreseeable environmental effects of a project, while excluding nonrecurring past effects, and to assess impacts on fish species, hydrologic patterns, environmental quality, developmental uses, treaty-related requirements, grid reliability, energy prices, and the integration of intermittent generation resources. It also requires consideration of appropriate mitigation strategies, including passage and non-passage options for fish, based on biological, operational, and economic factors.

Directs agencies to rely on fieldwork, literature reviews, monitoring, technical models, and other generally accepted scientific methodologies; encourages the use of open-sourced technical models where appropriate; requires validation analysis for models and data entered into the record; and makes modeling inputs and outputs reasonably available for review, subject to protections for intellectual property, trade secrets, and critical infrastructure information. It requires consideration of innovative solutions and emerging technologies and directs FERC to convene periodic technical conferences on new methods for quantifying hydrologic and related project effects.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Communications, Video, and Technology Accessibility Act of 2023, Sec. 401 ("Emerging Technology")
document_name: Communications, Video, and Technology Accessibility Act, Sec. 401 ("Emerging Technology")
body:
Requires the Commission to report on accessibility barriers in emerging AI and communication technologies. Mandates consideration of specific disabilities' impact. Obliges regulations update every 5 years to ensure accessible AI technologies for disabled individuals.

Amends Title VII of the Communications Act of 1934 to enhance accessibility.

Provides definitions related to emerging technology accessibility.

Defines augmentative and alternative communication as any tool, method, technology, strategy, service, training, coaching, or other support used to supplement or replace speech.

Defines disability using the meaning provided in section 3 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

Requires the Federal Communications Commission to submit a report to Congress no later than 3 years after enactment and every 5 years thereafter.

Requires the report to assess the extent to which accessibility barriers exist for individuals with disabilities with respect to emerging communications and video programming technologies and services, including technologies such as artificial intelligence, augmented and virtual reality, wireless technologies, robotics, the Internet of Things, and other advanced computing technologies.

Requires the report to identify solutions needed to ensure that emerging technologies are accessible to individuals with disabilities and compatible with peripheral devices or specialized customer premises equipment commonly used for accessibility.

Requires the Commission to consider the impact of emerging technologies on individuals with disabilities who face particular barriers to participation and communication, including those with multiple disabilities, limited language access, limited broadband access, or other socioeconomic barriers.

Requires the Commission to issue new or updated accessibility regulations, if necessary, within 2 years after submitting each report.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Comment Integrity and Management Act of 2024
document_name: Comment Integrity and Management Act
body:
Amends the E-Government Act to require verification of human origin for electronic comments, identify mass and AI-generated comments, and allow agencies to post representative samples. Directs OMB to issue guidance for managing these comments and mandates policy updates.

Amends the E-Government Act of 2002 to improve the handling of mass and computer-generated comments in the regulatory review process.

Requires agencies to verify whether electronic comments are submitted by humans.

Mandates agencies to identify and label mass comments and allows agencies to post representative samples of these comments.

Directs the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidance on verifying human submissions and managing mass comments, including the use of technology tools.

Obliges agencies to establish and publicly post policies on handling computer-generated and mass comments within one year of enactment.

Compels the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to report on the identification and impact of computer-generated comments within two years.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Combating Cartels on Social Media Act of 2023
document_name: Combating Cartels on Social Media Act of 2023
body:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to assess and counter cartel recruitment on social media by developing a national strategy, consulting with operators and communities, creating reporting mechanisms, and designating an official within CBP to manage and share intelligence

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to assess within 180 days how transnational criminal organizations use covered services, including social media and other online platforms, for recruitment and other illicit activities, and to evaluate existing government and operator responses

Mandates submission of a National Strategy to combat illicit recruitment activity by Transnational Criminal Organizations on social media and online platforms within one year

Proposes improvements in cooperation between government entities and social media operators, enhanced intelligence analysis, and proactive law enforcement efforts, international partnerships, and targeted outreach to youth in border communities

Requires establishment of a centralized mechanism for reporting recruitment efforts by transnational criminal organizations to the Department of Homeland Security

Excludes any legislative recommendations not enacted by strategy submission date, including encryption policies and Section 230 reforms

Instructs the Secretary to consult with various federal, state, and local entities, as well as social media companies and experts during strategy development and implementation

Mandates semiannual reporting on the implementation of the strategy and its progress to appropriate congressional committees for five years

Designates a specific official within U.S. Customs and Border Protection to manage intelligence related to recruitment activities and to facilitate voluntary information reporting from social media operators

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.")
document_name: Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.")
body:
Amends the Defense Production Act to restrict U.S. persons from engaging in covered activities involving AI and other sectors with countries of concern. Requires notification of certain activities, mandates regulations, and authorizes penalties for violations.

Amends the Defense Production Act to add Title VIII, focusing on protecting sectors like AI.

Defines "covered activities" involving U.S. persons and foreign entities in countries of concern, including AI-related investments and collaborations.

Mandates the President to publish and annually update a list of technologies posing national security risks.

Empowers the President to prohibit U.S. persons from engaging in certain activities with foreign entities in critical sectors, including AI.

Requires mandatory notifications for covered activities not prohibited, with confidentiality protections for submitted information.

Obligates annual reporting to Congress on notifications, trends, and effectiveness of measures.

Directs the President to issue regulations specifying covered activities and technologies.

Encourages multilateral engagement with U.S. allies to develop comparable mechanisms for managing risks in covered sectors.

Authorizes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for violations.

Provides for national interest waivers, requiring notification to Congress.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("Report on establishment of unmanned systems capabilities office")
document_name: HR 7659 Coast Guard Authorization Act 2024, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("unmanned systems capabilities office")
body:
Require the Coast Guard to report on establishing an office for unmanned systems technologies. Include strategies for management, service-wide coordination, contracting, collaboration, and data sharing. Develop operational concepts integrating AI and machine learning tools.

Mandates the Commandant to submit a report to the committees in the House of Representatives and Senate within one year outlining a plan for establishing an unmanned systems capabilities office within the Coast Guard to develop and counter unmanned systems of technology to expand the capabilities of the Coast Guard.

Requires the report to include a management strategy for the acquisition, development, and deployment of unmanned and counter-unmanned system technologies.

Specifies the need for a service-wide coordination strategy to synchronize efforts across the Coast Guard.

Identifies contracting and acquisition authorities necessary to expedite technology development and deployment of unmanned and counter-unmanned system technologies.

Lists commercially available technologies useful for the Coast Guard.

Calls for a cross-agency collaboration plan with the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and other relevant agencies to identify opportunities to partner in acquiring, contracting and sustaining systems.  

Requires sharing information about system awareness from government and commercial to improve maritime dominance awareness.

Requires the development of a concept of operations for a data ecosystem supporting unmanned systems, including AI and machine learning tools.

Provides definitions of counter-unmanned systems and unmanned systems.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2023, Sec. 212 ("Report on Establishment of an Unmanned Systems Capabilities Office")
document_name: HR 2741 Coast Guard Authorization Act 2023, Sec. 212 ("Unmanned Systems Capabilities Office")
body:
Requires the Commandant to report on establishing a Coast Guard office for developing and acquiring unmanned and counter-unmanned systems. Details management, coordination, contracting strategies, and collaboration with federal agencies, and emphasizes integrating AI and machine learning tools in operations.

Requires the Commandant to submit a report within one year outlining a plan for establishing an unmanned systems capabilities office within the Coast Guard.

Mandates inclusion of a management strategy for acquiring, developing, and deploying unmanned system and counter-unmanned system technologies.

Demands a coordination strategy to synchronize efforts across the Coast Guard and pursue expanded research, development, testing, and evaluation opportunities.

Requires identification of contracting and acquisition authorities needed for expedited technology development and deployment.

Lists the need for a detailed inventory of commercially available unmanned and counter-unmanned systems useful to the Coast Guard.

Calls for a cross-agency collaboration plan with the Department of Homeland Security, Department of Defense, and other relevant agencies.

Encourages opportunities to obtain and share unmanned system data to enhance maritime domain awareness.

Mandates the development of a concept of operations for a data ecosystem integrating unmanned system technologies with AI, machine learning, and information-sharing capabilities.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Closing Loopholes for the Overseas Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence Act
document_name: CLOUD AI Act
body:
Prohibits US persons and subsidiaries from supporting the use of remote or cloud integrated circuits by entities in China.

Grants authority to the Secretary of Commerce to prohibit US persons and subsidiaries from supporting the use of remote or cloud integrated circuits listed under Export Control Classification Number 3A090 and 4A090 of the Export Administration Regulations by entities located in the People’s Republic of China or Macau.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Civilian Agency AI Watermark Act
document_name: Civilian Agency AI Watermark Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to consult with relevant directors to develop an AI watermark system for civilian agency applications. Authorizes necessary appropriations annually for this purpose.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to consult with the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office within eight months to develop an AI watermark and trademark system for identifying Federal agency-approved AI applications for civilian agency use.

Authorizes the appropriation of necessary funds each fiscal year to the Secretary of Homeland Security to implement this AI watermark system.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024
document_name: Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits U.S. transactions with Chinese entities operating in AI, defense, and surveillance sectors. Requires sanctions against such entities. Mandates regular determinations of sanctioned firms. Allows presidential waiver for national security. Codifies and updates Executive Order 13959.

Mandates the imposition of sanctions on foreign persons engaged in China's defense, military-civil fusion, or surveillance technology sectors, effective 180 days post-enactment.

Prohibits U.S. jurisdictional foreign exchange transactions involving sanctioned entities.

Requires strict conditions or bans on U.S. accounts for foreign financial institutions conducting significant transactions with these entities.

Obliges the President to respond to congressional queries regarding sanction eligibility within 30 days.

Instructs the Secretary of the Treasury to annually assess sanction criteria compliance for specified entities and report to Congress.

Encourages focus on sectors like AI, quantum tech, robotics, and others in sanction assessments.

Implements penalties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act for violations.

Allows waiver of sanctions if deemed necessary for U.S. national security.

Excludes intelligence, law enforcement, and humanitarian activities from sanctions.

Sunsets authority to impose sanctions 7 years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024
document_name: Child Exploitation and AI Commission Act
body:
Establishes a Commission of Experts to evaluate the existing capabilities of law enforcement to detect and prosecute child exploitation crimes involving AI, and recommend solutions.

Establishes the Commission of Experts on Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence to investigate and recommend solutions for the prevention, detection, and prosecution of child exploitation crimes involving AI.

Directs the Commission to assess the role of AI in child exploitation and evaluate law enforcement's current capabilities to detect and prosecute such crimes.

Requires the Commission to recommend statutory or constitutional amendments to address obstacles to prosecution identified by the Commission and enhance law enforcement's ability to combat AI-facilitated child exploitation.

Mandates the Commission to submit to Congress interim reports as needed and a final report within two years of member appointments.

Details membership of the Commission as composed of 13 appointed experts from various fields, and outlines guidelines on membership qualifications and operational procedures.

Empowers the Commission to hold hearings, obtain official data, and utilize various support services for its operations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act
document_name: Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act
body:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to prohibit distributing AI-generated audio impersonating candidates' voices with intent to mislead voters, exempting certain media entities and satire. Imposes fines or imprisonment for violations, and requires the Federal Election Commission to issue regulations and reports on compliance.

Prohibits the distribution of political communications containing materially deceptive AI-generated audio that impersonates a candidate’s voice, with actual malice, intended to harm the candidate’s reputation or deceive voters.

Applies to communications distributed within 90 days of a general election or 60 days of a primary, special, or runoff election.

Exempts certain entities from liability such as radio or television stations that air deceptive AI-generated content as part of news coverage or communications that clearly constitute satire.

Defines "materially deceptive audio" as AI-generated impersonation of a candidate’s voice without approval and lacking a clear disclaimer.

Imposes criminal penalties of fines or up to 2 years imprisonment for individuals who knowingly and willfully violate the prohibition.

Requires the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to issue regulations to clarify disclaimer requirements and mandates the submission of annual compliance reports to Congress.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: CREATE AI Act of 2023
document_name: CREATE AI Act of 2023
body:
Establishes the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) to democratize access to AI resources, enhance U.S. AI research capacity, and foster diverse talent. Creates a steering subcommittee and program office to oversee governance, resource allocation, and compliance with privacy and ethical standards.

Establishes the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) to democratize access to AI research resources and spur innovation.

Creates a NAIRR Steering governance structure chaired by the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy to oversee governance and resource allocation.

Mandates the National Science Foundation to establish a Program Management Office to maintain day-to-day operations and ensure compliance.

Requires development of an Operating Entity through competitive processes to manage the NAIRR.

Ensures resources include computational resources, data repositories, educational tools, and AI testbeds.

Specifies criteria for user eligibility, emphasizing U.S.-based researchers and entities.

Imposes requirements and audits for privacy, ethics, civil rights, and security in AI research using NAIRR.

Authorizes a fee schedule with a free access tier to expand research participation.

Ensures adherence to national security, research integrity, and open-source principles.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: CONSULT Act of 2023
document_name: CONSULT Act
body:
Prohibits the Department of Defense from awarding contracts to any individual or entity, including those producing AI-powered products and services, that has entered into working agreements with any organization from a blacklist of national security threats.

Requires the Department of Defense to refrain from awarding contracts to any individual or entity, including those producing AI-powered products and services, that has worked with any organization from a blacklist of national security threats.

Authorizes the DOD to punish any contractor of the Department who has a proven conflict of interest with the DOD and fails to disclose that conflict of interest.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: CONSENT Act
document_name: CONSENT Act
body:
Establishes a private right of action against individuals sending unsolicited explicit visual depictions. Defines “machine-manipulated media” as AI-modified. Permits recipients to sue for damages and attorney fees. Exempts third-party providers and certain senders. Allows legal guardians to sue for minors. Permits minors to use initials for privacy. Ensures civil remedies do not supersede criminal laws. Includes severability clause.

Establishes a private right of action against individuals who send unsolicited visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct.

Defines “machine-manipulated media” as media substantially modified using machine-learning techniques.

Permits recipients to bring civil actions for statutory damages up to $500, compensatory damages for emotional distress, attorney fees, and injunctive relief.

Exempts third-party providers, good faith medical, educational, or law enforcement senders, and lawful adult websites from liability.

Allows legal guardians to sue on behalf of minors, incompetent, or incapacitated individuals.

Permits plaintiffs who were minors at the time of the incident to use initials for privacy in court documents.

Ensures civil remedies do not modify or supersede criminal laws.

Includes a severability clause to maintain the act’s provisions if parts are deemed unconstitutional.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Bureau of Industry and Security Information Technology Modernization Act
document_name: BIS IT Modernization Act
body:
Requires the Bureau of Industry and Security to integrate AI, machine learning, and advanced tools into IT systems. Mandates data fusion and analytics for export controls. Enhances data sharing and security. Allocates $25 million annually through 2028 for modernization.

Require the Bureau of Industry and Security to adopt advanced data and analytics tools to improve export licensing, assess global industrial ties, and detect evasive trade patterns.

Requires the Bureau to adopt and use modern data sharing and capabilities to exchange data securely and effectively with industry.

Directs the Bureau to enable the integration of AI and machine learning over time and to expedite Entity List actions and enforcement related to tracking military end users in high-risk countries.

Obligates the Bureau to expedite Entity List decisions and strengthen enforcement targeting military end users in countries of concern.

Collaborate with relevant agencies to map the PRC’s defense industrial base, military-civil fusion strategy, and its commercial ties with Russia.

Demands the modernization of the Bureau’s IT systems through 2029 by implementing a unified platform that enables seamless case management and analysis of external trade data.

Adopt advanced data analytics and sharing tools to streamline export licensing, strengthen enforcement and Entity List decisions, track military end users, and securely share data with partners.

Evaluate technology solutions based on their ability to improve efficiency, reduce costs, strengthen security, enable secure data sharing, and enhance user experience.

Instructs the Under Secretary to reassess staffing needs and consult Congress on personnel adjustments during the modernization.

Authorizes $25 million annually from 2025 to 2028 for these initiatives.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Building Resilient Supply Chains Act
document_name: Building Resilient Supply Chains Act
body:
Directs the Department of Commerce to establish a Supply Chain Resilience and Crisis Response Office to administer grants and loans to support domestic manufacturing and supply chain diversification for in key technology areas, including artificial intelligence.

Directs the Department of Commerce to establish a Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response Office, responsible for awarding grants, loans, and loan guarantees to critical industry and supply chain stakeholders that integrate artificial intelligence into manufacturing.

Mandates the DOC to improve the competitiveness of the advanced tech manufacturing sector, minimize supply chain shocks, and support the creation of related jobs in key technology focus areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum computing.

Directs the Inspector General of the DOC to audit activities supported by the Supply Chain Resiliency and Crisis Response Office's grants, loans, and loan guarantees every four years.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title
document_name: Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title
body:
Allocates $170 million for autonomous surveillance towers using AI for border security. Requires open competition for AI-enhanced non-intrusive inspection technology. Defines autonomous systems as those using AI to identify items of interest. Requires quarterly updates on AI technology impacts.

Allocates $170,000,000 for the procurement and deployment of autonomous surveillance tower systems using AI for border security.

Prohibits the use of funds for non-autonomous border security technology.

Defines "autonomous" systems as those utilizing sensors, onboard computing, and AI for identification.

Mandates quarterly reports on the performance and impact of border security technologies, including AI-driven non-intrusive inspection technology.

Requires acquisition of innovative technologies through open competition, integrating AI and machine learning to improve performance.

Obliges U.S. Customs and Border Protection to submit detailed expenditure plans for autonomous systems, including deployment timelines and sustainment costs.

Instructs the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct cost-benefit analyses before requesting Department of Defense assistance for border operations, including AI technology impacts.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023
document_name: Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
body:
Bans the use of federal funds to operate autonomous weapons systems which launch nuclear weapons or select targets for nuclear weapons without meaningful human control.

Prohibits the use of federal funds to operate autonomous weapons systems which launch nuclear weapons, or select or engage targets for nuclear weapons, without meaningful human control.

Defines 'meaningful human control' as the ability for humans to control the selection and engagement of targets, as well as the time, location and manner of the use of nuclear weapons.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Black Maternal Health Omnibus Act, Sec. 904 (Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care)
document_name: Black Maternal Health Omnibus Act, Sec. 904 (Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care)
body:
Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to commission a study on technology in maternity care. Requires examination of AI's impact on racial and ethnic biases. Includes patient monitoring devices. Specifies identification of bias reduction practices. Directs completion within 24 months.

Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to enter an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to study the use of technology in maternity care.

Requires the study to examine the use of innovative technology, including artificial intelligence, and its impact on racial or ethnic biases in maternal health care.

Includes patient monitoring devices, such as pulse oximeters, in the scope of the study, with a focus on their effect on racial or ethnic biases.

Outlines identification of best practices for reducing and preventing biases in the use of technology and monitoring devices in maternity care.

Requires the study to recommend best practices for using technology and monitoring devices for pregnant and postpartum individuals from minority groups.

Mandates the inclusion of best practices regarding privacy and security safeguards in the use of such technologies.

Directs the National Academies to complete the study and submit a report to Congress within 24 months of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203
document_name: Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203
body:
Amends the Social Security Act to require behavioral health information disclosure, including provider access, wait times, payment statistics, and denial data. Specifies AI and technology use in denial processes. Aims to enhance transparency and informed choice in behavioral health coverage.

Amends Section 1851(d)(4) of the Social Security Act to include provisions for behavioral health information starting in 2025.

Requires the provision of information on access to in-network behavioral health providers, including average wait times for new patient appointments and data on provider participation agreements.

Mandates disclosure of payment request statistics for mental health or substance use disorder services, specifying the percentage handled by in-network versus out-of-network providers.

Requires reporting on the number and percentage of denials for prior authorization or payment for mental health services compared to non-mental health services, categorized by denial type and service type.

Specifies the use of decision support, AI, machine learning, clinical decision-making, or other technologies in denial processes, with comparisons to similar physical health conditions.

Aims to promote informed choice by enhancing transparency in behavioral health service coverage.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201
document_name: Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201
body:
Amends Medicare Advantage plans to ensure mental health and substance use benefits parity. Mandates standards-based necessity determination and NQTL analyses. Imposes penalties for non-compliance. Extends parity to drug plans. Directs regulation issuance within 18 months. Allocates $10 million for implementation.

Amends Medicare Advantage plans to require parity in mental health and substance use disorder benefits, ensuring financial and treatment limitations are no more restrictive than those for medical benefits.

Mandates MA organizations to determine medical necessity for mental health and substance use benefits based on generally accepted standards.

Requires MA organizations to conduct and submit comparative analyses of nonquantitative treatment limitations (NQTLs) for mental health and substance use disorder benefits.

Imposes penalties for failing to comply with the mental health parity requirements.

Extends parity provisions to prescription drug plans, ensuring consistent application across Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue implementing regulations within 18 months.

Sets the effective date for amendments to plan years beginning two years post-enactment, with $10 million allocated for implementation funding through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Basic Allowance for Housing Calculation Improvement Act of 2023
document_name: Basic Allowance for Housing Calculation Improvement Act of 2023
body:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to conduct a pilot program to use AI for calculating monthly rates of basic allowance for housing.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct a pilot program to outsource the calculation of monthly Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH) rates using machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms by engaging a covered entity.

Mandates the submission of a report to the Senate and House Armed Services Committees evaluating the AI-calculated rates.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act
document_name: Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act/AV Accessibility Act
body:
Prohibits states from issuing licenses for Level 4 or 5 ADS-equipped vehicle operation that discriminate against individuals with disabilities. Requires the Secretary to study infrastructure improvements for accessible ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicles. Authorizes $5 million for this study.

Cites the Act as the “Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act” or the “AV Accessibility Act”.

Defines key terms including “disability,” “public transportation,” and “ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicle.”

Prohibits states from issuing licenses for Level 4 or Level 5 ADS-equipped vehicles in a manner that discriminates against individuals with disabilities, in accordance with the ADA.

Mandates the Secretary of Transportation to commission a study through the National Academies to identify changes needed in public transportation infrastructure to improve accessibility for individuals with disabilities using ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicles.

Authorizes $5,000,000 for the completion of the accessibility infrastructure study, available until expended.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act
document_name: Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act
body:
Analyzes potential AI applications in the nuclear supply chain, including cybersecurity, efficiency, maintenance, and workforce training. Evaluates AI's role in identifying counterfeit components and economic considerations. Considers regulatory challenges related to AI usage in the nuclear industry.

Mandates the Secretary of Energy to evaluate the U.S. nuclear supply chain within 270 days, including past efforts, future needs, and lessons from projects like Vogtle 3 and 4.

Analyzes regulatory challenges, including the necessity of N-stamps for nuclear components, cost implications, and potential certification streamlining.

Considers advanced manufacturing and innovative technologies like AI, 3D printing, and robotics for enhancing the nuclear supply chain, with attention to cybersecurity, efficiency, and workforce training.

Describes U.S.-Canada cooperation on nuclear components, assessing competitiveness and recommending collaboration to enhance North American nuclear leadership.

Assesses the impact of anticipated demand for advanced nuclear technology on the supply chain, proposing strategies for resilience.

Establishes U.S. policy to prioritize a robust HALEU market to strengthen energy independence and national security, addressing risks associated with increased nuclear technology demand.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Advancement of Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
document_name: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
body:
Advances nuclear regulatory oversight by encouraging the use of AI and machine learning to enhance risk-informed oversight and inspection decisions. Promotes efficiency through improved technology integration and staff training, while assessing and enabling licensee adoption of advanced technologies.

Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress on actions taken during the COVID-19 emergency, including revised or suspended regulatory policies and their impacts.

Mandates NRC to develop a report within one year identifying improvements in nuclear oversight and inspections using risk-informed, performance-based procedures, information technologies, and AI.

Obligates NRC to seek input from stakeholders like the Secretary of Energy, National Laboratories, and the nuclear energy industry.

Directs NRC to assess the use of AI and machine learning to enhance oversight and inspection decisions.

Instructs NRC to identify specific actions for incorporating advanced technologies into their activities without compromising their mission.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence and Biosecurity Risk Assessment Act
document_name: AI Biorisk Assessment Act
body:
Requires the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response to conduct risk assessments and implement strategic initiatives that address threats to public health posed by AI, especially using AI to develop novel pathogens and bioweapons.

Requires the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response to conduct risk assessments and implement strategic initiatives that address whether AI can develop novel pathogens, viruses, bioweapons, or chemical weapons, including monitoring and researching the global biological catastrophic risk landscape.

Requires the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response to include a summary of the risk assessment above in the National Health Security Strategy.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Weapon Accountability and Risk Evaluation Act of 2024
document_name: AWARE Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to create a ledger of AI-enabled military systems with regular updates and requires a comprehensive risk assessment process covering dependability, cybersecurity, privacy, and bias. Requires annual assessments, annotations for exports, and public reporting to ensure transparency and accountability.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to create a ledger of all uses by the Department of Defense of AI-enabled weapon, targeting, and decision support systems within three years.

Requires the ledger to be a structured, indexed database that is regularly updated.

Calls on the Secretary of Defense to develop a risk assessment process to evaluate dependability, cybersecurity, privacy, and civilian harm risk for each AI system.

Mandates annual reevaluations of each system, and when an AI model receives an update, a new system is procured, or a new weapons review is conducted.

Requires annotations in the ledger when AI systems are shared, exported, or used internationally, noting additional risks.

Obligates annual progress reports and submissions to Congress, including the ledger and risk assessment findings, to be publicly accessible

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Research, Innovation, and Accountability Act of 2023
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Research, Innovation, and Accountability Act of 2023
body:
Develops standards for online content verification, mandates best practices for AI detection, reviews government AI use, prohibits generative AI without user notice, requires transparency reports, and establishes oversight, risk assessments, certification, enforcement, and consumer education for AI.

Requires the Under Secretary of Commerce to develop standards for online content verification. Mandates best practices for detecting AI outputs. Directs review of AI usage in government. Prohibits generative AI without user notification. 
Requires AI transparency reports. Instructs NIST on AI oversight. Obligates risk assessments for critical-impact AI. Establishes AI Certification Advisory Committee. Empowers enforcement of compliance. Establishes consumer education working group.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
body:
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to launch a nationwide public education campaign on artificial intelligence. On the campaign, they must explain its benefits, risks, and everyday uses. They must also promote public understanding of AI-generated media and fraud risks, and call for reporting key performance indicators to Congress.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to create and lead a nationwide public awareness and education campaign about artificial intelligence, focusing on explaining what AI is, how it affects people’s daily lives, and the benefits and risks that come with using it.

Directs the Secretary to work with other federal agencies, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), to make sure the information shared with the public is accurate and up to date.

Instructs the Secretary to set clear goals and measurable results, known as key performance indicators, to track the campaign's effectiveness and gather data that demonstrates its impact.

It also encourages targeted education for groups more likely to be victims of AI scams or fraud, such as older adults, helping them recognize and avoid AI-driven deception. and it promotes public understanding of how AI is used in everyday technology, such as predictive text, navigation apps, and voice assistants, as well as in business applications like fraud detection and financial trading.

Requires the Secretary to consult experts from universities, research groups, private companies, and community organizations to guide the campaign and ensure it reflects real-world AI developments. Lastly, it mandates that the Secretary report to Congress one year after starting the campaign, including data on its success and recommendations for improvement or future AI-related outreach.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy Act of 2023
document_name: H. R. 6791 (AI Literacy Act of 2023)
body:
Amends the Digital Equity Act to promote AI literacy by establishing grants for AI education in schools, community colleges, and higher education. Supports teacher training, lab development, and virtual learning platforms and requires annual Congressional reports on AI education initiatives.

Amends the Digital Equity Act of 2021 to include artificial intelligence (AI) literacy within the scope of digital literacy.

Defines "artificial intelligence literacy" as understanding basic AI principles, applications, implications, limitations, and ethical considerations.

Requires grants to support AI literacy initiatives in public elementary and secondary schools, including teacher training, professional development, and resource development.

Supports higher education institutions to develop AI learning labs, virtual platforms, and educational tools for teachers and community educators.

Includes grants to community anchor institutions for AI education and training programs.

Mandates an annual report to Congress summarizing and analyzing the progress and impact of AI literacy initiatives, with recommendations for expansion or modification.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to submit a report to Congress on the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence

Requires the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to study  the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence, with a report on its findings submitted to Congress within two years of the Act's enactment.

Mandates that the EPA study examine the energy, water consumption, and pollution throughout the full lifecycle of AI models, hardware, and data centers, considering the effects of location, power sources, and AI model design on these environmental impacts.

Requires that the EPA study assess the positive environmental impacts associated with the use of AI, such as optimizing systems for energy efficiency or automatically monitoring environmental changes.

Directs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to work with other government officials to form a consortium comprising academic, civil society, and industry representatives to assess and report on AI's environmental impacts, including the feasibility of open-source tools for measurement and recommendations to mitigate negative environmental effects.

Instructs the Director of NIST to work with other government officials and the consortium to establish a voluntary reporting system for entities to report on their AI systems' environmental impact.

Requires the Administrator of EPA, Secretary of Energy and Director of NIST to submit a joint report on the consortium's findings and its proposed voluntary reporting system within four years of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023
body:
Requires the Department of Defense to develop a bug bounty program for AI products within 180 days. Directs briefing to Congress on program development and future plans within one year.

Mandates the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a bug bounty program for AI products within 180 days of enactment.

Allows collaboration with other government agencies possessing cybersecurity and AI expertise during program development.

Authorizes the implementation of the developed bug bounty program.

Ensures that Department of Defense contracts permit participation in the bug bounty program.

Requires the Chief to brief congressional defense committees within one year on the development, implementation, and long-term plans of relevant bug bounty programs.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Allied Collaboration for Crucial Operations, Research, and Development Act of 2024
document_name: AI ACCORD Act of 2024
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a strategy for enhancing AI-driven defense collaboration with Middle Eastern allies. Establishes a forum for combatant commands to coordinate AI tools and training. Mandates reporting to Congress on progress and recommendations for legislative action.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to submit a strategy to Congress within 180 days to enhance cooperation with Middle Eastern allies using partner-sharing network capabilities for joint defense.

Requires the strategy to include a summary of ongoing efforts, challenges, and recommended actions for implementing joint partner-sharing networks.

Directs the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to establish a forum for warfighters to coordinate on AI tools, methodologies, and training within 180 days.

Specifies that the forum should identify AI use cases, categorize risks, and prioritize AI tools while considering training shortfalls and opportunities for cooperation with allies.

Obligates the Secretary of Defense to report progress on the forum's establishment and recommend legislative actions to Congress within one year.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act of 2023
document_name: AI Advancement Act of 2023
body:
Requires a report on AI regulation in finance, establishes AI bug bounty programs, mandates vulnerability analysis for military AI, requires a report on data sharing, and for other purposes.

Requires a report on artificial intelligence regulation in the financial services industry, establishes artificial intelligence bug bounty programs, requires a vulnerability analysis study for artificial intelligence-enabled military applications, and requires a report on data sharing and coordination.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits federal agencies from acquiring AI products/services linked to foreign adversaries, requiring divestment within specified timelines. Mandates public disclosure of risky AI products/services. Exempts intelligence and specific Department of Defense activities from these restrictions.

Mandates the development of a list of artificial intelligence products or services posing national security risks, focusing on those associated with foreign entities of concern.

Requires the Executive Director, alongside the Under Secretary of Commerce and the Federal Acquisition Security Council, to publish and annually update this list.

Prohibits federal agencies from purchasing or procuring AI products or services included on this list.

Obligates contractors with federal agencies to divest from listed AI products within specified timeframes.

Allows exceptions for intelligence activities and specific Department of Defense operations related to defense intelligence and adversarial AI research.

Defines key terms including "artificial intelligence," "foreign person of concern," and "country of concern," specifying entities like China, Russia, and Iran as countries of concern.

Sets a timeline for initial list publication within one year of the Act's enactment and mandates public notification if no updates are made annually.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act
body:
Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to conduct a study on accountability mechanisms to provide assurances that an artificial intelligence (AI) system is trustworthy and hold public meetings to gather feedback on the disclosure of information about AI systems.

Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to study accountability mechanisms (e.g., audits, certifications, and assessments) that provide assurances that an AI system is trustworthy. This includes defining terms around AI “trustworthiness,” examining how mechanisms are incorporated into AI systems, and assessing their ability to reduce risks related to AI systems, such as cybersecurity threats. 

Requires the Assistant Secretary to solicit stakeholder feedback through public meetings while carrying out the study above and to report the study’s findings to Congress, including recommendations on effective accountability measures for AI systems. 

Requires the Assistant Secretary to consult with stakeholders through public meetings and report to Congress on what information should be disclosed to those who interact with, are affected by, or study AI systems, and the most effective methods for doing so.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment for the Americas"), Sec. 255 ("Transformational Energy Development")
document_name: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment"), Sec. 255 ("Energy Development")
body:
Establishes a Chief Energy Officer to promote transformational energy technologies, including AI, in energy infrastructure. Requires 30% of project support for these technologies. Mandates annual reporting on such projects. Creates a database for international energy finance coordination.

Amends the BUILD Act of 2018 to define "transformational energy technology," including AI applications for energy efficiency and grid operation.

Inserts a Chief Energy Officer position within the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to promote transformational energy technology exports and ensure at least 30% of DFC support targets such projects.

Requires annual and quarterly reports on transformational energy technology projects and international finance of energy generation.

Establishes an Office of Energy in the Export-Import Bank to promote and finance exports of eligible technologies, including those involving AI.

Mandates the creation of a Joint Energy Export, Development, and Trade Database to coordinate inter-agency efforts.

Increases the DFC's maximum contingent liability and adjusts the Export-Import Bank’s loan, guarantee, and insurance authority limits.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment for the Americas"), Sec. 202 ("Americas Partnership Business Advisory Board")
document_name: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment"), Sec. 202 ("Business Advisory Board")
body:
Advises Americas partner countries on aligning regulations related to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Coordinates with USMCA central regulatory bodies. Requires an annual report on business environments, highlighting investment opportunities and challenges.

Establishes a business advisory board under the Americas Partnership Secretariat to meet periodically and provide guidance on a case by case bases at the Secretariat.

Composes the board of representatives from private sector entities, civil society, and labor organizations from partner countries.

Allows the business board to advise on issues including regulatory hurdles, labor issues, dispute resolution, legal investment hurdles, and alignment on regulations related to emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, harmonizing of reference price systems, and other issues affecting business.

Requires coordination with central regulatory bodies as outlined in the USMCA.

Mandates the board to submit an annual report on the business environment on American partners, highlighting opportunities and challenges to investment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Americas Act, Title I ("Administration"), Sec. 103 ("Additional Duties of Institute")
document_name: Americas Act, Title I ("Administration"), Sec. 103 ("Duties of Institute")
body:
Requires the Institute to promote international collaboration with American partners on e-governance, incorporate emerging technologies like AI, ensure compliance with standards, and restrict data sharing with specific countries to protect privacy and security. Authorizes funding and technical assistance for partner countries.

Mandates the Institute to promote international collaboration on e-governance systems with Americas partner countries.

Requires assistance in developing e-governance systems under the framework from section 102, and systems development before the implementation of the Act.

Facilitates the development or adoption, in collaboration with appropriate national and international standards organizations, of technical standards to promote efficient system development.

Supports the creation of reference implementations for e-government services when appropriate.

Maintains infrastructure that can be shared by multiple services, including across multiple Americas partner countries.

Provides technical assistance to partner countries, including entering into contracts to develop or host services on their behalf, and may receive funding from those countries for such services.

Allows procurement or licensing of commercial technology for shared use and certifies audit organizations.

Permits partnerships with private sector entities and provides financing to support the development or modernization of systems.

Accounts for emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, and may incorporate such technologies into systems or recommend how partner countries integrate or regulate them.

Restricts procurement and data sharing under the e-governance framework with specific countries, including Russia and China, to ensure privacy and security.

Grants authority to exclude individuals, entities, or products not from approved countries to protect citizens’ privacy and security.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: American Privacy Rights Act of 2024, Sec. 114-5
document_name: American Privacy Rights Act of 2024, Sec. 114-5
body:
Establishes a pilot program to promote privacy-enhancing technologies like homomorphic encryption and federated learning. Requires development of a petition process and an auditing system for oversight. Mandates ongoing audits and allows withdrawal for non-compliance. Provides liability limitations for compliant participants.

Establishes a pilot program to encourage private sector use of privacy-enhancing technologies within one year of the Act's enactment to protect covered data.

Requires the Commission to develop a petition process for entities to join the pilot program and implement an auditing system using privacy-enhancing technologies for enforcement purposes.

Mandates ongoing audits of participating entities to ensure compliance with privacy-enhancing technologies.

Allows covered entities deemed compliant to be considered in compliance with section 109, with a rebuttable presumption in certain legal actions.

Obligates the Comptroller General to study the pilot program's progress and effectiveness, with an initial briefing and a final report to Congress.

Creates a new bureau within the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce the title with experts, including technologists experienced with AI.

Establishes a Privacy and Security Victims Relief Fund for consumer redress and technological research.

Requires the FTC to report to Congress on investigations and future plans related to the title.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: American Medical Innovation and Investment Act of 2024 (Sec. 5)
document_name: American Medical Innovation and Investment Act of 2024 (Sec. 5)
body:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance by January 1, 2026, on Medicare payment requirements for remote monitoring devices with AI components that transmit data to healthcare providers for patient management and treatment.

Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance on required Medicare payment for continuous glucose monitors by January 1, 2026. 

Specifies that the use AI components like continuous adjustment. 

Requires that these devices transmit information to healthcare providers for management and treatment purposes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: American Foreign Affairs Talent Expansion Act: Diversity in Diplomacy and Development, Section 112 (Mitigating bias in artificial intelligence use.)
document_name: American FATE Act, Sec 112 ("Mitigating bias in artificial intelligence use.")
body:
Urges agencies to address AI bias risks. Requires employing experts for developing bias-mitigation frameworks. Mandates biennial reports to Congress on efforts ensuring AI safety, testing for bias, and resource needs for effective bias correction over eight years.

Require international affairs agencies to employ experts, including technologists, social scientists, and legal experts, to develop a risk-mitigation framework for trustworthy AI systems, addressing bias in AI training data and applications.

Mandate reports from each agency to appropriate congressional committees, describing efforts to ensure safe, secure, and trustworthy AI development and use, including testing and correcting for bias, starting one year after the enactment of the Act and every two years for the following eight years.

Impose a congressional expectation to implement measures addressing AI bias to prevent negative or discriminatory outcomes in agency operations.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: American Economic Independence Act of 2024
document_name: American Economic Independence Act
body:
Requires regular reports on U.S.-China economic integration, assessing national security risks, including reliance on Chinese AI. Mandates analysis of risks like intellectual property theft and defense industrial base threats. Recommends mitigation steps and involves key government officials in the evaluation process.

Requires the President, through the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to submit a report to Congress on the state of economic integration between the U.S. and China, and the national security risks posed by this integration, every three years for 15 years. 

Mandates each report to assess the level of economic integration and its changes since 2000, with predictions for the next three years, specifically in priority sectors including artificial intelligence. Requires that the OMB looks at other priorities as well such as semiconductors, microelectronics, quantum computing, biotechnology, cloud and more. 

Includes analysis of risks such as reliance on Chinese entities that examine China linked capital investment, supply chain, economic espionage, defense industrial base and risk from subsidies and dumping into US markets. Requires recommendations for mitigating identified risks.

Requires other government entities to consult with the OMB to produces this report such as the State, Treasury, Defense, Attorney General, Interior, Commerce, Energy, HHS, DOJ, USTR, DNI, DHS, NSF and others. 

Permits consultation with nongovernmental entities and submission of the report in an unclassified form, potentially with a classified annex.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023
document_name: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023
body:
Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to issue rules requiring “covered entities” to conduct, document, and submit impact assessments for automated decision systems used in critical decisions (e.g., jobs, credit, housing, health, education). Requires initial and annual summary reports, stakeholder consultation, testing for performance and fairness, and mitigation of likely material harms resulting from automated decision systems. Creates an FTC Bureau of Technology, builds a public repository of summaries, redefines violations under the FTC Act, and authorizes state attorney general enforcement.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to issue regulations requiring covered entities to conduct and document impact assessments for automated decision systems (ADS) and augmented critical decision processes that materially affect consumers in areas such as employment, education, housing, healthcare, and finance.

Requires covered entities to perform pre-deployment and ongoing evaluations addressing privacy, security, reliability, fairness, and potential discriminatory or harmful impacts, and to mitigate any material negative effects identified.

Mandates stakeholder consultation with internal ethics and technology teams and external experts, advocates, and impacted communities during system design, testing, and deployment.

Requires covered entities to maintain detailed documentation and submit both initial and annual summary reports to the FTC in standardized, machine-readable formats describing system purpose, data sources, performance metrics, fairness testing, and mitigation measures.

Directs the FTC to establish a public, searchable repository containing non-confidential information from summary reports and to publish annual aggregate findings on the use and oversight of automated decision systems.

Establishes a Bureau of Technology within the FTC to oversee implementation, technical analysis, and enforcement, supported by additional staff and resources.

Treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts or practices (UDAP) under the FTC Act, authorizes state attorneys general to bring civil enforcement actions, and encourages coordination with other federal and state regulators.

Preserves existing state, tribal, and local laws while promoting consistent national oversight of algorithmic decision-making systems.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023
document_name: Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023
body:
Requires the FAA administrator to, within three years, mandate new safety requirements for commercial air tour operators,  including training in strategies for maintaining control, such as through the use of automated systems. Establishes a rulemaking committee to develop standards and recommendations, including algorithm-driven traffic advisory systems, whose findings the administrator reports to Congress.

Requires the FAA administrator to, within three years of enactment, mandate new safety requirements for all certified commercial air tour operators to incorporate avoidance training for controlled flight into terrain and in-flight loss of control, including strategies for maintaining control, such as the use of automated systems.

Mandates the FAA Administrator to convene an aviation rulemaking committee to review and develop standards for commercial air tour operators, including establishing methods for traffic avoidance utilizing advisory systems driven by algorithms.

Directs the committee to consider how flight data recording technologies can identify and correct hazardous trends, how data can be used to modify behavior to prevent accidents, and technological advancements in flight data recording technology.

Requires the FAA Administrator to submit a report to Congress within 20 months based on the committee's findings, issue an intent to proceed with proposed rulemakings within 12 months after the report, and issue final rules within three years of enactment.

Authorizes appropriations as necessary to implement the Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024
document_name: Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024
body:
Amends the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act to require biennial reports assessing national security gaps, including AI and cybersecurity. Establishes a Senior Advisor for National Security to coordinate activities and improve interagency collaboration on food and agriculture security vulnerabilities.

Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to prioritize national security alongside homeland security within the Department of Agriculture, including increasing staff with security clearances.

Establishes the position of Senior Advisor for National Security to advise the Secretary and coordinate with the National Security Council on national security matters related to food and agriculture.

Authorizes the Secretary to exchange personnel with defense, national security, law enforcement, and intelligence agencies to improve information sharing and risk mitigation.

Requires biennial reports to Congress and the National Security Council assessing national security gaps in the food and agriculture sector, including cybersecurity and AI, and detailing actions taken and recommendations for policy changes.

Addresses vulnerabilities concerning agricultural data, foreign influence, and emerging technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act
document_name: Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act
body:
Requires all entities that generate AI materials for public consumption to label them with watermarks.

Requires all AI-generated materials to be labeled with a watermark. 

Authorizes the federal government to establish requirements and standards for watermarks.

Enables the federal government to levy penalties against entities that violate the above stipulation.

Defines key terms including AI-generating entity, AI-generated material, and covered AI-generated material, specifying criteria for materials that must be watermarked.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act
document_name: Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act
body:
Directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to evaluate and integrate advanced technologies, including AI and machine learning, into nuclear oversight and inspection processes. Requires reports to Congress and stakeholder consultation to enhance risk-informed, performance-based regulation and operational efficiency.

Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress within 180 days on regulatory changes made during the COVID-19 emergency, examining their impact on licensing and safety.

Mandates the NRC to develop and submit a report within one year identifying specific improvements in oversight and inspection programs, emphasizing risk-informed, performance-based procedures and the use of advanced technologies, including AI and machine learning.

Directs the NRC to consult with the Department of Energy, National Laboratories, industry, and nongovernmental stakeholders in developing these reports.

Requires assessment of oversight processes, event reporting, staff training, and digital modernization to improve regulatory efficiency and safety without compromising public health or security.

Obligates the NRC to identify and implement actions based on assessments and recommendations to improve training, inspection, oversight, and licensing activities without compromising its mission. 

Instructs the Government Accountability Office to review the NRC’s facility and office space use to reduce costs for taxpayers and licensees.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advancing Automation Research and Development in Agriculture Act
document_name: Advancing Automation Research and Development in Agriculture Act
body:
Establishes a competitive grant program to advance mechanization and automation in specialty crops. Prioritizes projects enhancing labor efficiency, technology adoption, and human capital development. Requires non-Federal matching funds and scientific peer review. Allocates $20 million annually from 2024 onwards.

Establishes a stand-alone competitive research and extension grant program under the Department of Agriculture to advance mechanization and automation for specialty crops.

Mandates projects to create or improve cost-effective technologies that reduce manual labor and increase efficiency in crop production, resource management, and processing.

Requires projects to promote the adoption of mechanization and automation technologies by emphasizing factors such as connectivity, autonomy, and cost-effectiveness.

Specifies projects to accelerate automation through prototype development, in-field trials, and rapid commercialization.

Allows grants to be awarded to federal agencies, universities, research institutions, private organizations, and other eligible entities.

Mandates a competitive grant process based on scientific peer review and industry relevance.

Requires annual consultations with the specialty crops committee to review procedures, objectives, and grant awards.

Allocates $20 million annually from the Commodity Credit Corporation to fund the program starting fiscal year 2024.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act
document_name: Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act
body:
Directs the Department of Energy and NOAA to collaborate on AI and high-performance computing for climate and weather modeling. Establishes competitive processes, data sharing, and infrastructure improvements, with progress reports required two years post-enactment. Termination occurs five years post-enactment.

Directs the Department of Energy (DOE) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to collaborate on AI and high-performance computing research to improve climate models and weather prediction.

Requires the establishment of a memorandum of understanding to facilitate this collaboration through a competitive, merit-reviewed process.

Authorizes the Secretary of Energy and NOAA Administrator to conduct research on modeling, simulation, machine learning, data assimilation, and predictive analysis techniques.

Mandates the promotion of collaboration and data sharing among federal agencies, National Laboratories, educational institutions, and nonprofits, while ensuring compliance with national security policies.

Instructs the submission of a report within two years detailing interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities.

Initiates a high-performance computing project to enhance weather prediction models, requiring a comparative analysis with current forecasts.

Sunsets the authority for this initiative five years post-enactment.

Ensures compliance with research security provisions under the CHIPS Act of 2022.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act
document_name: S. 3642 Weather Model Computing Act
body:
Directs the Secretary of Energy and NOAA Administrator to conduct collaborative research using AI and advanced computing to improve weather models. Establishes initiatives and potential centers of excellence, promoting data sharing and workforce development.

Defines key terms regarding the use of AI in developing weather models.

Directs the Secretary of Energy and the NOAA Administrator to conduct collaborative research using advanced computing techniques, including AI, to improve weather models.

Requires establishment of a memorandum of understanding or similar agreement to facilitate this collaboration through a competitive, merit-reviewed process.

Supports the Secretary and Administrator to explore performance portability for weather models, advance large-scale data analysis methods, promote open collaboration and data sharing, support computing infrastructure, and use reimbursable agreements and interagency collaboration to maximize effectiveness.

Initiates a computing research initiative to develop and deploy advanced weather models using advanced computing techniques, including coordinating research to prevent duplication, supporting workforce development and infrastructure, conducting comparative forecast research, and sharing model innovations.

Permits establishment of up to three centers of excellence at National Laboratories to support advanced weather models through public-private partnerships, software optimization, and workforce development; prioritizes selection of Laboratories with AI-enabled computing systems and expertise in weather and climate modeling.

Mandates submission of reports to Congress detailing interagency coordination, achievements, and future opportunities for collaboration in advanced computing techniques.

category: U.S. federal laws
