title: Advanced Safe Testing at Residence Telehealth Act of 2023, Sec. 2 ("Coverage and Payment for Certain Tests and Assistive Telehealth Consultations; Demonstration Program Under Certain State Medicaid Programs")
document_name: Testing at Residence Telehealth Act, Sec. 2 ("Tests and Assistive Telehealth Consultations Demonstration")
body:
Establishes a Value-Based Insurance Design Model for Medicare, covering AI-driven wearable medical devices and assistive telehealth. Limits demonstration to 25 plans, promoting rural access, and requires demographic data for reimbursement. Allocates funding for state Medicaid telehealth programs.

Establishes a Value-Based Insurance Design Model (VBID) demonstration program to provide Medicare beneficiaries with assistive telehealth consultations and home-based care.

Requires eligible Medicare Advantage (MA) plans to cover medical tests, including those utilizing adaptive AI and machine learning, for various diseases and conditions.

Limits the VBID program to a maximum of 25 MA plans, with at least 10 plans serving rural or underserved areas.

Mandates demographic data collection for reimbursement claims, including age, race, ethnicity, gender, and chronic conditions.

Administers a grant program for state Medicaid programs to cover similar tests and telehealth consultations, with grants awarded to 5-10 states or territories for a 4-year period, not exceeding $12 million per state.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advanced Aviation Integration Act
document_name: Advanced Aviation Integration Act
body:
Designates the FAA Deputy Administrator to lead the integration of advanced aviation systems, establishes the Office of Advanced Integration, and creates the Advanced Aviation Coordination Unit to strengthen oversight, certification, and collaboration on unmanned and emerging aviation technologies within the national airspace.

Designates the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as the executive responsible for leading advanced aviation integration across the national airspace.

Requires coordination among FAA offices to manage policy, rulemaking, research, and workforce planning related to advanced aviation systems.

Mandates the Deputy Administrator to submit biannual reports on workforce requirements, staffing, and budget resources for advanced aviation oversight.

Establishes an Office of Advanced Integration, led by a Director, to manage coordination and leadership functions for advanced aviation system research, rulemaking, and certification.

Creates an Advanced Aviation Coordination Unit composed of representatives from FAA offices to promote safe integration, streamline certification, and develop consistent standards for advanced aviation systems.

Directs the formation of working groups on unmanned aircraft systems, advanced air mobility, and safety technology integration under the Coordination Unit.

Defines “advanced aviation system” to include unmanned, powered-lift, autonomous, electric, and hydrogen-powered aircraft, as well as digital and information-centric aviation systems.

Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to facilitate interagency coordination to support the FAA’s integration and standardization efforts.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Advanced Aviation Act
document_name: Advanced Aviation Act
body:
Establishes the Office of Advanced Aviation, headed by an Associate Administrator, to oversee rulemaking, certification, and integration of advanced aviation systems, including AI-driven technologies, into national airspace. Requires interagency coordination and stakeholder engagement for safe and timely integration.

Redesignates the Office of NextGen as the Office of Advanced Aviation within 1 year.

Appoints an Associate Administrator to oversee the Office of Advanced Aviation.

Coordinates rulemaking and approval processes for advanced aviation systems' standardization, certification, safety, and integration into national airspace.

Establishes an Office of Advanced Integration to manage responsibilities related to advanced aviation systems.

Forms an Advanced Aviation Coordination Unit to promote safe integration and certification of advanced aviation systems.

Redesignates the William J. Hughes Technical Center as the William J. Hughes Technical Center for Advanced Aviation, responsible for research, development, and integration of new aviation technologies.

Establishes an Aviation Innovation Program to evaluate and integrate new aviation-related technologies into the national airspace system.

Defines "advanced aviation systems" to include unmanned aircraft systems, counter-UAS systems, powered lift aircraft, and related technologies.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: ASSESS AI Act
document_name: ASSESS AI Act
body:
Establishes a task force to assess AI's privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties implications; outlines duties and responsibilities of task force.

Establishes a task force to assess privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties implications of artificial intelligence. 

Charges the task force to evaluate existing policy, regulatory, and legal gaps for AI applications and make legislative and regulatory recommendations.

Directs the task force to address the application of federal antidiscrimination laws, disparate impact standards, AI validation, and auditing in federal use of AI.

Instructs the task force to consider institutional changes for ongoing AI governance and the potential creation of a new oversight organization.

Requires the task force to submit an interim report within one year and a final report within 18 months.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: ASK Act
document_name: ASK Act
body:
Directs the FCC, in consultation with the FTC, to issue rules prohibiting the offer of artificial intelligence products to minors without parental consent.

Directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), in consultation with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), to issue rules prohibiting the offer of artificial intelligence products to minors without parental consent.

Mandates the rule to include a provision allowing parents and guardians to revoke consent at any time.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AREA Act, Part B ("National Center for Education Research"), Sec. 133 ("Duties")
document_name: AREA Act, Part B ("National Center for Education Research"), Sec. 133 ("Duties")
body:
Amends duties of the Research Commissioner to support AI and digital literacy research, coordinate evidence use, and advance educational technology. Mandates AI-focused studies on educational technology, including developing evidence-based practices and supporting research-practice partnerships with AI considerations.

Amends the duties of the Research Commissioner to include maintaining peer-review standards and supporting scientifically valid research.

Requires the Commissioner to propose and implement a research plan, ensuring the research is relevant and informs decision-making.

Mandates the support of evidence-based practices and the dissemination of research findings.

Grants authority to conduct research on underrepresented student populations and to support research-practice partnerships.

Obligates the Commissioner to ensure research is reviewed for inclusion in the National Education Research Database.

Allows for the provision of technical assistance to underrepresented researchers and institutions.

Supports research on educational technology, including artificial intelligence, digital literacy, and other significant educational topics.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI for National Security Act
document_name: AI for National Security Act
body:
Amends Section 1521 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 to expand the Department of Defense's procurement of cyber data products and services to include AI-driven endpoint security and to strengthen software supply chain security.

Amends Section 1521 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 to expand the Department of Defense's procurement of cyber data products and services to include AI-driven endpoint security and to strengthen software supply chain security.

Inserts a provision to enhance the security of the software supply chain of the Department of Defense using AI.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024
document_name: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024
body:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to require clear disclaimers on political ads using AI-generated content. Imposes penalties for non-compliance and mandates the Federal Election Commission to issue regulations and report compliance.

Requires the inclusion of disclaimers on political advertisements containing content substantially generated by AI.

Mandates that disclaimers must clearly state the use of AI in creating or materially altering the content.

Establishes safe harbor guidelines for what constitutes a "clear and conspicuous manner" in disclaimers for image, audio, and video communications.

Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to include penalties for violations of the disclaimer requirements, with fines up to $50,000.

Directs the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to issue regulations outlining criteria for determining substantially AI-generated content and requirements for the disclosure statement. 

Requires the FEC to report on compliance and enforcement within two years and biannually thereafter to Congress.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024
document_name: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024
body:
Mandates disclaimers on political ads containing AI-generated content, establishes penalties for non-compliance, and requires the Federal Election Commission to issue regulations and periodic reports on enforcement and compliance.

Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to require disclaimers on political advertisements containing content generated by AI.

Outlines requirements for clear disclosure in ads using AI-generated images, audio, or video, specifying format requirements for visibility and audibility.

Imposes penalties for non-compliance, with fines up to $50,000 per violation, and establishes enforcement mechanisms.

Obliges the Federal Election Commission to issue regulations within 90 days, outlining criteria for AI content identification and disclosure requirements.

Requires the FEC to report biannually on compliance and enforcement, providing recommendations for improvements.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Training Expansion Act of 2023
document_name: AI Training Expansion Act of 2023
body:
Expand training programs for helping executive branch employees better understand the function, risks and benefits, and nature of artificial intelligence.

Amends the Artificial Intelligence Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act to expand artificial intelligence training within the executive branch.

Requires the training program to cover capabilities, risks and benefits, and mitigation strategies associated with AI.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI PLAN Act
document_name: AI PLAN Act
body:
Requires the Secretaries of the Treasury, Homeland Security, and Commerce to submit an annual report to Congress on the risks of use of AI in the commission of financial crimes.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Secretary of Commerce to submit a joint report to Congress on the risks of use of AI in financial crimes, including fraud and misinformation, within 180 days of enactment and annually thereafter.

Mandates the inclusion in the report of interagency policies, procedures, and resources needed to defend against AI-driven financial crimes.

Directs the report to include the consideration of risks such as deepfakes, voice cloning, foreign election interference, synthetic identities, false market signals, and overall digital fraud.

Requires the subsequent submission of legislative recommendations and best practices to address risks identified within 90 days of each report.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Leadership Training Act
document_name: AI Leadership Training Act
body:
Establishes an AI leadership training program for executive agencies. Requires annual training on AI capabilities, risks, and ethics. Mandates topics cover AI basics, risks, and constitutional issues. Obligates updates biennially. Demands participation metrics. Permits Congressional oversight. Sets a 10-year sunset clause.

Establishes an AI leadership training program for management officials, supervisors, and other designated employees in executive agencies, to be developed and implemented within 18 months.

Requires annual training to cover AI capabilities, risks, safety, ethics, Federal Government requirements, and best practices related to AI procurement, use, testing, evaluation, and auditing.

Mandates program topics include AI basics, benefits, risks, data significance, AI system failures, continuous refinement, risk mitigation, organizational considerations, and constitutional risks related to AI use.

Obligates updates to the program every two years to incorporate new AI information and ensure compliance with training requirements.

Demands metrics to measure participation and feedback for program improvements.

Permits Congress to request detailed information about the program materials and responsible personnel.

Encourages interaction with experts from various sectors as part of the training.

Sets a sunset clause for the program 10 years after enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Leadership To Enable Accountable Deployment Act
document_name: AI LEAD Act
body:
Establishes the Chief AI Officers Council to promote and coordinate AI innovation and risk management. Requires each agency to appoint a CAIO responsible for developing and implementing AI strategies.

Establishes the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers Council to promote AI innovation, oversee compliance, and advise on best practices for AI technologies.

Requires each agency to designate a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer responsible for promoting AI use, managing risks, and ensuring transparency and privacy.

Mandates the creation of Artificial Intelligence Coordination Boards within agencies to address AI issues and publish guiding principles and goals.

Directs agencies to develop an AI strategy focused on responsible and trustworthy adoption, public trust, risk mitigation, and interagency coordination.

Requires the Comptroller General to report on the effectiveness of AI Coordination Boards, evaluate Chief AI Officers, and assess AI costs, benefits, and risks, including job impacts.

Directs the Office of Management and Budget Director to issue updated AI governance guidance within five years.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Labeling Act of 2023
document_name: AI Labeling Act
body:
Requires AI-generated content to include clear and conspicuous disclosures on AI-generated content in image, video, audio, multimedia, and text, and mandates developers and licensees to prevent disclosure removal; establishes a working group to create AI-content detection standards, with enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission.

Requires content generated by AI to include clear and conspicuous disclosures marking content as AI-generated. 

Mandates the disclosure to identify content as AI-generated, the tool used to create output, and the creation date and time, ensuring disclosures are permanent or not easily removed.

Compels developers and third-party licensees of generative AI systems to implement procedures preventing content distribution without disclosures, including contractual obligations and certifying compliance.

Treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act, granting enforcement powers to the FTC.

Establishes a working group to develop AI-generated content detection standards and assist platforms in identifying AI-generated content.

Requires the working group to publish a framework with guidelines and submit a report to Congress recommending legislative or administrative actions.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI LEAD Act
document_name: AI LEAD Act
body:
Establishes the CAIO Council to coordinate federal AI practices and risk management. Mandates each agency appoint a CAIO and requires AI Governance Boards in agencies.

Establishes the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers (CAIO) Council to coordinate federal AI practices, interagency activities, and risk management. Mandates each federal agency to appoint a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer responsible for promoting AI innovation, policy development, and risk management.

Requires the creation of Artificial Intelligence Governance Boards within each agency to oversee AI issues and ensure compliance with relevant laws and standards. Obligates agencies to develop AI strategies emphasizing trustworthy adoption, risk mitigation, transparency, and the protection of individual rights. Directs the Comptroller General to report on the effectiveness of the AI Governance Boards and CAIOs within two years of enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024
document_name: AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024
body:
Requires the National Science Foundation to support research on AI-enabled efficient technologies, focusing on smart grids, transportation, and emissions reduction. Emphasizes impact assessments and prioritizes projects at EPSCoR institutions. Mandates reporting findings and recommendations to Congress.

Mandates the National Science Foundation Director to support research on AI enabled efficient technologies.

Requires the National Science Foundation to consider projects that support research on the impact of artificial intelligence on efficient technologies.

Determines that research may focus on smart grids, transportation, agriculture, waste and emissions reduction, and resource conservation, while also assessing adoption feasibility and evaluating public understanding of AI technologies.

Requires to fund project must include an impact assessment evaluating the energy consumption of the AI technologies involved. 

Requires the director must also give special consideration to research conducted at EPSCoR institutions.

Create recommendation no later than 18 months after enactment of this Act that shall work with multiple agencies.

Requires the Director to submit a report within 4 years of enactment to designated Senate and House committees on the results of the research conducted under this section.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Incident Reporting and Security Enhancement Act
document_name: AI Incident Reporting and Security Enhancement Act
body:
Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to update the National Vulnerability Database for AI vulnerabilities and assess voluntary reporting of significant AI security and safety incidents. Requires multi-stakeholder collaboration to evaluate and develop definitions, standards, guidelines, and reporting mechanisms for incident tracking.

Directs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to update the National Vulnerability Database to include AI security vulnerabilities.

Requires NIST to establish common definitions for AI security vulnerabilities and develop standards for managing these vulnerabilities.

Mandates a multi-stakeholder process to assess voluntary reporting and tracking of substantial AI security and safety incidents, and to establish guidelines, best practices, and standardized mechanisms for reporting AI incidents.

Obligates NIST to submit a report to Congress within three years, detailing the findings and recommendations from the multi-stakeholder process on AI incident reporting and tracking.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024
document_name: AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the AI Grand Challenges Program to award competitive prizes for AI research in identified grand challenge areas like health, cybersecurity, and national security.

Establishes the AI Grand Challenges Program to stimulate AI research, development, and commercialization through prize competitions addressing grand challenges in various sectors like national security, health, and environment.

Requires the Director of the National Science Foundation, in coordination with public and private entities, to identify AI grand challenges and develop problem statements.

Mandates the creation of a specific grand challenge for AI-enabled cancer breakthroughs.

Sets eligibility criteria for participants, requiring private entities to be U.S.-based and individuals to be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

Requires submission of a report within 60 days of awarding a prize, detailing the winning submission and its benefits, as well as biennial reports to Congress on program activities and public outreach, to be made publicly accessible.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024
document_name: AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the AI Grand Challenges Program to award competitive prizes for AI research in sectors like health and cybersecurity, requiring public input, setting eligibility criteria, and mandating reports on winning submissions.

Establishes the AI Grand Challenges Program to incentivize AI research, development, and commercialization through prize competitions addressing grand challenges in various sectors like national security, health, and environment.

Mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation to coordinate with federal agencies and stakeholders, and public input, to identify and select AI grand challenges.

Designates a specific grand challenge for AI-enabled cancer breakthroughs.

Sets eligibility criteria for participants, requiring private entities to be U.S.-based and individuals to be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

Requires regular reporting to Congress on the program’s progress and results, ensuring public accessibility of reports and competition information.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Fraud Deterrence Act
document_name: AI Fraud Deterrence Act
body:
Increases penalties for financial crimes like mail fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, and money laundering when committed with the assistance of artificial intelligence, including higher fines (up to $2 million) and longer prison sentences (up to 30 years), and define "artificial intelligence" as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Amends penalties for financial crimes committed with the assistance of artificial intelligence, increasing fines to $1,000,000 and imprisonment terms.

Mandates fines for AI-assisted money laundering to be not more than $1,000,000 or thrice the value of the funds involved, with imprisonment terms up to 20 years.

Defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 definition.

Codifies increased penalties and definitions within the United States Code to deter AI-assisted financial crimes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023
document_name: AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2023
body:
Directs the Federal Trade Commission to issue transparency regulations for AI model training data and algorithms in consultation with relevant stakeholders within 9 months. Specifies the information categories to be publicly disclosed and updated annually.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to establish and routinely update standards for making training data and algorithms of AI foundation models publicly available.

Requires the FTC to promulgate regulations within 9 months and specifies information to be disclosed, including sources of training data and model performance evaluations.

Mandates consultation with relevant stakeholders, including NIST, OSTP, and the Register of Copyrights, in establishing these standards.

Treats violations of these regulations as violations under the FTC Act regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices.

Authorizes $10 million for fiscal year 2025 and $3 million annually thereafter for implementation.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Disclosure Act of 2023
document_name: AI Disclosure Act of 2023
body:
Requires generative AI to include a disclaimer on outputs and subjects violators to penalties and grants privileges.

Requires generative artificial intelligence to include a disclaimer on any output. Mandates the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce this disclosure requirement.

Classifies violations of the disclosure requirement as unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.Empowers the FTC to enforce the disclosure requirement using the same means, jurisdiction, powers, and duties as provided in the Federal Trade Commission Act. Subjects violators to penalties and grants them privileges and immunities in accordance with the Federal Trade Commission Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Development Practices Act of 2024
document_name: AI Development Practices Act of 2024
body:
Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to require developing voluntary AI development guidelines. Focuses on risk management, communication practices, and collaboration. Involves public reporting, security measures, and international standards alignment. Mandates committee briefings 18 months post-enactment.

Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to require the development of voluntary guidelines for AI system development, release, and assessment.

Mandates the Director of NIST to collaborate with public and private organizations to provide guidance for guidelines to help with development. 

Defines methods and guidelines for developing AI risk tolerances for variety of cases in regards to AI such as security risks, economic risks and social risks.

Requires categorization of practices related to security, safety, fairness, privacy, and other attributes of AI systems.

Obligates the Director to implement duties focused on voluntary risk management for a trust worthy AI, ensure that voluntary guidance is developed based on international and business standards, prohibits prescribing specific technologies, and requires collaboration with different entities such as public, industry, and academic entities for guidance development.

Demands a report to Congress within 18 months after enactment on new materials or systems programs, and follow policy recommendations that could improve communication and coordination between private-public sector coordination.

Defines "artificial intelligence red teaming" as structure process that tests systems through adversarial methods to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and undesirable behaviors.

Defines "artificial intelligence system" for clarity on meaning given in section 7223 of the Advancing American AI Act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI CONSENT Act
document_name: AI CONSENT Act
body:
Requires companies to obtain informed consent from consumers before using their data for training AI systems.

Requires companies to obtain informed consent from consumers before using their data to train AI systems.

Requires companies to explain clearly and concisely how consumer data will be used for AI training.

Mandates disclosure of further data usage, including transfers to third-party entities.

Directs the FTC to issue a report on the progress of converting covered data to de-identified data (for Congress' evaluation).

Treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act and subjects violators to penalties.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024
document_name: AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024
body:
Establishes the Center for AI Advancement and Reliability to lead efforts in AI research and development, and the evaluation of AI systems' robustness, resilience, and safety.

Establishes the Center for AI Advancement and Reliability to ensure U.S. leadership in AI research, development, and evaluation.

Outlines activities of the Center including conducting measurement research to develop best practices for AI reliability and safety, evaluating AI capabilities and developing methods for risk management.

Mandates the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology to coordinate with federal agencies in establishing the Center.

Creates a consortium of stakeholders to support the Center and the National Institute of Standards and Technology in AI-related activities.

Authorizes $10 million for fiscal year 2025 for the establishment of the Center.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Ads Act
document_name: AI Ads Act
body:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to include AI-generated content in prohibitions against fraudulent misrepresentation and solicitation. Expands the scope to cover any person misrepresenting candidates, parties, or committees for any purpose, not just candidates themselves.

Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to include fraudulent misrepresentation through content generated with artificial intelligence (AI) under its prohibitions.

Clarifies that fraudulent misrepresentation of campaign authority or solicitation of funds includes the use of AI-generated content.

Extends the prohibition against fraudulent misrepresentation beyond candidates to any person misrepresenting candidates, political parties, or committees for any purpose.

Broadens the scope of prohibited fraudulent solicitation to encompass any candidate, political party, or fictitious political organization, not just those directly involving a candidate or party employee.

Expands the provisions to cover AI-generated content used in misrepresentation or solicitation within political campaigns, ensuring comprehensive regulation of AI's role in electoral fraud.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: AI Act of 2024
document_name: AI Act of 2024
body:
Require financial regulators and the Treasury to study and publicly report on the benefits, risks, and regulatory impacts of AI use in banking, finance and housing markets, and to provide recommendations for responsible AI adoption, informed by public input.

Mandates financial regulators to submit and publicly publish reports within 180 days assessing the benefits and risks of AI in their sectors.

Requires banking regulators to examine AI's role in banking operations, fraud detection, cybersecurity, and fair lending practices, with a focus on smaller and community financial institutions.

Directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to explore AI's use in market research, portfolio management, and fraud detection in securities markets, and assess regulatory gaps and staffing challenges related to AI expertise.

Instructs housing and mortgage regulators to evaluate AI's impact on mortgage efficiency, credit decisions, and real estate practices, with particular focus on the impacts for underserved communities.

Requests the Treasury Department to report on AI's application supporting compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions laws, strengthening cybersecurity defenses, and protecting the financial system from national security threats

Mandates the inclusion of legislative recommendations in each report to promote responsible adoption of AI across these sectors, and requires public consultation to gather input for the drafting of reports.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to waive immunity under section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 for claims and charges related to generative artificial intelligence.
document_name: General AI Communications Act Immunity
body:
Removes Section 230 protection (federal liability protection) for providers of interactive computer services if the conduct giving rise to liability involves generative artificial intelligence.

Amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 (which prevents providers of an interactive computer service from being held legally liable for third-party content) to remove this protection for claims involving the use or provision of generative artificial intelligence.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to specify control and management of Department of Defense data and to establish the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council, and for other purposes.
document_name: S. 3004 (Chief AI Officer Governing Council)
body:
Establishes the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council to oversee AI policy, ethics, and coordination within the Department of Defense. Requires the Council to streamline AI development, ensure ethical practices, and provide periodic reports to Congress.

Establishes the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council to oversee and ensure ethical AI and data policies within the Department of Defense.

Requires the Council to oversee AI ethics, governance, and operational usage, with the aim of improving AI governance coordination and mitigating bias in AI systems. 

Regulates access to and distribution of critical AI assets—including data, models, tools, and testing infrastructure—while also overseeing education and training initiatives that build AI literacy across all levels of the Department workforce.

Mandates the Council to submit reports to the Secretary of Defense and congressional defense committees every 180 days initially and at least every 18 months thereafter.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to carry out a pilot program on using artificial intelligence-enabled software to optimize the workflow and operations of depots, shipyards, and other manufacturing facilities run by the Department of Defense, and for other purposes.
document_name: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to carry out a pilot program on using artificial intelligence-enabled software to optimize the workflow and operations of depots, shipyards, and other manufacturing facilities run by the Department of Defense, and for other purposes.
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to initiate a pilot program using AI-enabled software for optimizing Department of Defense facility operations. Mandates a $35 million minimum expenditure and consultation with military branches. Obligates a detailed evaluation report within one year.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to initiate a pilot program within 60 days to enable a artificial intelligence-software for optimizing workflow and operations in Department of Defense facilities, including depots and shipyards.

Requires assessment of AI-enabled software for contract administration, including adjudication and review of contracts managed by the Defense Contract Management Agency.

Directs the use of best-in-class software platforms, consideration of industry best practices, implementation based on human-centered design, and integration with enterprise platforms and relevant data sources.

Obligates a minimum expenditure of $35,000,000 for the pilot program.

Requires the Secretary to carry out the program in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Mandates a report to Congress within one year on the pilot program’s findings.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to require a study on the use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and artificial intelligence technologies by the Internal Revenue Service.
document_name: A bill to require a study on the use of commercial products and AI technologies by the IRS.
body:
Requires the Comptroller General to study IRS's use of AI and commercial-off-the-shelf products. Identifies efficiency, taxpayer service, cost savings, fairness, enforcement, and risk management as key factors. Details contractors, costs, contracting approaches, and expense allocations for IT projects.

Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a study and report to Congress on the IRS's use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and AI technologies within 12 months of the Act's enactment.

Identifies the IRS's use of such technologies to enhance operational efficiency, improve taxpayer services, generate cost savings, ensure fair enforcement, and improve tax collection efforts.

Requires the study to assess how the IRS manages AI-related risks, including errors, bias in audit selection, and data security.

Includes information on IT modernization projects, detailing contractors, project scope, costs, and contracting approaches.

Analyzes the allocation of expenses between contractors and IRS employees and compares costs between customized projects and commercial product alternatives.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to promote United States leadership in technical standards by directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Department of State to take certain actions to encourage and enable United States participation in developing standards and specifications for artificial intelligence and other critical and emerging technologies, and for other purposes.
document_name: S. 3849 (US Leadership in AI Standards)
body:
Requires NIST Director to brief Congress on federal AI standards participation within one year. Directs federal agencies to notify NIST of AI standards activities. Mandates NIST to create a reporting mechanism and establish a web portal. Establishes a pilot program for U.S.-based standards meetings. Obligates annual NIST briefings to Congress on the pilot program. Authorizes $10 million for the pilot program from 2024 to 2028.

Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to brief Congress within one year on federal participation opportunities in AI and emerging technology standards development.

Directs federal agencies to notify NIST of their involvement in AI standards activities and mandates NIST to create a reporting mechanism for this purpose.

Mandates NIST to establish a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international standards efforts and participation opportunities.

Establishes a pilot program for supporting U.S.-based standards meetings, including prestandardization and coordination meetings, through grants to eligible entities.

Obligates NIST to brief Congress annually on the pilot program’s effectiveness and provide recommendations for permanent implementation if deemed feasible.

Authorizes $10 million for the pilot program from fiscal years 2024 through 2028.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to prohibit and require notifications with respect to certain investments by United States persons in the People's Republic of China, and for other purposes.
document_name: A bill to prohibit certain US investments in China
body:
Prohibits U.S. persons from investing in certain prohibited technologies in China. Requires transactions in notifiable technologies to be reported. Allows for exemptions with Congressional notification. Imposes penalties for violations. Formulates a strategy for multilateral engagement to prevent proliferation.

Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in certain transactions with entities associated with China that involve "prohibited technologies," focusing on national security concerns.

Requires authorities to issue non-binding feedback on covered transactions and imposes civil penalties for violations.

Mandates U.S. persons provide written notification within 30 days post-transaction involving "notifiable technologies."

Establishes a process for identifying transactions lacking notifications and mandates confidentiality of submitted transaction information.

Obliges the Secretary of the Treasury to annually report to Congress on enforcement actions, updates to prohibited technologies, and assessment of national security threats.

Encourages multilateral engagement with U.S. allies to curb prohibited technology development/acquisition by countries of concern, including China.

Potentially establishes a public database for identifying covered foreign persons involved in prohibited technologies.

Exempts certain transactions deemed de minimis or in the national interest, and enables updates to prohibited or notifiable technologies to address national security needs.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A bill to establish protections for individual rights with respect to computational algorithms, and for other purposes.
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2024
body:
Prohibits discriminatory use of AI algorithms and mandates pre- and post-deployment evaluations. Requires transparency in algorithm use. Enforces compliance through Federal Trade Commission oversight, state actions, and private lawsuits. Establishes resources for algorithm auditing and consumer awareness initiatives.

Prohibits developers and deployers of AI algorithms from causing or contributing to discrimination based on protected characteristics.

Mandates developers and deployers to conduct pre-deployment evaluations and annual impact assessments of AI algorithms to identify potential harms or disparate impacts.

Requires independent audits of AI algorithms and obligates developers to provide relevant information to deployers for compliance.

Imposes transparency obligations, including public disclosures of AI practices and consumer rights, in multiple languages and accessible formats.

Grants the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) enforcement authority, including rulemaking, with violations treated as unfair or deceptive acts.

Provides a private right of action for individuals, enabling lawsuits for violations and barring pre-dispute arbitration agreements.

Establishes federal resources for algorithm auditing, including a new occupational series and additional personnel for the FTC to handle AI-related issues.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A Stronger Workforce for America Act, Chapter 3 (Performance Accountability)
document_name: A Stronger Workforce for America Act, Chapter 3 (Performance Accountability)
body: Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to allow states to use machine learning and advanced analytics in the improvement of state program operations and outcomes.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: A Bill to prohibit certain uses of automated decision systems by employers, and for other purposes.
document_name: No Robot Bosses Act
body:
Restricts the use of automated decision systems for employment-related decisions, including by requiring such systems to be tested for efficacy, non-discrimination, and relevant laws & standards.

Prohibits employers from making any employment-related decisions -- including to fire or discipline an employee -- based solely on the output of an automated decision system.

Requires any automated decision system used to inform employment-related decisions to be tested before deployment for efficacy and compliance with relevant employment laws & the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework from the National Institute of Standards & Technology. Systems must also be tested both before deployment and annually after deployment for non-discrimination on the basis of protected classes.

Requires employers to disclose to employees the use of automated decision systems for employment-related decisions and information on the workings of the system and the data used to reach its decision.

Establishes new roles and bodies in the Department of Labor to monitor and enforce this policy and to guide the development of future regulations on the use of automated decision systems in employment-related decision-making.

Establishes protections for whistleblowers who call attention to violations of this policy.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: 21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act")
document_name: 21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications")
body:
Prohibits entities from distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary-controlled applications in the U.S. Requires user data portability before prohibition. Allows civil penalties for violations. Permits exemptions for qualified divestitures and necessary services. Grants judicial review in D.C. Circuit.

Prohibits entities from distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary controlled applications within the U.S.

Requires data portability for users before prohibitions apply, enabling users to access their data in a machine-readable format.

Exempts applications undergoing "qualified divestiture" from prohibitions.

Enforces penalties up to $5,000 per user for distribution violations and $500 per user for data portability violations.

Mandates the Attorney General to investigate and enforce compliance through civil penalties or court actions.

Defines "foreign adversary controlled applications" and "qualified divestiture" to ensure clarity in application and exemptions.

Grants judicial review exclusively to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, with specified time limits for challenges.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Attorney General’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing California Laws to Artificial Intelligence
document_name: California AG’s Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing Laws to AI
body:
Guides AI developers and users in California on compliance with existing laws governing consumer protections, data protections, civil rights protections, competition laws, and new AI-specific laws.

Guides AI developers, sellers, and users in California on legal obligations under state consumer protection, civil rights, competition, and data privacy laws.

Requires that AI systems comply with laws against unfair practices, deceptive advertising, false advertising, and anticompetitive trusts.

Explains that under California law, it is unlawful to use AI for impersonation, false representation, and the creation of deceptive political content.

Addresses risks of bias and discrimination in AI systems by explaining state civil rights laws and protections. 

Explains how the California Consumer Privacy Act and other state privacy laws apply to the use of AI systems and protect Californians' data.

Details new AI legislation, effective January 2025, mandating disclosures and detection tools for AI-generated content, and explaining unauthorized AI uses in entertainment and election contexts.

Explains new laws expanding prohibitions on exploitative AI uses, including specific laws addressing child pornography and material produced by deepfake technologies.

Describes a new law requiring health insurers to ensure licensed physicians monitor AI decision-making tools.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: eSam
body:
41 government agencies are organized through eSam, a public collaboration mechanism for digitalization of the public sector, which has been implementing seven AI-related initiatives in 2023/2024, including i) use of AI in the creation of public documents, ii) Risks and prerequisites for exchanging models for AI development, iii) a common platform for chatbots, iv) practical application of AI solutions (interpretation), v) generative AI-based services, vi) AI for communication ops.

In Sweden, 41 government agencies work together through eSam, a cooperation forum for digitalisation of the public sector. The network coordinates projects to share knowledge, avoid duplication, and accelerate the responsible adoption of new technologies.

category: National – Strategy
title: White paper on the National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap
document_name: Peta Jalan Kecerdasan Artifisial Nasional
body:
Indonesia’s National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap (Peta Jalan Kecerdasan Artifisial Nasional), led by the Ministry of Communication and Digital, sets implementation priorities for 2025–2029. It operationalises and aligns with the National AI Strategy (STRANAS KA) 2020–2045 to support Indonesia Emas 2045 by focusing on ethics and governance, talent development, infrastructure and data, research and innovation, investment, priority use cases, and monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.

The roadmap addresses opportunities arising from the accelerating adoption of artificial intelligence alongside challenges identified at national level, including gaps in ethical readiness, infrastructure capacity, data availability, investment, research funding, and the supply and distribution of AI talent. It highlights risks such as algorithmic bias, privacy violations, data security issues, and the misuse of AI, while recognising Indonesia’s growing digital economy, high internet penetration, and increasing use of AI across government, industry, and society as key assets to build upon.
Its policy focus is organised across several interrelated axes, covering ethics and governance, policy and regulatory coherence, human capital development, infrastructure and data, research and industrial innovation, investment and financing, and the deployment of priority AI use cases. The roadmap identifies targeted application areas intended to deliver visible impact, including food security and agriculture, health services, education, economic and financial activities, and public administration. These priorities are linked to expected outcomes such as improved public services, higher productivity, expanded AI literacy, and broader adoption of responsible AI solutions.
Implementation relies on multi‑stakeholder involvement, with coordination among government institutions, academia, industry, associations, civil society, and other actors. Governance arrangements emphasise ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, accountability, data protection, security, inclusiveness, and human oversight across the AI lifecycle. The roadmap also provides for monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of strategic initiatives, using indicators and periodic review mechanisms coordinated at national level to ensure continued alignment with development priorities.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
title: Web Portal “Centre for Responsible Artificial Intelligence”
document_name: Вебпортал «Центр відповідального штучного інтелекту»
body:
The Centre for Responsible AI is a one-stop-shop web portal created by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine. It provides access to AI regulatory tools, guidelines, and educational materials, keeping stakeholders informed about Ukraine’s progress towards AI regulation. The portal also offers awareness resources for citizens on safe and responsible AI use.

The Centre for Responsible AI is a national initiative developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine to provide a central access point for regulatory, educational, and practical tools supporting the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). 
Methodology:
The portal is designed on a one-stop-shop principle, ensuring maximum integration of available instruments such as human rights impact assessments, AI labelling procedures, participation in a regulatory sandbox, joining codes of conduct, and training courses on safe AI interaction.
Objectives:
Beyond regulatory tools, the portal will serve as an information and awareness hub. It will provide citizens, businesses, and policymakers with guidance documents, white papers, and roadmaps, along with news and updates on AI governance and regulation in Ukraine. An important element is the educational component for society at large, aimed at improving digital and AI literacy while raising awareness of risks and safeguards against malicious use of AI.
Impact:
The initiative seeks to increase transparency, trust, and accountability in AI development and application. It provides stakeholders with a unified space to access recommendations, consult best practices, and take part in experimentation initiatives."

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity
body:
A ministerial voucher programme to subsidise the purchase/subscription of cloud and cybersecurity services by SMEs and self-employed persons (eligible products explicitly include cloud SaaS with integrated AI features such as productivity/ERP/CRM tools). The measure reduces infrastructure and security barriers for SMEs adopting AI-enabled software.

The Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity programme is a demand-side subsidy instrument operated by the Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy (MIMIT). It provides vouchers to eligible SMEs and self-employed persons (lavoratori autonomi) to offset the cost of purchasing or subscribing to cloud computing and cybersecurity services from a register of prequalified suppliers. Eligible products explicitly include cloud SaaS solutions with integrated AI features meaning the programme directly lowers the financial barrier to SME adoption of AI-enabled software without requiring beneficiaries to procure AI separately. Supplier preregistration opened on 27 February 2026, establishing the pool of eligible vendors from which SMEs may choose; the SME application window ran from March to April 2026. The programme complements Italy's broader SME digitalisation strategy, including the national Competence Centers network and the Transition 5.0 incentive scheme.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitisation of Romania
title: Virtual civil servants
body:
Two local communities have introduced 'virtual civil servants'. The creation of this 'civil servant,' based on artificial intelligence, is part of the digitisation process of procedures in the local public administration in Cluj. Galați City Hall also launched a virtual civil servant based on artificial intelligence. The virtual assistant is currently being trained and tested but will soon be able to provide information to citizens on town planning, taxes, fees, and other local revenues.

In Romania, several municipalities are experimenting with AI-based “virtual civil servants” as part of efforts to modernise local public administration. The initiative began in Cluj, where the system was introduced to support the digitisation of procedures and citizen services. Soon after, Galați City Hall launched its own version of the tool.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Virtual assistant in mObywatel
body:
The virtual assistant in mObywatel is an AI chatbot, powered by a Polish LLM (PLLuM), available through a national digital citizen app. It was created in order to make information about public services more available to citizens. It is meant to combat digital exclusion and provide a safe and verified alternative to general purpose chatbots in the official context.

The Virtual Assistant is an attempt to help the citizen navigate the multitude of available public services ranging from reporting an environmental violations, to registering the birth of a child. Every year many services are introduced, changed, or retired, making it difficult for the citizen to keep track of them. The ability to ask questions in natural language makes the services more approachable, and by extension helps every citizen access everything the modern state has to offer. As a secondary objective, the initiative strives to build trusted public AI – both in the terms of the information provided by the Virtual Assistant, and by legally and technically enshrining the safety of the citizen data. 

The virtual assistant differs from the commercial offerings by the strict validation and verification of the knowledge sources and close integration with government databases. The answers it provides are limited to the official documentation – it is also designed not to give opinions or judgement-based advice. This ensures the assistant can be trusted to help citizens, while at the same time saving the budgetary cost of citizens asking general-knowledge questions. Furthermore, the assistant is embedded in mObywatel - the official Polish state application that lets people keep digital versions of important documents and use many public services safely on their mobiles. Therefore, if the user asks about a service or a document available in the app, the assistant can link directly to that service, ensuring seamless user experience. 

Finally, the Virtual Assistant is designed from the ground up to be privacy-preserving. It does not link the conversations to a user preventing any profiling. Every message goes through a multi-step process designed to purge any personally identifiable information. The LLM infrastructure is fully self-managed, to prevent external API providers from accessing the conversation data. 

The Virtual Assistant has been used 600 000 times in the two months from its introduction. The performance of the assistant is measured in real time, based on the user feedback (surveys after a conversation and the ability to up and downvote specific answers). Specific answers receive 62% positive votes and 38% negative, while the whole conversations have an equal split of 44% good or very good and 44% of bad or very bad. The specific rated conversations and messages are then assessed both manually and automatically by analytical and data science teams to guide the development of the system. Moreover, the project is assessed using social science frameworks, i.e: moderated workshops and unmoderated online forms.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Ulysses chat
body:
Ulysses chat is an AI assistant developed for the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies. It considers official data and documents as well as the Chamber’s rules before answering questions.

The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies provides a wide range of internal services that support roughly 10,000 people, including 513 deputies, parliamentary staff, public servants and outsourced workers. Its operations span broadcasting (radio and TV), news services, medical care, engineering, architecture, finance, procurement, IT, legal services, training, a legislative university, dozens of legislative committees and extensive research and library functions. This diversity generates a constant demand for rapid access to accurate institutional information.

The Chamber’s traditional intranet model could no longer meet the speed and analytical depth required by employees in their daily work. As generative AI became widely used, staff increasingly turned to external platforms; however, using these tools without institutional context would require uploading large volumes of internal documents, creating risks around data privacy, rule misapplication and high duplication‑related costs. To address this, the Chamber developed Ulysses Chat—a generative AI‑based virtual assistant designed specifically for internal use and grounded in the institution’s own knowledge base. 
Ulysses Chat draws on a network of interconnected AI agents and operates within a governance layer designed to ensure privacy, security and responsible AI behaviour. It incorporates mechanisms for auditing, token accountability, minimising bias and hallucinations, and managing out‑of‑context queries. In its first implementation stage, the system answers questions using official institutional data, including internal standards, legislation, manuals, administrative rules, planning and budget information, logistics and human‑resources procedures, and legislative data such as bills, speeches and voting records. It also uses the Chamber’s organizational chart to contextualize information. In the current second phase, Ulysses Chat is beginning to automate selected internal processes through direct interaction with institutional systems. Across all information domains, data managers, data stewards and the Data Protection Officer oversee ongoing data‑quality monitoring.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Ulysses - Consolidated summaries of legislative bills
document_name: Ulysses - Consolidação de sumaríos de proposições legislativas
body:
Legislative consultants assist parliamentarians by producing consolidated executive summaries of bills, including justifications, amendments, attached bills, and approved substitutes. This process can take hours or days depending on the volume of related documents. The solution employs generative AI tools to help consultants create these summaries, which are then reviewed and supplemented as needed.

Legislative consultants, staff in charge of support the laymaking drafting, assist parliamentarians in reporting on legislative bills by producing consolidated executive summaries for each bill, including its justification and other related documents: amendments, attached bills, and approved substitutes. 

The production of these summaries can take hours or days, depending on the number of amendments and bills attached to the main bill being reported. This challenge is amplified along with the bills' lifecycle, once the set of documents increases eveyday and the updated version can assume a different meaning along with the time. In some cases, the bill intends to change other bills, resulting in a complex chain of documents.

The AI system uses generative AI tools to assist consultants in producing these summaries, which must be reviewed and supplemented by the consultants themselves according to thematic or contextual needs. These are the main objectives for this AI application: (i) decrease the time required to produce consolidated executive summaries from hours or days to minutes, enabling legislative consultants to work more efficiently; (ii) automatically identify and synthesize key information from all related documents to prevent oversight of critical content; and (iii) provide standardized, well-structured summaries that serve as a robust foundation for consultants to review and refine, ensuring uniformity across legislative reports. This initiative necessitates ongoing investment in ensuring the quality of both metadata and complete textual content of the legislative proposals under analysis and their respective cited legislation.

Results, outcomes and impacts:
A first positive impact achieved was the standardization of AI-generated summaries based on consensus obtained among the consultants who participated in the solution validation. For example, there are rules for initiating summary text, for limiting the number of words generated, for incorporating cited legislation into the summarization context, etc. We have begun collecting feedback-based measurements for ongoing investigation and continuous improvement of the deployed solution

Challenges and lessons learned:
Along the implementation of the AI system, it was necessary to perform extraction of textual and tabular content from documents produced in various different formats (e.g., .doc, .docx, .pdf, .tiff, among others). Some bills and regulations may contain both text and tables simultaneously. Moreover, varying context window constraints and behavioral differences were observed across different generative AI models, which required specific testing and targeted interventions to handle each encountered issue.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis
document_name: Ulysses - Análise de Roteamento Procedimental de Propostas Legislativas
body:
Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis is an AI system incoming legislative bills to identify procedural requirements and committee assignments, then produces a dispatch draft suggesting the bill's processing regime, committee routing order, and consideration procedures. It supports the Clerk’s staff before sending the bill to be discussed in the legislative committees. The Clerk staff are required to make many deep analyses of each incoming bill, which requires a lot of time.

The process of distributing legislative bills to the thematic committees – Initial Dispatch – requires manual and technical analysis by the Clerk staff. This activity, although critical for the proper progress of legislative processing, is susceptible to inconsistencies, delays, and work overload. Additionally, the growing volume of bills makes the process increasingly challenging in terms of time and accuracy. 
That process is composed of five modules and implemented by AI agents that evaluate the legislative document from different perspectives:
Assessment of the bill's procedural and constitutional requirementsSearch for similar legislative documents already being processed in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies, so that, instead of having independent processing, they can be attached to a similar billDefinition of the form of analysis of the legislative matter, that is, whether by characteristic or rule it will first be evaluated by thematic committees before being voted on in plenary, or whether it is possible for the legislative proposal to become law as long as it has a conclusive opinion in the thematic committees through which it must pass. Below are the alternatives for form of bill analysis procedure:
Bill subject to conclusive discussion by committeesBill subject to plenary discussion,Bill subject to internal discussions in committees.Definition of the processing regime: under Brazilian legislation, legislative matters can be processed under the following regimes: Ordinary, Priority, Urgency, Special.Distribution to thematic committees for evaluation of merit, financial adequacy, and constitutionality. In the Chamber of Deputies of Brazil there are 30 permanent committees. All these analyses approaches are supported by AI agents to choose the best option, complying with the procedural and constitutional rights and rules involved.

category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
title: UK Sovereign AI Unit
body:
The UK Sovereign AI Unit is a government body established within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) to build and harness the UK's domestic AI capabilities.

The Sovereign AI Unit was established in DSIT in 2025 as a core pillar of the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan. Chaired by venture capitalist James Wise (Balderton Capital), the Unit operates as a novel government fund structure designed to be the first choice for founders building essential parts of the UK's AI infrastructure. The Unit's mandate covers the full AI value chain: investing in compute infrastructure, supporting data assets, backing frontier model development, and enabling AI application companies. Key activities include launching open calls to researchers and companies through the AI Research Resource (AIRR), supporting 'Autonomous Labs' combining robotics and AI, and forging Memoranda of Understanding with leading AI firms such as Anthropic and OpenAI to advance responsible AI development aligned with UK values. The Unit works alongside the British Business Bank and UKRI, and collaborates with the UK Compute Roadmap to build a world-class compute ecosystem. It complements AI Growth Zones and the National Data Library as part of a broader national AI infrastructure strategy.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: UK National Data Library (NDL)
body:
The UK National Data Library (NDL) is a government initiative to create a central infrastructure for the responsible management and sharing of public sector data, enabling businesses, researchers and public servants to access high-value datasets to deliver better public services, drive economic growth and support AI innovation.

The National Data Library was announced as part of the UK Government's AI Opportunities Action Plan in January 2025, based on recommendations from entrepreneur and AI advisor Matt Clifford. Its creation is overseen by DSIT, with close involvement from the Government Digital Service (GDS). The NDL completed an extensive discovery phase in 2025, including public attitudes research, consultation with over 200 organisations and expert bodies (including the Open Data Institute, Wellcome Trust, Public Digital, The Tony Blair Institute and The Startup Coalition), and five 'kickstarter' projects designed to test approaches to systemic data reform. An architecture design contract of £650,000 was awarded to esynergy in November 2025 to produce a federated architecture blueprint for the NDL. The NDL's design principles prioritise: (1) public benefit and ethical data use; (2) data security and privacy safeguards; (3) a federated model that does not centralise data but provides shared infrastructure for access; (4) AI-readiness, with guidelines for making government datasets AI-ready published by GDS; and (5) public trust through ongoing citizen engagement. Economic analyses suggest a fully developed AI-ready data ecosystem underpinned by the NDL could generate £40 billion annually in productivity gains by 2030.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: UK Health Data Research Service (HDRS)
body:
The Health Data Research Service (HDRS) is a new UK-wide, government-owned company to transform how researchers and innovators access health and care data across the UK.

The HDRS was announced following the Sudlow Review ('Uniting the UK's Health Data: A Huge Opportunity for Society'), which identified the fragmented, slow and complex landscape for health data access as a critical barrier to research and innovation. At its core, the HDRS is built on a national network of Secure Data Environments (SDEs), expanding the existing NHS Research SDE Network. The HDRS will provide a 'single front door' through which researchers make standardised access requests, enabling them to access linked primary care, hospital, prescribing, mortality, genomic and diagnostic imaging data at national scale, while keeping data in secure environments and maintaining privacy through encryption, anonymisation and synthetic data techniques. The service has six stated goals: (1) providing secure access to linked national-scale health data; (2) leveraging major UK cohort studies and biobanks; (3) enabling access to diagnostic images, genomics and laboratory data for precision medicine; (4) supporting innovative data linkage; (5) streamlining governance; and (6) building public trust.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: UK AI for Science Strategy
body:
A national strategy designed to accelerate the application of artificial intelligence across scientific research and discovery in the United Kingdom.

The AI for Science Strategy was published by the UK government to accelerate the integration of artificial intelligence into scientific discovery and innovation. The strategy seeks to position the United Kingdom as a global leader in AI-enabled research by investing in infrastructure, data resources and interdisciplinary collaborations. It focuses on enabling scientists to use advanced AI systems to analyse complex datasets, simulate natural phenomena and accelerate breakthroughs in fields such as life sciences, materials science, climate research and energy. The strategy promotes the creation of mission-driven research programmes where AI techniques are applied to large-scale scientific challenges, while also strengthening the computing infrastructure required to train and run advanced models. It encourages collaboration between universities, national laboratories, startups and established industry actors. In addition, the strategy emphasises responsible innovation, skills development and access to shared data resources.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: UK AI Skills Hub
body:
A free national AI training programme targeting 10 million UK workers, with a specific goal of upskilling 2 million SME employees, delivered in partnership with 23 major technology companies.

The UK AI Skills Hub is a flagship component of the government's TechFirst initiative, launched in June 2025 and significantly expanded on 28 January 2026 (coinciding with the anniversary of the AI Opportunities Action Plan). The programme offers free AI training to all UK adults, delivered online through a government-backed platform developed in partnership with 23 major technology companies. Its stated ambition is to upskill 10 million workers by 2030, with 2 million of those targeted from the SME workforce. Courses range from foundational AI literacy modules (some under 20 minutes) suitable for non-technical staff, to professional-level qualifications for those in AI-adjacent roles. Completions are recognised through a government-backed AI Foundations digital badge, providing portable evidence of skills for employees and assurance for employers. The January 2026 expansion also introduced a £27 million TechLocal scheme to connect people with tech jobs in their local area, and a £7.8 million TechLocal AI Professional Degree and Traineeship Accelerator, which funds universities and colleges to develop new AI-focused higher education courses created with industry input.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Transform Paraná Program – Integrated Ecosystem of AI, Automation, and Data Governance (Subnational: Paraná)
document_name: Programa TRANSFORMA PARANÁ – Ecossistema Integrado de IA, Automação e Governança de Dados.
body:
The Transform Paraná Program uses AI to modernize state management and deliver faster, more efficient digital services. It creates a unified data foundation to overcome fragmentation and automate slow manual processes across government agencies. Citizens, rural producers, and safety officials benefit from diverse projects like smart food donation, environmental monitoring, and traffic safety analysis.

The Transforma Paraná Program establishes a statewide infrastructure for territorial and environmental intelligence designed to modernize public governance in Paraná. It responds to long‑standing structural challenges in public administration, including fragmented data across multiple systems, limited automation and heavy reliance on manual, time‑consuming processes. By combining artificial intelligence with cloud‑native architecture, the program aims to eliminate data silos and support faster, evidence‑based decision‑making across government.

At the heart of the initiative is the creation of a unified Data Foundation, implemented through a Macro State Data Lake that consolidates large volumes of information under a single governance framework. This foundation standardizes metadata, ensures interoperability and embeds compliance with Brazil’s General Data Protection Law (LGPD). It enables a range of high‑impact projects, including the Paraná Mais Sustentável platform for rural digital addressing and environmental monitoring; SISTRANSITO, which uses AI to analyze more than 82,000 traffic accident reports to improve road safety; and the J.A.C.A. project, which digitizes food donations at CEASA‑PR using conversational agents to reduce hunger and food waste.

The program is institutionalized through a strategic partnership between the Secretariat of Innovation and Artificial Intelligence (SEIA) and CELEPAR, ensuring that the technology is embedded in official state services and remains sustainable over time. Implementation follows a phased approach, starting with core infrastructure and pilot modules before scaling to full production. Continuous improvement is supported through automated pipelines and the introduction of an Agent Development Kit, enabling the deployment of intelligent, proactive digital services in areas such as health, education and public security. Concrete results are already visible. The Data Foundation has centralized petabytes of information, automated the analysis of 82,000 traffic accident reports and enabled the creation of unique digital addresses for 300,000 rural properties. Impact is measured through reductions in manual processing time, high levels of data structuring (exceeding 90% completeness) and the successful deployment of AI‑based conversational services for social programs.

Beyond these core initiatives, Transforma Paraná supports a broader innovation ecosystem. Complementary actions include the Conecta IA program to identify operational bottlenecks, Hub GovTech Paraná to promote open innovation, the Paraná Artificial Intelligence Cup for civil servants and AI solutions applied to public security and housing programs such as COHAPAR. Together, these efforts reduce bureaucracy, increase efficiency and modernize service delivery across multiple policy domains.
