title: Artificial Intelligence Boost Loan
document_name: Prêt Boost Intelligence Artificielle
body:
A fast, collateral-free online loan of between EUR 5,000 and EUR 75,000 for French very small firms (VSEs) and SMEs with fewer than 50 employees, enabling them to finance AI tool integration and project implementation.

The Prêt Boost Intelligence Artificielle is part of Bpifrance Flash's suite of online SME loans (alongside Prêt Boost Transformation Numérique, Prêt Boost Industrie, etc.). It is delivered entirely online through Bpifrance's digital platform with a response within 48 hours and disbursement within 7 days. The loan requires no personal or corporate guarantee (sans garantie ni caution personnelle) and operates on a co-financing basis: the applicant must have an existing bank loan with a remaining repayment period of more than 3 years. Loan duration is 3 to 5 years, with a repayment deferral period of up to 12 or 24 months to allow the business to realise AI benefits before repayments begin. Eligible expenses include AI software acquisition, implementation costs, consulting fees, and AI project costs. To be eligible, a company must: be a VSEs or SME under the EU definition with fewer than 49 employees; be incorporated and operating in France (metropolitan and DROM (overseas)); be at least 3 years old; and be financially sound.

document_name: Proyecto de Ley de Inteligencia Artificial en Colombia
body:
Introduced in July 2025, this Bill seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for the ethical, competitive, and innovative development and use of AI. It applies to all actors in the AI lifecycle. Central to the bill is a risk-based classification system that categorizes AI systems into four levels.

The goal of this bill is to protect fundamental rights, ensure human oversight, and promote social and environmental well-being. It responds to risks like identity fraud, deepfakes, and discriminatory algorithms, while fostering innovation, education, and inclusion. It seeks to balance technological progress with ethical safeguards, aligning Colombia with global standards.

title: America's AI Action Plan
document_name: America's AI Action Plan
body:
The Action Plan sets forth policy goals for near-term execution by the Federal government and articulates policy recommendations in line with the President’s vision for US leadership in AI. It is articulated around three main pillars: innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security.

The Plan identifies over 90 Federal policy actions across three pillars – Accelerating Innovation, Building American AI Infrastructure, and Leading in International Diplomacy and Security – to be implemented by the Trump Administration. Key policies in the AI Action Plan include:
Exporting American AI: The Commerce and State Departments will partner with industry to deliver secure, full-stack AI export packages – including hardware, models, software, applications, and standards – to America’s friends and allies around the world.
 Promoting Rapid Buildout of Data Centers: Expediting and modernizing permits for data centers and semiconductor fabs, as well as creating new national initiatives to increase high-demand occupations like electricians and HVAC technicians.
 Enabling Innovation and Adoption: Removing onerous Federal regulations that hinder AI development and deployment, and seek private sector input on rules to remove.
 Upholding Free Speech in Frontier Models: Updating Federal procurement guidelines to ensure that the government only contracts with frontier large language model developers who ensure that their systems are objective and free from top-down ideological bias.

title: Agent MIA (Argentine State's Artificial Intelligence Assistant)
document_name: MIA (Asistente de Inteligencia Artificial del Estado Argentino)
body:
MIA is integrated into the national government's chatbot (TINA). It was conceived as a support agent for citizen services management based on information security, administrative transparency, and human oversight principles. It offers personalized responses according to each user's needs and context. It is based on LLAMA 4 (Meta) for speed, low operating cost, and open-source nature. Currently in its initial phase with two use cases: SMEs and Mi Argentina (citizens' platform).

The initiative seeks to address inefficiencies in public services by modernizing them to achieve a more transparent, efficient, and citizen-centered government. Specifically, it addresses the following points:
 It aims to reduce waiting times and simplify digital processes for citizens. It solves the problem of misinformation by drawing on a closed knowledge base that uses only official data, thus ensuring accuracy and avoiding bias.Unlike traditional chatbots that only respond, MIA can act: query data, generate reports, and perform administrative tasks under human supervision.MIA's main objectives focus on improving the interaction between the government and society: 
Supporting SMEs and assisting the 26 million users of the Mi Argentina app with their digital transactions.Offer a more agile, efficient, simple, and secure conversational experience.Save time for both users and government support teams.MIA is expected to evolve from a consultation assistant to a comprehensive government management tool: • We are working to expand the initiative and achieve integration into critical environments such as the Electronic Document Management System (GDE), Online Procedures (TAD), and the official portal Argentina.gob.ar. MIA has been designed to scale to a wide range of topics and services. In the next 12 to 18 months, the goal is for these AI agents to significantly simplify people's lives and make public administration more efficient at all levels. 

Currently, it already registers more than 1.5 million conversations per month. Impacts are measured using internal performance metrics for continuous improvement and the exploratory application of UNESCO's RAM Methodology. In the future, MIA will evolve from conversational to agentic, executing administrative tasks and generating reports in systems such as GDE and TAD. Over the next 12-18 months, it is expected to be the cornerstone for positioning Argentina as a regional AI hub, enabling a government that not only responds but also acts to simplify citizens' lives and optimize public administration.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (NIST AI 100-2e2025)
body:
Published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in March 2025, NIST AI 100-2e2025 provides a taxonomy of concepts and terminology in the field of adversarial machine learning (AML). It covers key types of ML methods, life cycle stages of attack, and attacker goals, capabilities, and knowledge, alongside mitigation methods, aiming to establish a common language to inform standards and practice guides for assessing and managing the security of AI systems.

The report distinguishes between two broad classes of AI systems: predictive AI (PredAI), which still dominates industrial applications, and generative AI (GenAI), whose adoption in business and consumer contexts has increased rapidly. Real-world failures documented in the report include autonomous vehicles caused to swerve into oncoming lanes and stop signs misclassified as speed limit signs, illustrating the tangible stakes of AML vulnerabilities.
The taxonomy classifies attacks across five dimensions: the type of AI system targeted; the stage of the machine learning life cycle at which the attack occurs (from design and training through to deployment); the attacker's goals in terms of which system properties they seek to violate (availability, integrity, or privacy); the attacker's capabilities and access; and the attacker's knowledge of the learning process. For predictive AI, the taxonomy covers evasion, poisoning, and privacy attacks. For generative AI, it extends to supply chain attacks, direct and indirect prompt injection, misuse violations, and security of AI agents. Each category of attack is paired with corresponding mitigation strategies, along with an assessment of the limitations of those techniques.
The report is the product of an extensive literature review, expert consultation in the field of adversarial machine learning, and original research by its authors, drawn from NIST's Computer Security Division, Northeastern University, the U.S. AI Safety Institute, Cisco, and the U.K. AI Security Institute. It adopts the security, resilience, and robustness concepts from the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and aligns with the NCSC Machine Learning Principles. While the guidance is voluntary and not intended to supersede existing regulations or law, it is explicitly designed to inform future standards and practice guides. Its primary audience includes those responsible for designing, developing, deploying, evaluating, and governing AI systems.

document_name: План заходів з реалізації Концепції розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні на 2025–2026 роки
body:
Action Plan for the Implementation of the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine for 2025–2026 is an action plan of the Government of Ukraine that aims to implement Ukraine’s Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence by 2030. It includes actions related to the use of AI in higher education, cybersecurity, public administration, regulation, and national defence.

The initiative is aimed at implementing the national Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine by 2030. It addresses the issue of insufficient coordination of policies and the absence of a comprehensive approach to AI implementation in key sectors such as education, cybersecurity, public administration, and defence. The use of AI in these areas creates opportunities to improve the efficiency, security, and quality of public services.
Objectives:
Supporting research and development in AI, drafting national AI legislation, promoting the application of AI technologies in higher education, combating cyber threats, and using AI for analysis, forecasting, and modelling of public administration systems. Ensuring the safe use of AI in the defence sector, which is an essential aspect of national security.Impact:
The initiative is implemented through a set of measures including the development of regulatory legal acts, methodological recommendations, adoption of international standards, and the creation of educational programmes. Further institutionalised implementation is envisaged through coordination between government bodies and expanded international cooperation. This will facilitate scaling results and deeper integration of AI into various sectors.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: Act on Promotion of Research, Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-Related Technologies
body:
Japan’s 2025 AI Act establishes the country’s first dedicated legal framework for artificial intelligence, focusing on promoting research, development, and utilisation rather than imposing strict regulation. The law sets out basic principles and a national policy framework, including a “Basic AI Plan” and coordinated governance structures, while encouraging voluntary action by businesses.

Japan’s Act on the Promotion of Research and Development and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-Related Technologies (AI Act), enacted on 28 May 2025, is the country’s first law specifically addressing artificial intelligence. It establishes a national framework to promote AI research, development, and use, and sets out general principles and governance arrangements. 
The Act functions as a “fundamental law,” defining broad policy directions rather than detailed regulatory requirements. It provides for the development of a “Basic AI Plan” to guide and coordinate government action, alongside institutional structures for centralised policy oversight. It outlines roles for public authorities and private actors involved in AI, including expectations that businesses align with government policies and principles. It also enables future legislative, financial, and administrative measures to support AI.
The Act does not establish detailed compliance obligations or penalties, focusing instead on principles, coordination, and policy frameworks.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilisation of AI-related Technology
document_name: 人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用に関する法律
body:
The AI Act and the AI Basic Plan (established in Article 18, para. (1) of the Act) constitute a government-led policy framework designed to promote AI innovation while mitigating risks. It is intended for citizens, business operators, and R&D institutes, aiming to ensure that AI benefits society and supports economic growth. It is necessary to address delays in domestic AI development and public concerns about AI-related risks, while balancing innovation promotion with effective risk mitigation.

While AI technologies, including generative AI, contribute to improving citizens’ lives and advancing economic development, delays in domestic AI development and utilisation, as well as public concerns about associated risks, had become challenges. 
In response to these circumstances, and in order to balance the promotion of AI innovation with risk mitigation, the AI Act was promulgated and partially enforced on 4 June 2025 and fully enforced on 1 September 2025.

Furthermore, the AI Basic Plan stipulated in Article 18, Paragraph 1 of the Act sets forth the following “Three Principles” and “Four Basic Policies” as fundamental guidelines for promoting research, development, and utilization of AI-related technologies.

Three principles
Promoting innovation while mitigating risksAgile methodology that responds to changesPromoting integrated domestic and international policies
Four Basic Policies 
Accelerated promotion of AI deployment Strategic enhancement of AI development capabilitiesLeadership in AI governanceContinuous transformation toward an AI society

title: APS AI Plan - Artificial Intelligence (AI) Plan for the Australian Public Service (APS)
body:
The AI Plan for the Australian Public Service (APS) will improve government service delivery, policy outcomes, efficiency, and productivity, through substantially increasing the use of AI in government. Every public servant will have the training and guidance required to use generative AI safely and responsibly, alongside secure access to generative AI tools, and every agency will have a Chief AI Officer to drive adoption, with AI use tracked and reported on.

The Australian Government is focused on capturing the opportunity of AI and, to ensure the benefits of this technology are shared equitably, creating a higher standard of living for all Australians. The APS AI Plan positions the government to improve service delivery, policy outcomes, efficiency and productivity by substantially increasing the safe and responsible use of AI in government. The APS AI Plan is built around three core pillars that work together to enable the safe, effective and scalable use of artificial intelligence across the Australian Public Service.
Trust Pillar. Focuses on ensuring AI is used safely, ethically and transparently. It builds on existing security and privacy safeguard governing the use of ICT and data and strengthens governance and improves transparency to maintain public trust, manage risk, and ensure AI use aligns with APS values and community expectations.People Pillar. Focuses on building capability and supporting the public service workforce by ensuring ensures public servants are equipped with the right skills to use AI responsibly and effectively. This includes access to training, consultation and engagement, and other support to use AI confidently and responsibly, recognising the impact of AI on roles, skills and ways of working.Tools Pillar. Focuses on empowering the public service workforce through access to secure, fit for purpose AI technologies. It supports the rollout of shared platforms and tools that enable efficient adoption of AI, collaboration across government, and reuse of solutions where possible.APS AI Plan Objectives:
Improving AI literacy. As AI becomes increasingly widespread and available, everyone in government needs basic AI literacy and training. Leading by example. The government has an important role to play in modelling responsible and ethical AI adoption. Expanding generative AI use. Current levels of AI adoption are inconsistent. Improving our AI maturity means broadening the safe, responsible use of generative AI to all agencies. Coordinating the government’s approach. AI transformation needs to be coordinated across the pillars of trust, people and tools. Driving systemic adoption. Advancing AI maturity requires a coordinated program of projects and investments Implementation of the APS AI Plan.

body:
The APEC Digital & AI Ministerial Meeting, first held on 4 August 2025 in Incheon, is a regional initiative bringing together 21 member economies to advance cooperation on artificial intelligence and digital transformation. It is implemented through ministerial discussions and a shared statement setting a common vision focused on innovation, connectivity and safety to guide future AI and digital cooperation.

The meeting included discussions on how emerging digital technologies, particularly AI, can improve productivity and address social challenges, alongside the importance of sharing policy practices and strengthening cooperation. It also addressed closing the digital divide, enhancing digital skills, and increasing investment in infrastructure, while highlighting the need for coordinated efforts to respond to AI‑driven threats and build a secure digital environment.

title: ANAC Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2026
document_name: Estratégia de Inteligência Artificial da ANAC 2025-2026
body:
ANAC’s AI Strategy 2025–2026 is the Brazilian Civil Aviation Agency’s roadmap for adopting AI across the organisation in a broad, safe and responsible way. It links governance, capacity-building, risk management and implementation. It was created to improve public services, strengthen decision support and protect data, rights and trust.

ANAC’s AI Strategy 2025–2026 is the formal roadmap that operationalizes the agency’s AI Policy and translates AI adoption into concrete goals, governance arrangements, actions and monitoring routines. The strategy responds to a clear opportunity and challenge: to use AI to improve internal work, digital services and regulatory performance while ensuring safety, ethics, transparency, data protection and institutional accountability. The initiative is closely aligned with ANAC’s broader institutional planning. It connects to the agency’s Strategic Plan 2020–2026, its Digital Strategy 2024–2026 and the federal digital government agenda. Its strategic vision is to achieve excellence in the broad, safe and responsible adoption of AI to advance ANAC’s mission. To support this, the strategy defines key results for staff adoption and service transformation, and organizes implementation around five objectives: integrating AI into staff activities, increasing the capacity to develop AI-enabled solutions, improving data governance, ensuring security and ethics, and optimizing AI costs. The strategy is also a governance mechanism in practice, because it assigns roles and responsibilities across the institution. ANAC’s normative framework establishes an AI governance structure involving the IT Committee, the Superintendence of Technology and Digital Transformation, the data protection officer, technical advisory units, director-linked units and AI focal points. It also created an AI core with representatives from nearly all units, who met weekly, received training and helped design the policy and strategy. This creates a cross-functional model for prioritization, oversight, risk handling, implementation support and organizational learning. Looking ahead, the initiative is designed to become more institutionalized and scalable. ANAC established a roadmap, an operational model, periodic monitoring and evaluation routines, and requirements for existing AI systems to adapt to the new rules. The strategy foresees broader uptake across internal and external services, additional specific procurements if needed, and stronger reuse of models, standards and knowledge across the agency. In this sense, the initiative is not only a strategy document, but an institutional framework for trustworthy AI adoption in a federal regulator.

title: AMALIA – Automatic Multimodal Language Assistant with Artificial Intelligence
document_name: AMALIA – Assistente Multimodal Automático de Linguagem com Inteligência Artificial
body:
AMALIA is the first LLM designed for European Portuguese, with the aim of ensuring Portugal's linguistic and cultural sovereignty. The base version was launched in SEP25 and the full multimodal version (capable of interpreting text, images and video) arrives mid-2026. Use cases will focus on the areas of education, culture, speech, media, science and public administration. The model will be openly available so that it can be used and improved by scientists and development teams on any platform.

AMALIA is the first Large-Scale Language Model (LLM) designed specifically for European Portuguese language, using AI to process and generate natural language, with the ability to understand the linguistic diversity, cultural context, and historical references unique to Portugal. 

The main objective of AMALIA is to promote digital sovereignty, ensuring that sensitive national data can be processed securely and independently. It also aims to strengthen the national AI ecosystem by supporting innovation in key sectors such as education, culture, speech, media, science and public administration. 

AMALIA will be a multimodal model, capable of interpreting not only text but also speech, images and video, and its development implies an investment of €5,5 million, led by national research institutions and coordinated by the State Technological Reform Agency (ARTE). 

AMALIA shows strong performance in European Portuguese, outperforming other open models in lexicology and semantics. The base version is complete, and developed by over 60 researchers, reinforcing national digital sovereignty. Results are measured through technical benchmarking reports and evaluations in public services. Future impacts include broader use in education, public administration, and science, with the final version expected in mid-2026.

Key risks associated with AMALIA include establishing secure and compliant protocols for sharing non-public data, ensuring adequate funding and timely development of user interfaces for the defined use cases, and preventing data obsolescence. The critical conditions for the success of an initiative such as AMALIA include the effective productization of its use cases, ensuring that they move beyond prototypes into scalable, user-ready solutions, and the establishment of a robust inference infrastructure capable of supporting its widespread deployment across Public Administration.

All versions of the model, along with the training data, will be released as open source, making them freely available to researchers, public institutions, companies, and citizens. This initiative is the first major project under Portugal’s National Artificial Intelligence Agenda, reinforcing Portugal’s commitment to ethical, inclusive, and sovereign development. The current version is already available through the IAedu platform of the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT), while the final version of AMALIA is expected to be launched in mid-2026.

title: AI-specific programmes
body:
Twenty-two degree programmes in artificial intelligence are now offered at six Slovak universities. These programmes benefit students interested in studying AI and related fields. The initiative addresses growing demand for AI skills in education and the tech job market.

Slovakia is responding to the growing global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) expertise by expanding its higher education offerings in this field. The increasing importance of AI across industries has created a clear need for well-trained professionals who can build, apply, and manage intelligent systems. In Slovakia, this demand is seen both in the technology sector and in areas such as healthcare, transportation, finance, and public administration. By offering more specialised academic programmes, the country is creating new opportunities for students to gain skills that are valuable in the job market while also helping to strengthen its digital economy.
The main goal of this initiative is to give students structured, in-depth training in AI and related subjects like data science and intelligent systems. Twenty-two degree programmes in artificial intelligence are now offered at six Slovak universities. These programmes benefit students interested in studying AI and related fields. They provide a pathway to careers in software development, machine learning, robotics, data analytics, and research, among others. Courses typically combine theoretical foundations with practical applications, helping students to understand not only how AI works, but also how to use it to solve real-world problems.
According to AIpoint.SK, six universities in Slovakia collectively offer 22 AI‑specific degree programmes. These programmes cover undergraduate and graduate study in AI, data science, intelligent systems, and related areas, and are available at leading institutions such as the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Technical University of Košice, Comenius University, University of Žilina, Pavol Jozef Šafárik University, and Pan‑European University. The aim is to prepare a skilled workforce in AI and advanced data technologies aligned with industry demand and educational advancement across the country.
The development of these programmes reflects cooperation between universities, government agencies, and private sector stakeholders. It also shows a clear national commitment to preparing the next generation of digital professionals. Looking forward, the initiative may grow by adding more advanced courses, increasing partnerships with tech companies, or offering new specialisations based on industry trends. As AI continues to evolve, Slovakia’s universities are positioning themselves to train students who can lead in both domestic and international innovation landscapes.

title: AI-based Computer-Aided Detection Software Product
document_name: Програмний продукт автоматизованого виявлення на основі штучного інтелекту
body:
AI-powered CAD software helps doctors detect tuberculosis by analysing chest X-rays. It was developed to make screening faster, cheaper, and more reliable, especially where there are not enough specialists. The tool improves early diagnosis and protects people at risk, supporting global health efforts recommended by WHO.

Chest radiography (CXR) is an important tool for screening and triage of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). It helps to identify people who may have TB and guides further testing, improving case detection and cost-efficiency. Computer-aided detection (CAD) products powered by artificial intelligence (AI) can automatically analyse CXR images for signs of TB. They provide an abnormality score that indicates the likelihood of TB and signals the need for further diagnostic evaluation. This makes screening faster, more consistent, and less dependent on the availability of trained specialists.
Impact:
According to the World Health Organization (WHO) consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, CAD software can replace human readers in interpreting digital chest X-rays for TB screening and triage among people aged 15 years and older in populations where screening is recommended. This recommendation highlights CAD as a reliable and scalable solution that supports early TB detection and better use of health resources. By improving accuracy and accessibility, AI-powered CAD systems strengthen national TB control programmes and help protect at-risk communities."

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: AI verkstaden - AI node for public administration
document_name: AI-verkstaden
body:
The "AI-verkstaden" is a national initiative that provides public sector organisations with shared, secure environments and ready‑to‑use AI services to help them develop, test, and use AI solutions. It is designed to support government agencies, regions, and municipalities by offering technical tools, guidance, and trustworthy AI services. The initiative was developed to address common challenges such as limited AI competence and  legal uncertainty.

AI‑verkstaden is a national initiative designed to help Sweden’s public sector adopt artificial intelligence safely, efficiently and at scale. It responds to long‑standing challenges across agencies, regions and municipalities, including fragmented digital infrastructure, uneven AI competence, inconsistent data quality, legal uncertainty and unequal access to technical resources. Many smaller public organisations in particular lack the environments, support and guidance needed to use AI responsibly. Against this backdrop, AI‑verkstaden leverages rapid technological progress and Sweden’s growing need for digital sovereignty, secure data management and a coordinated approach to technology adoption.

The initiative’s core objective is to provide a shared, secure national infrastructure where public actors can experiment with, develop and deploy AI solutions. This includes lab, development and production environments; a catalogue of quality‑assured AI services; and structured support that ranges from self‑service resources to expert legal, technical and change‑management advice. By enabling public actors to share models, align standards and coordinate legal and technical assessments, AI‑verkstaden reduces redundant work and promotes more coherent, efficient and trustworthy AI use across the public sector. Its broader aim is to raise AI maturity, improve service quality and strengthen Sweden’s digital resilience and civil preparedness. AI‑verkstaden is being established over multiple years (2026–2030), gradually expanding its service catalogue, infrastructure and user base. It will move from pilots and foundational support functions toward full operational capacity using a hybrid model that combines a state‑controlled “community cloud” with approved private‑sector resources. Over time, it will be institutionalised through stable governance shared between the two government agencies responsible for its oversight. Its flexible architecture ensures it can adapt to evolving technologies, regulatory requirements and user needs.

Early experimentation has already demonstrated value. A pilot with the Mörbylånga municipality tested an AI service for masking personal data, showing that local actors can securely access and use AI within a governed environment. The pilot validated technical, legal and contractual processes and highlighted user support needs, helping refine requirements for future scaling. Early user feedback confirmed that the service lowered adoption barriers. These results were assessed through real‑world testing in operational settings.

The Institute for the Public Service of Malta is implementing training programmes for public officers in Artificial Intelligence under a three-year agreement with educational institutions and government bodies. The training aims to build knowledge in AI fundamentals, applications, and responsible use. It is designed to improve how public servants use AI to enhance service delivery.

In 2022, the Maltese government signed a Memorandum of Understanding involving the Institute for the Public Service, University of Malta, MCAST, eSkills Malta Foundation, and the Office of the Prime Minister. This agreement covers three years of AI training for public officers.
The aim of the training is to raise the capacity of public servants to apply Artificial Intelligence in government operations and internal processes. body:
The Inland Revenue Authority (Agenzia delle Entrate) leverages advanced analytics software to prevent tax avoidance by analysing data from the Tax Registry and Archive of Financial Relations. This system enables more effective identification of potential tax compliance issues while optimising resource allocation.

The Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Inland Revenue Authority) has implemented advanced AI and analytics software to strengthen tax administration and improve compliance monitoring. This initiative addresses the challenge of detecting tax avoidance and fraud within a large and complex national tax system, where manual monitoring is time-consuming and prone to gaps.
The system integrates data from the Tax Registry and the Archive of Financial Relations, enabling sophisticated analysis to identify potential irregularities, anomalies, and high-risk cases. By leveraging AI algorithms, the authority can prioritise investigations, allocate resources more efficiently, and focus on cases with the highest potential impact on revenue protection.

body:
The national program’s Scientific Advisory Committee, the PBC is happy to launch a new Call for Proposals: AI for Science Moonshot. The term "Moonshot" is used here to describe an ambitious and groundbreaking project aimed at achieving a goal perceived as difficult or nearly impossible, but which has the potential to revolutionize a given domain with far-reaching implications for technological and overall progress.

The current Call for Proposals will provide financial support for a group of top researchers from at least two different public research universities who will focus on solving a central AI challenge or problem. Its aim is to encourage project(s) with the highest potential for discovery, innovation and a significant expansion of existing knowledge in core AI research, thereby positioning Israeli academia at the forefront of scientific and technological development in AI.
The program is open to all Israeli public research universities. Researchers from other higher education institutions may participate and receive funding for research activities within the program. Collaboration between researchers from at least two public research universities is required.

body:
The Slovak government is exploring the use of AI for data-driven policymaking. This involves using AI to analyse large datasets to identify trends, predict outcomes, and inform policy decisions. Such initiatives aim to make policymaking more evidence-based and effective.

The Slovak government is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to strengthen data-driven policymaking. Public bodies hold large amounts of information, but turning this into timely insights is difficult. AI offers tools to analyse datasets more quickly, identify trends, and predict outcomes, supporting more evidence-based and effective governance.
The aim is to move policymaking from reactive to proactive. Applications include labour-market analysis, health forecasting, or infrastructure planning. By modelling likely impacts, AI can help policymakers anticipate challenges and make better use of public resources.
These efforts are guided by Slovakia’s national AI strategy and supported through partnerships with researchers and technology providers.

title: AI for Growth
body:
A CAD 174 million, three-year Canadian programme to accelerate domestic AI adoption by SMEs, delivered through Canada's National AI Institutes and Global Innovation Clusters.

AI for Growth is a targeted federal funding programme announced under Canada's 2025 Budget and operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED). It is delivered through Canada's three National AI Institutes — Amii (Alberta), Mila (Québec), and the Vector Institute (Ontario) — as well as the Global Innovation Clusters network. The programme has three primary objectives: to increase AI adoption among Canadian SMEs by connecting them with advisory support, tools, and funding; to accelerate the commercialisation of Canadian-developed AI research by facilitating pathways from lab to market; and to strengthen business capacity to adopt domestically developed AI technologies, thereby reducing reliance on foreign platforms. SMEs are the primary target beneficiary, with support encompassing access to compute resources, AI readiness assessments, structured adoption pathways, and skills development. The programme is designed to build on Canada's existing innovation infrastructure rather than create new parallel institutions, leveraging the established expertise and networks of the National AI Institutes.

title: AI and Health Data Strategy 2025–2028
document_name: Stratégie intelligence artificielle et données de santé 2025‑2028
body:
The “Stratégie intelligence artificielle et données de santé 2025‑2028” is a French government initiative launched in July 2025 to structure the use of health data and artificial intelligence. It aims to improve access, sharing, and quality of health data while supporting AI deployment through regulation, governance, infrastructure, and training, in alignment with European data regulations and national innovation programmes.

The strategy addresses structural challenges in the French health data ecosystem, particularly fragmentation, limited interoperability, and complex access procedures. It seeks to unlock the potential of existing datasets by improving their organisation, quality, and reuse, while ensuring compatibility across systems and supporting large-scale data-driven innovation. 
A major focus is the preparation for the European Health Data Space framework, which introduces new obligations for data sharing and reuse across the EU. The strategy outlines concrete steps to align national systems with these rules, including defining national bodies responsible for data access, setting up standardised procedures, and creating coordinated infrastructures to enable secure and efficient data exchange at both national and European levels.
The initiative also defines a comprehensive governance model to oversee the use of health data and AI. This includes strengthening institutional coordination, creating mechanisms for stakeholder participation, and establishing oversight structures to monitor compliance, security, and ethical standards. Particular emphasis is placed on protecting individuals’ rights, improving transparency around data use, and ensuring accountability in the management of sensitive health information.
In addition, the strategy introduces operational measures to accelerate innovation, such as the development of open tools, shared resources, and experimental environments to test new data uses and AI applications. It supports the emergence of new use cases while encouraging collaboration between public and private actors, including in research, healthcare delivery, and industrial development. 
Finally, the strategy incorporates mechanisms for long-term sustainability, including financial planning for data infrastructures and the introduction of economic models governing data access and reuse. It also establishes monitoring tools, indicators, and evaluation processes to assess the effectiveness, impact, and equity of data and AI use in healthcare over time.

title: AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program
body:
The AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program is a Government of Canada initiative launched under the Canadian Sovereign AI Compute Strategy to build a large‑scale, Canadian‑controlled public AI supercomputing system, improving access to advanced computing for researchers and innovative firms.

The AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program aims to strengthen Canada’s leadership in artificial intelligence by expanding national access to advanced, AI‑optimised computing infrastructure. Delivered as part of the Canadian Sovereign AI Compute Strategy and supported by recent federal budgets, the programme focuses on building a secure, sovereign public AI supercomputer to support world‑class research, innovation and economic growth in Canada. It is designed to provide researchers and businesses with the compute capacity required for transformative AI projects while enhancing Canadian sovereignty, resilience and technological independence.
The programme is structured around two integrated layers. The Infrastructure Build Layer is responsible for designing, constructing and operating the national supercomputing system, including hardware installation, data centre operations and system administration. The National Service Layer complements this by enabling effective use of the infrastructure through user support, training, research consulting and data services, and by integrating the new system with existing public access and allocation frameworks. Together, these layers form a coordinated national ecosystem intended to support long‑term innovation, reduce external reliance and retain high‑value expertise and intellectual property within Canada.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: AI Research Resource (AIRR)
body:
The AI Research Resource (AIRR) is a UK government initiative providing AI-specialised high-performance computing capacity to public researchers, academia, and small and medium-sized enterprises. Announced as part of the AI Opportunities Action Plan in January 2025, the government committed £1 billion to expand AIRR capacity by at least 20x by 2030. The programme operates through two compute clusters — Isambard-AI at the University of Bristol and Dawn at the University of Cambridge.

AIRR addresses a shortage of publicly available computing resources in the UK's research and development community. It is positioned as a critical enabler of AI innovation and the government's broader growth agenda, providing access to advanced hardware, software, and expert support through AI-optimised high-performance computing platforms. Use cases span growth sectors including healthcare and clean energy, as evidenced by AIRR Phase 1 projects.
The programme's two flagship clusters are Isambard-AI at the University of Bristol , the UK's most powerful public compute facility, comprising 5,448 Nvidia GH200 Grace-Hopper superchips supplied by HPE, and Dawn at the University of Cambridge, made up of 1,024 Intel Data Centre GPU Max 1550 GPUs, operated in close partnership with Intel and Dell at the Cambridge Open Zettascale Lab. The government has committed over £350 million to these two clusters by 2030.
Access is structured around three routes managed through the AIRRPortal. Rapid Access targets UK-registered micro, small and medium organisations for early-stage AI product development, offering up to 20,000 GPU hours within three months. Gateway supports first-time users from academia or industry for algorithm testing and benchmarking, also providing up to 10,000 GPU hours within three months. The Innovator route is designed for larger research partnerships, offering between 50,000 and 150,000 GPU hours over six months for activities including novel algorithm development and AI-driven data synthesis. All projects must be conducted in the UK, aimed at delivering UK benefits, and access is governed by the Subsidy Control Act 2022.

body:
A France 2030 competitive three-phase funding programme supporting breakthrough AI R&D projects by startups, SMEs, labs, and consortia, with phased funding from EUR 100K (feasibility) up to EUR 8M (market application), operated by Bpifrance and Agence de programmes Numérique (Inria).

Launched in September 2025 within France's national AI strategy (Phase 3) and France 2030 investment plan, the 'Pionniers de l'IA' programme is operated for the State by Bpifrance and the Agence de programmes Numérique (Inria). The programme targets projects developing breakthrough ('rupture') AI technologies with high economic impact and national sovereignty significance, particularly in five priority sectors: industrial design and manufacturing, biomedical and health, ecological transition, cybersecurity, and energy. Projects progress through three selective phases: Phase 1 — technical feasibility (100% grant, EUR 100K–EUR 200K, 6–12 months); Phase 2 — prototype and demonstrator development (50% grant/advance for enterprises, 100% for research, EUR 400K–EUR 800K, 6–18 months); Phase 3 — market application and MVP development (up to 50% for enterprises, EUR 3M–EUR 8M, 1–3 years). Passage between phases is selective. International consortia with European partners are eligible; European partners may access funding from the Current AI Foundation. 23 first-round laureates were announced in February 2026. The programme succeeds earlier France 2030 AI calls (Communs numériques pour l'IA générative, 2023; Accélération des usages de l'IA générative, 2024).

category: National – Strategy
org: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
body:
The UK Government's central AI strategy document, published in January 2025, setting out a comprehensive national agenda to secure the UK's position as a world-leading AI nation.

Published in January 2025, the AI Opportunities Action Plan represents the most comprehensive articulation of UK AI ambitions since the 2021 National AI Strategy and was received with a formal Government Response that committed to acting on all 50 of Clifford's recommendations. The Plan is structured around three strategic pillars. First, foundations for AI: securing the physical and data infrastructure necessary for AI development, including a UK Compute Roadmap targeting GBP 1.5 billion in public compute investment, the National Data Library, the Sovereign AI Unit, and AI Growth Zones. Second, unleashing AI across the economy: accelerating AI adoption in key sectors including healthcare, education, energy, finance and public services, with specific recommendations for NHS AI deployment, an AI for Science Strategy, and the expansion of BridgeAI's regional adoption hubs. Third, securing the UK's future in AI: ensuring the UK benefits economically and secures domestic capability in frontier AI development, including through investment in UKRI's AI research programme and partnerships with leading AI laboratories. The Plan also includes a specific chapter on international AI leadership and positions the UK as a bridging actor between the US and EU approaches to AI governance.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Federal Chancellery of Austria, Directorate General for Digitalisation and E-Government
title: AI Monitor
document_name: AI Monitor
body:
The AI Monitor aims to provide information about usage of AI as well as opportunities and challenges related to AI. Updated annually, it will comprise a dashboard with a broad range of quantitative data, alongside short introductions to lighthouse projects and initiatives within the Austrian AI ecosystem and contributions by the Austrian AI Advisory Board and the AI Stakeholder Forum.

Despite a wealth of data available on developments related to AI, this information is often not accessible in a centralised manner, thus hindering evidence-based discussion about developments related to AI. The AI Monitor seeks to address this issue by collecting and presenting quantitative data from a variety of sources, mainly publiclyavailable, and by supplementing this dashboard with information about existing initiatives which provide some form of support for actors in the Austrian AI ecosystem. In addition, qualitative assessments of the Austrian AI Advisory Board and the AI Stakeholder Forum on the opportunities and challenges related to AI will help tomonitor these developments from multiple perspectives.The Austrian AI Monitor will be hosted on digitalaustria.gv.at and will be published in 2025 with annual updates.The AI Monitor will be able to integrate further initiatives and data points, allowing for a gradual expansion of itsscope.
