body:
Eestablishes an initiative to improve the usability of AI systems through human factors, an expansion plan for high-performance computing infrastructure, a cost budgeting plan for data used in AI, and a report on the feasibility and advisability of a center(s) for AI-enabled weapon systems.

Establishes an initiative to improve the usability of AI systems, that are used by Department of Defense personnel, by considering human factors and cognitive ergonomics. It mandates the development of a guidance plan for their inclusion and evaluation in current and future programs. 

Establishes a program for high-performance computing infrastructure to support advanced AI capabilities, ensuring non-duplication with Department of Energy efforts. The instrument mandates the development of a roadmap that assesses the anticipated compute requirements, security standards, and relevant resources for the infrastructure required to enable advanced AI capabilities. 

Mandates developing a plan for costs and budgeting related to data used for various stages in the AI development and deployment lifecycle. This plan must include budgets for current programs and programs established by the enactment of this Act, as well as, costs related to data procurement, preparation, protection, and analysis. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to evaluate the feasibility of centers of excellence for AI-enabled weapon systems, focusing on national and international collaboration, training of personnel, and best practices. Requires a report and briefing to Congress.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges")
body:
Amends the Intelligence Authorization Act to enhance intelligence community-private sector talent exchanges, focusing on fields like AI.

Amends section 5306 to require public-private talent exchanges in intelligence or counterintelligence to focus on fields including artificial intelligence.

Extends the duration of temporary details for such exchanges from 3 years to 5 years.

Prohibits private-sector employees detailed to the intelligence community from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information.

Clarifies that participation in the exchange program does not create an organizational conflict of interest solely by virtue of involvement.

Requires implementation of systems to address any identified conflicts of interest.

Mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to Congress on the implementation and use of the exchange program, including recommendations for improvements, for three consecutive years.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 6504 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 6504 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center")
body:
Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Security Center within the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center of NSA to develop guidance against counter-AI techniques and promote secure AI adoption practices.

Mandates the Director of the National Security Agency to establish an Artificial Intelligence Security Center (within the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center of NSA) within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Requires the Center to develop guidance to prevent or mitigate counter-artificial intelligence techniques.

Promotes secure artificial intelligence adoption practices for managers of national security systems and the defense industrial base.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 237 ("Pilot program on use of artificial intelligence for certain workflow and operations tasks")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 237 ("Pilot program on use of artificial intelligence for certain workflow and operations tasks")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to initiate a pilot program using AI-enabled software to optimize specified Department of Defense workflows and operations tasks.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to initiate a pilot program within 60 days to evaluate AI-enabled software for optimizing workflows and operations at Department of Defense facilities, including depots and shipyards, and in contract administration.

Mandates the use of top-tier software platforms, consideration of industry best practices, implementation based on human-centered design, and connection to authoritative enterprise data sources.

Obliges consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, and the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Requires a report within one year detailing software evaluations, workflow modifications, and a quantitative assessment of the software's impact.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct a pilot program for developing AI for national security-related biotechnology applications through public-private partnerships.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to implement a pilot program demonstrating artificial intelligence in national security-related biotechnology applications.

Requires collaboration through public-private partnerships to execute the program.

Permits the use of Department of Defense laboratory facilities and computing infrastructure to support biotechnology experimentation and AI model validation.

Stipulates the program's commencement within one year of enactment and its termination five years after starting.

Obligates the Secretary to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees, detailing program progress, data resource assessments, cybersecurity measures, collaboration mechanisms, and AI roles in biotechnology.

Requires a transition plan to be submitted one year before program termination, outlining steps for operationalization, including costs, infrastructure needs, and ecosystem analysis.

Aims to assess the viability of transitioning technology developed in the pilot into operational use within the Department.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 235 ("Competitive demonstration of automated target recognition algorithms")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 235 ("Competitive demonstration of automated target recognition algorithms")
body:
Requires the Chief Digital and AI Officer to develop a venue and testing processes for comparing automated target recognition algorithms by June 1, 2025. Mandates testing of Replicator algorithms by September 1, 2025.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to establish a venue and processes for testing automated target recognition algorithms by June 1, 2025.

Mandate the testing of mission capability for at least two programs in the Replicator initiative using the developed venue by September 1, 2025.

Oblige the Secretary of Defense to brief the Senate and House Armed Services Committees on activities under this section within one year of the Act's enactment.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities")
body:
Requires development policies to leverage DOD operational data for military maintenance using AI and automated systems.

Mandates the development and implementation of policies to manage and utilize digital data for maintenance of aircraft, ships, and ground vehicles within one year.

Requires investment in advanced data infrastructure for efficient data processing.

Instructs the development of a strategy incorporating AI and automated systems for data organization.

Demands collaboration with vendors to overcome proprietary data limitations through open data approaches.

Addresses enhancement of data transmission capabilities with high-speed technologies and secure methods.

Mandates central compilation of maintenance data and creation of user interfaces for data analysis.

Requires vendor-agnostic, interoperable tagging systems unless exceptions are justified.

Calls for review of classification policies to ensure appropriate classification without limiting usability.

Establishes protocols for detecting unauthorized access to vehicle or platform systems.

Obligates a briefing to Senate and House Armed Services Committees on policy development and implementation status.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 232 ("Expansion of participation in the Digital On-Demand Program")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 232 ("Expansion of participation in the Digital On-Demand Program")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to expand and promote the Digital On-Demand education program across the Department of Defense.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to expand the Digital On-Demand Program to all organizations and elements, Armed Forces members, and civilian employees within the Department of Defense.

Requires active promotion of the Program throughout the Department.

Obligates the Secretary of Defense to submit a progress report to the Senate and House Armed Services Committees within 180 days of enactment and annually through 2029.

Defines the Digital On-Demand Program as an initiative overseen by the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, providing on-demand educational resources on AI, emerging technologies, and data literacy to Department of Defense personnel via a digital platform.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 225 ("Duties of Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council relating to artificial intelligence models and advanced artificial intelligence technologies")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 225 ("Duties of Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council relating to artificial intelligence models and advanced artificial intelligence technologies")
body:
Amends the duties of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council to assess AI models for national security risks, develop strategies against unauthorized access by adversaries, and recommend legislative or administrative actions on AI to Congress and agencies.

Amends the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act to include duties for the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Counci to evaluate and assesses AI models and technologies that could pose national security risks if accessed by U.S. adversaries.

Calls for the development of strategies to prevent unauthorized access and use of powerful AI models by adversarial countries.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy")
body:
Requires the development of distance education courses on AI and ML concepts, ethics, and applications, for Armed Forces members.

Amends Section 256 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 to mandate the development of AI and machine learning education platforms.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, to create distance education courses on foundational AI and machine learning concepts and their ethical and responsible use.

Mandates making these courses available to Armed Forces members within 180 days of the enactment of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to report to congressional defense committees on the progress of implementing this educational initiative within 270 days of the subsection's enactment.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Dense to appoint a 'Chief Digital Engineering Recruitment and Management Officer of the Department of Defense' responsible for AI workforce policy and planning.

Appoints a civilian official as the Chief Digital Engineering Recruitment and Management Officer by April 30, 2025, responsible for AI workforce policy and planning in the Department of Defense.

Requires the Officer to define and identify the AI workforce, clarify roles, code roles in workforce data systems, and develop qualification programs.

Mandates updating the Department's Human Capital Operating Plan to align with strategic goals and ensure consistent AI terminology.

Sets the expiration of the Officer's appointment on September 30, 2030.

Demands a briefing to congressional defense committees within 240 days, detailing AI workforce positions, required skills, current workforce state, and future requirements.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence")
body:
Declares that it is the policy of the United States to ensure AI use does not undermine the integrity of nuclear safeguards or human decision-making with respect to the use of nuclear weapons.

Expresses the sense of Congress that artificial intelligence and machine learning can strengthen strategic communications, improve planning efficiency, and enhance modeling capabilities for stockpile stewardship.

Emphasizes the need for caution to prevent AI from compromising critical strategic assets.

Establishes U.S. policy that AI use should not undermine nuclear safeguards, affect weapon system functionality, or alter the validation of command communications.

Requires positive human actions for nuclear weapon employment decisions by the President to remain intact.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1547 ("Joint partner-sharing network capabilities for Middle East defense integration")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1547 ("Joint partner-sharing network capabilities for Middle East defense integration")
body:
Obliges the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer to develop policies for a combatant command warfighter forum on AI, considering purposes such as AI tool use cases, risk categorization, and training needs.

Obliges the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer to develop policies for a combatant command warfighter forum on AI, considering purposes such as AI tool use cases, risk categorization, and training needs.

Demands identification of opportunities for AI cooperation with regional partners and allies.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to congressional defense committees detailing the initiatives, challenges, and policy needs for a combatant command warfighter forum on AI.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1515 ("Protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1515 ("Protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense")
body:
Orders an evaluation of potential protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense, including defenses against AI-driven smishing and phishing.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to evaluate cybersecurity products and services for mobile devices to enhance the Department of Defense's cybersecurity.

Requires the Secretary to evaluate technologies such as anonymizing-enabling technologies, network-enabled content inspection, on-device VPNs, and AI-based protection against smishing, phishing, and text/email compromises.

Requires the Secretary to assess the efficacy and scalability of these technologies within the Department of Defense and their integration with existing cybersecurity architecture.

Mandates submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 270 days detailing findings and recommendations on procuring or incorporating evaluated technologies.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1514 ("Management and cybersecurity of multi-cloud environments")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1514 ("Management and cybersecurity of multi-cloud environments")
body:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to develop a strategy for the management and cybersecurity of the DOD's multi-cloud environments, including assessing means to increase AI use in these multi-cloud environments and identifying policies for protecting government data, and brief the congressional defense committees on such a strategy.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to develop a multi-cloud management and cybersecurity strategy within 180 days.

Requires the strategy to assess means to increase AI adoption in the DOD's multi-cloud environments and identify opportunities to improve planning on data use and storage, including policies to enforce the protection of government data used for training AI models.

Directs the DOD's Chief Information Officer to submit the strategy and brief congressional defense committees within 240 days.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 125 ("Designation of official responsible for autonomous surface and underwater dual-modality vehicles")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 125 ("Designation of official responsible for autonomous surface and underwater dual-modality vehicles")
body:
Requires the Secretary of the Navy to designate an official responsible for developing and acquiring surface and underwater autonomous vehicles.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to designate an official responsible for developing and acquiring advanced autonomous surface and underwater vehicles within 180 days of enactment.

Mandates the inclusion of a dedicated program element in the Navy's budget for the development and acquisition of these autonomous vehicles.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination")
body:
Demands the Secretary of Defense to establish a Department of Defense working group to coordinate AI initiatives with allies.

Demands the Secretary of Defense to establish a Department of Defense working group to coordinate AI initiatives with U.S. allies and partners within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Designates a senior civilian or military officer to lead the group and determines allied participation.

Requires the group to develop AI strategies and interoperability for intelligence sharing, battlespace awareness, and other defense operations.

Mandates managing AI data security and evaluating defense industrial capabilities for AI integration.

Ensures knowledge and technical data remain under the control of the originating country’s export laws.

Terminates the group on September 30, 2028, unless extended for national security reasons by the Secretary.

Defines key terms such as "battlespace awareness" and "covered operational use."

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to study and report on the use of unmanned ground vehicle systems produced by specified foreign adversaries, and prohibits procuring the systems if a national security threat is found.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to study the use of unmanned ground vehicle systems by the Department of Defense manufactured by certain foreign entities.

Requires submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 180 days, assessing usage, national security threats, and identifying foreign manufacturers.

Calls for the evaluation of cybersecurity risks, technological vulnerabilities, and the foreign entities' military-civil nexus.

Demands an assessment of the feasibility of the Defense Innovation Unit developing a list of U.S. manufacturers.

Mandates an evaluation of whether a prohibition on procuring and operating these systems is advisable for U.S. national security.

Prohibits procurement and operation of these systems by the Department of Defense one year after the report submission, unless deemed in the national interest.

Exempts this prohibition if recommended as not in the best national security interest.

Defines "covered foreign countries" including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews")
body:
Directs the Secretary of Defense and requires a review of methods to protect against biological attacks using AI and related topics.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct comprehensive biodefense posture reviews by December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2029.

Mandates inclusion of an inventory and assessment of existing biodefense strategies and policies, relevant biological threats, and current Department of Defense programs related to biological threats.

Identifies methods using artificial intelligence and cyber capabilities to address biological attacks.

Recommends strengthening biodefense capabilities and improving interagency coordination.

Requires submittal of a review to congressional defense committees within 30 days of completion.

Specifies that reviews must be unclassified but may include a classified annex.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit annual reports on DoD approvals and deployments of lethal autonomous weapon systems to the congressional defense committees.

Mandates the Secretary of Defense to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees on lethal autonomous weapon systems by December 31, 2025, and annually until December 31, 2029.

Requires inclusion of a comprehensive list of lethal autonomous weapon systems approved for use, waived from review, under review, and not approved, along with relevant dates.

Specifies that the initial report should cover all relevant periods as determined by the Secretary, while subsequent reports cover periods since the last report.

Allows for reports to be unclassified but permits a classified annex.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles")
body:
Requires the Navy to demonstrate large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles by June 2025 and conduct related assessments.

Mandates the Secretary of the Navy to conduct a competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles by June 1, 2025, in coordination with relevant military entities.

Requires evaluation of user feedback on these vehicles as well as vehicles' integration with mission autonomy planning, capability in contested environments, performance attributes, technical maturity, and cost to procure, operate, and sustain.

Permits the use of fiscal year 2025 Navy funds for research, development, and demonstration activities.

Obligates the Secretary of the Navy and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to submit assessments to congressional defense committees by September 1, 2025, which may include recommendations and validation of underwater vehicle requirements.

Defines the vehicles as capable of submerged operation while supporting one or more missions with modular payload integration and a minimum range of 1,000 nautical miles.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture")
body:
Provides requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture that the Secretary of the Navy must implement within 180 days, including providing a forum and resources to facilitate industry participation in the creation and management of a modular open systems architecture for maritime unmanned systems.

Requires, within 180 days, the Secretary of the Navy to provide a forum and resources for industry participation in developing a vendor-agnostic and platform-agnostic modular open systems architecture for maritime unmanned systems.

Directs the Secretary of the Navy to adopt or join a governance model that includes both Government and industry for the maritime unmanned systems standards.

Mandates the implementation of a process for incorporating industry feedback into these standards and aligning them with leading industry practices.

Requires the standards for maritime unmanned systems to be tailored for each relevant Navy program or contract to meet the minimum standards necessary for desired operational capabilities.

Instructs the Secretary of the Navy to label and distribute the standards as open and publicly releasable information to the greatest extent possible.

category: NDAA provisions;FY2025 NDAA
title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Section 1007 ("Use of technology using artificial intelligence to facilitate audit of the financial statements of the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2025")
document_name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1007 ("Use of technology using artificial intelligence to facilitate audit of the financial statements of the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2025")
body:
Encourages the use of AI and machine learning to facilitate Department of Defense financial audits.

Encourages the Secretaries of Defense, Army, Navy, and Air Force to use AI and machine learning technologies to facilitate audits of the Department of Defense's financial statements for fiscal year 2025.

Requires the Director of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering and the Inspector General, to oversee the adoption of AI and machine learning technologies for financial management and enterprise business operations.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 5051, of 2019
document_name: Brazil Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 5051, of 2019
body:
Requires human supervision in AI systems and assigns civil liability for damages from AI usage to the supervisor.  Requires state entities to train workers on AI and create specific workers' protection policies.

Establishes nonexhaustive principles for AI usage in Brazil rooted in human dignity, transparency, and the protection of privacy and personal data.

Requires AI decision-making systems to be auxiliary to humans, with supervision compatible with the type and severity of decisions.

Attributes civil liability for AI-induced damages to the system’s human supervisor.

Directs government entities to promote AI education in the workforce, create worker protection policies, and ensure gradual AI adoption.

Requires government AI applications to enhance service quality and efficiency for the population.

Effective 45 days after publication.

category: GPAI
title: [GPAI] 2024 베오그라드 장관선언
document_name: GPAI Belgrade Ministerial Declaration / 「GPAI 베오그라드 각료선언」
body:
●기관: GPAI
●문서종류: 각료선언 / 글로벌 AI 파트너십 정상회의 결과문서
●문서명: GPAI Belgrade Ministerial Declaration / 「GPAI 베오그라드 각료선언」
●발표시점: 2024년 12월 4일
●핵심내용:2024년 12월 3~4일 세르비아 베오그라드에서 개최된 GPAI 정상회의 계기 채택된 각료선언임. 동 선언은 GPAI가 OECD와 통합된 파트너십 모델하에서 계속 운영됨을 확인하고, OECD AI 원칙을 기반으로 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI의 개발·활용을 촉진하는 다중이해관계자 국제협력 플랫폼으로서의 역할을 재확인함.
① GPAI는 OECD와의 통합 파트너십과 OECD AI 원칙을 기반으로 자유·민주주의·법치·인권을 존중하는 혁신적이고 신뢰 가능한 AI 활용 방향을 재확인함
② 주요 의제로 고용·노동, 데이터 거버넌스·프라이버시, 지식재산권, AI 위험, 환경영향, 지속가능 농업 등과 글로벌 AI 격차 해소를 제시함
③ GPAI 성과의 공개 확산과 다중이해관계자 참여를 확대하고, 개발도상국·신흥경제국을 포함한 신규 회원 확대 및 비회원·국제기구와의 협력 강화를 지향함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: North Carolina House Bill 591
document_name: North Carolina HB 591 (Modernize Sex Crimes)
body:
Defines "image" to include AI-modified depictions, criminalizing sexual extortion involving such images. Criminalizes creating or modifying visual depictions of minors using AI under sexual exploitation offenses. Clarifies disclosure offenses involving AI-altered private images, making violations a felony or misdemeanor.

Amends offenses related to sexual extortion by making it a criminal act to use threats involving private images, including those modified by AI, to coerce victims, punishable as felonies depending on the circumstances.

Enhances definitions related to minors in sexual content, including AI-modified images, and escalates penalties for various degrees of exploitation, employing AI tools.

Mandates reporting to authorities if AI technology is used to distribute unlawful material depicting minors, extending jurisdiction over such offenses.

Incorporates AI-generated images into existing laws against the unauthorized disclosure of private images, classifying violations as felonies and establishing a civil cause of action.

Updates sex offender registration guidelines, emphasizing offenses involving digital or AI-enhanced sexual exploits of minors.

Sets effective date for enforcement of these provisions as December 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Georgia Technology Authority Artificial Intelligence Responsible Use (SS-23-002)
document_name: Georgia Technology Authority AI Responsible Use
body:
Regulates state agencies' ethical, transparent use of AI, prioritizing rights and minimizing harm. Requires GTA oversight in AI deployment, bias identification, privacy protection, training, and misuse reporting. Ensures collaboration transparency, rigorous testing, and contingency planning.

Outlines protocols for the responsible use of AI within Georgia state agencies, focusing on ethics, transparency, and accountability.

Requires agencies to align AI use with legal standards and agency objectives and to report AI tools to the Georgia Technology Authority (GTA).

Mandates testing and monitoring of AI solutions to ensure safety and accuracy, while addressing ethical, legal, and societal implications.

Specifies guidelines for contracting third-party AI services, emphasizing adherence to GTA and NIST standards and practices for responsible AI.

Instructs agencies to identify and mitigate biases and inaccuracies in AI-generated outputs.

Ensures data protection by adhering to Enterprise's Data Protection Policies and obtaining consent for data use.

Stipulates training and awareness for responsible AI use and a system for reporting AI misuse or unintended impacts.

Requires rigorous testing and ongoing monitoring for AI development and collaboration.

Allows State CIO or GTA OIS to terminate the use of AI tools posing risks.

category: Editors' Picks;Chinese law and policy
title: Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance)
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance)
body:
Encourages industry self-regulation through the establishment of AI safety and risk management teams, rigorous model testing, data protection measures, infrastructure security, enhanced transparency, and safety research. Signed by major companies, including Alibaba, Baidu, Huawei, Tencent, and others, to uphold AI for good principles.

Calls for the establishment of safety teams and risk management mechanisms for AI safety and security.

Mandates safety and security testing for AI models, prioritizing evaluations in critical domains.

Implements data security measures to protect training and operational data, ensuring privacy and accuracy.

Enhances infrastructure security through regular penetration tests and incident response protocols.

Requires transparency in AI model capabilities, limitations, and risk disclosures.

Advances research in AI safety and security, addressing potential biases and risks in frontier applications.

Signatories include Alibaba, Baidu, Huawei, Tencent, and other major Chinese tech companies.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SB 892 (Public contracts: automated decision systems: procurement standards)
document_name: California SB 892 (Automated decision systems procurement standards)
body:
Directs the Department of Technology to develop and adopt ADS procurement regulations, emphasizing risk assessments, equity analysis, and data minimization. Prohibits state agencies from procuring ADS without these regulations effective January 1, 2027. Requires ongoing regulatory reviews and vendor compliance.

Enacts a requirement for the California Department of Technology to develop and adopt regulations for an Automated Decision System (ADS) procurement standard.

Defines "AI" and "ADS" with exemptions for non-ADS software like spam filters.

Requires consideration of existing frameworks such as the AI Bill of Rights and NIST guidelines.

Specifies the standard must include risk assessments, risk controls, monitoring procedures, prohibition of certain ADS uses, equity assessments, data minimization, and human oversight assessments.

Instructs collaboration with various stakeholders, consultation with the California Privacy Protection Agency, and solicitation of public comments in the standard's development.

Requires the department to review and update standards annually beginning January 1, 2026.

Prohibits state agencies from procuring ADS contracts starting January 1, 2027, until regulations are adopted, mandating contracts to adhere to specified procurement standards and provide individual notice and opt-out options. 

Excludes pre-2027 budget-approved projects from these requirements.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California ACR 96 Relative to the 23 Asilomar AI Principles 2023
document_name: California ACR 96 Asilomar AI Principles 2023
body:
Supports the 23 Asilomar AI Principles as guiding values for AI development and policy. Emphasizes safety, transparency, value alignment, shared benefit, and privacy. Urges cooperation among AI researchers and policymakers, and promotes avoiding an AI arms race.

Expresses support by the California Legislature for the Asilomar AI Principles to guide the development of artificial intelligence and related public policy.

Supports creating AI with beneficial intelligence, ensuring robust systems that align with human values.

Encourages collaboration between AI researchers and policymakers and cooperation among AI developers to maintain safety standards.

Emphasizes AI safety, transparency in system failures and judicial use, and designer responsibility for AI implications.

Advocates for AI systems to respect human dignity, privacy, cultural diversity, and to empower people while sharing economic prosperity.

Stipulates human control over AI decision-making and discourages AI arms races.

Calls for cautious planning for advanced AI development, focusing on mitigating catastrophic risks.

Urges that superintelligence development serves ethical ideals and benefits all humanity.

Requests the Chief Clerk of the Assembly to distribute the resolution appropriately.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 3211 (Digital Content Provenance Standards)
document_name: California AB 3211 (Digital Content Provenance Standards)
body:
Establishes California standards for labeling generative AI (GenAI) content, requiring providers to apply and secure provenance data. Obligates large online platforms to label detected synthetic content. Imposes penalties for non-compliance, effective July 1, 2026.

Requires generative AI providers to apply provenance data to synthetic content that is difficult to remove or disassociate. 

Instructs providers to create or allow access to provenance detection tools for determining whether content was created or altered by AI.

Mandates adversarial testing of provenance data methods and submission of reports to the Department of Technology.

Prohibits entities from providing tools designed to remove provenance data deceptively.

Obligates recording devices sold in California to offer provenance data options for nonsynthetic content.

Compels large online platforms to use labels disclosing provenance data for synthetic content distributed on their platforms.

Prescribes penalties for intentional and unintentional violations.

Establishes the Digital Content Provenance Administrative Fund, funded by collected penalties, to administer the chapter.

Sets the operative date for July 1, 2026, with annual requirement for transparency reports from large online platforms on synthetic content moderation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 2930 (Automated decision systems)
document_name: California AB 2930 (Automated decision systems)
body:
Requires deployers and developers of automated decision systems to conduct impact assessments to mitigate algorithmic discrimination. Mandates notification to natural persons affected by these systems. Establishes enforcement mechanisms through the Civil Rights Department. Excludes cybersecurity technology.

Regulates the use of automated decision systems, focusing on preventing algorithmic discrimination based on protected classifications.

Requires deployers and developers to conduct impact assessments before deploying or making these systems available, and annually thereafter.

Mandates notification to individuals affected by consequential decisions made by automated systems, including an explanation and the opportunity for alternative processes.

Obligates deployers and developers to publicly disclose policies on the use and risk management of automated decision systems.

Prohibits using systems identified as posing algorithmic discrimination risks until mitigated.

Allows the Civil Rights Department to investigate violations, request impact assessments, and bring civil actions, potentially resulting in penalties for violations involving discrimination.

Exempts cybersecurity technologies and ensures confidentiality of trade secrets in impact assessments. 

Mandates compliance with existing anti-discrimination laws, ensuring cumulative protections and remedies.

category: Multinational
title: Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes)
document_name: Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes)
body:
Commits to establish a shared scientific basis for AI risk assessments. Requires risk assessments to be actionable, transparent, comprehensive, multistakeholder, iterative, and reproducible. Encourages collaboration among stakeholders and adapting methodologies as AI systems evolve.

Highlights six key aspects for risk assessment of advanced AI systems: actionable, transparent, comprehensive, multistakeholder, iterative, and reproducible.

Commits to developing a shared scientific basis for risk assessments via joint evaluations and cooperative research, allowing flexibility for members to adapt assessments according to international and domestic frameworks.

Emphasizes actionable assessments that inform effective mitigation based on specified criteria, and transparency to ensure evidence-based outcomes and broader understanding.

Advocates for comprehensiveness by linking potential risks to real-world harms and benefits, considering impacts from large-scale AI adoption, and aligning assessments with Sustainable Development Goals.

Stresses a multistakeholder approach, incorporating diverse perspectives from industry, academia, civil society, government, and multiple disciplines.

Calls for iterative assessments, adapting to AI advancements, ongoing safety research, and post-deployment monitoring.

Encourages reproducibility to enhance verification, validation, and interoperability among methods and actors.

title: [G20] 2024 리우데자네이루 정상선언
document_name: G20 Rio de Janeiro Leaders’ Declaration / 「G20 리우데자네이루 정상선언」
body:
●기관: G20
●문서종류: 정상회의 선언문 / 정상급 합의문
●문서명: G20 Rio de Janeiro Leaders’ Declaration / 「G20 리우데자네이루 정상선언」
●채택시점: 2024년 11월 18~19일
●핵심내용:2024년 11월 18~19일 브라질 리우데자네이루에서 개최된 G20 정상회의 결과문서로, 브라질 의장국의 3대 우선순위인 사회적 포용과 기아·빈곤 퇴치, 지속가능발전·에너지 전환·기후행동, 글로벌 거버넌스 개혁을 중심으로 국제협력 방향을 제시함. 선언문은 불평등 완화와 지속가능한 지구를 핵심 메시지로 삼고, 글로벌 기아·빈곤 퇴치 연합, 기후변화 대응, 국제금융체제 및 다자기구 개혁, 디지털 전환과 AI 거버넌스 등을 포괄함.
① G20은 기아·빈곤 퇴치와 불평등 완화를 최우선 의제로 설정하고, 「Global Alliance against Hunger and Poverty」를 주요 성과로 제시
② 지속가능발전·에너지 전환·기후행동과 함께 국제금융체제·다자개발은행·유엔 등 글로벌 거버넌스 개혁 필요성을 강조함
③ 디지털 전환과 AI 분야에서는 인간중심·포용성·투명성·책임성·안전성·개인정보 보호를 바탕으로 신뢰 가능한 AI 활용과 디지털 격차 해소를 위한 국제협력 필요성을 제시함

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Provisions Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern
document_name: Outbound Investment Security Rule (U.S. Treasury)
body:
Defines AI systems and outlines U.S. regulations for investments in national security technologies with countries of concern. Requires notification of certain AI-related transactions, classifies them as notifiable or prohibited and mandates compliance oversight, reporting, and potential penalties for violations.

Implements Executive Order 14105 by requiring U.S. persons to notify the Department of the Treasury about transactions involving national security technologies in "countries of concern," and prohibits certain transactions that pose acute national security threats.

Defines AI systems as machine-based systems capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions that affect environments, thereby impacting transactions involving AI development and deployment.

Specifies which transactions are notifiable or prohibited, including those involving AI systems intended for military, intelligence, or surveillance uses as well as those of a specified computing power.

Mandates U.S. persons to file notifications and prohibits knowingly directing others to undertake prohibited transactions.

Details civil and criminal penalties for violations, including fines up to $250,000 or imprisonment up to 20 years.

Outlines exceptions, including certain public securities transactions and specific national interest exemptions.

Permits the Secretary of the Treasury to compel divestment of any prohibited transaction, with the aid of the Attorney General.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: State of New Hampshire Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies Policy
document_name: New Hampshire State Use of AI Policy
body:
Guides New Hampshire State Employees on ethical AI use, emphasizing human oversight, transparency, and data protection. Requires agency heads to ensure compliance and report AI use. Employs AI for public services under strict ethical guidelines and accountability measures. Maps to NIST standards.

Requires all New Hampshire State Employees to adhere to ethical guidelines for AI use, emphasizing protection of Personal Identifying Information (PII) and sensitive data.

Dictates a human-centric approach, transparency, fairness, privacy, and continuous monitoring in AI deployment for government services.

Allows AI for decision support, public engagement, predictive analytics, image and video analysis, natural language processing, generative content, healthcare, environmental monitoring, and transportation, subject to stringent data protection and human oversight.

Mandates AI systems to explain decisions and actions and undergo ethical reviews when high-risk.

Instructs employees to ensure data protection and adhere to cybersecurity measures per the Statewide Information Security Manual and NIST-800-53 standard.

Requires informing users about AI interactions and data handling.

Assigns Agency heads responsibility for policy adherence, with AI technologies reported to the Business Relationship Management Division.

References New Hampshire AI ethics code and laws related to deepfakes and AI use.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Oklahoma H 3642
document_name: Oklahoma H 3642 (Oklahoma Law on Obscenity and Child Pornography)
body:
Defines "child pornography" to include computergenerated images and establishes severe penalties for production and possession. Requires registration as a sex offender for possession of 100+ depictions. Effective November 1, 2024, the act targets explicit computer-generated images involving minors.

Amends Oklahoma laws to enhance penalties for offenses involving child pornography, specifically targeting AI-generated images. 

Defines "child pornography" to include computer-generated images and altered images that depict minors in sexually explicit conduct, regardless of whether the image is real or synthetic. 

Establishes that possessing, distributing, or creating such images, including those utilizing AI technology, is a felony with penalties up to 20 years imprisonment and a $25,000 fine. 

Specifies that possession of 100 or more images constitutes aggravated possession, punishable by life imprisonment and a $10,000 fine, with required sex offender registration.  

Clarifies that AI-generated and computer-altered images count as independent offenses. 

Mandates that this act becomes effective on November 1, 2024.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive)
document_name: JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (UK MoD)
body:
Requires the Ministry of Defense’s development and use of AI to be governed by national and international law and to align with the principles of human centricity, responsibility, understanding, bias and harm mitigation, and reliability; provides guidance on AI ethics governance, AI lifecycle agnostic requirements, quality, safety, and security, and AI assurance.

Explains the Ministry of Defense’s adopted definition of AI, the scope of the document, and the delegation of responsibilities for TLB Holders and Chief Executives, and requires the JSP to be applied by all MOD staff in all phases of the AI lifecycle.

Requires the MOD’s development and use of AI to be governed by national and international law and to align with the principles of human centricity, responsibility, understanding, bias and harm mitigation, and reliability. 

Provides requirements related to AI ethics governance, including that each TLB appoint a RAISO and that large AI projects with significant ethical risks have an ethics manager and an independent ethics assurance mechanism.

Addresses the teaming of humans with AI by mandating the adoption of a Human Centered Design approach across AI systems’ lifecycles, encouraging the identification of AI systems’ workforce implications, and providing guidance on the training implications of AI.

Explains AI development and use lifecycle concepts, such as DevOps, and provides guidance on lifecycle agnostic requirements, including those related to planning, data collection and control, and AI verification and validation.

Requires safety risk analysis, security risk analysis, and other measures to ensure  requirements related to AI quality, safety, and security. 

Obliges AI suppliers to deliver products at a level of confidence that is commensurate with their use, and provides guidance on AI assurance.

category: Chinese law and policy
title: Artificial Intelligence Security Standardization White Paper, Section 5 ("Recommendations for AI security standardization work")
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Security Standardization White Paper, Section 5 ("Recommendations for AI security standardization work")
body:
Recommends coordinating AI security standards, emphasizing ethical principles, and accelerating standards development in key areas. Promotes AI security standards application, talent training, and international collaboration. Suggests high-risk AI early warning mechanisms and improving AI security supervision and supply chain management.

Launch AI security standardization work by coordinating a system of AI security standards, focusing on foundational and application-specific research.

Accelerate development of AI security standards in key areas, driven by urgent needs and safety incidents, to address security risks and ethical issues.

Promote the application of AI security standards through pilot mechanisms and collaboration between academia, industry, and research institutions.

Strengthen training for AI security standardization talent by establishing multi-level training programs and fostering collaboration among universities, research institutes, and enterprises.

Participate actively in international AI security standardization by aligning Chinese efforts with global achievements, enhancing China's influence, and facilitating international cooperation.

Establish an early warning mechanism for high-security-risk AI technologies and products, including a catalog of risks and management standards.

Improve AI security supervision by developing an index evaluation system, enhancing AI supply chain security management, and formulating supportive standards.

category: Editors' Picks
title: Compliance of products with embedded artificial intelligence (ECE/TRADE/486)
document_name: Compliance of products with embedded artificial intelligence
body:
Establishes a common regulatory arrangement (CRA) for products with embedded AI, promoting harmonization, risk assessment, and conformity assessment procedures across nations. Calls for surveillance, human oversight in high-risk products, and adherence to international standards. Encourages regulatory convergence and interoperability internationally.

Establishes a Common Regulatory Arrangement (CRA) for products with embedded AI to harmonize international standards and regulations, aiming to facilitate market access.

Encourages adoption of the CRA at the national level to converge technical regulations and conformity assessment procedures across borders.

Recommends regulatory objectives to assess risk levels and ensure human oversight in high-risk AI systems, such as medical devices.

Addresses societal impacts by emphasizing the mitigation of bias, safeguarding individual autonomy, and ensuring equitable access for emerging economies.

Promotes international standards such as ISO/IEC, WHO, and OECD guidelines for AI systems.

Calls for rigorous conformity assessment methods proportionate to product risk, advocating for third-party assessments for high-risk technologies.

Mandates continuous market surveillance to ensure compliance post-market entry, involving regular audits and withdrawal of non-compliant products.

Urges regulatory cooperation and shared examples of product regulations to promote alignment of technical standards globally.

category: 미국
title: [미국] 미국의 AI 리더십 증진, 국가안보 목표 달성을 위한 AI 활용, 안전·보안·신뢰 가능한 AI 촉진에 관한 국가안보각서

body:
●국가: 미국
●기관: 백악관 / 국가안보회의(NSC)
●문서종류: 국가안보각서
●문서명: National Security Memorandum on Advancing the United States’ Leadership in Artificial Intelligence; Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Fulfill National Security Objectives; and Fostering the Safety, Security, and Trustworthiness of Artificial Intelligence/ 「미국의 AI 리더십 증진, 국가안보 목표 달성을 위한 AI 활용, 안전·보안·신뢰 가능한 AI 촉진에 관한 국가안보각서」

●핵심내용미국의 AI 국가안보 활용 원칙을 정한 최초의 포괄적 국가안보각서. AI 반도체·컴퓨팅·인재·공급망 보호와 함께, 국가안보 분야 AI 활용 시 인권·시민권·프라이버시·안전 보호를 병행하도록 규정함.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies;Editors' Picks
title: Memorandum on Advancing the United States’ Leadership in Artificial Intelligence; Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Fulfill National Security Objectives; and Fostering the Safety, Security, and Trustworthiness of Artificial Intelligence
document_name: National Security Memorandum on AI
body:
Directs the U.S. government to lead safe AI development, enhance national security through AI, and foster global AI governance. Prioritizes AI safety, security, and talent acquisition. Establishes AI governance frameworks and partnerships to ensure responsible AI use and international collaboration.

Develop advanced AI computational infrastructure and adopt measures to attract top technical talent to work in the United States to ensure innovation and technological superiority in AI.

Instructs relevant agencies to protect AI intellectual property from foreign threats. 

Issue guidance on testing and evaluating frontier foundational AI systems to manage safety and security risks.

Directs national security institutions to harness AI to advance national security objectives through clear policies, strategies and coordination, while safeguarding human rights, civil liberties, and privacy.

Produce a strategy for the advancement of international AI governance norms in line with safe, secure, and trustworthy AI, and democratic values.

Requires covered agencies to appoint Chief AI Officer to managing risks and opportunities of AI

Requires the formation of an interagency National Security Coordination Group to harmonize polices related to AI in National Security

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies;Editors' Picks
title: Framework to Advance AI Governance and Risk Management in National Security
document_name: National Security Memorandum on AI: Governance and Risk Management Framework
body:
Classifies prohibited and "high-impact" AI use cases based on risks to national security, human rights, and effect on Federal personnel. Defines minimum risk assessment standards, mandates monitoring mechanisms for high-impact AI and training guidelines for the development and use of AI systems.

Mandates agencies to identify prohibited and high-impact AI use cases, emphasizing risks to national security, human rights, and civil liberties. 

Restricts the use of AI whose output serves as the primary basis for decisions that could pose significant risks to human rights or national security, unless accompanied by human oversight.

Requires agencies to conduct risk assessments and implement minimum risk management practices for high-impact AI uses, ensuring human oversight and accountability.

Mandates annual inventories of high-impact AI use cases and establishes data management policies prioritizing AI systems.

Obligates agencies to appoint Chief AI Officers and establish AI Governance Boards to oversee AI activities and compliance. 

Stipulates standardized training for responsible AI use and development, ensuring accountability and documentation.

Allows waivers for certain risk management practices under strict conditions and oversight.

Ensures transparency and public trust through periodic reporting on AI oversight activities, with unclassified information made publicly available where possible.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Common Intelligence Community Interim Guidance Regarding the Acquisition and Use of Foundation AI Models
document_name: Common Intelligence Community Interim Guidance Regarding the Acquisition and Use of Foundation AI Models
body:
Provides guidance for the Intelligence Community on acquiring, modifying, and using foundation AI models while ensuring compliance with Attorney General guidelines. Requires lawful acquisition, safeguards for U.S. person information, and regular reviews to address privacy implications.

Provides interim guidance for the Intelligence Community (IC) on acquiring and using foundation AI models, focusing on model acquisition, modification, and outputs.

Requires model acquisition to comply with legal standards, ensuring alignment with established IC frameworks.

Mandates prompts and outputs be used for authorized purposes and treated as collected data when applicable, ensuring compliance with existing guidelines on retention and dissemination.

Emphasizes the need for oversight mechanisms to track U.S. person information used or retrieved from AI models.

category: G7
title: [G7] 히로시마 AI 프로세스 보고 프레임워크 파일럿 결과
document_name: Overview of the OECD Pilot of the Hiroshima Artificial Intelligence Process Reporting Framework / 「히로시마 AI 프로세스 보고 프레임워크 OECD 시범운영 개요」
body:
●기관: G7 이탈리아 의장국
●문서종류: 개요문서 / 히로시마 AI 프로세스 보고 프레임워크 시범운영 결과
●문서명: Overview of the OECD Pilot of the Hiroshima Artificial Intelligence Process Reporting Framework / 「히로시마 AI 프로세스 보고 프레임워크 OECD 시범운영 개요」
●발표시점: 2024년 10월 15일
●핵심내용:G7 이탈리아 의장국이 히로시마 AI 프로세스 국제 행동규범의 자발적 이행을 점검하기 위해 OECD와 함께 추진한 보고 프레임워크 시범운영 결과를 정리한 문서임. 2024년 7월부터 9월까지 10개국 20개 기관이 참여한 파일럿을 통해, 고도 AI 시스템 개발 조직이 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI 개발을 위해 어떤 조치를 취하고 있는지 자발적으로 보고할 수 있는 체계의 실효성과 개선방향을 검토함.
① G7 이탈리아 의장국은 히로시마 AI 프로세스 국제 행동규범의 확산·채택·이행을 주요 우선순위로 설정하고, OECD에 자발적 이행을 점검할 보고 프레임워크 개발을 요청함
② OECD는 기업·학계·시민사회 등 전문가 의견과 10개국 20개 기관의 파일럿 참여를 바탕으로 고도 AI 시스템 개발 조직을 위한 보고 프레임워크 초안을 마련함
③ 향후 기존 보고체계와의 중복을 줄이고 문안·온라인 인터페이스를 개선해, 안전하고 신뢰 가능한 AI 개발을 위한 자발적 행동규범 이행 점검 도구로 발전시키는 방향을 제시함

category: G7
title: [G7] 공공부문 AI 활용 툴킷
document_name: G7 Toolkit for Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector / 「공공부문 인공지능을 위한 G7 툴킷」
body:
●기관: G7
●문서종류: 툴킷 / 공공부문 AI 정책·활용 지침
●문서명: G7 Toolkit for Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector / 「공공부문 인공지능을 위한 G7 툴킷」
●발표시점: 2024년 10월 15일
●핵심내용:G7 맥락에서 OECD와 UNESCO가 작성한 공공부문 AI 활용 지침으로, 정책결정자와 공공부문 리더가 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI 원칙을 실제 정책과 행정 활용으로 전환할 수 있도록 지원하는 툴킷임. 공공부문 AI가 내부 운영 효율성, 정책결정 효과성, 공공서비스 대응성, 투명성과 책임성을 높일 수 있음을 전제로, G7 회원국의 활용사례와 정책대응, 실행단계별 고려사항을 제시함.
① 문서는 공공부문의 AI 원칙을 선언적 수준에서 실제 정책·조직 운영·서비스 설계로 전환하기 위한 실무적 지침을 제시함
② AI가 행정 운영·정책 수립·공공서비스·투명성·책임성 강화에 기여할 수 있는 가능성과 함께 윤리·위험관리·신뢰성 확보 필요성을 강조함

category: Editors' Picks;Corporate policies and commitments
title: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy
document_name: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy
body:
Establishes AI Safety Level Standards (ASLs) for AI model testing, deployment and security. Requires ASL-2 standards for current models, with ASL-3 for higher-risk capabilities like Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapon development or autonomous R&D. Implements Capability Thresholds to trigger safeguard upgrades. Outlines regular assessments, reviews, and transparency requirements.

Establishes AI Safety Level (ASL) Standards to guide safe deployment and security for current and future AI models, categorizing measures into Deployment and Security Standards.

Requires all current models to meet ASL-2 standards, focusing on safe usage and protection from unauthorized access.

Introduces Capability Thresholds to determine when stronger safeguards (ASL-3 or higher) are needed, specifying Required Safeguards for particular risks including Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) capabilities and Autonomous AI R&D.

Mandates comprehensive assessments to ensure models remain below Capability Thresholds, with stricter ASL-3 standards implemented if thresholds are surpassed.

Outlines internal governance practices including a Responsible Scaling Officer role, transparency measures, and procedures for noncompliance whistleblowing.

Commits to public transparency, expert input, and notifying US Government if standards beyond ASL-2 are needed.

body:
●기관: 세계경제포럼(WEF)

●발표시점: 2024년 10월 8일
●핵심내용:세계경제포럼이 생성형 AI의 급속한 발전에 대응하여 정책결정자와 규제기관이 활용할 수 있는 실행 가능한 거버넌스 전략을 제시한 백서임. 동 보고서는 생성형 AI가 산업, 경제, 사회 전반을 재편하는 상황에서 예측적이고 포용적이며 상호운용 가능한 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 환경을 조성하기 위해 360도 거버넌스 프레임워크를 제안함.
① 문서는 생성형 AI의 빠른 발전으로 규제 공백·국가별 접근 차이·책임 불명확성 등 새로운 거버넌스 과제가 부상하고 있다고 지적함

③ 생성형 AI 거버넌스는 표준·책임성·위험관리·국제협력·민관협력·규제 상호운용성을 결합한 360도 접근으로 추진해야 한다고 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Alabama House Bill 172
document_name: Alabama HB 172 (Use of Materially Deceptive Media in Elections)
body:
Criminalizes distributing AI-generated materially deceptive media to influence elections. Exempts media with clear disclaimers. Permits injunctive relief by affected parties. Provides exceptions for certain media outlets and satire. Effective October 1, 2024, with penalties for second offenses.

Prohibits the distribution of materially deceptive media, produced by AI, within 90 days before an election if intended to harm a candidate's reputation or influence voting patterns.

Defines "materially deceptive media" as AI-generated content falsely depicting individuals in actions or speech they did not partake in.

Allows exceptions if disclaimers clearly state the media's manipulation and provide source citations for edited content.

Classifies violations as Class A misdemeanors, with repeat offenses within five years as Class D felonies.

Permits the Attorney General, depicted individuals, candidates, and voter-representing entities to seek permanent injunctive relief against violators.

Excludes distributors without knowledge of deception or intent to harm from violations, including media entities distributing content as part of legitimate news coverage.

Protects satire and parody, provided they don't rely on AI for impersonation.

Effective October 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents;Editors' Picks
title: Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier Artificial Intelligence Models Act (SB 1047)
document_name: Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier AI Act (SB 1047)
body:
Requires developers of frontier AI models to implement comprehensive safety and security protocols and detailed risk assessments. Requires annual audits, mandates incident reporting within 72 hours, creates a regulatory board and introduces plans for a public cloud computing cluster called CalCompute.

Requires developers of frontier AI models to implement comprehensive safety and security protocols, including cybersecurity protections, full shutdown capabilities, and detailed risk assessments.

Mandates annual independent audits and public disclosure of redacted audit reports and obligates developers to report AI safety incidents to the Attorney General within 72 hours.

Establishes policies for entities operating computer clusters to assess whether customers intend to use the clusters for training covered models.

Creates the Board of Frontier Models to update AI model thresholds and auditing requirements, ensuring alignment with technological advancements and best practices.

Imposes penalties for non-compliance, including civil penalties, injunctive relief, and punitive damages.

Introduces CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster to support AI research and innovation, with a framework to be developed by a consortium.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Senate Bill 1381 (2024)
document_name: California SB 1381 (Crimes: child pornography) (2024)
body:
Expands legal prohibitions to include child pornography generated or altered by artificial intelligence. Subjects such AI-generated content to penalties. Allows forfeiture and destruction of such content without a criminal conviction. Becomes operative with AB 1831 enactment.

Expands existing child pornography laws to include materials digitally altered or generated by artificial intelligence.

Prohibits the production, distribution, or possession of AI-generated depictions involving minors engaging in sexual conduct.

Imposes penalties including fines and imprisonment for violations involving AI-generated content depicting minors, including recruiting minors to create such content.

Specifies exemptions for legally emancipated minors; law enforcement; legitimate medical, educational, or scientific activities; and lawful conduct between spouses.

Allows forfeiture of AI-generated depictions involving minors engaging in sexual conduct that is in the possession of city, county, or state officials or agencies.

Allows destruction of AI-generated materials regardless of criminal conviction.

Mandates that the act becomes operative only if AB 1831 is enacted by January 1, 2025.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Senate Bill 1288 (2024)
document_name: California SB 1288 (Public schools: artificial intelligence working group) (2024)
body:
Requires the Superintendent to convene a working group to develop guidance and a model policy on AI's safe use in education by 2026. Mandates reporting findings by 2027 and repeals provisions by 2031.

Requires the Superintendent of Public Instruction to form a working group to address artificial intelligence in public schools.

Requires the working group to develop guidance and a model policy for safe AI use in education by January 1, 2026.

Instructs the working group to create a model policy by July 1, 2026, for the safe and beneficial use of AI that does not negatively impact students or educators.

Mandates that the working group consist of certain stakeholders, including public school teachers and schoolsite administrators.

Calls the working group to assess AI use in education, including technologies in use, costs, and impacts on educators, and to detail current uses of artificial intelligence in educational settings.

Requires the working group to conduct at least three public meetings for stakeholder feedback.

Requires the working group to identify other ways in which the state can promote effective practices that minimize risk and maximize benefits to pupils and educators, including establishing communities of practice on the use of artificial intelligence in education.

Obliges the group to report findings and recommendations to the Legislature by January 1, 2027.

Dissolves the working group upon report submission and repeals provisions by January 1, 2031.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Senate Bill 1120 (2024)
document_name: California SB 1120 (Health care coverage: utilization review) (2024)
body:
Requires health care service plans and disability insurers using AI for utilization review to ensure compliance with clinical criteria, non-discrimination, transparency, and auditability. Prohibits AI from replacing provider decision-making or denying services based on medical necessity.

Requires health plans and disability insurers that use AI for utilization review or work with an entity that uses AI for utilization review to ensure that the AI is lawful; nondiscriminatory; based on clinical information; open to review; responsibly uses patient data; does not supplant health care provider decisionmaking; and does not cause harm to the enrollee.

Prohibits health plans and disability insurers that use AI for utilization review from denying, delaying, or modifying health care services based on medical necessity and mandates that only licensed health care professionals make determinations of medical necessity by evaluating clinical issues on a case-by-case basis; clarifies that state departments may issue guidance to help implement federal rules regarding AI in healthcare; and requires that health plans have a medical director review and report on the health care service plan's compliance with requirements

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Assembly Bill 2876 (2024)
document_name: California AB 2876 (Pupil instruction: media literacy: artificial intelligence literacy: curriculum frameworks: instructional materials) (2024)
body:
Require the California Instructional Quality Commission to incorporate AI literacy in curriculum frameworks for mathematics, science, and history-social science and consider AI literacy in its criteria for evaluating instructional materials when they are next adopted by the state board after January 1, 2025.

Defines "AI literacy" as the knowledge, skills, and attitudes related to how artificial intelligence works, including its principles, concepts, applications, limitations, implications, and ethical considerations.

Mandates the commission to consider incorporating AI literacy content into the mathematics, science, and history-social science curriculum frameworks when those frameworks are next revised after January 1, 2025.

Requires the commission to consider including AI literacy in the criteria for evaluating mathematics, science, and history-social science instructional materials adopted by the state board after January 1, 2025.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Senate Bill 896 Generative Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act (2024)
document_name: California SB 896 Generative Artificial Intelligence Accountability Act (2024)
body:
Promotes generative AI workforce training by the state. Directs the Department of Technology to update a report to the Governor about generative AI risks and directs the Office of Emergency Services to perform a risk analysis of potential threats posed by the use of generative AI to California’s critical infrastructure. Instructs state agencies to explore potential effective generative AI use cases and implement disclaimers in communications produced by generative AI.

States that no individual or group should be discriminated against by AI systems, encourages agency collaboration and the creation of public-private partnerships to train the AI workforce, and directs state agencies to protect people from generative AI risks, including through rulemaking or clarification of the applicability of existing rules to AI

Defines artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence

Directs the Department of Technology to update a report to the Governor about generative AI risks

Directs the Office of Emergency Services to perform a risk analysis of potential threats posed by the use of generative AI to California’s critical infrastructure and summarize the analysis for the Legislature annually

Instructs state agencies to explore potential effective generative AI use cases while ensuring compliance with state procurement policies.

Directs state agencies to implement disclaimers and human contact information in communications generated by generative AI

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Assembly Bill 1831 (2024)
document_name: California AB 1831 (Child Pornography Crimes)
body:
Prohibits the creation, distribution, possession, and exhibition of AI-generated child sexual assault material (CSAM) in California and imposes severe penalties.

Clarifies that child sexual assault material (CSAM) generated by artificial intelligence (AI) is obscene and prohibits the creation, distribution, and possession of this material in California.

Defines AI as a machine-based system that can infer from inputs how to generate outputs that influence environments.

Punishes the distribution or possession of AI-generated CSAM depicting minors under 18 engaging in sexual conduct with imprisonment and fines and classifies this conduct as a felony in certain cases 

Exempts law enforcement; medical, scientific, educational activities; lawful conduct between spouses; and legally emancipated children under 18 from these provisions.

Specifies enhanced penalties for possessing certain material and for repeat offenders

Specifies enhanced penalties for using government-owned computers, computer networks, or property for CSAM-related offenses.

Requires revenue from fines to support sexual assault investigator training and services for human trafficking victims.

Becomes operative only if Senate Bill 1381 is enacted by January 1, 2025.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Assembly Bill 3030 (2024)
document_name: California AB 3030 (AI Health Care Services)
body:
Require health facilities using generative AI for patient communications to include disclaimers and contact instructions for human providers but exempt communications reviewed by a human health care provider from these requirements. Impose enforcement mechanisms for violations by health facilities, clinics, and physicians.

Requires health facilities, clinics, and physician offices using generative AI for patient communications in a variety of modalities to include a disclaimer indicating AI generation.

Mandates the disclaimer's prominence at the beginning, end, and/or throughout written, audio, and video communications, with instructions for contacting a human provider.

Exempts communications reviewed by a licensed health care provider from disclaimer requirements.

Defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence," "generative artificial intelligence," and "patient clinical information."

Subjects licensed health facilities, clinics, and physicians violating these requirements to enforcement mechanisms.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Assembly Bill 2013 (2024)
document_name: California AB 2013 (AI Training Data)
body:
Requires developers to disclose training data for generative AI systems publicly by January 1, 2026, and for each subsequent release. Exempts AI systems focused on security, aircraft operation, and national defense. Specifies detailed documentation requirements for datasets, including sources, content types, and modifications.

Defines key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "developer," "generative artificial intelligence," and "synthetic data generation" to clarify the scope and applicability of the regulations.

Mandates developers of generative AI systems, including parties that release a new system or make substantial modifications to a system, released on or after January 1, 2022 to publicly disclose training data documentation on their websites by January 1, 2026, and for each subsequent release.

Requires documentation to include a summary of datasets, sources, purposes, data points, intellectual property status, personal information, any data processing or modifications, and the use of synthetic data generation.

Exempts AI systems solely for security, aircraft operation in national airspace, or national security and defense provided they are only available to federal entities.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 2885 (2024)
document_name: California (2024) AB 2885 (Artificial Intelligence)
body:
Directs the California Department of Technology to inventory high-risk automated decision systems by September 2024; requires the Secretary of Government Operations to evaluate deepfakes, digital content forgery technology, and digital content provenance by October 2024; and requires local agencies to annually report on AI's impact on jobs in warehouse distribution centers that have received economic development subsidies.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as systems that infer from inputs how to influence environments and "high-risk automated decision systems" as a computational process that issues output intended to replace human discretionary decisionmaking in areas such as housing, education, and employment.

Requires, by September 1, 2024, the California Department of Technology to inventory high-risk automated decision systems that currently are or may be used, developed, or procured by state agencies, detailing decision-making roles, data usage, and risk mitigation measures.

Requires the Department to submit an annual report on the inventory of high-risk systems to legislative committees until 2029.

Defines terms related to the creation and tracking of misleading AI-generated material, including "deepfake," "digital content forgery," and "digital content provenance."

Requires the Secretary of Government Operations to evaluate the impact of deepfakes, digital content forgery technologies, and digital content provenance on state governance and residents and create a plan to develop digital content provenance mechanisms, with a report to the Legislature due by October 1, 2024.

Requires local agencies to annually report on automation impacts, including AI, on jobs in warehouse distribution centers that are beneficiaries of economic development subsidies and submit the report to the Governor’s Office of Business and Economic Development.
