category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 3061 (Vehicles: Autonomous Vehicle Incident Reporting 2024)
document_name: California AB 3061 (Vehicles: Autonomous Vehicle Incident Reporting 2024)
body:
Adds Section 38760 to California's Vehicle Code, requiring autonomous vehicle manufacturers to report collisions, disengagements, and traffic violations from July 31, 2025. Mandates quarterly reports on vehicle miles and incidents. Requires data publication and redaction by the DMV starting January 1, 2028.

Adds Section 38760 to the California Vehicle Code to enhance transparency and public safety concerning autonomous vehicles.

Requires autonomous vehicle manufacturers, beginning July 31, 2025, to report collisions and disengagements to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) when vehicles operate in autonomous mode on public roads.

Mandates the inclusion of detailed incident information in reports, such as collision narratives, road conditions, and vehicle permits.

Obligates manufacturers to submit quarterly summaries of incidents, vehicle miles traveled, immobilizations, and unresolved traffic citations.

Instructs the DMV, starting July 1, 2025, to maintain and, from January 1, 2028, publish incident reports while redacting personal and proprietary information.

Permits the DMV to establish additional regulations and assess fees to recover costs related to implementing these requirements. 

Ensures public access to data and supports safe deployment of autonomous vehicles through comprehensive reporting and regulatory oversight.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 2286 (Vehicles: Autonomous Vehicles 2024)
document_name: California AB 2286 (Autonomous Vehicles 2024)
body:
Regulates autonomous vehicles over 10,001 pounds, requiring a human safety operator during testing and operation. Instructs the Department of Motor Vehicles to report by 2030 on safety and employment impacts, consulting several agencies. Mandates collision and annual disengagement reports from manufacturers.

Enacts new regulations for autonomous vehicles in California with a focus on vehicles weighing over 10,001 pounds.

Prohibits operation of these vehicles without a human safety operator physically present.

Instructs the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to submit a report by 2030 evaluating the technology's impact on safety and employment.

Requires consultation with the California Highway Patrol, Labor and Workforce Development Agency, Department of Transportation, State Air Resources Board, and independent experts.

Dictates that the DMV cannot issue deployment permits without a human safety operator until one year after an oversight hearing and legislative approval.

Mandates collision and disengagement reporting for vehicles over 10,001 pounds, specifying circumstances of disengagements.

Defines "disengagement" as any deactivation of autonomous mode due to technology failure or safety requirements.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Fraudulent Misrepresentation of Campaign Authority
document_name: Fraudulent Misrepresentation of Campaign Authority
body:
Clarifies that 52 U.S.C. 30124 and 11 CFR 110.16 apply to fraudulent misrepresentation using AI. States that the statute is technology-neutral, covering fraud via AI-generated content or other means. Emphasizes non-binding nature of this interpretive guidance.

Clarifies that 52 U.S.C. 30124 and 11 CFR 110.16 apply to fraudulent misrepresentation in federal election campaigns, regardless of the technology used, including AI.

Emphasizes that the statute is technology neutral and covers AI-assisted media, forged signatures, and other means of fraudulent activity.

States that the legal focus is on whether individuals fraudulently represent themselves as acting for a candidate or political party.

Announces that this interpretation will guide the Commission's future actions concerning evolving technologies.

Specifies that this interpretive rule does not require notice and comment procedures, nor does it bind the Commission or public.

Excludes the applicability of the Regulatory Flexibility Act, as the interpretive rule does not involve binding agency action.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act, Section 4 ("Advanced pipeline materials and technologies demonstration initiative")
document_name: H. R. 7073 Pipelines R&D Act, Section 4 ("Advanced pipeline materials and technologies demonstration initiative")
body:
Requires the Secretary of Energy to establish a demonstration initiative to advance pipeline and related infrastructure technologies, such as autonomous sensor systems; advanced computational, data analytics, and machine learning models; and autonomous robotic and patch technologies. Requires the Secretary of Energy to evaluate projects' technical performance and economic feasibility during the selection process.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to establish a demonstration initiative awarding financial assistance for demonstration projects, of low- to mid-technology readiness, for pipelines and associated infrastructure technologies.

Declares advanced sensor technologies such as autonomous sensor systems, including uncrewed aircraft, eligible for financial assistance through the initiative.

Declares advanced computational, data analytics, and machine learning models, as well as autonomous robotic and patch technologies, eligible for financial assistance through the initiative.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to evaluate projects' technical performance and economic feasibility, for return on investment impact, in the selection process for the initiative. 

Authorizes $45 million for fiscal year 2025 and $50 million annually for fiscal years 2026-2029 from designated offices to implement the initiative.

Terminates the initiative five years after enactment.

category: Multinational
title: Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies
document_name: Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies
body:
Urges governments to align AI practices with human rights laws, assess and monitor high-risk AI systems for impacts on equity, fairness, and safety. Requires public disclosure for risks, remedies for harms, support for personnel training, and secure AI procurement processes.

Endorses the responsible use and regulation of AI to enhance public service delivery while safeguarding human rights, as reiterated by the Freedom Online Coalition (FOC).

Acknowledges the potential risks of AI misuse, including bias, privacy violations, and exacerbation of inequalities, especially for marginalized populations.

Urges governments to adhere to international legal obligations, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, when employing AI systems.

Mandates assessment and management of AI risks in high-risk contexts.

Advocates for continuous monitoring and external audits of AI systems to maintain fairness and rights protection.

Mandates support for adequate training for personnel involved in AI to comprehend its impact on human rights.

Demands transparency, public consultation on AI uses, and mechanisms for public feedback and opting out of AI-enabled decisions.

Calls for effective remedies and redress for individuals harmed by AI systems.

Incorporates these practices into government procurement to ensure AI trustworthiness and conformity with human rights standards.

Defines high-risk AI as those that may impact human rights and safety with likely applications in healthcare, law enforcement and justice, and provision of public benefits.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Assembly Bill 2905 (2024)
document_name: California Assembly Bill 2905 (Telecommunications: automatic dialing-announcing devices: artificial voices) (2024)
body:
Requires a person placing a call through the use of an automatic dialing-announcing device to make an unrecorded, natural voice announcement before using AI-generated voices in calls. Requires person calling to disconnect device upon termination of the call by either the person calling or the person called and defines "artificial intelligence" and "artificial voice."

Amends the Public Utilities Code to regulate the use of automatic dialing-announcing devices in California.

Requires person calling to make a natural voice announcement before using an automatic dialing-announcing device, which includes stating the nature of the call and the business or organization details; inquiring whether the called person consents to hear a prerecorded message; and informing the called person if the message uses an artificial voice.

Requires person calling to disconnect the device after call termination by either party.

Defines the terms “artificial intelligence” and “artificial voice."

category: UN
title: [UN] 글로벌 디지털 협약(미래를 위한 협약 부속문서)
document_name: Global Digital Compact / 「글로벌 디지털 콤팩트」
body:
●기관: 유엔총회(UN General Assembly)
●문서종류: 글로벌 디지털 협력 프레임워크 / 「미래를 위한 협약」 부속문서
●문서명: Global Digital Compact / 「글로벌 디지털 콤팩트」
●채택시점: 2024년 9월 22일
●핵심내용:유엔 「미래를 위한 협약」의 부속문서로 채택된 디지털 협력 및 AI 거버넌스에 관한 포괄적 글로벌 프레임워크임. 193개 유엔 회원국 간 협상을 통해 마련되었으며, 포용적이고 개방적이며 안전하고 보안성 있는 디지털 미래를 목표로 디지털 격차 해소, 디지털 공간의 인권·안전 보장, 데이터 거버넌스 및 AI 국제협력 제도화를 주요 과제로 제시함.
① 문서는 보편적 연결성 확대와 디지털 공공재·인프라 투자를 통해 모든 사람의 디지털 접근성을 높이고, 여성·청년·중소기업의 디지털경제 참여를 지원해야 한다고 제시함
② 온라인 공간에서 인권·아동보호·정보 신뢰성을 강화하고, 상호운용 가능한 데이터 거버넌스와 신뢰 기반 데이터 협력을 발전시킬 필요가 있다고 강조함
③ AI 과학패널·글로벌 대화·역량강화 파트너십과 재원조성 방안을 통해 국제 AI 협력을 강화하고, 개발도상국의 AI 접근성과 활용역량 격차를 완화해야 한다고 제시함

category: UN
title: [UN] 미래를 위한 협약 – 글로벌 디지털 협약 포함(A/RES/79/1)
document_name: The Pact for the Future / 「미래를 위한 협약」
body:
●기관: 유엔총회(UN General Assembly)
●문서종류: 유엔총회 결의 / 미래정상회의 결과문서
●문서명: The Pact for the Future / 「미래를 위한 협약」
●채택시점: 2024년 9월 22일
●핵심내용:유엔총회가 2024년 미래정상회의에서 채택한 정상급 합의문으로, 지속가능발전, 국제평화와 안보, 과학기술혁신과 디지털 협력, 청년과 미래세대, 글로벌 거버넌스 개혁을 포괄하는 다자협력 의제를 제시함. 동 결의는 본문인 「미래를 위한 협약」과 부속문서인 「글로벌 디지털 콤팩트」 및 「미래세대 선언」으로 구성되며, AI를 포함한 디지털 기술이 인권, 지속가능발전, 포용성, 안전성에 부합하도록 국제협력을 강화할 필요성을 강조함.
① 문서는 SDGs 이행·빈곤퇴치·개발재원 확대와 국제금융체제 개혁을 통해 개발도상국의 지속가능발전 기반을 강화해야 한다고 제시함
② 과학기술혁신과 디지털 협력을 핵심 수단으로 보고, 「글로벌 디지털 콤팩트」를 통해 디지털 격차 해소·데이터 거버넌스·AI 국제협력·디지털 인권 보호를 강조함
③ 청년·미래세대의 정책참여와 권익 보호를 강화하고, 안전보장이사회·국제금융기구·다자개발은행 등 글로벌 거버넌스의 대표성·효과성·책임성을 높여야 한다고 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 2681 (Weapons Robotic Devices 2024)
document_name: California AB 2681 (Weapons Robotic Devices 2024)
body:
Prohibits manufacturing, modifying, selling, transferring, or operating weapon-equipped robotic devices. Exempts defense companies, researchers, the Department of Defense, certain competitions, entertainment props, and academic research. Imposes fines of $100-$2,000 for violations. Authorizes government officials to use equipped devices for explosives disposal.

Prohibits the manufacture, modification, sale, transfer, or operation of robotic devices equipped with weapons for general use.

Defines "defense industrial company" and "robotic device" to clarify applicable entities and technologies.

Exempts defense industrial companies engaged with the U.S. Department of Defense and developers modifying devices to prevent unauthorized weaponization.

Excludes the U.S. Department of Defense, nonautonomous devices in supervised competitions, and academic research.

Permits government officials to use such robotic devices for explosive disposal or urgent threat situations.

Specifies infractions are punishable by fines ranging from $100 to $2,000.

Clarifies exclusions for blank-firing weapons used as props in entertainment and media production.

Stipulates no reimbursement required by the act for local agencies or district costs due to the creation or alteration of crimes or infractions.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Senate Bill 942 (2024)
document_name: California AI Transparency Act (2024)
body:
Enacts the California AI Transparency Act, requiring AI providers with over 1 million users to offer free AI detection tools and include clear disclosures in AI-generated content. Establishes enforcement through civil penalties and mandates preservation of disclosure features in licensed products.

Enacts the California AI Transparency Act, requiring covered providers of generative AI systems with significant user bases to offer free AI detection tools that allow users to assess whether image, video, or audio content was created or altered by the provider’s system.

Requires AI-generated content to include both manifest and latent disclosures, identifying it as AI-generated, with details about the provider and system.

Requires ongoing evaluation of AI-detection tools while prohibiting the collection or retention of personal information from detection tool users, except in specific opt-in scenarios.

Mandates disclosure capabilities to be clear and permanent, and demands that licenses for GenAI systems include obligations for content disclosures.

Imposes civil penalties of $5,000 per violation for non-compliance, with each day constituting a separate violation.

Excludes specific entertainment products from applicability and sets the operative date as January 1, 2026.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 2839 (2024)
document_name: California AB 2839 (Election Advertisements)
body:
Prohibits malicious distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated election content, requires disclosures for manipulated media with exclusions for news broadcasts, and allows injunctive relief and damages for violations.

Prohibits the malicious distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated content related to elections, such as deepfakes, during specified periods before and after elections in California. 

Requires candidates who use manipulated media in election communications to include clear disclosures to ensure transparency.

Allows recipients of deceptive content, candidates, or election officials to seek injunctive relief and damages against violators.

Exempts broadcasting stations from liability under certain conditions, such as bona fide news coverage or compliance with existing federal laws.

Applies provisions regardless of language and mandates that disclosures match the language of the advertisement.

Declares the act an urgency clause, making it effective immediately to protect upcoming elections from AI-driven disinformation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 2355 (2024), Section 8
document_name: California AB 2355 (AI in political advertisements), Sec 8
body:
Requires political advertisements generated or altered by AI to disclose “Ad generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence.” Permits enforcement actions for non-compliance. Defines AI-related terms and specifies disclosure methods. Exempts service providers' rights under Section 230.

Requires committees creating or distributing qualified political advertisements to include a disclosure stating, “Ad generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence,” in a clear and conspicuous manner.

Mandates that the disclosure be displayed or spoken as specified in existing sections of the Government Code.

Excludes alteration or negation of rights under Section 230 of Title 47 of the U.S. Code for interactive service providers.

Authorizes the Commission to seek injunctive relief or pursue administrative or civil remedies if committees fail to comply with disclosure requirements.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and specifies conditions under which media is considered "generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence.”

Clarifies that immaterial alterations, such as cosmetic adjustments or resizing, do not qualify as being substantially altered by artificial intelligence.

Specifies that non-compliance does not constitute a misdemeanor.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 1836
document_name: California AB 1836 (Use of likeness: digital replica)
body:
Amends California Civil Code to require consent for using deceased personalities' likenesses in AI-generated replicas. Exempts certain expressive works. Imposes liability for unauthorized use with fines up to $10,000. Specifies consent requirements and transferrable rights for digital likenesses.

Amends the California Civil Code to impose liability on individuals using a deceased personality's likeness without consent, including AI-generated digital replicas. Requires violators to compensate for unauthorized use, with statutory minimums and profit disgorgement. Excludes certain uses such as news, satire, and fleeting references from consent requirements. 

Recognizes posthumous rights as transferable property interests, extending rights to heirs or designated persons. Limits rights duration to 70 years post-death and outlines specific inheritance rules. Mandates registration with the Secretary of State for enforcing claims, making these registrations public records.

Clarifies that certain artistic and informational works are exempt unless they serve commercial product promotion. Outlines exceptions for media owners unless knowingly complicit in unauthorized use. Enforces consistency with existing law by rendering remedies cumulative. Establishes retroactive application of rights back to those deceased before January 1, 1985.

title: [G20] 2024 마세이오 디지털 포용 장관선언
document_name: G20 Maceió Ministerial Declaration on Digital Inclusion for All / 「모두를 위한 디지털 포용에 관한 G20 마세이오 장관선언」
body:
●기관: G20 브라질 의장국
●문서종류: 디지털경제 장관선언 / 장관급 합의문
●문서명: G20 Maceió Ministerial Declaration on Digital Inclusion for All / 「모두를 위한 디지털 포용에 관한 G20 마세이오 장관선언」
●채택시점: 2024년 9월 13일
●핵심내용:2024년 9월 13일 브라질 마세이오에서 개최된 G20 디지털경제 장관회의 결과문서로, 디지털 포용, 보편적·의미 있는 연결성, 디지털정부와 포용적 디지털 공공인프라, 온라인 정보무결성, 포용적 지속가능발전과 불평등 완화를 위한 AI 활용을 핵심 의제로 다룸. 선언문은 인간 중심의 안전하고 신뢰 가능한 디지털경제를 구축하고, 디지털 전환의 혜택이 개발도상국과 취약계층을 포함해 모두에게 확산되도록 국제협력과 역량강화를 강화해야 한다고 강조함.
① 문서는 보편적 연결성과 디지털 공공인프라를 디지털 포용과 공공서비스 혁신의 핵심 기반으로 보고, 접근성·상호운용성·디지털 신원·데이터 공유 등을 강화해야 한다고 제시함
② 온라인 허위정보와 AI 생성 콘텐츠에 대응하기 위해 정보무결성·플랫폼 책임성·콘텐츠 출처확인과 함께 AI의 투명성·감사가능성·인간 감독·인권 보호를 강조함
③ AI와 디지털 격차 완화를 위해 개발도상국의 역량강화·공동연구·기술이전·데이터·컴퓨팅 접근성을 확대하고, 관련 준비도·연결성·디지털 신원 지침을 정책도구로 제시함

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters
document_name: Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters (Proposed Rule)
body:
Creates reporting requirements for covered persons, including quarterly notifications if conducting AI model training or acquiring computing clusters that meet specified computational thresholds and  quarterly affirmations if covered persons have no applicable activities to report.

Requires covered persons to submit quarterly notifications to the BIS if conducting AI model training or acquiring or developing computing clusters that meet specified computational thresholds.

Mandates covered persons to respond to BIS inquiries within 30 days and correct incomplete submissions within 14 days.

Requires covered persons to respond to clarification questions within seven days and mandates quarterly affirmations if covered persons have no applicable activities to report.

Specifies topics that covered persons must address, including information regarding any ongoing or planned activities related to training or developing dual-use foundation models, and the red-team testing results of any developed dual-use foundation model.

Defines key terms, including AI red-teaming, dual-use foundation models, and large-scale computing clusters, for reporting purposes.

category: Editors' Picks;Multinational
title: Consensus Statement on AI Safety as a Global Public Good
document_name: Consensus Statement on AI Safety as a Global Public Good (IDAIS)
body:
Recognizes AI safety as a global public good, urging international cooperation on governance. Calls on states to encourage AI Safety Institutes, emergency preparedness, a Safety Assurance Framework, and independent verification research. Emphasizes global coordination, independent audits, and comprehensive verification of AI safety claims.

Recognizes AI safety as a global public good, urging global governance to mitigate risks from advanced AI systems.

Encourages states and AI developers to commit to foundational principles for responsible AI development, fostering cooperation at intergovernmental summits.

Calls for states to establish and resource AI Safety Institutes to advance testing, research, and standards-setting.

Urges development of domestic authorities to detect and respond to AI incidents, coordinating globally for contingency planning.

Proposes Emergency Preparedness Agreements and Institutions for model registration, incident reporting, and contingency plans.

Establishes a Safety Assurance Framework requiring developers to demonstrate AI safety before deployment.

Calls for post-deployment monitoring and independent audits to ensure AI systems' safety.

Calls for independent global AI safety and verification research, funded by a diverse range of stakeholders.

Encourages international collaboration to develop verification methods, enabling credible safety claims and fostering trust.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California AB 1777 (Autonomous vehicles)
document_name: California AB 1777 (Autonomous vehicles)
body:
Regulates autonomous vehicles in California, requiring Department of Motor Vehicles approval before public road operation and certification of safety compliance. Imposes insurance requirements and allows emergency geofencing. Sets mandates for vehicle override and communication with emergency officials. Specifies compliance with federal law.

Amends California's Vehicle Code to regulate autonomous vehicles (AVs) with Level 3, 4, or 5 autonomy according to SAE standards.

Requires manufacturers to submit applications for AV operation on public roads, which must be approved by the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) based on compliance with safety and technical standards.

Mandates a $5 million insurance, bond, or self-insurance for testing and operation.

Instructs the DMV to establish regulations for AV safety, testing, and compliance monitoring.

Requires manufacturers to maintain emergency response capabilities, including a dedicated phone line and remote vehicle control for emergency response officials.

Obligates manufacturers to provide disclosure on data collection and comply with emergency geofencing directives.

Clarifies noncompliance notice procedures without presuming AV safety failure, requiring manufacturers to report notices to the DMV within 72 hours.

Specifies provisions for zero-emission AVs starting in 2030 and sets additional requirements for vehicles over 10,001 pounds.

category: 기타
title: [유럽평의회] AI·인권·민주주의·법치에 관한 기본협약
document_name: The Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law / 「인공지능과 인권, 민주주의 및 법치에 관한 기본협약」
body:
●기관: 유럽평의회(Council of Europe)
●문서종류: 국제협약 / AI·인권·민주주의·법치에 관한 법적 구속력 있는 조약
●문서명: The Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law / 「인공지능과 인권, 민주주의 및 법치에 관한 기본협약」
●채택시점: 2024년 5월 17일
●서명개방: 2024년 9월 5일
●핵심내용:유럽평의회가 마련한 AI 분야 최초의 법적 구속력 있는 국제조약으로, AI 시스템의 생애주기 전반이 인권, 민주주의, 법치와 부합하도록 보장하는 것을 목표로 함. 동 협약은 기술 자체를 세부적으로 규제하기보다 기술중립적 방식으로 기본원칙, 절차적 권리, 위험·영향관리, 이행점검 체계를 제시함.
① 협약은 AI 생애주기 전반에서 인간 존엄·자율성·평등·비차별·프라이버시·투명성·책임성·안전성을 보장해야 한다고 제시함
② AI 사용과 결정에 대한 문서화·고지·이의제기·불복절차를 보장하고, 인권·민주주의·법치에 미치는 영향을 반복적으로 평가해 예방·완화 조치를 마련하도록 요구함
③ 당사국은 특정 AI 활용에 금지·일시중지 등 레드라인을 도입할 수 있으며, 당사국총회를 통해 협약 이행을 점검하고 이해관계자 협력을 촉진하도록 제시함

category: UN
title: [UNESCO] 교원용 AI 역량 프레임워크
document_name: AI Competency Framework for Teachers / 「교원용 AI 역량 프레임워크」
body:
●기관: UNESCO
●문서종류: 역량 프레임워크 / 교사 AI 역량 지침
●문서명: AI Competency Framework for Teachers / 「교원용 AI 역량 프레임워크」
●발표시점: 2024년 9월
●핵심내용:UNESCO가 AI 시대에 교사가 갖추어야 할 지식, 기술, 가치, 태도를 체계화한 글로벌 역량 프레임워크임. 동 문서는 교사의 권리 보호, 인간 행위성 강화, 지속가능성 증진을 원칙으로 하며, 국가별 교사 역량체계, 교원양성, 현직교사 연수, 평가기준 설계에 활용할 수 있는 국제 참고틀을 제시함.
① 문서는 교사의 AI 역량을 인간 중심 사고·AI 윤리·AI 기초와 응용·AI 교수법·전문성 개발의 5개 차원으로 제시함
② 교사 역량을 습득·심화·창조의 3단계로 구분하고, AI가 교사를 대체하기보다 전문성과 인간 중심 교육을 보완하도록 활용해야 한다고 강조함
③ 국가 AI 교육과정·교원양성·교사 연수·역량평가 도구 개발에 활용할 수 있는 글로벌 기준으로 제시함

●발표시점: 2024년 9월
●핵심내용:G20 브라질 의장국의 디지털경제작업반 소개자료로, 연결성, 디지털정부, 정보무결성, 인공지능을 2024년 디지털경제 의제의 핵심 주제로 제시함. 디지털 전환을 포용적 사회경제 발전과 공공참여 확대의 수단으로 보고, 디지털 접근성 격차와 AI 역량·데이터·인프라 집중 문제를 주요 정책과제로 다룸.

③ AI 분야에서는 생성형 AI의 윤리적·책임 있는 활용과 함께 역량·데이터·인프라가 소수에 집중돼 언어·문화·인종·지역 다양성이 충분히 반영되지 않는 문제를 지적함

category: Editors' Picks;Chinese law and policy
title: AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC)
document_name: AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (TC260)
body:
Establishes principles for AI safety governance and promotes a people-centered approach to AI governance and emphasizes stakeholder cooperation to prevent AI safety risks and outlines safety guidelines.

Establishes principles for AI safety governance, emphasizing a balance between development and security and involving all stakeholders in a coordinated approach.

Explains AI safety risks, including risks from algorithms, risks from data, and cybersecurity risks.

Implements the Global AI Governance Initiative and promotes consensus and coordinated efforts. 

Supports the formulation and refinement of governance, and tracks trends in AI research, development, and application; with a focus on agile governance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: North Carolina State Government Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Framework
document_name: North Carolina Government Responsible Use of AI Framework
body:
Require state agencies to follow the AI Framework, which emphasizes principles such as human oversight, transparency, security, data privacy, diversity, auditing, and workforce empowerment. Obligate agencies to maintain AI inventories and conduct risk assessments using the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

Establishes the North Carolina State Government Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Framework to ensure ethical AI application across state agencies.

Requires state agencies to follow guidelines which emphasize human-centered AI with oversight ensuring AI use benefits citizens without negatively impacting rights or access to services.

Stipulates transparency, requiring agencies to notify individuals of AI use and its impacts in accessible language.

Mandates robust security measures, ongoing monitoring, and risk assessments to ensure the safety and effectiveness of AI systems.

Demands strict data privacy controls throughout AI lifecycle stages and promotes equitable AI development free from biases.

Insists on accountability where agencies must audit AI use and provide necessary training to personnel.

Empowers staff through AI training to maximize public service effectiveness.

Requires agencies to maintain an AI inventory, report it for transparency, and conduct risk assessments using NIST AI RMF guided by state offices for comprehensive risk management.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Public Act 103-0804
document_name: Illinois Public Act 103-0804
body:
Prohibits employers in Illinois from using AI in employment practices that result in discrimination based on protected classes. Requires employers to notify employees when AI is used for employment decisions. Mandates rule adoption for implementation and enforcement. Effective January 1, 2026.

Amends the Illinois Human Rights Act to regulate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in employment-related decisions.

Prohibits employers from using AI in recruitment, hiring, promotion, or other employment practices if it results in discrimination based on protected classes.

Requires employers to notify employees if AI is used in employment decisions.

Mandates the Illinois Department of Human Rights to adopt rules for implementing these AI-related provisions, including specifying conditions and timelines for providing notice.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system generating outputs like predictions or decisions that can influence environments.

Includes "generative artificial intelligence" as systems producing content simulating human-produced content based on prompts.

Takes effect on January 1, 2026.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois House Bill 4875
document_name: Illinois HB 4875 (Publicity Act)
body:
Amends the Right of Publicity Act to regulate AI-generated digital replicas, prohibiting unauthorized commercial use without consent. Establishes liability for knowingly distributing such replicas. Exempts certain uses, like news or satire. Applies protections for 50 years posthumously. Effective January 1, 2025.

Amends the Right of Publicity Act in Illinois to define "artificial intelligence" as systems that generate outputs influencing environments, including generative AI.

Defines "digital replica" as an electronic representation of an individual created using AI without their actual participation.

Prohibits the use of an individual's identity or digital replica for commercial purposes without consent during their lifetime and for 50 years posthumously.

Restricts the distribution of works containing unauthorized digital replicas without consent.

Exempts certain uses, such as in news, political campaigns, or works of public interest, unless they falsely create the impression of authenticity.

Incorporates elements from federal law to exempt certain service providers from liability if they act to remove unauthorized replicas upon gaining knowledge.

Applies to acts occurring after January 1, 2025, excluding ongoing or prior legal actions.

title: [개인정보보호위원회] 인공지능 개발,서비스를 위한 공개된 개인정보 처리 안내서

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Hawaii Senate Bill 2284 (Relating To A Wildfire Forecast System For Hawaii)
document_name: Hawaii SB 2284 (Relating To A Wildfire Forecast System For Hawaii)
body:
Requires the University of Hawaii to establish a two-year program using AI to develop a wildfire forecast system. Appropriates $1,000,000 for this purpose. Mandates reporting on program effectiveness and recommendations before the 2026 legislative session.

Mandates the University of Hawaii to establish a two-year program for developing a wildfire forecast system using artificial intelligence.

Requires the system to forecast wildfire risks statewide to enhance public safety and improve preparedness and risk mitigation measures.

Obligates the University of Hawaii to report on the program's effectiveness and provide findings, recommendations, and any proposed legislation to the legislature before the 2026 regular session.

Appropriates $1,000,000 from the state's general revenues for fiscal year 2024-2025 to fund the development of the wildfire forecast system.

Specifies that the Act will take effect on July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Hampshire House Bill 1596
document_name: New Hampshire HB 1596 (AI Usage in Political Advertising)
body:
Prohibits the distribution of deceptive AI-generated deepfakes in political advertising within 90 days of an election unless clear disclosures are provided, and establishes civil remedies and exemptions for specific actors and contexts

Prohibits the distribution of deepfake content created using artificial intelligence or generative AI within 90 days of an election if it involves candidates, election officials, or parties.

Exempts from the prohibition any media that includes a clear disclosure indicating manipulation by AI, specifying whether it is an image, video, or audio, with requirements for disclosures to be easily readable or audible based on the media type.

Allows affected candidates or election officials to seek legal action for injunctive relief or damages.

Excludes liability for platforms providing content from third parties, individuals unaware of the deepfake nature, and excludes satire or parody content that doesn't rely on AI.

title: [G20] 2024 브라질 DEWG AI 개발 동향 분석
document_name: Mapping the Development, Deployment and Adoption of AI for Enhanced Public Services in the G20 Members / 「G20 회원국의 공공서비스 고도화를 위한 AI 개발·배치·도입 현황 분석」
body:
●기관: G20 브라질 의장국
●문서종류: 정책보고서 / G20 회원국 공공부문 AI 활용 현황 분석

●핵심내용:G20 브라질 의장국이 2024년 디지털경제 의제 중 “포용적 지속가능발전과 불평등 완화를 위한 AI” 논의를 뒷받침하기 위해 마련한 정책보고서임. G20 회원국의 공공부문 AI 개발·배치·도입 사례를 비교하고, 공공서비스 개선을 위한 AI 활용 가능성과 함께 거버넌스, 역량, 인프라, 데이터, 신뢰성 확보 과제를 제시함.
① G20 공공부문에서 AI가 행정·보건·교육·복지·조세·교통 등 다양한 서비스의 접근성·효율성·대응성 향상에 활용되고 있다고 분석함
② 공공부문 AI 도입을 위해 고품질 데이터·상호운용 인프라·컴퓨팅·전문인력·조달역량·법제도가 필요하며, 투명성·설명가능성·책임성·개인정보 보호·인간 감독을 보장해야 한다고 강조함
③ G20 회원국 간 모범사례 공유·역량강화·공동연구·개발도상국 지원을 통해 포용적이고 책임 있는 AI 활용을 촉진하고, 이를 지속가능발전과 불평등 완화의 정책수단으로 제시함

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Section 106.11 Application: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
document_name: Section 106.11 Application: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
body:
Declines to expand examples of conduct under sex-based harassment regulations to include AI technologies, but reinforces responsibility for conduct within a recipient's disciplinary authority, including off-campus and online activities. Clarifies Title IX obligations for addressing hostile environments linked to education programs.

Requires recipients to address sex-based harassment within their education programs or activities, including off-campus and remote settings, aligning with recent court decisions.

Clarifies that institutions are responsible for discrimination within contexts they control, such as AI technologies used in educational settings.

Acknowledges requests for examples involving AI and other specific circumstances but declines to provide additional examples or exhaustive lists.

Confirms obligations for conduct during institution-sponsored events, online classes, and use of digital platforms, including AI technologies.

Deletes references to sex-based harassment occurring outside the U.S. but maintains the obligation to address contributing conduct external to the program or activity.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Louisiana Senate Bill 6
document_name: Louisiana SB 6 (Unlawful Dissemination of AI Images)
body:
Enacts a law criminalizing the intentional dissemination or sale of AI-generated nude images of identifiable individuals without authorization. Exempts certain service providers from liability. Defines "another person" as a recognizable individual depicted in the images.

Enacts R.S. 14:73.14 to criminalize the unlawful dissemination or sale of AI-generated images depicting nudity without authorization, with intent to coerce, harass, or intimidate.

Defines the crime as involving images where the distributor knows they lack the authority to distribute or sell the images.

Exempts interactive computer services and providers of telecommunications or information services from liability if their systems are used for such acts by others.

Defines "another person" as someone whose recognizable image is used in creating AI-generated content meant to depict a real individual.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence Part 1: Digital Replicas July 2024
document_name: Copyright Office Part 1 Digital Replicas 2024
body:
Recommends Congress establish a federal right to protect individuals from unauthorized digital replicas, make the right licensable but not assignable with civil remedies, apply secondary liability with conditioned safe harbor for OSPs, include First Amendment accommodations, avoid full preemption of state publicity rights, and rely on the Copyright Office as a resource for Congress and other branches in considering these recommendations and future developments

Recommends that Congress establish a federal right to protect individuals from the distribution of unauthorized digital replicas during their lifetimes. 

Proposes that this right be licensable and subject to guardrails but not assignable, with remedies such as monetary damages and injunctive relief available. 

Recommends applying traditional rules of secondary liability, with a safe harbor for online service providers suitably conditioned.

Suggests explicit First Amendment accommodations in the law.

Advises against full preemption of state laws, recognizing well-developed state rights of publicity. 

Offers the Copyright Office as a resource for Congress, the courts, and the executive branch in implementing these recommendations and addressing future developments.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Michigan House Bill 5507
document_name: Michigan H 5507 (School Aid)
body:
Allocates $500,000 for a statewide AI research hub, enhancing expertise on responsible AI use in schools. Supports virtual education, best practices, and policy recommendations. Fosters innovation in instructional technology and virtual learning models for Michigan's education system.

Allocates up to $500,000 to enhance awareness and responsible use of artificial intelligence in schools.

Requires Michigan Virtual University to integrate AI principles in its training programs for educational personnel.

Mandates the Michigan Virtual Learning Research Institute to research and recommend virtual education delivery models leveraging AI.

Instructs the institute to analyze and report on AI-enhanced virtual learning effectiveness by reviewing data from virtual course providers.

Encourages partnerships with districts to study AI-driven competency-based virtual learning models.

Tasks the institute with policy recommendations to the governor on AI and virtual learning implementation.

Designates funds for AI-related professional development programs for educators and stakeholders.

Requires ongoing reports on the implementation of AI in virtual education, including its effectiveness, with a focus on elevating education delivery models in Michigan.

Supports the dissemination of best practices and standards for AI-integrated virtual learning across the state.

title: [미국] AI 위험관리 프레임워크: 생성형 AI 프로파일 (NIST AI 600-1)

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Jersey Senate Bill 3432
document_name: New Jersey S 3432 (Next New Jersey Program Act)
body:
Establishes the "Next New Jersey Program Act" promoting AI development by granting tax credits to eligible AI businesses. Requires capital investments in AI facilities, job creation, and collaboration with NJ-based institutions. Mandates compliance with sustainability standards, prevailing wages, and regulatory requirements. Limits apply to tax credit value and duration.

Establishes the "Next New Jersey Program" to drive investment into New Jersey’s AI sector, creating jobs and economic opportunities.

Requires businesses to invest a minimum of $100 million in capital and create at least 100 new full-time jobs to be eligible for tax credits.

Mandates businesses or divisions engaged in AI or large-scale AI data centers, demonstrating over 50% of revenue or employment in AI activities.

Stipulates collaboration with New Jersey-based research entities or startups.

Enforces compliance with environmental and labor standards, including prevailing wage for construction workers.

Enables businesses meeting criteria to apply for tax credits valid until March 1, 2029.

Empowers the New Jersey Economic Development Authority to oversee eligibility and award decisions, ensuring businesses remain compliant to retain credits.

Allows tax credit transfer certificates, with conditions on their sale and application.

Caps overall tax credits under the act at $250 million annually from a broader $11.5 billion limit across various programs over nine years.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Massachusetts House Bill 4885
document_name: Massachusetts H 4885 (Firearm Laws), Section 148
body:
Establishes a special legislative commission to investigate emerging firearm technologies, including the risks and impacts of using digital firearm manufacturing code for machine learning and AI. Requires a report with findings and recommendations by March 1, 2025.

Establishes a special legislative commission to study emerging firearm technology, including personalized and microstamp technologies.

Requires the commission to evaluate the risks associated with using digital firearm manufacturing codes for machine learning and artificial intelligence.

Mandates the investigation of the accuracy, effectiveness, and utility of personalized firearm and microstamp technologies.

Instructs the commission to review any legal or constitutional issues relating to these technologies.

Tasks the commission with evaluating the commercial availability of these technologies for new and existing firearms.

Directs the commission to assess the feasibility and utility of a tax incentive program for personalized firearm technology.

Obliges the commission to submit its study and recommendations, including legislative suggestions, by March 1, 2025.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2025 Action Plan (Turkey)
document_name: National AI Strategy 2024-2025 Action Plan (Turkey)
body:
Implements mechanisms to attract AI talent, including increased support for AI research and education. Develops national occupational AI standards and vocational training and expands AI data infrastructures, international cooperation, and regulatory frameworks to enhance the AI workforce.

Implements mechanisms under the TechVisa Program to attract AI talents to Turkey.

Increases support for international research and doctoral programs to bolster AI workforce competence.

Coordinates curriculum updates to include AI and data science across non-AI scientific fields.

Establishes associate, undergraduate, and graduate AI degree programs based on workforce analysis.

Provides AI training post-education tailored to sectoral applications for workforce development.

Sets standards for private AI certification training programs.

Launches advanced analytics and AI training for public personnel competence.

Develops national occupational standards and qualifications in AI with relevant infrastructure.

Establishes ethical and technical standards for locally developed generative AI models.

Supports the development of a Turkish large language model in collaboration with the international community.

Creates a "Legal Assessment Guide for AI Applications" to ensure legal compliance of AI. 

Designs a customized AI education model to support workforce transformation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Hampshire H1688 (2024)
document_name: New Hampshire H1688 (AI Use By State Agencies)
body:
Prohibits state agencies from using AI for unlawful discrimination, public surveillance without a warrant, and malicious deepfakes. Requires human review for irreversible AI decisions. Mandates disclosure for AI-generated content. Ensures compliance via audits and annual reporting to authorities.

Define "artificial intelligence," "generative AI," "deepfake," and "state agency" in relation to AI governance.

Apply provisions to all state agency computer systems, with exceptions for research and personal use systems.

Prohibit uses by state agencies for classifying individuals leading to discrimination, surveillance in public spaces without a warrant, and malicious use of deepfakes.

Allow AI use with human oversight on irreversible decisions, disclosure of AI-generated content, and informing users of AI interactions.

Require state agencies to review AI use, modify inconsistent procedures, and document compliance within nine months, reporting to the department of information technology.

Mandate annual reporting and updates on AI system compliance and procurement to key government officials and public posting on the department website.

Sever provisions to ensure remaining regulations remain in effect if parts are invalidated.

Enact the chapter on July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Hampshire House Bill 1432
document_name: New Hampshire HB 1432 (Deepfakes)
body:
Prohibits knowingly creating or distributing deepfakes for harm. Establishes civil claims for damages from such use. Exempts bona fide news, satire, or parody. Disallows lobbyist registration for convicted offenders. Effective January 1, 2025.

Prohibits the creation, distribution, or presentation of deepfakes intended to embarrass, harass, entrap, defame, extort, or harm reputations or finances, categorizing such acts as a class B felony.

Establishes an additional offense and liability for legal expenses if the deepfake results in an individual's arrest.

Exempts interactive services, media entities engaged in bona fide news reporting, election communications with appropriate disclaimers, and satire or parody from these prohibitions.

Allows individuals to sue those who knowingly create harmful deepfakes for damages.

Mandates that the secretary of state reject lobbyist registrations from entities convicted of deepfake-related offenses.

Specifies that provisions are severable, ensuring unaffected provisions remain enforceable if any part is invalidated.

Sets the act's effective date as January 1, 2025, following its approval on July 19, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Idaho House Bill 2472
document_name: Idaho HB 2472 (Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act), Sec. 30
body:
Requires utilization review programs using algorithmic processes to ensure clinical peers make adverse determinations, comply with accreditation standards, and include policies for algorithm verification. Establishes registration every two years with proof of compliance. Sets appeal procedures for adverse determinations.

Amends the Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act to require utilization review programs using algorithmic automated processes to ensure that only clinical peers make adverse determinations based on medical necessity.

Mandates these programs to register with the Department of Insurance every two years and provide proof of compliance with Health Utilization Management Standards or equivalent standards.

Requires licensed physicians with relevant board certifications to establish criteria for these automated processes and verify their accuracy.

Obliges health care plans to have appeals procedures, allowing appeals to be filed orally or in writing, with decisions rendered within specified timeframes.

Ensures confidentiality of patient-specific information obtained during utilization reviews, restricting access to authorized individuals.

Permits adverse determination appeals to an external independent review, with potential further appeals to the Department if found arbitrary or capricious.

Authorizes the Department to issue corrective actions or cease and desist orders for non-compliance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Delaware House Bill 333
document_name: Delaware  H 333  (Artificial Intelligence Commission )
body:
Establishes the Delaware AI Commission to recommend AI-related legislative and executive actions, develop guidelines, encourage AI use in agencies, and ensure AI safety and rights compliance. Requires an annual report and conducts a Generative AI inventory. Expires in 10 years.

Establishes the Delaware Artificial Intelligence (AI) Commission to make legislative and executive recommendations on AI.

Mandates the development of statewide AI processes, principles, and guidelines for government agencies.

Encourages the use of AI in agencies to improve service delivery and ensures AI usage does not violate individual rights.

Requires an inventory of Generative AI use within state agencies to identify high-risk areas.

Comprises a 19-member commission, with appointments from state officials, academia, and the private sector.

Requires the commission to submit an annual report on activities, goals, and policy recommendations.

Places the commission within the Department of Technology and Information, with staffing support from the Chief Information Officer.

Sets an expiration of the Act 10 years after enactment unless extended by the General Assembly.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Hampshire House Bill 1688
document_name: New Hampshire HB 1688 (AI Use By State Agencies)
body:
Establishes rules governing state agency use of AI, including prohibiting discriminatory and surveillance uses, and requires human review of irreversible AI decisions, with disclosures of AI-generated content.

Prohibits state agencies from using AI to classify individuals based on behavior, socio-economic status, or personal characteristics if it results in unlawful discrimination.

Bans real-time and remote biometric identification systems for public surveillance, except by law enforcement with a warrant.

Mandates human review of AI-generated, irreversible recommendations or decisions before implementation.

Requires disclosure for content generated by generative AI if not reviewed by a human.

Obligates state agencies to review AI use for compliance within nine months, align procedures with the chapter and ethics code, and remove prohibited AI systems, ensuring new AI deployments comply with regulations.

Directs the Department of Information Technology to report annually on AI systems used by state agencies, noting compliance and changes.

category: 기타
title: [WAIC] 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 상하이 선언
document_name: Shanghai Declaration on Global AI Governance / 「글로벌 AI 거버넌스에 관한 상하이 선언」
body:
●기관: 2024 세계인공지능대회(WAIC) / 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 고위급회의
●문서종류: 선언문 / 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 원칙 문서
●문서명: Shanghai Declaration on Global AI Governance / 「글로벌 AI 거버넌스에 관한 상하이 선언」
●발표시점: 2024년 7월 4일
●핵심내용:2024 세계인공지능대회(WAIC) 및 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 고위급회의에서 발표된 AI 거버넌스 선언문임. AI의 발전과 활용을 촉진하되 안전성, 신뢰성, 통제 가능성, 공정성을 함께 확보해야 한다는 원칙을 제시하고, 유엔 중심의 글로벌 AI 거버넌스 체계와 개발도상국의 대표성 확대를 강조함.
① 문서는 의료·교육·교통·농업·산업·환경 등 다양한 분야에서 AI 연구개발과 활용을 확대하고, 인프라·기술이전·고품질 데이터 협력을 통해 글로벌 AI 발전 기반을 강화해야 한다고 제시함
② AI 안전을 위해 데이터·개인정보 보호, 위험기반 시험·평가, 기술윤리 심사, 사이버보안, 허위정보 대응 등을 강화해야 한다고 강조함
③ 유엔 중심의 글로벌 AI 거버넌스와 개발도상국의 참여를 확대하고, 공공참여·AI 문해력·남북·남남협력을 통해 포용적이고 지속가능한 AI 활용을 촉진해야 한다고 제시함

category: GPAI
title: [GPAI] 2024 뉴델리 선언, GPAI·OECD 통합 파트너십 출범
document_name: 2024 GPAI New Delhi Declaration / 「2024 GPAI 뉴델리 선언」
body:
●기관: GPAI
●문서종류: 각료선언 / GPAI-OECD 통합 파트너십 합의문
●문서명: 2024 GPAI New Delhi Declaration / 「2024 GPAI 뉴델리 선언」
●채택시점: 2024년 7월 3~4일
●핵심내용:2024년 7월 3~4일 인도 뉴델리에서 개최된 GPAI 정상회의 계기 채택된 각료선언으로, GPAI와 OECD의 통합 파트너십 구축을 공식화한 문서임. 동 선언은 GPAI의 독립적 정체성과 다중이해관계자 성격을 유지하면서, OECD AI 권고에 기반해 모든 OECD 회원국과 GPAI 참여국이 동등한 기반에서 협력하는 새로운 운영모델을 제시함.
① 문서는 AI의 지속가능발전·사회경제적 잠재력을 인정하면서도 안전·허위정보·편향·개인정보·아동복지·환경·일자리 전환 등 다양한 위험을 함께 관리해야 한다고 강조함
② OECD AI 권고와 UNESCO AI 윤리 권고를 재확인하고, GPAI를 OECD와 통합된 파트너십으로 운영하되 GPAI 브랜드와 회원 간 동등한 참여구조를 유지하도록 제시함
③ GPAI의 다중이해관계자 전문가 네트워크를 강화하고, 디지털 격차 해소와 신뢰 가능한 AI 촉진 및 G20·G7·히로시마 AI 프로세스 등 국제 이니셔티브와의 협력 강화를 제시함

category: 중국
title: [중국] 국가 AI 산업 종합 표준화 체계 구축 지침 2024년판
document_name: 《国家人工智能产业综合标准化体系建设指南（2024版）》/ 「국가 인공지능 산업 종합 표준화 체계 구축 지침 2024년판」
body:
●국가: 중국
●기관: 공업정보화부·중앙인터넷정보판공실·국가발전개혁위원회·국가표준화관리위원회
●문서종류: 국가 표준화 지침
●문서명: 《国家人工智能产业综合标准化体系建设指南（2024版）》/ 「국가 인공지능 산업 종합 표준화 체계 구축 지침 2024년판」
●발표시점: 2024년 7월 3일
●핵심내용AI 산업 전반의 표준체계 구축을 위한 국가 차원의 표준화 로드맵. 2026년까지 국가·산업표준 50건 이상, 국제표준 참여 20건 이상을 목표로 제시함.
