category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Hawaii Senate Bill 2687
document_name: Hawaii SB 2687 (Deceptive Media)
body:
Prohibits reckless distribution of materially deceptive media using AI during elections. Exempts certain broadcasters and services and requires disclaimers for manipulated media. Establishes criminal penalties and civil remedies for violations.

Prohibits the reckless distribution of materially deceptive media, including deepfake and generative AI content, during election periods, to protect candidates' reputations and electoral prospects.

Establishes criminal penalties for violations, including petty misdemeanors, misdemeanors for repeat offenses, and class C felonies for intent to cause violence or harm.

Allows exceptions for broadcasters and online services that did not create the deceptive media, or if disclaimers indicate manipulation.

Mandates that disclaimers must be clearly visible and in the same language as the media, with specific requirements for video, image, and audio content.

Provides civil remedies for individuals or organizations harmed by deceptive media, including damages, attorney's fees, and injunctive relief.

Empowers the attorney general, campaign spending commission, and other authorities to enforce these provisions and seek injunctions.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and "materially deceptive media" for clarity and enforcement purposes.

category: UN
title: [UN] AI 역량강화에 관한 국제협력 증진(A/RES/78/311)
document_name: Enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence / 「인공지능 역량강화에 관한 국제협력 증진」
body:
●기관: 유엔 총회
●문서종류: 결의안 / AI 역량강화 국제협력 결의
●문서명: Enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence / 「인공지능 역량강화에 관한 국제협력 증진」
●채택시점: 2024년 7월 1일
●핵심내용:동 결의는 개발도상국의 AI 역량강화를 위한 국제협력을 확대하고, 국가 간·국가 내 AI 및 디지털 격차를 해소하기 위해 채택된 유엔 총회 결의임. 결의는 AI가 지속가능발전목표(SDGs) 달성과 경제·사회·환경 발전을 촉진할 수 있지만, 부적절하거나 악의적인 설계·개발·배치·사용은 위험을 초래할 수 있다고 보고, 안전하고 보안성이 있으며 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 시스템을 인권과 국제법에 부합하게 활용해야 한다고 강조함.
① 결의는 AI·디지털 격차 해소와 개발도상국의 AI 역량강화를 핵심 목표로 설정하고, 국제협력·재정 등을 각국의 개발계획과 연계하도록 권고함
② AI는 인간중심적·신뢰 가능·설명 가능·윤리적·포용적으로 개발·활용되어야 하며, 전 생애주기에서 인권과 국제법을 준수해야 한다고 강조함
③ 정책교류·기술이전·인력훈련·공동연구·오픈소스 AI·디지털 공공인프라 등을 활용한 역량강화를 추진하고, 다언어·문화 다양성 보호와 알고리즘 편향 대응을 강화하도록 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah Senate Bill 131 Information Technology Act Amendments (2024)
document_name: Utah SB 131 (Information Technology Act Amendments)
body:
Requires disclosures for synthetic media in political communications, including AI-generated content labels and tamper-evident digital provenance. Imposes penalties for violations. Considers AI use in crimes as an aggravating sentencing factor. Effective May 1, 2024; sentencing provisions effective July 1, 2024.

Enacts requirements for disclosure of synthetic media generated by AI in election-related communications, effective May 1, 2024. 

Mandates audio communications with synthetic audio to state, "Contains content generated by AI," at both the beginning and end. 

Requires visual communications with synthetic media to display phrases such as "This content generated by AI" throughout the video or image. 

Imposes a requirement for creators and sponsors to include tamper-evident digital content provenance in online advertisements, detailing the creators, edits, and AI usage.

Allows civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.

Considers the intentional use of AI as an aggravating factor in criminal sentencing, effective July 1, 2024. 

Permits judges and parole boards to regard AI-assisted crime as an aggravating factor during sentencing. 

Maintains judicial discretion in sentencing decisions despite AI-related aggravating factors.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois HB 4844 (2024), Section 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force")
document_name: Illinois HB 4844, Sec 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force")
body:
Directs the Illinois Department of Innovation and Technology to establish a Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force to investigate and report on generative AI and natural language processing software.

Amends the Illinois Department of Innovation and Technology Act to establish a Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force within the Department of Innovation and Technology.

Investigates generative AI and natural language processing software and producing a report on findings.

Specifies the composition of the Task Force, which includes legislative appointees from both chambers and both parties, with the Speaker of the House and Senate President appointees serving as co-chairs.

Includes a range of state officials as members, including the Secretary of Innovation and Technology, State Superintendent of Education, heads of the Illinois Community College Board and Board of Higher Education, and the Attorney General.

Includes Governor-appointed members representing teachers, principals, cybersecurity experts, AI experts, statewide business associations, and statewide labor associations, as well as the Statewide Chief Information Security Officer.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Idaho House Bill 575
document_name: Idaho HB 575 (Disclosing Explicit Synthetic Media)
body:
Criminalizes disclosing or threatening to disclose explicit synthetic media without consent if it causes distress, is intended to harass, or is used for blackmail. Defines terms, provides penalties, and exemptions. Excludes certain services from liability unless they aid disclosure of explicit synthetic material.

Establishes the crime of disclosing or threatening to disclose explicit synthetic media without consent, intending to cause distress or obtain valuables, punishable as a misdemeanor or felony for repeat offenders.

Defines "explicit synthetic media" as AI-altered images or videos depicting sexual conduct involving identifiable individuals without their engagement.

Exempts disclosures for lawful purposes, such as criminal investigations, public interest reporting, scientific research, or legal proceedings.

Excludes liability for interactive computer services and telecommunications providers for third-party content, unless they intentionally aid disclosures.

Declares provisions severable, ensuring unaffected sections remain valid if parts are invalidated.

Declares an emergency and sets the effective date for July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York Senate Bill 9678
document_name: New York SB 9678 (Materially Deceptive Media in Political Communications)
body:
Amends election law to require disclosure of materially deceptive media in political communications. Exempts satire, parody, and certain news reporting. Allows candidates to seek legal remedies if their likeness is used deceptively. Establishes burden of proof for plaintiffs.

Amends the election law to require disclosure for political communications using materially deceptive media.

Mandates visual disclosures to be legibly printed, stating "This (image, video, or audio) has been manipulated."

Requires audio disclosures to be stated clearly at the beginning, end, and periodically for messages longer than two minutes.

Exempts satire, bona fide news reporting with clear disclosures, stations with consistent disclaimer requirements, and platforms disseminating third-party content in good faith.

Permits candidates depicted in deceptive media to seek legal relief, including court costs, attorney fees, and injunctions against unauthorized dissemination.

Grants courts authority to provide preliminary relief to plaintiffs likely to succeed in proving violations in upcoming elections.

Places the burden of proof on plaintiffs to establish use of deceptive media by clear and convincing evidence.

Clarifies that federal law takes precedence over state requirements for media labeling in political communications.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Jersey Assembly Resolution 141 (2024)
document_name: New Jersey AR 141 (2024)
body:
Urges AI platforms to voluntarily prevent and remove deepfake and cheapfake content. Requires transmission of this resolution to AI company CEOs in New Jersey. Highlights harmful impacts of altered media and suggests responsible AI use offers societal benefits.

Urges platforms generating and disseminating deepfake and cheapfake media to voluntarily commit to preventing and removing harmful content.

Defines deepfakes as media that appears to depict authentic speech or conduct through substantial technical means, and cheapfakes as any software-generated audiovisual alteration.

Notes that generative AI platforms can anticipate and prevent the creation of harmful content, with social media and content-sharing forums capable of taking steps to remove such media.

Recognizes the potential negative impact, including impersonation, fraud, and political misinformation, while acknowledging the promise of AI if used responsibly.

Encourages the development of AI accountability and transparency standards, following examples set by the federal government and other states.

Calls for New Jersey to become a leader in responsible media technology through these voluntary commitments.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: City of San Jose Artificial Intelligence Policy 1.7.12
document_name: San Jose AI Policy 1.7.12
body:
Defines roles for AI governance, requiring San José to align AI usage with security and privacy policies. Prohibits real-time biometric identification, emotion analysis, and social scoring. Requires an AI review, technical documentation, and immediate reporting of harmful incidents. Enforces policy compliance with potential disciplinary actions.

Establishes a governance framework for AI use in San José, aligning with the City’s data security, privacy, and existing policies.

Directs the Chief Information Officer (CIO) to manage the AI Handbook, with the City Information Security Officer (CISO) and City Digital Privacy Officer (CDPO) ensuring system security, resilience, privacy, and policy compliance.

Requires users to uphold guiding principles such as effectiveness, transparency, equity, accountability, privacy, and security.

Prohibits AI applications involving real-time biometric identification, emotion analysis, fully automated impactful decisions, social scoring, and cognitive manipulation.

Mandates reporting AI-caused harm within 24 hours.

Implements sunset procedures for outdated AI systems.

Obliges compliance with public records laws and City’s transparency policies.

Enforces policy adherence, with violations subject to disciplinary action.

Requires Finance to obtain AI usage disclosures in procurement.

Defines AI and related system terms within the policy context.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence Regulation in Ukraine: Vision of the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine 2024
document_name: White Paper on AI Regulation in Ukraine 2024 (Stages 1 and 2)
body:
Supports the development of tools to help businesses and the state prepare for future regulation, including a methodology to assess AI's impact on human rights; proposes creating general and sectoral AI recommendations and voluntary codes of conduct; calls for the gradual implementation of EU regulation and the creation of an AI supervisory body before EU accession.

Proposes the development of tools to help businesses and the state prepare for future regulation, including a methodology for assessing AI's impact on human rights and a regulatory sandbox.

Promotes the voluntary labeling of AI systems to foster transparency, trust, and accountability.

Calls for the creation of general and sectoral recommendations, voluntary codes of conduct, and a web portal for the Responsible AI center. 

Explains how the proposed soft tolls and training tools are expected to positively impact businesses, citizens, and the state.

Advocates for drafting Ukrainian AI regulation law immediately after the adoption of EU AI regulation; supports the gradual implementation of EU AI regulation and the deferral of certain provisions in order to provide more preparation time.

Emphasizes the need for Ukraine to transpose EU AI Regulation and establish an AI supervisory body before EU accession.

Encourages partnerships with leading AI platforms to address potential human rights violations; proposes applying the Trusted Flagger concept, which would involve Ukrainian NGOs acting as Trusted Flaggers that monitor and filter complaints about human rights violations related to AI use.

Allows stakeholders, such as government bodies and academia, to provide feedback on the White Paper within 3 months of its publication.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Budget Act of 2024
document_name: California AB 107 (Budget Act 2024), Sec. 2.00, Item 0511-001-0001 (For support of Secretary of Government Operations)
body:
Establishes monthly AI meetings with legislative staff to discuss Executive Order N-12-23. Defines AI and GenAI. Requires GenAI pilot data as personal information. Prohibits projects with sensitive data. Mandates compliance with GenAI guidelines. Allows de-identified data for research.

Establishes monthly Generative AI meetings with legislative staff to discuss Executive Order N-12-23 implementation.

Requires updates on deliverable completion, proof of concept implementation, and funding source identification.

Supports budget requests for generative AI technology solutions if additional resources are needed.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and "generative artificial intelligence" within the provisions.

Treats data collected in GenAI pilot projects as personal information per Civil Code Section 1798.3.

Prohibits GenAI pilot projects from including sensitive personal information, data on minors, educational records, or medical information.

Mandates compliance with California's GenAI Guidelines for departments in GenAI pilot projects.

Permits the use of de-identified data for research to justify resource requests if expanding pilot program scope.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Grand National Assembly of Turkey)
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Turkish Parliament)
body:
Establishes a regulatory framework ensuring safe, ethical, and fair AI use. Requires risk assessment, registration of high-risk systems, and adherence to principles of safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy. Imposes fines for non-compliance and assigns supervisory authority enforcement powers.

Ensure the safe, ethical, and fair use of AI technologies to protect personal data and privacy rights.

Apply to all stakeholders, including providers, users, importers, and distributors of AI systems.

Mandate adherence to principles of safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy in AI systems.

Require risk assessments and registration for high-risk AI systems with supervisory authorities.

Obligate AI operators to comply with the Law and allow supervisory authorities to monitor compliance and detect violations.

Impose fines up to 35 million Turkish Liras or 7% of annual turnover for violations, with varying penalties based on the nature of the breach.

Enforce the Law upon publication, with the President executing its provisions.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Texas HB 4695
document_name: Texas HB 4695 ("AI and Mental Health")
body:
Requires commission approval for AI mental health applications and mandates licensed supervision, informed consent, and clear AI disclosure.

Requires commission approval for AI mental health applications and mandates licensed supervision, informed consent, and clear AI disclosure. Permits liability-free testing with specialized consent. 

Mandates that licensed mental health professionals supervise AI mental health services, ensuring availability for review, communication, and intervention. Obliges providers to obtain informed consent and clearly inform users about the use of AI technology.
Subjects AI mental health service providers to the same disciplinary actions and record-keeping requirements as licensed mental health professionals.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Rhode Island SB 146
document_name: Rhode Island SB 146 ("Consumer Protection Gaming Act")
body:
Prohibits the use of facial recognition, biometric recognition, and certain automated decision systems in video-lottery terminals and online betting applications. Restricts AI use for influencing gaming outcomes. Excludes standardized rewards programs from these prohibitions.

Prohibits the use of facial recognition technology and biometric recognition programs in video-lottery terminals and online betting applications.

Prohibits the use of algorithmic programs that modify gaming based on a consumer's betting history to increase wagers.

Prohibits the use of artificial intelligence or automated decision systems to promote increased play through intermittent reinforcement based on cognitive-behavioral algorithms and prior gaming data.

Applies these prohibitions to sports betting applications and vendors of gambling products licensed by Rhode Island.

Excludes standardized rewards programs from these prohibitions.

Takes effect upon passage.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Rhode Island HB 6286
document_name: Rhode Island HB 6286 ("GenAI Operating Standards")
body:
Authorizes the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office to regulate large-scale generative AI models, ensuring that they meet disclosure, informed consent, and data management standards.

Prohibits companies from using large-scale generative AI models to engage in targeted bias and discrimination.

Mandates companies to label outputs created using large-scale generative AI models with a distinctive watermark.

Requires companies to secure informed consent from consumers before using their data for training models.

Requires companies, to the best of the their extent, to protect the security of collected data from individuals and shield their identities.

Requires companies to conduct regular risk assessments that identify and mitigate reasonably foreseeable risks and harms.

Mandates companies using large-scale generative AI models to register them with the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office. 

Requires the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office to maintain a public registry of all companies that have registered under the above stipulation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Mexico SM 63
document_name: New Mexico SM 63 ("Structured Decision-making in Child Abuse")
body:
Requests the attorney general to create a task force to study how well the state’s AI-based child welfare decision-making tools are working, gather input from stakeholders, and report findings by August 1, 2024.

New Mexico’s Children, Youth and Families Department (CYFD) adopted structured decision-making (SDM) tools in 2019 to help staff assess child abuse and neglect cases. 

These tools are described as artificial intelligence based systems that use set criteria to guide decisions about investigating families, evaluating safety risks, and determining whether children should remain at home or be taken into state custody. 

However, concerns have been raised about whether these AI-related tools are working as intended. State officials have acknowledged problems with training and implementation, and there is growing concern that relying on these tools may have weakened professional judgment in high-stress situations.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Jersey SB 3876
document_name: New Jersey SB 3876 ("Artificial Intelligence Officer")
body:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Officer and Implementation Officer to oversee AI systems in New Jersey's state agencies. Mandates development of procedures for using AI in critical decisions, ensuring compliance with national standards, and mitigating risks. Creates an AI Advisory Board for oversight and recommendations.

Establishes the position of Artificial Intelligence Officer to develop and update procedures regulating automated systems used by state agencies for critical decisions.

Mandates state agencies to comply with these procedures and submit inventories of their automated systems, which will be published online.

Creates the New Jersey Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board to advise state agencies, hold public hearings on preliminary procedures, and issue reports and recommendations.

Establishes the position of Artificial Intelligence Implementation Officer to review and approve or deny new automated systems based on compliance with procedures, and conduct periodic reevaluations.

Forms a task force to study AI and create an AI Bill of Rights, with a report due within one year.

Subjects officers and the board to open public records laws while protecting trade secrets and work product protections.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Jersey Bill A537
document_name: New Jersey Bill A537 ("Discrimination in Automobile Insurance")
body:
Requires automobile insurers using artificial intelligence or other automated underwriting systems to annually submit documentation to New Jersey’s Department of Banking and Insurance proving their pricing practices are nondiscriminatory and balanced across policyholders. Authorizes the Commissioner to issue rules to enforce compliance.

Requires automobile insurers using automated or predictive underwriting systems to annually provide the Department of Banking and Insurance with documentation demonstrating no discriminatory outcomes in pricing based on race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or religion.

Mandates insurers to show that each pricing segment is balanced and not disproportionate to the overall policyholder population.

Defines automated or predictive underwriting system as a computer-generated process, including robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, or other specialized technology, used to evaluate risk and determine insurance rates.

Authorizes the Commissioner of Banking and Insurance to adopt rules and regulations to implement the act.

Specifies that the act takes effect six months after enactment and applies to all automobile insurance policies issued or renewed thereafter.

category: G7
title: [G7] 2024 아풀리아 정상 커뮤니케(Apulia G7 Leaders’ Communiqué)
document_name: Apulia G7 Leaders’ Communiqué / 「G7 아풀리아 정상 공동성명」
body:
●기관: G7 이탈리아 의장국
●문서종류: 정상회의 공동성명 / 정상급 합의문
●문서명: Apulia G7 Leaders’ Communiqué / 「G7 아풀리아 정상 공동성명」
●채택시점: 2024년 6월 14일
●핵심내용:2024년 6월 13~15일 이탈리아 아풀리아에서 개최된 G7 정상회의 결과문서로, 우크라이나 지원, 중동 정세, 아프리카와의 파트너십, 개발금융, 식량안보, 기후·에너지, 이주, AI, 경제안보 등 주요 글로벌 현안을 포괄함. AI 분야에서는 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI를 촉진하고, 히로시마 AI 프로세스, 서울 AI 정상회의, 공공부문 AI 활용, 노동시장 영향, 개발도상국 AI 역량강화 등을 주요 협력과제로 제시함.
① 문서는 민주적 가치·인권에 기반한 인간중심 AI를 추진하고, 거버넌스 상호운용성과 위험기반 접근을 통해 혁신·포용성장·지속가능발전과 위험완화를 함께 추구해야 한다고 강조함
② 히로시마 AI 프로세스 보고체계와 공공부문 AI 툴킷을 발전시키고, 노동 분야에서는 양질의 일자리·노동자 권리·재교육·사회적 대화를 강화하도록 제시함
③ 중소기업의 AI 도입을 지원하고 개발도상국·신흥경제국의 디지털 격차 해소와 AI·첨단컴퓨팅 접근성 확대를 위해 UNDP와 지속가능발전 AI Hub 설립을 추진한다고 언급함

category: EU
title: [EU] AI에 관한 조화된 규칙을 정하는 규정 — AI 기본법
document_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence — Artificial Intelligence Act/ 「인공지능에 관한 조화된 규칙을 정하는 규정 — 인공지능법」
body:
●국가: EU
●기관: 유럽의회 / EU 이사회
●문서종류: 규정(Regulation) / AI 기본법
●문서명: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence — Artificial Intelligence Act/ 「인공지능에 관한 조화된 규칙을 정하는 규정 — 인공지능법」
●채택시점: 2024년 6월 13일
●관보게재: 2024년 7월 12일
●발효시점: 2024년 8월 1일
●핵심내용EU AI Act는 세계 최초의 포괄적 AI 규제법으로, AI 시스템을 위험 수준에 따라 차등 규율하는 것이 핵심임. EU 단일시장 내 AI 개발·배포·사용에 공통 규칙을 적용하여 기본권, 안전, 민주주의, 법치, 환경 보호를 보장하면서도 신뢰 가능한 AI 혁신을 촉진하려는 법률임.
5대 핵심 축:① 위험기반 규제체계: AI 시스템을 금지 AI, 고위험 AI, 제한적 위험 AI, 일반 AI로 구분하고 위험 수준에 따라 의무를 차등 적용② 금지 AI 관행: 사회적 점수화, 취약성 악용, 조작적 기법, 일부 생체인식·감정인식·예측치안 등 기본권 침해 가능성이 큰 AI 사용 제한③ 고위험 AI 관리: 의료, 교육, 고용, 금융, 법집행, 중요 인프라 등 고위험 분야 AI에 대해 위험관리, 데이터 거버넌스, 기술문서, 기록보존, 투명성, 인간감독, 정확성·견고성·사이버보안 의무 부과④ 범용 AI 모델 규율: 범용 AI 모델 제공자에게 기술문서, 저작권 준수 정책, 학습데이터 요약 공개 의무를 부과하고, 시스템적 위험이 있는 고성능 모델에는 평가·위험완화·사고보고·사이버보안 의무 추가⑤ 거버넌스·집행체계: EU AI Office, 회원국 시장감시기관, AI Board를 통해 이행을 감독하고, 위반 유형에 따라 최대 3,500만 유로 또는 전 세계 매출 7%까지 과징금 부과 가능

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations)
document_name: Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations)
body:
Allows railroads to petition for rulemaking or waivers to use non-compliant rail automation technology. Requires safety justification for autonomous operations with fewer crew members. Supports technological advancements in rail safety and automation through research and funding.

Require railroads seeking to use automation technology non-compliant with FRA safety regulations to file a petition for rulemaking or a waiver.

Mandate a risk assessment before initiating operations under special approval processes.

Acknowledge freight rail industry's concerns about competition with automated trucking but emphasize rail safety hazards from reduced crew sizes.

Disagree with assertions that labor-saving technologies like PTC justify removal of crew members, stating such technologies are not fully developed.

Support technological advancement in rail through research on AI and automation, including drones and real-time safety systems.

Permit railroads to petition for rulemaking or waivers to use technology that doesn't meet existing regulatory requirements, ensuring safety justifications are provided.

Clarify that the rule does not impede innovation but requires description of technology used to support tasks typically performed by a second crew member.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Colorado House Bill 24-1468
document_name: Colorado HB 1468 (Artificial Intelligence Impact Task Force)
body:
Creates the Artificial Intelligence Impact Task Force to develop policy recommendations against AI system risks and algorithmic discrimination affecting consumers and workers. Requires diverse membership and adherence to transparency standards. Mandates a report by February 2025 to the legislature and governor; task force sunsets in 2027.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Impact Task Force in Colorado to develop policy recommendations for protecting consumers and workers from harms posed by AI systems and automated decision systems.

Defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence system," "automated decision system," and "algorithmic discrimination."

Requires the task force to consider transparency, disclosure, and protection measures against algorithmic discrimination, and to recommend best practices for the ethical and equitable use of AI.

Mandates the task force to include diverse representation and expertise in AI and related fields, with a focus on communities that have been historically impacted by algorithmic discrimination.

Obligates the task force to convene by September 1, 2024, and submit a report of findings and recommendations to the legislature and governor by February 1, 2025.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act Authorizing And Adjusting Bonds Of The State And Concerning Provisions Related To State And Municipal Tax Administration, General Government And School Building Projects
document_name: Connecticut H 5524 (General Government And School Building Projects), Sec. 143-144
body:
Establishes an AI education tool pilot program for selected school districts, requiring compliance with privacy laws. Provides professional development for educators on using AI tools in classrooms, focusing on safety, benefits, and legal compliance.

Administers an artificial intelligence education tool pilot program by the Department of Education for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2025.

Awards a grant by the Commissioner of Education for implementing an AI tool in classrooms, involving five selected school districts.

Requires the inclusion of at least one rural, suburban, and urban district, reflecting state diversity.

Mandates compliance of the AI tool with laws on AI use and student data privacy, including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as technology using data to train algorithms for tasks usually associated with human intelligence.

Provides professional development for educators in the pilot program, covering AI tool utilization and privacy laws.

Trains educators on AI benefits for instruction, student learning, academic achievement, and workforce development.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap
document_name: Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap
body:
Emphasizes AI training for employees and IT developers. Requires departments to set clear objectives before AI deployment and conduct proofs of concept. Advises AI tools remain secure, ethical, and data privacy is protected. Encourages transparency and human-centric AI use.

Establishes two distinct user segments for AI tools: City Employees and IT Professionals, requiring tailored training for each group.

Instructs non-technical department leadership to set clear goals before AI tool deployment.

Encourages piloting AI tools to understand their strengths and weaknesses before widespread use.

Anticipates most AI tools will be accessed through existing software platforms.

Emphasizes the need for adaptable AI tools that align with evolving data and requirements.

Advises staying current on AI tools and frameworks for maximized effectiveness.

Requires comprehensive AI training for both users and developers, highlighting security and ethical considerations.

Insists on cybersecurity and data privacy for AI implementation.

Highlights AI as a long-term investment needing high-quality data and data transparency.

Asserts City data ownership and the need for ethical, transparent, and human-centered AI tools.

Outlines a roadmap for training, deploying AI tools, and developing ethics guidelines for the City.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: West Virginia HB 5690 (Artificial Intelligence Task Force)
document_name: West Virginia HB 5690 (AI Task Force)
body:
Establishes the West Virginia Task Force on Artificial Intelligence to recommend AI definitions, policies, legislation, and best practices. Requires submission of a report by July 1, 2025, and terminates the Task Force upon report submission or on July 1, 2025.

Establishes the West Virginia Task Force on Artificial Intelligence within the Office of the Governor. 

Specifies membership including representatives from government, industry, education, and health sectors, appointed by various authorities. 

Charges the Task Force with responsibilities such as recommending AI definitions for legislation, identifying relevant state agencies for AI policy oversight, and developing best practices for public sector AI use. 

Mandates recommendations on AI's impact on employment, protecting individual rights and data, and addressing AI use in education. 

Requires the Task Force to assess current AI use in state agencies and consider extending its mandate to keep pace with AI advancements. 

Obligates submission of a comprehensive report by July 1, 2025, after which the Task Force terminates. 

Requires initial appointments within 90 days and quarterly meetings, with administrative support provided by the Office of Technology.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2
document_name: Microsoft Responsible AI Standard, v2
body:
Establishes Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard, requiring AI systems to undergo ongoing evaluations and impact assessments, oversight for adverse impacts, and fit-for-purpose validation, mandating clear documentation on capabilities and limitations, human oversight, and compliance with privacy, security, and accessibility standards.

Mandates Microsoft to conduct Impact Assessments for AI systems early in development to evaluate societal impacts, ensuring AI systems are fit for purpose, with annual updates and reviews for significant adverse impacts.

Demands human oversight by identifying responsible stakeholders, providing necessary tools, and ensuring appropriate documentation for system control and intervention.

Requires intelligibility for decision-making, enabling stakeholders to interpret system outputs and minimize automation bias.

Mandates transparency and communication about system capabilities, limitations, and any AI-generated content.

Ensures fairness by focusing on quality of service and opportunities and minimizing disparities for demographic groups in AI system outputs. 

Emphasizes reliability and safety, requiring evaluation for safe performance within operational ranges, and ongoing monitoring and feedback. 

Insists on compliance with Microsoft’s Privacy, Security, and Accessibility Standards to ensure AI systems are inclusive, secure, and respect privacy.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Louisiana (2024) HCR 66
document_name: Louisiana HCR 66
body:
Requests the Joint Legislative Committee on Technology and Cybersecurity to study and recommend AI use and regulation. Requires data and testimony solicitation. Instructs the committee to make annual policy recommendation reports to the Louisiana legislature.

Requests the Joint Legislative Committee on Technology and Cybersecurity to study and make recommendations concerning the use and regulation of artificial intelligence.

Instructs the joint committee to solicit data and testimony from relevant persons, entities, agencies, and institutions.

Requires the joint committee to make annual reports with policy recommendations to the legislature.

Recognizes the multifaceted potential threats of artificial intelligence in education, criminal justice, finance, health, welfare, and state fiscal health.

Acknowledges the potential for beneficial uses of artificial intelligence to improve government operations and service efficiency.

Emphasizes the necessity for more information before developing policies to maximize AI benefits and minimize its misuse in the state of Louisiana.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Tennessee House Bill 2325
document_name: Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council Act
body:
Establishes the Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council to recommend AI action plans for state government, focusing on economic benefits, responsible use, labor market impacts, and transparency. Requires annual reports through 2028, with a final report due by December 31, 2028.

Establishes the Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council to guide AI awareness, education, and usage in state government.

Requires the council to submit an action plan to the governor for leveraging AI to improve government service efficiency and capture economic benefits.

Mandates the council to report annually on AI's impact on the labor market, propose legal and policy changes, and recommend workforce development strategies.

Directs the council to submit a final report by December 31, 2028, outlining AI governance frameworks, risk analyses, and recommendations for AI deployment in government.

Requires all state departments to cooperate with the council and allows the council to consult with AI experts.

Specifies that the council members will not receive compensation but will be reimbursed for travel expenses.

Repeals the act on December 31, 2028, and takes effect upon becoming law.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Arizona 2024 Senate Bill 1359
document_name: Arizona SB 1359 (Deepfakes in Election Communications)
body:
Prohibits creating and distributing deceptive deepfakes of election candidates without clear AI-generated content disclosure within 90 days before elections. Exempts satire, parody, and interactive computer services. Imposes civil penalties for non-disclosure violations. Defines key terms including "creator" and "synthetic media."

Prohibits the creation and distribution of deceptive and fraudulent deepfakes of election candidates within ninety days before an election unless there is a clear disclosure that the content is generated by artificial intelligence.

Exempts satire, parody, and interactive computer services from this prohibition.

Imposes a civil penalty for each day a deceptive deepfake is distributed without the required disclosure.

Defines a "creator" as a person using AI or digital technology to generate synthetic media, excluding technology providers.

Clarifies "deceptive and fraudulent deepfake" as synthetic media intended to mislead people about a candidate's actions or statements.

Defines "synthetic media" as digitally manipulated images, audio, or video to create realistic but false impressions.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Colorado House Bill 1147
document_name: Colorado HB 1147 (Candidate Election Deepfake Disclosures)
body:
Prohibits distributing AI-generated deepfakes about candidates close to elections without disclosures. Requires clear notifications in such communications. Allows candidates to seek legal remedies for unauthorized deepfakes. Effective July 1, 2024, with enforcement by the Secretary of State.

Prohibits the distribution of deepfakes concerning candidates for elective office without a clear disclosure, within 60 days before a primary or 90 days before a general election.

Requires a disclosure stating the content has been falsified if a deepfake is distributed.

Mandates that disclosures in visual and audio communications meet specific size and clarity standards.

Allows candidates affected by deepfakes to seek injunctive relief, damages, and other remedies against violators.

Exempts bona fide news, satire, and parody from the prohibition, as well as certain media and technology providers.

Obligates the Secretary of State to promulgate rules to enforce these provisions.

Permits civil penalties and administrative complaints for violations.

Establishes the act's effective date as July 1, 2024, with applicability to communications distributed thereafter.

category: AI Summit
title: [AI 서울 정상회의] 서울 AI 기업 서약
document_name: Seoul AI Business Pledge / 「서울 AI 기업 서약」
body:
●기관: AI Seoul Summit
●문서종류: 기업 서약 / 프런티어 AI 안전·책임 이행 문서
●문서명: Seoul AI Business Pledge / 「서울 AI 기업 서약」
●발표시점: 2024년 5월 22일
●핵심내용:2024년 AI 서울 정상회의 계기 발표된 기업 서약으로, 주요 AI 기업들이 AI 기술의 혁신적 잠재력과 사회적 영향력을 인식하고, 안전하고 책임 있는 AI 개발·활용을 위해 협력하겠다는 의지를 표명한 문서임. 동 서약은 기업이 AI 생태계의 핵심 행위자로서 안전성, 책임성, 포용성, 지속가능성, 국제협력에 관한 역할과 책임을 수행해야 한다는 점을 강조함.
① 문서는 AI 기업이 광범위한 경제·사회적 영향에 대한 책임을 인식하고, 안전성·보안성·신뢰성·책임성을 기반으로 AI 위험을 지속적으로 관리해야 한다고 강조함
② AI 혁신의 혜택이 사회 전반에 확산되도록 포용성·접근성·공정성·다양성을 고려하고, 중소기업·스타트업·연구기관 등 다양한 주체의 참여를 확대할 필요가 있다고 제시함
③ 지속가능한 AI 발전을 위해 환경영향·에너지 효율·사회적 책임을 고려하고, 국제협력을 통한 책임 있는 AI 생태계 조성이 필요하다고 제시함

body:
●기관: AI Seoul Summit

●발표시점: 2024년 5월 22일
●핵심내용:2024년 5월 22일 AI 서울 정상회의 장관세션에서 합의된 성명으로, 안전, 혁신, 포용을 AI 거버넌스의 상호 연계된 핵심 목표로 제시함. 각국은 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI와 지속가능한 AI 발전을 위해 국제협력을 강화하고, 프런티어 AI 위험관리, 공공·산업 부문 AI 활용, AI 역량강화와 디지털 격차 해소를 추진할 필요성을 확인함.
① 문서는 프런티어 AI의 중대한 위험에 대응하기 위해 투명성·설명가능성·프라이버시·책임성·인간 감독과 함께 역량·악용 가능성·배포 맥락을 고려한 위험관리와 안전장치를 강화해야 한다고 강조함
② AI 안전연구소 등 기관 간 평가 데이터·시험지침·모범사례 공유와 문화·언어 다양성을 고려한 시험 상호운용성을 확대하고, 연구개발·투자·인력·법제도를 포함한 거버넌스를 구축해야 한다고 제시함
③ 공공·산업 분야의 AI 도입과 생산성 향상을 촉진하되 노동자 권리·안전을 보호하고, 교육·역량강화·공동연구·개발도상국 참여 확대를 통해 AI 혜택을 공평하게 공유해야 한다고 제시함

●문서명: Seoul Statement of Intent toward International Cooperation on AI Safety Science / 「AI 안전과학 국제협력에 관한 서울 의향성명」
