●핵심내용:2024년 5월 21일 AI 서울 정상회의 계기 발표된 AI 안전과학 국제협력 관련 부속 성명임. 호주, 캐나다, EU, 프랑스, 독일, 이탈리아, 일본, 한국, 싱가포르, 영국, 미국 등 주요 파트너가 AI 안전 연구·시험·평가 역량을 강화하고, AI 안전에 관한 공통의 과학적 이해를 형성하기 위한 국제협력 의향을 확인함.
① 문서는 책임 있는 AI 혁신을 위해 안전을 핵심 요소로 보고, AI 안전과학 발전을 위한 국제적 조정·협력과 AI Safety Institute 등 관련 기관의 역할 확대를 강조함
② 신뢰 가능하고 재현 가능한 증거와 국제 AI 안전 평가를 기반으로 모델의 역량·한계·위험 정보를 공유하고, 안전사고 모니터링·평가·데이터셋·기준의 공동 개발을 추진하도록 제시함
③ 연구·시험·지침 역량과 공동 기술자원·연구보안·국제표준 협력을 강화하고, 주요 파트너 간 국제 네트워크를 통해 AI 안전과학 협력을 지속할 의향을 표명함

category: AI Summit
title: [AI 서울 정상회의] 안전하고 혁신적이며 포용적인 AI를 위한 서울 선언
document_name: Seoul Declaration for safe, innovative and inclusive AI / 「안전하고 혁신적이며 포용적인 AI를 위한 서울 선언」
body:
●기관: AI Seoul Summit
●문서종류: 정상선언 / AI 안전·혁신·포용 국제협력 문서
●문서명: Seoul Declaration for safe, innovative and inclusive AI / 「안전하고 혁신적이며 포용적인 AI를 위한 서울 선언」
●발표시점: 2024년 5월 21일
●핵심내용:2024년 5월 21일 AI 서울 정상회의 정상세션에서 주요국 정상급 대표들이 합의한 선언문으로, AI 안전, 혁신, 포용을 상호 연계된 AI 거버넌스의 핵심 목표로 제시함. 블레츨리 파크 AI 안전 정상회의 논의를 계승하면서, 위험기반 접근, 히로시마 AI 프로세스 국제 행동규범의 이행, AI 안전연구 협력, 디지털 격차 해소, 민주적 가치와 인권 보호를 강조함.
① AI 안전·혁신·포용을 상호 연계된 목표로 보고, 거버넌스 상호운용성과 위험기반 접근과 히로시마 AI 프로세스의 지속적 이행을 강조함
② 프런티어 AI 개발·배포 조직의 책임과 안전공약을 강조하고, AI 안전연구소·감독기관 확대와 모범사례 공유 등을 통한 국제협력을 제시함
③ 인간 중심 AI를 통해 인권·프라이버시·다양성·환경 지속가능성을 보장하고 AI·디지털 격차를 완화하며, 다중이해관계자와 기존 국제 이니셔티브 간 협력을 강화해야 한다고 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: South Carolina 2023 H 4754 (Section 4)
document_name: South Carolina 2023 H 4754 (Sec 4)
body:
Holds licensees accountable for work produced using AI or machine learning, treating violations by these programs as direct violations by the licensee.

Amends Article 7, Chapter 57, Title 40 of the S.C. Code by adding Section 40-57-820.

Holds a licensee accountable for all work produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar programs.

Treats violations committed through the use of these technologies as if committed directly by the licensee.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
document_name: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
body:
Announces on behalf of the UK and Republic of Korea governments companies that have committed to the Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Outlines three outcomes related to frontier AI safety that companies are expected to realize.

Announces on behalf of the UK and Republic of Korea governments companies, including Amazon, Google, and OpenAI, that have committed to the Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Mandates that companies publish a safety framework, requires transparency on evolving safety approaches, and implement various best practices.

Defines outcome one as organizations identifying, assessing, and managing risks when developing and deploying frontier AI systems. Defines five sub-outcomes, including internal and external evaluations, establishment of risk thresholds and response processes for violations, and investment in risk mitigation effectiveness.

Defines outcome two as organizational accountability established through the development and review of governance frameworks. 

Defines outcome three as established transparency about organizational approaches to frontier AI safety for external actors, including governments. Mandates provision of information about best practice implementation to the public and explanation of how external actors are involved in risk assessment and framework adherence.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Arizona 2024 House Bill 2394
document_name: Arizona HB 2394 (Digital Impersonation of Candidate for Public Office)
body:
Prohibits digital impersonation using AI to deceive voters in Arizona elections. Allows candidates or citizens to seek declaratory relief within two years of impersonation. Shields service providers from liability for third-party content. Requires clear and convincing evidence for relief.

Amends Arizona Revised Statutes to prohibit digital impersonation using AI techniques.

Allows candidates or citizens to take legal action against digital impersonation within two years of awareness.

Mandates proof of unauthorized publication and lack of clear indication of impersonation to prevail in court.

Restricts legal action to originators of paid advertisements containing impersonations.

Exempts interactive computer service providers from liability for third-party content.

Permits filing for preliminary declaratory relief in superior court with expedited ruling requirements.

Specifies conditions for granting preliminary relief, such as immediate elections or significant harm.

Allows further injunctive relief and damages for impersonations involving sexual or criminal content.

Sets standards of proof as clear and convincing evidence for relief actions.

Defines "digital impersonation" as AI-manipulated media designed to deceive, excluding parody or artistic expression.

Operates as an emergency measure effective immediately to protect public peace and safety.

category: Chinese law and policy
title: National Standard of the People’s Republic of China: Cybersecurity Technology – Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Feedback)
document_name: Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (National Standard - Draft for Feedback)
body:
Establishes safety and security requirements for generative AI services and service providers. Requires data filtering, intellectual property management, personal information protection, and secure model output with an emphasis on preventing AI systems from generating detrimental content.

Establishes basic safety requirements for generative AI services, focusing on training data safety, model safety, and safety measures.

Requires service providers to conduct safety assessments and manage training data sources, ensuring data does not contain over 5% illegal content.

Mandates the verification of intellectual property rights and personal information consent before using data for training.

Stipulates regular security audits and monitoring of models to prevent malicious attacks and ensure content accuracy.

Obliges disclosure of service limitations, models, and personal data usage to users.

Demands the implementation of mechanisms for complaints and a backup strategy for service continuity.

Sets specific guidelines for minors, requiring parental controls and restrictions on unsuitable content.

Requires transparency in service provision, detailing applicable scenarios and user consent for data use in training.

Mandates service providers to construct banks of unsafe key words and questions which AI models should and should not refuse to answer.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Minnesota House Bill 4772
document_name: Minnesota H 4772 (Elections policy), Sec. 76-77
body:
Criminalizes disseminating deep fakes to influence elections within specified periods. Imposes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, based on offender history and intent. Disqualifies convicted candidates from holding office. Effective July 1, 2024, for crimes thereafter.

Amends Minnesota law to criminalize the dissemination of deep fakes intended to influence elections.

Prohibits the distribution of deep fakes within 90 days before elections or political conventions without consent if intended to harm a candidate or influence election outcomes.

Excludes broadcasters following federal law from these prohibitions.

Imposes penalties for violations, including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to $10,000 based on prior offenses or intent to cause harm.

Requires that candidates convicted under this law forfeit their nomination or office.

Disqualifies individuals convicted under this law from holding certain public offices.

Sets the effective date for July 1, 2024, applicable to crimes committed thereafter.

category: Editors' Picks;Multinational
title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
document_name: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
body:
Ensures AI activities align with human rights, democracy, and the rule of law and requires measures for transparency, accountability, non-discrimination, and privacy protection. Establishes oversight guidelines and risk management frameworks for signatories and encourages cooperation between signatories and with other states on AI-related issues.

Mandates signatories to adopt measures ensuring AI systems align with human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.

Explains that signatories are not required to apply the Convention to activities within the lifecycle of AI related to the protection of national security interests, but insists that such activities adhere to international human rights law and respect democratic processes.

Requires implementation of measures that ensure transparency, accountability, and non-discrimination, and the protection of privacy, human dignity, and democratic processes within the lifecycle of AI systems.

Calls for the adoption of remedies and procedural safeguards for human rights violations resulting from activities within the lifecycle of AI systems.

Demands the creation of risk assessment and mitigation strategies for AI, with a focus on risks to human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.

Encourages signatories to consult the public on AI–related questions and promote digital literacy and skills to the entire population.

Establishes a follow-up mechanism for the implementation of the Convention and encourages signatories to cooperate with relevant stakeholders and other states on AI-related challenges.

Stipulates that signatories must establish or designate independent oversight mechanisms to ensure compliance with the Convention.

Permits dispute settlements, amendments to, and denunciations of the Convention.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Colorado SB 24-205 (Concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems 2024)
document_name: Colorado SB 24-205 (Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence 2024)
body:
Defines "high-risk AI systems" and mandates developers and deployers in Colorado to use care against algorithmic discrimination, with documentation and risk management requirements effective February 1, 2026. Grants the Attorney General enforcement authority and rule-making power.

Defines "algorithmic discrimination" as any AI system-created unlawful differential treatment based on specific protected classifications. 

Requires developers of high-risk AI systems, by February 1, 2026, to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination, and provide detailed documentation to deployers about potential risks and data usage.

Instructs deployers of high-risk AI systems to establish a risk management policy and annually complete impact assessments to identify and mitigate algorithmic discrimination risks.

Mandates disclosure to consumers when high-risk AI systems influence consequential decisions, detailing purposes, data usage, and consumer rights.

Grants exclusive enforcement authority to the Attorney General, who may issue rules on compliance requirements for developers and deployers.

Exempts certain entities and uses from these obligations, including research activities and federal government-acquired AI systems.

Clarifies that these regulations do not apply if compliance would violate other laws or rights such as freedom of speech.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act concerning consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
document_name: Colorado AI Act (SB 205)
body:
Establishes consumer protections and imposes disclosure, evaluation, and performance obligations on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems that may generate algorithmic discrimination in making consequential decisions (related to employment, housing, health benefits, etc.).

Requires developers of high-risk AI systems to disclose foreseeable uses and risks of their systems, the inputs used in their training data, and how the systems were evaluated for performance.

Requires developers to display these disclosures publicly on their websites in a public use case inventory.

Mandates developers to disclose to the Colorado Attorney General, within 90 days, if their systems have caused or will likely cause algorithmic discrimination.

Requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to notify consumers of how AI is used to make consequential decisions and inform them of their right to opt out of the processing of their personal data.

Requires deployers to give consumers the opportunity to correct erroneous personal data and appeal adverse consequential decisions.

Mandates deployers to make all these disclosures publicly available on their websites.

Provides exemptions to the Colorado AI Act for certain deployers of high-risk AI systems including those who employ less than 50 people and do not use thier own data to train the system.

Grants the Colorado Attorney General exclusive authority to enforce all regulations laid out by this act and engage in any additional rulemaking necessary for the implementation and enforcement of this act.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 908 ("Part 107 Waiver Improvements")
document_name: American Aviation Act, Sec. 908 ("Part 107 Waiver Improvements")
body:
Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to leverage big data analytics and machine learning in reviewing requests for certificates of waiver under section 107.200 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations.Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to improve waiver request processes by leveraging big data analytics and machine learning.Adopts a performance- and risk-based approach for waiver requests. Prohibits open-ended prompts unless necessary. Utilizes big data and machine learning for waiver data. Publishes waivers online, protecting proprietary info. Expedites similar waiver modifications and renewals. Considers property access control.

Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to leverage big data analytics and machine learning in reviewing requests for certificates of waiver under section 107.200 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations.Adopts a performance- and risk-based approach for reviewing waiver requests under section 107.200 of title 14, CFR.

Improves the waiver application process and prohibits the use of open-ended descriptive prompts, except for unusual or irregular operations.

Leverages data, including big data analytics and machine learning, from previous waiver requests.

Requires consideration of control over access to real property within the operation area and recognizes safety enhancements from such control.

Publishes all issued certificates of waiver on the FAA website, including terms, conditions, limitations, and airspace class, while protecting proprietary information.

Allows streamlined approval for waiver applications substantially similar to previously approved ones.

Establishes an expedited review process for modifying or renewing previously issued waivers.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1028 ("Air Traffic Control Training")
document_name: American Aviation Act, Sec. 1028 ("Air Traffic Control Training")
body:
Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to assess the benefits of deploying AI and other advanced technologies in enhancing air traffic controller training. Mandates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress on research findings within one year.

Mandates the Administrator to carry out a research program assessing the benefits of deploying advanced technologies such as AI to modernize, enhance, and streamline on-the-job training for FAA air traffic controllers.

Requires the Administrator to include collaboration with labor organizations and other stakeholders in the research program.

Mandates the Administrator to report findings to Congress within 1 year of the Act's enactment.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Securing Growth and Robust Leadership in American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Technology Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Technologies")
document_name: American Aviation Act, Sec. 1024 ("Review of AI and ML Technologies")
body:
Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct a review of current and planned AI and machine learning technologies to enhance airport efficiency and safety. Asks the administrator to consider best practices from previous applications of AI and Chinese use cases in enhancing airport operations.

Requires the Administrator to conduct a review of current and planned AI and machine learning technologies to enhance airport efficiency and safety.

Asks the Administrator to consider best practices and lessons learned from domestic and international AI and machine learning applications.

Permits coordination with other Federal agencies to identify China's use of AI and machine learning in airport operations.

Mandates the review to include AI and machine learning applications in jet bridges, airport service vehicles, aircraft taxi, air traffic control operations, and other areas deemed necessary by the Administrator.

Obligates the Administrator to submit a report to Congress within one year detailing the review's findings.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Maryland Senate Bill 360
document_name: Maryland S 360 (Budget Bill Fiscal Year 2025), Section 21., Subsection (50)
body:
Allocates $500,000 to Morgan State University's Center for Equitable AI and Machine Learning Systems, with funds restricted from transfer to other purposes and reverting to the General Fund if unspent.

Adds $500,000 in general funds to support the Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems at Morgan State University.

Prohibits the transfer of unexpended funds to any other purpose.

Requires unspent funds to revert to the General Fund.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Tennessee House Bill 2163 (Sexual Exploitation of Children)
document_name: Tennessee HB 2163 (Sexual Exploitation of Children)
body:
Amends the definition of computer-generated images to include those modified by AI for sexual exploitation offenses. Defines "artificial intelligence" and "generative artificial intelligence" related to content creation. Takes effect on July 1, 2024.

Amends Tennessee Code to include computer-generated images created, adapted, or modified by artificial intelligence under the definition of materials related to the sexual exploitation of children.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions, influencing environments, or learning autonomously, developed in any context, including software or hardware, and solving tasks requiring human-like abilities.

Includes "generative artificial intelligence" as a system capable of creating new content or data, such as text, images, audio, or video when prompted.

Takes effect on July 1, 2024, for the purpose of public welfare.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024
document_name: Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024
body:
Creates the AI Authority to oversee AI regulation, ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and compliance while supporting innovation, public engagement, and regulatory alignment across sectors. Businesses must disclose training data, ensure ethical AI use, allow independent audits, and comply with regulations, which may impose fines and require parliamentary approval.

Establishes the AI Authority to ensure regulators take accountability for AI, align regulatory approaches, review legislation, monitor regulatory frameworks, assess risks, support testbeds, and promote international interoperability.

Mandates the AI Authority to adhere to principles ensuring AI safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, compliance with laws, and inclusivity.

Requires the creation of regulatory sandboxes for testing AI innovations with consumer protections.

Obligates businesses using AI to appoint AI responsible officers to ensure ethical use and unbiased data.

Imposes transparency and IP obligations, requiring disclosing records of data used in AI training and independent audits.

Mandates the implementation of public engagement programs on AI opportunities and risks.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Maryland Senate Bill 1068
document_name: Maryland S 1068 (Evaluation and Development of a 3-1-1 Portal)
body:
Requires the Maryland Department of Information Technology to evaluate AI's potential in developing a statewide virtual 3–1–1 portal for nonemergency government information and services, and if feasible, prioritize its creation by July 1, 2024.

Requires the Maryland Department of Information Technology to evaluate the potential use of artificial intelligence in developing a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal for nonemergency government information and services.

Mandates the prioritization of creating the virtual 3-1-1 portal if the AI application is deemed feasible.

Sets the effective date of this Act as July 1, 2024.

Receives approval from the Governor on May 9, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Maryland House Bill 1128
document_name: Maryland  H 1128  (Talent Innovation Program and Fund )
body:
Establishes the Talent Innovation Program to enhance AI job training using innovative financing. Creates a nonlapsing Talent Innovation Fund to support the program, including AI sector initiatives. Allows fund investments and requires annual reporting to government officials starting in 2025.

Establishes the Talent Innovation Program in the Maryland Department of Labor to increase access to high-quality job training, with a focus on industries such as artificial intelligence.

Creates the Talent Innovation Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to support the program, including job training and talent financing mechanisms.

Requires the program to conduct pilots, research, and stakeholder engagement to develop sustainable talent financing approaches.

Mandates an initial pilot program focused on the cybersecurity sector to expand regional cyber ranges for job training.

Authorizes the Department to provide grants and funding to various entities and individuals for training and support services.

Directs the State Treasurer to invest the fund's money, with interest earnings credited to the fund.

Compels the Department to adopt regulations and report annually on program activities and fund utilization to state leadership.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Iowa Senate Bill 2435
document_name: Iowa S 2435 (Appropriations to the Education System), Division III, Section 6. ("GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS")
body:
Allocates $2.8 million to Iowa State University for expanding AI, cybersecurity, computer science, and related technology programs to address workforce needs and foster innovation in digital agriculture, manufacturing, and biosciences.

Allocate $2.8 million to Iowa State University of Science and Technology to address workforce needs in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) by expanding degree and certificate programs in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, computer science, and related fields.

Promote innovation in areas such as digital agriculture, manufacturing, water quality, vaccine delivery technologies, and biosciences with the allocated funds.

Ensure that the state board of regents and the institutions of higher learning governed by them do not reduce budgeted funds for their police departments for the fiscal year 2024-2025.

Require the state board of regents to submit a quarterly financial report to the general assembly, including details on five-year graduation rates for the regents universities in the report for the quarter ending December 31, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: St Louis, MO Board Bill Number 185 2023-24
document_name: St Louis MO, Board Bill No. 185 2023-24 ("Regulating the City's Use of Surveillance Technology")
body:
Require the Board of Aldermen to approve any procurement or use of surveillance technology by City Entities, detailing requirements for Surveillance Use Plans. Enforce disclosure, reporting, and public involvement. Mandate protections against discriminatory impacts, audits, and whistleblower protections.

Requires a City Entity in St. Louis to obtain Board of Aldermen approval before accepting funds, acquiring, or using surveillance technology, including AI surveillance tools.

Defines surveillance technology broadly to include AI-based systems.

Mandates public availability and Board approval of a Surveillance Use Plan (SUP) before technology use.

Prohibits unauthorized surveillance use that discriminates or infringes civil rights.

Obligates annual reporting on surveillance technology use, data sharing, and impacts.

Protects whistleblowers disclosing ordinance violations.

Allows temporary use of surveillance technology in exigent circumstances with strict limits and reporting requirements.

Establishes remedies and disciplinary actions for ordinance violations.

Ensures public participation and transparency in the surveillance approval process.

Seeks to balance surveillance benefits with civil rights protections, assessing potential discriminatory impacts.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
org: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities
document_name: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities, § 92.210
body:
Prohibits covered entities from discriminating in health programs using patient care decision support tools based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability. Requires identifying and mitigating discrimination risks in these tools.

Prohibits covered entities from discriminating based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability through the use of patient care decision support tools in health programs or activities.

Requires covered entities to make reasonable efforts to identify uses of such tools that employ input variables or factors measuring race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.

Mandates covered entities to make reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risks from identified tools in their health programs or activities.

category: OECD
title: [OECD] AI 권고 개정안(C/MIN(2024)16/FINAL)
document_name: Revised Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence / 「인공지능에 관한 OECD 이사회 개정 권고」
body:
●기관: OECD
●문서종류: 이사회 권고 / AI 원칙 개정문
●문서명: Revised Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence / 「인공지능에 관한 OECD 이사회 개정 권고」
●채택시점: 2024년 5월 3일
●핵심내용:OECD 각료이사회가 2019년 「인공지능에 관한 OECD 이사회 권고」를 개정하여 채택한 문서로, 신뢰 가능한 AI를 위한 국제 원칙과 정책 권고를 최신 AI 기술 발전에 맞게 보완함. 개정 권고는 AI 시스템, AI 생애주기, AI 행위자, AI 지식 등 핵심 개념을 정리하고, 책임 있는 AI 관리 원칙과 국가정책·국제협력 방향을 제시함.
① OECD는 신뢰 가능한 AI의 핵심 원칙으로 포용적 성장·인권·민주적 가치·투명성·설명가능성·안전성·책임성을 제시하고, AI 생애주기 전반에서 비차별·프라이버시·노동권 등을 존중해야 한다고 강조함
② 정부에는 신뢰 가능한 AI 연구개발과 오픈소스·데이터·컴퓨팅·연결 인프라에 투자하고, 혁신·경쟁과 상호운용 가능한 거버넌스를 병행하는 유연한 정책환경을 조성하도록 권고함
③ AI 확산에 따른 노동시장 전환에 대응해 재교육·노동자 보호·사회적 대화를 강화하고, 국제협력·기술표준·AI 측정지표와 증거기반 정책평가를 확대하도록 제시함

category: Editors' Picks;Multinational
title: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (5/2/2024)
document_name: OECD AI Principles (May 2024 update)
body:
Recommends principles for trustworthy AI including inclusivity, transparency, robustness, and accountability. Encourages investment in AI R&D, the creation of inclusive digital ecosystems, and the establishment of adaptable policy frameworks; advocates for international cooperation and capacity-building to advance AI governance and labor market transformation.

Recommends that AI actors and stakeholders promote principles for responsible AI, including inclusive growth, respect for human rights, transparency, robustness, and accountability.

Calls on governments and AI actors to invest in AI research and development, focusing on ethics, privacy, and reducing bias.

Advises governments to develop flexible governance environments and adapt policies to facilitate the deployment of AI systems.

Promotes building human capacity and preparing for labor market changes through skills training and fair transitions for workers as AI is deployed.

Urges governments to cooperate internationally to share AI knowledge, establish global technical standards, and promote use of internationally comparable indicators for AI progress.

Instructs the Digital Policy Committee to continue advancing AI governance by developing practical guidance and reporting on the implementation of these recommendations.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah House Bill 249 (Utah Legal Personhood Amendments)
document_name: Utah HB 249 (Utah Legal Personhood Amendments)
body:
Prohibits governmental entities in Utah from granting or recognizing legal personhood for artificial intelligence and other non-human entities. Enacts restrictions effective May 1, 2024, reinforcing the exclusive legal personhood of human beings.

Prohibits governmental entities in Utah from granting or recognizing legal personhood for artificial intelligence.

Restricts legal personhood to human beings and excludes inanimate objects, bodies of water, land, real property, atmospheric gases, astronomical objects, weather, plants, nonhuman animals, or any non-human taxonomic domain.

Applies these restrictions regardless of other legal provisions.

Enacts the bill with an effective date of May 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Hawaii House Concurrent Resolution 71
document_name: Hawaii HCR 71 (2024)
body:
Request the Department of Health to convene a Stakeholder Working Group to assess language access in healthcare, including AI impacts, and to recommend enhancements. Require a report to the Legislature by 2025 detailing findings, recommendations, and proposed legislation.

Request the Department of Health to convene a Stakeholder Working Group to study language access in health care settings, focusing on the benefits and impacts of technologies such as artificial intelligence.

Instruct the Working Group to assess experiences of limited English proficiency (LEP) populations, existing language services, and disparities in health care access.

Advise the Group to make recommendations for enhancing meaningful access to health care, including options for utilizing AI-based solutions.

Require the Department of Health to invite stakeholders, including LEP individuals, health care providers, insurers, community-based organizations, and language service providers to participate in the Group.

Instruct the Department of Health to submit a report of the Group's findings and recommendations, along with proposed legislation, to the Legislature by a specified deadline.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Mississippi Senate Bill 2577
document_name: Mississippi SB 2577 (Wrongful Dissemination of Digitizations)
body:
Criminalizes dissemination of AI-generated deepfakes within 90 days of an election, without consent, intending to harm candidates or influence elections. Imposes penalties up to five years imprisonment or $10,000 fine. Exempts satire, news, and security-related activities. Effective July 1, 2024.

Establishes criminal penalties for wrongful dissemination of deepfakes, defined as realistic digital alterations of images or audio using AI or other technologies, particularly if used to influence elections.

Criminalizes dissemination within 90 days of an election without consent and with intent to harm a candidate or election outcome.

Imposes penalties of up to five years imprisonment or $10,000 fines for violations intended to incite violence or deter voting, with lesser penalties for other cases.

Allows injunctive relief actions by various parties, including the Attorney General and affected candidates, to prevent violations and remove disseminated deepfakes.

Exempts certain broadcasters and publishers, including those involved in bona fide news reporting or satire, from liability.

Requires clear labeling of deepfakes as a defense to prosecution.

Takes effect on July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration
document_name: USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration
body:
Requires USDA to guide state, local, tribal, and territorial agencies on AI use in nutrition benefits, ensuring accessibility, compliance with merit systems, notification to USDA, human review options, auditability, and equitable outcomes. Encourages responsible AI innovation while protecting rights and safety.

The framework mandates the USDA to guide states, localities, tribes, and territories in the responsible use of AI for administering USDA nutrition benefits, as per Executive Order 14110.

Ensures AI systems maximize access for eligible recipients and comply with merit system requirements.

Requires notification to the Secretary in cases of reliance on AI, allowing appeals to human reviewers and ensuring auditability of AI decisions.

Mandates equitable outcomes from AI systems and prohibits AI from directly making adverse decisions in benefits administration.

Advocates for transparency and accountability, providing opt-out options from AI systems.

Encourages responsible innovation, requiring AI usage only with appropriate training and governance.

Requires SLTT agencies to report AI usage and its impact, with ongoing monitoring to mitigate risks and biases.

Stresses collaboration with tribes to respect data sovereignty.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
org: Office of Science and Technology Policy
title: NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening
document_name: NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening
body:
Requires providers and manufacturers to implement screening for synthetic nucleic acids and equipment, identify sequences of concern, verify customer legitimacy, report suspicious orders, retain records, and enhance cybersecurity. Mandates adherence for federally funded research, with updates based on technological advances.

Mandates the federal government to mitigate misuse risks of synthetic nucleic acids by establishing a procurement screening framework.

Requires synthetic nucleic acid providers and equipment manufacturers to implement comprehensive screening measures for sequences of concern (SOCs) and verify customer legitimacy.

Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to collaborate with industry to refine technical specifications for effective screening.

Obliges federal funding agencies to ensure compliance with the framework for research funded by federal life sciences grants.

Instructs providers and manufacturers to report suspicious purchase orders to relevant authorities and retain records for at least three years.

Imposes cybersecurity measures to protect sensitive data and customer information, following specific security guidelines.

Anticipates framework updates based on technological advancements and encourages the use of independent audits for compliance verification.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
org: Department of Health and Human Services
title: HHS Public Benefits and AI
document_name: HHS Public Benefits and AI
body:
Encourages state and local governments to use AI responsibly in public benefits administration. Recommends risk assessment, fairness, transparency, human oversight, and privacy protection. Emphasizes equity, accountability, and civil rights compliance. Supports developing frameworks and resources for AI governance and innovation.

Requires the United States Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to promote responsible AI use in public benefits administration by State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Governments (STLTs).

Encourages STLTs to align with the principles of the National Institute of Standards and Technology AI Risk Management Framework and the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.

Recommends STLTs assess AI systems for equitable outcomes, notify recipients about AI use, and ensure human oversight and appeal processes.

Supports STLTs in developing AI policies and practices through guidance, technical assistance, and resources.

Urges STLTs to focus on safeguarding privacy, civil rights, and safety, and to provide opt-out options for AI systems.

Emphasizes the need for transparency, public engagement, and governance to manage AI-associated risks.

Directs HHS to work with STLTs and other agencies to ensure AI systems in public benefits programs are safe, equitable, and efficient.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
org: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms
document_name: Guidance on Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms
body:
Prohibits discriminatory use of AI in housing-related ads under the Fair Housing Act. Addresses potential violations via audience targeting, custom audiences, and algorithmic delivery. Recommends advertisers and platforms audit practices, avoid proxies for protected characteristics, and ensure equitable ad delivery.

Explains how the Fair Housing Act applies to housing-related advertising via AI and algorithmic systems on digital platforms.

Prohibits discriminatory advertising practices based on protected characteristics such as race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, or disability.

Warns that audience categorization and algorithmic delivery tools can unintentionally lead to discrimination by excluding or targeting groups based on protected characteristics.

Requires advertisers and platforms to avoid using AI tools that segment audiences by protected characteristics or proxies like geographic location.

Urges ad platforms to disable certain targeting functions for housing ads and conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with the Act.

Recommends that advertisers and platforms manage discriminatory risks by utilizing separate processes for housing-related ads and monitoring ad delivery outcomes for bias.

Advises documenting and publicly sharing information on ad targeting functions to ensure transparency and accountability.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Federal Register Doc. No. 2024-01580. Taking Additional Steps To Address the National Emergency With Respect to Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities
document_name: AI Cloud KYC Proposed Rule (Department of Commerce)
body:
Require U.S. IaaS providers to implement Customer Identification Programs (CIP) for foreign customers to prevent malicious use of AI models. 
Requires IaaS infrastructure to train large AI models which could have the potential to be used in malicious cyber-enabled activity.

Requires U.S. Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) providers to implement a Customer Identification Program (CIP) for verifying foreign customers' identities and maintaining relevant records to prevent malicious cyber activities. 

Obligates foreign resellers to adhere to similar CIP standards and mandates U.S. IaaS providers to report on these. 

Proposes regulations implementing Executive Order 13984 and Executive Order 14110

Requires IaaS providers to establish and maintain written Customer Identification Programs.  

Institutes penalties for non-compliance, including civil and criminal liabilities. 

Mandates reporting to the Department of Commerce for violations or suspicious activities associated with AI model training.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: Increasing AI Capacity Across the Federal Government: AI Talent Surge Progress and Recommendations
document_name: Increasing AI Capacity Across the Federal Government: AI Talent Surge Progress and Recommendations
body:
Implements Executive Order 14110, launching a National AI Talent Surge to recruit AI professionals for federal use, policy development, and R&D. Establishes expedited hiring authorities, training initiatives, and diverse recruitment efforts to strengthen the federal AI workforce and infrastructure.

Mandates Federal agencies strengthen AI safety, security, privacy, equity, civil rights, and innovation through Executive Order 14110, signed by President Biden.

Launches a National AI Talent Surge to recruit AI professionals into the Federal Government, enhancing AI regulatory and policy capacity, government use of AI, and AI R&D ecosystem.

Facilitates AI hiring with Direct Hire Authority and Excepted Service Appointments granted by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).

Establishes Chief AI Officers and enhances AI competencies with training programs for the Federal workforce.

Recommends funding increases for AI talent, institutionalizing tech talent programs, improving USAJOBS, and piloting skills-based hiring.

Proposes an AI scholarship-for-service program and public service cultivation within the tech ecosystem.

Encourages global AI talent engagement and provides guidance for improving Federal hiring experiences.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Florida Senate Bill 1680
document_name: Florida SB 1680 (Advanced Technology)
body:
Creates the Government Technology Modernization Council to study AI and technology, recommend regulations, assess AI's legal effects, and propose ethics reforms. Requires annual legislative recommendations to modernize technology and protect against AI misuse. Prohibits creation and possession of generated child pornography.

Create the Government Technology Modernization Council within Florida's Department of Management Services to study and monitor new technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI).

Require the council to recommend legislative and administrative actions to promote data modernization and AI system deployment, and establish AI safety standards.

Mandate the council to assess AI's impact on legal rights and its use by governmental and private entities, focusing on potential exploitation by bad actors.

Direct the council to evaluate the need for digital literacy curricula and submit annual recommendations for government technology modernization.

Prohibit knowingly possessing, controlling, or intentionally viewing generated child pornography, with violations constituting a third-degree felony.

Forbid intentionally creating generated child pornography, imposing similar felony penalties.

Prohibit reproduction of generated child pornography in criminal proceedings, ensuring secure custody by law enforcement.

Specify the act's effective date as July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Florida House Bill 919
document_name: Florida HB 919 (AI Use in Political Advertising)
body:
Requires political ads using generative AI to include a disclaimer. Specifies disclaimer format based on media type. Imposes first-degree misdemeanor for non-compliance. Authorizes complaints to the Florida Elections Commission with expedited hearings. Effective July 1, 2024.

Establishes requirements for disclaimers on political advertisements using generative artificial intelligence in Florida.

Defines "generative artificial intelligence" as a system emulating input data to create synthetic content.

Requires advertisements with AI-generated content depicting actions that did not occur to include a prominent disclaimer stating "Created in whole or in part with the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI)."

Specifies format requirements for disclaimers across various media, including print, television, internet, and audio.

Imposes first-degree misdemeanor penalties for failure to include required disclaimers, in addition to other civil penalties.

Authorizes any person to file complaints with the Florida Elections Commission for violations of this requirement.

Mandates expedited hearings for such complaints.

Sets an effective date of July 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Nebraska L 1284 (Teacher Incentive Programs), Sec. 2.
document_name: Nebraska L 1284 (Teacher Incentive Programs), Sec. 2.
body:
Creates the Dyslexia Research Grant Program for Nebraska businesses researching AI-based writing assistance for dyslexia. Limits total grants to $500,000 from the Education Future Fund. Requires compliance; misuse triggers legal action to recover funds. Allows State Board rulemaking.

Create the Dyslexia Research Grant Program, administered by the State Department of Education, to support research on AI-based writing assistance for individuals with dyslexia.

Allow privately owned businesses in Nebraska researching AI writing tools for dyslexia to apply for grants, using a prescribed form.

Limit the total grant awards to $500,000, intended to be funded by the Education Future Fund.

Require all grant funds to be used specifically for researching AI tools that use aggregate writing analytics to help develop literacy plans for dyslexic students.

Mandate notification of the Attorney General if grant funds are misused, prompting a civil action to recover funds, which are then credited back to the Education Future Fund.

Authorize the State Board of Education to adopt rules and regulations to implement the program.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Maryland House Bill 1390
document_name: Maryland H 1390 (Public School Construction Funding and Administration), Sec. 5.
body:
Requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction to report on the eligibility for school construction funding for AI weapon detection systems by December 15, 2024.

Directs the Interagency Commission on School Construction to report to the General Assembly by December 15, 2024.

Requires the report to assess the eligibility for school construction funding for artificial intelligence weapon detection systems.

category: OECD
title: [OECD] AI 권고 이행보고서(C/MIN(2024)17)
document_name: Report on the Implementation of the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence / 「인공지능에 관한 OECD 권고 이행보고서」
body:
●기관: OECD
●문서종류: 이행보고서 / OECD AI 권고 이행·확산·적실성 평가보고서
●문서명: Report on the Implementation of the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence / 「인공지능에 관한 OECD 권고 이행보고서」
●발표시점: 2024년 4월 24일
●핵심내용:OECD가 2019년 채택된 「인공지능에 관한 OECD 이사회 권고」의 이행, 확산, 지속적 적실성을 평가한 보고서임. 보고서는 OECD AI 원칙이 각국 국가 AI 전략과 규제·정책 프레임워크에 폭넓게 반영되고 있으며, 생성형 AI 등 기술 발전을 고려해 권고의 일부 업데이트가 필요하다고 분석함.
① 보고서는 OECD AI 권고가 신뢰 가능한 AI와 인권·민주적 가치 보장을 위한 최초의 정부 간 AI 표준으로서, G20 AI 원칙과 주요국 AI 정책·규제의 기반으로 활용되고 있다고 평가함
② 권고 참여국 대부분이 국가 AI 전략을 마련하고 있으며, 포용적 성장·지속가능발전·인간 중심 가치·공정성·AI 연구개발·인적역량 강화를 공통 정책방향으로 제시함
③ 현행 권고는 전반적으로 목적에 부합하지만, 생성형 AI 확산에 대응해 허위정보·오용·투명성·책임 있는 공개·피해 대응·책임 있는 기업행동 관련 내용을 보완할 필요가 있다고 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York Assembly Bill A8808A
document_name: New York A 8808, Part MM (Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Practices Act)
body:
Enacts the "Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Practices Act." Expands privacy rights against unauthorized use of likenesses through AI. Establishes liability for creating or distributing deceptive AI-altered media, particularly in election contexts. Defines penalties and enforcement mechanisms, including damages and injunctions.

Enacts laws addressing artificial intelligence (AI) deceptive practices to protect privacy and combat unauthorized digital alterations. 

Defines "digitization" as using AI and other technologies to alter realistic images or audio. 

Amends civil rights laws to establish a private right of action for false light invasion of privacy and unauthorized use of likeness or voice, including digitally altered depictions. 

Requires platforms and individuals to obtain consent before disseminating digitized images or audio depicting individuals in sensitive contexts without consent.

Mandates disclosures for political communications produced with digitized deceptive media within 60 days of an election, excluding satire, parody, or news reporting.

Prohibits coercion or impersonation using digitization, with heightened penalties for identity theft involving AI-altered representations. 

Allows legal actions against those intentionally causing emotional, financial, or social harm via AI-fabricated media. 

Incorporates these provisions into criminal and election laws, with penalties for violations and the possibility for injunctive relief.

category: 일본
title: [일본] AI 사업자 가이드라인 (제1.0판)
body:
총무성·경제산업성이 공동 발표한 일본의 핵심 AI 사업자 가이드라인. AI 개발자·제공자·이용자 전체를 포괄하며,
① 10대 AI 기본원칙(인간 중심·안전·공정·투명성·프라이버시·보안·혁신 등),
② 주체별 행동지침(개발자의 설계 의무, 제공자의 사용자 고지, 이용자의 적절 사용),
③ 각 원칙의 실천 방법과 우선순위 판단 기준,
④ EU AI Act·OECD AI 원칙·G7 Hiroshima Process와의 정합성을 의식한 국제 정합성 확보 설계를 담고 있다.
이후 1.1판(2025.03), 1.2판(2026.03)으로 지속 업데이트된다.

title: [G20] 2024 브라질 DEWG AI 세미나 의장 요약
document_name: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Social Equity and Sustainable Development – A G20 Side Event / 「사회적 형평성과 지속가능발전을 위한 인공지능 활용: G20 부대행사」
body:
●기관: G20 브라질 의장국
●문서종류: 부대행사 의장요약 / AI·지속가능발전 정책논의 결과문서
●문서명: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Social Equity and Sustainable Development – A G20 Side Event / 「사회적 형평성과 지속가능발전을 위한 인공지능 활용: G20 부대행사」
●발표시점: 2024년 4월 17일
●핵심내용:브라질 G20 의장국의 디지털경제작업반이 “지속가능발전과 불평등 완화를 위한 AI”를 주요 의제로 다루는 맥락에서 개최한 부대행사 의장요약 문서임. 학계, 정부, 산업계, 시민사회가 참여하여 AI 인프라 격차, 디지털 주권, 윤리적 AI, 인재양성, 거버넌스, 국제협력 등을 논의하고, AI가 지속가능발전과 사회적 형평성에 기여하기 위한 정책적 조건을 제시함.
① 문서는 글로벌 노스와 글로벌 사우스 간 AI 인프라·데이터·컴퓨팅·인재 격차가 불평등을 심화시킬 수 있어, 공평한 접근성과 개발도상국의 디지털 주권·전략적 자율성 강화가 필요하다고 지적함
② 윤리적 AI를 위해 인권·인간 존엄·성평등·문화·언어 다양성을 반영하고, 공공서비스 AI에는 투명성·책임성·구제절차와 공무원 AI 문해력을 보장해야 한다고 강조함
③ 다중이해관계자 기반의 상호운용 가능한 AI 거버넌스를 구축하고, 공동 인프라·기술이전·인재양성·지식공유·지역 AI 생태계 조성을 통해 AI 격차를 완화하도록 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Oregon Senate Bill 5701
document_name: Oregon S 5701 (State Financial Administration), Section 488.
body:
Increases funding by $100,000 for the University of Oregon Labor Education and Research Center to research AI and automation's potential workforce impacts across Oregon's key economic industries.

Increases the General Fund appropriation to the Higher Education Coordinating Commission for public university programs by $100,000.

Allocates this increased funding to the University of Oregon Labor Education and Research Center.

Directs the Center to research the potential workforce impacts of automation and artificial intelligence across Oregon’s key economic industries.

category: Editors' Picks;Miscellaneous documents
title: Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks
document_name: Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks
body:
Establishes a framework for federal oversight of frontier AI models to mitigate extreme risks. Proposes potential oversight entities and mandates expert involvement to address biosecurity, chemical, cybersecurity, and nuclear threats.

Establishes a framework for federal oversight of advanced AI models, termed "frontier models," to mitigate extreme AI-enabled risks like biological, chemical, cyber, and nuclear threats.

Defines frontier models as those requiring computing power exceeding 10^26 operations, and capable of diverse tasks or intended for specific high-risk areas.

Mandates entities selling or renting large computing resources to report usage and exercise due diligence, particularly concerning foreign clients.

Requires developers to notify an oversight entity before training frontier models and integrate safeguards against extreme risks.

Obligates developers to adhere to cybersecurity standards and report risk mitigation steps.

Imposes an evaluation and licensing process before deploying frontier models, using a tiered structure based on risk level to determine deployment scope.

Suggests options for an oversight entity, including an interagency body, new agency, or existing federal agencies, emphasizing expert involvement.

Tasks the oversight entity to report on emerging challenges and risks, ensuring framework adaptability.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images)
document_name: Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images)
body:
Amends Iowa law to prohibit knowingly possessing AI-created depictions of identifiable minors in prohibited sexual acts. Treats images of different minors as separate offenses; repeated violations escalate to a class "C" felony.

Amends existing law to make it unlawful to knowingly purchase or possess visual depictions of a minor engaging in a prohibited sexual act or its simulation.

Requires separate prosecution and punishment for each different minor depicted in such visual content, though multiple depictions of the same minor are treated as a single offense.

Classifies a first offense as a class "D" felony and a second or subsequent offense as a class "C" felony.

Establishes that prior convictions or deferred judgments under this law, or similar laws in other jurisdictions, constitute second or subsequent offenses.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Virginia Senate Bill 487
document_name: Virginia SB 487 (Use of Artificial Intelligence by Public Bodies)
body:
Requires JCOTS to analyze AI use by public bodies, focusing on procurement, implementation, and discrimination prevention. Instructs JCOTS to assess creating a Commission on AI to advise on related issues. Mandates JCOTS's report submission to legislative committees by December 1, 2024.

Mandates the Joint Commission on Technology and Science (JCOTS) to conduct an analysis of artificial intelligence use by public bodies in Virginia.

Requires JCOTS analysis to include examination public bodies' policies & procedures on AI procurement, implementation, and assessment of AI systems. 

Requires JCOTS analysis to also ensure public bodies continually review the impact of AI systems to avoid discrimination and unlawful outcomes against an individual or a group.

Mandates consideration of establishing a Commission on Artificial Intelligence to advise the General Assembly on AI-related issues.

Requires JCOTS to evaluate the composition and duties of this commission based on specified criteria.

Obligates JCOTS to report findings and recommendations to relevant House and Senate committees by December 1, 2024.

category: AI SAFETY SUMMIT
title: [AI SAFETY SUMMIT] The Bletchley Declaration

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024
document_name: The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024, Rule 25. "Generative AI"
body:
Require parties using generative AI for court documents to disclose its use and name the specific tool. Include examples like ChatGPT, Bing AI, or Google Bard. Ensure compliance with existing filing standards under 12 O.S. §2011.

Require any attorney, pro se defendant, victim, or other party using generative AI in drafting documents for the Municipal Criminal Court to disclose the use of such AI.

Specify the name of the generative AI tool used in the filing.

Include ChatGPT, Bing AI, and Google Bard under the definition of generative AI.

Maintain the applicability of 12 O.S. §2011 to all filings, ensuring compliance is certified by the person signing the document.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Washington Senate Bill 5950
document_name: Washington S 5950, Sec. 129, Subsection 50
body:
Provide $300,000 in 2024 and $500,000 in 2025 for Seattle to lease space for technology startups, focusing on AI, and to develop curricula for worker skills in AI as a business resource.

Allocate $300,000 from the general fund for fiscal year 2024 to the city of Seattle for leasing space dedicated to nonprofit and academic institutions.

Provide $500,000 for fiscal year 2025 for the same purpose.

Focus efforts on incubating technology business startups with an emphasis on artificial intelligence.

Support the development and teaching of curricula aimed at equipping workers with skills to utilize AI as a business resource.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Virginia 2024 SB 731
document_name: Virginia SB 731 (Child Pornography)
body:
Amends the state's definition of child pornography to explicitly include visual material where "the minor depicted does not have to actually exist". Establishes mandatory prison sentences based on the age difference and repeat offenses, with substantial penalties for violations.

Defines "child pornography" to include sexually explicit visual material involving identifiable minors or minors who "do not have to actually exist," thus affecting both real and digitally created images.

Establishes penalties for production, solicitation, and financing of child pornography, escalating based on the minor’s age and the offender's age difference, with mandatory minimum sentences.

Permits the age of the depicted person to be inferred by the visual material's "text, title or appearance," confirming that proof of the subject's actual age is not required for prosecution.

Allows for venue of prosecution in the jurisdiction where the unlawful act occurs, the offender resides, or where the sexually explicit visual material is produced, stored, or possessed.

Notes that the provisions of the act may result in a net increase in periods of imprisonment, requiring the Virginia Criminal Sentencing Commission to assign a minimum fiscal impact of $50,000 for adult correctional facilities due to an unknown appropriation amount.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act preventing a dystopian work environment.
document_name: An Act preventing a dystopian work environment.
body:
Mandates that Massachusetts employers inform workers of the use of automated decision systems, requires impact assessments on such systems, and sets conditions under which they can be used.

Mandates that employers inform workers of data collection and distribution, including inputs for Automated Decision Systems (ADS), bans employers from collecting data for non-necessary business purposes, and mandates security measures to protect worker data.

Requires employers to inform workers before ADS use and annually provide workers with notice of all ADS in use, bans ADS use for employment decisions where there is potential for bias and/or discrimination, and requires third-party impact assessments to be conducted on such systems before and after use.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Oregon Senate Bill 1571
document_name: Oregon SB 1571 (AI in Campaign Ads)
body:
Require campaign communications using synthetic media to disclose manipulation. Allow the Secretary of State and Attorney General to enforce compliance through legal actions and penalties. Exempt certain media and satire. Enable rule adoption for implementation. Declare an emergency for immediate effect.

Mandates that campaign communications using synthetic media include a disclosure stating the manipulation of images, audio, or video.

Allows the Secretary of State and the Attorney General to initiate legal proceedings to prevent violations of the requirement for disclosure in campaign communications using synthetic media.

Imposes a civil penalty of up to $10,000 for violations, with penalties directed to the State Treasury's General Fund.

Excludes certain media providers, broadcasters, and publications from the disclosure requirement, provided they acknowledge potential authenticity issues or involve satire or parody.

Adds the new provisions to Oregon Revised Statutes chapter 260 and amends ORS 260.345 to incorporate enforcement mechanisms for violations involving synthetic media in campaign communications.

Permits the Secretary of State to establish rules to implement these provisions.

Declares an emergency for immediate enactment to preserve public peace, health, and safety.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Oregon House Bill 4153
document_name: Oregon HB 4153 (AI Task Force)
body:
Establishes a 14-member Task Force on Artificial Intelligence in Oregon. Requires examination of AI-related terms for legislation, aligning with federal definitions. Directs submission of a report by December 1, 2024. Declares an emergency for immediate effect.

Establishes the Task Force on Artificial Intelligence in Oregon, comprising 14 members with diverse expertise.

Requires task force members to have proficiency in computer science, AI, technology industries, workforce development, or data privacy.

Mandates the task force to examine and define AI-related terms for potential legislation, aligning closely with federal definitions.

Requires the task force to gather input from a wide range of stakeholders, including academia, consumer groups, and businesses.

Directs the task force to report recommendations to an interim committee by December 1, 2024.

Provides that the Legislative Policy and Research Director offers staff support, and state agencies assist the task force.

Specifies that the task force ceases on January 1, 2025, with an emergency declared for the act's immediate implementation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Idaho House Bill 664 (Freedom From AI-Rigged Elections Act)
document_name: Idaho HB 664 (Freedom From AI-Rigged Elections Act)
body:
Prohibits publishing synthetic media in electioneering communications without disclosure. Allows candidates to seek legal relief and damages. Establishes liability for content providers and certain media. Requires clear evidence and encourages expedited court proceedings. Provides exceptions and severability.

Enacts the "Freedom From AI-Rigged (FAIR) Elections Act" to regulate synthetic media in electioneering communications.

Defines "synthetic media" as altered audio or video intended to mislead about real events or speech through advanced digital techniques.

Allows candidates misrepresented by synthetic media to seek injunctive relief and damages against the creators or distributors.

Requires disclosures on synthetic media: a visible text or audible notice stating the media is manipulated.

Places the burden on plaintiffs to prove synthetic media use by clear and convincing evidence.

Holds information content providers liable, not the medium, unless disclosures are altered or removed.

Encourages courts to resolve cases swiftly.

Declares provisions severable to maintain the act's enforceability if parts are invalidated.

Implements the act immediately upon passage due to an emergency declaration.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Wyoming House Bill 1
document_name: Wyoming H 1 (General Government Appropriations), Section 067
body:
Allocates $2.5 million to build AI expertise at the University of Wyoming, conditioned on equal matching funds from non-public entities. Excludes funds from future budgets to encourage temporary, targeted development efforts in AI infrastructure and capability.

Appropriates $2.5 million for building artificial intelligence expertise at the University of Wyoming, requiring a matching ratio of 1:1 from non-public sources.

Specifies that the AI-related funding should not be included in the university's standard budget for the next fiscal biennium.

Conditions the use of AI funds upon securing matched contributions from individuals, partnerships, corporations, or other entities.

Prohibits the transfer or expenditure of AI appropriation for any purpose other than building AI expertise.

Includes intent for developing AI expertise funding to be temporary and contingent on nonstate matching funds.

States that the appropriation's intent is not to support any office or program related to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Overall, emphasizes the development of AI expertise through matched funding, with specific conditions and limitations on its use and future budget inclusion.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report: Policies, Principles & Guidelines
document_name: Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report, County Administrative Order (EMPLOYEE USE OF AI)
body:
Requires Miami-Dade County employees under the Mayor to use artificial intelligence (AI) tools ethically and responsibly. Instructs the Human Resources (HR) and Information Technology Departments (ITD) to provide necessary training and oversight. Directs ITD to oversee AI procurement, deployment, and data security. Establishes guidelines for AI training, risk assessments, data handling, and community engagement, ensuring compliance with privacy and ethical standards.

Guides Miami-Dade County employees in the responsible and ethical use of AI, focusing on transparency, data security, and privacy.

Requires adherence to public records laws and ethical guidelines.

Instructs the Human Resources and Information Technology Departments to provide AI training, emphasizing ethical use, bias recognition, and data management.

Mandates risk assessments prior to AI implementation.

Tasks the Information Technology Department with overseeing AI procurement, deployment, and system security.

Establishes protocols for data governance, encryption, and privacy.

Defines roles for directors, supervisors, and employees in AI project management, ethical leadership, and compliance.

Implements regular audits, assessments, and vendor evaluations to maintain AI system integrity.

Encourages community engagement and stakeholder discussions on AI deployment.

Commits to continuous improvement with annual assessments and updates by the IT Department, involving multidisciplinary teams and beta testing initiatives.

Provides resources through the IT Department’s website.

category: UN
title: [UN] 지속가능발전을 위한 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰할 수 있는 인공지능 시스템의 기회 활용(A/RES/78/265)
document_name: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development / 「지속가능발전을 위한 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰할 수 있는 인공지능 시스템의 기회 활용」
body:
●기관: 유엔 총회(UN General Assembly)
●문서종류: 결의 / AI와 지속가능발전 관련 총회 결의
●문서명: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development / 「지속가능발전을 위한 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰할 수 있는 인공지능 시스템의 기회 활용」
●채택시점: 2024년 3월 21일
●핵심내용:동 결의는 유엔 총회가 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 시스템을 통해 2030 지속가능발전의제와 17개 SDGs 달성을 가속화하고, 국가 간·국내 AI 및 디지털 격차를 해소할 필요성을 제시한 문서임. 결의는 AI의 설계·개발·배치·사용 전 생애주기에서 인권과 기본적 자유를 존중·보호·증진해야 하며, 국제법과 양립할 수 없거나 인권 향유에 과도한 위험을 초래하는 AI 시스템 사용을 중단해야 한다고 강조함.
① 결의는 안전하고 신뢰 가능한 AI가 보건·교육·빈곤퇴치·기후대응 등 SDGs 달성에 기여할 수 있으나, 부적절한 활용은 불평등·차별·정보무결성 훼손·프라이버시 침해 등 위험을 확대할 수 있다고 지적함
② 국가·국내 AI 격차 해소와 개발도상국의 참여 확대를 위해 역량강화·기술이전·금융·디지털 인프라를 지원하고, 각국에는 위험 식별·평가·시험·완화를 포함한 책임 있는 AI 거버넌스를 구축하도록 권고함
③ AI 전 생애주기의 데이터·보안·인권·비차별·인간 감독과 구제절차를 강화하고, 공정한 데이터 거버넌스와 국경 간 데이터 협력 및 중소기업·인재의 참여 확대를 촉진하도록 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Wisconsin Act 2023-123 (Artificial Intelligence Content Disclosure)
document_name: Wisconsin Act 2023-123 (AI Content Disclosure)
body:
Requires the disclosure of AI generative content in political advertisements. Amends the 11.1303 title to define synthetic media. Enforces fines for violations.

Amends the 11.1303 title to define synthetic media.

Defines synthetic media as audio or video produced in part by generative artificial intelligence.

Requires that any issue advocacy communications that contain any AI should include a writing stating "Contains content generated by AI".

Requires the label to be visible through each portion containing synthetic media.

States that compliance does not create any exemption from civil or criminal liability.

Enforces fines of up to $ 1,000 for each violation.

Mandates that the liability only affects the person responsible for the communication.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Utah House Bill 534
document_name: Utah H 534 (Boards and Commissions Modifications), Section 55-56
body:
Amends the law to oversee a deep technology initiative, including funding expanded educational programs in areas like artificial intelligence. Requires collaboration with employers and evaluation by an advisory council. Mandates institutions report annually on program outcomes and funding effectiveness.

Amends legislation to define "deep technology" to include artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Mandates the development and oversight of a deep technology talent initiative by the board, effective May 1, 2024.

Requires institutions of higher education to submit proposals for partnering with employers to create programs in deep technology fields.

Stipulates proposal criteria must include program responsiveness to state needs, partnerships, and employer involvement.

Obligates the advisory council to review and prioritize program proposals based on capacity expansion, integration, and cost-effectiveness.

Directs the board to fund approved programs by evaluating recommendations from the advisory council and considering legislative appropriations.

Requires funded institutions to report annually on program activities and outcomes, including student enrollment and employment metrics.

Compels the board to provide an annual report on program successes and challenges to legislative committees.

category: Editors' Picks;U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 39, Chapter 14, Part 1 and Title 47, relative to the protection of personal rights.
document_name: ELVIS Act (Tennessee)
body:
Amends Tennessee law to protect individuals' rights to their name, photograph, voice, or likeness, including simulated versions, against unauthorized commercial use. Imposes liability for unauthorized AI-generated likenesses. Allows fair use exceptions and extends rights posthumously. Effective July 1, 2024.

Expands the "Personal Rights Protection Act of 1984," renaming it the "Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security Act of 2024."

Grants individuals property rights over their name, photograph, voice, or likeness across all mediums.

Defines "voice" to include both actual and simulated sounds identifiable to an individual.

Terminates exclusive commercial rights after two years of non-use, beginning ten years after death.

Imposes civil liability for the unauthorized commercial use of an individual's name, photograph, voice, or likeness.

Prohibits distribution of technology primarily used to produce unauthorized likenesses. 

Allows individuals or parties with exclusive contracts for personal services or sound recordings to enforce rights. 

Exempts certain uses protected by the First Amendment as fair use, including news, commentary, and satire. 

Mandates that employees or owners of any medium used for advertising be liable if they publish or disseminate an advertisement in violation of this act, and if they should have known about the violation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Washington Senate Bill 5838 (2024)
document_name: Washington S 5838 (Artificial Intelligence Task Force)
body:
Establishes a task force to assess AI use and trends, recommending guidelines and legislation. Requires examination of AI's impact on safety, privacy, and rights. Mandates reports by 2026. Defines AI-related terms. Task force expires June 30, 2027.

Establishes a task force in Washington State to assess current AI uses and trends and recommend guidelines and potential legislation for AI systems.

Composes the task force of an executive committee with appointed members from legislative bodies, the attorney general's office, technology experts, industry representatives, and community advocates.

Charges the task force with examining AI development and use, focusing on safety, privacy, and civil rights, and submitting recommendations to the legislature.

Mandates a literature review on AI public policy issues, analysis of existing legal protections, and proposals for ethical AI guidelines and high-risk AI use identification.

Tasks the office of the attorney general with administering the task force, retaining consultants, and supporting subcommittee formation.

Requires the task force to deliver reports to the governor and legislature, with a final report due by July 1, 2026.

Expires the task force on June 30, 2027.

category: Editors' Picks;Chinese law and policy
title: Artificial Intelligence Law of the People’s Republic of China (Draft for Suggestions from Scholars)
document_name: Artificial Intelligence Law of the People’s Republic of China (Scholars' Draft)
body:
Outlines key principles and aims for innovative and safe AI development use in the public and private sector. Details compliance and supervision mechanisms, with special attention to critical AI. Encourages international cooperation and imposes penalties for non-compliance measures.

Mandates the regulation of AI development and use activities within and outside China if they affect Chinese national interests.

Establishes principles of ethics, fairness, transparency, safety, and accountability in AI development and use.

Establishes aims and support measures for AI adoption, infrastructure development and supports data sharing, compute resources, and algorithmic innovation.

Protects intellectual property laws, user privacy rights and encourages applications of energy efficient AI products.

Implements a comprehensive oversight and coordination framework involving multiple government agencies. Mandate compliance with safety and security assessments, especially for critical AI systems.

Provides legal liability structures for violations, including administrative penalties, tort liability, and public interest litigation.

Promotes international cooperation in AI governance and allows for countermeasures against discriminatory foreign actions.
