category: U.S. federal laws;NDAA provisions;FY2024 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence")
body:
Directs Secretary of Defense to implement a bug bounty program on DoD AI use and a competition on AI detection and watermarking. Instructs Secretary of Defense to develop guidance on various aspects of AI use within DoD, including bias mitigation, security, and human oversight of autonomous systems, and mandates a study on vulnerabilities of AI in the military.

Updates and extends the DoD's AI and ML acquisition framework and requires a plan for acquisition authority delegation and a demonstration of acquisition authority capabilities.

Mandates the creation of a bug bounty program for foundational AI models within the DoD, promoting collaboration with federal entities and cybersecurity experts. Requires briefing the congressional defense committees on the program within one year.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a competition to advance technologies for detecting and watermarking generative AI content. Requires annual briefing to the congressional defense committees.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to issue DoD-wide guidance and policy on AI, including with regard to ethical AI use, bias mitigation, cybersecurity, technical workforce assessments, AI literacy needs and related training programs, protection against adversarial AI, protecting the intellectual property of DoD AI system suppliers, AI's potential role in developing offensive actions, availability of inputs for AI, verification and evaluation frameworks, potential vulnerabilities of AI models and human oversight of autonomous systems. Requires briefing the congressional defense committees within 150 days.

Requires a study on the vulnerabilities of AI-enabled military applications, focusing on explainability, security risks, and the integration of decision support systems, with a final report for the congressional defense committees detailing findings and research gaps.

document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management")
body:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a council known as the ‘Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council’ to provide policy oversight in order to ensure the responsible, and ethical employment of data and artificial intelligence capabilities across Department of Defense missions; requires any data collection, use, or retention measure to be compliant with applicable laws; establishes a pilot program to assess the feasibility and advisability of implementing industry open technical standards.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish the 'Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council' to oversee policy ensuring responsible and ethical use of data and AI in Department of Defense missions.

Requires  The council, led by the Chief Digital and AI Officer, to develop, implement, and oversee AI, coordinating governance, and providing ethical guidance. 

Instructs the council to identify, monitor, and update recommendations for AI use, review program funding,  and ensure compliance with AI policies. 

Instructs the council to issue guidance on access and distribution restrictions relating to data, models, tool sets, testing or validation infrastructure.

Instructs the council to implement and oversee an educational program on data and artificial intelligence, to familiarize personnel department on the applications of artificial intelligence.

Mandates all data collection, use, or retention measures  to comply with relevant laws and regulations, including those concerning data related to US persons.

Requires an establishment of a course of education at the Defense Information School, the purpose of which shall be to provide instruction on the practical concepts and skills.

Instructs the Director of the Defense Media Activity to carry out a pilot program to assess the feasibility and advisability of implementing industry open technical standards for digital content provenance for official photographs and videos of the Department of Defense

Creates a new Office of Strategic Capital in the Department of Defense.

Directs the new Office to invest in companies developing critical technologies, including autonomous robots, that may benefit the Department of Defense. 

Permits the Office to launch a pilot program for providing capital assistance that supports the defense industrial base. 

Requires the Office's investments to meet certain criteria, including restrictions on interest rates and loan repayment periods as well as requirements for non-Federal investments in selected companies, subject to various exceptions. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees an annual report on the Office's activities, in addition to notifying the congressional defense committees whenever it provides capital assistance.

category: U.S. federal laws;NDAA provisions;FY2024 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process")
body:
Requires the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to develop a streamlined requirements development process for the Department of Defense; requires  processes for software, artificial intelligence, data, and related capability areas to be more rapid and iterative than the requirements processes for traditional hardware systems. Requires the Secretary of Defense to cooperate  with other military leaders.

Requires the Secretary of Defense in coordination with military leaders to develop streamlined requirements of development processes for the Department of Defense, in order to modernize war fighting technology and reduce the time needed to deliver capabilities to warfighters.

Requires revisions to requirements management practices that maximizes the use of commercial products or services and allow for a broader range of new or alternative technological opportunities to be incorporated without the requirement being validated again.

Establishes a process to rapidly validate the ability of commercial products and services to meet capability needs or opportunities.

Requires retiring and replacing the Department of Defense Architecture Framework with a new structure focused on enabling interoperability  through application program interfaces, enterprise architectures and platforms, and government and commercial standards.

Requires the secretary to develop a formal career path, training, and structure for requirements managers.

Establishes the required processes for software, artificial intelligence, data, and related capability areas to be more rapid and iterative than the requirements processes for traditional hardware systems.

Requires the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to collaborate with industry partners, contractors, and Department of Defense science and technology reinvention laboratories in designing the new requirements development process.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees an interim report and a final report on the development and implementation of the new requirements development process.

document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7513 ("Policies established by Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence capabilities")
body:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to implement policies for the third-party acquisition, development, and use of artificial intelligence capabilities.

Instructs the Director of National Intelligence, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and other intelligence officials to maintain, develop, and annually revise various AI policies.

Requires the establishment of a lexicon relating to machine learning and AI use by the intelligence community.

Requires the establishment of guidelines for evaluating model performance by specifying conditions for AI capability monitoring, documenting performance objectives, specifying model auditing processes, and specifying conditions for vulnerability testing and privacy evaluations.

Requires the establishment of guidelines for tracking dependencies in related systems, documentation requirements for capabilities procured from third-party and training data usage, and guidance on the usage of third-party-trained models.

title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7510 ("Requirement to ensure intelligence community directives appropriately account for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools in intelligence products")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7510 ("Requirement to ensure intelligence community directives appropriately account for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools in intelligence products")
body:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief Congress on whether existing directives provide sufficient guidance on the use of AI in intelligence and, if necessary, on a plan to update the guidance.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief the congressional appropriations and intelligence committees on whether intelligence community directives provide sufficient guidance on how to use, document, and disclose AI and machine learning tools in intelligence. 

Requires the Director to either (a) justify the assertion that existing intelligence community directives do sufficiently provide such guidance or (b) provide a plan and timeline for updating the directives as necessary.

title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence")
body:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to establish or oversee a program to advance microelectronics research, focused on applications in artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence, acting through the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity, to establish or oversee a program to advance microelectronics research. 

Requires the program described above to focus on applications in artificial intelligence, advanced computing, advanced computing materials, optical communication networks, quantum technologies, or other emerging technologies. 

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to consider a variety of factors when crafting the research program, including input from the Secretary of Commerce and from an array of stakeholders including representatives of industry and academia.

Requires the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity to brief the congressional intelligence, appropriations, and commerce committees on the progress of the research program described above and recommendations for future research priorities.

category: U.S. federal laws;NDAA provisions;FY2024 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 7356 ("Analysis of commercial cloud initiatives of intelligence community")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7356 ("Analysis of commercial cloud initiatives of intelligence community")
body:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to (a) analyze the intelligence community's commercial cloud initiatives -- including their ability to support artificial intelligence capabilities -- and (b) brief the congressional intelligence and appropriations committees on the findings of that analysis.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to produce a comprehensive analysis of the intelligence community's cloud initiatives relating to the Commercial Cloud Enterprise contract entered into by the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency in November of 2020. 

Requires the above analysis to include projected cloud computing costs, plans for the termination of legacy data storage mechanisms, an assessment of the value and efficacy of cloud computing tools and analytics, and the suitability of existing computing arrangements to service artificial intelligence systems for the intelligence community. 

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief the congressional intelligence and appropriations committees on the findings of the analysis detailed above.

document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 6303 ("Establishment of the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of State")

Creates the position of Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer within the Department of State.

Creates the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer position, who will be responsible for (a) the evaluation and facilitation of responsible AI and machine learning usage and (b) advising the Secretary of State on ethical AI and analytics usage in diplomacy.

Instructs the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer to partner with the Chief Information Officer on scaling AI use cases.

document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization")
body:
Requires the Secretary of the Navy to (a) develop a strategy for using artificial intelligence to better predict maintenance needs at U.S. Navy shipyards, and (b) evaluate the potential maintenance cost savings of doing so.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy, in coordination with the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program of the Department of the Navy, to develop a strategy for using artificial intelligence to better predict maintenance needs at U.S. Navy shipyards.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to evaluate the potential cost savings of adopting artificial intelligence predictive maintenance technologies.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to brief congressional defense committees on the strategy and evaluation described above.

title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence")
body:
Mandates the Department of Defense, in partnership with the Air Force, to launch a pilot program to optimize the logistics of aerial refueling and fuel management using  artificial intelligence and advanced digital technologies.

Mandates the Department of Defense and the Air Force to work together in launching a pilot program that optimizes aerial refueling and fuel management using artificial intelligence and advanced digital technologies.

Directs the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer to (a) coordinate with the Commander of the United States Transportation Command and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to align the pilot program with existing operational requirements and (b) consult relevant experts in AI.

Requires the pilot program to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of artificial intelligence-driven approaches and evaluate the interoperability and compatibility of artificial intelligence-enabled systems with the existing logistics infrastructure of the Department of Defense.

Requires an assessment of potential challenges and risks associated with the integration of artificial intelligence and other advanced digital technologies, including those related to cybersecurity.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer to submit a report on the pilot program's design, progress, and results to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate within one year.

category: U.S. federal laws;NDAA provisions;FY2024 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 253 ("Annual review of status of implementation plan for digital engineering career tracks")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 253 ("Annual review of status of implementation plan for digital engineering career tracks")
body:
Requires an annual report on the Department of Defense's digital engineer career track plan by the Secretary of Defense to Congress, including an assessment of how advances in machine learning affect the plan.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct annually, through 2029, an internal review of the Department of Defense's plan for the digital engineer career track. The review shall include consideration of how the rapid rate of technological change in data science and machine learning may affect the implementation of the plan.

Requires the Secretary to submit annually, through 2029, a report to the congressional defense committees on the findings of that internal review. The report shall include the Secretary's plan for addressing the digital engineer personnel needs of the Department.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to brief the congressional defense committees on the nature and purpose of any modifications to Department of Defense Directive 300.09, which relates to autonomy in weapons systems, within 30 days of making the modifications.

category: U.S. federal laws;NDAA provisions;FY2024 NDAA
title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices")
document_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices")
body:
Submit matrices that detail engineering, manufacturing, and development for Next Generation Air Dominance and Collaborative Combat Aircraft programs to congressional defense committees as well as the Comptroller General. 

Provide updates on progress and cost estimates every 6 months.

Develops key performance parameters for the program and its objectives to make sure there is transparency and oversight within the system.

Submit goals for Next Generation Air Dominance and Collaborative Combat Aircraft programs to congressional defense committees and the Comptroller General concurrent with the President's budget submission. Include key milestones, testing events, and performance goals, subdivided into six-month increments. 

Provide information on technology readiness levels, design maturity, software maturity, integration maturity, manufacturing readiness levels, reliability, availability for flight operations, and maintainability.

Provide updates on progress and cost estimates for the program every 6 months. It details progress made toward the goals identified in the matrices and provides updated cost estimates for air vehicles, propulsion, mission systems, software, program management, system test and evaluation, support and training systems, and more.

Develop key performance parameters (cost KPPs) for cost thresholds and objectives for the programs. Specify threshold and objective values for categories such as unit recurring flyaway cost, average procurement unit cost, gross/weapon system unit cost, aircraft cost-per-tail-per-year, and aircraft cost-per-flight-hour. 

Ensure that each Secretary concerned works on these parameters for the respective programs and includes them in the related documents.

Ensure assessment of the sufficiency of matrices by the Comptroller General, who will review them and submit assessments to congressional defense committees, identifying any cost, schedule, or performance trends.

Grants the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer authority to access and control data on behalf of the Secretary of Defense and establishes a council to oversee the responsible deployment of AI across Department of Defense operations.

body:
Requires the Secretary of the Army to submit to Congress a report on the strategy 
of the Army for tactical wheeled vehicles -- including autonomous vehicles -- for FY 2025, 2030, and 2035. The report shall include a description of the force structure and funding necessary for the tactical wheeled vehicle program to support the U.S.'s national security strategy.

Requires the Secretary of the Army to submit to Congress a report on the strategy of the Army for tactical wheeled vehicles, including autonomous vehicles. The report shall be submitted with the budget justification materials submitted in support of the budget of the Department of Defense for each of FY 2025, 2030, and 2035.

Requires the report to include a description of the force structure and funding necessary for the tactical wheeled vehicle program to support the U.S.'s national security strategy, along with detailed rundown of a program for the construction of tactical wheeled vehicles and the estimated cost of such a program. 

Requires the Secretary of the Army to, within 15 days of the budget materials submission described above, brief the congressional defense committees on the investment needed for each platform of tactical wheeled vehicle.

title: OpenAI Preparedness Framework (Beta)
document_name: OpenAI Preparedness Framework (Beta)
body:
Introduces OpenAI's Preparedness Framework to track, evaluate, forecast, and mitigate catastrophic AI risks. Establishes processes for risk evaluation, unknown risk identification, safety baselines, and cross-functional advisory. Limits model deployment or development based on risk levels. Forms a dedicated Preparedness team and Safety Advisory Group to oversee safety measures and decision-making.

Commits to continually evaluating and forecasting key areas of risk along several Tracked Risk Categories and indicating current pre- and post-mitigation risk in a Scorecard.

Commits to establishing safety baselines where only models with a post-mitigation score of "medium" or below can be deployed and only models with a post-mitigation score of "high" or below can be developed further.

Announces creation of a Safety Advisory Group to assist OpenAI leadership and Board of Directors with making safety decisions by overseeing risk assessments and handling emergency scenarios via fast-track process.

Tasks Preparedness team with conducting research, evaluations, and forecasting of risks, submitting regular reports to the Safety Advisory Group, coordinating with other OpenAI teams on recommended mitigations, and managing safety drills and third-party auditing.

title: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligence: Regulations and Ethics
document_name: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligence: Regulations and Ethics
body:
Promotes responsible AI innovation through sector-specific regulation, risk-based approaches, and "soft" regulatory tools. Establishes an AI Policy Coordination Center to advise and coordinate AI regulation, fostering international consistency. Recommends adopting ethical AI principles and creating tools for responsible AI development.

Establishes a governmental policy framework for AI regulation, emphasizing sector-specific regulation and consistency with international approaches.

Adopts a risk-based approach and promotes incremental development and regulatory experimentation.

Encourages the use of "soft" regulatory tools and multistakeholder cooperation.

Recommends adopting ethical AI principles based on the OECD AI Principles, focusing on growth, human-centric AI, equality, transparency, reliability, and accountability.

Proposes the creation of an AI Policy Coordination Center to advise regulators, promote inter-agency coordination, and lead international representation.

Mandates mapping AI uses and associated challenges in regulated sectors.

Calls for the establishment of forums for regulators and public participation to ensure coordination and open discussions.

Urges active involvement in international forums to develop AI regulation and standards.

Advocates developing tools for responsible AI, including a risk management framework.

title: Illinois Senate Bill 382
document_name: Illinois SB 382 (Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Sexual Images)
body:
Amends the Act to include liability exceptions for good faith dissemination of digitally altered sexual images. Specifies exceptions don't apply if dissemination serves sexual arousal or commercial gain. Clarifies images with political messages aren't public concern solely due to public figures.

Amends the Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act to include "digitally altered sexual image" as a defined term, expanding the scope of protection to cover images that are substantially altered to falsely appear authentic.

Specifies that exceptions to liability apply to both private sexual images and digitally altered sexual images, maintaining exceptions for good faith actions by law enforcement, legal proceedings, medical education, and reports of unlawful or unwelcome conduct.

Clarifies that the dissemination of a private or digitally altered sexual image is not a matter of public concern solely because it involves a public figure or is accompanied by a political message.

Retains provisions that a parent or guardian is not liable for dissemination unless done for prohibited purposes, such as sexual gratification or commercial gain. 

Establishes that the Act takes effect upon becoming law, without acceleration or delay from previous or other legislative changes.

document_name: Ohio State Administrative Policy on AI
body:
Establishes statewide governance for AI use by Ohio state agencies, including AI solution development, procurement, security, and privacy requirements. Mandates AI Council oversight, training for workforce use, vendor compliance, and ongoing monitoring for data quality and bias.

Establishes statewide governance for AI implementation, emphasizing data protection and quality in Ohio.

Requires state agencies to document and approve AI use cases and submit them to the AI Council for approval.

Mandates testing and ongoing monitoring to prevent bias and errors in AI outputs.

Requires human oversight to verify AI decisions, especially those impacting legal or regulatory areas.

Dictates AI procurement procedures, ensuring security, privacy, and proper data licensing.

Charges the Ohio Department of Administrative Services with developing AI training for state workers, emphasizing ethical considerations and the responsible use of generative AI.

Mandates security and privacy controls, prohibiting the input of sensitive data into generative AI without consent.

Instructs the Chief Data Officer Council to establish data governance for AI, focusing on data integrity and regulation.

Assigns the multi-agency AI Council with overseeing AI use, evaluating societal impacts, and maintaining AI solution repositories.

title: Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0
document_name: Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0
body:
Seeks to establish AI as a public good in Singapore; aiming to build excellence and empowerment through industry, government, and research collaboration. Prioritizes infrastructure, talent, and trusted AI governance.

Aims to harness AI for public good and position Singapore as a leader in AI innovation. 

Sets two primary goals: achieving excellence in AI to maximize value creation and empowering communities to use AI with confidence. 

Outlines a focus on three systems: Activity Drivers, People & Communities, and Infrastructure & Environment, supported by 10 enablers. 

Plans to establish AI Centers of Excellence, strengthen the AI start-up ecosystem, and drive public sector AI adoption. 

Aims to attract global AI talent and boost its AI practitioner pool to support AI demand. 

Emphasizes building a trusted AI environment through updated regulatory frameworks, security measures, and international collaboration. 

Seeks to enhance data management and privacy technologies for responsible AI development and position Singapore as a global AI governance leader.

Encourages making more public sector data available for AI development that serves the Public Good.

title: Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023
document_name: Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 (Commission on AI Development)
body:
Establishes a study commission to review and recommend policies for the City's AI use, emphasizing trustworthy, transparent AI applications. Requires public input, expert engagement, and collaboration with local departments. Mandates a final report by July 2024 for policy guidance.

Establishes a study commission named the "Commission on Artificial Intelligence Development" to review and analyze the City and County's current use of artificial intelligence.

Requires the commission to gather insights from AI experts, industry leaders, and community members on future AI applications to improve city services.

Mandates the commission to recommend policies for trustworthy and transparent AI usage to the Mayor and City-County Council.

Directs the commission to suggest modifications or new ordinances for AI usage.

Composes the commission of nine members, including Councillors, IT directors, and citizen members, all residents of Marion County.

Requires city departments to share information and cooperate with the commission.

Obligates the commission to present a final report by the July 2024 meeting, available on the City’s website.

Initiates operations as soon as practical and outlines a meeting and research timeline. 

Permits public comment under commission-devised rules.

title: Michigan House Bill 5144 of 2023 (Election Law)
document_name: Michigan HB 2023-5144 (Election Law)
body:
Prohibits distributing AI-generated deceptive media within 90 days before elections if intended to harm a candidate or deceive voters. Requires disclaimers for exceptions. Penalizes violations with fines and imprisonment. Allows injunctive relief by affected parties or the attorney general.

Prohibits the distribution of materially deceptive media produced by artificial intelligence within 90 days of an election if intended to harm a candidate's reputation or alter voting behavior.

Exempts media with a clear disclaimer that it has been manipulated and includes a citation to the original source.

Classifies violations as a misdemeanor for the first offense and a felony for subsequent offenses within five years.

Allows the attorney general, affected individuals, candidates, or voter organizations to seek permanent injunctive relief in certain courts.

Requires that injunctive relief complaints be non-frivolous and supported by clear and convincing evidence.

Defines "materially deceptive media" as AI-generated content that falsely depicts individuals in misleading ways.

Conditions the act's effectiveness on the enactment of House Bill No. 5143.

title: Boise Regulations 4.30q City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
document_name: Boise Regulations 4.30q (City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI))
body:
Requires Boise's city departments and contractors to obtain IT approval for AI use, validate AI-generated content before publication, disclose AI use in significant communications, and avoid sharing sensitive data in AI prompts. Promotes transparency, ethical AI governance, and continuous improvement.

Mandates IT Department approval before accessing or acquiring AI products, with a maintained list of approved AI technologies.

Requires fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content, especially for public communications, to ensure accuracy, proper attribution, and absence of bias or harmful material.

Stipulates disclosure of AI usage in significant public communications to build trust and transparency.

Prohibits sharing sensitive or private information in AI prompts to prevent unintended data exposure.

Directs annual reviews and updates of the regulation to align with technological advancements and best practices.

Tasks the Information Technology department with overseeing AI initiatives, compliance, and periodic audits for effectiveness and ethical considerations.

Aims to govern AI use responsibly and ethically, enhancing public services and fostering innovation for community benefit.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Michigan House Bill 5141
document_name: Michigan HB 5141 (Campaign Practices)
body:
Requires political advertisements generated substantially by AI to include disclaimers indicating AI involvement. Mandates specific formatting for AI disclaimers in graphic, audio, and video ads. Establishes fines for non-compliance and outlines exemptions for certain media and platforms.

Amends campaign finance law to require that political advertisements generated substantially by artificial intelligence include a clear and conspicuous statement indicating AI involvement.

Mandates that AI-generated political advertisements in graphic form display the statement in large text, while audio communications must audibly disclose AI use at the beginning or end.

Requires video advertisements to display the statement for at least four seconds and include an audible disclosure.

Imposes fines for violations, with $250 for the first offense and up to $1,000 for subsequent offenses.

Exempts bona fide news coverage and platforms with clear policies on AI content disclosure from these requirements.

Defines "qualified political advertisement" as including various advertising formats related to elections or ballot questions using AI-generated content.

Conditions the act’s effectiveness on the enactment of House Bill No. 5143.

title: Michigan HB 5143
document_name: Michigan HB 5143 (Campaign Finance Act)
body:
Defines artificial intelligence as machine-based systems capable of influencing environments via predictions, recommendations, or decisions using both machine and human inputs. Specifies conditions for the definition's applicability contingent on the enactment of related legislation.

Define "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions for human-defined objectives, affecting real or virtual environments, using both machine and human inputs.

Mandate AI systems to perceive environments, abstract perceptions into models through automated analysis, and use model inference for decision-making.

Condition enactment of this amendment on the passage of House Bill No. 5141.

document_name: Temporary AI Commission Act
body:
Establishes a temporary New York state commission to study the impact of AI, robotics, and automation and how to regulate these technologies.

Establishes a temporary New York state commission, composed of 13 members appointed by stakeholders in government and academia, to study the impact of and make determinations on how to regulate AI, robotics, and automation.

Requires the commission to study existing state laws and comparative state regulations for AI, the impact of AI on employment and data privacy, public sector AI applications, and the potential impact of AI regulation on industry. Requires the commission to make determinations regarding criminal and civil liability for AI-enabled violations of law and potential restrictions on AI use in weaponry. 

Requires the commission to issue a final report to the governor and other state leaders before December 31, 2024.

title: San Francisco Generative AI Guidelines
document_name: San Francisco Generative AI Guidelines
body:
The San Francisco Generative AI guidelines basically establish citywide requirements for the responsible use of generative AI by San Francisco personnel. It also mandates human oversight, fact-checking, and transparency disclosures under Chapter 22J. Furthermore, it prohibits deepfakes or AI-driven decision-making without expert review. It also restricts the use of public AI tools as it requires documentation and an inventory of enterprise systems. It also imposes governance, auditing, and compliance duties to protect privacy, equity, and public trust.

Establish mandatory guardrails for generative AI (GenAI) use by City personnel, applying to all employees, contractors, consultants, volunteers, and vendors working on behalf of the City of San Francisco. This means that it requires human accountability for all AI-generated content. 

Furthermore, it mandates transparency and disclosure for public-facing or sensitive AI use under Chapter 22J. In short, it requires documentation of GenAI systems in the City’s inventory, direct notice to impacted individuals when AI substantially contributes to work product. 

It also limits which AI tools can be used and how they are used. This allows City-approved enterprise tools for certain tasks. It also strongly discourages public or consumer AI tools. This requires prior approval for non-approved systems. 

It also bans high-risk or deceptive uses of AI, including creating deepfakes, impersonating real people, fabricating public input, hiding AI use, or allowing AI to make final decisions that affect people’s rights, services, safety, or legal matters without expert human review.

Require States to ensure military AI use complies with international law, particularly international humanitarian law.

Mandate accountability through a responsible human command chain.

Impose legal reviews to align military AI with international obligations and enhance civilian protection.

Demand oversight by senior officials for high-consequence AI applications.

Advocate minimizing unintended bias in military AI.

Insist on transparent, auditable methodologies and documentation for military AI development.

Oblige training for personnel to understand AI capabilities and limitations, preventing automation bias.

Prescribe explicit, well-defined uses for military AI, with rigorous testing for safety and effectiveness.

Implement safeguards to detect and mitigate AI failures, with the ability to deactivate systems if needed.

Encourage States to publicly commit to these measures, support responsible AI use, and engage internationally to refine and promote these standards.

body:
●기관: AI Safety Summit 2023
●문서종류: 선언문 / 프런티어 AI 안전 국제협력 문서
●문서명: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023 / 「2023 AI 안전 정상회의 참석국 블레츨리 선언」
●발표시점: 2023년 11월 1일
●핵심내용:2023년 11월 1~2일 영국 블레츨리 파크에서 개최된 AI Safety Summit 계기 참석국들이 채택한 선언문으로, 프런티어 AI의 기회와 위험에 대한 최초의 광범위한 국제 공동인식을 형성한 문서임. 선언은 AI가 인류 복지, 평화, 번영, 지속가능발전에 기여할 수 있으나, 특히 고성능 범용 AI와 기반모델에서 발생할 수 있는 안전위험에 대응하기 위해 국제협력, 과학적 이해, 위험기반 정책, 안전성 테스트가 필요하다고 강조함.
① 선언은 AI가 인간 중심적·신뢰 가능·책임 있는 방식으로 개발·활용되어야 하며, 인권과 기본적 자유를 보호하면서 포용적 성장과 지속가능발전에 기여해야 한다고 강조함
② 프런티어 AI가 사이버보안·생명공학·허위정보와 통제 문제에서 심각한 위험을 초래할 수 있다고 지적하고, 개발자에게 안전성 시험·평가·투명성·위험 모니터링과 완화에 대한 강화된 책임을 제시함
③ AI 위험의 국제적 성격을 고려해 과학적·증거기반 연구, 위험기반 정책, 평가도구·공공부문 역량을 강화하고 국제 연구 네트워크와 후속 AI 안전 협력을 지속하도록 제시함

category: Editors' Picks;Multinational
title: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit
document_name: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit
body:
Affirms the need for safe, human-centric AI, addressing risks through international cooperation. Emphasizes responsibility for frontier AI safety, transparency, and accountability. Encourages inclusive dialogue and research to maximize AI benefits while mitigating risks. Promotes a risk-based governance approach.

Affirms the need for AI to be developed and used safely, human-centrically, and responsibly.

Recognizes AI's transformative potential in public sectors like health and education while addressing risks such as disinformation and misuse.

Welcomes international cooperation to tackle AI risks, emphasizing transparency, fairness, accountability, and human rights protection.

Identifies particular risks with frontier AI, including potential catastrophic harm and manipulation of content.

Resolves to intensify cooperation on AI safety, especially regarding frontier AI, through international collaboration and future AI Safety Summits.

Encourages actors, including nations and companies, to ensure AI safety through testing and monitoring harmful capabilities.

Calls for building risk-based policies and enhancing AI capacity in developing countries.

Supports an international network of scientific research on AI safety and sustains a global dialogue to harness AI benefits responsibly.

Commits to further meetings and cooperation to address AI governance, involving countries like the US, EU, China, and others.

category: Multinational
title: IDAIS-Oxford Statement (2023)
document_name: IDAIS-Oxford Statement (2023)
body:
Urges global cooperation between governments and AI developers to manage AI risks through the implementation of mandatory registration, third-party audits for advanced AI models, and immediate shutdown procedures for unsafe AI. Calls on AI developers and government agencies to increase investments into AI safety and governance research.

Encourages governments worldwide to develop measures to prevent worst-case AI outcomes from malicious or careless actors and manage AI safety risks.

Recommends mandatory registration for creating, selling, or using AI models above a certain capability threshold to enhance government visibility into emerging risks.

Encourages governments to implement requirements to monitor large-scale data centers, track AI incidents, and mandate independent third-party audits for AI developers concerning information security and model safety.

Proposes defining clear red lines that, if crossed, mandate immediate termination of an AI system through rapid and safe shut-down procedures.

Urges international cooperation to establish and maintain the capacity to shut down AI systems crossing red lines.

Calls for AI developers to demonstrate to regulators that their systems will not cross defined red lines before deployment.

Advocates for substantial research progress to ensure advanced AI alignment with designers' intent and robustness against malicious actors.

Encourages a global network of AI safety research and governance institutions, with leading developers committing significant resources to AI safety.

title: [G7] 히로시마 AI 프로세스 종합정책 프레임워크 환영 정상 성명
document_name: G7 Leaders’ Statement on the Hiroshima AI Process / 「히로시마 AI 프로세스에 관한 G7 정상성명」
body:
●기관: G7
●문서종류: 정상성명 / 히로시마 AI 프로세스 종합 정책 프레임워크

●발표시점: 2023년 10월 30일
●핵심내용:G7 정상들이 히로시마 AI 프로세스 하에서 마련된 생성형 AI 및 고도 AI 시스템 관련 국제 원칙과 자발적 행동규범을 환영한 정상성명임. 동 성명은 생성형 AI의 기회와 위험을 함께 고려하면서, 안전하고 보안성 있으며 신뢰 가능한 AI를 촉진하기 위한 국제 공통기준과 정책협력 틀을 제시함.
① 히로시마 AI 프로세스 종합 정책 프레임워크는 생성형 AI 위험·기회 분석, 국제 지침원칙, 고도 AI 개발조직 행동규범, 책임 있는 AI 도구·모범사례 협력의 네 가지 축으로 구성됨을 제시함
② AI 생태계 전반에는 안전하고 신뢰 가능한 AI 활용 원칙을, 고도 AI 개발조직에는 위험평가·완화·보안·투명성·정보공유·콘텐츠 인증·책임 있는 배포를 포함한 자발적 행동규범을 제시함
③ 생성형 AI의 허위정보·악의적 이용·개인정보·안전보안 위험에 국제적으로 대응하고, 민주적 가치와 인권을 기반으로 국제기구·표준기구·민간부문과의 협력을 강화할 필요성을 강조함

●문서종류: 국제 행동규범 / 고도 AI 시스템 개발조직 대상 자율지침

③ 인권·아동·취약계층·개인정보·지식재산권·편향·허위정보·환경영향을 고려한 위험완화와 데이터 품질관리를 강화하고, 글로벌 과제 해결을 위한 AI 개발과 디지털·AI 문해력 증진을 지원하도록 강조함

title: Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection)
document_name: Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection)
body:
Implements a phased, responsible scaling of AI models, emphasizing pre-deployment safety, post-launch monitoring, and global governance. Requires rigorous model evaluations, data input controls, and security measures. Encourages research on AI risks and standardization of AI-generated content identification.

Commits Inflection to a disciplined, phased approach to scaling AI models, emphasizing pre-deployment safety, post-launch monitoring, and global governance.

Requires robust evaluations and third-party red-teaming before public launch to ensure models do not provide harmful information or engage in discriminatory conduct.

Implements strict data input controls and audits, involving executive review and legal evaluations of training data for compliance with legal and ethical standards.

Ensures high-level security controls to prevent unauthorized access and misuse of AI models, including internal restrictions and a bug bounty program.

Maintains around-the-clock monitoring to detect and mitigate model misuse, employing frontier AI to enhance situational awareness.

Publishes model capabilities and limitations, supporting transparency and enabling risk assessment by users and regulators.

Advocates for standardized vulnerability reporting structures and participates in a pilot bug bounty program to encourage third-party disclosures.

Prioritizes research on AI risks and supports the creation of an International Panel on AI Safety.

Promotes cross-industry collaboration for identifying AI-generated material, focusing on child safety and standardized watermarking.

category: Editors' Picks;Multinational
title: Hiroshima Process International Guiding Principles for Advanced AI Systems
document_name: Hiroshima Process International Guiding Principles for Advanced AI Systems
body:
Establishes international guiding principles on AI development and deployment, which include proactive risk identification and mitigation, public disclosure of AI systems' capabilities, information sharing among government, industry, and civil society stakeholders, data privacy protection measures, and content authentication and provenance mechanisms.

Establishes international guiding principles around the safe, secure, and trustworthy development and deployment of artificial intelligence worldwide.

Recommends proactive mitigation of risks across the AI lifecycle and investment in physical, cyber, and insider threat security controls.

Recommends the public disclosure of advanced AI systems' capabilities, limitations, and appropriate or inappropriate uses.

Recommends information sharing and reporting of incidents among relevant industry, government, and civil society stakeholders

Recommends the deployment of content authentication and provenance mechanisms to enable users to identify AI-generated content.

Encourages development of advanced AI systems foremost to address key global challenge in alignment with the UN SDG goals.

Recommends the development and adoption of international technical standards.

Recommends the implementation of personal data privacy and IP protection measures.

category: Editors' Picks;Multinational
title: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
document_name: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
body:
Promotes safe, secure AI through voluntary guidance for developing advanced AI systems. Emphasizes risk assessment, transparency, security controls, and responsible AI governance. Encourages research, international standards, and societal benefits. Prohibits harmful AI applications undermining democratic values or human rights.

Promotes the safe, secure, and trustworthy development of AI by providing voluntary guidance for organizations developing advanced AI systems.

Encourages organizations to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks across the AI lifecycle, employing diverse testing methods and ensuring traceability through documented development practices.

Urges ongoing monitoring of AI systems post-deployment to identify vulnerabilities and misuse, through collaboration with stakeholders to mitigate risks, while advocating for public reporting and enhanced transparency regarding identified limitations.

Encourages information sharing and incident reporting, as well as the development and disclosure of AI governance and risk management policies among stakeholders to promote safety and trustworthiness.

Recommends robust security controls, including cybersecurity measures and insider threat safeguards, to protect AI system components from unauthorized access.

Promotes the development of content authentication mechanisms to identify AI-generated content and the creation of international technical standards for AI development.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Google DeepMind)
document_name: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Google DeepMind)
body:
Outlines Google DeepMind's commitment to responsible AI, emphasizing safety, transparency, and ethical standards. Establishes a Responsible AI Council for oversight, uses evaluations and red-teaming for risk assessment, and promotes information sharing. Supports AI for societal benefits like education and climate solutions.

Describes Google DeepMind's commitment to responsible AI development, emphasizing adherence to AI Principles to ensure technologies are socially beneficial, avoid bias, uphold safety standards, and respect privacy. 

Establishes a Responsible AI Council and Responsible Development and Innovation team to assess ethics and safety risks in AI models, guiding model and product development. 

Outlines a comprehensive evaluation process, including red-teaming for risk assessment, to identify and mitigate potential model risks, particularly for emerging "frontier" AI models. 

Promotes transparency through model reporting and information sharing, using tools like model cards and data sheets to document AI systems. 

Engages in post-deployment monitoring and employs a bug bounty program to address vulnerabilities and misuse of AI models. 

Implements robust security measures to protect AI models, including a Secure AI Framework and engagement with external security experts. 

Explores technical solutions like watermarking and metadata to identify AI-generated content's provenance. 

Prioritizes research on societal, safety, and security risks, supporting external AI impact research through initiatives like the Digital Futures Project.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit)
document_name: OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit)
body:
Describes OpenAI's progress on realizing the company's voluntary commitments to promote safety, security, and trust in AI, initially made in July 2023. Details OpenAI's approach to mitigating frontier risks, which are the focus of the UK AI Safety Summit, and the development of a Preparedness Framework.

States that OpenAI's is establishing a Preparedness Framework to manage risks from frontier AI models, focusing on a development process governance structure and preemption of catastrophic outcomes; this work will complement existing risk mitigation work and includes a joint Deployment Safety Board with Microsoft. 

States that OpenAI is creating Superalignment and Preparedness teams within the company to align AI systems with human intent and track and prepare for frontier risks, including cybersecurity, CBRN, persuasion, and autonomous replication and adaptation. Notes that OpenAI is also increasing investment into cybersecurity and insider threat safeguards.

States that OpenAI implemened red-teaming and evaluations to assess new models for safety, including GPT-4 and DALL-E 3, focusing on dual-use capabilities, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and self-replication.

States that OpenAI will include the publication of a system card in every new AI system, which informs users of key factors impacting system behavior.

States that OpenAI has initiated a reporting mechanism for responsible disclosure of dangerous capabilities among AI labs, focusing on national security-related risks.

Details OpenAI's emphasis post-deployment monitoring for misuse, security controls to protect intellectual property and data, and the development progress provenance techniques to identify AI-generated content.

States that OpenAI implemented data input controls and provides mechanisms for users to opt-out of their data being used for AI training.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Microsoft)
document_name: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Microsoft)
body:
Describes Microsoft's responsible AI development and deployment framework, encompassing multi-layered governance, red teaming and evaluation practices, cybersecurity and data input controls, and transparency mechanisms; establishes a joint Microsoft-OpenAI Deployment Safety Board for pre-release frontier model review; and supports a coordinated global licensing regime for frontier models.

Establishes a joint Microsoft-OpenAI Deployment Safety Board (DSB) for pre-release frontier model capability review, and supports a globally coordinated licensing regime for frontier model oversight.

Implements multi-layered responsible AI governance through the Responsible AI Council, Responsible AI Division Leads, and iterative risk mapping, measurement, and management across the product lifecycle.

Describes and implements red teaming practices at model and application levels, including AI-specific metrics and post-deployment monitoring pipelines.

Establishes cybersecurity controls for AI systems including Security Development Lifecycle (SDL)-based threat modeling, model weight encryption, access controls, and the Adversarial ML Threat Matrix developed with MITRE.

Describes Microsoft's Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure process and establishes a new AI-specific bug bounty program and responsible disclosure framework through the Frontier Model Forum.

Outlines data input controls, privacy practices, and General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliance for AI systems, and commits to defending customers against copyright claims through the Copilot Copyright Commitment.

Describes stakeholder-specific transparency and disclosure mechanisms and commits to an annual responsible AI transparency report and cross-industry collaboration through the Frontier Model Forum.

Establishes Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA)-based provenance standards and watermarking for identifying AI-generated content, and commits to expanding these capabilities across Microsoft products.

Implements iterative post-deployment abuse monitoring and misuse prevention, with continuous adjustment of security controls in response to new misuse patterns.

Describes AI safety research investments through the Accelerate Foundation Models Research (AFMR)= grant program and commits to expanding academic access to AI computing resources through the National AI Research Resource.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: City of Seattle Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy
document_name: Seattle Generative AI Policy
body:
Regulates City departments' acquisition and use of generative AI, requiring Seattle IT to approve exceptions and conduct risk reviews. Mandates human review of AI outputs, attribution, and bias reduction. Prohibits AI training using City data without controls.

Regulates City departments' acquisition and use of generative AI, requiring adherence to principles of innovation, transparency, and bias reduction.

Requires Seattle IT to evaluate generative AI acquisition requests and has authority to approve, deny, or revoke use based on risk assessments.

Mandates human review of AI-generated outputs before official use with documentation of review processes.

Requires attribution for AI-generated content, specifying inclusion of system names and review assertions.

Obliges the use of Racial Equity Toolkit prior to using generative AI tools to combat bias and discrimination.

Prohibits submission of confidential City data to AI systems without adequate enterprise controls and data protection.

Classifies AI-generated records as public and mandates retention and disclosure compliance.

Assigns the Chief Technology Officer responsibility for policy enforcement, with potential penalties for non-compliance.

Specifies the Director of DPAC and Chief Privacy Officer maintain risk criteria and exception processes.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta)
document_name: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta)
body:
Commits to responsible AI development through safety, security, privacy, and transparency; following White House Commitments to ensure AI guardrails. Conducted extensive model evaluations, red teaming, and information sharing.

Commits Meta to responsible AI development, prioritizing safety and transparency in AI systems, including the Llama 2 model.

Demonstrates actions taken in furtherance of the White House Commitments to establish AI guardrails, focusing on safety, security, and trust.

Conducted extensive model evaluations and red teaming, including external testing at DEFCON, to identify and mitigate risks in AI models including adversarial inputs like unqualified advice.

Requires information sharing and reporting on AI vulnerabilities with established feedback mechanisms for continuous improvement.

Implemented robust security controls for AI model weights to ensure model relliability, treating them as core intellectual property.

Participated in industry initiatives like the Synthetic Media Framework to ensure identification and disclosure of AI-generated content.

Invested in research on AI societal, safety, and security risks, and collaborates with policymakers through the Open Loop program.

Conducted privacy reviews for AI data inputs, excluding private user data, and offers users control over data shared with generative AI features.

category: 기타
title: [WHO] 보건 분야 AI 규제 고려사항
document_name: Regulatory considerations on artificial intelligence for health / 「보건을 위한 인공지능에 관한 규제 고려사항」
body:
●기관: 세계보건기구(WHO)
●문서종류: 규제 가이던스 / 보건의료 AI 규제 고려사항
●문서명: Regulatory considerations on artificial intelligence for health / 「보건을 위한 인공지능에 관한 규제 고려사항」
●발표시점: 2023년 10월 19일
●핵심내용:WHO가 보건의료 분야 AI 시스템의 안전성, 효과성, 윤리성, 형평성을 보장하기 위해 규제기관과 정책결정자가 고려해야 할 사항을 제시한 가이던스임. 동 문서는 AI가 의료서비스와 공중보건에 기여할 수 있으나, 데이터 품질, 편향, 개인정보 보호, 투명성, 임상 검증, 책임성 등 위험을 관리하기 위한 규제체계가 필요하다고 강조함.
① 문서는 보건의료 AI 규제가 환자 안전·공중보건·인권·형평성·신뢰성을 중심으로 설계되고, 전 생애주기에서 데이터 품질·편향·개인정보·사이버보안을 관리해야 한다고 강조함
② AI 도구의 안전성·성능·효과성을 확보하기 위해 임상 검증·독립적 평가·사후 모니터링을 실시하고, 투명성·설명가능성·문서화·추적가능성을 강화하도록 제시함
③ 개발자·의료기관·보건당국 등의 책임과 피해구제 체계를 명확히 하고, 다양한 보건시스템에서 형평성 있는 AI 활용을 위해 규제 역량강화·국제협력·표준 조화를 추진하도록 권고함

category: Chinese law and policy
title: Global AI Governance Initiative
document_name: Global AI Governance Initiative
body:
Calls for global cooperation to enhance AI governance, prevent risks, and ensure equitable access. Opposes AI misuse, disinformation, and sovereignty violations. Promotes ethical principles, legal frameworks, and equal rights in AI development. Encourages international collaboration, especially supporting developing countries.

Recognizes that artificial intelligence is a new and developing area of technology for humans and has a profound influence on the progress of human civilization.

Calls on countries to enhance information exchange and technological cooperation for AI governance, focusing on working together to fight against risk and to develop an AI framework to make AI technology secure, reliability, and equitable.

Calls to support the role of AI in promoting sustainable development and tackling global challenges such as climate change and biodiversity conservation.

Opposes using AI for manipulating public opinion, spreading disinformation, or interfering in other nations' affairs.

Urges adherence to international laws and prevention of AI misuse by malicious actors and instead develop principles for AI to use that align with humanities common values of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. 

Emphasizes call for global collaboration to make AI technologies open-source and accessible, resisting technological monopolies, drawing ideological lines or forming exclusive groups to obstruct other countries developing AI.

Promotes testing and assessment systems for AI based on risk levels (by carrying out tiered and category based management), ensuring AI remains under human control.

Advocates for laws ensuring privacy and data security in R&D and application of AI and also opposing illegal data practices of personal information.

Stresses fairness and non-discrimination in AI development processes and to avoid bias and discrimination.

Calls for ethical principles and accountability mechanisms to formulate AI ethical guidelines, and build sci-tech ethical review and regulatory system to address ethical concerns in a timely manner.

Encourages wide participation and consensus-based decision-making in AI governance.

Seeks increased representation of developing countries in global AI governance.

Supports UN discussions for an international AI governing institution.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An act to add Section 11546.45.5 to the Government Code, relating to automated decision systems
document_name: California AB 302 (2023)
body:
Requires the California Department of Technology to analyze the benefits and risks of all high-risk automated decision systems that are in use by, or have been proposed for use by, state agencies.

Requires the California Department of Technology, in coordination with other agencies, to analyze the benefits and risks of all high-risk automated decision systems that have been proposed for use, development, or procurement by, or are being used, developed, or procured by, state agencies. 

Requires the analysis to include a description of, among other things, the categories of data and personal information the automated decision system uses to make its decisions. 

Requires the Department of Technology to submit an annual report on the above-described comprehensive analysis to specified committees of the California Legislature.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Jersey Executive Order No. 346
document_name: New Jersey EO 346
body:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to study AI technologies, assess societal impacts, and recommend government actions for ethical use. Involves Executive Branch officials, allows public and expert consultation, and requires a report to the Governor within 12 months.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Task Force responsible for studying AI technologies' societal impacts and recommending government actions for ethical use.

Includes the Chief Technology Officer, Chief Innovation Officer, Chief Executive Officer of the Economic Development Authority, and other key officials as members.

Authorizes the Task Force to gather data from state departments and agencies.

Requires executive branch cooperation and assistance to fulfill the Task Force's objectives.

Directs the Task Force to consult with academics, industry professionals, and consumer advocates.

Issues a reporting requirement to the Governor within 12 months of the Order’s enactment, to be shared with the Legislature and public.

Permits additional appointments by the Governor as necessary.

Clarifies the Task Force’s advisory nature in providing advice to the Governor and executive branches. 

Takes effect immediately upon issuance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: City of St. Louis Information Technology Policy #2023-001 Guidance on Generative AI
document_name: Guidance on generative AI for City of St. Louis employees
body:
Advises City employees on generative AI use. Requires compliance with the City's IT Acceptable Use Policy. Requires ITSA approval for AI purchases. Prohibits uploading sensitive information. Encourages validating AI-generated content. Warns of copyright issues. Requires disclosure under Sunshine Law.

Instructs City employees to adhere to the Information Technology Acceptable Use Policy when using generative AI tools.

Requires ITSA to vet the purchase of AI-related technology and software.

Prohibits the use of City passwords for logging onto AI platforms and advises caution due to evolving malware threats.

Forbids the upload of sensitive or confidential information when using AI systems.

Advises a review and validation of AI-generated content due to potential bias or inaccuracies.

Cautions that AI-generated content might be copyright-protected and requires proper attribution.

Warns that content generated by AI may be subject to disclosure under Sunshine Law.

Indicates that ITSA and the Mayor’s Office will continue to evaluate the use of AI and develop policies accordingly.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California (2023-2024) AB 96
document_name: California AB 96 (Public Employment: Automated Vehicle Tech)
body:
Requires public transit employers to notify employee representatives 10 months before procurement of autonomous transit vehicle technology affecting jobs. Allows collective bargaining on technology development, implementation, workforce transition, and training plans. Grants Public Employment Relations Board jurisdiction over unfair practice charges.

Require public transit employers in California to notify the exclusive employee representative at least 10 months before starting a procurement process for autonomous transit vehicle technology that could eliminate jobs.

Mandate collective bargaining within 30 days upon notification or within 10 days of the public transit employer receiving a written request from the exclusive employee representative, focusing on developing and implementing the autonomous transit technology, creating transition plans for affected workers, and preparing them for new roles.

Ensure that this chapter does not impose any labor requirements that are less protective than existing statutory or contractual obligations.

Grant the Public Employment Relations Board jurisdiction to handle unfair practice charges related to this chapter.

Authorize the board to establish, amend, or repeal regulations necessary to implement the chapter, including emergency regulations for the immediate preservation of public welfare.

category: Editors' Picks;Chinese law and policy
title: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews
document_name: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews
body:
Regulates the circumstances under which ethics reviews for AI-related research must be conducted and review processes. Requires organizations conducting research involving potentially ethically problematic scientific research to establish ethics review committees.

Requires organizations conducting research involving sensitive science and technology ethics areas, including life sciences and AI, to establish ethics review committees.

Obliges these committees to guide risk assessments, conduct ethics reviews, and manage interdisciplinary membership for unbiased decision-making.

Requires ethics reviews for activities involving data and algorithms, mandating that data handling activities comply with relevant data security and personal information laws.

Mandates expert reconsiderations for high-risk emerging technologies, including algorithms and automated decision-making systems.

Mandates that AI research organizations conduct comprehensive ethical risk assessments and develop emergency response plans.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: North Carolina House Bill 259
document_name: North Carolina Current Operations Appropriations Act of 2023, SECTION 7.36.(h)
body:
Allocates $3.2 million to New Hanover and $2 million to Davidson County Schools for AI-powered school safety systems. Requires reporting by January 15, 2025, on participant schools, spending, safety outcomes, AI capabilities, and additional relevant information.

Allocates $3.2 million to New Hanover County Schools and $2 million to Davidson County Schools for an AI School Safety Pilot Program.

Requires use of funds to implement AI technology into existing school safety systems, including access controls, alerting protocols, and intercom systems.

Mandates participating public school units to report to the Joint Legislative Education Oversight Committee by January 15, 2025.

Directs reports to include details on school participation, fund usage, impact on safety outcomes, AI system capabilities compared to traditional safety measures, and any additional relevant information.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Republic of Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy: 2023-2033
document_name: Ghana National AI Strategy: 2023-2033
body:
Creates a National AI Strategy to accelerate Ghana's development through responsible AI use. Establishes a Responsible AI Office to implement the strategy, coordinates stakeholders, and ensures ethical AI deployment. Identifies key pillars like AI education, digital infrastructure, data governance, and public sector AI adoption for growth.

Develops Ghana's National AI Strategy through the Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation, supported by various international partners to drive inclusive growth and AI adoption.

Establishes a Responsible AI Office to implement the strategy, coordinate stakeholders, and ensure responsible AI deployment.

Identifies eight pillars focusing on AI education and training, youth empowerment, digital infrastructure, data access and governance, community coordination, sectoral AI adoption, applied research, and public sector AI utilization. 

Recommends annual skills assessments, AI education expansions, remote job facilitation, data governance policy enforcement, and AI pilot projects in key sectors, among others.

Coordinates the development of infrastructure like data centers and encourages investment in AI through incentives and legal clarifications.

Promotes international collaboration through platforms like OECD and Global Partnership on AI.

Prioritizes regulatory clarity, inclusive growth, and tackling AI-related risks like bias and privacy concerns to position Ghana as an African AI hub.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon)
document_name: AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon)
body:
Describes Amazon's AI initiatives, emphasizing AWS's role in providing AI services, including model evaluation and risk assessments. Outlines security measures, responsible AI documentation, and vulnerability reporting for AI products. Highlights Amazon's research, partnerships, and policies to address societal AI risks, privacy, and bias.

Facilitates AI development and deployment through Amazon Web Services (AWS), offering a comprehensive suite of AI and ML services, including Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Titan Foundation Models, which support generative AI applications.

Implements risk management and safety protocols, including systematic model evaluation, red teaming, and ongoing security assessments, to mitigate potential AI risks.

Protects AI models and data using robust logical and physical security measures, such as encryption, access controls, and least privilege principles.

Shares AI service information transparently through AI Service Cards, detailing intended use cases, limitations, and responsible AI design considerations.

Encourages responsible AI use and prohibits misuse through the AWS Responsible AI Policy, which addresses concerns like disinformation and privacy violations.

Invests in research and academic partnerships to advance responsible AI practices and develop tools for bias mitigation and human oversight.

Monitors AI misuse post-release, employing classifier guardrails and automated abuse detection to identify and address harmful content and misuse patterns.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York Senate Bill 1042
document_name: New York SB 1042 (Unlawful Dissemination of Intimate Images)
body:
Amends the penal law to criminalize dissemination or publication of digitized intimate images without consent. Defines "digitization" as realistic alteration using images of another person or computer-generated images. Repeals subdivision 2-a of section 245.15.

Amends the penal law to include the unlawful dissemination or publication of intimate images created or altered by digitization.

Defines "digitization" as altering an image realistically using other persons' images or computer-generated images.

Defines unlawful dissemination of intimate images, including AI-generated or digitally altered images, as intentional, non-consensual acts causing emotional, financial, or physical harm to individuals.

Mandates that the actor knew or should have known that the person depicted did not consent to the dissemination or publication.

Repeals subdivision 2-a of section 245.15 of the penal law.

Specifies that the act takes effect on the sixtieth day after becoming law.
