category: U.S. state and local documents
title: City of San Jose Generative AI Guidelines
document_name: San Jose Generative AI Guidelines
body:
Regulates the use of Generative AI in the City of San José, requiring users to avoid entering confidential information, ensure accuracy, cite AI usage, and create separate City-use accounts. Instructs departments to offer additional rules and engage in AI working groups.

Establishes guidelines for using Generative AI within the City of San José, emphasizing privacy, accuracy, transparency, equity, accountability, and beneficial use.

Requires users to cite AI where substantial content is AI-generated and to verify AI output against trustworthy sources.

Prohibits submission of personal or confidential information into Generative AI platforms and mandates the creation of separate accounts for City-related work using Generative AI.

Subjects AI usage to public records laws, recommending users to opt out of data collection where possible and verify AI-generated content for copyright compliance.

Offers collaborative working groups to enhance AI governance and provides risk assessment criteria for Generative AI use cases.

Encourages active participation in AI workgroups and emphasizes the importance of adapting guidelines as technology and laws evolve.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Artificial Intelligence and the Information Privacy Principles
document_name: Artificial Intelligence and the Information Privacy Principles
body:
Requires agencies using AI tools in New Zealand to conduct privacy impact assessments, ensure transparency, engage with Māori communities, and implement human review of AI outputs. Emphasizes compliance with the Privacy Act 2020 and its Information Privacy Principles.

Requires organizations in New Zealand using AI tools to comply with the Privacy Act 2020 and its Information Privacy Principles. 

Mandates senior leadership approval for AI tool usage and a privacy impact assessment (PIA) to evaluate privacy risks.

Demands transparency about AI tool usage, including engaging with Māori on potential impacts, assessing the necessity and proportionality of AI tools, and considering privacy implications.

Advises on proactive privacy measures, including developing privacy policies, engaging with affected communities, and evaluating training data provenance.

Highlights potential privacy issues with AI, such as automation blindness and overseas data disclosure risks.

Encourages organizations to secure personal information and comply with access, correction, and disclosure requirements.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Virginia Executive Directive 5 (2023)
document_name: Virginia (2023) ED 5 (Recognizing the Risks and Seizing the Opportunities of Artificial Intelligence)
body:
Directs the Office of Regulatory Management to establish AI standards, review laws, ensure transparency, and make recommendations for AI use. Tasks coordination with education and workforce institutions for AI guidelines. Requires completion of actions by December 15, 2023.

Directs the Office of Regulatory Management, with the Chief Information Officer and relevant Secretariats, to establish AI usage standards for Virginia's state government.

Requires reviewing laws and regulations affecting AI, including privacy and intellectual property laws, to ensure public protection.

Ensures AI usage is transparent, secure, and impartial with adequate privacy safeguards.

Recommends uniform AI standards across state agencies, including education and IT guidelines.

Collaborates with educational institutions to integrate AI in curricula and promote responsible AI usage in learning environments.

Prepares students and the workforce for careers involving AI through partnerships with colleges and industry.

Identifies opportunities for AI to enhance state government efficiency and ethical decision-making.

Explores AI's economic impacts, encouraging industry innovation and supporting displaced workers.

Works with the Virginia Department of Energy to assess AI's impact on power requirements.

Requires completion of these actions and recommendations by December 15, 2023.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Pennsylvania Executive Order 2023-19
document_name: Pennsylvania EO 2023-19 (Governing Use of Gen AI in Pennsylvania)
body:
Establishes the Generative AI Governing Board to oversee AI use, ensuring alignment with core values such as accuracy, equity, and privacy. Instructs the Office of Administration to develop policies and training for responsible AI use within Pennsylvania's agencies.

Creates the Generative AI Governing Board to oversee the ethical and effective use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) by Commonwealth of Pennsylvania agencies.

Requires agencies to apply core values such as accuracy, adaptability, equity, innovation, mission alignment, privacy, proportionality, safety, security, and transparency in using Generative AI technologies.

Charges the Office of Administration (OA) with developing policies to ensure responsible AI use, including auditing outputs for accuracy and protecting user privacy.

Instructs the Board to recommend guidelines and assess agency requests to utilize Generative AI, ensuring adherence to core values, bias testing, and aligning applications with governmental missions.

Composes the Board of key government officials and mandates monthly meetings.

Encourages collaboration with external AI experts and stakeholders for feedback on AI usage.

Orders OA to provide training for employees on using Generative AI tools effectively.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: County of Santa Cruz Artificial Intelligence Appropriate Use Policy
document_name: County of Santa Cruz AI Appropriate Use Policy
body:
Establishes the County of Santa Cruz AI policy for responsible generative AI use by employees. Prohibits PII input and impactful decisions with AI. Requires compliance with data privacy laws, ethical use, informed consent, transparency, and authorized tools. Encourages training.

Establishes the County of Santa Cruz's principles for responsible use of generative AI by employees, contractors, and third parties, ensuring alignment with ethical and legal standards.

Requires compliance with data privacy laws, such as HIPAA and CCPA, and informs the public of AI tool interactions, offering alternatives.

Prohibits the use of AI for unauthorized access, handling of personally identifiable information, unlawful activities, hiring decisions, and entering sensitive data into AI systems.

Permits only approved AI tools like Google Bard, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Scribe.

Requires employees to exercise judgment, report concerns, and use County email for AI tool accounts.

Encourages comprehension of AI policies and participation in workgroups while emphasizing responsible, ethical, and transparent AI usage, avoiding bias, and not relying on AI for significant decision-making.

title: [G20] 2023 뉴델리 정상선언
document_name: G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration / 「G20 뉴델리 정상선언」
body:
●기관: G20 인도 의장국
●문서종류: 정상선언 / 정상급 합의문
●문서명: G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration / 「G20 뉴델리 정상선언」
●채택시점: 2023년 9월 9~10일
●핵심내용:2023년 9월 9~10일 인도 뉴델리에서 개최된 G20 정상회의 결과문서로, “하나의 지구, 하나의 가족, 하나의 미래”를 기조로 지속가능발전, 포용성장, 기후·에너지 전환, 다자개혁, 디지털 공공인프라, 디지털경제와 AI 등을 포괄함. AI 분야에서는 공익을 위한 책임 있고 포용적이며 인간 중심적인 AI 활용을 강조하고, G20 AI 원칙 재확인, 혁신친화적 규제·거버넌스 접근, SDGs 달성을 위한 책임 있는 AI 활용을 주요 방향으로 제시함.
① 문서는 디지털 공공인프라를 포용적 성장과 혁신의 핵심 기반으로 보고, G20 DPI 프레임워크와 개발도상국의 DPI 구축을 지원하는 국제협력 구상을 제시함
② AI는 공익을 위해 책임 있고 포용적·인간 중심적으로 활용되어야 하며, 인권·투명성·설명가능성·공정성·책임성·안전성·개인정보 보호와 인간 감독을 보장해야 한다고 강조함
③ G20 AI 원칙을 재확인하고, AI 혜택의 공평한 공유와 위험 완화를 위해 국제협력과 혁신친화적 AI 규제·거버넌스 등을 촉진하도록 제시함

category: UN
title: [UNESCO] 교육·연구 분야 생성형 AI 가이드라인
document_name: Guidance for generative AI in education and research / 「교육과 연구에서의 생성형 AI 가이던스」
body:
●기관: UNESCO
●문서종류: 가이던스 / 생성형 AI 교육·연구 활용 지침
●문서명: Guidance for generative AI in education and research / 「교육과 연구에서의 생성형 AI 가이던스」
●발표시점: 2023년 9월 7일
●핵심내용:UNESCO가 교육과 연구 분야에서 생성형 AI를 인간 중심적으로 활용하기 위해 마련한 글로벌 가이던스임. 동 문서는 생성형 AI 도구의 확산 속도가 각국 규제체계와 교육기관의 대응 속도를 앞서고 있다는 문제의식 아래, 데이터 프라이버시 보호, 연령 제한, 윤리적 검증, 교육적 설계, 장기적 정책 프레임워크 마련을 주요 과제로 제시함.
① 문서는 생성형 AI의 개념·기술·모델 유형과 교육·연구 분야의 활용 가능성을 검토하고, 데이터 프라이버시·안전성·형평성 등 주요 윤리·정책 쟁점을 제시함

③ 각국에는 교육과정·교수·학습·연구에서 생성형 AI를 책임 있게 활용할 수 있도록 일관되고 포괄적인 정책 프레임워크를 마련하도록 제안함

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act
document_name: Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act
body:
Establishes a licensing regime for AI developers, requiring risk management and compliance with oversight audits. Holds AI companies accountable for harms, including privacy violations and deepfake creation. Limits AI technology exports to adversaries. Demands transparency and consumer protection, especially for children.

Establishes a licensing regime requiring companies developing sophisticated A.I. models to register with an independent oversight body. 

Requires developers to maintain risk management, pre-deployment testing, and reporting programs as part of licensing conditions.

Grants the oversight body authority to audit companies and cooperate with state Attorneys General.

Mandates Congress to ensure A.I. companies are legally accountable for harms caused by their models, including privacy breaches and civil rights violations.

Urges Congress to use export controls and sanctions to limit A.I. technology transfers to adversary nations.

Promotes transparency by requiring companies to disclose A.I. model information and ensure users know they are interacting with A.I.

Requires A.I. system providers to label deepfakes and maintain a public database of A.I. information.

Obliges companies to implement consumer protections, including safety brakes and data usage control, especially concerning children.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California Executive Order N-12-23
document_name: California Executive Order N-12-23 (State use of GenAI)
body:
Directs California agencies to draft reports and guidelines on GenAI use, focusing on risks and equitable outcomes. Establishes GenAI pilot projects and partnerships with universities. Promotes workforce training and risk analysis, particularly for infrastructure and regulatory impacts.

Orders California's Government Operations Agency and related entities to draft a report for the Governor within 60 days on beneficial uses and risks of Generative AI (GenAI) by the state.

Requires the California Cybersecurity Integration Center and related bodies to perform a risk analysis by March 2024 on GenAI threats to energy infrastructure, brief the Governor on findings, and make public recommendations for actions to guard against GenAI threats when appropriate. 

Directs various California departments to issue procurement and training guidelines for GenAI by January 2024.

Instructs relevant agencies to develop guidelines by July 2024 for using GenAI tools with vulnerable communities.

Mandates establishment of GenAI pilot project infrastructure by March 2024.

Urges the Governor's Office to partner with UC Berkeley and Stanford to evaluate GenAI's impact.

Tasks legal counsel to assess GenAI's regulatory impact and recommend updates.

Emphasizes collaboration with civil society, academia, and industry experts in drafting guidelines and conducting analyses.

category: Miscellaneous documents
org: Government of the United Arab Emirates
title: Dubai International Financial Centre Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10 ("Personal data processed through autonomous and semi-autonomous systems")
document_name: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10
body:
Establishes comprehensive obligations for entities deploying or operating AI systems that process personal data. Requires clear notices, transparency, accountability, and ethics in AI design. Mandates compliance with audit and certification requirements, ensuring systems process data for human-defined purposes.

Requires Deployers and Operators of autonomous and semi-autonomous systems to adhere to personal data processing principles.

Mandates clear notification to users of such systems about underlying technology and data processing purposes, with detailed descriptions of system capabilities and safeguards.

Obligates the provision of evidence of compliance with audit and certification requirements, and human intervention algorithms in cases of bias or legal non-compliance.

Imposes design requirements focused on ethics, fairness, transparency, security, and accountability.

Prohibits systems from processing personal data unless in compliance with human-defined purposes and legal frameworks.

Forbids use in high-risk processing without compliance with certification requirements and appointment of an Autonomous Systems Officer.

Deems Deployers as Controllers and Operators as Processors of personal data.

Allows data subjects to challenge processing outcomes per applicable law.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Wisconsin Executive Order #211
document_name: Wisconsin Executive Order #211 (Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence)
body:
Establishes the Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence, chaired by the Secretary of the Department of Workforce Development. Directs the Task Force to analyze AI's labor market impact, advance equity, and recommend workforce and education policy solutions.

Creates the Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence, chaired by the Secretary of the Department of Workforce Development or a designee.

Appoints additional members from key state departments, educational institutions, and other stakeholders, as determined by the Governor.

Instructs the Task Force to gather and analyze information to produce an advisory action plan for the Governor.

Requires the plan to assess generative AI’s impact on Wisconsin’s labor market, predict future impacts, and identify effects on key industries and skillsets.

Explores initiatives to advance equity and economic opportunity related to AI-driven changes.

Recommends solutions, including policy changes in workforce development and education, based on identified impacts.

Attaches the Task Force to the Department of Workforce Development.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California SCR 17 (Relative to Artificial Intelligence 2023)
document_name: California SCR 17 (Relative to Artificial Intelligence 2023)
body:
Affirms California Legislature's commitment to President Biden's safe AI vision and the "Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights." Commits to examine and implement these principles in state legislation and policies on automated systems use and deployment.

Affirms the California Legislature's commitment to President Biden’s vision for safe AI and the principles outlined in the "Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights."

Commits to examining and implementing the principles of Safe and Effective Systems, Algorithmic Discrimination Protections, Data Privacy, Notice and Explanation, and Human Alternatives, Consideration, and Fallback in state legislation and policies.

Addresses significant challenges posed by automated systems to democracy and public rights, such as unsafe, biased systems in healthcare and discriminatory algorithms in hiring and credit decisions.

Recognizes the potential benefits of AI, including increased efficiency in agriculture and revolutionary industrial advancements through data analysis.

Instructs the Secretary of the Senate to transmit copies of this resolution to the author for distribution.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: California 2023 SCR 17 (Relative to AI)
document_name: California 2023 SCR 17 (Relative to AI)
body:
Affirms California Legislature's commitment to President Biden's safe AI vision and "Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights" principles. Commits to examining and implementing these principles in state legislation and policies related to automated systems.

Affirms the California Legislature's commitment to President Biden’s vision for safe AI and the "Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights."

Directs the Secretary of the Senate to transmit copies of this resolution for distribution.

document_name: G20 Digital Economy Ministers Meeting Outcome Document and Chair’s Summary / 「G20 디지털경제 장관회의 결과문서 및 의장요약」
body:
●기관: G20 인도 의장국
●문서종류: 디지털경제 장관회의 결과문서 / 의장요약
●문서명: G20 Digital Economy Ministers Meeting Outcome Document and Chair’s Summary / 「G20 디지털경제 장관회의 결과문서 및 의장요약」
●채택시점: 2023년 8월 19일
●핵심내용:2023년 8월 19일 인도 벵갈루루에서 개최된 G20 디지털경제 장관회의 결과문서로, 디지털 공공인프라(DPI), 디지털경제의 안전·보안·회복력·신뢰, 디지털 역량강화를 핵심 의제로 다룸. 문서 대부분은 G20 회원국이 합의한 결과문서이며, 일부 문단은 의장요약으로 처리되었고, 디지털 전환을 포용적 성장과 지속가능발전의 핵심 기반으로 제시함.
① 문서는 DPI를 안전하고 상호운용 가능한 공유 디지털 시스템으로 보고, G20 DPI 프레임워크를 기반으로 각국 상황에 맞는 포용적·인간 중심·지속가능한 DPI 구축 필요성을 제시함
② 디지털경제의 신뢰를 위해 기업 보안·회복력을 강화하고, 아동·청소년 온라인 안전·프라이버시·사이버불링·성착취·기술매개 젠더폭력 등에 대응해야 한다고 강조함
③ 디지털·성별 격차 완화를 위해 재교육·향상교육·디지털 문해력과 취약계층 지원을 강화하고, G20 툴킷과 로드맵을 통해 국가 간 디지털 역량 비교와 인력 격차 해소를 촉진하도록 제시함

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Canadian Guardrails for Generative AI – Code of Practice
document_name: Canadian Guardrails for Generative AI – Code of Practice
body:
Proposes a voluntary code of practice for generative AI in Canada to avoid harmful impacts and build trust in AI systems. Requires developers, deployers, and operators to prevent misuse, assess bias, ensure human oversight, and conduct rigorous testing.

Proposes a voluntary code of practice for generative AI systems in Canada to ensure safety, security, and trust ahead of binding regulation.

Requires developers, deployers, and operators to identify and prevent malicious and inappropriate uses, mitigating safety risks of AI systems throughout their lifecycle.

Mandates assessment and curation of datasets to avoid biases and ensure fairness.

Emphasizes transparency through methods like watermarking AI-generated content and explaining system development processes.

Encourages human oversight and monitoring, including mechanisms to report adverse impacts and routine model updates.

Calls for accountability with internal governance, independent audits, and defined roles and responsibilities.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois HB 3563
document_name: Illinois HB 3563 ("GenAI Task Force")
body:
Amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act to establish the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force. Tasks the Task Force with investigation, public meetings, recommendations, and a comprehensive report by December 31, 2024.

Amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act to establish the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force.

Requires the Task Force to investigate and report on generative AI and natural language processing software.

Comprises the Task Force of appointed members from various government, educational, and expert backgrounds.

Mandates the Task Force to hold at least five public meetings across different regions of Illinois.

Tasks the Task Force with recommending legislation for consumer information protection, model policies for schools, and assessing AI's impact on public services, civil rights, employment, and cybersecurity.

Obligates the Department to provide administrative and technical support to the Task Force.

Requires the Task Force to file a comprehensive report by December 31, 2024, with the Governor and the General Assembly.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Kansas Policy and Procedures Memorandum 8200.00
document_name: Kansas PPM 8200.00 (Gen AI Policy)
body:
Outlines acceptable use of generative AI for Kansas's Executive Branch agencies. Requires human review of AI outputs for accuracy and prohibits reliance on AI for official statements. Bans input of Restricted Use Information and copyrighted material into AI.

Outlines the acceptable use of generative AI by Executive Branch Cabinet and Non-Cabinet Agencies in Kansas, emphasizing safety, privacy, and intellectual property protection.

Requires entities to review AI-generated content for accuracy, appropriateness, privacy, and security before dissemination.

Prohibits verbatim use of AI-generated content, reliance on it for final decisions or official statements, and impersonation of individuals or organizations.

Forbids input of Restricted Use Information, inappropriate, copyrighted, or proprietary material into AI systems.

Directs agencies to require contractors to disclose AI usage in contracts and prohibits use of state confidential data without approval.

Allows software code from AI only after risk mitigation and mandates annotation.

Tasks agency heads with procedural compliance and the Office of Information Technology Services (OITS) with policy maintenance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois House Bill 2123
document_name: Illinois HB 2123 (Digital Forgeries Act)
body:
Amends the Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act to allow depicted individuals to sue for harm from intentional dissemination of private, altered sexual images without consent. Provides exceptions and specifies potential damages and remedies.

Amends the Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act to define terms such as "depicted individual," "consent," and "dissemination."

Establishes a cause of action for depicted individuals against those who intentionally disseminate or threaten to disseminate private sexual images without consent, knowing or disregarding the individual's lack of consent and identifiability.

Clarifies that consent to creation or previous disclosure of an image does not imply consent to further dissemination.

Specifies exceptions to liability, including good faith actions by law enforcement, legal proceedings, and medical contexts, and outlines conditions under which parents or guardians are not liable.

Allows prevailing plaintiffs to recover damages, attorney's fees, and seek injunctive relief, while considering factors like age and dissemination scope.

States that disclosure of digitally altered images is not a defense and does not impose liability on interactive computer services for third-party content.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023
document_name: CREATE AI Act of 2023
body:
Establishes the National AI Research Resource to provide computational resources, data, educational tools, and testbeds for AI researchers.

Establishes a steering committee to oversee the NAIRR.

Authorizes the National Science Foundation, in coordination with the NAIRR steering committee, to establish the National AI Research Resource.

Creates a NAIRR Program Management Office to manage the NAIRR's day-to-day operations.

Directs the Program Management Office to solicit bids for an Operating Entity for the NAIRR and to oversee that Entity.

Provides for the NAIRR to be resourced with computational resources, data, educational tools and services, and AI testbeds.

Specifies eligibility for access to resources in the NAIRR, including academic, nonprofit, government, and small businesses, among others.

Provides for procedures to establish privacy, ethical, safety and scientific integrity requirements for users of the NAIRR.

Authorizes the NAIRR to charge fees for users at various tiers, including free and subsidized tiers.

Provides for security requirements to prevent unauthorized access and protect research security.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Washington Senate Bill 5152
document_name: Washington SB 5152 (Synthetic Media)
body:
Defines "synthetic media" in political campaigns as manipulated media creating false impressions. Permits candidates to seek legal relief against such media use. Requires disclosure of manipulation. Holds sponsors liable, not media, unless disclosure is altered. Encourages prompt court rulings.

Defines "synthetic media" as manipulated images, audio, or video that create a false impression of a real individual's appearance, speech, or conduct.

Allows candidates to seek injunctive relief or damages if their appearance, speech, or conduct is altered using synthetic media in electioneering communications.

Requires disclosure for synthetic media, stating, "This (image/video/audio) has been manipulated," with specific guidelines for visibility and audibility.

Places the burden of proof on plaintiffs to demonstrate synthetic media use by clear and convincing evidence.

Encourages courts to expedite proceedings related to synthetic media disputes.

Holds sponsors, but not mediums, liable unless mediums alter content or remove required disclosures.

Exempts interactive computer services from being treated as publishers of third-party content, except under specific conditions.

Mandates the public disclosure commission to adopt rules supporting this chapter without constituting violations under existing campaign finance laws.

category: Corporate policies and commitments
title: Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies
document_name: Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies
body:
Establishes the commitments of leading artificial intelligence companies to manage risks posed by AI.

Announces the Biden-Harris Administration's development of an executive order and intent to pursue bipartisan legislation in these matters.

Acknowledges the voluntary commitments received from Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Inflection, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI to the Biden-Harris Administration to help move toward the safe, secure, and transparent development of AI technology.   

Specifies various actionable commitments that will support three broad goals: ensuring products are safe before public release, building systems that put security first, and earning public trust. Commitments include internal and external security testing, sharing information across the industry and with governments, civil society, and academia, and investing in cybersecurity and insider threat safeguards.

Announces the Biden-Harris Administration's development of an executive order and intent to pursue bipartisan legislation in these matters.

category: Chinese law and policy
title: Remarks by Ambassador Zhang Jun at the UN Security Council Briefing on Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Risks for International Peace and Security
document_name: 2023 Remarks by Ambassador Zhang at the UNSC Briefing on AI
body:
Emphasizes the need for AI governance with principles prioritizing ethics, safety, fairness, openness, and peaceful use. Advocates for global cooperation, especially through the UN, to develop inclusive AI policies. Opposes technological hegemony and emphasizes China's commitment to responsible AI development and international collaboration.

Calls for adherence to ethical principles in AI development, emphasizing people-oriented AI and the need to establish ethical norms and regulatory systems tailored to national conditions.

Stresses safety and controllability, urging the international community to establish risk control mechanisms and accountability structures to prevent AI misuse and autonomous lethal technologies.

Advocates for fairness and inclusiveness, highlighting the importance of ensuring equal access to AI benefits for developing countries and opposing technological hegemony and exclusionary practices.

Promotes openness and inclusivity, encouraging international cooperation across disciplines, regions, and organizations under the UN framework to create a non-discriminatory environment for AI.

Emphasizes peaceful utilization of AI, underscoring the necessity of AI for sustainable development and responsible defense policies to prevent its misuse in military contexts.

Underlines China's commitment to international cooperation in AI governance, referencing past initiatives and ongoing efforts to establish a global framework for AI security governance.

category: Chinese law and policy
title: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
document_name: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
body:
Regulates generative AI services in mainland China, emphasizing legal compliance, societal ethics, and security. Encourages innovation while preventing discrimination and protecting personal information. Mandates providers to ensure content accuracy, transparency, and user privacy. Enforces penalties for non-compliance.

Establishes legal framework for the use and governance of generative AI services in mainland China, promoting innovation while ensuring security and compliance with national values.

Applies to public generative AI services generating text, images, audio, video, but excludes non-public research and development.

Mandates adherence to laws, ethical standards, and the protection of intellectual property, personal information, and societal values.

Encourages independent innovation and international cooperation in AI technology, emphasizing lawful data handling and quality improvement.

Requires providers to ensure information security, sign service agreements with users, and prevent misuse by minors and illegal activities.

Obligates providers to label AI-generated content, maintain service stability, and establish complaint mechanisms.

Imposes oversight by relevant state departments, requiring security assessments for AI with social mobilization potential.

Specifies penalties for non-compliance, including warnings, service suspension, and legal action for serious violations.

Takes effect on August 15, 2023, with provisions for foreign investment compliance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York A7838
document_name: New York A7838 ("Long-term impact of AI on workforce")
body:
Requires the New York Department of Labor to study AI's long-term impact on the workforce, issuing interim reports every five years and a final report by 2035. Prohibits state entities from using AI to displace employees until the final report.

Mandates the Department of Labor to begin a study on the long-term impact of artificial intelligence on the state workforce within six months.

Requires consultation with the Department of Civil Service and the Office of Information Technology Services.

Calls for examination of job performance, productivity, training, education requirements, privacy, and security.

Obligates the Department of Labor to issue an interim report every five years and a final report by January 1, 2035, with recommendations for legislative action.

Prohibits all state departments and governmental entities from using AI to displace any natural person from their employment until the final report and recommendations are received.

Ensures immediate effect upon enactment.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Amendment to Rules of NY City (Use of Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools)
document_name: NYC Rules Amendment for Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools
body:
Requires New York City employers to conduct and disclose annual bias audits of Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDT) for hiring and promotions. Specifies calculation of selection and impact ratios by sex, race, and ethnicity.

Mandates that employers or employment agencies conduct a bias audit of Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDTs) at least annually.

Requires bias audits to calculate selection and scoring rates, and impact ratios across sex, race/ethnicity, and intersectional categories.

Mandates AEDT users to publish bias audit summaries online, detailing data sources and impact ratios, accessible for at least 6 months after each AEDT use.

Requires notification to candidates and employees 10 business days before AEDT use, offering options via website, job postings, mail, or email.

Enforces online publication of AEDT data retention policies and types of data collected.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Initial advice on Generative Artificial Intelligence in the public service (New Zealand)
document_name: Initial advice on Generative Artificial Intelligence in the public service (New Zealand)
body:
Advises New Zealand Public Service on cautious use of GenAI, emphasizing data privacy, security, and ethical considerations. Prohibits using GenAI with sensitive or personal data externally. Stresses governance, transparency, and collaboration, especially concerning Māori data and interests.

Prohibits the use of GenAI for data classified as SENSITIVE or higher, and personal information should not be input into external GenAI tools.

Recommends agencies avoid using GenAI for business-critical information, systems, or public-facing channels due to risks of inaccuracy and bias.

Advises against using GenAI as Shadow IT, emphasizing the need for robust governance and accountability in AI application.

Encourages agencies to develop GenAI policies, ensuring ethical use, and promoting transparency and accountability.

Emphasizes the importance of considering privacy risks, recommending privacy impact assessments and engagement with Māori communities regarding Māori data.

Warns of security risks, including insecure code generation and data spills, advising strong cybersecurity practices.

Urges agencies to remain transparent about GenAI usage, ensure human oversight, and validate AI outputs for accuracy.

Suggests using sandboxes for testing GenAI safely and advises on procurement principles to mitigate vendor-related risks. 

This guidance serves as an interim measure while longer-term AI regulatory frameworks are developed.

title: Pennsylvania HR 170
document_name: Pennsylvania HR 170 ("AI Advisory Committee")
body:
Directs the Joint State Government Commission to study AI's impact in Pennsylvania, establish an advisory committee, and assess AI development, risks, and benefits. Requires legislative proposals, ethical guidelines, and an evaluation report within 18 months to state leaders.

Directs the Joint State Government Commission to establish an advisory committee to study artificial intelligence's impact in Pennsylvania.

Mandates an assessment of AI development and use, including benefits, risks, and fiscal impacts on the state.

Proposes legislation for state AI regulation and a definition for AI.

Recommends evaluating AI's effects on students' academic performance and addressing AI-driven disinformation.

Urges studying potential job displacement due to AI automation and assessing implications for organized labor.

Calls for a proposal on ethical and responsible AI development in Pennsylvania.

Advises considering the creation of a permanent commission for AI study.

Allows the Joint State Government Commission to request information from state agencies for the study.

Requires a report with findings and recommendations within 18 months to various governmental leaders and committees.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act regulating the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in providing mental health services.
document_name: Massachusetts AI in Mental Health Act
body:
Requires licensed mental health professionals seeking to offer AI-assisted mental health services to obtain approval from a licensing board, inform patients about AI use, and obtain patient consent; requires AI systems delivering mental health services to prioritize patient safety and well-being. Imposes disciplinary action by a licensing board for violations.

Instructs licensed mental health professionals who wish to provide mental health services through AI to seek approval from a licensing board, inform patients of the use of AI in their treatment, provide non-AI alternatives, and obtain patient consent.

Requires any AI system used to provide mental health services to prioritize the safety and well-being of patients and be subject to continuous monitoring by a licensed mental health professional. 

Establishes disciplinary action by the relevant professional licensing board for mental health professionals who violate the provisions above.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy
document_name: Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy
body:
Regulates use of generative AI chatbots for county work. Prohibits sharing proprietary or confidential data. Requires Executive approval and accuracy checks on AI-generated content. Mandates training for employees. Enforces ethical use, with potential disciplinary action for violations.

Outlines the use of generative AI chatbots, like ChatGPT and Bard, for Kendall County employees. 

Prohibits using county email addresses and submitting proprietary or confidential data into these platforms. 

Requires employees to consult with Executives regarding chatbot use, who may approve, deny, or modify usage parameters. 

Mandates proper citation and accuracy checks for AI-generated content. 

Enforces disciplinary actions, including termination, for policy violations or inappropriate use, ensuring ethical compliance with conduct and antidiscrimination policies. 

Instructs employees to undergo training on proper chatbot use. 

Applies Technology and Record Retention Policies when using AI with County equipment. 

Addresses training queries with Human Resources or the Information, Communication and Technology Department Director.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: City of Tempe Ethical Artificial Intelligence Policy
document_name: Tempe Ethical AI Policy
body:
Establishes guidelines in Tempe for ethical AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and accountability. Requires departments and Information Technology to collaborate on AI reviews. Mandates regular assessments and stakeholder engagement. Ensures adherence to legal standards and privacy protection. Promotes AI literacy and compliance.

Establishes the City of Tempe's commitment to ethical AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, accountability, and protection of rights.

Applies this policy to all AI technologies in city operations, including predictive analytics, machine learning, and automated decision-making.

Requires defined objectives, data privacy, and human-AI collaboration, while ensuring human control.

Tasks departments with setting AI objectives, conducting reviews, and collaborating with IT for oversight.

Instructs the Technology and Innovation Steering Committee to monitor AI compliance, develop reporting mechanisms, and define non-compliance consequences.

Mandates Information Technology to develop a review process, conduct training, and support compliance.

Commits to ongoing monitoring, stakeholder engagement, and ethical improvement of AI practices.

Promotes public engagement and awareness campaigns about AI activities.

Requires compliance with applicable laws and regulations and supports ethical AI frameworks development. 

Commits to periodic policy reviews to address emerging AI challenges and advancements.

category: 중앙대학교
title: [중앙대학교] 생성형AI 활용 가이드라인

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Rhode Island House Resolution 6423
document_name: Rhode Island H6423 (2023)
body:
Requests the Department of Administration and RI Division of Information Technology to report on the use, validation, and evaluation of algorithmic decision-making, address biases in AI, and propose regulatory actions. Requires submission of findings to the House by September 29, 2023.

Requests the Department of Administration and the RI Division of Information Technology report on the extent of algorithmic decision-making used by the State of Rhode Island.

Tasks them with assessing the validation, testing, and evaluation of automated decision systems, especially regarding biases such as racial and gender biases.

Instructs them to provide recommendations on regulatory or legislative action regarding the use of automated decision systems by state offices, compliance with data protection laws, and timelines for the implementation of AI technologies.

Requires delivery of this information to the House of Representatives and the Chair of the House Committee on Innovation, Internet, and Technology by September 29, 2023.

Authorizes the Secretary of State to transmit certified copies of this resolution to relevant state officials.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act relating to the creation of the artificial intelligence advisory council
document_name: Texas AI advisory council
body:
Establishes an artificial intelligence advisory council to study and monitor AI systems used by Texas state agencies, and requires those agencies to submit inventory reports describing the AI systems they use.

Establishes an artificial intelligence advisory council -- to be disbanded at the start of 2025 -- to study and monitor AI systems developed, employed, or procured by Texas state agencies.

Instructs the advisory council to assess the need for an AI code of ethics for the state government, review automated decision systems inventory reports submitted by state agencies, and recommend administrative actions as needed. 

Requires the advisory council to submit a report on its activities and findings to the legislature. 

Requires each state agency to submit to the legislature and advisory council an inventory report of all automated decision systems that are being developed,
employed, or procured by the agency.

Requires the inventory reports described above to assess each AI system's purpose, capabilities, data management practices, data output, and fiscal impact, as well as any information available on bias testing conducted on the system and the forms of data inputted into the system.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Pennsylvania HB 1380
document_name: Pennsylvania HB 1380 ("Administration of Assistance Programs")
body:
Utilizes artificial intelligence for eligibility verification and fraud detection in public assistance programs. Authorizes data access from state agencies to verify residency and eligibility. Prioritizes job training programs to increase employment and self-reliance.

Authorizes the department to utilize data analytics and artificial intelligence for eligibility verification and fraud detection in public assistance programs.

Permits the department to access data from other state agencies to verify residency and eligibility of applicants.

Empowers the department to establish rules, regulations, and standards for assistance program administration, including eligibility criteria and benefit modifications.

Requires the department to ensure expenditures do not exceed appropriations and to seek necessary federal waivers or approvals.

Allows the establishment of health savings accounts and medical assistance premiums to aid residents transitioning out of assistance programs.

Mandates physical health managed care organizations to share medical assistance claims data with providers.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Louisiana SCR 49
document_name: Louisiana (2023) SCR 49 (Study Impact of AI)
body:
Urges the Joint Legislative Committee on Technology and Cybersecurity to study AI's impact on operations, procurement, and policy. Requires a written report with recommendations submitted to relevant committees 60 days before Louisiana's 2024 Regular Session; encourages the committee to solicit input from several governmental and industry entities.

Urges the Joint Legislative Committee on Technology and Cybersecurity to study the impact of artificial intelligence on operations, procurement, and policy in Louisiana.

Requires the committee to submit a written report of its findings to the House Committee on Commerce and the Senate Committee on Commerce, Consumer Protection and International Affairs at least sixty days before the 2024 Regular Session.

Instructs the report to propose recommendations and legislative proposals to aid government and businesses in leveraging AI benefits while protecting consumers.

Encourages the committee to seek input from the Department of Economic Development, the office of technology services, Division of Administration, the Department of Justice, and industry partners.

Transmits a copy of the resolution to the Joint Legislative Committee on Technology and Cybersecurity.

category: 유럽연합 집행위원회
title: [유럽연합 집행위원회] Ethical guidelines on the use of artificial intelligence and data in teaching and learning for educators

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: West Virginia House Bill 3214
document_name: West Virginia H 3214 (Road Optimization Assessment Data Pilot Program)
body:
Creates the "Road Optimization and Assessment Data Road Pilot Program" using AI and ML for road condition assessment. Requires data collection via GPS, laser systems, and video imagery in Monongalia and Preston Counties. Aims for predictive road maintenance over three years.

Creates the "Road Optimization and Assessment Data Road Pilot Program" to study alternative methods for assessing and financing road maintenance. 

Mandates the use of Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to evaluate road conditions in Monongalia and Preston Counties.

Requires the Commissioner of Highways to promulgate rules for legislative approval concerning data collection and road assessment.

Instructs the Division of Highways employees to drive all roads in the pilot counties for data capture.

Utilizes GPS, geotagged positioning, and laser measuring systems to assess road geometry and conditions.

Employs video documentation and reflectometer systems for comprehensive road condition analysis.

Requires biannual data capture and processing over three years to track road condition changes and provide predictive maintenance analysis.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Connecticut Substitute Senate Bill 1103
document_name: Connecticut SB 1103 (AI Automated Decision Making)
body:
Requires state agencies to inventory and annually assess AI systems for discrimination risks, and mandates the development of AI governance policies by February 2024. Prohibits AI implementation without impact assessments and establishes a working group to recommend AI best practices and future legislation.

Mandates the Department of Administrative Services to inventory AI systems used by state agencies and make this information publicly available, identifying the system's vendor, capabilities, use, and impact assessment before implementation. 

Directs the Office of Policy and Management to establish AI policies and procedures for state agencies by February 1, 2024, governing procurement and implementation to avoid discrimination.

Requires ongoing assessments of AI systems to prevent unlawful discrimination or disparate impacts, in accordance with established procedures, and prohibits state agencies from implementing AI systems without such impact assessments.

Obligates the Judicial Department to inventory its AI systems, adopt AI governance policies, and continuously monitor system use to prevent discrimination.

Prohibits state contracts with businesses unless they require compliance with applicable AI statutory requirements.

Creates a working group to recommend ethical AI use in government, assess federal AI guidelines, and propose potential legislation modeled after the OSTP AI Bill of Rights, reporting findings by February 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act Concerning Artificial Intelligence, Automated Decision-Making and Personal Data Privacy
document_name: Artificial Intelligence, Automated Decision-Making and Personal Data Privacy Act
body:
Requires the state government to establish a public inventory of its use of artificial intelligence systems and to mandate impact assessments of its AI systems to prevent unlawful discrimination; establishes a working group to make recommendations on the state government's use of AI systems

Requires the Department of Administrative Services to establish a public inventory of state agencies' existing use of AI systems; this inventory should include whether the system was employed to independently make or inform decisions, and whether it undergone an impact assessment before implementation

Requires the Office of Policy and Management to develop policies to govern state agencies' procurement and use of AI systems; this includes requiring state agencies to conduct impact assessments for these systems and to ensure systems do not unlawfully discriminate against individuals or groups

Bans state agencies from implementing any AI system unless it had performed an impact assessment to prevent unlawful discrimination, effective February 1 2024

Requires the Judicial Department to establish a public inventory of its systems that employ AI, including whether the AI system had undergone impact assessments and was used to make or support conclusions; also requires the department to introduce policies to govern the use of AI, and to prevent unlawful discrimination

Establishes a working group comprising industry representatives and academics to engage stakeholders and experts and make recommendations on the state government's use of AI; this includes recommendations on the adoption of a Connecticut artificial intelligence bill of rights based on the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy's 'Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights'

category: Chinese law and policy
title: Measures of Beijing Municipality on Promoting the Innovative Development of Artificial General Intelligence
document_name: Measures for Promoting Innovation and Development of Artificial General Intelligence in Beijing
body:
Promotes Beijing's AGI sector growth by boosting computing power, enhancing high-quality data supply, exploring large models, and fostering AGI applications in various sectors. Establishes regulatory policies for secure advancement, emphasizing innovation, risk prevention, security, and principles management in AI activities.

Mobilizes commercial computing resources to meet the requirements of the AGI sector, showcasing cooperation with cloud service providers to enhance access to diverse and high-quality computing power.

Promotes the construction of new computing facilities, including the Beijing AI Public Computing Power Center, to advance computing capabilities.

Establishes an integrated multi-cloud computing management platform to optimize computing power management and operations.

Collects high-quality training datasets, ensuring legal compliance and promoting the trading of data through legitimate channels.

Plans to set up data training bases and a crowdsourcing service platform for dataset annotation, enhancing data quality and collaboration.

Explores innovative algorithms for large models, supporting an open-source technical ecosystem and developing governance tools for data management.

Facilitates the practical application of AGI in various sectors, including government, medicine, finance, and urban governance.

Innovates regulatory policies, promoting inclusive and prudent supervision systems while strengthening network and data security.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Minnesota HF 1370 (Deepfake Accountability and Public Safety)
document_name: Minnesota HF 1370 (Deepfake Accountability and Public Safety)
body:
Establishes legal actions for nonconsensual dissemination of deep fake sexual images, including damages and penalties. Criminalizes using deep fake technology to influence elections. Specifies exceptions and venue rules. Grants immunity to certain service providers. Effective August 1, 2023.

Establishes a cause of action for the nonconsensual dissemination of deep fake sexual images in Minnesota, allowing plaintiffs to seek damages, including financial losses and mental anguish.

Defines the crime of using deep fake technology to influence elections, with penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations committed within 90 days before an election.

Criminalizes the intentional dissemination of deep fake images depicting intimate parts or sexual acts without consent, with increased penalties for aggravating factors such as intent to profit or harass.

Allows for injunctions and restraining orders to prevent further harm and includes confidentiality measures for plaintiffs.

Provides exemptions for lawful purposes, such as criminal investigations, reporting unlawful conduct, or scientific research, while ensuring compliance with federal law.

Specifies that these provisions are effective from August 1, 2023, and outlines jurisdiction and venue rules for related legal actions.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An act relating to state affairs and government -- commission to monitor the use of artificial intelligence in state government.
document_name: Rhode Island AI Commission Act
body:
Establishes a permanent commission to monitor the use of artificial intelligence in Rhode Island state government and recommend changes to the state’s use of automated decision-making (ADM) systems. Requires the commission to submit an annual, public report detailing their findings.

Establishes a permanent commission to monitor the use of AI in Rhode Island state government and recommend changes to the state’s use of automated decision-making (ADM) systems that may affect human welfare. 

Instructs the commission to continuously survey the state’s use of ADM systems, including identifying gaps in the procurement, evaluation, and ongoing testing of ADM systems, the training given to individuals using these systems, the transparency, explicability, and auditability of ADM systems, identifying and mitigating disparate outcomes due to protected characteristics, and addressing data security and intellectual property concerns. 

Requires the commission to include representatives from multiple state agencies (commerce, business regulation, children, youth, and families, etc.) and four from academic institutions. 

Requires the commission to submit an annual public report to the Governor and state legislature detailing its activities and findings, regulatory or legislative recommendations–specifically where state offices should or should not use automated decision systems, progress implementing previous recommendations, and the extent of algorithmic decision-making used by the state.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York S7422
document_name: New York S7422 ("AI Displacing Actors")
body:
Exclude film productions using AI, which displaces existing employees, from tax credits provided to "qualified films" under the Empire State Film Production Credit.

Exclude productions using AI that displace employees from being considered a "qualified film" for the Empire State Film Production Credit.

Carves out an exception to the above for films covered by current collective bargaining agreements that allow for AI to displace employees.

category: G7
title: [G7] 2023 히로시마 정상 커뮤니케(G7 Hiroshima Leaders’ Communiqué)
document_name: G7 Hiroshima Leaders’ Communiqué / 「G7 히로시마 정상 공동성명」
body:
●기관: G7 일본 의장국
●문서종류: 정상 공동성명 / 정상급 합의문
●문서명: G7 Hiroshima Leaders’ Communiqué / 「G7 히로시마 정상 공동성명」
●채택시점: 2023년 5월 20일
●핵심내용:2023년 5월 19~21일 일본 히로시마에서 개최된 G7 정상회의 결과문서로, 우크라이나 지원, 핵군축·비확산, 경제안보, 기후·에너지, 식량안보, 글로벌 인프라, 디지털 전환과 AI 등 주요 국제현안을 포괄함. AI 분야에서는 신뢰 가능한 AI라는 공동 목표를 위해 포용적 AI 거버넌스 논의와 거버넌스 프레임워크 간 상호운용성을 진전시키고, 생성형 AI 대응을 위한 히로시마 AI 프로세스 출범을 지시함.
① 문서는 디지털경제와 AI 거버넌스가 공정성·책임성·투명성·프라이버시·인권 등 민주적 가치에 부합해야 하며, 다중이해관계자 기반의 국제표준과 거버넌스 상호운용성을 강화해야 한다고 강조함
② 생성형 AI의 기회와 위험에 대응하기 위해 OECD·GPAI와 협력하는 히로시마 AI 프로세스를 출범하고, 거버넌스·지식재산권·투명성·허위정보·책임 있는 AI 활용을 주요 논의 의제로 제시함
③ 신뢰 가능한 AI 도구의 글로벌 상호운용성과 국제기술표준 개발을 촉진하고, 몰입형 기술·메타버스의 거버넌스·공공안전·인권 문제에 대한 공동 접근 필요성을 제시함

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI
document_name: City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI
body:
Provides interim guidelines for City of Boston agencies (excluding Boston Public Schools) on using generative AI. Instructs fact-checking AI-generated content, transparency about AI's use, and avoiding sensitive data in prompts. Encourages experimentation and outlines responsible use principles for empowerment, inclusion, transparency, privacy, security, and public service.

Instructs the City agencies and departments of Boston, excluding Boston Public Schools, to use generative AI responsibly, with guidelines focusing on transparency, accountability, and inclusiveness.

Requires fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content for public communication to avoid inaccuracies and biases.

Emphasizes disclosing AI usage, including model type and version, to promote trust and transparency.

Prohibits sharing of sensitive or private information in AI prompts to protect residents' data privacy.

Encourages responsible experimentation with generative AI to support efficient, equitable city services while managing risks.

Directs the Department of Innovation and Technology to facilitate learning events and workshops on generative AI.

Advises consultation with relevant city offices and community organizations before publicizing AI-created content to ensure accessibility, accuracy, and sensitivity.

Promotes AI use in drafting documents, summarizing text, coding, and creating multimedia, while highlighting the importance of human oversight and editing.

Encourages engaging stakeholders for potential impacts on arts and society.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Minnesota Senate Bill 2909
document_name: Minnesota S 2909 (State Government)
body:
Require the Minnesota Fusion Center (MNFC) to annually report on the use of surveillance technologies, including artificial intelligence, types of activities monitored, and inter-agency data sharing. Involves AI governance and data practices oversight.

Requires the superintendent to prepare an annual report on the Minnesota Fusion Center (MNFC), detailing its general activities and monitored types, including AI or social media analysis tools.

Mandates inclusion of the MNFC's budget, staffing, and the technological tools utilized, specifically AI and data analysis technologies.

Obliges reporting on audit findings, data requests, suspicious activity reports (SARs), and the impact of AI tools in processing these reports.

Specifies the report must contain information on the MNFC's collaborations with local, state, and federal agencies, including data sharing and investigations aided by SARs and requests for information (RFIs).

Ensures the report's availability to relevant legislative committees and online by February 15 each year, starting in 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New York A7106
document_name: New York A7106 ("PAID Act")
body:
Amends election law to require disclosure of synthetic media in use in printed or digital political communications by writing or speaking, "This political communication was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence." Defines synthetic media as AI-modified text, image, video, or sound.

Amends the election law to mandate disclosure of synthetic media in political communications.

Requires disclosure for printed or digital political communications to display, "This political communication was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence."

Mandates non-printed or digital political communications, such as radio, to clearly display or speak the same statement.

Defines "synthetic media" as any form of media, including text, image, video, or sound, created or modified using AI algorithms.

Sets the effective date of this act to January 1, 2024.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Maryland House Bill 622
document_name: Maryland HB 622 (Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program)
body:
Establishes a grant program for small and medium-sized manufacturers to adopt Industry 4.0 technologies, including AI. Allocates grants competitively, requiring matching funds. Creates a special fund for grants. Mandates annual budget appropriations to support the program until 2028.

Establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program in Maryland's Department of Commerce to support small and medium-sized manufacturers in implementing advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to improve productivity and competitiveness.

Creates a special, nonlapsing Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund to provide financial support, with grants ranging from $25,000 to $500,000, requiring matching funds based on company size.

Reserves 20% of funds for manufacturers with 50 or fewer employees, allowing unused reserves to be reallocated to larger companies.

Requires grant recipients to report on fund usage within one year and mandates potential repayment if conditions are unmet.

Mandates the Governor to allocate $1,000,000 annually from 2024 to 2028 to the Fund.

Directs the Secretary to establish regulations for program implementation and commence the Act on October 1, 2023.

category: U.S. regulations, executive orders, and agency policies
title: National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update
document_name: National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan 2023 Update
body:
Updates the National AI R&D Strategic Plan to prioritize responsible AI research, human-AI collaboration, ethical considerations, AI safety, shared datasets, and workforce development. Expands public-private partnerships and international collaboration to advance equitable and trustworthy AI systems.

Requires the federal government to coordinate and focus R&D investments in AI to ensure U.S. leadership in trustworthy AI systems. 

Reaffirms eight strategies and adds a ninth to emphasize international collaboration in AI research.

Prioritizes investments in fundamental and responsible AI research, human-AI collaboration, and understanding ethical, legal, and societal implications.

Advances safety and security standards for AI systems, ensuring they are reliable and secure from vulnerabilities.

Develops shared public datasets and environments for AI training and testing to democratize access to AI resources.

Establishes benchmarks and standards for evaluating AI systems, including fairness, privacy, and bias considerations.

Addresses workforce needs by training and retraining a diverse AI-ready workforce.

Expands public-private partnerships to accelerate AI advances and facilitate global collaborations for responsible AI development.

Emphasizes the importance of AI governance and the development of international guidelines and standards for AI systems.

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 2338, of 2023
document_name: Brazil Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 2338, of 2023
body:
Establishes regulations for developing, implementing, and using AI systems in Brazil, emphasizing human rights, privacy, non-discrimination, and transparency. Requires risk assessment for AI applications, prohibiting excessive-risk systems. Defines governance and accountability for high-risk AI, stipulating rights to contest automated decisions. Designates a competent authority for oversight and enforcement, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance. Encourages innovation through regulatory sandboxes while ensuring data protection and ethical AI usage.

Sets general rules for AI development, implementation, and use in Brazil, prioritizing human rights, democratic values, and innovation.

Establishes principles such as transparency, non-discrimination, and human oversight for AI systems.

Defines 'artificial intelligence system' and 'artificial intelligence agents,' and assigns regulation and oversight to a designated competent authority.

Mandates that AI systems undergo preliminary risk assessment, with high-risk systems requiring algorithmic impact assessments.

Prohibits AI systems that exploit vulnerabilities or use subliminal techniques to harm individuals.

Requires transparency and accountability in AI systems, including the right to contest automated decisions and request human intervention.

Stipulates civil liability provisions, holding AI providers or operators accountable for damages, with stricter liability for high-risk systems.

Encourages innovation through regulatory sandboxes and considers AI impact on copyright and intellectual property.

Designates a competent authority for enforcement, inspection, and issuance of sanctions for non-compliance.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An act to amend Chapter 12 of Title 31 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the control of hazardous conditions, preventable diseases, and metabolic disorders [...]
document_name: Georgia House Bill 203 (2023)
body:
Regulates the use of artificial intelligence and other technology in eye assessments for medical purposes, including by requiring medical professionals to analyze any data collected or generated by automated systems.

Requires all eye assessments that utilize artificial intelligence or other advanced technology to conform to the traditional standards of in-person care.

Requires a medical professional to analyze any information collected or generated by an automated system during the eye assessment process.

Requires all eye assessments to involve the collection of a patient's relevant medical information, which must be stored in a medical record for at least 7 years.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An Act amending Title 18 (Crimes and Offenses) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in sexual offenses, providing for the offense of unlawful dissemination of artificially generated depiction; and, in minors, further providing for the offense of sexual abuse of children and for the offense of transmission of sexually explicit images by minor.
document_name: Creation and Dissemination of Sexually Explicit Content Act
body:
Makes it illegal to disseminate deepfake pornography -- lifelike visual content that depicts sexual scenes which did not occur in reality, including images of nudity and sexual acts -- in the state of Pennsylvania.

Proscibes disseminating "deepfake pornography" -- lifelike visual content that depicts sexual scenes which did not occur in reality, including images of nudity and sexual acts -- with the intent to harass, annoy, or alarm the depicted individual as a criminal misdemeanor offense in the state of Pennsylvania.

Exempts cases in which deepfake pornography was disseminated with the consent of the depicted individual from punishment under this law.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An act relating to a study on the establishment of a program administered by the Texas Workforce Commission to train individuals in certain skills related to artificial intelligence systems.
document_name: Texas Workforce Commission Act
body:
Requires the Texas House of Representatives committee overseeing workforce development to conduct a study on whether to establish an AI-related workforce training program.

Requires the Texas House of Representatives committee overseeing workforce development to conduct a study on whether to establish a workforce training program, administered by the Texas Workforce Commission, to train individuals currently in the workforce in the use, operation, and creation of AI systems. 

Requires the committee to report the results of the study to the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Speaker of the House, and corresponding committee in the Senate no later than December 1, 2024.

category: 한국지능정보사회진흥원(NIA)
title: [한국지능정보사회진흥원(NIA)] 2022 한국인터넷백서

category: Miscellaneous documents
title: Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada)
document_name: Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Canada)
body:
Mandates federal institutions to assess and mitigate risks of automated decision systems through Algorithmic Impact Assessments. Requires transparency, bias testing, data governance, peer review, and recourse mechanisms to ensure responsible, fair, and auditable AI use in administrative decisions.

Requires Algorithmic Impact Assessments before production of any automated decision system, with regular updates and public disclosure of results in accessible formats.

Mandate transparency by notifying individuals when decisions are made in whole or in part by automated systems, and by providing plain-language explanations of how and why decisions were made.

Direct rigorous testing and continuous monitoring of automated decision systems to detect and mitigate unintended biases and ensure compliance with laws. 

Obligates data governance and quality assurance, including peer reviews and Gender-based Analysis Plus.

Ensures the possibility of human intervention in automated decisions and provides clients with recourse options to challenge decisions.

Specifies consequences for non-compliance under the Financial Administration Act.

Designates the Chief Information Officer to provide guidance and maintain the Algorithmic Impact Assessment.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Mississippi Senate Bill 3000
document_name: Mississippi S 3000 (Eight Universities Fund), Section 42
body:
Reappropriates $53,478,000 from the Education Enhancement Fund for fiscal year 2023–2024 to the Institutions of Higher Learning. Allocate $15 million to the University of Mississippi for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence expenses as part of reauthorized Education Enhancement Funds for fiscal year 2023-2024.

Reappropriates $53,478,000 from the Education Enhancement Fund for fiscal year 2023–2024 to the Institutions of Higher Learning, consistent with the purposes.

Restricts total expenditures to the unexpended balance of funds remaining as of June 30, 2023, and does not alter the original purposes for which the funds were authorized.

Allocates $2,478,000 to multiple institutions for specified projects, including Delta State University for flight simulators and aviation equipment.

Allocations also include $12,000,000 to Mississippi State University for construction and high-performance computing infrastructure, $4,500,000 to Alcorn State University for facility improvements and STEM programs, $5,000,000 to Jackson State University for residence hall construction or renovation, and $2,500,000 to Mississippi University for Women for nursing program expansion.

Allocates $15,000,000 to the University of Mississippi for expenses in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, Healthcare Innovation, and related infrastructure.

Ensures funds support technology transfer and entrepreneurial programs including efforts potentially connected to Department of Defense and related federal research.

Requires consistency with the original authorization in Senate Bill 3002 from the 2022 Regular Session.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: State of Arizona Senate Bill 1565, An Act Amending Sections 16-442, 16-552 and 16-621, Arizona Revised Statutes; Relating to Conduct of Elections.
document_name: Bill limiting use of AI in elections
body:
Bans the use of artificial intelligence in counting, processing, or adjudicating ballots, and in verifying voters' affidavits, in Arizona.

Bans the use of artificial intelligence in the hardware or software used to (a) count, process, or adjudicate ballots, or (b) verify voters' affidavits, in Arizona.

category: Chinese law and policy
title: Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Comment)
document_name: Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Draft for Comment)
body:
Requires AI-generated content in China to meet a series of criteria, including accuracy, intellectual property protection, and respect for individual privacy; also requires AI developers to perform security assessments on their generative AI systems and submit those assessments to regulators.

Requires AI-generated content in China to meet a series of criteria, including accuracy, non-discrimination with regard to an array of protected characteristics, intellectual property protection, exclusion of violent content or content that subverts state power, and respect for individual privacy.

Requires AI developers to conduct a security assessment on generative AI systems that evaluates the cybersecurity of the system and its ability to comply with regulations; the assessment must be submitted to regulators before the system can be released for public use. 

Requires AI developers to prevent their generative AI systems from being used for various purposes, including engaging in unfair economic competition, and requires generative AI systems to make themselves inaccessible to individuals who use the systems for such purposes. 

Describes the legal liability that developers hold for the content generated by their AI systems and the punishments, including fines, they may face for violating these rules.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: An act to amend and reenact subsection 8 of section 1-01-49 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the definition of person; and to declare an emergency
document_name: North Dakota HB 1361 (2023)
body: Clarifies that artificial intelligence cannot qualify as a "person" for the purpose of North Dakota state law.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: New Mexico Senate Bill 192
document_name: New Mexico S 192 (Appropriations and Legislative Confidentiality), Section 9.
body:

title: A Bill in the District of Columbia to prohibit users of algorithmic decision-making from utilizing algorithmic eligibility determinations in a discriminatory manner, to require corresponding notices to individuals whose personal information is used, and to provide for appropriate means of civil enforcement.
document_name: Stop Discrimination by Algorithms Act of 2023
body:
Prohibits algorithms used to determine access to important opportunities (e.g., employment) or information about them in Washington D.C. from discriminating on the basis of protected classes; also mandates related algorithm audits, disclosures, and remedies for decisions made based on inaccurate data.

Prohibits entities in Washington D.C. from determining eligibility for, or access to information about, "important life opportunities" (e.g., housing or employment) on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, familial status, source of income, or disability in a discriminatory manner.

Requires entities to provide a public notice describing any algorithmic tools they use to determine eligibility for, or access to information about, important life opportunities. The notice must be sent to any individual about whom such a determination is made.

Requires the notice described above to cover the data collected by algorithmic tools and how that data is shared externally, how that data informs the tool's decisions, and the rights provided under this act.

Requires entities to provide notice, to any individual against whom they take any adverse action (e.g., firing) on the basis of an algorithmic determination, that the individual may access and submit corrections to any personal information considered by the algorithm. A human must then redo the decision based on the corrected information.  

Requires entities to audit their algorithmic decision-making tools before deployment and annually thereafter to analyze discriminatory effects and other impacts, and then implement reasonable measures to address findings of unlawful disparate impact. Entities must submit a report on the audit to the DC government.

Permits affected individuals or the DC Attorney General to file a civil action in response to violations of this law, with fines up to $10,000 per violation.

 and oversight of personal data (Section 7)
document_name: New York Data Privacy Act, Section 7
body:
Requires entities that decline access to important services (e.g. healthcare and financing) on the basis of an AI system's decision to evaluate the system for accuracy & discrimination, to disclose the system's use, and to enable affected individuals to appeal the decision to a human being.

Requires any entity in New York that uses AI or another automated process as the sole basis of a decision that denies access to financial services, insurance, housing, public accommodation, healthcare, or basic necessities to:

(a) Clearly and conspicuously disclose that the decision was made solely on the basis of an automated process; and

(b) Enable any affected individual to appeal the decision, including by giving them the right to have a human review it.

Requires the above entities, and additionally those that use an automated decision systems to determine access to employment and education, to annually solicit an outside auditor to conduct, and make publicly available, an impact assessment of the system that:

(a) Evaluates the system's objectives, design, and training data, as well as how the system was tested for accuracy and discrimination; and 

(b) Assesses whether the system produces discriminatory results on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, familial status, biometric information, lawful source of income, or disability.

title: 21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology")
document_name: 21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology")
body:
Requires a software algorithm device for assisting users in digital pathology -- an in vitro device intended to evaluate acquired scanned pathology images to assist in diagnosis -- to be subject to special control from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Those special controls require detailed product labeling; device performance assessments meeting specific standards; a detailed description of the device's software; and a risk management plan, including measures to protect cybersecurity.

Classifies a software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology -- an in vitro device intended to evaluate acquired scanned pathology whole slide images to assist in diagnosis -- into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II, requiring special controls. That set of special controls:

Requires detailed product labeling, including instructions for use and notices of the device's limitations.

Requires performance assessments of the device that meets pre-set standards for rigor, evaluate the device's performance when used by its intended users, and cover the entire spectrum of challenging cases likely to be encountered in the device's operation. 

Requires a detailed description of the workings of the device's software.

Requires a risk management plan, including mechanisms to mitigate cybersecurity risks.
