body:
In Mexico, ANIA organizes working groups on AI to democratize knowledge and contribute to public policies and best practices. The need for an AI "sandbox" as a flexible mechanism to address technical, legal, and ethical implications was highlighted. In collaboration with the UK Embassy and AMCID, an analysis was initiated to promote technical exchange between the two countries and update the AI landscape in Mexico.

The collaboration between the British Embassy in Mexico, the Mexican Academy of Cybersecurity and Digital Law and ANIA is a significant step towards the consolidation of the AI ecosystem in Mexico. This project seeks to identify, together with regulators and experts, alternatives and tools to establish ethical standards and uses in the implementation of AI. Through the participation of specialists from various sectors, the aim is to answer crucial questions about the regulation, design and governance of  regulatory sandboxes,  paving the way for a more trustworthy, responsible and ethical digital future in Mexico.

The AI Politeia Lab, a project of the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications (IIT), one of five National Centres for Scientific Research (NCSR) “Demokritos”, is an interdisciplinary lab set up to explore how to ensure a responsible and sustainable technology-enabled future by fostering innovative academic and industrial research across domains in a virtual environment.

The AI Politeia Lab, part of the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications (IIT) at NCSR “Demokritos,” is an interdisciplinary research hub in Greece dedicated to studying how AI can be developed and applied responsibly. It was established to combine insights from technology, ethics, and policy in order to shape a sustainable, human-centred digital future. Working in a virtual, cross-domain environment, the lab fosters collaboration between academia and industry, supporting projects that test innovative approaches to governance, accountability, and the social impact of AI. Its role is to serve as a space where technological advances are critically assessed and aligned with long-term societal values.

title: AI Pilot Schools: Learning and Teaching with AI Tools
document_name: KI-Pilotschulen: Lernen und Lehren mit KI-Tools
body:
The initiative žAI Pilot Schools explores the integration of AI tools in Austrian classrooms through empirical research. It includes three phases: an initial survey on AI use, a second survey documenting practical experiences, and ongoing documentation by teachers. The initiative aims to provide insights into AI-supported teaching and learning.

The initiative žAI Pilot Schools, spearheaded by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science, and Research, examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools. The project involves three empirical phases: Baseline Survey (2023/24): A comprehensive questionnaire was distributed to assess the status quo of AI usage in Austrian schools. This survey combined rating scales and open questions to gather insights into the existing knowledge and tools available. Focus Survey (2024): Building on the initial results, a second quantitative survey titled žAI Pilot Schools in Focus documented teachers' experiences with AI technologies in their classrooms. Ongoing Documentation (2024): Teachers were provided with a structured template to record their qualitative experiences with AI-based learning tools throughout 2024.The surveys and documentation are conducted online, ensuring direct communication with the participating pilot schools. Data from the surveys have been analyzed using SPSS, while the qualitative documentation is being evaluated with MAXQDA software. These insights aim to support evidence-based recommendations for AI integration in education, enhancing teaching practices and student learning outcomes in the digital age.

title: AI Idea Workshop for Environmental Protection
document_name: KI-Ideenworkshop für Umweltschutz

category: National – Strategy

title: AI Action Plan
document_name: KI-Aktionsplan
body:
The German Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR)'s strategic update to Germany's national AI strategy, comprising 50+ existing and 20+ new AI measures across eleven action areas, backed by over EUR 1.6B in BMFTR AI investment in the current legislative period.

Presented by the BMFTR (then BMBF) in November 2023, the KI-Aktionsplan is Germany's operational update to the federal AI strategy first adopted in 2018 (updated December 2020). It identifies 11 action areas: (1) strengthen the research base; (2) set a new research agenda; (3) expand AI infrastructure; (4) drive an AI skills offensive; (5) explore and shape AI in education; (6) accelerate transfer to economic growth; (7) AI in health for societal benefit; (8) unlock societal and scientific AI value; (9) deepen European and international cooperation; (10) promote responsible AI; (11) improve AI governance. The plan encompasses 50 ongoing initiatives and at least 20 new ones. BMFTR alone commits over EUR 1.6B in AI investment in the current legislative period (2021–2025). Core instruments include the 6 national AI Competence Centres, the DFKI, the National High-Performance Computing Alliance (NHR), the AI in Production (ProKI) network, the ZIM programme, the Forschungszulage, and international collaborations through the OECD, G7, G20 and EU. The plan explicitly aims to make Germany and Europe leaders in AI — 'KI made in Germany' — while resisting overregulation. Target audience spans the entire German AI ecosystem: research institutions, SMEs, large industry, the public sector, and the education system.

title: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation
body:
A UK regulatory framework proposal designed to accelerate innovation while ensuring safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence across sectors.

The Blueprint for AI Regulation outlines the United Kingdom’s proposed approach to regulating artificial intelligence through a flexible and pro-innovation framework. Rather than establishing a single central regulator, the blueprint builds on existing sector-specific regulators and provides them with guidance and tools to oversee AI applications within their respective domains. A key component of the blueprint is the proposed AI Growth Lab, a regulatory experimentation platform designed to test innovative AI products and services under controlled regulatory conditions. The Growth Lab would function as a cross-sector regulatory sandbox, allowing companies to pilot AI technologies while regulators monitor outcomes, evaluate risks and adapt regulatory frameworks accordingly. The initiative aims to reduce regulatory uncertainty, accelerate market entry for new AI applications and generate evidence for future rule-making.

This joint initiative by the education programme Vedliai and Lietuvos Junior Achievement (LJA) addresses the gap in practical digital and entrepreneurial education for young students in Lithuania. Many pupils in grades 5–8 are not exposed early enough to how computer science and entrepreneurship can connect to real-world opportunities. The project aims to change this by offering integrated lessons that combine coding, digital creativity, and business thinking in ways that are accessible and engaging.
The programme is delivered directly in schools, supported by trained teachers and mentors who adapt the lessons to pupils’ age and interests. By blending computer science with entrepreneurship, it equips students with both technical and problem-solving skills while encouraging creativity and teamwork. Over time, the project plans to expand to more schools across Lithuania, ensuring that a larger share of pupils gain the knowledge and confidence needed to participate in the country’s growing digital economy.

Classifies the Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid, a machine-learning software program and device used in the diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder, into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II regulatory category requiring special controls. The mandated special controls are as follows:

Requires clinical performance testing to demonstrate that the device performs as intended under anticipated conditions of use, including an evaluation of sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value using a reference method of diagnosis and assessment of patient behavioral symptomology.

body:
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to appoint a lead coordinator to address the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems, develop a comprehensive action plan, and report findings to Congress. Encourages collaboration among members of the Five Eyes Partnership and Israel in countering these threats.

Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to designate an official from the intelligence community to serve as the lead coordinator for countering and neutralizing the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems.

Requires this Coordinator to develop a comprehensive plan of action, driven by intelligence information, for countering and neutralizing the threats posed by the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems and submit a briefing of such plans to the Congress.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a final report on the activities and findings of the Coordinator to the appropriate committees of Congress.

document_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6505 ("Assessments of production of semiconductors by the People's Republic of China")
body:
After this act is passed, the Director of National Intelligence must submit a detailed report about the production of semiconductors in China. The Director must also meet with federal agencies' heads to discuss the report and other findings related to the Chinese production of semiconductors.

Begins discussing the phrase “appropriate committees of Congress” and what organizations are actually a part of this phrase when benign referred. Also defines the term “legacy semiconductor” in terms of the definition given in another legislation document.

Annually for 3 years after this act is passed, the Director of National Intelligence must submit an unclassified assessment report regarding China’s production of semiconductors through China’s firms and business sectors to the appropriate committees of Congress.

The Director of National Intelligence must meet with the heads of federal agencies to discuss the elements of the assessment. They must discuss the self-sufficiency of China in the fields of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, autonomous vehicles, and other newer-technological areas. They must discuss China’s access to intellectual property related to leading edge process nodes, including electronic design automation technology. They must discuss Chinese firms’s production of semiconductors that are not legacy conductors and stockpiling efforts of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. They must discuss the relative market share and its trends of Chinese semiconductor manufacturers at different process nodes. They must discuss the outside recruitment activity into Chinese semiconductors firms and the capability of the Chinese workforce in developing semiconductors that are not legacy semiconductors and relevant equipment.

title: James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 162 ("Assessment and strategy for fielding capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms")
document_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 162 ("Assessment and strategy for fielding capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms")
body:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to assess the threats and national security implications of unmanned aerial system swarms and review the capabilities of the Defense Department to counter these threats. Directs the Secretary of Defense to develop a strategy to field capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms and report the assessment findings and strategy to the congressional defense committees.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to assess threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms to installations and deployed Armed Forces, the use of these swarms by adversaries and their national security implications such as autonomous intelligence and machine learning, current capabilities of the Defense Department and their effectiveness in countering these threats, and efforts by the Defense Department to develop and field technology that can counter swarms.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a strategy to field capabilities to counter threats from unmanned aerial system swarms. The strategy should define "unmanned aerial system swarm," outline plans for developing, testing, fielding, and acquiring capabilities to counter swarms, estimate resources needed by each Armed Force to implement the strategy, and determine the legislative action necessary for the Defense Department to counter swarm threats.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to consider incorporating the strategy into a comprehensive strategy to defend against unmanned aerial systems and to report the assessment findings and strategy to the congressional defense committees within 270 days.

title: James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence")
document_name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence")
body:
Requires the Commander of the United States Cyber Command and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a five-year implementation plan for rapidly adopting and acquiring artificial intelligence systems to support the Department of Defense.

Requires the Commander of the United States Cyber Command and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a five-year implementation plan for rapidly adopting artificial intelligence systems to support the Department of Defense. 

The plan shall: 

(a) Identify and prioritize AI systems and data that currently affect, or may benefit in the future, the Department's cybersecurity and cyber operations. 

(b) Lay out a plan to acquire AI systems and data identified in part (a).

(c) Identify relevant skill deficiencies.

(d) Identify opportunities to solicit AI system operator feedback.

(e) Identify and address long term technology gaps for the Department's cyber war fighting mission.

(f) Evaluate the risks posed by adversary AI-based attacks.

(g) Furnish a timeline with target milestones, investments, and required expenditures.
 
(h) Incorporate metrics to evaluate AI adoption.

(i) Identify further funding, authorities, and policies that may be necessary.

(j) Define a maturity model describing desired cyber capabilities independent of specific technology solutions.

body:

body:
Subjects deep synthesis technology in China to a variety of regulations, including restrictions on false or otherwise unwanted content, sending notification to individuals if their biometric information is being edited, and labelling deep synthesis content. Mandates security assessments and implementation of security measures.

Prohibits generative AI ("deep synthesis") systems in China from producing a variety of forms of unwanted content, including false information or content that harms lawful rights, national security and "social order."

Requires deep synthesis systems to verify the true identity of each of their users.

Requires deep synthesis developers to assess the security of their AI systems, including by assessing the systems' cybersecurity attributes and their ability to abide by relevant regulations.

Requires deep synthesis systems to notify any individuals whose biometric information is edited in the production of AI-generated content.

Requires the labelling or watermarking  of realistic deep synthesis content that could potentially mislead or confuse the public.

Requires deep synthesis developers to submit filings with the relevant authorities, and requires regulators to carry out inspections of deep synthesis systems.

title: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
document_name: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
body:
Requires pre-deployment testing, risk mitigation, and ongoing monitoring for automated systems' safety and effectiveness. Mandates independent evaluations, public reporting, and avoiding inappropriate data. Demands protections against algorithmic discrimination and data privacy. Institutes oversight on surveillance technologies. Requires clear user notifications and explanations. Insists on transparency and accountability through independent evaluations.

Requires automated systems to undergo pre-deployment testing, risk identification, mitigation, and ongoing monitoring to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Requires that systems avoid the use of inappropriate or irrelevant data and that independent evaluations and public reporting confirm system safety and effectiveness.

Imposes protections against algorithmic discrimination by incorporating proactive equity assessments, representative data usage, and continuous disparity testing and mitigation.

Enforces data privacy through built-in protections, user consent for data collection, and limitations on data use and sharing, particularly in sensitive domains such as health, education, and finance.

Institutes heightened oversight and limits on surveillance technologies to protect civil liberties, privacy, and democratic values, with specific restrictions on continuous surveillance in sensitive contexts.

Requires designers and deployers of automated systems to provide clear, timely, and accessible notice and explanations of system use, including the rationale behind decisions impacting individuals.

Calls for independent evaluations and public reporting to ensure transparency and accountability in the use of automated systems, with detailed documentation and assessments.

title: California (2021-2022) SB 1398
document_name: California SB 1398 (Consumer notices of automated vehicles)
body:
Requires dealers and manufacturers to provide distinct notices of partial driving automation feature functions and limitations at time of sale or upgrade, and prohibits misleading marketing language implying full autonomous vehicle functionality.

Prohibits dealers and manufacturers from selling or upgrading vehicles with partial driving automation features without providing a distinct notice including the feature's name, functions, and limitations.

Prohibits manufacturers and dealers from using language in marketing materials that implies partial driving automation features make a vehicle fully autonomous when they do not.

Defines "partial driving automation feature" as Level 2 partial driving automation per Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) Standard J3016 (April 2021).

Requires manufacturers to provide dealers with specific recommended language for the required notice before vehicle delivery.

Specifies that compliance does not alter existing duty of care or civil liability for negligence or product defects, and that manufacturers are not held in violation if they provide required information to dealers who fail to notify buyers.

category: U.S. federal laws
title: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future")
document_name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future")
body:
Provides scholarships and fellowships for AI-related studies to recruit and train the next generation of AI professionals in US government. Grants competitive grants and fellowships for organizations advancing risk assessment through AI. Adds AI and machine learning to the list of research areas that the Director of the National Science Foundation can award grants to. Makes awards available for supporting basic research to advance critical minerals mining strategies that involve AI. Requires the development and testing of models to inform implementation of government-wide data infrastructure for statistical activities. Requires a study on U.S. higher education's AI research capacity and an annual update to key technology focus areas.

Instructs the Director of the National Science Foundation (Director) to develop a report on the need and feasibility as well as construct plans to implement a program to recruit and train the next generation of AI professionals in US government. Mandates that the report include statistical data on the federal AI workforce, assessments of current and future demand for AI expertise across the federal government and the ability of higher education institutions to prepare students to meet this demand, and an evaluation of the need for and feasibility of establishing a scholarship-for-service program for AI professionals in US government, as well as the possibility of leveraging existing programs such as the Federal Cyber Scholarship-for-Service Program. 

Authorizes the Director and other appropriate agency heads to establish a Federal AI scholarship-for-service program to recruit and train AI professionals to achieve the missions of US government. Requires the Director, in coordination with other agency heads, to establish criteria such as excellence in AI education and the ability to attract diverse students to designate qualified institutions of higher education that shall be eligible to participate in the program. Requires the program to provide scholarships through qualified higher education institutions to students pursuing fields of study related to AI, provide scholarship recipients with temporary appointments related to work on AI in the federal government, prioritize placement of scholarship recipients in executive agencies, identify opportunities to promote multidisciplinary programs of study, support capacity building for educational institutions to enable them to train the next-generation AI workforce, create courses in technology ethics for scholarship recipients, and award fellowships to masters and doctoral students who are pursuing degrees or research in AI and related fields. Instructs scholarship amounts to cover a student’s tuition and fees for not more than 3 years with an additional stipend, and obligates scholarship recipients to work for a period of time equivalent to the length of the scholarship in the AI mission of the US government entity or affiliated entity.

Instructs the Director to establish competitive awards to institutions to advance knowledge of risk assessment including the utilization of AI in our ability to understand and predict extreme events and natural hazards, create engineered system solutions and develop instrumentation for innovation in resilient infrastructure, and advance research on multidisciplinary wildfire science and behaviors related to increasing resilience.

Amends Section 506(a) of the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010 by adding AI and machine learning to the list of research areas that fall under information technologies for manufacturing that the Director can award grants to.

Instructs the Director to make competitive awards to institutions to support basic research to advance critical minerals mining strategies to make better use of domestic resources and eliminate national reliance on minerals subject to supply chain disruptions, including the application of AI for geological exploration of critical minerals and the application of machine learning for detection and sorting of critical minerals.

Requires the Director to conduct or support the development of a study on AI research capacity at US institutions of higher education. Requires the study to, at minimum, address which universities are putting out significant peer-reviewed AI research based on quantity and number of citations, which factors of these universities such as computing power enable their research, promising practices at these universities for advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in AI research programs, geographic diversity of universities that have AI research-enabling factors, and how universities that are not currently top producers of AI research could improve, including potential pilot programs that the federal government could develop or support to help universities produce AI research.

Instructs the Director, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the interagency committee established under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020, to develop and test models to inform the implementation of a government-wide data linkage and access infrastructure for statistical activities.

Requires the Director to identify, and annually review and update a list of not more than 10 key technology focus areas, which includes AI, machine learning, autonomy, and related advances.

body:

Define "assessment mechanism" to include AI and technology used for remote or in-person eye assessments.

Require such mechanisms to offer patient-provider interaction, gather patient history, and acknowledge limitations, including not replacing in-person exams or issuing initial contact lens prescriptions.

Impose civil penalties up to $10,000 for violations, with rights to hearings and appeals.

category: Multinational
title: AI Liability Directive
document_name: AI Liability Directive
body:
Establishes common rules for AI-related civil damages claims, including disclosure and preservation of evidence for high-risk AI systems, rebuttable presumptions on non-compliance and causation, and implementation and review requirements for Member States and the Commission.

Establishes common EU rules for fault-based civil claims involving AI systems. It clarifies the Directive’s scope and relationship to other Union and national liability regimes, allowing Member States to maintain or adopt more claimant-oriented compatible rules, and defines key terms including AI system, high-risk AI system, provider, user, claimant, and duty of care. It empowers national courts, under specified conditions, to order the disclosure and preservation of evidence concerning high-risk AI systems, subject to proportionality, confidentiality, and procedural safeguards, and creates rebuttable presumptions regarding non-compliance with a duty of care and the causal link between fault and an AI system’s output or failure to produce an output. It also specifies how those presumptions apply to providers and users of high-risk AI systems, when they are limited or unavailable, and the defendant’s right to rebut them. 

In addition, it requires Commission review, monitoring, and reporting on the Directive’s operation, including consideration of possible no-fault liability and insurance rules, amends Directive (EU) 2020/1828, and requires Member States to transpose the Directive into national law and communicate their implementing measures to the Commission.

Requires that adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicators -- medical devices used to predict cardiovascular health -- be subject to special controls in the U.S. Those controls include the following:

Requires a risk assessment of the device, including full disclosure of software specs and different inputs considered when making predictions about future cardiovascular health.

Requires scientific justification for the device's efficacy, including verification of algorithm calculations and validation using an independent data set.

Requires a human factors and usability engineering assessment to evaluate the risk of misinterpretation of device output.

Requires a clinical data assessment that specifies the clinical data used and an evaluation of output consistency.

title: An Act concerning discrimination and automated decision systems and supplementing P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.).
document_name: New Jersey SB1402
body:
Prohibits financial lenders, insurance companies and healthcare providers from using automated decision systems to discriminate against protected classes in providing services.

Bans banks, mortgage companies and other lending institutions from using AI systems which discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in the provision of loans and credit terms.

Bans insurance companies from using AI systems which discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in providing insurance coverage and setting the terms and rates of such coverage.

Bans health care providers from using AI systems to discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in assessing eligibility for healthcare services.

Categorizes the above use of AI systems which discriminate against members of protected classes as unlawful discrimination; such companies and service providers are subject to fines not exceeding $10,000 on the first instance, if these companies have not committed prior violations within five years of the charge, and permits victims to file civil lawsuits against such companies.

The strategy aims to optimize and integrate existing health information systems, improve data security, and enhance the efficiency of healthcare management processes. title: Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls
document_name: Ulysses - Análises inteligentes em enquetes
body:
“Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls” is an AI algorithm that analyses citizens' comments on e-polls about legislative bills available. The algorithm identifies the main arguments for and against each legislative bill in progress, grouping them. As all legislative bills are available for e-polls, there is a huge number of citizens contributing opinions. In addition, quantitative indicators are not sufficient to effectively identify exactly the items of articles accepted or rejection by citizens.

The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies defined that all bills presented by parliamentarians are systematically made available to receive citizens' contributions through e-polls. There are about 16,000 proposals per year, and some of them receive more than 1,000,000 suggestions/comments from citizens during the weeks of greatest discussion on the topic. 
It was observed that merely knowing the percentage of citizens who were for/against a legislative bill is not sufficient to improve the legislative text. Therefore, it was necessary to add an analysis of a free field in the e-poll through which citizens are invited to leave their comments and opinions. A human full analysis on these opinions is practically impossible, due to the large number and the timeliness with which parliamentarians need to position themselves in debates regarding those bills. 
The "Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls" algorithm identifies the main arguments for and against each legislative bill in progress, grouping them and showing how distant the opinion groups are from each other. The analysis is semantic, which enables deep analysis of opinions, identifying situations of irony included in the texts. In addition to results presented in text format, the algorithm also presents a graphical view of citizens' opinion groups.
Results, outcomes and impacts
More accurate and timely analysis of the arguments for and against a legislative bill, which makes it possible to identify: 
Which part of the legislative text is most accepted or rejected by citizens; Whether there is any problem with society's interpretation of the legislative proposal, which may have resulted from disinformation.Challenges and lessons learned
Qualitative analyses of large volumes of data need to be incorporated into analyses on content received from citizens;This type of analysis is an important mechanism for identifying the impact that disinformation has on citizens' opinions

title: Transitional study support
body:
To facilitate the re-skilling of professionals (not only on AI), in 2022, the government introduced the study support, which gives adults aged between 27 and 62 the opportunity to study and broaden their skills. For one year, professionals can receive a study grant equivalent to 80% of their pre-study salary, and for a further year, they can apply for a student loan.

In a rapidly changing job market, many adults need to update or learn new skills to stay competitive and meet the demands of evolving industries. This challenge is not limited to technology fields like artificial intelligence but affects a wide range of professions. To support working professionals in this transition, the government introduced a study support program in 2022. The program aims to help adults between the ages of 27 and 62 take time to study and expand their skills without losing financial stability.
The main goal of the program is to make it easier for adults to return to education and improve their qualifications, whether they want to specialize in new areas like AI or pursue other fields. To do this, the program offers financial aid that covers part of the individual’s income during their studies. Specifically, for the first year of study, participants receive a grant equal to 80% of their previous salary. This support helps reduce the financial risks involved in leaving work temporarily to focus on learning. After this initial year, those who want to continue their education can apply for a student loan to help cover the costs for a second year.
This initiative involves the government working together with educational institutions and financial agencies to manage the program and provide funding. Eligible adults can apply for this support and choose study programs that fit their career plans and the needs of the labor market. By providing both grants and loans, the program offers a flexible way for professionals to reskill or upskill in a way that suits their individual situations.
The initiative reflects a commitment to lifelong learning, helping workers remain employable and productive as industries evolve, especially with the ongoing impact of technologies like artificial intelligence.

France participates in the five Testing and experimentation facilities for AI. French players coordinate two of them (PREVAIL and AI MATTERS). France is also coordinating the ALT-EDIC initiative that integrates evaluation activities for advanced AI models.

France participates in the EU network of Testing & Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) to help companies trial AI in real-world settings and de-risk deployment. French actors are involved across all five TEFs and **coordinate two of them—PREVAIL and AI-MATTERS—**bringing national labs, firms, and public bodies together to run large-scale, sector-specific tests and share results.
In parallel, France leads the ALT-EDIC initiative, which integrates evaluation activities for advanced AI models, complementing TEF pilots with common methods, benchmarks, and governance so solutions proven in TEFs can be assessed consistently across the EU.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Technology Incubation Project
body:
This initiative focuses on developing a network of technology incubation hubs in Czechia to foster the growth of start-ups and spin-offs, especially in innovative AI fields. By 2025, the project aims to support around 250 start-ups with both financial aid and mentoring, helping them bring new AI-driven products and services to market.

The Technology Incubation programme in Czechia supports early-stage start-ups and spin-offs in fields like AI, mobility, space, and sustainability. It was created to address the lack of early funding, mentoring, and customer access that often prevents young teams from growing. By 2025, the aim is to help around 250 start-ups bring new products and services to market.
Selected start-ups receive non-equity grants, tailored mentoring, and access to specialised hubs across the country. New cohorts are admitted in waves, and AI has emerged as one of the strongest tracks with dozens of projects already in incubation. The long-term plan is to build a national ecosystem where successful alumni and investors feed back into supporting the next generation of start-ups.

body:

This project on unlocking the power of sensitive data for use in AI is running from December 2019 to March 2020 and is budgeted at AED 1 million.The initiative has the following objectives:To test (through attack scenarios) the degree to which synthetic data can retain the privacy and other sensitive aspects of classified data, whilst also retaining the underlying relationships between variables.To test the technical performance of AI models trained on synthetic data alongside models using real data, and to establish the usefulness of synthetic data in a range of use cases (focused on highly sophisticated analytics and AI product development).To explore the potential of creating a synthetic city data store to boost the supply of high quality, high value data for AI.

Hungary’s Recovery and Resilience Plan includes a health-sector digitalization component that seeks to modernize prevention, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up through ICT. The measures are framed to improve efficiency and access while strengthening data security, reducing administrative load, and building digital skills across institutions. Planned actions include upgrading core e-health infrastructure, expanding interoperable services for clinicians and patients, and coordinating implementation so that hospitals and primary care adopt common standards and tools. The intent is to create a more connected system where health data can be used safely for care, management, and quality improvement.

The plan supports the development of intelligent transport systems (ITS) and multimodal transport solutions.

The Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030 sets out a comprehensive roadmap for modernizing Slovakia’s transport sector using AI and digital technologies. It emphasizes the systematic development of Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) to enable real-time traffic management, automation, and operational efficiency across all transport modes.

Road transport: Developing peripheral infrastructure on highways and major roads to support intelligent transport technologiesRail transport: Modernizing the European Railway Traffic Management System (ERTMS) and the European Train Control System (ETCS) to improve automation and safetyWater transport: Implementing River Information Services (RIS) with AI-driven systems for better navigation and operational efficiencyMultimodal transport: Enhancing AI-based models for planning and operational coordination across transport modesThe plan reflects Slovakia’s commitment to adopting AI technologies in line with broader EU standards and objectives, aiming to increase safety, optimize traffic flows, and improve overall transport functionality. title: Regulatory Framework for Automated Vehicles in Australia
document_name: Regulatory Framework for Automated Vehicles in Australia
body:
Policy paper, which was subsequently endorsed by the Infrastructure and Transport Ministers' Meeting in February 2022. The paper outlines the proposed end-to-end regulatory framework for the commercial deployment of automated vehicles in Australia. The design of this framework represents the culmination of work led by the NTC over the five years on national reforms for automated vehicles, and was developed in consultation withgovernments and industry.

On 11 February 2022, at the meeting of Infrastructure and Transport Ministers (ITMM), transport ministers from all Australian jurisdictions agreed that the future Automated Vehicle Safety Law will be implemented through Commonwealth law. This agreement built on a 2020 agreement to work towards establishing a national approach to regulating automated vehicles when they are commercially deployed on Australian roads. Earlier work (from 2016-2018) focused on a safety assurance system for automated driving systems, to ensure the safety of automated vehicles when they are first supplied to the market.The initiative has the following objective(s):The purpose of this paper is to present proposals on the end-to-end regulatory framework for the commercial deployment of automated vehicles. This framework consists of existing Commonwealth and state and territory frameworks, frameworks already agreed by ministers as part of automated vehicle reforms, and recommendations for in-service safety. The NTC undertook targeted consultation with key stakeholders to understand whether the regulatory framework will achieve national outcomes, potential gaps, and how it will impact on different sectors. The framework presented in the paper includes recommendations on the detailed content of the proposed in-service Automated Vehicle Safety Law. It also identifies further work on the reform program, focused on amendments to state and territory law to accommodate automated vehicles.

title: Reform of Higher Education for a Green and Resilient Transition to Society 5.0
body:
This reform supports the digital transformation of education by improving digital skills and teaching practices in higher education. It includes pilot projects in AI, cybersecurity, and other advanced technologies, as well as training for educators. It also introduces micro-credentials to quickly meet changing skill needs.

Slovenia is actively working to modernize its higher education system by supporting the digital transformation of teaching and learning. The goal is to equip both students and educators with the skills needed to succeed in a world shaped by advanced technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, and blockchain. This reform addresses the urgent need to update digital skills and teaching methods so that graduates are prepared for the demands of the modern labor market, especially in fast-growing tech sectors.
As part of a broader education reform, guidelines and an implementation plan were developed to enhance digital competencies through pilot projects and targeted training. The initiative focuses on advanced digital skills such as AI, blockchain, and cybersecurity, and aims to strengthen digital teaching abilities in higher education. A key element is the introduction of micro-credentials, enabling universities to respond flexibly to evolving labor market demands, particularly in emerging tech fields like AI, though funding for AI-specific actions is still being finalised. These micro-credentials provide a way for students and professionals to gain recognition for specific skills in a short time, helping to keep pace with rapid changes in technology and industry needs.
The reform includes pilot projects that test new approaches to teaching with digital tools and technologies in Slovenian universities. Educators receive focused training to better incorporate these advanced subjects into their courses. Collaboration among universities, government bodies, and industry stakeholders ensures that the curriculum remains relevant and aligned with the skills required in the workplace. By embedding these practices within higher education, Slovenia aims to create a learning environment that balances theoretical knowledge with practical application of digital technologies.
Looking to the future, this initiative is expected to grow as additional funding becomes available, especially for AI-related activities. The use of micro-credentials offers a flexible, scalable solution that allows universities to quickly adapt and introduce new programs aligned with the evolving needs of the digital economy. Through these efforts, Slovenia is building a foundation for ongoing improvement in digital education, helping students and educators stay ahead in a rapidly changing technological landscape.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: ROBUST
body:
The ROBUST consortium, initiated in 2022, is a 10-year research project focusing on reliable and trustworthy AI. Comprising 54 partners in AI labs, including knowledge institutions, private companies, and civil society organisations, ROBUST aims to enhance AI systems across five dimensions: accuracy, reliability, repeatability, resilience, and safety. It seeks to formalize AI reliability through contracts and develop methods to foster trust in AI systems.

The ROBUST consortium, which began in 2022, is a major European research effort spanning ten years that is designed to strengthen the reliability and trustworthiness of AI systems. With 54 partners drawn from universities, research institutions, industry, and civil-society organizations, the initiative brings together a wide spectrum of expertise. Its goal is to improve AI across five core dimensions: accuracy, reliability, repeatability, resilience, and safety. One important strand of work is to formalize notions of reliability in AI using flexible contracts or guarantees, so that users and developers can trust behaviour in changing environments. The consortium also develops methods, tools, and frameworks aimed at building trust—for instance by making AI decisions more interpretable, robust to faults, and verifiable.

REASSURE supports decision-making for energy operators and policymakers, helping them manage both current operations and future energy challenges.

Contributing to the green transition, supporting sustainable and environmentally friendly solutions.Increasing investment in research and development, to strengthen Slovenia’s innovation capacity.Enhancing productivity, including material and energy efficiency, through advanced technologies.Boosting the competitiveness of the economy, particularly by fostering innovation-driven growth.From this initiative:
95 R&D projects carried out by consortia of companies received public co-funding.18 projects specifically focused on the application of artificial intelligence, underscoring the growing importance of AI in economic transformation.AI was integrated not only within the ICT programme, but also partially into nine other sectoral programmes overseen by the ministry.This initiative illustrates how Slovenia is embedding AI into broader economic development and innovation strategies, ensuring that digital technologies contribute to sustainability, competitiveness, and long-term growth.
Looking ahead, these measures are expected to stimulate AI adoption across industries, foster cross-sectoral innovation, and further align national R&D with EU green and digital priorities.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation (MAETD; Ministerio de Asuntos Económicos y Transformación Digital)
title: Quantum Spain
document_name: Quantum Spain
body:
Quantum Spain promotes and funds a competitive quantum computing infrastructure to strengthen Spain’s scientific and technological base in quantum computing and its AI applications. It supports the national ecosystem with essential tools and resources. In 2023, Spanish authorities announced that Southern Europe’s first quantum computer would be installed in Barcelona.

Quantum Spain aims is to address the reinforcement in the quantum field envisaged in ENIA Action Line N. 15, through the implementation of a cooperative project financed through the direct award of grants to a group of entities belonging to the Spanish Supercomputing Network (RES by its Spanish acronym), for the creation of an IA quantum computing ecosystem. 
The initiative has the following objectives:
Building a high-performance quantum computer and making it accesible to the scientific communityCreating a remote cloud access service to the quantum processor, to enable industry and the public sector to experiment with quantum algorithmsDeveloping libraries of quantum algorithms and quantum machine learning, applicable to real problems, for end users in both companies and public entities

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Ministry of University and Research; National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP)
title: Quantum Computing Research and Development Programme
document_name: Programma di Ricerca e Sviluppo sul Calcolo Quantistico
body:
The Italian quantum computing initiative is a key component of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP). This programme is designed to bolster Italy’s quantum computing capabilities by supporting the entire research and development spectrum—from fundamental research to technological applications and market deployment.

The NQSTI is a three-year programme with a total funding of €115.9 million under the NRRP, specifically aligned with the European Union’s NextGenerationEU framework. The initiative encompasses three main action lines:
Enhancing Research Infrastructure
Developing state-of-the-art facilities and platforms for quantum research, including integration with high-performance computing infrastructures and the European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI).Fostering Collaboration Between Academia and Industry
Establishing a network of national quantum institutes to optimize resources, bridge research with industry, and stimulate industrial innovation through joint laboratories and prototyping.Developing Innovative Research Models
Implementing new standards, training programs, and fostering the creation of spin-offs and start-ups, particularly focusing on the southern regions of Italy to promote balanced regional development.The NQSTI is a consortium that includes over 20 institutions, comprising research centres, universities, and enterprises across Italy. It aims to translate quantum research into industrial applications, addressing the entire innovation chain—from fundamental research to market deployment.
A significant aspect of the programme is its emphasis on education and outreach, aiming to make quantum science and technology pervasive in society. This includes initiatives in secondary and higher education, public engagement, and the development of a skilled workforce to support the growing quantum industry.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Pumice
body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation co-funds the project, the goal of which it is to develop educational content and examples of AI’s use in various subjects and activities in primary and secondary schools, with a focus on practical demonstrations of AI’s usefulness in teaching subject content, e.g. Slovenian language, history, chemistry, biology, art.

As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more common in daily life, there is growing need for students—not just in technical fields—to understand how AI works and how it affects the world around them. Many students encounter AI only through media or social platforms, with limited opportunities to explore its educational value. To change this, the Slovenian Ministry of Digital Transformation is co-funding a project aimed at introducing AI into primary and secondary school classrooms—not as a separate subject, but as a tool to enhance learning in a wide range of subjects.
The main goal of the project is to create educational content and practical examples that show how AI can be used in the teaching of existing subjects. This includes disciplines such as Slovenian language, history, chemistry, biology, and art. Instead of treating AI as something only for computer science classes, the project focuses on how it can support learning across the curriculum. For example, AI tools might be used to help students explore historical data, analyse language patterns, or generate visual representations in art lessons. This approach helps students see AI as a useful and relevant part of their education, not just a complex or distant technology.
The project is being carried out in partnership with educators, content developers, and experts in both AI and pedagogy. These teams are working together to design and test new teaching materials that use AI in ways that are meaningful, age-appropriate, and aligned with national learning goals. Special emphasis is placed on practical demonstrations, making sure teachers and students can directly see how AI adds value to their lessons. The Ministry provides financial support and strategic guidance, helping to ensure that the content developed is both high quality and suitable for broader adoption.
In the future, the results of this project may lead to a wider rollout of AI-integrated teaching practices across Slovenian schools. If successful, the content and methods developed could be included in national guidelines, teacher training programmes, or even embedded in digital learning platforms. By starting with small-scale, subject-based integration, Slovenia is taking a measured and inclusive approach to preparing young learners for an AI-influenced world—where understanding and applying these technologies will be increasingly important across all areas of life and work.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
org: Agency for the development of the Electronic Government and Society Information and Technology (AGESIC)  and Unit for Access to Public Information (UAIP)
title: Public Sector Artificial Intelligence Observatory
document_name: Observatorio de Inteligencia Artificial en Estado
body:
The Public Sector AI Observatory promotes the ethical and safe use of AI in Uruguay's government. It provides information on AI projects, shares clear guidelines for public institutions, and creates spaces for collaboration across sectors. The Observatory also monitors progress on national AI and data strategies to ensure responsible development.

The creation of the Artificial Intelligence Observatory was established in Commitment 1.6 of the Fifth National Action Plan for Open Government 2021-2024, undertaken by Agesic and the Unit for Access to Public Information (UAIP).The Observatory is focused on:Promoting and encouraging the ethical, responsible, safe, and reliable use of AI technology.Strengthening the AI ecosystem in Uruguay.Promoting access to information about AI applications in the State.The Observatory was created by integrating contributions from various actors in the public sector, private sector, academia, and civil society, who participated in specific exchange workshops for its design and in dialogue tables as part of the process of reviewing the Artificial Intelligence Strategy and developing the National Data Strategy. The first survey of AI application in the State was conducted from December 2023 to May 2024 through a questionnaire sent to the directors and general managers of organizations, as well as to IT and e-government sector leaders in various branches of the Central Administration, Decentralized Services, Autonomous Entities, and Departmental Governments. It was also sent to some non-state public entities, such as the National Agency for Research and Innovation (ANII) and Ceibal, as well as the Judicial Power and Legislative Power.The survey form consists of 3 sections:Section 1: Introduction, explaining the purpose of the survey and some considerations for reporting initiatives, as well as examples of what is considered AI applications for the purposes of the survey. It specifically asked for cases or initiatives that have identified the problem to be solved and are included in the strategic plan of the responding organization.Section 2: Identification of the organization.Section 3: Identification of the system or initiative to report, including: description, technical development data, information about the team working or who worked on the initiative, decision-making data, and the main challenges encountered.Additionally, a questionnaire was included for cases where the organization does not have AI applications, to identify potential areas or applications of interest that could be developed.This survey was the initial step for the first version of the Observatory, which will be updated periodically with new reported cases.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Project on Spanish Language and AI
document_name: Lengua Española e Inteligencia Artificial
body:
The Spanish Language and AI (LEIA) project is an initiative promoted by the Royal Spanish Academy (RAE) and the Association of Spanish Language Academies (ASALE) that has had the initial support of Telefnica.

Protected by the authority granted by the speakers themselves during its 300 years of history, the RAE, in collaboration with ASALE, leads the project and coordinates the work with the other members. It also manages language issues and contributes its resources.The initiative has the following objectives:To ensure that correct Spanish is taught to machines.To work on the development of tools and applications that help humans acquire a good use of Spanish.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Center for the Development of Digital Competencies
title: Programme for the development of digital competencies
document_name: Program rozwoju kompetencji cyfrowych
body:
This horizontal multi-stakeholder programme, coordinated by the Center for the Development of Digital Competencies (Centrum Rozwoju Kompetencji Cyfrowych - CRKC), situated in the office of the Minister of Informatisation, aims to significantly increase the digital competencies of Poland’s population, both with regard to the general population, ICT specialists and particularly women.

The implementation of activities is taken place under the following five priorities: i) Development of digital education; ii) Providing everyone with opportunities to develop digital competencies; iii) Supporting digital competence of employees in various sectors; iv) Development of advanced digital competencies; v) Strengthening the management of digital competence development.
While this programme is not AI-specific, a specific component on AI is the “Activity to prepare teachers to develop students' skills in artificial intelligence in the educational process and to expand young people's skills in artificial intelligence” (2023-2025), led by the Ministry of Education.

org: Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry
title: Programme for Modern Enterprises
document_name: Modern vállalkozások programmeja
body:
Implemented by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, this programme assists SMEs in their digital transformation by providing resources and guidance on digital tools and technologies, including AI. It offers personalised IT audits, access to accredited IT suppliers, information on funding opportunities, thematic events, and a digital knowledge repository.

The “Vállalkozz Digitálisan!” programme, run by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MKIK), supports SMEs in adopting digital technologies as part of their transformation journey. It provides tailored services such as personalised IT audits, recommendations, and connections to accredited IT suppliers.
The initiative also gives businesses access to a digital knowledge repository, organizes thematic events and training, and shares information on available funding opportunities. By combining practical guidance with direct support, it helps SMEs integrate tools including AI into their operations more effectively.

title: ProChile - AI and Digital Services Export Promotion Line
body: ProChile has established export promotion lines for knowledge‑based services, explicitly including AI, data analytics, and advanced software. Services include international fairs, buyer missions, and export matchmaking tailored to digital and AI firms.

document_name: Privacy Enhancing Technologies Sandbox

The PET Sandbox provides opportunities for companies to work with trusted PET digital solution providers to develop use cases and pilot PETs, to facilitate experimentation with PETs.

The initiative has the following objectives:Matchmake use case owners to a panel of PET digital solution providers.Provide grant support to user companies to scope and implement pilot projects.Provide regulatory support to ensure that PETs are deployed in a compliant manner.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Ministry of Digital Government and Gender Equality
title: Plan for new technology and automation of the public sector
body:
Plan for new technology and automation of the public sector. The joint public digitalisation strategy 2022-2025 contains an initiative to use new technologies such as AI to free up labour for other tasks in the public sector. New technological solutions, such as automation, AI, and robotics, are increasingly being implemented in the public sector. The state, municipalities, and regions have therefore agreed to launch a 10-year plan for new technology and automation of the public sector.

The initiative aims to help address the expected labor shortage, particularly in areas related to citizen-centric welfare.
A sandbox for testing of AI solutions has been established (see also previous section) that is open to public and private organisations.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Pilot projects to enhance energy efficiency and the enhancement of the use of renewables in the economy
document_name: Pilotni projekti za izboljšanje energetske učinkovitosti in povečanje uporabe obnovljivih virov v gospodarstvu
body:
Slovenia has launched pilot projects to improve energy efficiency and increase the use of renewable energy in the economy. These projects use advanced digital technologies, including AI, to make business processes more sustainable. Key initiatives include a peer-to-peer renewables marketplace, emissions monitoring, and digital solutions for circular construction.

As part of its strategic plan for energy efficiency and renewable energy, Slovenia introduced three pilot projects in 2022 that integrate AI and advanced digital technologies to promote environmentally friendly and sustainable development. The initiatives are designed to test innovative approaches and demonstrate their potential for wider adoption.
Key measures include:
Peer-to-peer marketplace for renewables: enabling businesses and individuals to trade renewable energy efficientlyRMV (Recording, Measurement, and Verification of Emissions): improving the Emissions Trading System (ETS) through more accurate monitoringDigital solution for BIM (Building Information Modelling) - circular construction: supporting sustainable construction practices and resource efficiencyA green corporate e-identity tool was also proposed as a web service on the Energy Agency’s website, allowing companies to track and showcase their sustainability efforts digitally.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: SPIRIT Slovenia – Public Agency for Entrepreneurship, Internationalisation, Foreign Investments and Technology
title: Pilot demonstration projects
document_name: Javni razpis za sofinanciranje pilotno-demonstracijskih projektov na področju krožnega gospodarstva v skladu z NEPN
body:
Slovenia funded 21 consortia to run pilot projects supporting the circular economy as part of its National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN). These projects aim to test and demonstrate innovative solutions that reduce environmental impact and improve resource efficiency. Three of the projects apply artificial intelligence to advance sustainability goals.

The pilot demonstration projects were launched to help Slovenia meet the environmental targets of the National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN). By supporting circular economy initiatives, the programme promotes innovation that reduces waste, optimises resource use, and fosters sustainable growth.
Out of the 21 projects funded, three specifically focus on applying artificial intelligence. These AI-driven projects are used to optimise processes, enhance monitoring and data analysis, and enable smarter decision-making in resource management. This reflects Slovenia’s broader strategy to integrate digital and green technologies for climate action.
The projects are implemented by consortia bringing together companies, research institutions, and public bodies. By working in partnership, these actors ensure that solutions are both technologically advanced and practically applicable.
Looking ahead, these pilots are expected to provide scalable models that can be replicated across industries and regions, strengthening Slovenia’s contribution to the EU’s climate and sustainability targets while also enhancing its national innovation ecosystem.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Panhellenic Educational Robotics Competition
document_name: Πανελλήνιος Διαγωνισμός Εκπαιδευτικής Ρομποτικής
body:
The National Competition on Educational Robotics introduces robotics and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) into the official school system. It helps students develop 21st-century skills and promotes STEM as a core teaching methodology in compulsory education.

The National Competition on Educational Robotics is designed to integrate educational robotics and the broader STEM approach into mainstream education. It serves as a platform where students, teachers, and schools can explore hands-on learning, creativity, and problem-solving through robotics projects.
The competition’s objectives include:
Introducing robotics into classrooms as part of the official curriculumPromoting STEM as a teaching methodology for compulsory educationDefining clear ways for students to acquire 21st-century skills, such as critical thinking, collaboration, and digital literacyThrough national-level contests and activities, students gain practical experience in building and programming robots while learning scientific principles. Teachers receive guidance on how to integrate STEM concepts into their lessons, creating a pipeline of future innovators and technology-savvy professionals.
Looking ahead, the competition aims to expand participation across regions, strengthen partnerships with schools, and further embed STEM-based learning in the education system to enhance the country’s innovation capacity.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Presidency of the Government of Spain
title: PERTE Chip Semiconductor Ecosystem
document_name: Proyecto Estratégico de Microelectrónica y Semiconductores
body:
PERTE Chip aims to strengthen the design and production capabilities of the microelectronics and semiconductor industry in Spain and promote national and EU strategic autonomy in this sector, in line with the EU Chip Law. Its 4 strategic axes cover the entire value chain of the industry in different phases: conception, design, production of chips and manufacturing ICT electronic products, so that it acts as a generator of demand for the microchips produced and boosts the semiconductor ecosystem.

The following actions will be carried out:
- Strengthening scientific capacity. 
- Strengthen R&D&I on cutting-edge microprocessors and alternative architectures and integrated photonics, developing quantum chips and launching a line of financing to strengthen the Important European Project of Common Interest (IPCEI) on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies. 
- Design strategy. 
- Enhance Spanish capacity in microprocessor design through the creation of fabless companies for the design of cutting-edge microprocessors and alternative architectures; test pilot lines; semiconductor training network. 
- Construction of manufacturing plants. 
- To equip the national semiconductor production capacity for the manufacture of cutting-edge technology (below 5 nm) and mid-range (over 5 nm). 
- Boosting the ICT manufacturing industry. It includes actions such as the creation of a capital fund focused on chips to finance startups, scaleups and innovative SMEs in the national semiconductor sector, with an initial public allocation of 200 million euros. It is also aimed at strengthening the internal production of electronic product manufacturing – which uses microchips as an input – so that it acts as a driver for the semiconductor industry and absorbs part of its production.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Order no. 234/2022 regarding professional training and development programs for civil servants
document_name: ORDIN nr. 234/2022 pentru stabilirea domeniilor prioritare de formare și perfecționare profesională și a tematicii specifice programelor de formare și perfecționare profesională a funcționarilor publici
body:
The purpose of this initiative is to train civil servants in ICT and emerging technologies, including AI, as foreseen in the Order of the National Agency of Public Officers no. 234/2022.

Romania has introduced a training programme for civil servants under Order no. 234/2022, issued by the National Agency of Public Officers. The goal is to update staff skills in ICT and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to meet the growing digital demands of public administration.
The Order sets out priority areas (including digital literacy, cybersecurity, data management, and AI awareness) that ministries and agencies must include in their annual training plans. Courses are delivered through the National Institute of Administration and accredited providers, ranging from introductory modules to more advanced training.

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
org: Latvian Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development (VARAM); State Chancellery Riga 2024
title: Open Data Action Plan
body:
Building on the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021–2027, this initiative is aimed at updating Latvia’s approach to open data management in order to enhance data access and usage for societal and economic benefits.

Based on the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021–2027, Latvia has set out measures to update its approach to open data management. The initiative is framed around improving access to and use of public data with the intention of generating broader societal and economic value.
Planned activities include adjustments to standards for formats, metadata, and interoperability, alongside efforts to encourage reuse of datasets by different stakeholders. These steps are expected to support the gradual development of a more coordinated national data ecosystem.

The Province of Ontario passed an act that requires employers to notify employees of electronic employee monitoring policies.

category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
title: OECD Framework or the Classification of AI Systems
document_name: OECD Framework or the Classification of AI Systems
body:
The framework helps policy-makers, regulators, legislators and others to assess the opportunities and risks that different types of AI systems present.

AI is changing how we learn, work, play, interact and live. Policy makers and others need smart tools to differentiate between the types of AI systems and the impact that they can have on people's lives, whether good or bad. This covers what AI systems can do but also where and how they do it. For example, facial recognition can be very effective for smartphone security but used in other contexts it can infringe upon human rights.The OECD.AI Network of Experts developed the OECD Framework for Classifying AI Systems as a tool for policy-makers, regulators, legislators and others so that they can assess the opportunities and risks that different types of AI systems present and to inform their national AI strategies.The Framework links the technical characteristics of AI with the policy implications set out in the OECD AI Principles.

category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
title: OECD Catalogue of Tools and Metrics
document_name: OECD Catalogue of Tools and Metrics
body:
This catalogue makes it easier to find tools and metrics by providing a one-stop-shop for helpful approaches, mechanisms and practices for trustworthy AI.

There are tools and metrics out there that help AI actors to build and deploy AI systems that are trustworthy. However, these tools and metrics are often hard to find and absent from the ongoing AI policy discussions. This catalogue makes it easier to find tools and metrics by providing a one-stop-shop for helpful approaches, mechanisms and practices for trustworthy AI.

body:
OBIA serves as a public, open-access repository designed to compile and provide information on AI developments in Brazil and to connect with other international observatories.

Its main goal is to track AI development, impact, and adoption in Brazil, both quantitatively and qualitatively.

title: NpUI Government working group
document_name: Delovna skupina vlade za izvajanje Nacionalnega programa spodbujanja razvoja in uporabe umetne inteligence v Republiki Sloveniji do leta 2025
body:
Working group is the decision making group for implementation of National AI programme - NpUI.

Slovenia adopted National AI plan (NpUI) in May 2021, which envisaged proper governance structure for effective implementation. The implementation is led by inter-ministerial gropup at the level of state secretaries that enables efficient monitoring, decision making and refining implementation of the NpUI measures.The initiative has the following objectives:- Guides and monitors the implementation of actions to achieve the strategic objectives of the NpUI;implementation of the NpUI (e.g. at the level of strategic objectives or actions);- provide suggestions and guidance to improve stakeholders' involvement in the implemenation of artificial intelligence in the Republic of Slovenia;- approve the establishment of sectoral working groups appointed by the Ministries for implementation specific actions, addressing specific horizontal problem areas or areas of- monitor the work of the sectoral working groups and guide their work through preparing opinions and proposals;- ensure coordinated and continuous inter-ministerial cooperation in planning and the implementation of the actions.- assess the progress of the implementation of the actions led and implemented by the ministries and propose changes to the measures, their implementation or the implementing instruments for the implementation:- proposing financial resources for the implementation of the individual actions of the NpUI;

category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
title: Next Generation Energy Systems (NexSys)
body:
The Next Generation Energy Systems (NexSys) project develops pathways toward a net-zero energy system in Ireland. It uses AI in the Cities & Communities hub to analyse geospatial and sensor data for smarter energy use. The project combines big data analysis and citizen science to improve energy efficiency at neighbourhood and city levels.

The NexSys collaborative project aims to accelerate Ireland’s transition to a net-zero energy system by integrating research across five key areas:
Energy SystemsWaterTransportCities & Communities (CC)Offshore WindWithin the Cities & Communities hub, AI is applied to the Earth Observation Big Data work package to:
Mine geospatial data, including satellite imageryLeverage data from in-situ sensors to identify clusters of energy consumersEnable energy sharing, where the waste energy of one user can be repurposed as a resource for another, improving neighbourhood efficiencyThe initiative combines top-down big data mining with bottom-up citizen science activities, feeding into AI-augmented monitoring and decision-support tools. This approach helps communities optimise energy use, reduce waste, and support informed decision-making at both local and regional levels.
