title: Human-Centered National Guidelines for AI Ethics
document_name: 사람이 중심이 되는 인공지능 윤리기준
body:
The Human-Centered National Guidelines for AI Ethics set government standards to ensure AI technology is used responsibly and fairly. It aims to protect people from risks like bias, discrimination, and privacy violations while supporting AI innovation. This initiative benefits society by promoting trustworthy AI that improves quality of life and industry productivity.

The Human-Centered National Guidelines for AI Ethics initiative addresses the urgent need to establish ethical standards in the rapidly growing field of artificial intelligence. As AI technologies become increasingly integrated into everyday life and industry, concerns about data bias, algorithmic discrimination, and privacy violations have emerged. These challenges risk undermining public trust in AI, which is crucial for its sustainable development and adoption. The initiative aims to create a clear and comprehensive ethical framework that guides the responsible development, deployment, and use of AI technologies across various sectors in South Korea.The main objectives of this initiative are to promote fairness, transparency, accountability, and respect for human rights within AI systems. By setting government-backed ethical standards, the guidelines seek to mitigate risks associated with AI, such as unfair treatment based on biased data or privacy breaches, while encouraging innovation and industrial growth. This approach balances the need for technological advancement with social responsibility, ensuring that AI benefits society as a whole without compromising ethical values.Looking ahead, the initiative is designed to be implemented through collaboration between government agencies, industry stakeholders, researchers, and civil society. It will be institutionalized as part of national AI policy, with ongoing updates to adapt to emerging technologies and societal needs. The initiative also includes efforts to develop and disseminate ethics education curricula to train AI professionals and raise awareness among the public. As trust in AI strengthens, these guidelines are expected to support wider adoption and integration of AI technologies in diverse fields such as healthcare, finance, education, and public services.Since its establishment as part of the broader National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in 2019, the initiative has evolved to incorporate feedback from multiple stakeholders and align with international ethical AI frameworks. It continues to expand its scope and influence by addressing new ethical challenges posed by advancements in AI capabilities. This dynamic evolution ensures that South Korea remains at the forefront of responsible AI development, positioning the country as a leader in creating human-centered AI ecosystems that prioritize social good alongside innovation.

body:
The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) has launched a call for tender for the procurement of a petascale supercomputer capable of executing more than 4 Petaflops, 4 million billion calculations per second and located in Sofia, Bulgaria.

The procurement includes the acquisition, delivery, installation and maintenance of a new petascale supercomputer co-owned by the EuroHPC JU and located in Sofia Tech Park, in Bulgaria.
Objectives:
To foster better science and enhance innovation in Europe by providing access to leading edge HPC infrastructures and services to a wide range of users from the research and scientific community as well as the industry and the public sector.
To develop top-of-the-range exascale supercomputers for processing big data, based on European technology.
Bulgaria currently has three HPC Supercomputer initiatives:
1) HEMUS Supercomputer 2023: An advanced computing facility integrated within Institute of Information and Communication Technologies’s infrastructure complex that delivers over 3 petaFLOPS of computing performance and provides 6.72 petabytes of data storage capacity. HEMUS is notable for its implementation of standardised data management practices that ensure research data is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable. The system was developed with support from the "Science and Education for Smart Growth" Operational programme.
2) Avitohol Supercomputer (in development): a specialised supercomputer operated by the National Center for High Performance and Distributed Calculations. The system's architecture is optimised for HPC applications. With 96 terabytes of storage capacity, Avitohol is expected to enhance Bulgaria's computational research infrastructure by providing essential resources for data-intensive scientific applications (National Centre for High Performance and Distributed Computing, n.d.[7]).
3) Discoverer Supercomputer (2021): a petascale supercomputer located in Sofia Tech Park that represents Bulgaria's first major investment in high-performance computing infrastructure. With performance exceeding 4.5 petaFLOPS, the system is specifically designed to support big data processing and AI applications (Discoverer) . Funding shared between EuroHPC (35%) and the Bulgarian government (65%)

body:
The guiding framework consists of the following seven guidelines:- Putting people at the heart of the matter- Conditions conducive to the development and use of AI- Transparency, traceability, and explainability- Liability- Security- Involvement of all relevant actors at national and international level

The Federal Council adopted the Guidelines for AI on 25 November 2020. Developed by the interdepartmental Artificial Intelligence working group under the leadership of the Federal Department of Economics, Education and Research (DEFR), these guidelines provide a guiding framework for the federal administration.The initiative has the following objectives:These Guidelines provide a guiding framework for the federal administration.The guiding framework consists of the following seven guidelines (briefly presented here): - Putting people at the heart of the matter: the dignity and well-being of each individual, as well as the public interest, must be at the forefront when developing and using AI systems. Special attention is paid to the protection of fundamental rights in the use of AI. - Conditions conducive to the development and use of AI: The Confederation continues to ensure the existence of conditions conducive to exploiting the opportunities offered by AI in order to strengthen value creation and sustainable development. Switzerland must continue to position itself as one of the main sites for the research, application and commercial exploitation of AI. - Transparency, traceability, and explainability: AI-based decision-making processes must be designed in such a way that they are identifiable and verifiable. - Liability: In order to determine liability in the event of damage, accident or violation of law, it is necessary to clearly establish liability when using AI. Responsibility should not be delegated to machines. - Security: By design, AI systems must be secure, robust and resilient in such a way that they produce positive effects and cannot be abused or misused.Active participation in AI governance: for Switzerland, it is essential to actively participate in global governance in the field of AI and to get involved in the development of international norms and standards in the field of AI. IA, while defending its own interests and values. - Involvement of all relevant actors at national and international level: Switzerland must make a commitment to ensure that decision-making processes on governance in the field of AI include all stakeholders.

body:
The Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) commissioned this report, which includes: a rigorous canvass of AI use at the 142 most significant Federal departments, agencies, and sub-agencies; a series of in-depth but accessible case studies of specific AI applications at seven leading agencies covering a range of governance tasks; and a set of cross-cutting analyses of the institutional, legal, and policy challenges raised by agency use of AI.

This report offers three cuts at Federal agency use of AI: a rigorous canvass of AI use at the 142 most significant Federal departments, agencies, and sub-agencies (Part I); a series of in-depth but accessible case studies of specific AI applications at seven leading agencies covering a range of governance tasks (Part II); and a set of cross-cutting analyses of the institutional, legal, and policy challenges raised by agency use of AI (Part III). Taken together, these analyses yield five main findings.First, the government's AI toolkit is diverse and spans the Federal administrative state.Second, and despite wide agency embrace of AI, the government still has a long way to go.Third, AI poses deep accountability challenges.Fourth, if people expect agencies to make responsible and smart use of AI, technical capacity must come from within.Fifth, AI has the potential to raise distributive concerns andfuel political anxieties.The initiative has the following objective(s):To map how Federal agencies are currently using AI to make and support decisions.To address how AI implicates core regulations and laws.To highlight potential uses of AI in Federal agencies.

body:
Cloud service for governmental bodies hosted by the Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (SIT) on the platform https://www.dmi.dk/frie-data, which is delivered as community cloud for SIT customers and offers data hosting on Danish territory. Used for distributing open meteorological data and for the National Data Portal among others.

The Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (SIT) runs a cloud service specifically for government bodies. This service provides a secure, nationally hosted platform that meets the needs of public institutions requiring reliable access to data while ensuring it stays within Danish borders for legal and privacy reasons. It helps agencies share and manage data efficiently and safely.
The service’s main goal is to offer a shared digital platform where government agencies can host and distribute data. It is used for important functions such as distributing open meteorological data and supporting the National Data Portal, a central hub for government data. By centralizing these services, the cloud reduces costs, improves collaboration, and enhances data availability for public use.
Hosted entirely in Denmark, the cloud operates as a community resource shared among various government users but with strong security and control measures. The platform is provided by the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) at https://www.dmi.dk/frie-data, while SIT oversees the infrastructure and customer support.

body:

The German Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) is funding the Mobility Data Space (MDS), a platform designed to facilitate the legally secure exchange of sensitive data. Within this space, private sector data can be voluntarily shared and traded while ensuring full respect for data sovereignty. The MDS operates as a non-profit joint venture and is managed by Datenraum Mobilität GmbH, established in May 2021.

The Mobility Data Space is a virtual marketplace for the exchange of mobility data (B2B and B2G).For this purpose, the MDS provides a data catalogue for searching data offers and an infrastructure for decentralised data exchange. document_name: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais
body:
The Brazilian data protection law includes information on the protection of personal data as well as a section on database ownership and database rights.

The General Law on Protection of Personal Data (Law n. 13,709, of August 14, 2018) regulates the treatment of personal data by natural person or corporation, both public and private, including but not restricted to digital data. Its objective is to protect the fundamental rights of freedom and privacy and the unbound development of the natural person's own personality. In order to apply the law and protect fundamental rights related to personal data, LGPD creates the National Data Protection Authority (Autoridade Nacional de Prote£o de Dados - ANDP), as established by the Decree n. 10,474 of August 26, 2020. Originally, LGDP would come into force on February 2020. However, under provision by the Provisional Measure 869 (Medida Provisrira 869 - a presidencial bylaw effective immediately and then subject to Congressional scrutiny), on December 27, 2018, LGPD would come into effect in August 2020. On April 3, 2020, the Senate approved a bill with several measures relative to the COVID-19 pandemic, including a specific ruling for the LGPD coming into force in January 2021.The initiative aims to unify the over 40 different statutes that currently govern personal data, both online and offline, by replacing certain regulations and supplementing others.

org: Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)|The White House
title: Executive Order on Promoting the Use of Trustworthy AI in Federal Government
document_name: Executive Order on Promoting the Use of Trustworthy AI in Federal Government
body:
On 3 December 2020, President Donald J. Trump signed the Executive Order on Promoting the Use of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in the Federal government, which establishes guidance for Federal agency adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI).

The Executive Order (EO) includes the following four actions: Principles for the Use of AI in Government: The EO directs Federal agencies to be guided by nine common principles for the design, development, acquisition, and use of AI. These principles emphasize that AI use by Federal agencies must be lawful; purposeful and performance-driven; accurate, reliable, and effective; safe, secure, and resilient; understandable; responsible and traceable; regularly monitored; transparent; and accountable. These principles build upon related principles already established by the defense and intelligence communities, and are designed to cover Federal applications beyond defense and national security. Common Policy for Implementing Principles: The EO establishes a process for implementing these principles through common policy guidance across agencies. The order directs OMB to develop and post a roadmap for policy guidance to better support the use of AI by agencies, consistent with this order. The order further calls on agencies to continue to use voluntary consensus standards developed with industry participation, as appropriate. Catalogue of Agency Use Cases of AI: The EO directs each agency to prepare an inventory of use cases of AI by the agency, and review and assess these use cases for consistency with this order. These inventories will be shared with other agencies, as appropriate, to improve interagency coordination for advancing the implementation of the principles in the design, development, acquisition, and use of AI. Enhanced AI Implementation Expertise: The EO directs the General Services Administration to establish an AI track within the Presidential Innovation Fellows program to attract experts from industry and academia to work within agencies to further the design, development, acquisition, and use of AI in government. The order further directs the Office of Personnel Management to determine how rotational programs can be best used to expand the number of employees with AI expertise at the agencies.The initiative has the following objective(s):To more effectively deliver services to the American people and foster public trust in artificial intelligence.

body:
Four European Digital Innovation Hubs operate in Bulgaria under the Digital Europe Programme, providing AI implementation support and technical expertise to SMEs and public organisations. The initiative is expanding with eight additional hubs. The four existing hubs include InnovationAmp, the European Digital Innovation Hub in the Construction Sector (EDIHCS); EDIH Thrace, and AgroHub.BG.

Bulgaria hosts a network of European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) under the Digital Europe Programme, designed to support the adoption and implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) and other advanced digital technologies. These hubs address a key challenge for Bulgarian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public organisations: accessing the expertise, infrastructure, and technical guidance required to deploy AI effectively and responsibly.
The current network comprises four operational hubs: InnovationAmp, the European Digital Innovation Hub in the Construction Sector (EDIHCS), EDIH Thrace, and AgroHub.BG. Each hub offers specialised services tailored to its sector or region, including support for AI integration, digital transformation strategies, and access to testing and experimentation environments. By providing hands-on guidance and resources, the hubs enable organisations to explore innovative solutions, improve operational efficiency, and accelerate the development of AI-driven products and services.
The initiative is expanding with eight additional hubs, aiming to broaden regional coverage and increase the accessibility of AI and digital innovation services throughout Bulgaria. This expansion will further strengthen the country’s innovation ecosystem, promote cross-sector collaboration, and enhance the competitiveness of Bulgarian enterprises in European and global markets.

body:
The Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles provides guidance on the ethical aspects of researching, testing, and deploying automated mobility, including AI-related systems. Established in 2020, it issues guidelines to ensure autonomous vehicle development follows ethical standards.

The Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles was created in 2020 to address the ethical implications of introducing automated and autonomous mobility solutions. Its work covers the full spectrum of AI-related aspects in this field — from research and testing to deployment in real-world contexts.
The commission’s objectives include:
Ensuring that ethical considerations are integrated into the design, testing, and use of automated and autonomous vehiclesProviding guidelines and recommendations for policymakers, researchers, and companies developing or deploying such systemsPromoting public trust and safety by aligning autonomous mobility with ethical and societal valuesBy issuing guidelines, the commission supports the responsible development and roll-out of automated mobility. It helps governments, industry, and researchers understand the ethical boundaries and societal expectations associated with AI-driven vehicles.
Looking ahead, the commission is expected to update and expand its guidelines as technology and societal expectations evolve. This ongoing work helps ensure that autonomous vehicle deployment remains safe, transparent, and ethically sound.

category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
org: National Advisor for Digital Transformation and Economic Affairs | Ministry of Information Technology and Communications (MinTIC)
title: Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Colombia
document_name: Marco Ético para la Inteligencia Artificial en Colombia
body:
The Ethical Framework for AI provides a set of ethical principles that should be considered in the design, development and implementation of AI systems. The document describes a methodology for determining how these principles should be considered and implemented in countries such as Colombia. Additionally, it includes a toolbox that describes a series of strategies that can be implemented to develop these principles in public entities.

This framework was conceived and described in the Colombian AI Strategy (Conpes 3975, 2019). The Strategy highlighted the importance of developing a series or principles that shoud guide the design, implementation and development of AI in Colombia. Additionally, the ethical framework answers to a new direction in the regulatory process, especially in the regulation of emerging technologies. This strategy has been designed by the National Advisor for Digital Transformation, Victor Munoz. The purpose of the Colombian government is to develop a regulation that is evidence-based. The ethical framework allows the country to address ethical challenges while collecting evidence that allows Colombian authorities to consider a regulatory framework in the future and only in those specific cases in which the regulation seems to be required. To promote the discussion on the ethics of artificial intelligence and its implementation in Colombia, the Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Colombia was launched for discussion. There have been 6 discussion tables on the latter led by the Berkman Klein Center from Harvard University, the Development Bank of Latin America (CAF) and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). A total of more than 50 national and international contributors participated in these roundtables. Participants included Unicef, the World Economic Forum, Oxford University, the Council of Europe, the OECD and members of the European Parliament.https://inteligenciaartificial.gov.co/en/roundtables/The final document was launched on October 12, 2021.The initiative has the following objectives:To address ethical challenges posed by the design, implementation and deployment of AI systems.To provide principles that must guide the ethical use of data in the public sector.To create a culture of digital transformation in Colombia that values ethical principles and social good.To increase knowledge about this technology its benefits and risks among public servants.To motivate the private sector to increase its efforts in developing ethical codes of conduct and other strategies to reduce ethical risks in the design and implementation of this technology in Colombia.To implement the recommendations of the OECD on this subject.

document_name: Eği̇ti̇m Bi̇lgi̇ aği
body:
EBA is a distance education platform prepared by the Ministry of National Education within the scope of the F.A.T.I.H. Project, which has been recently renewed and adapted to distance education during COVID-19.

Through EBA, teachers and students can interact with each other, teachers can send study materials to their students, and they can monitor their students' performances on study materials and general EBA usage. Students can track their progress via reports and portfolios. Parents can also track their children's progress via reports and portfolios.In addition to providing a customized interface and content for each student with personalization, the system recommends content according to the performance of the students - thanks to the smart suggestion system. In EBA, the contents are matched with the relevant curriculum objectives. Other contents that are not matched with the objectives are included in the Library area for free use and supportive course content. When teachers send study material to their students via EBA, the students' work is analyzed in detail by the system and the deficiencies of each student are determined separately based on objectives. Taking this analysis into account, the system determines the content that can help each student to remedy his/her deficiencies and recommends them to the student if the teacher approves. In addition, without teacher intervention, there is also a special content recommendation system that recommends additional content based on questions a student solves while using EBA and the answers he/she provides in the exams.The initiative has the following objectives:- To provide customized interface and content for each student with personalisation.- To recommend content according to the performance of the students through analysing work of each student with AI.

body:
The AI-Enabled Cameras for Vehicular Flows project uses video streams processed by AI to monitor traffic automatically. It identifies and reports traffic patterns, reducing the need for manual monitoring or storing large volumes of footage. The initiative improves traffic management efficiency.

The Proof of Concept project: Using AI-Enabled Cameras to Understand Vehicular Flows aims to enhance traffic monitoring and management through AI technology. By processing video streams automatically, the system can identify vehicles, track traffic flow, and generate reports without human intervention or large storage requirements.
Key objectives include:

body:
Recognizing the efforts of the continent's leadership to prioritize and accelerate digital transformation, and building on the vision of many African leaders, African countries are ready for a comprehensive digital transformation strategy to guide a common, coordinated response to reap the benefits of the fourth industrial revolution

title: Digital Research Centre Denmark (DIREC)
body:
DIREC’s research spans ten areas in advanced digital technology. It aims to develop and support research in AI, big data, IoT, and IT Security.

Digital Research Centre Denmark (DIREC) was created to strengthen Denmark’s position in digital technologies such as AI, big data, IoT, and cybersecurity. Many advanced digital tools are still developed abroad, and Denmark risks falling behind if it does not invest in its own research capacity. DIREC addresses this by uniting universities, companies, and public institutions to develop new knowledge and practical solutions, while also ensuring that digital innovation reflects Danish values and priorities.
The centre is a non-profit partnership of eight Danish universities and the Alexandra Institute. It funds and coordinates projects where researchers and industry work together on concrete challenges, from safer digital infrastructures to smarter health technologies. Since 2020, DIREC has expanded to dozens of projects and more than fifty partners.

title: Digital Pact for Schools
document_name: DigitalPakt Schule
body:
The Digital Pact for Schools supports Germany’s federal states in integrating AI technologies into education. It funds digital learning materials, adaptive learning systems, and student support to strengthen digital and AI-related skills. The initiative invests EUR 92 million in AI-related educational media infrastructure across nine cross-state projects.

The Digital Pact for Schools is a nationwide initiative in Germany designed to help federal states integrate AI technologies and digital tools into their education systems. It establishes the technical foundations needed for both teachers and students to acquire digital and AI-related competences.
Its key objectives include:
Funding and support for AI-based digital learning materials and adaptive learning systemsProviding targeted student support through technology-enabled approachesEnhancing educational media infrastructure across multiple federal statesThe initiative allocates EUR 92 million to nine cross-state projects, strengthening the infrastructure required for AI-related educational media. This funding ensures that schools have access to modern tools, platforms, and content that support innovative teaching and personalised learning.
Looking ahead, the Digital Pact for Schools is expected to expand its scope as AI and digital technologies continue to evolve. By embedding these tools into classrooms and teacher training, the programme builds long-term capacity for Germany’s education system to remain competitive and future-ready.

title: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (New Zealand, Singapore, Chile, and South Korea)
document_name: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (New Zealand, Singapore, Chile, and South Korea)
body:
The Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) between New Zealand, Singapore, Chile and South Korea will help establish new rules and practices for digital trade, and promote ongoing discussion on issues like digital inclusion, inclusive trade and support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the digital economy.

The Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) between New Zealand, Singapore and Chile is an agreement that establishes new approaches and collaborations in digital trade issues, promotes interoperability between different regimes and addresses the new issues brought about by digitalisation. The Republic of Korea joined the DEPA on 3 May 2024. The agreement covers broad areas, from e-invoicing to artificial intelligence, and will continue to evolve as new digital opportunities and issues emerge.The initiative has the following objectives:DEPAs commitments include: Cooperation - Implement the agreement and explore how to further enhance our digital economy partnership. Trade facilitation - Facilitate paperless trading, e-invoicing, e-payments and streamlined customs procedures for parcels. SMEs and the digital economy - Share information that SMEs need to operate in the digital economy and develop a Digital SME Dialogue. Consumer trust - Promote online consumer protection to ensure consumers have the information to trade with confidence and access to appropriate redress if things go wrong. Digital products “ Promote a level playing field for digital products through provisions regarding the non-discrimination of digital products and ICT products that use cryptography. Data issues - Protect personal information and ensure generally free cross-border data flows and freedom regarding the location of computer facilities. Innovation - Enhance and encourage innovation in the digital economy, such as through open government data.Digital identities - Start discussing digital identities, and share best practice on digital identity policies and regulations. Emerging technologies - Explore new issues, including competition in the digital economy. Promote financial technology and develop frameworks to support the safe and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. Digital inclusion - Establish a framework for future cooperation between partners on matters of digital inclusion and inclusive trade, including new people-to-people connections among Indigenous Peoples.

body:
The Data Sandbox platform is a collaborative space for Colombian public entities, which enables to carry out different pilot projects in Analytics and Big Data. The previous allows public entities to use the latest technologies in data science to test, experiment, assess and determine applicable solutions in a real-life context to public and/or citizen-related problems.

Through the CONPES No. 3920 of 2018 (National Data Exploitation Policy - Big Data), action number seven, the Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications, along with the National Planning Department, will, in December of 2021, will provide a collaborative space (data sandbox) in which the data sets used and generated during the advanced projects, as well as the documentation of the processes and its result, are published in a work environment that allows its public use. The previously mentioned document, states that the Data Sandbox must allow the testing of standards and the collaboration of public and private actors, academia, and civil society. Additionally, this space will facilitate the coordination between entities to join efforts in the implementation of projects using Analytics, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for common issues in accordance with their capabilities and interests. This will allow to boost the implementation of analytics projects and institutional implementation.The initiative has the following objectives:Search within the Data Sandbox, among different users from the same entity, datasets in a collaborative and interactive manner.Store and process structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data through the use of Big Data technologies.Make available to the country's public entities, a collaborative space (Data Sandbox) for the implementation of pilot projects of Analytics and Big Data, prior to compliance with the terms and conditions of use of the Data Sandbox and the current capacity to maintain the pilot projects.Provide, for state entities, an experimental and iterative environment for solution testing and evaluation of Big Data technologies.Provide a collaborative space that allows public entities to share data, documentation, algorithms, and other results of pilot projects regarding Analytics and Big Data in the public sector.

Chile is generating data thanks to the scientific work carried out in the country (i.e. astronomy and Earth observation). The Data Observatory seeks to democratise open access to the data and knowledge generated from these areas of research. To make this data available from anywhere, Chile is working with technology from the cloud. Through the availability of data, the country aims to maximise the benefit that can be obtained from it for science, research and productive development. At the same time, by making the data available, Chile aims to contribute to the generation of skills and talent to find new uses for them and the algorithms derived from them. Collaborative work is essential to tackle different projects that seek answers to various problems and that bring together the talent and capabilities of numerous sectors.The initiative has the following objectives:The DO's vision is to be at the forefront of data-centric innovation, leading the production of data-centric, talent and social capital solutions. title: Council Conclusions on Regulatory Sandboxes
document_name: Council Conclusions on Regulatory Sandboxes
body:
In November 2020, the Council of the European Union adopted a set of conclusions on the role of regulatory sandboxes and experimentation clauses in an innovation-friendly, future-proof, sustainable and resilient EU regulatory framework.

These conclusions call upon the European Commission to present the findings of its evaluation in the first half of 2021, followed up by practical recommendations for the possible future use of regulatory sandboxes and experimentation clauses at EU level in the second half of 2021. Regulatory sandboxes are increasingly used in a range of sectors, often including the use of new, emerging technologies - such as AI and blockchain - or the innovative use of existing technologies.The initiative has the following objectives:- To affirm that regulatory sandboxes offer significant opportunities, particularly to innovate and grow for all businesses, especially SMEs, including micro-enterprises as well as start-ups, in industry, services and other sectors.- To encourage the Commission to continue considering the use of experimentation clauses on a case-by-case basis when drafting and reviewing legislation, as well as to evaluate the use of experimentation clauses in ex-post evaluations and fitness checks on the basis of an exchange of information with member states.

title: Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence
document_name: Концепція розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні
body:
Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine was adopted in 2020 as one of the country’s key strategic documents in the AI sector. It focuses on promoting the development and integration of artificial intelligence across multiple areas of public life. The Concept was designed to foster innovation, improve public services, and strengthen economic growth.

Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine was approved in 2020 and sets out the national vision and strategic priorities for the development, deployment, and regulation of AI technologies across all sectors. The initiative addresses the lack of coordinated state policy in the AI field, the absence of a legal and ethical framework, and the growing need to ensure Ukraine’s global competitiveness in digital technologies.
Objectives:
To foster research and innovation in AI, promote the responsible and safe implementation of AI technologies, and support their integration into both the public and private sectors. To raise awareness of AI opportunities among citizens, develop educational programmes, and establish a governance system that ensures ethical, transparent, and human-centred use of AI. The Concept is expected to be updated with the forthcoming National AI Strategy 2030.

title: Climate Change Cockpit
document_name: Klimawandel-Cockpit Österreich
body:
The Climate Change Cockpit provides a centralised platform for environmental data in Austria’s tourism sector. It consolidates information from multiple sources to give a comprehensive overview of environmental conditions and trends. The initiative helps tourism organisations make better decisions and plan strategically to address climate-related challenges.

The Climate Change Cockpit was created to tackle the problem of fragmented environmental data, which made it difficult for the tourism sector to gain a holistic understanding of climate impacts. By consolidating disparate data sources into a single, accessible platform, the initiative enhances transparency and usability of environmental information.
Key objectives include:
Centralising environmental data relevant to tourism and climate changeProviding real-time overviews of environmental conditions and trendsSupporting decision-making and strategic planning for climate adaptation in the tourism sectorThe initiative was co-developed by the Austrian National Tourist Office and the Austrian Federal Computing Center, ensuring that both industry and technical expertise contribute to the platform. Through this collaboration, tourism stakeholders can access reliable, actionable data to inform sustainable practices and climate resilience strategies.

body:
The Forest Fire Protection AI Project uses AI and augmented reality to monitor forest fire protection zones. It aims to reduce the risk and impact of forest fires. The project combines automatic and participatory surveillance for more effective forest safety.

The initiative focuses on improving forest fire prevention and management through advanced technology. By applying AI algorithms and augmented reality tools, the project enables real-time monitoring of forest fire protection zones and supports decision-making during potential fire events.
Key objectives include:
Automatic detection of fire risks in protected forest areasParticipatory monitoring, allowing local communities and authorities to contribute to surveillanceMinimising the impact of forest fires through early warning and rapid responseThe project is led by the NOVA Laboratory for Computer Science and Informatics, which integrates cutting-edge research with practical applications. By combining AI, augmented reality, and community participation, the initiative seeks to enhance environmental protection and reduce forest fire-related damages.
Future outlook:
Expansion of surveillance capabilities using more advanced AI modelsIncreased community involvement in forest monitoringPotential replication of the system in other regions at risk of forest fires

To assist physicians in the diagnosis of COVID-19, an artificial intelligence application has been developed that diagnoses COVID-19 from Computed Tomography (CT) images. body:
The paper distinguishes between proven fact and speculation and illustrates how facial recognition technologies can have markedly different implications for society depending on the type of system and the reasons for its use.

The Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation (CDEI) is an advisory body set up by the UK government and led by an independent board of experts. It is tasked with identifying the measures we need to take to maximise the benefits of AI and data-driven technology for our society and economy. The CDEI has a unique mandate to advise government on these issues, drawing on expertise and perspectives from across society. The CDEI Snapshots are a series of briefing papers that aim to improve public understanding of topical issues related to the development and deployment of AI. These papers are intended to separate fact from fiction, clarify what is known and unknown, and suggest areas for further investigation.The initiative has the following objective(s):To create the conditions in which ethical innovation can thrive: an environment in which the public are confident their values are reflected in the way data-driven technology is developed and deployed; where we can trust that decisions informed by algorithms are fair; and where risks posed by innovation are identified and addressed. In this snapshot, we distinguish between proven fact and speculation and illustrates how facial recognition technologies can have markedly different implications for society depending on the type of system and the reasons for its use.

document_name: ARTIQ - AI Centres of Excellence
body:
The Artificial Intelligence & Data Analysis Centre (AIDA) is one of our four management centres of the public research centre NASK, focusing on coordinating, initiating and developing projects involving artificial intelligence applications, taking into account the needs of the administration, cybersecurity, education and the media. The goal of AIDA is to become a Central European centre of excellence specialising in artificial intelligence.

Advanced technologies are increasingly used to commit sophisticated criminal activities. Identifying, preventing and fighting modern crimes demands the implementation of ground-breaking technologies and methods. The EU-funded AIDA project is focussing on cybercrime and terrorism by approaching specific issues and challenges related to law enforcement agencies (LEAs) investigation and intelligence using pioneering machine learning and artificial intelligence methods.
The proposed solution aims to deliver a descriptive and predictive data analytics platform and related tools to prevent, detect, analyse, and combat criminal activities.
While cybercrime and terrorism pose distinct problems and may rely on different input datasets, the analysis of this data can benefit from the application of the same fundamental technology base framework, endowed with Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning techniques applied to big data analytics, and extended and tailored with crime- and task- specific additional analytic capabilities and tools.

The resulting TRL-7 integrated, modular and flexible AIDA framework will include LE-specific effective, efficient and automated data mining and analytics services to deal with intelligence and investigation workflows, extensive content acquisition, information extraction and fusion, knowledge management and enrichment through novel applications of Big Data processing, machine learning, artificial intelligence, predictive and visual analytics. The final solution will reach Technology Readiness Level 7: system prototype demonstration in operational environment.
AIDA system and tools will be made available to LEAs through a secure sandbox environment that aims to raise the technological readiness level of the solutions through their application in operational environment with real data.

title: Administrative Cloud Strategy (DVS)
document_name: Deutsche Verwaltungscloudstrategie
body:
The Administrative Cloud Strategy (DVS) is part of Germany’s efforts to enhance digital sovereignty in public administration by establishing a standardized, modular federal cloud infrastructure. The strategy aims to enable interoperability across federal, state, and local government levels by creating open standards and interfaces. It seeks to reduce dependence on single providers by fostering a diverse ecosystem of specialized IT service providers.

The DVS focuses on five key areas: 
i) standardized development platforms, ii) application management, iii) code repository systems, iv) infrastructure services, and iv) a harmonized operational model. These measures collectively aim to make federal cloud solutions interoperable and compatible across all levels of government, thereby enhancing the efficiency and resilience of Germany’s public sector IT systems.

The CNIL, Commission Nationale Informatique & Libertes, is the French Data Protection Agency. As part of its support strategy, the CNIL has launched a first "personal data sandbox" session, in the form of a call for projects in the field of health.

Created in 1978, the CNIL is an independent administrative body that operates in accordance with the data protection legislation of the 6th January 1978 as amended on the 6th August 2004. The independence of the CNIL is guaranteed on account of its composition and organisation. The CNIL is responsible for ensuring that information technology remains at the service of citizens. Ten projects will benefit from CNIL support in 2021, four of which will receive enhanced support in order to come up with a solution that respects the privacy of individuals. CNIL has published several documents on artificial intelligence, such as their paper on algorithmic discrimination (2020) and "How can humans keep the upper hand? Report on the ethical matters raised by algorithms and artificial intelligence" (2017).The initiative has the following objectives:To ensure that data privacy law is applied to the collection, storage, and use of personal data.To foster data-driven innovation such as AI applications.To support the development of GDPR-compliant solutions (especially in the field of health for the 2021/2022 session, and edtech for 2022/2023).

As part of the national AI strategy, Germany aimed to fund 100 new AI professorships by 2025, a target achieved in 2022 with a total of 150 professorships created by 2023. These include positions supported by various measures, such as the Alexander von Humboldt Professorship for AI, university AI competence centres, the tenure-track programme, DFG projects, and collaborations with non-university research institutions.

Germany faced a shortage of long-term academic posts in AI, limiting teaching capacity and slowing research transfer. Under its national AI strategy, the federal government and Länder set a target of 100 new AI professorships by 2025 to expand expertise nationwide. That goal was reached ahead of schedule.
The initiative draws on several instruments: Alexander von Humboldt AI professorships to attract top international talent, AI competence centres at universities, tenure-track and DFG projects, and partnerships with non-university institutes.

body:
The Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia from 2020 to 2025 defines the introduction of content on artificial intelligence into our educational system. As part of the curriculum in the seventh grade, the subjects Engineering and Technology and Informatics and Computing are compulsory.

Twice a week during the school year, seventh grade students study the role and importance of artificial intelligence through these subjects, but also gain knowledge about its application in everyday life and the impact of artificial intelligence on humans.In the eighth grade, students continue to expand their knowledge of artificial intelligence through the compulsory subject of Engineering and Technology. Students have two hours a week at their disposal to assemble and control a simple school robot with the use of artificial intelligence by the end of the school year, thanks to construction modeling.

AI Hub Tampere is a research centre hosted by Tampere University and supported by public funding. Its mission is to advance the use of applied artificial intelligence by connecting academic expertise with the needs of industry and society. The hub was created to help organisations better understand how AI can be used in real-world contexts. The initiative brings together a coalition of around 25 professors from different disciplines, reflecting the diverse ways AI affects technology, business, and society. This interdisciplinary base allows the hub to study the technical aspects of AI, like machine learning methods and data analytics, as well as the wider socio-technical impacts of digital transformation, including ethics, regulation, and human interaction with intelligent systems. AI Hub Tampere offers workshops, demonstrations, and collaboration projects that help companies and public organisations explore AI opportunities.

title: AI Covid-19 Response
document_name: IA y Ciencia de Datos para la detección temprana de potenciales brotes epidémicos y pandémicos post-COVID-19: Implementación de una estrategia escalable de historias cl­ínicas electrónicas, género-inclusiva y socialmente responsable en Argentina
body:
The project will help develop a central objective for the national sanitary policy: promoting quality and equitable access to public health services despite gender, age, economic or geographic conditions.

This initiative is part of a national strategy in health, science, technology, and innovation, explicitly supported by two key national ministries responsible for these areas. The National Government, which oversees the federal health system, is responsible for implementing measures to build a more efficient, balanced, and equitable system across all Argentine provinces.The project was designed in response to the emergency crisis caused by COVID-19. Its goal is to equip the National Health System with new technological capabilities to better manage health crises.In Argentina, the first COVID-19 case was registered on March 3, 2020. By early July, there were 1,490 deaths and over 75,000 infections. The infection rate grew rapidly in poor neighborhoods where overcrowding and fragile living conditions made it difficult to maintain hygiene and social distancing. The pandemic also had a differential impact on men and women's ability to exercise their right to health, increasing vulnerability for women due to factors such as rising domestic violence, a higher proportion of female health workers exposed to infection, and socially assigned caregiving roles predominantly shouldered by women.Besides COVID-19, Argentina faces other epidemic outbreaks. Since early 2019, there has been the most extensive measles outbreak since the virus was eliminated in 2000, with nearly 200 cases. Dengue fever also put the National Health Surveillance System on alert, with over 51,000 local cases and 1,000 imported cases between 2019 and 2020”marking the largest outbreak in the country's history. Dengue mainly affects the most vulnerable and disadvantaged provinces, including Jujuy, Salta, Misiones, and Tucum¡n. In Buenos Aires, over half of the cases occurred in vulnerable neighborhoods. These social, environmental, and health determinants directly influence the effectiveness of epidemiological surveillance.Early detection of outbreaks is a major health policy challenge. It is essential because:Preventive actions help avoid the spread of infectious diseases.Early detection allows health systems to prepare and respond effectively.Alerts can be issued to other provinces and the wider Latin American region.Early diagnosis leads to better treatment outcomes.New technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) and the analysis of large, high-quality datasets, have proven highly effective in predicting potential epidemic outbreaks globally and in the region.The initiative aims to develop a national system that uses AI and electronic medical records to detect pandemics and epidemic outbreaks at an early stage, enabling faster and more effective responses.

body:
An industry association that strengthens Bulgaria's AI ecosystem by providing targeted support to AI companies and fostering collaboration across sectors. The cluster offers specialised programmes including professional development training, financing facilitation, technical guidance for AI implementation, and access to testing infrastructure. It creates partnerships between AI companies, research institutions, and government agencies to accelerate AI adoption in Bulgaria's business sector.

AI Cluster Bulgaria is an industry association dedicated to strengthening Bulgaria’s artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem and accelerating the adoption of AI technologies across the economy. It responds to the growing need for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and capacity building among businesses, research organisations, and public institutions working with AI.
The cluster provides targeted support to AI companies through a range of specialised programmes and initiatives. These include professional development and training opportunities, facilitation of access to financing, and technical guidance for AI implementation. By connecting businesses with resources, expertise, and partners, AI Cluster Bulgaria helps organisations of all sizes integrate AI solutions into their operations effectively and responsibly.
A core focus of the cluster is on fostering cross-sector collaboration between AI companies, research institutions, and government agencies. Through partnerships and joint initiatives, it supports the creation of new AI products and services while ensuring that innovation aligns with national and European priorities for digital transformation. The cluster also offers access to testing environments and infrastructure, helping companies pilot and scale their AI technologies.

body:
Prioritizes AI systems' benefits to individuals, society, and environment. Ensures respect for human rights, fairness, privacy, and data security. Requires transparency, explainability, and mechanisms for contestability. Holds accountable those responsible for AI throughout its lifecycle.

Prioritizes AI systems that benefit individuals, society, and the environment throughout their lifecycle.

Requires AI systems to respect human rights, diversity, and individual autonomy, promoting an equitable society.

Mandates fairness by ensuring AI inclusivity and accessibility, prohibiting unfair discrimination.

Demands privacy protection and data security, with ongoing data governance and vulnerability assessments.

Ensures AI reliability and safety, mandating operation in line with intended purposes and risk management.

Calls for transparency and explainability, necessitating timely and responsible disclosures of AI impacts.

Establishes contestability, allowing challenges to AI impacts on individuals or communities through clear processes.

Holds relevant parties accountable for AI outcomes, requiring identifiable responsibility and human oversight.

body:
Urges President and Congress to develop an AI Advisory Committee with the push of the Senate and the Assembly of the State of California. Highlights need for AI policy, ethical standards, workforce planning, and innovation. Calls for bridging tech-regulation gaps. Directs resolution to federal and state officials.

Urges the President and Congress to develop a comprehensive Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee. 

Recognizes that 77% of consumers use artificial intelligence powered by many services and that one-half of the major 10 artificial intelligence startups have been brought to the United States. Notes that research further supports that robots and digital agents will displace blue-collar and white-collar workers. 

Requires the President and Congress to take a role in protecting the nation’s workforce and addressing the future changes that artificial intelligence will bring due to its potential to revolutionize the economy.

Urges officials to recognize that many countries such as Canada, China, United Kingdom and France are developing AI implementation.  

Requires Congress and the President to establish ethical principles when using artificial intelligence. Recognizes that there is a growing gap between regulatory response and the growth of technology. 

Requires the Senate and the Assembly of the State of California to work together in urging the President and Congress to develop an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee to develop artificial intelligence policy.

title: Alabama (2019) SB 47
document_name: Alabama (2019) SB 47 (Autonomous Commercial Vehicles)
body:
Authorizes autonomous commercial vehicles and teleoperation systems to operate without a conventional driver present. Mandates compliance with federal and state laws, registration, certification, and liability coverage. Assigns jurisdiction to Alabama's Department of Transportation. Specifies operator responsibilities and emergency protocols.

Authorizes autonomous commercial vehicles and vehicles with teleoperation systems to operate without a conventional driver physically present in Alabama.

Grants jurisdiction exclusively to the Department of Transportation over these vehicles and prohibits additional requirements by local entities.

Requires automated vehicles to comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards and maintain motor vehicle liability coverage of at least $2,000,000.

Establishes that the vehicle owner or lessee is considered the operator for legal compliance and that automated driving systems are licensed operators.

Mandates accident protocols requiring vehicles remain on the scene with prompt law enforcement notification.

Requires remote drivers to hold the appropriate licenses and obey state traffic laws, subject to alcohol and drug testing in cooperation with local law enforcement.

Clarifies that this act does not alter existing liability laws for vehicle stakeholders.

Specifies that the act is effective upon the Governor’s approval or enactment into law.

body:
Endeavors to provide an enabling environment for human-centered AI promoting innovation and investment. Recognizes AI's potential for inclusive growth. Commits to a human-centered approach guided by AI principles. Promotes privacy protection, international cooperation, and AI capacity building.

Endeavors to create an enabling environment for human-centered AI that fosters innovation, investment, digital entrepreneurship, and adoption of AI by MSMEs.

Recognizes AI's potential to promote inclusive economic growth and societal benefits, advancing sustainable and inclusive societies while empowering individuals.

Commits to addressing societal challenges posed by AI, such as transitions in the labor market, privacy, security, and ethical issues, through a human-centered approach guided by the G20 AI Principles.

Stipulates principles of inclusive growth, human-centered values, transparency, robustness, and accountability to maximize AI benefits while minimizing risks, with a focus on international cooperation and inclusion of developing countries.

Affirms the need to promote privacy protection, AI capacity building, and skills development.

Commits to international cooperation in research, policy development, and information sharing through the G20 Repository of Digital Policies and collaborative efforts.

body:
Encourages stakeholders to engage in responsible AI development for positive societal outcomes. Requires AI systems to be transparent, robust, secure, and accountable. Promotes public and private investment in AI R&D. Supports international cooperation and the development of global standards.

Support the responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI by engaging stakeholders to achieve inclusive growth, sustainable development, and well-being.

Require AI actors to respect human-centered values, including the rule of law, human rights, and democratic values, throughout the AI lifecycle, supported by appropriate safeguards.

Commit AI actors to transparency and explainability, providing clear information to foster AI understanding and accountability.

Ensure robustness, security, and safety of AI systems, with traceability and systematic risk management throughout their lifecycle.

Hold AI actors accountable for aligning with the principles based on roles and context.

Encourage governments to invest in AI R&D, supporting open, unbiased datasets, and fostering a digital AI ecosystem.

Promote an enabling policy environment for AI, ensuring policy adaptation, assessment mechanisms, and readiness for labor market transformation.

Engage in international cooperation to advance AI principles, share AI knowledge, and develop global technical standards.

Encourage multi-stakeholder collaboration to monitor AI developments and ensure adherence to these principles.

Comprises members appointed by the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, House Speaker, and Senate President Pro Tempore, including experts in AI, workforce development, technology, ethics, privacy, or computer science.

Requires the commission to submit a report by May 1, 2020, with findings and recommendations for administrative or policy actions related to AI, available on the website of the Office of the Governor.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles)
document_name: Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles)
body:
Permits driverless vehicles on Iowa highways if compliant with safety laws and manufacturer certification. Requires insurance for autonomous vehicles and mandates accident reporting. Allows on-demand driverless vehicle networks. Centralizes regulation authority, prohibiting local restrictions or taxes on automated vehicles.

Defines key terms like "automated driving system" and "driverless-capable vehicle" relevant to motor vehicles operated by autonomous systems.

Allows the operation of driverless-capable vehicles on public highways without a human driver present, provided they meet safety and compliance standards.

Requires system-equipped vehicles to operate within designated operational domains and comply with state traffic and safety laws unless exempted.

Mandates financial liability coverage for system-equipped vehicles before they can operate on public highways.

Stipulates that automated vehicles involved in accidents must remain at the scene and report to law enforcement, holding vehicle owners accountable for compliance.

Permits the operation of on-demand driverless-capable vehicle networks for transporting persons or goods, integrating with digital transport services.

Grants exclusive governance and regulatory authority over automated systems to the state department, prohibiting additional local regulations or taxes on such systems.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Arkansas SB 656
document_name: Arkansas SB 656 ("Data-Driven Decision-Making Task Force")
body:
Establishes a task force composed of twelve legislative members to study and recommend a shared services model for statewide data sharing, including necessary legislation and funding mechanisms.

Creates the Data-Sharing and Data-Driven Decision-Making Task Force, comprised of twelve members appointed from the Senate and House of Representatives.

Mandates the task force to study and recommend the implementation of a statewide data-sharing system across state agencies.

Requires the task force to evaluate current data management inefficiencies, and propose necessary legislation and funding mechanisms for system implementation. Empowers the task force to hire external consultants if necessary.

Requires the task force to meet at least monthly and report findings to the Governor and legislative leaders by December 31, 2019; expires the task force on January 1, 2020.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Senate Resolution requesting the State to convene an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee to investigate how to implement, develop, and regulate artificial intelligence in the State.
document_name: Hawaii AI Advisory Committee Resolution
body:
Establishes an AI advisory committee in Hawaii to investigate how to implement, develop, and regulate AI in the state. Requires the committee to survey AI applications in other governments, methods for encouraging AI R&D in Hawaii, and potential dangers of, and regulatory systems for, integrating AI into state operations.

Establishes an AI advisory committee in Hawaii to investigate how to implement, develop, and regulate AI in the state; the committee will be composed of government, academic, and industry stakeholders.

Requires the committee to evaluate and make recommendations on AI applications in other governments, competitive advantages to be gained by integrating AI into Hawaii’s economy, methods for encouraging AI R&D in universities and private sector, the potential danger of integrating AI into state operations, and potential regulatory systems for AI. 

Requires the committee to submit a report of findings and proposed legislation to the Legislature before its convening in 2020.

document_name: New Jersey (2019) AJR 164 (Advanced Autonomous Vehicle Task Force)
body:
Establishes the "New Jersey Advanced Autonomous Vehicle Task Force" to study and recommend integration laws for advanced autonomous vehicles. Requires issuing a report evaluating existing laws, suggesting pilot programs, and recommending safe integration on public roads within 180 days after its initial meeting.

Establishes the "New Jersey Advanced Autonomous Vehicle Task Force" to study and recommend policies for the safe integration of autonomous vehicles on state roads.

Comprises 11 members, including key state officials and public experts appointed by the Governor.

Mandates the task force to hold its initial meeting within 90 days of the law's effective date and to elect a chair from among its members.

Requires the task force to issue a report within 180 days after its first meeting, evaluating existing laws, proposing pilot programs, and suggesting legislative measures.

Entitles the task force to utilize the services of state employees and receive assistance from the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission, Department of Transportation, and Alan M. Voorhees Transportation Center.

Defines "advanced autonomous vehicle" as one with a driving automation level of 3, 4, or 5, per SAE J3016 standards.

Expires the act upon the report's submission.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Delaware House Concurrent Resolution 7 (2019-2020)
document_name: Delaware (2019-20) HCR 7 (Planning for the Impacts of AI on the Workforce)
body:
Urges Delaware State Agencies and Government branches to plan for the effects of automation, robotics, and AI. Recognizes the need for daily operational and long-term strategic preparations to limit negative impacts on Delawareans.

Recognizes the potential impact of robotics, automation, and AI on the workforce and the importance of planning for their effects.

Requires Delaware State Agencies and government branches to implement daily operational and long-term strategic planning to mitigate negative impacts of these technologies.

Encourages consideration of legal and ethical implications in AI development without hindering innovation.

Emphasizes the need for AI applications to prioritize security, ethics, dignity, autonomy, and self-determination.

Highlights the risk of technological displacement and its effects on public and private sectors.

Aims to prepare Delaware for changes in employment due to advancements in AI and automation.

category: U.S. state and local documents
title: Illinois House Bill 2557 (2019)
document_name: Illinois HB 2557 (AI Video Interview Act)
body:
Requires employers in Illinois using AI for video interview analysis to notify applicants, explain AI functionality, and obtain consent. Prohibits sharing videos except with necessary evaluators. Instructs employers to delete videos upon applicant request within 30 days.

Requires employers in Illinois to notify job applicants if artificial intelligence will analyze their video interviews and to provide information on how the AI works, including characteristics it evaluates.

Requires employers to obtain applicants' consent before using AI to evaluate them.

Prohibits employers from using AI analysis on applicants who do not consent.

Permits sharing of applicant videos only with individuals necessary for evaluating the applicant's fitness for the position.

Obliges employers to delete video interviews and instruct any recipients to do the same, including backup copies, within 30 days if the applicant requests it.

title: Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859)
document_name: Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859)
body:
Establishes the American AI Initiative to maintain U.S. leadership in AI, emphasizing R&D investment, workforce training, international collaboration, and requires federal agencies to pursue and promote AI innovation through the development of regulatory guidance.

Mandates the Federal Government to maintain U.S. leadership in AI through a coordinated strategy known as the American AI Initiative.

Requires agencies to pursue strategic guidelines to prioritize AI R&D, enhance data accessibility, and reduce barriers for AI deployment, ensuring protection of civil liberties and privacy.

Obligates agencies to develop technical standards to minimize vulnerabilities and foster public trust in AI systems.

Directs the prioritization and training of American workers in AI-related skills to prepare them for future job markets.

Instructs the development of international standards and promotes global collaboration while safeguarding critical AI technologies from foreign adversaries.

Develops an action plan to protect U.S. advantages in AI technology against strategic competitors and adversaries.

The platform plans to integrate multiple sources of input, including citizen feedback, and expand its coverage over time.

On 9 September 2019, the White House hosted its Summit on AI in Government.

Over the last several years, the private sector has demonstrated that AI can improve the quality of services, create new products, and increase efficiency. The Federal government now has the opportunity to improve its services on behalf of the American people by partnering with the private sector to leverage this knowledge and capability. Some Federal agencies are already leading the way by using AI to process grant applications, check Federal solicitations for regulatory compliance, improve nautical charts, process satellite imagery, perform predictive maintenance, and much more. Still, there is significant room for growth. A number of inter-related challenges must be addressed ” some technical, some requiring process changes, and some involving talent and workforce issues.The initiative has the following objective(s):To find near-term solutions to these challenges to improve government services using AI.

org: Centre for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles |Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy |Department for Transport
title: Trialling Automated Vehicle Technologies in Public
document_name: Trialling Automated Vehicle Technologies in Public
body:
This code of practice provides guidance on trialling automated vehicle technologies on public roads or in other public places in the UK. It makes recommendations on how to maintain safety and minimise potential risks.

The UK Government recognises and welcomes the growing appetite to test and trial automated vehicle technologies and services in the UK. New technologies will have a major impact on traditional mobility business models, and the changing landscape of the passenger and freight services markets. The Government believes that automated road vehicle technologies and services have the potential to offer benefits of increased safety and accessibility to the travelling public and create new opportunities for UK industry. Therefore, the Government wishes to support and facilitate the safe development and introduction of these technologies to the UK's roads. Trialling any level of automated vehicle technology is possible on any UK road if carried out in line with UK law. Trialling organisations do not need to obtain permits or pay surety bonds when conducting trials in the UK. As part of complying with the law, they will need to ensure that they have: a driver or operator, in or out of the vehicle, who is ready, able, and willing to resume control of the vehicle;a roadworthy vehicle;appropriate insurance in place; The Code also notes that those planning tests should speak with the road and enforcement authorities, develop engagement plans, and have data recorders fitted. The Government acknowledges the desire to conduct advanced trials on public roads. Such trials may not readily fit within current UK legislation, so the Department for Transport's motoring agencies will introduce and operate a process to support those looking to safely conduct advanced trials. This process will be available to support industry when they are ready to do such trials. Those planning to conduct advanced trials should contact the Centre for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles in advance (see Annex A for contact details). Failure to follow the Code may be relevant to liability in any legal proceedings. Similarly, compliance with the expectations set by the Code does not guarantee immunity from liability in such circumstances.The initiative has the following objective(s):To organise safe trials for automated vehicle technologies on public roads and in public places.

title: Towards Trustworthy AI: Malta's Ethical AI Framework 2019
document_name: Towards Trustworthy AI: Malta's Ethical AI Framework 2019
body:
A strong ethical AI framework as a supplement to the current legal and regulatory system is a core component of Malta's AI strategy to ensure that AI development is ethically aligned, transparent and socially responsible.

In developing the Malta Ethical AI Framework, the Government recognises that developing trustworthy AI is a complex task that will require the Framework to intersect with various policy initiatives including existing laws and regulations, investments in tools and continuous monitoring mechanisms, skills and capabilities, innovation ecosystem and regulatory mechanisms. A National Technology Ethics Committee will be set up under the Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) to oversee the Ethical AI Framework and its intersection across these areas. The purpose of the Malta Ethical AI Framework is to establish a set of guiding principles and trustworthy AI governance and control practices that can serve as the foundation for the design and implementation of these broader constructs, as a supplement to the legal and regulatory system.The initiative has the following objectives:To make of Malta the Ultimate AI launchpad “ a place in which local and foreign companies, and entrepreneurs, can develop, prototype, test and scale AI. In other words, create the conditions for AI to springboard from Malta to the world.To create a regulatory and innovation ecosystem that develops trustworthy AI.

title: The Ultimate AI Launchpad: A strategy and vision for Artificial Intelligence in Malta 2030
document_name: Strateġija u Viżjoni tal-Intelliġenza Artifiċjali għall-IA f'Malta 2030
body:
Malta's AI Strategy 2030 aims to make the country a leader in artificial intelligence by encouraging investment, innovation, and use of AI in both public and private sectors. It supports six pilot projects in areas like health, education, and traffic to improve services and quality of life. This initiative helps businesses and citizens benefit from smarter, more efficient solutions.

The AI Strategy harness the potential of artificial intelligence and is designed to establish a thriving AI ecosystem through strategic investments, support for start-ups, and fostering innovation. The Strategy prioritises the adoption of AI in the public sector and support measures for the adoption of AI in the private sector to improve public services, and promote transparency, ensuring that AI-driven solutions align with societal needs and public interests. This holistic approach positions the public sector as a catalyst for broader AI adoption and development.The Strategy aims to be expansive in nature, looking at the commercial and social impact, areas of economic opportunity and the need for special consideration, where AI use cases potentially intersect with national priorities, values and citizen's rights.Due to societal changes and new technologicla trends, Malta is currently in the process of realigning its National AI Strategy, including AI for society, wellbeing and sustainability.

In March 2024, the Danish government reached a political agreement to enhance the quality of primary and lower secondary education, introducing Technology Comprehension as a new element in the curriculum. This initiative aims to:
Embed Technology Comprehension into traditional subjects, ensuring students develop digital literacy and critical thinking skills.Provide students with the ability to reflect critically on, and competently use, emerging digital technologies, including AI tools.Assign an expert group to determine the subjects and grade levels where Technology Comprehension will be integrated, ensuring age-appropriate learning outcomes.Support the broader goal of preparing students for a digitally advanced society, enhancing both educational quality and digital readiness.By integrating Technology Comprehension, the initiative seeks to equip students with essential skills for the digital age, fostering both practical competence and ethical awareness in technology use.

The initiative has the following objectives:The Program has the objective of realising conceptual frameworks on the use of emerging technologies based on 5G in order to promote entrepreneurial development within the Italian territory. The design and implementation phases of the Program interventions will take place through the involvement, at various levels, of public administrations, with "5G environments" being tested. title: Start-up Hub Portal
body:
The Start-up Hub Portal in Portugal is an online platform that maps the country’s start-up ecosystem. It gathers information on start-ups, incubators, investors, and support programmes, offering a real-time view of the sector. The portal makes it easier for entrepreneurs, investors, and institutions to connect and collaborate.

The Start-up Hub Portal is a comprehensive digital platform designed to provide a clear and up-to-date picture of Portugal’s entrepreneurship landscape. By mapping start-ups, incubators, accelerators, and investment programmes, it responds to the need for a central reference point that both policymakers and entrepreneurs can rely on. Its main function is to bring visibility and structure to a dynamic but sometimes fragmented ecosystem.
The initiative pursues several key objectives:
Identify and geolocate start-ups, incubators, and accelerators across Portugal.Aggregate and benchmark public and private initiatives that support entrepreneurship.Provide real-time information on support measures, funding opportunities, and ecosystem players.Foster collaboration by connecting entrepreneurs, investors, and institutions.Implementation is centred on building a single access point for the entrepreneurship ecosystem. The portal collects, organises, and updates data so that different actors—whether a new entrepreneur seeking an incubator, an investor scouting opportunities, or a policymaker analysing sector growth—can access reliable and comprehensive information.
Over time, the Start-up Hub Portal is expected to evolve into a more interactive and data-driven tool, with expanded features for matchmaking, personalised recommendations, and international visibility. By scaling its reach and improving functionality, the initiative strengthens Portugal’s position as a competitive and transparent environment for entrepreneurship and innovation.
